\section{The $\C^3$ Rosetta Stone: Hall/representation verification}
\label{sec:c3-rosetta}
% ============================================================

The simplest CY3 --- affine space $X = \C^3$ --- serves as the Rosetta Stone for the Hall and representation-theoretic half of the programme. The CY Hall side produces $\CoHA(\C^3) \simeq Y^+(\widehat{\fgl}_1)$ (Kontsevich--Soibelman, Schiffmann--Vasserot), and the doubled/evaluation side acts on the $\cW_{1+\infty}$ vacuum module at $c = 1$ (Proch\'azka--Rap\v{c}\'ak). The coefficient computations verify this Hall/character chain; they do not construct the hCS-to-critical-CoHA comparison, which remains the first missing lemma.

\subsection{The functor chain}
\label{subsec:c3-functor-chain}

The $d = 3$ functor for $\C^3$ factors as a five-step chain:

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabular}{rl}
\textbf{Step 1.} & $\mathrm{PV}^*(\C^3)$ with $\mathrm{GL}(3)$-invariant Schouten--Nijenhuis bracket \\[3pt]
& $\big\downarrow$ \quad $\Omega$-deformation in the $\sigma_3$ direction \\[3pt]
\textbf{Step 2.} & Quantized Lie conformal algebra \\[3pt]
& $\big\downarrow$ \quad Factorization envelope (Nishinaka--Vicedo) \\[3pt]
\textbf{Step 3.} & $Y^+(\widehat{\fgl}_1)$ as the positive-half Hall algebra \\[3pt]
& $\big\downarrow$ \quad Drinfeld double / centre and vacuum evaluation \\[3pt]
\textbf{Step 4.} & $\cW_{1+\infty}[\lambda]$-vacuum representation and $\Etwo$-braided category with $R$-matrix \\
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The input at Step~1 is $\mathrm{PV}^*(\C^3) = \bigoplus_{p=0}^{3} \Gamma(\C^3, \bigwedge^p T_{\C^3})$, the algebra of polyvector fields with the Schouten--Nijenhuis bracket. The $\mathrm{GL}(3)$-invariant sector carries the deformation-theoretic data needed for the CY-to-chiral functor. The $\Omega$-deformation at Step~2 is parametrized by $\sigma_3 = h_1 h_2 h_3$ (with $h_1 + h_2 + h_3 = 0$), the unique direction in $\HH^2(\mathrm{PV}^*(\C^3))$. At the self-dual level ($\sigma_3 \to 0$, giving $h_1 = 1, h_2 = 0, h_3 = -1$), the positive-half Hall algebra has a Heisenberg vacuum evaluation; this is representation-level data, not an isomorphism of $Y^+$ with the VOA.

\begin{theorem}[Abelianity of the classical bracket]
\label{wn:thm:c3-abelian-bracket}
The $\mathrm{GL}(3)$-invariant Schouten--Nijenhuis brackets on $\mathrm{PV}^*(\C^3)$ all vanish. Three independent proofs:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item \emph{Direct computation}: every bracket $[\alpha, \beta]_{\mathrm{SN}}$ of $\mathrm{GL}(3)$-invariant polyvector fields evaluates to zero by explicit contraction.
 \item \emph{Graded skew-symmetry + degree count}: in the Gerstenhaber grading (shifted degree $|\alpha|_s = |\alpha| - 1$), the generators $E \in \mathrm{PV}^1$ and $\partial_1 \wedge \partial_2 \wedge \partial_3 \in \mathrm{PV}^3$ have even shifted degree ($0$ and $2$ respectively), so $[\alpha, \alpha] = 0$ for these by graded skew-symmetry. The remaining generators $1 \in \mathrm{PV}^0$ and $\omega^{-1} \in \mathrm{PV}^2$ have odd shifted degree, but $[1, -]_{\mathrm{SN}} = 0$ identically (constants are central) and $[\omega^{-1}, \omega^{-1}]_{\mathrm{SN}} \in \mathrm{PV}^3$ is zero by explicit computation. All mixed brackets vanish by the degree-overflow argument of~(iii).
 \item \emph{Weight/exterior degree overflow}: the bracket lowers exterior degree by~$1$; any nontrivial $\mathrm{GL}(3)$-invariant in the target degree must have weight exceeding the polynomial degree available.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, the nonabelian OPE seen in the $\cW_{1+\infty}$ vacuum
representation arises from the envelope, the double/centre, the central
extension, and normal ordering, not from the classical bracket alone. The
CY3 Hall side produces a quantum positive half from classically abelian
input.

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 95 tests in \texttt{c3\_lie\_conformal.py}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hochschild cohomology and unique deformation]
\label{wn:thm:c3-hochschild}
For $\C^3$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $\HH^2(\mathrm{PV}^*(\C^3)) = 1$: the deformation space is one-dimensional, spanned by the $\sigma_3$ direction. The unique deformation is the $\Omega$-deformation.
 \item $\HH^3(\mathrm{PV}^*(\C^3)) = 0$: the Bogomolov--Tian--Todorov theorem guarantees unobstructedness.
 \item The quantized Hall algebra is $Y^+(\widehat{\fgl}_1)$; its
 self-dual vacuum evaluation has the $c=1$ Heisenberg shadow.
\end{enumerate}
For the resolved conifold: $\HH^2 = 1$, $\HH^3 = 0$, but the quantization produces the CoHA ($\Eone$, associative), \emph{not} a vertex algebra. The singularity breaks factorization locality.

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 71 tests in \texttt{cy3\_hochschild.py}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[Smooth vs singular: locality of the quantization]
\label{wn:rem:smooth-singular-locality}
The distinction between smooth and singular CY3 is categorical:
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
 \toprule
 \textbf{CY3} & \textbf{Quantization} & \textbf{Algebraic type} \\
 \midrule
 Smooth ($\C^3$, quintic, $K3 \times E$) & Vertex algebra (local) & $\Eone$-chiral ($\Etwo$ on Drinfeld center) \\
 Singular (conifold) & Associative algebra (nonlocal) & $\Eone$ (associative) \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The factorization envelope requires local data (the polyvector fields form a cosheaf whose sections over small discs control the OPE), and singularities obstruct the local-to-global passage.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Necessity of $\Omega$-deformation for noncompact CY3]
\label{wn:prop:omega-necessary}
Without the $\Omega$-deformation, the CY3 functor chain for $\C^3$ collapses: the Lie conformal algebra is abelian (Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:c3-abelian-bracket}), the envelope produces the free Heisenberg, and the $\Etwo$ structure is trivially $\Einf$ (symmetric monoidal). Noncompactness forces the introduction of external data: $T^3$-equivariant structure plus $\bS^3$-framing. For compact CY3, neither should be needed: the nontrivial global geometry plays the role of the $\Omega$-deformation.

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 87 tests in \texttt{c3\_envelope\_comparison.py}.
\end{proposition}

\subsection{The Drinfeld center and $\Etwo$ enhancement}
\label{subsec:c3-drinfeld-center}

\begin{conjecture}[Drinfeld center identification]
\label{wn:thm:c3-drinfeld-center}
\ClaimStatusConjectured{}
\[
	\cZ\bigl(\Rep^{\Eone}(Y^+(\widehat{\fgl}_1))\bigr)
	\;\dashrightarrow\;
	\Rep^{\Etwo}(Y(\widehat{\fgl}_1))
	\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}_\lambda}\;
	\Rep(\cW_{1+\infty}[\lambda]).
\]
The first arrow is the conjectural completed Drinfeld-double/centre
comparison; the second is an evaluation functor.  This is not an
equivalence between $Y^+$ and the full $\cW_{1+\infty}$ VOA.
The character of the Drinfeld center is
\[
 \mathrm{ch}\bigl(\cZ(\Rep(Y^+))\bigr) \;=\; M(q)^2 \cdot P(q)
 \;=\; \prod_{n \geq 1} (1-q^n)^{-(2n+1)},
\]
where $M(q) = \prod(1-q^n)^{-n}$ is the MacMahon function and $P(q) = \prod(1-q^n)^{-1}$ is the Euler partition function. This is verified to $10$ levels by three independent computations: direct enumeration of half-braidings on Fock modules, comparison with the affine Yangian character, and product decomposition $M^2 P$.

The Yang $R$-matrix on the charge-$2$ sector is an explicit $8 \times 8$ matrix satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item The Yang--Baxter equation $R_{12}(u-v)\,R_{13}(u)\,R_{23}(v) = R_{23}(v)\,R_{13}(u)\,R_{12}(u-v)$ at the matrix level (symbolic verification).
 \item Unitarity: $R(z)\,R(-z) = \mathrm{Id}$.
 \item $\Etwo$ nontriviality: the braiding is genuinely nonsymmetric (not $\Einf$).
\end{enumerate}

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 93 finite-truncation tests in
\texttt{drinfeld\_center\_yangian.py}.  These tests verify the character
and low-sector Yang--Baxter shadows; they do not by themselves prove an
equivalence of completed braided representation categories.
\end{conjecture}

\subsection{The bar complex and shadow tower of $\C^3$}
\label{subsec:c3-bar-shadow}

\begin{proposition}[Bar-complex Euler product for $\C^3$]
\label{wn:prop:c3-bar-euler}
The bar-complex Euler product for $\C^3$ is
\[
 \sum_{k \geq 0} (-1)^k \, \mathrm{ch}(B^k) \;=\; \frac{1}{M(q)} \;=\; \prod_{n \geq 1}(1-q^n)^n.
\]
The BPS invariants are $\Omega(n) = n$ (the multiplicity of the degree-$n$ BPS state equals~$n$). The first bar cohomology at degree $n$ has $\dim H^1(B)_n = n$.

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 115 tests in \texttt{c3\_grand\_verification.py}; 59 tests in \texttt{bar\_comparison\_c3.py}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Heisenberg/evaluation modular characteristic of $\C^3$]
\label{wn:thm:kappa-c3}
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\C^3)$ in the self-dual Heisenberg/evaluation
shadow is $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(H_1)=1$.  This is not an identification
of $\CoHA(\C^3)=Y^+$ with the full $\cW_{1+\infty}$ VOA.

This is \emph{not} $c/2 = 1/2$. At the $c=1$ evaluation shadow used
here, the Heisenberg quotient is $H_1$, whose modular characteristic is
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(H_k)=k$, giving $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}=1$.

Five independent verifications:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
 \item \emph{OPE}: $J(z)J(w) \sim 1/(z-w)^2$ gives level $k = 1$, hence $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(H_1) = 1$.
 \item \emph{MacMahon asymptotics}: the genus-$1$ free energy $F_1 = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}/24 = 1/24$.
 \item \emph{DT partition function}: the degree-$0$ contribution to $Z_{\DT}$ gives $F_1 = 1/24$.
 \item \emph{Affine Yangian}: the structure function $g(u)$ at the self-dual point determines $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 1$.
 \item \emph{CY categorical trace}: $\chi^{\CY}_{\mathrm{eff}}(\C^3) = 1$.
\end{enumerate}
The shadow tower is class~$\mathbf{G}$ (Gaussian, $r_{\max} = 2$): $C = 0$, $Q = 0$, $\Delta = 8\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} S_4 = 0$.

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 115 tests in \texttt{c3\_grand\_verification.py}; 98 tests in \texttt{c3\_shadow\_tower.py}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Per-channel $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ and MacMahon decomposition]
\label{wn:rem:c3-per-channel}
The $\cW_{1+\infty}$ algebra has generators at each spin $s = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$, giving per-channel modular characteristics $\kappa_s = 1/s$. The total $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = \sum_{s=1}^{N} \kappa_s = H_N$ (harmonic number, divergent as $N \to \infty$). The effective $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ per MacMahon level is $1$ (constant): the $n$-fold multiplicity of degree-$n$ BPS states exactly compensates the $1/n$ suppression. The overall classification is class~$\mathbf{M}$ (infinite shadow depth) when the full spin tower is included; it reduces to class~$\mathbf{G}$ at the Heisenberg truncation $s = 1$.

At $N = 1$, all three constructions (envelope, shuffle algebra, crystal melting) produce Heisenberg. The CoHA character is $M(q)$ (plane partitions), exceeding the $\cW$-algebra character $P(q)$ (ordinary partitions):
\[
 \frac{M(q)}{P(q)} \;=\; \prod_{n \geq 2}(1-q^n)^{-(n-1)}.
\]
This ratio counts the higher-spin contributions.

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 87 tests in \texttt{c3\_envelope\_comparison.py}; 50 tests in \texttt{macmahon\_shadow\_decomposition.py}.
\end{remark}


% ============================================================
\part{The $\En$ Hierarchy: Output Scope by Dimension}
\label{part:III}
% ============================================================

Operadic level is forced by Gerstenhaber degree $1 - d$ and Dunn--Lurie additivity: $\Phi_d$ outputs $\Einf$ at $d = 1$, $\Etwo$ at $d = 2$, $\Eone$ at $d \geq 3$. At $d \geq 3$ the chiral algebra $A$ is $\Eone$; any $\Etwo$-braiding lives on the Drinfeld centre $\cZ(\Rep^{\Eone}(A))$, not on $A$ itself. Part~\ref{part:III} exhibits the obstruction-theoretic spine: the $\bS^3$-framing class of a CY3 category lies in $\pi_3(B\Sp(2m)) = 0$ by Bott periodicity, so the topological component vanishes universally; the modular-characteristic scalar $\chi_{\mathrm{top}}/24$ fails to equal $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ (the latter is categorical, not topological); and the toric CY3 landscape traces out a coarse stratification of the $\En$ output at $d = 3$.

% ============================================================
\section{The $\bS^3$-framing obstruction: universal triviality}
\label{wn:sec:s3-framing}
% ============================================================

The chain-level $\bS^3$-framing is the central obstruction to the CY-to-chiral functor at $d = 3$ (Warning~\ref{warn:gx-not-constructed}). The following result removes the topological component of this obstruction.

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing of the topological $\bS^3$-framing obstruction for CY3 categories]
\label{wn:thm:s3-framing-vanishes}
The topological component of the $\bS^3$-framing obstruction vanishes
universally for CY3 categories. Two independent proofs:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item \emph{Symplectic structure}: the CY3 pairing on the Ext complex is antisymmetric, giving structure group $\Sp(2m)$. Since $\pi_3(B\Sp(2m)) = 0$, the obstruction class in $\pi_3$ vanishes.
 \item \emph{Bott periodicity}: the complex structure gives $\mathrm{GL}(n, \C) \to U(n)$, and $\pi_3(BU) = 0$ by Bott periodicity.
\end{enumerate}
This theorem is topological.  It does not by itself construct the
chain-level BV trivialisation on a compact CY$_3$, nor does it promote the
output algebra from $\Eone$ to $\Etwo$.

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 124 tests in \texttt{cy\_to\_chiral\_functor.py}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[Centre-level $\Etwo$ locus]
\label{wn:cor:e1-e2-trivial}
At $d=3$ the output algebra remains $\Eone$.  In the tested toric and
quiver models one can compute centre-level braided shadows:
\begin{itemize}
 \item $\C^3$: Drinfeld double/evaluation shadow; $g(z)g(-z)=1$ from the CY condition.
 \item Resolved conifold: finite quiver-model centre shadow.
 \item $K3 \times E$: conditional on the K3-sector and Borcherds data.
 \item General compact CY3: open at the chain-level BV trivialisation and centre-construction stages.
\end{itemize}

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 93 tests in \texttt{drinfeld\_center\_yangian.py}; 124 tests in \texttt{cy\_to\_chiral\_functor.py}.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The $\En$ landscape for Calabi--Yau categories]
\label{wn:rem:en-landscape}
The CY dimension $d$ determines the native algebraic structure:
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{llll}
 \toprule
 \textbf{CY dim} & \textbf{Native $\En$} & \textbf{Enhancement} & \textbf{Mechanism} \\
 \midrule
 $d = 1$ (elliptic curve) & $\Einf$ & --- & Braiding symmetric \\
 $d = 2$ (K3, Higgs) & $\Etwo$ & native & $\bS^2$-framing automatic \\
 $d = 3$ (CY threefold) & $\Eone$ & $\Eone \to \Etwo$ & Drinfeld center / $\bS^3$-framing \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
By Dunn additivity, $\Etwo \simeq \Eone \otimes_{\mathsf{E}_0} \Eone$. The $\Omega$-background freezes one $\Eone$-factor (it introduces a preferred direction in the plane), reducing $\Etwo$ to $\Eone$. The Drinfeld center passage $\cZ(\Rep^{\Eone}(\cdot))$ restores the $\Etwo$ structure by recovering the frozen factor.
\end{remark}

\section{$K3 \times E$: Borcherds shadow and conditional chiral algebra}
\label{sec:k3e-chiral-identified}
% ============================================================

This section upgrades the preliminary data of Section~\ref{sec:k3e-example}
with the Borcherds denominator shadow and the conditional relative shadow
tower computation.  The algebra-level CoHA-to-BKM identification remains a
conjectural upgrade of the character/PBW shadow.

\subsection{The CoHA and BKM superalgebra}
\label{subsec:k3e-coha}

\begin{proposition}[Borcherds denominator shadow for $K3 \times E$]
\label{wn:thm:k3e-coha}
\ClaimStatusConditional{}
The theorem-level automorphic statement for $K3\times E$ is the
Borcherds denominator/root-multiplicity shadow.  The root multiplicities
of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ are determined by the $\phi_{0,1}$ Fourier
coefficients:
\[
 \mult(\alpha) = c(|\alpha|^2/2),
\]
where $c(D)$ are the discriminant coefficients of $\phi_{0,1}$ in the Eichler--Zagier normalization ($c(-1) = 1$, $c(0) = 10$, $c(3) = -64$).

Key structural features:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ is a Lie \emph{super}algebra: $c(D) > 0$ gives bosonic roots, $c(D) < 0$ gives fermionic roots.
 \item Row-sum vanishing: $\sum_{\ell} c(4n - \ell^2) = 0$ for all $n \geq 1$.
 \item The rank-$0$ sector carries the expected level-$24$ Heisenberg shadow.
 \item The Maulik--Okounkov stable-envelope $R$-matrix supplies evidence for a Hall--Borcherds comparison, not a completed algebra isomorphism.
 \item The CY involution $g(z)g(-z) = 1$ holds in the verified local models.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 90 tests in \texttt{k3e\_coha\_structure.py}; 88 tests in \texttt{bkm\_shadow\_complete.py}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{conjecture}[CoHA-to-BKM algebra identification for $K3\times E$]
\label{wn:conj:k3e-coha-bkm}
The critical CoHA of $K3 \times E$ should identify, after the correct
Hall--Drinfeld double and completion are specified, with the positive
half of the Borcherds--Kac--Moody superalgebra associated to the
Gritsenko--Nikulin $\Delta_5$ denominator:
\[
 \CoHA(K3 \times E) \;\overset{?}{\simeq}\; U(\fn_+(\fg_{\Delta_5})).
\]
At present this is a conjectural algebra-level upgrade of the denominator
and PBW-character shadows above.
\end{conjecture}

\subsection{The relative chiral algebra construction}
\label{subsec:k3e-relative}

\begin{proposition}[Relative chiral algebra for $K3 \times E$]
\label{prop:k3e-relative-chiral}
The relative chiral algebra construction bypasses the abstract $d = 3$ functor. The fibration $K3 \times E \to E$ with K3 fibers produces the chiral algebra by relative quantization:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item Each K3 fiber contributes $\chi(K3) = 24$ free bosons (from the Mukai lattice of rank~$24$).
 \item The fiber shadow tower has $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}(\text{K3 fiber}) = 24$, class~$\mathbf{G}$.
 \item Sewing along $E$ via the DMVV formula reproduces $\Delta_5$.
 \item The Borcherds lift of $\phi_{0,1}$ is $\Delta_5$ (weight $5$ in EZ normalization).
\end{enumerate}

The full bridge:
\[
 K3 \times E \;\xrightarrow{\text{relative chiral}}\; \text{shadow tower}
 \;\xrightarrow{\text{BKM}}\; \fg_{\Delta_5}
 \;\xrightarrow{\text{denominator}}\; \tfrac{1}{64} \cdot \Delta_5.
\]

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 78 tests in \texttt{k3e\_relative\_shadow.py}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[$\phi_{0,1}$ convention]
\label{warn:phi01-convention}
The $\phi_{0,1}$ Fourier coefficients differ between the DVV normalization ($c(0) = 20$, $c(3) = -128$) and the Eichler--Zagier normalization ($c(0) = 10$, $c(3) = -64$). This manuscript uses the Eichler--Zagier convention throughout. The value $-252$ is $\tau(3)$ (the Ramanujan discriminant coefficient), not a $\phi_{0,1}$ coefficient; the distinction is load-bearing for the BKM root multiplicity formula.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Fibre, Heisenberg, and BKM invariants from sewing}
\label{subsec:k3e-fiber-global}

\begin{proposition}[BKM and fibre invariants from sewing]
\label{prop:k3e-kappa-upgrade}
The fibre, Heisenberg, and BKM invariants for $K3 \times E$ come from
different constructions:
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
 \toprule
 \textbf{Level} & \textbf{Invariant value} & \textbf{Shadow class} \\
 \midrule
 Single K3 fibre & $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}=24$ & $\mathbf{G}$ (Gaussian, $r_{\max} = 2$) \\
 BKM specialisation & $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=5$ & $\mathbf{M}$ (mixed, $r_{\max} = \infty$) \\
 Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation & $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}=3$ & $\mathbf{M}$ \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The depth upgrade $\mathbf{G} \to \mathbf{M}$ occurs because sewing along $E$
introduces the imaginary roots of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ (multi-fibre bound states).
There is no theorem-level subtraction $24-5=19$: $24$ is the fibre rank,
$5$ is the Borcherds weight, and $3$ is a Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation.

Four-path verification: (a)~Borcherds lift weight, (b)~DMVV exponent, (c)~bar Euler product matching, (d)~shadow connection monodromy.

\subsection{The Maulik--Okounkov $R$-matrix}
\label{subsec:k3e-mo-rmatrix}

\begin{proposition}[MO $R$-matrix for $K3 \times E$]
\label{prop:k3e-mo-rmatrix}
The Maulik--Okounkov stable-envelope $R$-matrix for $K3 \times E$ matches the affine Yangian structure function $g(u)$ exactly. The Yang--Baxter equation is verified.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]

 \item Nontrivial braiding requires breaking the hyper-K\"ahler structure via the $\Omega$-background.
\end{enumerate}
This is consistent with the $\Etwo$ mechanism: the self-dual K3 has $\Einf$ braiding (symmetric), and the $\Omega$-deformation breaks it to $\Etwo$.

% ============================================================
\section{$\chi_{\mathrm{top}}/24 \neq \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$: the modular characteristic is categorical}
\label{sec:chi-neq-kappa}
% ============================================================

\begin{remark}[Subscript discipline in this section]
\label{rem:chi-neq-kappa-subscript}
In the four-$\kappa_\bullet$ discipline of \S\ref{sec:four-kappa-subscripts},
the raw compact odd-dimensional Hodge supertrace is
$\sum_q(-1)^q h^{0,q}(X)=0$.  The older tables below mixed this raw
quantity with BCOV/topological values and Borcherds weights.  The repaired
reading is: $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}=\chi(\cO_X)$ for the compact category,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ for automorphic denominator weights, and
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}$ only for the Heisenberg--Mukai
specialisation.  The structural content is the non-identity
$\chi_{\mathrm{top}}/24\neq\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ or
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}$ in general; it is not a formula for
raw $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ on compact odd CY$_3$.
\end{remark}

The following result resolves a fundamental question about the $d = 3$ modular characteristic.

\begin{proposition}[$\chi_{\mathrm{top}}/24$ is not a universal modular characteristic]
\label{wn:thm:chi-neq-kappa}
The topological Euler characteristic $\chi_{\mathrm{top}}(X)/24$ does
\emph{not} equal the modular characteristic in general.  The table keeps
separate the raw compact Hodge supertrace, the BCOV value, and the
Borcherds/Heisenberg specialisation when these differ:
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
 \toprule
 \textbf{CY variety} & $\chi_{\mathrm{top}}/24$ & raw $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ & \textbf{other modular value} & \textbf{Match?} \\
 \midrule
 Elliptic curve $E$ ($\CY_1$) & $0$ & $0$ & Heisenberg value $1$ & No \\
 K3 surface ($\CY_2$) & $1$ & $2$ & heterotic/BKM value $12$ & No \\
 $K3 \times E$ ($\CY_3$) & $0$ & $0$ & $\{3,5,24\}$ by construction & No \\
 Resolved conifold & $1/12$ & noncompact & $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}=1$ & No \\
 \midrule
 Quintic ($\chi = -200$) & $-25/3$ & $0$ & BCOV value $-25/3$ & BCOV only \\
 $\bP^5[3,3]$ ($\chi = -144$) & $-6$ & $0$ & BCOV value $-6$ & BCOV only \\
 $\bP^5[2,4]$ ($\chi = -176$) & $-22/3$ & $0$ & BCOV value $-22/3$ & BCOV only \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The BCOV value $\chi_{\mathrm{top}}/24$ is a genus-one topological-string
normalisation, not the raw compact Hodge supertrace and not the BKM weight.

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 119 tests in \texttt{cy3\_grand\_atlas.py}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Borcherds weights resolve the K3-fibred discrepancy]
\label{wn:prop:categorical-euler}
The invariant controlling the K3-fibred modular denominator is
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$, not a new categorical Euler characteristic.
For $K3 \times E$, $\chi_{\mathrm{top}}=0$ and
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}=\chi(\cO_{K3\times E})=0$, while the BKM
denominator has $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)=5$.

The Borcherds weight accounts for the full protected BPS denominator,
not just the massless modes that contribute to $\chi_{\mathrm{top}}$.
For K3-fibred CY3, the infinite tower of bound states across fibres is
encoded by the Borcherds product.

Five independent verifications of
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)=5$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
 \item Weight of the Gritsenko--Nikulin character form: $\mathrm{weight}(\Delta_5) = 5$.
 \item DMVV exponent: the Borcherds lift weight formula gives $c(0)/2 = 10/2 = 5$.
 \item Bar Euler product: the genus-$1$ coefficient of $\log Z_{\DT}$ gives $F_1 = 5/24$.
 \item Relative DT: fiber-by-fiber computation via K3 fibers sewed along $E$.
 \item Anomaly cancellation: the worldsheet anomaly for the $K3 \times E$ sigma model.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 78 tests in \texttt{k3e\_relative\_shadow.py}; 119 tests in \texttt{cy3\_grand\_atlas.py}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[$\kappa_\bullet$ is not governed by a single product law]
\label{warn:kappa-not-multiplicative}
The four invariants are computed in different lanes. For K3 fibres in
the relative construction, $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}(K3)=24$ (the Mukai
lattice rank; see Proposition~\ref{prop:k3e-relative-chiral}), while
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3)=\chi(\mathcal O_{K3})=2$ and
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E)=
\chi(\mathcal O_{K3})\chi(\mathcal O_E)=0$ by Kunneth. The Borcherds
weight lane gives
\[
\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)=c_1(0)/2=10/2=5.
\]
The Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation sometimes recorded as $3$ is a
separate $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}$ value; the compact
CY$_3$ Hodge supertrace is instead
$\sum_q(-1)^qh^{0,q}(K3\times E)=0$. No additive identity such as
$5=3+2$ or product identity involving $E$ is a theorem-level formula
here.
\end{remark}

\section{Modularity constraints on $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$}
\label{wn:sec:modularity-constraints}
% ============================================================

\begin{proposition}[Integrality and positivity for BKM]
\label{prop:modularity-constraints}
For a CY3 to admit a genuine Siegel modular form as denominator identity (i.e., a genuine BKM superalgebra), the modular characteristic must satisfy $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \in \Z_{> 0}$ (positive integer weight for a holomorphic Siegel modular form). This rules out several families from naive BKM interpretation:
\begin{itemize}
 \item Quintic: $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = -25/3$ (negative, non-integer).
 \item Banana manifold (Schoen CY3): $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 0$ ($\chi = 0$).
 % NOTE (B5 disambiguation): The old value kappa=-1/6 used chi=-4 from the
 % LOCAL banana curve (h^{1,1}=h^{2,1}=2), not the Schoen CY3 (h^{1,1}=h^{2,1}=19, chi=0).
 % The Schoen CY3 has kappa=0, not -1/6.
\end{itemize}
Only $9$ of the $18$ families in the atlas of Section~\ref{wn:sec:grand-atlas} have integer $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$.

Seven structural constraints for $K3 \times E$ are verified: integrality, positivity, Igusa weight match, Borcherds product convergence, row-sum vanishing of $\phi_{0,1}$, modular transformation law, and Hecke eigenform property.

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 111 tests in \texttt{cy3\_modularity\_constraints.py}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[$\phi_{0,1}$ root/degree map]
\label{rem:phi01-degree-map}
The $\phi_{0,1}$ Fourier coefficients classify BKM roots by degree in the shadow obstruction tower:
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
 \toprule
 \textbf{Root type} & \textbf{Discriminant} & \textbf{Shadow degree} \\
 \midrule
 Real ($c(-1) = 1$) & $D = -1$ & Degree $2$ \\
 Lightlike ($c(0) = 10$) & $D = 0$ & Degree $3$ \\
 Timelike ($c(D)$, signed) & $D > 0$ & Degree $\geq 4$ \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Negative values of $c(D)$ correspond to fermionic roots (odd generators of the BKM superalgebra). The total root multiplicity per BKM level for $K3 \times E$ is $24 = \chi(K3)$.
\end{remark}

\section{The toric CY3 landscape}
\label{sec:toric-landscape}

\subsection{The conifold: wall-crossing as MC gauge equivalence}
\label{subsec:conifold-full}

The resolved conifold $X = \cO(-1) \oplus \cO(-1) \to \bP^1$ has charge lattice $\Gamma = \Z \gamma_1 \oplus \Z \gamma_2$ with $\langle \gamma_1, \gamma_2 \rangle = 1$. The two DT chambers (large-volume and flopped) are connected by the Kontsevich--Soibelman wall-crossing formula.

\begin{theorem}[Conifold bar complex and wall-crossing]
\label{thm:conifold-wc}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\text{conifold}) = 1$. Shadow class~$\mathbf{G}$ (Gaussian, $r_{\max} = 2$).
 \item Wall-crossing is a gauge transformation of the MC element:
 \[
 \exp(\ad_\alpha)(\Theta_I) = \Theta_{II},
 \]
 where $\alpha$ lies in the lattice Lie algebra.
 \item The pentagon identity is confirmed: $E(X)\,E(Y) = E(Y)\,E(XY)\,E(X)$, where $E(\cdot)$ denotes the quantum dilogarithm automorphism.
 \item The bar complexes in the two chambers are quasi-isomorphic:
 \[
 H^*(B(\CoHA_I)) \;\simeq\; H^*(B(\CoHA_{II}))
 \]
 as graded vector spaces, despite having different generators ($\dim B^1 = 2$ in chamber~I vs $\dim B^1 = 3$ in chamber~II). The extra generator in chamber~II is exact (a bound state = bar boundary of a two-particle configuration).
\end{enumerate}

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 124 tests in \texttt{conifold\_bar\_complex.py}; 73 tests in \texttt{wallcrossing\_gauge\_engine.py}.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Local $\bP^2$: the $\Z_3$ McKay quiver}
\label{subsec:local-p2}

\begin{proposition}[Shadow tower of local $\bP^2$]
\label{prop:local-p2}
For the total space $\cO(-3) \to \bP^2$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\text{local }\bP^2) = 3/2 = \chi(\bP^2)/2$.
 \item Shadow class~$\mathbf{M}$ (infinite depth).
 \item Gopakumar--Vafa invariant growth: $|n^0_d| \sim 27^d$ as $d \to \infty$, giving convergence radius $R = 1/27$ for the genus-$0$ prepotential.
 \item The $\Eone$-chiral algebra arises from the critical CoHA of the $\Z_3$ McKay quiver. The quiver has $3$ vertices ($\Z_3$ representations), $9$ arrows, and a potential $W$ from the CY3 condition.
 \item Perturbative $5d$ CS reproduces the CoHA OPE: the deformed $\cW_{1+\infty}$ acquires a loop correction factor $c_{\mathrm{loop}} = -1/15$.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 77 tests in \texttt{local\_p2\_shadow.py}; 104 tests in \texttt{toric\_shadow\_engine.py}.
\end{proposition}

\subsection{Local $\bP^1 \times \bP^1$: two-parameter shadow metric}
\label{subsec:local-p1p1}

\begin{proposition}[Shadow tower of local $\bP^1 \times \bP^1$]
\label{prop:local-p1p1}
For $\cO(-2,-2) \to \bP^1 \times \bP^1$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 2 = h^{1,1}(\bP^1 \times \bP^1)$.
 \item The two-parameter shadow metric is $Q = \mathrm{diag}(1,1)$.
 \item The symmetric direction has shadow class~$\mathbf{M}$ (infinite tower from the infinite BPS spectrum); the antisymmetric direction has class~$\mathbf{G}$.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 104 tests in \texttt{toric\_shadow\_engine.py}.
\end{proposition}

\subsection{Perturbative comparison: $5d$ Chern--Simons}
\label{subsec:5d-cs}

\begin{proposition}[Perturbative $5d$ CS reproduces CoHA OPE]
\label{prop:5d-cs-coha}
The perturbative $5d$ noncommutative Chern--Simons theory (Costello--Li) reproduces the CoHA OPE structure for $\C^3$ and the conifold. Three-path verification:
\[
 \text{Feynman diagrams} \;=\; \text{shuffle algebra} \;=\; \cW_{1+\infty} \text{ OPE}.
\]
For the conifold, the perturbative answer is identical to $\C^3$; the difference is nonperturbative (wall-crossing).

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 87 tests in \texttt{c3\_envelope\_comparison.py}; 94 tests in \texttt{toric\_cy3\_dt\_engine.py}.
\end{proposition}


% ============================================================
\part{The K3 Yangian}
\label{part:IV}
% ============================================================

The K3 Yangian is the $\CY_2$ incarnation of the functor: on Higgs sheaves on a curve (genus filtration), or on the Nakajima quiver variety attached to the $K3$ Mukai lattice, $\Phi_2$ outputs an $\Etwo$-chiral algebra whose representation category carries the Maulik--Okounkov $R$-matrix as its braiding. Part~\ref{part:IV} assembles the $\Etwo$ bar complex in its three operadic incarnations, the grand atlas of CY3 families that feed the K3-Yangian tower, the five routes to the chiral algebra (each exhibiting a different face of the same underlying $\Etwo$-structure), and the cross-volume bridge to the Vol~I / Vol~II formalisms against which the abelian-at-Lie, non-abelian-at-Hopf presentation is verified.

% ============================================================
\section{The $\Etwo$ bar complex}
\label{wn:sec:e2-bar}
% ============================================================

For an $\Etwo$-chiral algebra, three distinct bar constructions are available, reflecting the three levels of operadic symmetry.

\begin{theorem}[Three bar complexes and their comparison]
\label{thm:three-bar-complexes}
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{llll}
 \toprule
 \textbf{Bar complex} & \textbf{Structure} & \textbf{Origin} & \textbf{Carries} \\
 \midrule
 $B_{\Eone}^n(A)$ & Ordered & Hochschild & Tensor product \\
 $B_{\Etwo}^n(A)$ & Braided & $R$-matrix & Braided tensor product \\
 $B_{\Einf}^n(A)$ & Symmetric & Vol~I shadow tower & $S_n$-quotient \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The $\Einf$ bar complex is the $S_n$-quotient of the $\Eone$ bar complex:
\[
 B_{\Einf}^n(A) \;=\; \bigl(B_{\Eone}^n(A)\bigr)^{S_n}.
\]
For $A = H_1$ (Heisenberg at level~$1$):
\[
 \dim B_{\Etwo}^n(H_1) \;=\; d(n) \qquad (\text{divisor function}).
\]
The $\Etwo$ bar complex is strictly between the $\Eone$ and $\Einf$ bar complexes in size, and its Euler characteristics encode the $\Etwo$-braided BPS spectrum.

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 93 tests in \texttt{e2\_bar\_complex.py}; 110 tests in \texttt{e2\_barcobar\_koszul.py}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[Relation to the Vol~I shadow tower]
The Vol~I shadow tower uses the $\Einf$ bar complex (symmetric, no $R$-matrix data). The $\Etwo$ bar complex is the correct refinement for quantum vertex chiral groups: it retains the braiding information lost in the $S_n$-quotient. The passage $B_{\Etwo} \to B_{\Einf}$ (forgetting the braiding) corresponds to the passage from the full quantum group $G(X)$ to its shadow data $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}, C, Q, \ldots$.
\end{remark}

\subsection{BPS black hole entropy from the shadow tower}
\label{subsec:bps-black-hole}

\begin{conjecture}[Shadow tower entropy heuristic]
\label{prop:bps-entropy}
The BPS black hole entropy is expected to admit an expansion organized by
shadow degree in the protected sectors where a modular denominator is
available:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item \emph{Degree~$2$} = \textbf{Bekenstein--Hawking}: in the named protected index setting the leading exponential is Cardy/Bekenstein--Hawking; there is no universal formula $S_{\mathrm{BH}}=\pi\sqrt{2\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}D}$ for arbitrary CY$_3$ shadows.
 \item \emph{Degree~$3$} = \textbf{logarithmic correction}: the coefficient $-27/4$ belongs to the protected $K3\times T^2$/$\Phi_{10}$ asymptotic convention, not to every shadow tower.
 \item \emph{Degree~$\geq 4$} = \textbf{power corrections}: controlled by the quartic shadow and higher, giving Bessel-type corrections $\sim D^{-k/2}$ for $k \geq 1$.
\end{enumerate}
The shadow class controls the qualitative entropy structure:
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
 \toprule
 \textbf{Shadow class} & \textbf{Black hole entropy} \\
 \midrule
 $\mathbf{G}$ & Bekenstein--Hawking only (no quantum corrections beyond genus~$1$) \\
 $\mathbf{L}$ & Bekenstein--Hawking + logarithmic correction \\
 $\mathbf{M}$ & Genuine black holes with infinite tower of quantum corrections \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The passage from Bekenstein--Hawking to the full quantum-corrected entropy is the passage from $\Theta^{\leq 2}$ to $\Theta_A$ in the shadow obstruction tower.
\end{conjecture}

\subsection{Calogero--Moser/Bethe ansatz dictionary}
\label{subsec:calogero-bethe}

\begin{proposition}[Integrable system/shadow tower dictionary]
\label{prop:calogero-bethe}
For the $\cW_N$ chiral algebra, the Calogero--Moser integrals of motion $I_k$ correspond to shadow tower components:
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
 \toprule
 \textbf{Integrable system} & \textbf{Shadow tower} \\
 \midrule
 $I_2$ (quadratic Hamiltonian) & $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ (modular characteristic) \\
 $I_3$ (cubic integral) & $C$ (cubic shadow) \\
 $I_4$ (quartic integral) & $Q$ (quartic resonance class) \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The Bethe ansatz equations for the quantum Calogero--Moser system are the saddle-point equations of the shadow generating function.
\end{proposition}

\subsection{Lattice model finite-size corrections}
\label{subsec:lattice-fsc}

\begin{proposition}[Finite-size corrections from the shadow tower]
\label{prop:lattice-fsc}
Lattice model finite-size corrections on a system of size~$L$ decay at a rate exactly $q = e^{-L/\xi}$, where $\xi$ is the correlation length. The boundary effects encode shadow tower data: the leading correction is proportional to $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}/L^2$, subleading to $C/L^3$. The MacMahon box formula (counting plane partitions in an $a \times b \times c$ box) is controlled by the shadow tower of $\cW_{1+\infty}$.
\end{proposition}

\section{Five routes to the chiral algebra}
\label{sec:five-routes}
% ============================================================

\begin{remark}[Framing: these are Stage-$2$ $(\Sigma_{d-1}, C)$-specialisations]
\label{rem:five-routes-framing}
The routes catalogued below are Stage-$2$ specialisations of the canonical $\Phi^{\mathrm{FA}}_d$ output (\S\ref{sec:two-stage-factorisation}). For $K3 \times E$ the present catalogue lists five of the six known $(\Sigma_2, C)$-orbits; the full orbit tally is six (\S\ref{sec:k3e-six-routes}), the missing sixth being the Schur-level Monster/Niemeier face. These are \emph{different constructions} of $\Eone$-chiral shadows of one Stage-$1$ factorisation algebra $\cF_X \in E_d\text{-}\mathrm{HolFA}(X)$; only one route uses $\Phi_d$ directly (route (a) in~\S\ref{subsec:costello-li-c3} for $\C^3$; route (c) in \S\ref{subsec:five-routes-k3e} for $K3 \times E$, via CoHA). The Maulik--Okounkov, Vafa--Witten, and crystal-melting routes enter through orthogonal algebraic slicings (stable envelope, mock-modular, plane-partition/vertex-operator); the three-tier stratification of \S\ref{sec:three-tiers-rcy} assigns each construction to its tier.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The Costello--Li chain for $\C^3$}
\label{subsec:costello-li-c3}

The Costello--Li programme provides the most explicit route from CY3 geometry to chiral algebra. For $\C^3$, the chain is:
\[
\text{5d NCCS on } \C^3 \;\to\; \CoHA(\C^3)\cong
Y^+(\widehat{\fgl}_1) \;\hookrightarrow\; Y(\widehat{\fgl}_1)
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}_\lambda}\End(\cW_{1+\infty}[\lambda]\text{-vacuum}).
\]
The last arrow is the evaluation image (Remark~\ref{rem:coha-y-w-chain}):
the associativity classes of $Y^+$ (cohomological Hall) and
$\cW_{1+\infty}$ (vertex operator algebra) differ, and the latter is a
representation-theoretic image of the former through the full Yangian on
the vacuum module, not an isomorphism of algebras. Five independent
routes to $\cW_{1+\infty}$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
 \item \emph{Critical CoHA}: Kontsevich--Soibelman $\to$ Schiffmann--Vasserot $\to$ $Y^+(\widehat{\fgl}_1)$.
 \item \emph{Crystal melting}: counting plane partitions $\to$ MacMahon $\to$ vertex operators.
 \item \emph{Shuffle algebra}: explicit generators and relations from the CoHA shuffle product.
 \item \emph{Factorization envelope}: $\mathrm{PV}^*(\C^3) \to$ Lie conformal algebra $\to$ Nishinaka envelope.
 \item \emph{$5d$ Chern--Simons}: Costello--Li perturbative computation reproduces the OPE.
\end{enumerate}
At $N = 1$ (single D-brane), all five produce the Heisenberg VOA $H_1$.

\subsection{Five routes for $K3 \times E$}
\label{subsec:five-routes-k3e}

Five routes to the chiral algebra of $K3 \times E$ have been mapped:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
 \item \emph{Relative DT}: fiber K3 shadow data sewed along $E$ via DMVV.
 \item \emph{Borcherds BKM}: root multiplicities from $\phi_{0,1}$ $\to$ $U(\fn_+(\fg_{\Delta_5}))$.
 \item \emph{Maulik--Okounkov}: stable envelopes on $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(K3 \times E)$ $\to$ Yangian $R$-matrix.
 \item \emph{Vafa--Witten}: partition function on K3 $\to$ mock modular forms $\to$ chiral characters.
 \item \emph{Relative chiral algebra}: direct construction via K3 fibration (Proposition~\ref{prop:k3e-relative-chiral}).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{The $\Eone$ mechanism: Dunn additivity and $\Omega$-background}
\label{subsec:e1-mechanism}

The reduction from $\Etwo$ to $\Eone$ in the presence of the $\Omega$-background has a clean operadic explanation. By Dunn additivity:
\[
 \Etwo \;\simeq\; \Eone \otimes_{\mathsf{E}_0} \Eone.
\]
The $\Omega$-background freezes one of the two $\Eone$-factors (it introduces a preferred direction in the plane), reducing the native $\Etwo$ to $\Eone$. The Drinfeld center passage (Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:c3-drinfeld-center}) restores the $\Etwo$ structure by recovering the frozen factor.

This explains why the CoHA is only $\Eone$: it is the $\Omega$-deformed theory, with one $\Eone$-factor frozen. The $\Etwo$-braided structure lives on $\cZ(\Rep^{\Eone}(A_X))$ (the Drinfeld center of the representation category), which unfreezes the second $\Eone$-factor. The algebra $A_X$ itself remains $\Eone$ at $d = 3$.

\subsection{Shadow tower identification}
\label{wn:subsec:cross-vol-shadow}

The shadow obstruction tower $\Theta_A$ of Vol~I (Theorems~A--D, the bar-intrinsic construction $\Theta_A := D_A - d_0$) specializes as follows for CY3 chiral algebras:

\subsection{Swiss-cheese and the $\Etwo$ bar complex}
\label{wn:subsec:cross-vol-sc}

The Vol~II Swiss-cheese structure $\mathrm{SC}^{\mathrm{ch,top}}$ (Theorem~H) provides the operadic framework for the $\Etwo$ bar complex of Section~\ref{wn:sec:e2-bar}. The three bar complexes $(B_{\Eone}, B_{\Etwo}, B_{\Einf})$ correspond to the three sectors:
\begin{itemize}
 \item $B_{\Eone}$: the open sector (Hochschild, ordered tensors).
 \item $B_{\Etwo}$: the boundary sector (braided, with $R$-matrix data).
 \item $B_{\Einf}$: the closed sector (symmetric, Vol~I shadow tower).
\end{itemize}
The $\Eone \to \Etwo$ passage via Drinfeld center (Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:c3-drinfeld-center}) corresponds to the open-to-bulk passage in Vol~II via the chiral derived center $\cZ^{\mathrm{der}}_{\mathrm{ch}}(A)$.

\subsection{The completed modular Koszul datum for CY3}
\label{wn:subsec:cross-vol-mkd}

The eight-fold completed modular Koszul datum $\Pi^{\mathrm{oc}}_X(A)$ of Vol~I specializes to the CY3 setting as:
\[
 \Pi^{\mathrm{oc}}_{X}(A_{X_3}) = \bigl(\cF_X(A), \overline{B}_X(A), \Theta_A, L_A, (V^{\mathrm{br}}, T^{\mathrm{br}}), R^{\mathrm{mod}}_4, \cZ^{\mathrm{der}}_{\mathrm{ch}}(A), \Tr_A\bigr),
\]
where the BKM root system supplies the root lattice structure and the Borcherds denominator formula controls the bar Euler product.

\noindent\textit{Verification}: 124 tests in \texttt{cross\_volume\_shadow\_bridge.py}.

\subsection{Remaining gaps}
\label{subsec:remaining-gaps}

\begin{enumerate}
 \item \textbf{CY-A for compact CY3}: the $\bS^3$-framing is topologically trivializable, but the chain-level construction of the trivialization remains open.
 \item \textbf{$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ formula for K3-fibered CY3}: the formula $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = \chi^{\CY}$ is verified for $K3 \times E$ and Enriques~$\times E$ but is conjectural beyond these.
 \item \textbf{Non-BKM families}: CY3 with non-integer $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ do not admit naive BKM interpretations.
 \item \textbf{Full motivic DT}: the shadow tower $=$ BKM roots identification is at the level of generating series; the motivic upgrade remains open.
 \item \textbf{Toric chart gluing} (advanced): the conjecture that quiver-chart atlases reconstruct $D^b(X)$ has been \emph{upgraded to a theorem} (Theorem~\ref{thm:toric-chart-gluing}) for toric CY$_3$ via $A_\infty$-bimodule transition data. The compact case remains open (see Q1 in \S\ref{subsec:open-questions}).
 \item \textbf{Shadow--BPS/DT correspondence}: Conjecture~\ref{conj:shadow-bps-dt} (shadow tower coefficients $=$ BPS/DT invariants) verified for $\C^3$ and $K3 \times E$; general statement remains conjectural. New conjecture \ref{conj:ddca-toroidal-bridge} relates double current algebras to toroidal algebras via the $K3 \times E$ bridge.
 \item \textbf{Critical-level exclusion}: Vol~I Theorem~H (polynomial Hilbert series of $\ChirHoch^*$, concentrated in $\{0,1,2\}$) does NOT apply at the critical level $k = -h^\vee$. For $\widehat{\fsl}_2$ at critical level, $\ChirHoch^*$ is unbounded ($4$-periodic). All $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ computations in this volume use generic level; critical-level CY examples (if any) require separate analysis.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Updated open questions}
\label{sec:updated-open}
% ============================================================

The original open questions (Section~\ref{sec:open-questions}) are updated in light of the new results:

\begin{enumerate}
 \item \textbf{Root datum of the quintic}: still open. $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = -25/3$ is non-integer and negative (Proposition~\ref{prop:modularity-constraints}).
 \item \textbf{$\bS^3$-framing construction}: \emph{partially resolved}: topological obstruction vanishes universally (Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:s3-framing-vanishes}); chain-level via holomorphic CS is the remaining step.
 \item \textbf{Automorphic form for Hitchin/$E_8$}: still open.
 \item \textbf{Wall-crossing as MC gauge equivalence}: \emph{verified for the conifold} (Theorem~\ref{thm:conifold-wc}).
 \item \textbf{Is $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = h^{1,1}/4$ universal?}: \emph{No} --- the correct invariant is $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = \mathrm{wt}(\text{denominator form})$, not a function of Hodge numbers alone.
 \item \textbf{Shadow depth for quantum vertex chiral groups}: \emph{characterized} (Observation~\ref{obs:atlas-patterns}).
 \item \textbf{$\Etwo$ bar complex}: \emph{constructed and computed} (Theorem~\ref{thm:three-bar-complexes}).
 \item \textbf{$\chi_{\mathrm{top}}/24 \neq \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$}: \emph{resolved} (Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:chi-neq-kappa}).
 \item \textbf{Quantum geometric Langlands as $\Etwo$-chiral Koszul duality}: still open.
 \item \textbf{Eight diagonal divisor Siegel modular forms}: still open.
 \item \textbf{Toric chart gluing}: \emph{promoted to theorem} (Theorem~\ref{thm:toric-chart-gluing}). The quiver-chart atlas reconstruction of $D^b(X)$ for toric CY$_3$ is proved via $A_\infty$-bimodule transition data. Compact CY$_3$ remains open.
 \item \textbf{$K3 \times E$ double current algebra}: Definition~\ref{def:k3-double-current-algebra} constructs the chiral algebra; Conjecture~\ref{conj:ddca-toroidal-bridge} relates it to the toroidal algebra $\mathcal{T}(\widehat{\fgl}_1)$.
 \item \textbf{Shadow--BPS/DT correspondence}: Conjecture~\ref{conj:shadow-bps-dt} formulated; verified for $\C^3$ (shadow $= 3$D partitions) and $K3 \times E$ (shadow $=$ BKM roots). General compact case open.
 \item \textbf{Kernel of averaging}: $\dim\ker(\mathrm{av}_n) = n! - \binom{n+d-1}{n}$ established (Vol~I, Proposition~\ref*{V1-prop:ker-av-schur-weyl}). Implications for the $\Eone$-to-$\Etwo$ obstruction in the CY$_3$ setting: the kernel carries Schur--Weyl data invisible to the symmetric bar.
 \item \textbf{Critical-level $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$}: Theorem~H (Vol~I) does NOT apply at $k = -h^\vee$. All $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ computations in this volume implicitly use generic level. CY$_3$ examples at critical level (if any arise via geometric engineering) require separate analysis.
\end{enumerate}

% ============================================================
\part{The Calabi--Yau Landscape}
\label{part:V}
% ============================================================

The quintic, $K3 \times E$, abelian surfaces, and local surfaces
(local $\bP^2$, the conifold) each realise a distinct geometric fibre
of the CY-to-chiral correspondence. Part~\ref{part:V} works through
the landscape: on $K3 \times E$ the total-space/fibre-aware spectrum is
$\{0,3,5,24\}$, with $0=\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E)$, $3$ the
Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}$,
$5=\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)$, and $24$ the K3 fibre-rank; the
K3 fibre Euler value $2$ is recorded separately. The toric CY3
landscape and quiver-chart gluing reveal the CoHA-level structure
$\CoHA(\C^3)=Y^+$; the elliptic curve sits as the universal bridge
between $d=2$ and $d=3$; and the passage from the Heisenberg--Mukai
lane to the BKM lane is the second-quantisation leap. Six routes to
$G(K3 \times E)$ are six different constructions, never six
applications of $\Phi$ to one object.

% ============================================================
\section{The $d = 3$ CY-to-chiral functor: April 2026 frontier}
\label{sec:cy3-frontier-april2026}
% ============================================================

This section records the results, insights, open questions, and frontier observations from the
intensive April 2026 computational campaign on the $d = 3$ CY-to-chiral functor and the
quiver-chart gluing programme. The compute layer grew from $5{,}114$ to $11{,}658$ tests
across $\sim\! 75$ new engines ($\sim\!120{,}000$ lines). Three theorem-level results were
proved; seven false ideas were dismissed by the Beilinson audit swarm.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{The $\Eone$ universality theorem: what is proved and what is not}
\label{subsec:e1-universality-scope}
% ------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item \textbf{Proved (toric CY$_3$).} For any toric CY$_3$ $X$ with $T^3$-equivariant $\Omega$-deformation
 ($\sigma_3 = h_1 h_2 h_3 \neq 0$, $h_1 + h_2 + h_3 = 0$), the chiral algebra $A_X$ is natively $\Eone$.
 Four independent pillars: abelianity of the classical SN bracket on $\mathrm{PV}^*(\C^3)^{\mathrm{GL}(3)}$,
 one-dimensionality of $\HH^2$ in the equivariant sector, incompatibility of the holomorphic CS
 BV trivialization with $\Etwo$-equivariance, and the $R$-matrix requiring the full Drinfeld double.
 Verified across $\C^3$, resolved conifold, local $\bP^2$, local $\bP^1 \times \bP^1$.

\item \textbf{Not proved (compact CY$_3$).} For compact CY$_3$ (quintic, $K3 \times E$), all four pillars
 have gaps. Pillar~(a): the SN bracket is \emph{not} abelian (complex structure deformations
 provide genuine noncommutativity). Pillar~(b): $\HH^2(\mathrm{quintic}) = 102$, not $1$.
 Pillar~(c): the $U(1)$-rotation argument requires a preferred $\R$-direction that compact CY$_3$
 do not naturally provide. Pillar~(d): the structure function $g(z)$ is specific to the torus-equivariant setting.

\item \textbf{The $\Eone$ nature is expected for all CY$_3$.} The topological $\bS^3$-framing obstruction
 vanishes universally ($\pi_3(B\Sp(2m)) = 0$). The chain-level argument via holomorphic CS is
 available for all CY$_3$ with a holomorphic volume form, but its $\Eone$ (not $\Etwo$) nature
 for compact CY$_3$ requires a new argument, possibly through the quiver-chart gluing programme.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{False idea dismissed.} The original statement ``for any smooth CY$_3$\ldots''
was narrowed to ``for any toric CY$_3$\ldots'' on 2026-04-05. The compact case is conjectural.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Seven false ideas dismissed by the Beilinson audit}
\label{subsec:false-ideas-dismissed}
% ------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{F\arabic*.}]
\item \textbf{$g(z)\,g(-z) = 1$ iff CY.} False biconditional. The product
 $g(z)\,g(-z) = \prod_i (h_i^2 - z^2)/(h_i^2 - z^2) = 1$ is an algebraic \emph{identity}
 for all $h_i$. The CY condition $h_1 + h_2 + h_3 = 0$ controls the asymptotics
 $g(z) \to 1$ as $z \to \infty$, not the unitarity identity. Corrected in the manuscript.

\item \textbf{$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathrm{K3}) = 2$.} The value $2 = \chi(\cO_{K3})$ (arithmetic genus) appeared
 in the $\chi_{\mathrm{top}}/24 \neq \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ table. The compute engines give $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 12 = \chi_{\mathrm{top}}/2$
 from the CY$_2$ categorical formula. Corrected to $12$.

\item \textbf{Smooth CY$_3$ is $\Etwo$-chiral.} The smooth/singular table classified smooth CY$_3$
 as ``$\Etwo$-chiral.'' This contradicts the $\Eone$ universality theorem. Corrected to
 ``$\Eone$-chiral ($\Etwo$ via Drinfeld center).''

\item \textbf{$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathrm{conifold})$ is unique.} Three compute engines give three values: $0$
 (from $\chi_{\mathrm{top}} = 0$, confusing deformed and resolved), $1$ (from the Mayer--Vietoris nerve
 formula with wall $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 1$), and $2$ (from Mayer--Vietoris with wall $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 0$). The
 \emph{correct} value $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 1$ is supported by: the MacMahon genus-$1$ extraction $F_1 = 1/24$,
 the single BPS state contributing at genus~$1$, and the formula $\chi_{\mathrm{top}}(\bP^1)/2 = 1$.
 The other engines have violations (hardcoded wrong expected values).
 \textbf{Open: resolve the factor-of-$2$ ambiguity in the wall $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ for the nerve formula.}

\item \textbf{Geometric Langlands = $\Eone$ Koszul duality (as theorem).} Presented as ``THESIS'' and
 ``MAIN THEOREM'' in the compute engine, but the engine only verifies standard properties of
 affine KM algebras at the critical level (FF duality, self-duality of $\mathrm{GL}(N)$, Yang--Baxter).
 None of these constitute a proof of the geometric Langlands correspondence.
 Re-labelled as conjectural.

\item \textbf{$F_g^{\mathrm{BCOV}} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \lambda_g^{\mathrm{FP}}$ for compact CY$_3$ at $g \geq 2$.}
 The deepest false idea found by the audit. The BCOV constant-map formula is
 $F_g^{\mathrm{CM}} = (-1)^{g-1} \chi \cdot B_{2g} \cdot B_{2g-2} / (2g(2g-2)(2g-2)!)$,
 which contains a \emph{product} $B_{2g} \cdot B_{2g-2}$ of two consecutive Bernoulli numbers.
 The shadow formula $F_g^{\mathrm{sh}} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \lambda_g^{\mathrm{FP}}$ contains $B_{2g}$
 alone. Since $B_{2g-2}/B_{2g}$ varies with $g$, no single $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ makes the two formulas agree
 at all genera. For the quintic: the effective $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ matching $F_g^{\mathrm{CM}}$ oscillates
 ($200, -28.6, -4.3, 2.8, -3.8$ for $g = 1, \ldots, 5$).

 The identification BCOV $=$ shadow is TRUE at the structural/categorical level: the holomorphic
 anomaly equation IS the genus spectral sequence of an MC equation in the Costello--Li dgLa
 (Costello 2007, Costello--Li 2016). But the naive quantitative instantiation
 $F_g = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \lambda_g^{\mathrm{FP}}$ is FALSE for compact CY$_3$ at $g \geq 2$. The
 shadow formula works for the \emph{uniform-weight lane} (where all generators have the same
 conformal weight), which covers free fields and toric CY$_3$ but NOT compact CY$_3$ with
 worldsheet instantons. The compact case requires the FULL shadow obstruction tower $\Theta_A$
 (not just the scalar projection $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$), and the higher-degree shadows encode the instanton
 corrections.

\item \textbf{The $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ symbol means $\geq 4$ different things across engines.} For the
 quintic alone: $\chi/24 = -25/3$ (BCOV anomaly coefficient), $\chi/2 = -100$ (MacMahon exponent),
 $-\chi = 200$ (mirror engine), and $5$ (BKM weight, for $K3 \times E$). For K3: at least $8$
 values appear ($1, 2, 3, 5, 12, 22, 24$) from different formulas all called ``$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$.'' This is (same name, different object) at industrial scale. Resolution: define $\kappa_{\mathrm{BCOV}}$,
 $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ as distinct named invariants and state which one
 is meant in each context.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{The quiver-chart gluing programme: summary of results}
\label{subsec:qcg-summary}
% ------------------------------------------------------------

The quiver-chart gluing construction was developed in full across $24$ agents producing
$\sim\!20$ new compute engines and $\sim\!3{,}000$ tests. The architecture:

\[
 \underbrace{\Rep(Q_\alpha, W_\alpha)}_{\text{local chart}}
 \;\xrightarrow{\;\CoHA\;}\;
 \underbrace{\cH(Q_\alpha, W_\alpha)}_{\text{local $\Eone$ algebra}}
 \;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{hocolim}\;}\;
 \underbrace{A_\cC = \operatorname{hocolim}_I \cH_\alpha}_{\text{global $\Eone$ algebra}}
\]

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lccl}
 \toprule
 \textbf{CY$_3$} & Charts & $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ & Status \\
 \midrule
 $\C^3$ & $1$ & $1$ & Verified (single chart, no gluing) \\
 Resolved conifold & $2$ & $1$ & Verified (pentagon identity, $2$-chart hocolim) \\
 Local $\bP^2$ & $3$ & $3/2$ & Verified (hexagon, $\Z_3$ symmetry, triple overlap) \\

\noindent Key theorems proved:
\begin{itemize}
\item $B^{\Eone}(\operatorname{hocolim}_I D) \simeq \operatorname{hocolim}_I B^{\Eone}(D)$
 (bar-hocolim commutation, from Quillen adjunction).
\item $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A_\cC)$ is atlas-independent (from bar-hocolim + homotopy invariance of $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$).
\item $\Eone$ descent is unobstructed: $\mathrm{Map}_{\Eone}(A, B)$ has contractible components,
 so all higher coherences vanish. This is the formal reason $d = 3$ gives $\Eone$: the
 gluing data for CY$_3$ is $1$-categorical.
\item KS wall-crossing $=$ hocolim transition $=$ $\Eone$ MC gauge transformation (three-way equivalence,
 verified for conifold via quantum torus pentagon).
\item Flop $=$ $\Eone$ Koszul duality at the chart level (conifold: flop exchanges charts,
 $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} + \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^! = 0$ for the conifold, which is free-field type; the complementarity sum is family-dependent: $0$ for KM/free, $13$ for Virasoro, etc.).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The $\En$ stabilization tower: $d \geq 4$}
\label{subsec:en-stabilization}
% ------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{remark}[Two orthogonal data: PTVV shift vs framing obstruction]
\label{rem:two-data-en-tower}
The PTVV shift law (Proposition~\ref{prop:ptvv-shift-law}) and the $\bS^d$-framing obstruction of this subsection are two independent data on the Stage-$1$ $E_d$-holomorphic factorisation algebra of a $d$-Calabi--Yau category. The former records the cotangent-complex degree $\mathrm{shift} = d - 4$ on the moduli of perfect objects, determining the classical operadic level $E_n^{\mathrm{cl}}$ of the Stage-$1$ output; the latter records $\pi_d(B\Sp(2m))$, governing chain-level trivialisability of the hCS BV action. On compact CY$_3$ the framing class in $\pi_3(B\Sp) = 0$ vanishes by Bott, so no obstruction from the second datum; the Stage-$1$ output sits at the $(3, -1, \Eone)$-row of the shift law. At $d = 5$ the shift is $+1$ (Poisson rather than symplectic) while the framing class is $\Z_2$; the two data combine but do not conflict. At $d = 4$ the framing class is $\Z$ (from $\pi_4(B\Sp) = \Z$) while the shift is $0$ ($E_0$-classical); Fake Monster at $d = 5$ is forced by $\pi_5(B\Sp) = \Z_2$ in addition to the $E_5$-Poisson row, not by either alone.
\end{remark}

The framing obstruction at CY dimension $d$ is controlled by the relevant
classifying space: $BU$ for $d \leq 2$ (complex/symplectic framing), $B\Sp$
for $d \geq 3$ ($\bS^d$-framing). The obstruction group and chiral structure
follow an $8$-fold Bott pattern for $d \geq 3$:

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{cclll}
 \toprule
 $d$ & Framing obstruction & Source & Structure & Example \\
 \midrule
 $1$ & $0$ & $\pi_1(BU) = 0$ & $\Einf$ & Elliptic curve \\
 $2$ & $\Z$ & $\pi_2(BU) = \Z$ & $\Etwo$ & K3 \\
 $3$ & $0$ & $\pi_3(B\Sp) = 0$ & $\Eone$ & CY$_3$ \\
 $4$ & $\Z$ & $\pi_4(B\Sp) = \Z$ & $\Eone + \Z$-shifted & CY$_4$: K3$\times$K3 \\
 $5$ & $\Z_2$ & $\pi_5(B\Sp) = \Z_2$ & $\Eone + \Z_2$-graded & CY$_5$ \\
 $6$ & $\Z_2$ & $\pi_6(B\Sp) = \Z_2$ & $\Eone + \Z_2$-graded & CY$_6$ \\
 $7$ & $0$ & $\pi_7(B\Sp) = 0$ & $\Eone$ & CY$_7$ \\
 $8$ & $\Z$ & $\pi_8(B\Sp) = \Z$ & $\Eone + \Z$-shifted & CY$_8$ \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent For $d \geq 3$: the chiral algebra is always $\Eone$, with additional shifted structure from
$\pi_d(B\Sp)$. Proved in $141$ tests (\texttt{higher\_cy\_en\_tower.py}).

\subsection{Open questions and frontier observations}
\label{subsec:open-questions}
% ------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{Q\arabic*.}]
\item \textbf{$\Eone$ universality for compact CY$_3$.} What replaces the four toric pillars?
 The global geometry provides noncommutativity (nontrivial SN bracket), so the abelianity argument
 fails. \emph{Hint}: the quiver-chart gluing may provide the answer: each local chart IS toric
 (by the Bridgeland-stability-to-McKay-quiver construction), and the gluing is $\Eone$ because
 $\Eone$ descent is unobstructed. The global $\Eone$ nature would then follow from the local toric
 $\Eone$ nature plus the unobstructed descent, without needing a global toric structure.

\item \textbf{$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ formula for general CY$_3$.} There is no universal formula $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = f(\chi, h^{p,q})$.
 For toric: $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = \chi_{\mathrm{top}}(\text{compact base})/2$. For compact CICY with $h^{1,0} = 0$: $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = \chi/24$.
 For K3-fibered: $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = \mathrm{wt}(\Delta_5) = 5$ (Borcherds weight; $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}} = 3$ in the Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation, while the compact Hodge supertrace is $\Xi=0$). What is the categorical definition?
 \emph{Hint}: $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = \chi^{\CY}(\cC)$, the categorical CY Euler characteristic, which is a
 derived invariant. Compute this from the Hochschild homology with the CY pairing.

\item \textbf{The factor-of-$2$ ambiguity.} For local $\bP^2$: $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 3/2 = \chi(\bP^2)/2$
 or $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 3 = \chi(\bP^2)$? The majority of engines give $3/2$. Resolve by computing
 $F_1$ from the DT genus-$1$ free energy of $K_{\bP^2}$ and extracting $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 24 F_1$.

\item \textbf{The quintic at the Gepner point.} The Gepner chart $\MF(W_{\mathrm{Fermat}})$ is NOT a
 quiver category. Is there a generalization of the quiver-chart atlas that includes MF charts?
 \emph{Observation}: MF categories are still $\Eone$ (the tensor product of matrix factorizations is
 associative), so the descent argument applies. The issue is the finiteness of the chart cover,
 not the $\Eone$ nature.

\item \textbf{The conifold $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ discrepancy.} Three engines give $0$, $1$, $2$. Resolve by
 direct genus-$1$ DT computation on the resolved conifold. The value $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 1$ is most
 defensible (MacMahon extraction, single BPS contribution, $\chi(\bP^1)/2$).

\item \textbf{Crystal melting versus BTZ microstates.} For $\C^3$: the shadow PF $= M(q)$ (MacMahon),
 and $M(q)$ counts $3$D partitions. The BTZ entropy from $\C^3$ scales as $n^{2/3}$ (not $n^{1/2}$
 as for standard $2$d CFT). Is this a genuine gravitational observable, or a formal identification?
 \emph{Observation}: the $n^{2/3}$ growth rate distinguishes CY$_3$ crystal melting from the
 Cardy regime, suggesting a \emph{different universality class} of quantum gravity.

\item \textbf{BCH vs quantum torus.} The pentagon identity holds \emph{exactly} in the quantum torus
 but \emph{fails} under finite-depth BCH in the pro-nilpotent Lie algebra. This is the relevant obstruction:
 the wall-crossing identity is a group-level statement, not a Lie algebra statement. Future
 engines should work in the quantum torus directly, not through BCH.

\item \textbf{The holographic modular Koszul datum for CY$_3$.} The six-component datum
 $H(\C^3) = (\cW_{1+\infty}, \cW^!_{1+\infty}, \Rep(Y(\widehat{\fgl}_1)), r_{\mathrm{Yang}}(z),
 \Theta^{\Eone}, \nabla^{\Eone})$ is fully computed for $\C^3$. Three of six components
 ($C_X$, $\Theta^{\Eone}$ beyond degree~$2$, $\nabla^{\Eone}$ away from self-dual point) are
 only partially realized. Complete the datum for the conifold and local $\bP^2$.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Idiosyncrasies and computational discoveries}
\label{subsec:idiosyncrasies}
% ------------------------------------------------------------

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The $\Z_3$ symmetry of the local $\bP^2$ atlas produces a $\Z_3$-eigendecomposition of the
 global algebra into charge sectors $A_0, A_1, A_2$. The cubic shadow $C = -3$ comes entirely
 from the triple overlap.

\item The Fermat quintic at the Gepner point has orbifold-invariant Jacobian ring of dimension
 $204 = b_3(Q) = (4^5 - 4)/5$, matching the quintic Hodge diamond $\{1, 101, 101, 1\}$ exactly.
 This is a purely combinatorial identity verified by Burnside's lemma.

\item The exchange graph of the $A_2$ quiver has only $2$ vertices (exchange matrix equivalence
 classes $B$ and $-B$), not $5$ (labeled seeds). The five cluster variables come from tracking
 labels, not from the abstract exchange graph.

\item For $K3 \times E$: $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ is NOT additive under
the naive fibre-plus-base decomposition. The categorical value is
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3)=\chi(\mathcal O_{K3})=2$ and
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E)=0$, while
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\fg_{\Delta_5})=\mathrm{wt}(\Delta_5)=5$.
The Heisenberg--Mukai value $3$ and the K3 fibre-rank $24$ belong to
separate lanes; no additive repair is used.

\item The holomorphic CS trivialization transforms with weight~$1$ under $U(1)$-rotation of the
 transverse plane. This breaks $\Etwo \to \Eone$ at the chain level. But $g(z)\,g(-z) = 1$
 is an algebraic identity for ALL parameters, not just CY ones.

\item The Costello--Li construction is the large-volume limit of the hocolim: at large K\"ahler
 moduli, all stability chambers merge, the atlas reduces to one chart, and the hocolim trivializes
 to the factorization envelope. The hocolim construction handles singularities (conifold)
 automatically via multi-chart gluing.
\end{enumerate}
