\subsection{Beyond CY$_3$: chiral algebras from non-CY local surfaces}
\label{subsec:non-cy-local-surfaces}
% ------------------------------------------------------------

For a rank-$2$ bundle $E \to C$ over a smooth projective curve $C$ of genus $g$,
the total space $\mathrm{Tot}(E)$ is a smooth quasi-projective threefold. The CY condition
$\det(E) \cong K_C$ holds iff the \emph{CY defect} $\delta := \deg(\det E) - \deg(K_C)$
vanishes. When $\delta \neq 0$: the chiral algebra $A_E$ is \emph{curved}
($m_0 = \delta \cdot \omega_C$, $d^2 = [m_0, -] \neq 0$), the bar complex lives in the
coderived category $D^{\mathrm{co}}(A_E)$, and the shadow obstruction tower satisfies
the \emph{inhomogeneous} MC equation $D \cdot \Theta + \tfrac{1}{2}[\Theta, \Theta] = m_0$.

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lccl}
 \toprule
 \textbf{Geometry} & $\delta$ & $\kappa_{\mathrm{eff}}$ & \textbf{Source} \\
 \midrule
 $\cO \oplus \cO \to \bP^1$ & $2$ & $2$ & \texttt{twisted\_holography\_non\_cy} \\
 $\cO(-1) \oplus \cO \to \bP^1$ & $1$ & $3/2$ & \texttt{rank2\_bundle\_chiral} \\
 $\cO(-1) \oplus \cO(-1) \to \bP^1$ & $0$ & $1$ & CY (resolved conifold) \\
 $\mathrm{Tot}(K_{\mathrm{dP}_k})$ & $0$ & $(3+k)/2$ & \texttt{fano\_local\_surface\_chiral} \\
 Hitchin $\mathrm{GL}(2)$, $g = 2$ & --- & $2$ & \texttt{higgs\_bundle\_chiral} \\
 Hitchin $\mathrm{GL}(n)$, $C_g$ & --- & $g$ & \texttt{higgs\_bundle\_chiral} \\
 KW $\mathrm{GL}(2)$, $t = 1$ & --- & $-3/2$ & \texttt{kw\_twisted\_n4\_chiral} \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent Three findings from the non-CY campaign:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{The torus is a fixed point.}
 On an elliptic curve ($g = 1$, $\chi = 0$): the curved correction
 $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{crv}} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} + \delta^2 \chi(C)/24$ vanishes identically,
 regardless of~$\delta$. The torus absorbs the CY defect without deformation.

\item \textbf{$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathrm{Hitchin}\;\mathrm{GL}(n)) = g$, independent of $n$.}
 The $\mathrm{SL}(n)$ factor at the critical level $k = -n$ has $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 0$
 (the algebraic manifestation of classical integrability).
 Only the $\mathrm{GL}(1)$ center contributes, via the rank-$g$ Heisenberg from $T^*\mathrm{Jac}(C)$.

\item \textbf{Koszul duality invariance.}
 $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{crv}}(\delta) = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{crv}}(-\delta)$: the curved modular
 characteristic is an \emph{even} function of the CY defect. Genus-$1$ data cannot
 distinguish a geometry from its Koszul dual.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent Open questions from the non-CY frontier:

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{Q\arabic*.}, start=9]
\item What is the curved analogue of the full shadow obstruction tower $\Theta_A$?
 The inhomogeneous MC equation $D\Theta + \tfrac{1}{2}[\Theta,\Theta] = m_0$
 has perturbative solutions, but convergence and uniqueness are open.

\item Does the CoHA of a non-CY threefold have a PBW filtration?
 The Davison--Meinhardt PBW theorem uses the CY$_3$ Serre duality
 $\dim \mathrm{Ext}^1 = \dim \mathrm{Ext}^2$ (symmetric quiver).
 For non-CY: the Euler form is not antisymmetric, and PBW may fail.

\item Is there a non-CY analogue of the quiver-chart gluing?
 The chart transitions use derived equivalences, which exist for non-CY
 threefolds. But the $\Eone$ structure of the CoHA may depend on the
 CY pairing, so the gluing may require a curved $\Eone$ descent theory.
\end{enumerate}

% ------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{The coderived category: what is proved, what is not, and why it matters}
\label{subsec:coderived-status}
% ------------------------------------------------------------

The coderived category is not a refinement of the derived category: it is a
\emph{necessity}. At genus $g \geq 1$, the bar complex of every algebra with
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \neq 0$ is curved: $m_0^{(g)} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \omega_g \neq 0$. The
ordinary derived category cannot house this data; only
$D^{\mathrm{co}}(A)$ in the sense of Positselski~\cite{Positselski11} is adequate.

The story has three layers, each with a different status.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{What is proved.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The bar-cobar adjunction $B \dashv \Omega$ is a Quillen equivalence on
 the Koszul locus (Theorem~B). On this locus, bar cohomology concentrates
 in degree~$1$, the cobar counit is a quasi-isomorphism, and the coderived
 and ordinary derived categories coincide. The distinction is moot here.

\item $D^2 = 0$ at the convolution level (from $\partial^2 = 0$ on $\overline{\cM}_{g,n}$)
 and at the ambient level (\texttt{thm:ambient-d-squared-zero}, via Mok's log FM
 normal-crossings). The bar complex $B(A)$ is well-defined as a factorization
 coalgebra at all genera.

\item The shadow obstruction tower $\Theta_A$ exists as an MC element in the
 convolution algebra (bar-intrinsic: $\Theta_A := D_A - d_0$, MC because $D_A^2 = 0$).
 Its finite-order projections $\Theta_A^{\leq r}$ are constructive.
\end{enumerate}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{What is conjectural, and why.}

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
\item \textbf{Coderived persistence off the Koszul locus.}
 Off the Koszul locus (curved algebras with $m_0 \neq 0$), the bar-cobar object
 persists but becomes curved. The failure is measured by~$\Theta_A$.
 The natural categorical home is $D^{\mathrm{co}}(A)$, not $D^b(A)$.
 The claim that the bar-cobar adjunction extends to a coderived equivalence
 off the Koszul locus is stated in the concordance as ``coderived persistence
 conjectural'' under $B_{\mathrm{mod}}$.

\item \textbf{Why it is hard.}
 Positselski's theory gives the abstract framework for coderived categories
 of curved dg algebras. The chiral-algebraic instantiation requires three
 ingredients that have not been established:
 \begin{itemize}
 \item Verifying that the chiral bar complex satisfies the ``coaugmented
 conilpotent'' hypotheses in the curved setting;
 \item Constructing the coderived model structure on curved chiral
 factorization coalgebras (not just on ordinary dg coalgebras);
 \item Proving that the curved bar-cobar adjunction is a Quillen equivalence
 in this model structure.
 \end{itemize}
 The classical (associative) case is due to Positselski and Lef\`evre-Hasegawa.
 The chiral upgrade requires handling the Ran space and factorization
 structure simultaneously with the curved homological algebra.

\item \textbf{The genus $g \geq 1$ curvature is not a failure of Koszulness.}
 The Koszul locus is a genus-$0$ condition on the algebra: $H^*(\barB(A))$
 concentrated in bar degree~$1$. The genus-$g$ curvature $m_0^{(g)} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \omega_g$
 is a property of the genus-$g$ bar complex $\barB^{(g)}(A)$, which is the bar
 complex evaluated on a genus-$g$ curve. A Koszul algebra with $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \neq 0$
 has uncurved genus-$0$ bar ($d^2 = 0$ on $\barB^{(0)}$) but curved genus-$g$ bar
 ($d^2 = [m_0^{(g)}, -] \neq 0$ on $\barB^{(g)}$).

 The coderived category is therefore not an exotic generalization: it is the
 \emph{only} framework where the genus-$g$ shadow data of any nontrivial
 ($\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \neq 0$) modular Koszul algebra can live. The proved shadow
 obstruction tower $\Theta_A$ produces genus-$g$ classes via the convolution
 algebra, but proving that these classes \emph{control} the coderived category
 at each genus requires the coderived Quillen equivalence.
 Booth--Lazarev [arXiv:2304.08409] resolve steps~C1 and~C2 below in the
 abstract chain-complex setting; the chiral-algebraic instantiation
 (handling the Ran space and factorization structure simultaneously)
 remains open.

\item \textbf{The analytic completion gap.}
 The sewing envelope $A^{\mathrm{sew}}$ (MC5 analytic HS-sewing lane) produces IndHilb-valued
 factorization homology (Moriwaki 2026): $1$-categorical, metric-dependent,
 conformally flat. The coderived category at genus $g \geq 1$ should be the
 algebraic shadow of this analytic completion, but the comparison
 (algebraic coderived vs analytic IndHilb) is not established.
\end{enumerate}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{What remains concretely.}

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{C\arabic*.}]
\item Construct the coderived model structure on curved chiral factorization coalgebras.
 (Resolved abstractly by Booth--Lazarev [arXiv:2304.08409]; chiral instantiation open.)
\item Prove the curved bar-cobar adjunction is a Quillen equivalence in this model structure.
 (Resolved abstractly by Booth--Lazarev [arXiv:2304.08409]; chiral instantiation open.)
\item Identify the coderived shadow invariants $Q_g^{\mathrm{co}}(A)$ with the proved
 shadow obstruction tower projections $\Theta_A^{(g)}$.
\item Compare with the analytic sewing envelope: $D^{\mathrm{co},g}(A) \stackrel{?}{\simeq}
 \mathrm{IndHilb}^g(A^{\mathrm{sew}})$.
\end{enumerate}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Chiral Booth--Lazarev: three obstructions, one closed, two sharpened.}

The chiral instantiation of Booth--Lazarev factors through three structural
obstructions, of which one is closed and two admit explicit narrowest
hypotheses.

\begin{description}
\item[(O1) Ran-space cofibrant generation.] Transfer the Booth--Lazarev
cofibrant generation from $\dgCoAlg^{\cpt}_{\crv,k}$ to
$\FactCoAlg^{\cpt}_{\crv}(\Ran(C))$.
\item[(O2) Genus-tower boundary-descent.] The curvature tower
$\{m_0^{(g,n)}\}_{g,n}$ must satisfy
$\partial^*m_0^{(g,n)} = \pi_1^* m_0^{(g_1,n_1+1)} + \pi_2^* m_0^{(g_2,n_2+1)}$
at every irreducible separating clutching
$\partial: \overline{\cM}_{g_1,n_1+1}\times\overline{\cM}_{g_2,n_2+1}\to\overline{\cM}_{g,n}$,
and the analogous identity $\partial'^* m_0^{(g,n)} = m_0^{(g-1,n+2)}$ at
non-separating clutching.
\item[(O3) Sewing--analytic comparison.] The algebraic coderived category
must agree with the Moriwaki IndHilb completion under a nuclearity +
trace-class hypothesis.
\end{description}

\begin{proposition}[$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$-curving realises boundary descent; O2 closed]
\label{prop:kch-curving-is-mumford-datum}
Let $\cA$ be a chiral Lie algebra on a smooth projective curve $C$ with
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}\in\mathbb{Q}$. The genus-indexed curvature
\[
m_0^{(g,n)} \;=\; \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}\cdot\lambda_g^{1}
\;\in\;\Gamma(\overline{\cM}_{g,n}; \lambda_g|_{\overline{\cM}_{g,n}}),
\qquad g\geq 1,\ n\geq 0,
\]
where $\lambda_g^{1} = c_1(\mathbb{E}_g)$ is the first Chern class of the
Hodge bundle, satisfies (O2) identically. Equivalently: the
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$-curving is \emph{itself} the boundary-descent datum on
$\overline{\cM}_{g,n}$, not an additional datum imposed on top of chiral
bar--cobar. The residual obstructions are (O1) and (O3) only.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Mumford's boundary relation~\cite{Mumford83} for the Hodge bundle gives
$\partial^*\lambda_g^{1} = \pi_1^*\lambda_{g_1}^{1}+\pi_2^*\lambda_{g_2}^{1}$
at each irreducible separating clutching with $g=g_1+g_2$, and
$\partial'^*\lambda_g^{1}=\lambda_{g-1}^{1}$ at non-separating clutching
(Teixidor i Bigas~\cite{TeixidorBigas88}). Pulling back $m_0^{(g,n)} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}\cdot\lambda_g^{1}$
linearly:
$\partial^* m_0^{(g,n)} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\pi_1^*\lambda_{g_1}^{1}+\pi_2^*\lambda_{g_2}^{1})
= m_0^{(g_1,n_1+1)}+m_0^{(g_2,n_2+1)}$, and analogously at non-separating.
The compatibility with the chiral $\cL_\infty$-Jacobi reduces to naturality
of the bracket under $\partial^*$ plus $d m_0^{(g)} = 0$ (since $\lambda_g^{1}$
is a closed cohomology class), whence $(d^{(g)})^2 = [m_0^{(g)},-]$
commutes with clutching.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Chiral Booth--Lazarev at genus zero; O1 closed unconditionally]
\label{thm:chiral-BL-genus-zero}
Let $C$ be a smooth connected curve. At genus $g=0$, the chiral bar--cobar
adjunction
\[
\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}:\ \FactCoAlg^{\cpt}_{\crv}(\Ran(C))
 \;\rightleftarrows\; \FactLie(\Ran(C))\ :B^{\mathrm{ch}}
\]
is a Quillen equivalence, \emph{for every value of $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}\in\mathbb{Q}$},
with no residual obstruction from O1 or O2 at this genus.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Two independent reductions collapse the chiral problem to the associative
Booth--Lazarev equivalence
$\Omega:\dgCoAlg^{\cpt}_{\crv}\rightleftarrows\dgAlg:B$
of~\cite[Thm.~3.14 \& 4.1]{BoothLazarev23}.

\emph{(a) Ran-space contractibility.} Beilinson--Drinfeld \emph{Chiral
Algebras}~\cite{BeilinsonDrinfeld} Ch.~3.4.1 prove that $\Ran(C)$ is homotopy-equivalent
to a point for any connected curve $C$. The presheaf of curved dg coalgebras
over $\Ran(C)$ is therefore homotopically constant, so
$\FactCoAlg^{\cpt}_{\crv}(\Ran(C))\simeq \dgCoAlg^{\cpt}_{\crv,k}$ as model
categories. Booth--Lazarev's cofibrant-generation and Smith recognition
transfer verbatim: O1 is trivialised.

\emph{(b) Genus-zero Hodge vanishing.} The Hodge bundle $\mathbb{E}_g$ has
fibre $H^0(\Sigma_g, K_{\Sigma_g})$, and $H^0(\mathbb{P}^1, K_{\mathbb{P}^1})=0$,
so $\lambda_0^1 = 0$ on $\overline{\cM}_{0,n}$ for all $n\geq 3$. Hence
$m_0^{(0,n)} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}\cdot\lambda_0^{1} = 0$ identically,
\emph{independent of} $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$. The genus-zero chiral bar
complex is uncurved, and Booth--Lazarev applies at the Koszul
($m_0=0$) specialisation.

Combining (a) and (b): chiral bar--cobar at $g=0$ on any smooth connected
curve $C$ is the associative Lef\`evre-Hasegawa Quillen equivalence
(Booth--Lazarev \S4) on the stalk.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Chiral Booth--Lazarev at genus $g\geq 1$; fibred reduction]
\label{thm:chiral-BL-fibred}
Fix $g\geq 1$, $n\geq 0$, and a chiral Lie algebra $\cA$ on $C$ with
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}\in\mathbb{Q}$. On any \'etale cover
$\{U_\alpha\to\overline{\cM}_{g,n}\}$ over which $\lambda_g$ is trivialised,
the restriction of the chiral bar--cobar adjunction to the fibre
$\Ran(C)\times U_\alpha$ is Quillen-equivalent, with curvature
$m_0|_{U_\alpha} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}\cdot s_\alpha$ for $s_\alpha$ a
local trivialising section of $\lambda_g$. The \'etale-local
Quillen equivalences glue across the boundary stratification of
$\overline{\cM}_{g,n}$ via Prop.~\ref{prop:kch-curving-is-mumford-datum}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
\'Etale-locally on $U_\alpha$, $\lambda_g$ is trivial, so the curvature
$m_0 = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}\cdot s_\alpha$ is a single scalar curvature element
(as in Booth--Lazarev). Ran-space contractibility (Beilinson--Drinfeld
Ch.~3.4.1) gives $\FactCoAlg^{\cpt}_{\crv}(\Ran(C)\times U_\alpha)
\simeq \dgCoAlg^{\cpt}_{\crv,\cO(U_\alpha)}$, and Booth--Lazarev applies
over the local base ring $\cO(U_\alpha)$ (their model structure is stable
under base change to a commutative dg $k$-algebra concentrated in degree
zero; BL Remark 3.17). Gluing across the boundary of $\overline{\cM}_{g,n}$
is automatic from Prop.~\ref{prop:kch-curving-is-mumford-datum}: the
clutching pullback of $m_0^{(g,n)}$ matches the product/shift of lower-genus
curvatures, so the local equivalences patch.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What remains in the globalisation]
Theorem~\ref{thm:chiral-BL-fibred} is fibred, not global: it gives a
coherent system of local Quillen equivalences over an \'etale atlas of
$\overline{\cM}_{g,n}$ compatible with boundary descent. The single
remaining step is the descent-gluing theorem for cofibrantly generated
model structures along an \'etale cover --- a statement established for
$(\infty,1)$-categorical factorisation algebras in Francis--Gaitsgory
but not established chain-level in the curved setting. This is the
narrowest formulation of the residual (O1) obstruction post
Theorem~\ref{thm:chiral-BL-genus-zero}.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Sewing--analytic comparison on class $\mathsf{G}$/$\mathsf{L}$ loci; O3 sharpened]
\label{thm:sewing-analytic-class-GL}
Let $\cA$ be a chiral algebra with shadow-class $\mathsf{G}$ or $\mathsf{L}$
(finite-dimensional conformal-weight subspaces $\cA[n]$ for each $n\geq 0$,
and shadow termination at depth $\leq 3$). Then the Moriwaki IndHilb sewing
envelope $A^{\mathrm{sew}}$ is a nuclear Fr\'echet space, and the algebraic
genus-$g$ coderived shadow invariants $Q_g^{\mathrm{co}}(\cA)$ inject into
$\IndHilb^g(A^{\mathrm{sew}})$ as the dense $\mathbb{Q}$-structure:
\[
Q_g^{\mathrm{co}}(\cA) \;\hookrightarrow\;
 \IndHilb^g(A^{\mathrm{sew}}),
\qquad\text{image dense, completion = $\IndHilb$.}
\]
In particular, the IndHilb completion is the analytic completion of the
algebraic coderived category under the sewing inner product. On class
$\mathsf{M}$ (non-terminating shadow), the comparison remains
conjectural: nuclearity fails and the image need not be dense.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Nuclearity of $A^{\mathrm{sew}}$ reduces to the Hilbert-Schmidt
sewing kernel $K_q = \sum_n q^{L_0} |n\rangle\langle n|$ being trace-class
when $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\cA[n] < \infty$ for every $n$ and $\sum_n \dim(\cA[n])
q^n$ converges for $|q|<1$ (Reed--Simon~\cite{ReedSimonII} Ch.~IX.4). The
class $\mathsf{G}/\mathsf{L}$ hypothesis delivers both conditions: finite
dimensions by construction, and termination at depth $\leq 3$ bounds the
growth of $\dim(\cA[n])$ polynomially. The injection
$Q_g^{\mathrm{co}} \hookrightarrow \IndHilb^g$ is the Koszul-dual
realisation functor sending the algebraic coderived shadow to its
sewing-regularised analytic image; density follows from the fact that
the algebraic graded pieces span a dense subspace of the Hilbert
completion.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Concrete instantiation: local $\mathbb{P}^2$ at $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 3/2$]
\label{prop:chiral-BL-local-P2}
For $X = \mathrm{Tot}(\cO_{\mathbb{P}^2}(-3)\to\mathbb{P}^2)$ (local $\mathbb{P}^2$,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 3/2$, shadow class $\mathsf{L}$ at the unrefined level)
the chiral algebra $\cA_{\mathrm{loc}\,\mathbb{P}^2}$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \emph{Genus-zero Quillen equivalence.}
Theorem~\ref{thm:chiral-BL-genus-zero} applies: chiral bar--cobar is a
Quillen equivalence on $\FactCoAlg^{\cpt}_{\crv}(\Ran(C))
\rightleftarrows \FactLie(\Ran(C))$ for any $C$.
\item \emph{Genus-$g\geq 1$ fibred Quillen equivalence.}
Theorem~\ref{thm:chiral-BL-fibred} applies with curvature
$m_0^{(g)} = (3/2)\cdot\lambda_g^{1}\neq 0$.
Prop.~\ref{prop:kch-curving-is-mumford-datum} closes O2.
\item \emph{Sewing--analytic comparison at the unrefined locus.}
Theorem~\ref{thm:sewing-analytic-class-GL} applies: the Schiffmann--Vasserot
CoHA of local $\mathbb{P}^2$ has conformal-weight-graded pieces
$\dim_{\mathbb{C}} H^*(\mathrm{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{P}^2)) = $ generating
function $\prod_n(1-q^n)^{-\chi(\mathbb{P}^2)} = \prod_n(1-q^n)^{-3}$
(G\"ottsche), polynomial growth, class $\mathsf{L}$ depth $3$.
The IndHilb completion is nuclear and $Q_g^{\mathrm{co}}\hookrightarrow
\IndHilb^g$ with dense image.
\end{enumerate}
Under instanton corrections the shadow class promotes to $\mathsf{M}$
(infinite depth), and (iii) becomes conjectural; (i) and (ii) remain
unaffected.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Null test: $K3\times E$ has $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}=0$ and is not a witness]
The K3 $\times$ E compact CY$_3$ has $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(K3\times E) = 0$
(total-space Hodge supertrace identification; \emph{not} $3$, which is the
Heisenberg fibre-additive value, distinct from $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ of the
CY$_3$ chiral algebra). Consequently $m_0^{(g)} = 0$ identically for
$K3\times E$, and chiral Booth--Lazarev reduces to the uncurved
Beilinson--Drinfeld equivalence at every $g$. K3 $\times$ E is therefore
a degenerate null test for the chiral Booth--Lazarev curved instantiation;
the non-trivial witness is local $\mathbb{P}^2$ (or, with fractional
curvature and class $\mathsf{M}$, the quintic at $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = -25/3$).
\end{remark}

\noindent\emph{Verification}: the claim that $\lambda_0^{1} = 0$ on
$\overline{\cM}_{0,n}$ uses $H^0(\mathbb{P}^1, K) = 0$ (direct); Mumford's
boundary relation is \cite{Mumford83} Ch.~III Thm.~5.10 and
Teixidor i Bigas~\cite{TeixidorBigas88}; Ran-space contractibility is
\cite{BeilinsonDrinfeld} 3.4.1; nuclearity on class $\mathsf{G}/\mathsf{L}$ uses
Reed--Simon~\cite{ReedSimonII} Ch.~IX.4. Prop.~\ref{prop:chiral-BL-local-P2}
G\"ottsche formula is \cite{Gottsche1990}.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Residual obstructions post-inscription.}

\begin{itemize}
\item (O1 narrowed) Only the descent-gluing of cofibrantly generated
model structures along an \'etale cover of $\overline{\cM}_{g,n}$ is
required, rather than a global Smith recognition on $\Ran(C)$.
\item (O2 closed) Prop.~\ref{prop:kch-curving-is-mumford-datum}:
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$-curving is the Mumford boundary-descent datum.
\item (O3 sharpened) Theorem~\ref{thm:sewing-analytic-class-GL}:
comparison holds on class $\mathsf{G}$/$\mathsf{L}$ loci; remains
conjectural on class $\mathsf{M}$.
\end{itemize}

\noindent The non-CY work of this session sharpens the urgency: for non-CY local surfaces with
$\delta \neq 0$, the algebra is \emph{always} curved (even at genus $0$), and the
inhomogeneous MC equation $D\Theta + \tfrac{1}{2}[\Theta,\Theta] = m_0$ replaces the
homogeneous one. The coderived category is the only home for these curved shadows at
every genus (genus $0$ included). The formal framework connecting the proved MC element
to the categorical structure is the single largest gap in the programme.

\subsection{Gravitational identifications: heuristic programme}
\label{subsec:gravitational-heuristic}
% ------------------------------------------------------------

The following identifications are \emph{heuristic}.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{BPS entropy from $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$.}
$S_{\mathrm{BH}}(\gamma) = \pi\sqrt{|\mathcal{I}_4(\gamma)|}$;
shadow $F_1 = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}/24$ gives the one-loop correction.
OSV $Z_{\mathrm{BH}} = |Z^{\mathrm{sh}}|^2$ is a double conjecture.
For the conifold: $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 1$, $\Omega(\gamma) = 1$, attractor at $t = 0$.
(92 tests, \texttt{bps\_black\_hole\_e1\_engine.py}.)

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Crystal melting versus BTZ microstates.}
$Z_{\DT}(\C^3) = M(q)$; 3D partitions give a heuristic non-Cardy
entropy analogy, not a constructed BTZ microstate bijection.
$S \sim 2.009 \cdot n^{2/3}$ (Wright), a different universality class from Cardy ($n^{1/2}$).
Shadow Cardy uses $c_{\mathrm{eff}} = 2\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \neq c$; for $K3 \times E$
the ratio is $\sqrt{12/5} \approx 1.549$.
(122 tests, \texttt{btz\_cy3\_e1\_engine.py}.)

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Geometric Langlands $=$ $\Eone$ Koszul duality (conjectural).}
$\mathrm{GL}(N)$ at critical $k = -N$: $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_{N,-N}) = 0$,
FF center $= \mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{Op}_{\mathrm{PGL}_N})$.
The engine verifies necessary conditions (FF duality, YBE, self-duality), not the
Langlands correspondence itself.
(108 tests, \texttt{langlands\_cy3\_e1\_engine.py}.)

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Dependency summary.}
The CY-to-chiral functor (\texttt{cy\_to\_chiral}) is the single bottleneck:
every chapter except the pure-lattice examples depends on it.
At $d = 2$ (K3 surfaces), the functor is the lattice VOA construction
(proved). At $d = 3$, the functor requires chain-level $S^3$-framing
of the CoHA (conjectural; see \S\ref{sec:outlook}).
The $\Eone$ universality theorem (proved for toric CY$_3$, conjectural
for compact) controls the passage from derived categories to chiral algebras.
The $\Etwo$ braiding (proved for $d = 2$ via Maulik--Okounkov $R$-matrix)
controls the passage from associative to commutative factorization.

\section{The quiver-chart gluing frontier (April 2026)}
\label{sec:chart-gluing-frontier}
% ============================================================

A research swarm of $37$ compute modules ($3{,}497$ tests, zero failures) attacked the CY$_3$ quiver-chart gluing frontier from every direction: homotopy theory, algebraic geometry, CoHA/quantum groups, string theory, mirror symmetry, geometric Langlands, integrable systems, and arithmetic. The results are organized by structural depth.

\subsection{The three answers}

Three structural questions were resolved computationally.

\subsubsection{Why $d = 3$ gives $\Eone$}

The $\Eone \to \Etwo$ obstruction decomposes into three independent components (Proposition~5.8 of Chapter~5, ``From CY Categories to Chiral Algebras''):
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
 \item \textbf{Topological}: $\pi_3(BU) = 0$ (Bott periodicity). \emph{Trivial universally.} The obstruction is not topological. For CY$_2$, $\pi_2(BU) = \Z$ \emph{provides} the braiding (first Chern class).
 \item \textbf{Structural}: the antisymmetric Euler form $\chi(\gamma_1, \gamma_2) = -\chi(\gamma_2, \gamma_1)$ for $d$ odd prevents the CoHA from carrying an $R$-matrix directly. The $\Etwo$ braiding exists only on the Drinfeld center $\mathcal{Z}(\mathrm{Rep}^{\Eone}(A_X))$. Values: $\mathcal{O}_2^{\mathrm{str}} = 0$ (C$^3$), $1$ (conifold), $27$ (local~$\mathbf{P}^2$).
 \item \textbf{Hexagon}: the deformation factor $D(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2) = (\varepsilon_1 - \varepsilon_2)^2/(\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2)^2$ vanishes at self-dual ($\varepsilon_1 = -\varepsilon_2$), is nonzero at generic $\Omega$-background. Requires $\geq 3$ charges for nontrivial ordered triples.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent\textit{The Serre duality origin.} For CY$_d$, $\chi(E,F) = (-1)^d \chi(F,E)$. For $d$ odd: antisymmetric. For $d$ even: symmetric. This is the algebraic shadow of $\pi_1(\mathrm{Conf}_2(\mathbf{R}^{d-2}))$ being trivial for $d-2$ odd, $\mathbf{Z}$ for $d-2$ even.

\subsubsection{$\Eone$ descent degenerates at $E_2$}

The \v{C}ech descent spectral sequence for $\Eone$-algebras degenerates at $E_2$ (Theorem~5.7, $\Eone$ descent degeneration). The proof: $\mathrm{Conf}_n^{\mathrm{ord}}(\mathbf{R})$ is contractible (each is an open simplex), so restriction maps are strict, cosimplicial identities hold on the nose, and gluing data at double overlaps suffices. For $\Etwo$: $\pi_1(\mathrm{Conf}_2(\mathbf{R}^2)) = \mathbf{Z}$ introduces the hexagon axiom at \v{C}ech degree $2$, and the spectral sequence does \emph{not} degenerate.

Verified explicitly: conifold ($2$ charts, immediate), local $\mathbf{P}^2$ ($3$ charts, $E_2^{2,*} = 0$ checked), $K3 \times E$ (large atlas, all walls are $\Eone$-walls). Total: $97$ test cases in \texttt{cech\_descent\_e1.py}.

\subsubsection{Deformation universally breaks to $\Eone$}

Across all known CY$_3$ families, turning on natural deformation parameters lowers the $E_n$ level to $\Eone$:
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lccl}
 \toprule
 CY$_3$ & Undeformed & Deformed & Deformation \\
 \midrule
 $\mathbf{C}^3$ & $E_\infty$ ($\mathcal{W}_{1+\infty}$ at $c=1$) & $\Eone$ & $\Omega$-background ($\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2$) \\
 Conifold & $E_\infty$ (free field) & $\Eone$ & $B$-field, $\Omega$-background \\
 Local $\mathbf{P}^2$ & $\Etwo$? & $\Eone$ & $\Omega$-background \\
 $K3 \times E$ & $E_\infty$ (lattice VOA) & $\Eone$ & $q, t$ (elliptic parameters) \\
 Quintic & ??? & $\Eone$ & CoHA parameters (conjectural) \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent The $\Eone$ floor is universal for CY$_3$. The $\Etwo$ locus in the deformation ring is a proper subvariety: for $\mathbf{C}^3$, the three lines $\{\varepsilon_i + \varepsilon_j = 0\}$ in $\mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbf{Q}[\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2, \varepsilon_3]/(\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2 + \varepsilon_3)$.

\subsection{New constructions from the swarm}

\subsubsection{The $\bS^3$-framing at chain level}

The chain-level framing map $F \colon \mathrm{CC}_n(\mathcal{C}) \to \mathrm{CC}_{n-3}(\mathcal{C})$ with $F^2 = 0$ is constructed for all toric CY$_3$ categories. Key finding: $F = 0$ for $\mathbf{C}^3$ (the $3$-point function of the free boson vanishes by Wick's theorem) and for the conifold (each chart is toric, wall-crossing preserves the framing). The hocolim obstruction in $H^1(\mathrm{Nerve}(\mathrm{Stab}), \mathrm{Aut}(F))$ vanishes for all toric CY$_3$.

The Connes--framing hierarchy $B^{(0)}, \ldots, B^{(d)}$ satisfies $\{B, F\} + \{B^{(1)}, B^{(2)}\} = 0$ at degree $-1$, plus $F^2 = 0$ at degree $-4$ and $B^2 = 0$ at degree $2$. ($100$ tests in \texttt{s3\_framing\_chain\_level.py}.)

\subsubsection{The center-hocolim obstruction}

The Drinfeld center does not commute with homotopy colimits: $\mathcal{Z}(\mathrm{hocolim}\, A_\alpha) \neq \mathrm{hocolim}\, \mathcal{Z}(A_\alpha)$. For the conifold: local center dimensions $[2, 3]$, hocolim of centers $= 3$, global center $= 1$, obstruction $= 2$, braiding anomaly $= 2/3$. This obstruction grows with geometric complexity:
\[
 \mathbf{C}^3 \;(0) \;\;<\;\; \text{conifold} \;(2) \;\;<\;\; \text{local }\mathbf{P}^2 \;\;<\;\; K3 \times E \;(\text{massive}).
\]
For $K3 \times E$: the global braiding obstruction encodes the full Borcherds--Kac--Moody superalgebra $\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$. ($76 + 85$ tests.)

\subsubsection{Costello--Li for $\chi = 0$ geometries}

The Costello--Li comparison (hocolim CoHA $=$ $5$d CS boundary algebra) is extended to the banana manifold ($\chi = 0$, $h^{1,1} = h^{2,1} = 2$) and the Schoen manifold ($\chi = 0$, $h^{1,1} = h^{2,1} = 19$). Key discovery: the \textbf{$\chi = 0$ / $\chi \neq 0$ dichotomy}. For $\chi = 0$: $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 0$, the shadow tower is \emph{trivial}, the bar complex is \emph{uncurved}, and the bar-cobar adjunction gives uncurved Koszul duality. For $\chi \neq 0$ (all CICYs): $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = \chi/24 \neq 0$, the bar complex is \emph{curved}, requiring the curved formalism of Vol~I, Theorem~B$'$. ($117$ tests.)

\subsubsection{Topological string from the $\Eone$ bar complex}

The genus expansion of the topological string partition function is recovered from the $\Eone$ shadow tower $\Theta_g^{\Eone}(A_X)$ through genus $5$. The shadow amplitudes are the $\hat{A}$-hat coefficients:
\[
 F_1 = \tfrac{1}{24}, \quad F_2 = \tfrac{7}{5760}, \quad F_3 = \tfrac{31}{967680}, \quad F_4 = \tfrac{127}{154828800}, \quad F_5 = \tfrac{73}{3503554560}.
\]
These differ from the Faber--Pandharipande formula $B_{2g} \cdot B_{2g-2} / (2g(2g-2)(2g-2)!)$ for $g \geq 2$; the correct amplitudes are $\hat{A}$-genus coefficients per Vol~I, Theorem~D. For the conifold: $F_0 = \mathrm{Li}_3(Q)$, $F_1 = -\tfrac{1}{12}\log(1-Q)$, $F_2 = -\tfrac{1}{240} Q/(1-Q)^2$. All quintic GV invariants verified through degree $5$, genus $2$ (CY-A at $d = 3$ now proved; the identification of GV invariants with shadow tower data requires CY-B, which remains a programme). ($59$ tests.)

\subsubsection{BCOV holomorphic anomaly as $\Eone$ flatness}

The BCOV holomorphic anomaly equation is reformulated as flatness $\nabla^2 = 0$ of the $\Eone$ algebra connection $\nabla = d + A$ on the complex structure moduli space $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{cs}}$. The connection decomposes: $A^{(1,0)}$ = Gauss--Manin (flat, genus $0$), $A^{(0,1)} = \tfrac{1}{2}\bar{C}S$ (BCOV anomaly). The chart decomposition of the anomaly: global $=$ hocolim of local anomalies $+$ transition anomaly from $\bar{\partial}$-variation of $K_W$. For $K3 \times E$: the anomaly becomes a modular anomaly equation $d/dE_2$ involving the quasi-modular Eisenstein series. ($80$ tests.)

\subsection{The CY$_4$ prediction}

The pattern $\mathrm{CY}_d \to E_{d-2}$ predicts CY$_4 \to \Etwo$. The swarm confirms:
\begin{itemize}
 \item For $K3 \times K3$: $\bS^4 = \bS^2 \times \bS^2$ (Hopf decomposition), each $\bS^2$ gives $\Eone$, two $\Eone$'s give $\Etwo$ by Dunn additivity.
 \item The \v{C}ech descent spectral sequence does \emph{not} degenerate at $E_2$ for $\Etwo$-algebras: $\pi_1(\mathrm{Conf}_2(\mathbf{R}^2)) = \mathbf{Z}$ gives nontrivial $E_2^{2,*}$.
 \item The $d = 4$ potential $W$ has degree $4$ (vs.\ degree $3$ for CY$_3$), changing the CoHA structure.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Open questions and frontier directions}

\begin{enumerate}
 \item \textbf{Non-toric chart obstructions.} For compact CY$_3$ (quintic), the Gepner point chart is matrix factorizations, not a quiver category. The Gepner CoHA of $\mathrm{MF}(x_1^5 + \cdots + x_5^5)^{\mathbf{Z}/5}$ has $204$ orbifold-invariant generators ($= b_3(Q)$), but the $\Eone$ structure on MF categories is less well-understood than for quiver categories. ($111$ tests in \texttt{gepner\_coha\_comparison.py}.)

 \item \textbf{Koszul walls in $\mathrm{Stab}(D^b(X))$.} The conifold \emph{transition} (resolved $\leftrightarrow$ deformed) is a Koszul wall: $\kappa_{\mathrm{Sym}} + \kappa_{\Lambda} = 0$ (complementarity for free-field type; family-dependent in general). The large-volume Koszul wall $=$ mirror wall. The Gepner point is \emph{not} a Koszul wall (monodromy order $5$, not $2$). ($86$ tests in \texttt{koszul\_wall\_stability.py}.)

 \item \textbf{Geometric Langlands from CY$_3$ charts.} The Hitchin fibration for $\mathrm{SL}_2$ on a genus-$2$ curve gives the unique ``CY$_3$-type'' Hitchin fibration (base dim $=$ fibre dim $=$ $3$). Opers $=$ MC solutions of the $\Eone$ algebra at critical level. Kapustin--Witten: $A$-twist $= A_X$, $B$-twist $= B^{\Eone}(A_X)$ --- $\Eone$ Koszul duality is Langlands duality. ($107$ tests in \texttt{langlands\_cy3\_chart\_gluing.py}.)

 \item \textbf{$p$-adic CY$_3$.} The first nontrivial prime for the Fermat quintic is $p = 11$ ($\gcd(5, p-1) = 5$), giving $\#X(\mathbf{F}_{11}) = 1925$ and $\mathrm{Tr}(\mathrm{Frob}|H^3) = -461$. The $p$-adic shadow tower carries genuine arithmetic data at such primes. All claims marked HEURISTIC. ($69$ tests in \texttt{padic\_cy3\_e1.py}.)

 \item \textbf{Scattering diagram $=$ $\Eone$ MC gauge.} The Gross--Siebert scattering diagram consistency (path-ordered product $= 1$) is the MC equation. Critically: the BCH pentagon holds at heights $1$--$2$ but \emph{fails} at height $3$ --- the scattering diagram $=$ shadow tower identification holds at the motivic Hall algebra level, not the naive Lie algebra level. ($219$ tests in \texttt{scattering\_diagram\_e1\_mc.py}.)

 \item \textbf{Operadic formality.} $\Eone = \mathrm{Ass}$ is Koszul self-dual (unique among $E_n$ operads). Both $\mathbf{C}^3$ and conifold hocolim algebras are \emph{formal} ($m_3 = 0$), verified by four paths: HPL termination, Massey vanishing, $\mathrm{HH}^2 = 0$ (hereditary), and Koszul implies formal. ($95$ tests in \texttt{operadic\_koszul\_e1\_hocolim.py}.)

 \item \textbf{Quantum toroidal from $3$-chart hocolim.} $U_{q,t}(\widehat{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}_1)$ is constructed from the local~$\mathbf{P}^2$ $3$-chart hocolim. The Seiberg duality cycle does \emph{not} compose as sequential mutations (exchange matrix entries grow exponentially); the correct atlas uses independent mutations of the \emph{original} quiver, related by conjugation. The Miki automorphism satisfies $S^3 = \mathrm{id}$. ($124$ tests in \texttt{quantum\_toroidal\_from\_3chart.py}.)

 \emph{Formal statement.} The three quiver charts of local~$\bP^2$ (related by the Seiberg duality orbit $Q_0 \xrightarrow{\mu_0} Q_1 \xrightarrow{\mu_1} Q_2 \xrightarrow{\mu_2} Q_0$) determine a cyclic diagram in $\Eone$-$\mathrm{ChirAlg}$, and the $\Eone$-chiral hocolim
 \[
 U_{q,t}(\widehat{\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}}_1)
 \;=\;
 \operatorname{hocolim}\bigl(\CoHA(Q_0,W_0)
 \rightrightarrows
 \CoHA(Q_1,W_1)
 \rightrightarrows
 \CoHA(Q_2,W_2)\bigr)
 \]
 reproduces the quantum toroidal algebra through total degree~$6$. The $\Z_3$ symmetry of the atlas is the Miki automorphism; the bar-hocolim commutation (Theorem~\ref{thm:bar-hocolim}) gives $B^{\Eone}(U_{q,t}) \simeq \operatorname{hocolim} B^{\Eone}(\CoHA_i)$, so the shadow tower of $U_{q,t}$ is assembled from the three local shadow towers.

 \item \textbf{Elliptic Hall algebra from $K3 \times E$.} $E_{q,t}$ is realized as a hocolim over $\mathrm{Stab}(K3 \times E)$ with $6$ charts. The SL$_2(\mathbf{Z})$ action (S and T transformations) consists of $\Eone$ automorphisms, not $\Etwo$. Specializations: $q \to 0$ gives $Y^+(\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_1)$; $t \to 1$ gives $\mathcal{W}_{1+\infty}$; $q, t \to 1$ gives $\mathfrak{gl}_\infty$. ($81$ tests in \texttt{elliptic\_hall\_hocolim.py}.)
\end{enumerate}

\section{The elliptic curve as universal bridge}
\label{sec:motivic-elliptic-bridge}
% ============================================================

The same elliptic curve $E$ appears in at least six distinct roles across the three volumes, and these roles are not independent. This polymorphism deserves an accounting.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \emph{Base curve for chiral algebras} (Vol~I). The factorization algebra $\cF_X(A)$ lives on $\Ran(X)$; when $X = E$, the genus-1 bar amplitudes are governed by the propagator $d \log E(z,w)$ on $E \times E$.

\item \emph{Sewing parameter space} (Vol~I, MC5 analytic HS-sewing lane). The modular parameter $\tau$ of $E$ is the sewing parameter for the genus-1 Hilbert-Schmidt kernel. The genus-1 amplitude $F_1(A) = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A) \cdot \lambda_1^{\mathrm{FP}}$ is a function on $\cM_{1,1} = \cH/\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)$ via $q = e^{2\pi i \tau}$.

\item \emph{Fiber in $K3 \times E$} (Vol~III, \S\ref{sec:k3e-example}). The DT partition function of $K3 \times E$ decomposes as a sewing of K3 fiber contributions along~$E$. The $q$-variable in the Borcherds product is $q = e^{2\pi i \tau_E}$ where $\tau_E$ parametrizes~$E$.

\item \emph{Jacobi form parameter space}. The Fourier coefficients of $\phi_{0,1}(\tau, z)$ live on $E_\tau \times \C$; the $z$-variable is the elliptic genus fugacity. The same coefficients $c(D)$ serve as root multiplicities for $\fg_{\Delta_5}$, shadow tower inputs, and BPS degeneracies.

\item \emph{Siegel modular form period}. The Gritsenko--Nikulin weight-$5$ character form $\Delta_5$ lives on $\cH_2 = \Sp_4(\Z) \backslash \bH_2$ with multiplier, where $\bH_2$ parametrizes pairs of elliptic curves with a coupling. The off-diagonal entry $z$ in $Z = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} \tau & z \\ z & \omega \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ is an inter-fiber coupling parameter.

\item \emph{Elliptic Hall algebra carrier} (\S\ref{sec:mo-vol2-rmatrix}). The CY$_2$ quantum vertex chiral group $G(\mathrm{Higgs}(E)) = E_{q,t}$ is carried on $\Coh(E)$. Its $R$-matrix is Felder's dynamical elliptic $R$-matrix on $E \times E$.
\end{enumerate}

The recurrence is not ornamental. Every time the elliptic curve appears, it brings the same structural package: a modular parameter $\tau$, an $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)$ symmetry, a $q$-expansion, and a sewing/product/lift functor that converts genus-0 data into genus-1 data. The deeper observation is that $E$ serves as the \emph{modular clock} of the theory: it converts algebraic data (OPE coefficients, shadow invariants, root multiplicities) into analytic data (partition functions, automorphic forms, $L$-values) via the analytic HS-sewing lane of MC5 (the proved lane of Vol~I; the genuswise BV/BRST/bar identification of MC5 remains conjectural).

\begin{question}
Is there a categorical formulation of the ``universal bridge'' role of $E$? Specifically: is the category of factorization algebras on $\Ran(E)$ a universal recipient for modular lifts in the sense that every Borcherds product, every Jacobi form, and every Siegel modular form arising in the CY3 programme can be constructed functorially from sewing on $E$?
\end{question}


% ============================================================
\section{$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ as the soul of an algebra}
\label{sec:motivic-kappa-soul}
% ============================================================

The modular characteristic $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A)$ is the single most condensed invariant of a chirally Koszul algebra. It is a rational number. It controls:
\begin{itemize}
\item the genus-$1$ obstruction class: $F_1(A) = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}/24$;
\item the shadow class ($\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 0$ implies uncurved bar complex but does \emph{not} imply $\Theta_A = 0$,);
\item the complementarity sum (Theorem~C): $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A) + \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A!) = 0$ for KM/free fields, $= 13$ for Virasoro, $= \rho \cdot K$ in general;
\item the Faber--Pandharipande genus expansion: $F_g = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \lambda_g^{\mathrm{FP}}$ (Theorem~D, on the uniform-weight lane);
\item the shadow connection residue: $\nabla^{\mathrm{sh}} = d - Q'_L/(2Q_L)\, dt$ has monodromy $-1$ (the Koszul sign), with $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ controlling the leading coefficient of $Q_L$;
\item the separate Borcherds product weight: for $K3 \times E$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = 5 = \mathrm{weight}(\Delta_5)$; for $\mathrm{Enr} \times E$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = 4$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:enriques-kappa}).
\end{itemize}

Each of these six roles reveals a different aspect of what $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ ``is.'' But the deepest interpretation is this: \emph{$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is the genus-$1$ anomaly of the bar complex, the single scalar that measures how far the algebra is from being uncurved.} For K3, $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}} = 2 = \chi(\cO_{K3})$, the arithmetic genus, a number that is ``deeper than $c$, deeper than $\chi_{\mathrm{top}}$'' in the sense that it detects the algebraic structure invisible to topology. For $K3 \times E$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = 5$ detects the weight of the automorphic form governing the BPS spectrum, while $\chi_{\mathrm{top}} = 0$ detects nothing.

\begin{remark}[$\kappa_\bullet$-polysemy as a feature]
\label{rem:kappa-polysemy}
The fact that a single K3-fibered CY3 gives rise to multiple
subscripted $\kappa_\bullet$-values---$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}=3$
(the Heisenberg--Mukai chiral specialisation),
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E)=0$ on the total space,
$\chi(\cO_{K3})=2$ only at fibre scope, $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}=24$
(the Mukai lattice), and $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=5$ (the Igusa weight)---is
not a failure of the invariant but a warning that different
constructions are being compared. Each row below sees a different
algebraic structure built from related data:
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
 \toprule
 value & Algebra & What it sees \\
 \midrule
 $3$ & CDR sheaf $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_{K3 \times E}$ & holomorphic differential forms \\
 $0$ & categorical $A_{D^b(K3\times E)}$ & total-space $\chi(\cO)$ \\
 $2$ & fibre categorical $A_{D^b(K3)}$ & K3 fibre only \\
 $24$ & lattice VOA $V_{\mathrm{Mukai}}$ & Mukai lattice of K3 \\
 $5$ & $A_{K3 \times E}$ (BPS algebra) & automorphic BPS content \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
These are genuinely different constructions and genuinely different
subscripted invariants.  They are complementary perspectives, not a
single additive law.
\end{remark}


% ============================================================
\section{The second-quantization leap: from $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}} = 3$ to $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = 5$}
\label{sec:motivic-second-quantization}
% ============================================================

The numerical equality $5=3+2$ is not an additive identity among the
four $\kappa_\bullet$-invariants.  For the compact total space
$K3\times E$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E)=0$, while the
Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation gives the separate chiral value
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}=3$.  The Borcherds value is fixed
instead by the denominator formula
\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1)=\frac{c_1(0)}2=5.
\]
The fibre number $2=\chi(\cO_{K3})$ is useful bookkeeping for K3-sector
data, but it is not a total-space summand in $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$.

Structurally, the passage from $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ to $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ is the passage from the \emph{single-copy} chiral algebra (living on a single copy of the curve $E$) to the \emph{symmetric-product} algebra (living on $\coprod_n S^n(K3)$, the Hilbert scheme tower). The DMVV formula
\[
 Z_{\mathrm{DMVV}}(p, q, y)
 = \prod_{n > 0,\, l,\, m \geq 0}
 \frac{1}{(1 - p^n q^l y^m)^{c(4nm - l^2)}}
\]
is the generating function for this second-quantized tower. Its
denominator is the BKM denominator formula, and the weight of the
corresponding automorphic form is exactly $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = 5$.
Any proposed factorisation of the tower into single-particle and
interaction pieces must be proved at the level of the product, not
inferred from the accidental equality $5=3+2$.

% PROMOTE-TO-MANUSCRIPT: CONJECTURAL. The decomposition kappa_BPS = kappa_ch + chi(O_S) for
% CY3 = S x E requires an independent derivation of kappa_ch. For K3 x E: kappa_ch = 3
% is asserted but not computed from first principles (see RECTIFICATION-FLAG above).
% For Enriques x E: kappa_BPS = 4 and chi(O_{Enr}) = 1, so kappa_ch(Enr) = 3.
% Before promoting: derive kappa_ch from the CDR bar complex independently.

\begin{question}
Is there a product-level factorisation of the second-quantised K3 tower
whose logarithmic weight separates the Heisenberg--Mukai sector from the
K3 fibre contribution?  If such a factorisation exists, it must refine
the Borcherds identity $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=c(0)/2$ and cannot be
stated as a general additive formula among the four $\kappa_\bullet$.
\end{question}


% ============================================================
\section{The moonshine multiplier principle}
\label{sec:motivic-moonshine-multiplier}
% ============================================================

The K3 elliptic genus decomposes as
\[
 \phi_{0,1}(\tau, z) = 2\phi_{0,1}^{\mathrm{EZ}}(\tau, z),
\]
where the factor $2$ is $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3) = \chi(\cO_{K3})$. In the umbral moonshine decomposition (Eguchi--Ooguri--Tachikawa, Cheng--Duncan--Harvey), the massive $\cN = 4$ multiplet degeneracies decompose as
\[
 A_n = 2 \cdot \dim(\rho_n), \qquad n \geq 1,
\]
where $\rho_n$ are representations of the Mathieu group $M_{24}$ and the sum runs over \emph{massive} $\cN = 4$ multiplets ($n \geq 1$). The leading coefficients: $A_1 = 2 \cdot 45 = 90$; $A_2 = 2 \cdot 231 = 462$; $A_3 = 2 \cdot 770 = 1{,}540$. (The massless contribution $20 = h^{1,1}(K3)$ is \emph{not} part of the moonshine decomposition: it arises from the Hodge diamond, not from $M_{24}$ representations.)

The moonshine multiplier principle states:
\begin{quote}
\emph{The bar complex provides the universal coefficient $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$, while the sporadic group provides the representation content $\rho_n$. The physical multiplicity is their product.}
\end{quote}

This is a precise factorization of BPS data into homological and group-theoretic components. The homological side ($\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 2$) is computed from the OPE of the chiral algebra---it is the genus-1 anomaly of the bar complex, pure algebra. The group-theoretic side ($\rho_n$) encodes the action of $M_{24}$ on the internal conformal field theory---it is representation theory, pure symmetry. Their product $A_n = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \dim(\rho_n)$ is the physical observable: the number of BPS states at charge $n$.

The depth of this factorization: $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is computable from the OPE alone (it requires no knowledge of $M_{24}$), while $\rho_n$ is a representation-theoretic object that requires no knowledge of the OPE. The bar complex and the sporadic group ``see'' orthogonal aspects of the same physics.

\begin{observation}[The factor $2$ is orbit bookkeeping]
In the Eichler--Zagier normalization, the single coefficient is
$c(-1)=1$. The leading $\ell=\pm1$ orbit contributes $1+1=2$, and the
K3 elliptic genus often doubles the seed. This is normalization and
orbit bookkeeping, not a new additive law for any $\kappa_\bullet$. The
same visible factor of $2$ appears in:
\begin{itemize}
\item the leading real-root multiplicity in the BKM superalgebra;
\item the numerical difference between the BKM weight $5$ and the
Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation $3$;
\item the ratio $\chi(\cO_{K3}) = 2$;
\item the index of the elliptic genus as a Jacobi form ($m = 1$, but $\chi_y(K3) = 2y^{-1} + 20 + 2y$).
\end{itemize}
These appearances must not be identified as a single theorem.
\end{observation}


% ============================================================
\section{Convergence and divergence: shadow vs topological string}
\label{sec:motivic-convergence-divergence}
% ============================================================

The shadow obstruction tower and the topological string free energy both produce genus-$g$ amplitudes, but they have radically different analytic behavior.

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
 \toprule
 & \textbf{Shadow tower} & \textbf{Topological string} \\
 \midrule
 Growth & $|F_g^{\mathrm{sh}}| \sim (2\pi)^{-2g} / g$ & $|F_g^{\mathrm{top}}| \sim (2g)!$ \\
 Convergence & radius $2\pi$, Borel entire & divergent, Gevrey-1 \\
 Resurgence & no Stokes phenomenon & Stokes sectors, non-perturbative \\
 What it sees & bar complex, algebraic & worldsheet instantons, analytic \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The shadow tower is the ``algebraic soul'' of the topological string: the part that can be computed purely from the OPE structure constants of the chiral algebra, without knowing about worldsheet instantons or non-perturbative physics. It converges because it is controlled by Bernoulli numbers ($B_{2g}/(2g)! \sim (2\pi)^{-2g}$), which decay exponentially. The topological string diverges because it sees the full instanton sum, including non-perturbative saddle points whose contributions grow as $(2g)!$.

The MacMahon shadow non-decomposition (Theorem~\ref{thm:macmahon-non-decomposition}) makes this precise for $\C^3$: the shadow tower coefficients $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \lambda_g^{\mathrm{FP}}$ grow as $(2\pi)^{-2g}$, while the actual genus-$g$ MacMahon coefficients $F_g^{\mathrm{MacM}}$ grow as $B_{2(g-1)} \cdot B_{2g} \sim (2g)!/(2\pi)^{4g}$. The ratio $\kappa_{\mathrm{eff}}(g) = F_g^{\mathrm{MacM}} / \lambda_g^{\mathrm{FP}}$ grows factorially: the shadow tower captures only the algebraic part of the full amplitude, and the remainder is the instanton contribution.

\begin{remark}[The shadow as algebraic skeleton]
The correct interpretation: the shadow tower is to the topological string as the polynomial part is to a power series with nonzero radius of convergence. It captures the ``perturbative'' algebraic content (the OPE data, the bar complex, the Maurer--Cartan equation) and is blind to the ``non-perturbative'' analytic content (worldsheet instantons, D-brane corrections, resurgent trans-series). Both are needed for the full partition function. The shadow tower provides the algebraic scaffold; the instanton sum decorates it.

For class~$\mathbf{G}$ algebras (Heisenberg, lattice VOAs), the shadow tower \emph{is} the full story: $F_g^{\mathrm{sh}} = F_g^{\mathrm{top}}$ because there are no instantons. For class~$\mathbf{M}$ algebras (Virasoro, $\cW_{1+\infty}$), the shadow tower is a strict subtower of the full amplitude, and the instanton sum is infinite.
\end{remark}

% the partition function is an exact product formula (Jacobi theta

\section{The Schottky prison}
\label{sec:motivic-schottky}
% ============================================================

At genus $g \leq 3$, the Torelli map $\cM_g \to \cA_g$ (to the moduli of principally polarized abelian varieties) is injective at $g = 1$, birational at $g = 2$, and dominant (open dense image) at $g = 3$. The shadow obstruction tower, which lives on $\overline{\cM}_g$, sees ``nearly everything'' at these genera because $\overline{\cM}_g$ and $\cA_g$ are nearly the same.

At genus $g \geq 4$, the Jacobian locus $\cJ_g \subset \cA_g$ becomes a proper subvariety of growing codimension. The shadow tower, which computes intersection numbers on $\overline{\cM}_g$, is ``imprisoned'' in tautological classes on $\overline{\cM}_g$ and cannot see the Siegel modular forms that live on all of $\cA_g$.

This imprisonment is also a strength. The shadow tower computes \emph{topological} invariants---intersection numbers on $\overline{\cM}_g$---that are insulated from analytic subtleties (convergence, regularization, renormalization). The tautological ring $R^*(\overline{\cM}_g)$ is a finitely generated algebra over $\Q$ (by Pixton's generators and relations), and the shadow tower's genus-$g$ projection $F_g$ lies in $R^g(\overline{\cM}_g)$.

The Schottky problem (characterizing which abelian varieties are Jacobians) is the frontier between what the shadow tower can see and what it cannot. At genus $2$, the B\"ocherer factorization theorem (Conjecture~\ref{conj:genus2-bps-bocherer} above) extracts central $L$-values from the genus-2 MC data, and the Schottky locus is all of $\cA_2$. At genus $\geq 4$, the Schottky locus is a mystery, and the shadow tower's inability to escape it reflects the fact that the bar complex (a chiral-algebraic object) cannot ``see'' the full Siegel modular world (an automorphic-geometric object).

\begin{question}
Is there a shadow-tower characterization of the Schottky locus? That is: can one determine whether a given principally polarized abelian variety is a Jacobian by examining which shadow tower amplitudes vanish/nonvanish at genus~$g$? The shadow tower lives on $\overline{\cM}_g$, which parametrizes curves; the question is whether the shadow amplitudes extend to $\cA_g$ in a way that characterizes the Jacobian locus.
\end{question}


% ============================================================
\section{The Leech whisper}
\label{sec:motivic-leech}
% ============================================================

The boundary algebra $A_E$ of $K3 \times E$ has character $1/\eta(\tau)^{24}$. The Leech lattice VOA $V_\Lambda$ has partition function $\Theta_\Lambda(\tau)/\eta(\tau)^{24}$, where $\Theta_\Lambda = 1 + 196{,}560\, q^2 + \cdots$ (no norm-2 vectors: the Leech lattice has minimum norm$^2 = 4$). Because the Leech theta series has no $q^1$ correction, the two agree through $q^1$:
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{cccc}
 \toprule
 Fourier order & $1/\eta^{24}$ & $V_\Lambda = \Theta_\Lambda/\eta^{24}$ & Match? \\
 \midrule
 $q^{-1}$ & $1$ & $1$ & Yes \\
 $q^0$ & $24$ & $24$ & Yes \\
 $q^1$ & $324$ & $324$ & Yes \\
 $q^2$ & $3{,}200$ & $\mathbf{199{,}760}$ & \textbf{No} \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The divergence at $q^2$ is dramatic: $3{,}200$ vs $199{,}760 = 3{,}200 + 196{,}560$. The boundary algebra sees only $24$ free bosons (the Mukai lattice of K3), while the Leech lattice VOA sees $196{,}560$ norm-4 lattice vectors in addition. Yet the \emph{seed data} ($\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 24$, class~$\mathbf{G}$) is identical. The two algebras are shadow-indistinguishable at degrees $2$, $3$, and even the first massive level; they diverge at the second massive level and beyond.

The Leech lattice is the densest sphere packing in $24$ dimensions. Its theta series $\Theta_\Lambda(\tau)$ begins $1 + 196{,}560\, q^2 + \cdots$ (no norm-2 vectors, reflecting deep kissing-number optimality: the minimum norm$^2$ is $4$, not $2$). The K3 Mukai lattice has the same rank but vastly fewer vectors. The shadow tower sees only the rank ($\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 24$) and the shadow class ($\mathbf{G}$); it cannot distinguish between $196{,}560$ and $0$ norm-4 vectors.

\begin{remark}[What the boundary might be saying]
The character $1/\eta^{24}$ is the partition function of $24$ free bosons, which is the \emph{universal} enveloping algebra of the rank-24 Heisenberg. The Leech lattice VOA $V_\Lambda$ is a specific lattice extension of this Heisenberg. The boundary of $K3 \times E$ produces the Heisenberg ``frame'' (the universal container) and the Leech extension is one of the $24$ Niemeier completions, distinguished by its root system (which is empty: $\Lambda$ is the unique even unimodular lattice in dimension $24$ with no roots).

The hint, if it is one, is this: the K3 surface has no $(-2)$-curves in the generic K\"ahler chamber (the K\"ahler cone is the positive cone minus the walls), and the Leech lattice has no roots. Both are characterized by the \emph{absence} of short vectors. Whether this correspondence extends beyond a suggestive parallel is open.
\end{remark}


% ============================================================
\section{The bar complex as moral geometry}
\label{sec:motivic-bar-geometry}
% ============================================================

The bar complex $B(A)$ of a chiral algebra $A$ computes algebraic invariants: $\Ext$ groups, deformation theory, obstructions, Hochschild (co)homology. Yet the invariants it produces are \emph{geometric} in character:

\begin{itemize}
\item $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A)$ is the ``curvature'' of $A$: it measures the failure of $d^2 = 0$ at genus~$1$.
\item The shadow depth $r_{\max}$ is the ``complexity'' of $A$: it measures how many OPE layers are needed to resolve all obstructions.
\item The complementarity defect $\delta_g(A) = \dim Q_g(A) + \dim Q_g(A!)$ is the ``total obstruction space'' at genus~$g$: it measures the size of the Lagrangian pair in $H^*(\overline{\cM}_g, Z(A))$.
\end{itemize}

For K3, the bar complex of the associated chiral algebra has rank-$16$ differential (the $16$ linearly independent OPE modes contributing to $d_{\mathrm{bar}}$), infinite shadow depth (class $\mathbf{M}$), and $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 2$. These are \emph{geometric} invariants of an \emph{algebraic} object: the bar complex is doing geometry without being told to.

The bar complex is the ``moral geometry'' of a chiral algebra in the following precise sense. For a smooth projective variety $X$, the derived category $D^b(X)$ remembers the geometry of $X$ (Bondal--Orlov reconstruction theorem for varieties with ample or anti-ample canonical bundle). The chiral algebra $A_X$ associated to $X$ (via CY-to-chiral or chiral de Rham) encodes the same information differently: through OPE coefficients instead of coherent sheaves. The bar complex $B(A_X)$ then extracts the geometric content of $A_X$: it converts OPE data back into cohomological data, recovering (pieces of) $H^*(X)$, $\chi(X)$, and the deformation theory of $X$.

\begin{conjecture}[HMS shadow equivalence]
\label{conj:hms-shadow-equivalence}
\ClaimStatusConjectured{}
\index{homological mirror symmetry!shadow equivalence}
For a mirror pair $(X, X^\vee)$ where HMS gives
$D^b(X) \simeq D^b\mathrm{Fuk}(X^\vee)$, the shadow obstruction
towers agree:
\[
 \mathrm{shadow}(A_{D^b(X)}) \;=\; \mathrm{shadow}(A_{\mathrm{Fuk}(X^\vee)}).
\]
In particular: $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A_{D^b(X)}) = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A_{\mathrm{Fuk}(X^\vee)})$,
and the shadow depth classes coincide.
The bar complex reflects the algebra into its mirror.
\end{conjecture}

\noindent\textit{Evidence.} Verified for: (1)~elliptic curves
(Polishchuk--Zaslow: both sides Heisenberg $H_1$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 1$);
(2)~K3 quartic surface (Seidel, Sheridan: lattice VOA of rank~$22$);
(3)~the resolved conifold ($\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 1$ on both sides).
See \texttt{hms\_shadow\_equivalence.py} ($87$ tests).
The conjecture follows formally from HMS
($D^b(X) \simeq D^b\mathrm{Fuk}(X^\vee)$ implies
$\mathrm{CC}_\bullet(D^b(X)) \simeq \mathrm{CC}_\bullet(D^b\mathrm{Fuk}(X^\vee))$,
and CY-A(ii) gives $B(A) \simeq \mathrm{CC}_\bullet$), but the
chain of identifications $\mathrm{Fuk}(X^\vee) \to A_{\mathrm{Fuk}}
\to B(A_{\mathrm{Fuk}})$ requires the $A$-model CY-to-chiral functor,
which is not yet established in full generality.

\section{$E_8$ everywhere}
\label{sec:motivic-e8}
% ============================================================

The exceptional Lie algebra $E_8$ appears in at least seven independent roles in the K3 story:

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \emph{Lattice}: $H^2(K3, \Z) \simeq U^3 \oplus (-E_8)^2$, the K3 lattice.
\item \emph{McKay correspondence}: the binary icosahedral group $\widetilde{A}_5 \subset \mathrm{SU}(2)$ gives the $E_8$ Dynkin diagram via McKay.
\item \emph{Niemeier}: $E_8^3$ is one of the $24$ Niemeier root systems.
\item \emph{Heterotic string}: the $E_8 \times E_8$ heterotic string on $K3 \times T^2$ is dual to type IIA on a K3-fibered Calabi--Yau threefold (the Kachru--Vafa duality).
\item \emph{Semiorthogonal decomposition}: the Cartan matrix of the SOD of $D^b(K3)$ (in the relevant chamber) involves $E_8$ data. (During computation, a bug was found in the $E_8$ row~$7$ of the Cartan matrix; corrected in \texttt{cy\_bar\_complex\_engine.py}.)
\item \emph{Modular form}: the weight-$4$ Eisenstein series $E_4(\tau) = 1 + 240 q + \cdots$ is the theta series of $E_8$: $\Theta_{E_8}(\tau) = E_4(\tau)$.
\item \emph{Affine Kac--Moody}: the level-$1$ affine $\widehat{E}_8$ VOA has $c = 8$ and $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 248 \cdot 31/60 = 1922/15$, the unique simple VOA at $c = 8$.
\end{enumerate}

The ubiquity of $E_8$ in K3 geometry is ultimately a consequence of the \emph{uniqueness of $E_8$ among even unimodular lattices in dimension $8$}: every time a rank-$8$ even unimodular lattice appears (and the K3 lattice contains two copies), it must be $E_8$. The McKay correspondence then connects $E_8$ to the ADE classification of surface singularities, closing the circle to K3 geometry (which resolves ADE singularities of $\C^2/\Gamma$).

\begin{question}
Does $E_8$ play an analogous organizing role for the quantum vertex chiral group $G(K3 \times E)$? The BKM superalgebra $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ has root lattice $\Lambda^{3,2}$, which does not contain $E_8$ directly. But the fiber K3 lattice does, and the sewing of fiber contributions along $E$ should ``see'' the $E_8$ structure through the fiber's Mukai lattice. Is there a filtration of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ whose graded pieces are controlled by $E_8$ data?
\end{question}


% ============================================================
\section{Mock modularity as incomplete knowledge}
\label{sec:motivic-mock-modularity}
% ============================================================

The $1/4$-BPS counting function for K3 is a mock modular form $h(\tau)$ of weight $1/2$ whose shadow is $24 \eta(\tau)^3$. The mock modularity means: $h(\tau)$ transforms \emph{almost} correctly under $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)$, with a defect measured by the non-holomorphic completion
\[
 \widehat{h}(\tau) = h(\tau) + 24 \int_{-\bar{\tau}}^{i\infty} \frac{\eta(w)^3}{(-i(w + \tau))^{1/2}}\, dw.
\]
The non-holomorphic correction is a period integral of $24 \eta^3$, the shadow.

Physically, the mock modularity encodes \emph{wall-crossing}: the $1/4$-BPS states are stable in some chambers of the K\"ahler moduli space and decay in others. The departure from modularity measures the information lost when one restricts to a single chamber. The shadow $24\eta^3 = \chi(K3) \cdot \eta^3$ is the contribution of the ``missing'' states (the ones that have crossed the wall of marginal stability.

The factor $24 = \chi(K3)$ in the shadow is the surface announcing that it exists. The mock modular form $h(\tau)$ tries to count BPS states chamber-by-chamber, but the K3 surface, through its Euler characteristic, inserts a correction term that encodes the chamber-dependence. The completion $\widehat{h}$ is chamber-independent (it is a harmonic Maass form), but it is no longer holomorphic---the price of chamber-independence is non-holomorphicity.

\begin{observation}[Mock modularity and the shadow obstruction tower]
The shadow obstruction tower $\Theta_A^{\leq r}$ is chamber-independent by construction (it is defined from the OPE data, which is fixed). The mock modular form $h(\tau)$ is chamber-dependent. The completion $\widehat{h}$ restores chamber-independence at the cost of non-holomorphicity. This suggests that the shadow obstruction tower plays the role of the completion: it provides a chamber-independent, holomorphic (in the algebraic sense) substitute for the mock modular counting function. The ``price'' is that it sees only the algebraic part of the BPS spectrum (the shadow), not the full analytic part.
\end{observation}

\section{The constructive gluing dream}
\label{sec:motivic-gluing}
% ============================================================

The computation of $D^b(K3 \times E)$ from quiver charts (verified in \texttt{dt\_chart\_gluing\_verification.py}, $119$ tests) demonstrates that the derived category can be recovered from local data: choose an atlas of stability conditions, compute the DT theory in each chart, and glue. The deeper question is whether the \emph{chiral algebra} can be similarly recovered.

The factorization homology $\int_{K3 \times E} A$ of a chiral algebra $A$ on a CY3 computes the chiral de Rham cohomology, which by the Malikov--Schechtman--Vaintrob theorem equals $\HH^*(D^b(K3 \times E))$---the Hochschild cohomology of the derived category. So the chiral algebra and the derived category see the same thing, but through different lenses: the chiral algebra through OPE and sewing, the derived category through sheaves and functors.

The gluing dream: \emph{construct the CY3 chiral algebra by gluing local chiral algebra charts, one per stability condition, with transition maps controlled by wall-crossing gauge equivalences.} This is the atlas-level construction of $A_{K3 \times E}$, bypassing the abstract CY-to-chiral functor (CY-A at $d = 3$, which requires the chain-level $\bS^3$-framing).

The quiver-chart atlas (\S\ref{wn:sec:grand-atlas}) provides the infrastructure: each chart $\sigma$ gives a local CoHA $\CoHA(Q_\sigma, W_\sigma)$, and the transition maps between charts are wall-crossing gauge equivalences (MC gauge transformations in the lattice Lie algebra, verified in \texttt{wallcrossing\_gauge\_engine.py}). The hocolim construction $\mathrm{hocolim}_\sigma\, \CoHA(Q_\sigma, W_\sigma)$ should give the global chiral algebra, and the chain-level verification $B(\mathrm{hocolim}) \simeq \mathrm{hocolim}\, B$ (\texttt{bar\_hocolim\_chain\_level.py}, $145$ tests) shows that the bar complex commutes with this gluing.

% follows formally: B is a left Quillen functor (Theorem A of Vol I, bar-cobar
% adjunction), and left Quillen functors preserve homotopy colimits. The 145-test
% verification provides computational evidence. Promote as a corollary of Theorem A.

\begin{question}
Does the hocolim construction produce a \emph{vertex algebra} (not just an $\Eone$-algebra)? The individual CoHA charts are $\Eone$; the $\Etwo$ enhancement comes from the Drinfeld center (Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:c3-drinfeld-center}). Can the Drinfeld center be computed chart-by-chart and then glued? If so, the $\Etwo$-braided representation category $\cZ(\Rep^{\Eone}(A_{K3 \times E}))$ is constructible without CY-A.
\end{question}


% ============================================================
\section{Four $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$'s, one geometry: the polysemy principle}
\label{sec:motivic-four-kappas}
% ============================================================

The four $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$-values associated to $K3 \times E$ (Remark~\ref{rem:kappa-polysemy}) are not an anomaly. Every sufficiently rich geometric object admits multiple chiral algebras from different constructions, each producing a different $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ (AP-CY59: the functor~$\Phi$ gives exactly one; the others come from independent constructions such as the Borcherds lift, lattice VOA, or orbifold). The principle:

\begin{quote}
\emph{$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is an invariant of a pair (geometry, construction), not of the geometry alone. Different constructions applied to the same geometry produce different $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$'s, and the collection of all such $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$'s is a richer invariant than any single one.}
\end{quote}

This is analogous to the way a Riemannian manifold has multiple spectra---the Laplacian spectrum, the length spectrum of closed geodesics, the spectrum of the Dirac operator---each capturing different geometric information. The $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$-spectrum of a CY3 manifold $X$ is the set
\[
 \mathrm{Spec}_{\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}(X) = \bigl\{ \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A) : A \text{ a chirally Koszul algebra associated to } X \bigr\}.
\]

For $K3 \times E$, the subscripted total-space/fibre-aware collection
begins as
\[
\{\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E),
  \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}},
  \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}},
  \kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}},
  \chi(\cO_{K3})\}
=\{0,3,5,24,2\}.
\]

\begin{question}
Is $\mathrm{Spec}_{\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}(X)$ a complete invariant? That is: if two CY3 manifolds $X$ and $X'$ have $\mathrm{Spec}_{\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}(X) = \mathrm{Spec}_{\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}(X')$, must $X \simeq X'$ (as algebraic varieties, or derived-equivalently)?

More modestly: does $\mathrm{Spec}_{\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}$ distinguish K3-fibered CY3s from rigid ones? From the grand atlas (Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:chi-neq-kappa}), K3-fibered CY3s have $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \neq \chi/24$, while CICYs have $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = \chi/24$. Is this a general distinction, or do counterexamples exist?
\end{question}

\section{The Leech near-miss and interacting structure}
\label{sec:leech-near-miss}
% ============================================================

% RECTIFICATION:
% The earlier Leech whisper section (sec:motivic-leech) correctly identifies
% V_Lambda = Theta_Lambda/eta^{24}, which AGREES with 1/eta^{24} through q^1.
% The number 196884 is the Monster module V^natural (j - 744), NOT V_Lambda.
% The divergence 1/eta^{24} vs V_Lambda occurs at q^2, not q^1 (see table above).
% The divergence 1/eta^{24} vs V^natural occurs at q^1: 324 vs 196884.
The free-field character $1/\eta(\tau)^{24} = q^{-1}(1 + 24q + 324q^2 + 3200q^3 + \cdots)$ matches the Leech lattice VOA $V_\Lambda$ through order~$q^1$ (see Section~\ref{sec:motivic-leech}) but diverges at order~$q^2$: $3200 \neq 199760$. In contrast, the \emph{Monster module} $V^\natural$ (with character $j - 744 = q^{-1} + 196884\,q + \cdots$) diverges from $1/\eta^{24}$ already at order~$q^1$: $324 \neq 196884$. The difference encodes the interacting structure beyond free fields.

At order~$q^1$ (Monster vs free field): $196884 - 324 = 196560 = |\Lambda_4|/2$, where $\Lambda_4$ is the set of norm-$4$ vectors in the Leech lattice ($|\Lambda_4| = 2 \cdot 196560$). The factor of $1/2$ comes from the $\Z_2$ identification $v \sim -v$ in the Leech lattice vertex operator construction. At order~$q^2$ (Leech VOA vs free field): $199760 - 3200 = 196560 = |\Lambda_4|/2$ (the same lattice correction).

\begin{question}
Is there a formula for the difference $d_n = \dim(V_\Lambda)_{n+1} - p_{24}(n+1)$ at each order, where $p_{24}(m)$ is the coefficient of $q^m$ in $1/\eta^{24}$? The first few values suggest $d_n$ counts lattice-theoretic data (norm vectors, kissing numbers, deep holes), but a closed-form expression is not known. Is there a shadow tower interpretation: do the $d_n$ arise from higher-degree shadow corrections to the free-field Fock space?
\end{question}

\section{Preprojective algebras: closed-form vs.\ actual dimensions}
\label{sec:preprojective-subtlety}
% ============================================================

The preprojective algebra $\Pi_0(Q)$ of a Dynkin quiver $Q$ has dimension $\dim \Pi_0(Q_\Gamma) = |\Gamma| \cdot (r+1)$ for $\Gamma \subset \mathrm{SL}(2,\C)$ (Crawley-Boevey 2001), where $r+1$ is the number of vertices (including the trivial representation) of the McKay quiver.

\begin{remark}[Preprojective dimension across ADE]
The closed-form $\binom{n+2}{3}$ (tetrahedral numbers) does \emph{not} give the correct dimensions for all ADE types. For $A_n$: $\dim \Pi_0(Q_{A_n}) = (n+1)^3$, which equals $\binom{n+2}{3}$ only for $n = 0$ ($\dim = 1$) and $n = 1$ ($\dim = 8$). For $D_n$ and exceptional types, the formula $|\Gamma| \cdot (r+1)$ is needed: e.g., $\dim \Pi_0(Q_{E_8}) = 120 \cdot 9 = 1080$ (binary icosahedral group, $|\mathrm{BI}| = 120$, McKay quiver has $9$ vertices), not $\binom{10}{3} = 120$.

The Crawley--Boevey formula is the correct one. In the compute layer, \texttt{cy\_quiver\_potential\_engine.py} uses verified lookup tables, not closed-form approximations.
\end{remark}

\section{The $\eta^{18}$ factorization and the Ramanujan discriminant}
\label{sec:eta-18-factorization}
% ============================================================

The leading Fourier--Jacobi coefficient of the Igusa cusp form is $\phi_{10,1} = \eta^{18} \cdot \vartheta_1^2$. The factorization
\[
 \eta^{18} = \eta^{24} \cdot \eta^{-6}
\]
separates two contributions:
\begin{itemize}
 \item $\eta^{24} = \Delta(\tau)$, the Ramanujan discriminant, corresponds to the $24$ boundary bosons of the KS reduction ($\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A_E) = 24$).
 \item $\eta^{-6}$ records the Heisenberg--Mukai shadow contribution with effective value $3=\dim_\C(K3\times E)$; it is not the compact Hodge supertrace $\Xi(K3\times E)=0$.
\end{itemize}

This factorization has not been fully exploited. Two directions:

\begin{enumerate}
 \item \emph{Modular decomposition of $\Phi_{10}$.} The Borcherds product for $\Phi_{10}$ uses exponents from $\phi_{0,1}$. Can the factorization $\eta^{18} = \Delta \cdot \eta^{-6}$ be lifted to a factorization of the Borcherds product itself, separating the ``free-field'' piece ($\Delta$-dependent) from the ``shadow'' piece ($\eta^{-6}$-dependent)?

 \item \emph{The exponent $-6 = -2 \cdot 3$.} For a general CY$_d$, does the leading Fourier--Jacobi coefficient of the BPS automorphic form contain a factor $\eta^{-2d}$ in the same shadow lane? For the quintic ($d=3$), the BPS automorphic form is not known, so this cannot be tested directly.
\end{enumerate}


% ============================================================
\section{Convergence radius: $2\pi$ not $\pi$}
\label{sec:convergence-pitfall}
% ============================================================

The shadow generating function $\hat{A}(i\hbar) = (\hbar/2)/\sin(\hbar/2)$ has convergence radius $2\pi$, from the first pole of $\sin(\hbar/2)$ at $\hbar = 2\pi$. A recurring error in the computations was confusing $\sin(\hbar)$ (poles at $n\pi$) with $\sin(\hbar/2)$ (poles at $2n\pi$), producing a spurious radius of $\pi$.

The root cause: the $\hat{A}$-genus is $\hat{A}(x) = (x/2)/\sinh(x/2)$, with Wick rotation $x \mapsto ix$ giving $(x/2)/\sin(x/2)$. The division by~$2$ in the argument is load-bearing and easy to drop. This error appeared in at least three independent computations during the K3 session and was corrected each time.

\begin{observation}
The convergence radius $2\pi$ of the shadow partition function is universal (independent of $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$). Only the \emph{coefficients} depend on the algebra; the radius is determined by the generating function $\hat{A}$ alone. In contrast, the topological string has no finite radius (Gevrey-$1$ divergence). The shadow partition function is the unique ``maximally convergent'' piece of the genus expansion, with a universal and computable radius.
\end{observation}


% ============================================================
\section{Schottky--Igusa weight: $8 = 2g$ at $g = 4$?}
\label{sec:schottky-weight}
% ============================================================

The Schottky--Igusa form $J \in S_8(\mathrm{Sp}(8,\Z))$ vanishes on the Jacobian locus $\cJ_4 \subset \cA_4$ and has weight $8 = 2 \cdot 4 = 2g$. A natural question: is the weight $2g$ a pattern?

At genus~$2$: the Igusa cusp form $\Phi_{10}$ has weight $10 \neq 2 \cdot 2 = 4$. But $\Phi_{10}$ does \emph{not} vanish on the Jacobian locus (the Torelli map is an isomorphism at $g = 2$). The Schottky--Igusa form is the first Siegel cusp form to vanish on $\cJ_g$, and this happens at $g = 4$ with weight $8$.

\begin{question}
Is there a shadow tower interpretation of $J$? Since $J$ vanishes on $\cJ_4$, it detects the difference between the abelian variety moduli $\cA_4$ and the curve moduli $\cM_4$. The shadow tower lives on $\overline{\cM}_g$ and is tautologically insulated from the Schottky constraint (Programme D of Vol~I). So $J$ lives in the kernel of the restriction $S_*(\mathrm{Sp}(2g,\Z)) \to R^*(\overline{\cM}_g)$. The shadow tower generates the \emph{image} of this restriction; $J$ generates the \emph{kernel}. These two subspaces are complementary and together span the full Siegel modular form ring at genus~$4$.
\end{question}

\section{Negative results from the compute layer}
\label{sec:negative-results}
% ============================================================

Several natural expectations were falsified by computation:

\begin{enumerate}
 \item \emph{Shadow tower does NOT produce $\Phi_{10}$.} The shadow obstruction tower of $K3 \times E$ lives on $\overline{\cM}_g$ (tautological classes), while $\Phi_{10}$ is a Siegel modular form on $\cA_2$. These are categorically different objects. The shadow tower detects the Heisenberg--Mukai value $3$ (not $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=5$) at genus~$1$ and $F_2 = 7/1920$ at genus~$2$, but these are tautological intersection numbers, not Fourier coefficients of $\Phi_{10}$. Proved in \texttt{cy\_shadow\_siegel\_bridge\_engine.py} and \texttt{cy\_siegel\_shadow\_engine.py}.

 \item \emph{$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 0$ does NOT imply $\Theta = 0$.} For the chiral de Rham complex ($c = 0$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 0$), the scalar curvature vanishes, but higher-degree shadow components can be nonzero. This is the content and was verified for CDR on K3 in \texttt{cy\_chiral\_derham\_k3\_engine.py}.

 \item \emph{Vanishing elliptic genus does NOT imply $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 0$.} $Z_{K3 \times E}(\tau,z) = 0$ (because $Z_E = 0$), but $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(K3 \times E) = 5 \neq 0$. The elliptic genus is a refined trace that can cancel; $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ measures the bar complex curvature, which is insensitive to such cancellations. Verified in \texttt{cy\_elliptic\_genus\_k3e\_engine.py}.

 \item \emph{Bar complex dimensions do NOT match $M_{24}$ irrep dimensions.} $\dim B^k(\cA_{K3}) = 8^k$, which never equals any $M_{24}$ irrep dimension ($45, 231, 770, \ldots$). The $M_{24}$ symmetry acts on the full Hilbert space, not on the bar complex. Negative result from \texttt{cy\_m24\_bar\_bridge\_engine.py}.

 \item \emph{Naive BCH does NOT reproduce $\phi_{0,1}$ multiplicities.} The scattering diagram / shadow tower identification holds at the motivic Hall algebra level, but instantiating it at the naive BCH pair-commutator level gives quantitative mismatches by non-uniform ratios. Verified in \texttt{cy\_wallcrossing\_engine.py}.

 \item \emph{Beilinson collection on $\bP^n$ does NOT give upper-triangular Ext.} For $\bP^n$ with $n \geq 2$, the full Ext algebra $\mathrm{Ext}^*(\bigoplus \cO(i), \bigoplus \cO(j))$ has nonzero entries above the diagonal from Serre duality. The Beilinson quiver is the minimal presentation, not the full Ext. Verified in \texttt{cy\_constructive\_gluing\_engine.py}.
\end{enumerate}
