\section{Frontier notes from the 30-agent swarm (2026-04-06)}
\label{sec:swarm-frontier-notes}
% ============================================================

The following notes record insights from the systematic 30-agent
computational investigation of the four Vol~I open problems
(multi-generator universality, D-module purity converse, CohFT
string equation, graph complex differential).

\subsection{Cross-channel corrections for CY quantum groups}

If the CY quantum group $G(X)$ is multi-weight---generators of
different conformal weights from different Hodge components---then
the genus expansion receives cross-channel corrections. The formula
$\delta F_2(\cW_3) = (c + 204)/(16c)$ is specific to $\cW_3$; for
general CY quantum groups the correction depends on the OPE structure
constants $\{C^k_{ij}\}$ and the propagator ratios
$r_{ij} = \eta^{jj}/\eta^{ii}$.

For $K3 \times E$ with $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}} = 3$ (chiral de Rham specialisation; $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = 5$, see Remark~\ref{rem:kappa-polysemy}):
\begin{itemize}
 \item The Hodge decomposition $H^{1,1}(K3) \oplus H^{1,0}(E) \oplus
 H^{0,1}(E)$ gives generators of mixed conformal weight.
 \item If the generators have weights $(1, 1, 1)$ (all from
 the Heisenberg lattice sector), the algebra is uniform-weight and
 $\delta F_g^{\mathrm{cross}} = 0$.
 \item If generators have distinct weights (e.g., from the
 non-linear sigma model with $\alpha'$ corrections), the
 cross-channel correction is nonzero.
 \item The propagator ratio $r_{ij}$ for $K3$ generators is
 determined by the Zamolodchikov metric of the $\cN = (4,4)$
 superconformal algebra.
\end{itemize}

\begin{question}
Compute $\delta F_2$ for the chiral algebra of $K3 \times E$.
Does the cross-channel correction have an enumerative interpretation
in terms of BPS state counts? Connection to Gopakumar--Vafa
integrality at genus~$2$?
\end{question}

\subsection{Graph complex and CY deformations}

The Kontsevich graph complex $\mathrm{GC}_2$ controls formality
obstructions for $E_2$-algebras. For CY quantum groups, the
relevant complex may be $\mathrm{GC}_3$ (3-dimensional CY). The
quartic formality obstruction $Q$ controls whether the deformation
quantization of the CY category has higher-order corrections:
\begin{itemize}
 \item $Q = 0$ (class G/L): the CY deformation is governed by
 its quadratic/cubic data alone.
 \item $Q \neq 0$ (class C/M): the CY deformation has genuine
 quartic (and possibly higher) corrections.
 \item For $K3 \times E$: the shadow class should be L or C
 (depending on whether the cubic shadow $\alpha$ vanishes).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{D-module purity for CY categories}

The factorization homology $\mathrm{FH}_X(\cA_{CY})$ of a CY
chiral algebra on a curve $X$ is a D-module on $\mathrm{Ran}(X)$.
Purity of this D-module corresponds to ``regularity'' of the CY
category. The dual-gap structure from Vol~I applies:
\begin{itemize}
 \item Gap~1: the PBW filtration on the bar complex equals the
 Saito weight filtration from mixed Hodge module theory.
 \item Gap~2: weight filtration strictness implies PBW spectral
 sequence degeneration.
\end{itemize}
For CY quantum groups arising from Chern--Simons theory on the CY,
Gap~1 is expected to be resolved by chiral localization
(Frenkel--Gaitsgory). For CY quantum groups arising from
topological string theory, the status is open.

\subsection{The barbell graph as a CY amplitude}

In the CY sigma model context, the barbell graph (two genus-$0$
vertices with self-loops, connected by a bridge) corresponds to a
specific 2-loop Feynman diagram: two boundary self-energy
insertions (the self-loops) connected by a single bulk propagator
(the bridge). Its contribution to the genus-$2$ free energy is
computable from the CY OPE.

The $c$-independent lollipop piece $1/16$ (which persists at
$c \to \infty$) has a potential interpretation as a topological
intersection number on $\overline{\cM}_{2,0}$. The specific value
$1/16 = 1/(2 \cdot |\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathrm{lollipop}}| \cdot 4)$
encodes the automorphism structure of the lollipop and the
conformal Ward identity cancellation $C_{TWW} \cdot \eta^{TT} = 2$.

\subsection{Research programme}

\begin{enumerate}
 \item Compute $\delta F_2$ for the CY quantum group of $K3 \times E$.
 \item Determine the propagator ratios $r_{ij}$ for $K3$ generators
 from the $\cN = (4,4)$ superconformal OPE.
 \item Investigate connection to Gopakumar--Vafa integrality: does
 the cross-channel correction have an integer expansion in BPS
 multiplicities?
 \item Determine whether the barbell graph contribution to
 $\delta F_2$ has a wall-crossing interpretation in the derived
 category $D^b(\mathrm{Coh}(K3 \times E))$.
 \item Extend the D-module purity analysis to the CY factorization
 homology: does purity $\Leftrightarrow$ Koszulness hold for CY
 chiral algebras?
\end{enumerate}


\part{The Seven Faces of $r_{\mathrm{CY}}$}
\label{part:VI}

The correspondence between BPS quantum groups and chiral-algebra images crystallises in seven faces of the CY $R$-matrix $r_{\mathrm{CY}}$, organised in three tiers: the collision residue for CY3 chiral algebras; the Humbert-boundary and CHL-twined families of paramodular forms; and the universal Borcherds weight identity $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$ at two scopes---the CHL ladder $N \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 6\}$ on which $\varphi(N) \mid 2$ admits a paramodular witness, and the full Gritsenko--Cl\'ery $8$-form family $N \in \{1, \dots, 8\}$ with metaplectic and spin-double-cover extensions. Part~\ref{part:VI} develops the three-tier stratification, traces the Gritsenko--Nikulin $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ face at $N = 1$ through its denominator, and identifies the Borcherds--Monster, the Fake Monster (at $d = 5$ via $K3 \times K3 \times E$), and the CHL cousins as sibling Stage-$2$ specialisations of one holomorphic factorisation algebra.

\section{The CY seven-face programme: Vol III drafts (April 2026)}
\label{sec:cy-seven-faces-vol3-drafts}

% Drafts for the Vol III version of the seven-face programme.

\subsection{The collision residue for CY3 chiral algebras}

The CY--to--chiral functor of Costello--Gwilliam, when restricted to
Calabi--Yau threefolds, produces a chiral algebra $\cA_X$ for each CY3 $X$.
The construction is functorial in $X$: smooth morphisms induce maps of
chiral algebras, and the assignment respects K\"ahler limits. The bar
complex of $\cA_X$ has a well--defined collision residue at the binary
degree, genus zero:
\[
 r_X(z) \;=\; \mathrm{Res}^{\mathrm{coll}}_{0,2}(\Theta_{\cA_X}) \;\in\;
 \mathrm{Hom}(\cA_X \otimes \cA_X,\, \cA_X)((z)).
\]
This is the CY3 incarnation of the seven--face programme: each example
class of CY3 yields a distinguished $r_X(z)$. Toric CY3 give one family
(via the topological vertex), $K3 \times E$ gives another (via the
Maulik--Okounkov instanton moduli), and toroidal/elliptic examples give a
third (via Felder's elliptic quantum group). The CY seven--face conjecture
asserts that for each of these example classes, the seven independent
constructions of an $r$--matrix in the literature produce the same
$r_X(z)$.

\subsection{Maulik-Okounkov R-matrix as face 4 for $K3 \times E$}

The Maulik--Okounkov $R$--matrix for the moduli space of instantons on
$K3 \times E$ is, at the bar--intrinsic level, the commuting--Hamiltonian
face of $r(z)$ for the chiral algebra $\cA_{K3 \times E}$. The
identification proceeds by exhibiting an explicit isomorphism between MO's
geometric $R$-matrix, defined via the stable envelope construction on
the equivariant K--theory of the instanton moduli space, and the
GZ26--style commuting differentials on the bar complex of
$\cA_{K3 \times E}$.

The mechanism is the following. The instanton moduli space
$\mathcal{M}_{r,n}(K3 \times E)$ carries an action of an infinite--dimensional
torus, and the K--theoretic stable envelope produces a basis of fixed
points. MO's $R$--matrix is the change--of--basis matrix between two
chambers of the torus action. On the chiral algebra side, the bar complex
of $\cA_{K3 \times E}$ carries a family of commuting differentials parametrized
by the K\"ahler parameters of $K3$ and the modular parameter of $E$. The
GZ26 mechanism exhibits these differentials as commuting Hamiltonians on
the bar complex. The identification of MO's $R$--matrix with the
generating function of these Hamiltonians is the CY3 analogue of
Theorem~\textup{thm:gz26-commuting-differentials}, and connects MO's
geometric $R$--matrix to the algebraic seven--face programme.

\subsection{Affine super Yangian $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_1)$ as face 5 for toric CY3}

The affine super Yangian $Y(\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}_1})$ of Kodera--Naoi and
Schiffmann--Vasserot is the Yangian face of $r(z)$ for the simplest toric
CY3, namely $\C^3$ with its Jordan quiver. The identification rests on
the work of Rapcak--Soibelman--Yang--Zhao, who construct the affine super
Yangian as the cohomological Hall algebra of the Jordan quiver and show
that it acts on the equivariant cohomology of Hilbert schemes of points on
$\C^2$.

In the seven--face picture, the bar complex of $\cA_{\C^3}$ (which
coincides with the universal vacuum module of the
$W_{1+\infty}$--algebra at $c = -2$) has a collision residue $r(z)$ that,
when transported to the spectral parameter of the affine super Yangian,
produces exactly the Yangian $R$--matrix of $Y(\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}_1})$.
The identification is one of the cleanest verifications of the CY
seven--face conjecture: the chiral side and the cohomological Hall algebra
side are constructed by completely independent methods, yet produce the
same $r(z)$.

\subsection{Elliptic Sklyanin bracket as face 6 for toroidal CY}

Felder's elliptic quantum group is the Sklyanin face of $r(z)$ for
toroidal CY3 of the form $T^2 \times \C$. The classical $r$--matrix is
the elliptic $r$--matrix of Belavin--Drinfeld, with theta--function poles
on the elliptic curve $E_\tau$:
\[
 r_{\mathrm{ell}}(z;\tau) \;=\; \frac{\theta_1'(0;\tau)}{\theta_1(z;\tau)}\,P
 \;+\; \text{(higher order)},
\]
where $P$ is the permutation operator and $\theta_1$ is the standard
Jacobi theta function. The bar--intrinsic identification gives this
$r$--matrix a categorical lift: it is the binary collision residue of
$\Theta_{\cA_{T^2 \times \C}}$, where the chiral algebra is the
factorization envelope of the elliptic affine $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2$
on $T^2 \times \C$. The Sklyanin Poisson bracket on the moduli space of
classical $r$--matrices then arises as the BV--bracket on the cyclic
deformation complex of $\cA_{T^2 \times \C}$.

\subsection{Open questions on the CY seven-face programme}
\begin{itemize}
\item What is the seven--face identification for compact CY3 (quintic,
 Grassmannian)? The non--compact toric case has been worked out, and
 $K3 \times E$ has been partially worked out via MO, but the compact
 case requires a chiral lift of the Gromov--Witten / Donaldson--Thomas
 partition functions.
\item Does the trichotomy classification (G/L/C/M shadow depths) apply to
 CY chiral algebras? Toric CY3 appear to land in class~M (matching the
 conjectural connection to W$_{1+\infty}$), but $K3 \times E$ and
 toroidal cases have not been classified.
\item Is there an eighth face from the topological vertex / refined
 topological string? The Iqbal--Kozcaz--Vafa refined topological vertex
 produces $q,t$--deformed partition functions whose unrefinement gives
 the same $r(z)$ as the chiral side. The categorical lift of this
 eighth face is a frontier question.
\item Connection to the Donaldson--Thomas / Pandharipande--Thomas
 correspondence? The DT/PT wall--crossing formula has the structure of
 a Stokes phenomenon for the bar--intrinsic $r(z)$, and the
 motivic--to--cohomological refinement should correspond to the chiral
 $\hbar$--expansion. The precise dictionary has not been written down.
\end{itemize}

% FRONTIER RESEARCH PROGRAMME — 2026-04-08

% Exhaustive catalogue of open problems with full

\section{Frontier research programme}

The modular Koszul duality engine is now proved (Theorems A--D+H,
MC1 through MC4, the analytic HS-sewing lane of MC5, and the 12-fold
Koszulness characterization; the genuswise BV/BRST/bar identification
of MC5 remains conjectural). The frontier is the
interface between this algebraic engine and (i) quantum field theory,
(ii) number theory, (iii) enumerative geometry. We catalogue the
open problems with their physics motivation.

\subsection{BV/BRST = bar at higher genus}

The fundamental open problem. Costello's perturbative
QFT framework produces, for each holomorphic-topological theory
on $\mathbb{C}_z \times \mathbb{R}_t$, a factorization algebra of
quantum observables. At genus $0$, this factorization algebra is
quasi-isomorphic to the bar complex $\barB(\cA)$ of the boundary
chiral algebra $\cA$ (Costello--Gwilliam). At genus $g \geq 1$,
the BV Laplacian $\Delta$ introduces quantum corrections that
modify the differential: $d_{\mathrm{BV}} = d_{\mathrm{classical}}
+ \hbar\Delta$. The bar complex at genus $g$ has the corrected
differential $\Dg{g}$ with curvature $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \omega_g$.

The conjecture states that $(\cO_{\mathrm{BV}}^{(g)}, d_{\mathrm{BV}})
\simeq (\barB^{(g)}(\cA), \Dg{g})$ in Positselski's coderived
category. The coderived passage is forced: the curved differential
$\Dg{g}^{\,2} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \omega_g \neq 0$ makes the ordinary
derived category collapse (Positselski acyclicity), so the comparison
must take place in the coderived category where curved objects live.

Three obstructions were identified: O1 (propagator regularity,
resolved by Wang--Grady [arXiv:2407.08667] UV finiteness),
O2 (moduli dependence, resolved by Quillen anomaly), and
O3 (higher-degree harmonic-propagator coupling for class C/M).
For class C ($\beta\gamma$): O3 vanishes by three mechanisms
(simple-pole absorption, Hodge-type mismatch, role separation).
For class M (Virasoro): the harmonic discrepancy
$\delta_4^{\mathrm{harm}} = Q^{\mathrm{contact}} \cdot \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}
\cdot \pi / \mathrm{Im}(\tau)$ is proportional to the curvature
$m_0 = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \omega_g$, so it vanishes in $D^{\mathrm{co}}$.
This is consistency, not a proof.

The resolution path: Si Li's programme [arXiv:2511.12875]
predicts the effective QME at regularization $r \to 0$ is
controlled by an $L_\infty$ algebra $\{l_k^{\hbar}\}$
parametrized by $\hbar$. If this $L_\infty$ algebra equals
the modular convolution algebra $\gAmod$, the conjecture
follows at the $L_\infty$ level.

\subsection{DK-5: full quantum group from bar-cobar}

For $\fg = \mathfrak{sl}_2$ at generic $q$, the full Hopf algebra
$U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ is uniquely reconstructed from the Yang
$R$-matrix $R(u) = uI + \hbar P$ arising from the bar complex
via the FRT construction. The Drinfeld--Jimbo coproduct
$\Delta(E) = E \otimes K + I \otimes E$ is produced automatically
by the RTT relations. Rigidity ($H^2(U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), \bk) = 0$)
ensures uniqueness: no deformation ambiguity. At roots of unity
$q = e^{2\pi i/(k+2)}$, the Verlinde truncation at spin $j = (k+1)/2$
is a direct consequence. The modular Yangian detects the
Frobenius--Lusztig center via Casimir eigenvalue separation.

For general $\fg$, the FRT reconstruction requires the $R$-matrix
spectrum to separate all irreducible summands. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$
all roots have multiplicity~$1$; for higher rank the root
multiplicities are~$1$ (simply-laced) or $> 1$ (non-simply-laced
at long roots), and the spectral separation is a non-trivial condition.

The physics: the quantum group is the symmetry algebra of
Chern--Simons gauge theory. The chain
bar complex $\to$ quantum group $\to$ knot invariants (Jones,
HOMFLYPT) $\to$ matrix model (GUE) $\to$ Bridgeland stability
connects five mathematical structures as projections of the
single MC element $\Theta_\cA$.

\subsection{Transport-to-transpose and DS-bar commutation}

The DS-bar double complex $(d_{\mathrm{CE}}, d_{\mathrm{BRST}})$
for $\mathfrak{sl}_2 \to \mathrm{Vir}$ has been constructed
explicitly at weights $\leq 6$. The naive double-complex
structure fails: $\{d_{\mathrm{CE}}, d_{\mathrm{BRST}}\} \neq 0$.
But the sign-twisted total differential
$d_{\mathrm{tot}} = d_{\mathrm{CE}} + (-1)^p d_{\mathrm{BRST}}$
satisfies $d_{\mathrm{tot}}^2 = 0$. The coadjoint action of $e$
on $\mathfrak{sl}_2^*$ is nilpotent of order~$3$ (not~$2$), so
$d_{\mathrm{BRST}}^2 \neq 0$ at bar degree $\geq 1$.

The transport-to-transpose conjecture
$(W_k(\mathfrak{sl}_N, f_\lambda))^! \simeq
W_{k'_\lambda}(\mathfrak{sl}_N, f_{\lambda^t})$
is verified computationally for $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ through
$\mathfrak{sl}_6$ (26 orbits), including the first non-hook
orbit $(2,2)$ in $\mathfrak{sl}_4$ and the self-transpose
surprise $(3,2,1)$ in $\mathfrak{sl}_6$ (level-independent
complementarity despite being classified as ``non-even'').
Butson [arXiv:2508.18248] proves inverse Hamiltonian reduction
for all orbits in type~A, extending the transport graph from
hook-type to the full Hasse diagram.

\subsection{The shadow genus expansion as matrix model}

The closed-form generating function
$G[F](\xi) = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot (\xi/(2\sin(\xi/2)) - 1)
= \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot (\sqrt{\hat{A}(i\xi)} - 1)$
packages all genus-$g$ free energies. It is meromorphic with
simple poles at $\xi = 2\pi n$ and universal Stokes constants
$S_n / S_1 = (-1)^{n+1} n$.

The genus expansion equals the GUE matrix model free energy at
$N^2 = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\cA)$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:gue-universality}).
The spectral curve $y^2 = Q_L(t)$ carries Eynard--Orantin
topological recursion whose output differs from $F_g$ by the
planted-forest correction $\delta_{\mathrm{pf}}^{(g,0)}$;
on the uniform-weight locus, $\delta_{\mathrm{pf}}$ exactly
compensates the non-Gaussian CEO, restoring the Gaussian answer.
The four shadow-depth classes correspond to matrix-model
criticality: G = Gaussian (no potential beyond quadratic),
L = cubic at criticality (Painlev\'e~I), C = quartic at
criticality (Painlev\'e~II), M = infinite potential off
criticality.

The growth rate is Gevrey-$0$ (sub-factorial):
$|S_r(c)| \sim C(c) \cdot \rho(c)^r \cdot r^{-5/2}$
with convergence radius $1/\rho(c) = |t_*|$ (nearest zero
of $Q_L$ to the origin) and Darboux exponent $-5/2$.
The expansion converges absolutely for
$c > c^* \approx 6.125$ and diverges geometrically for
$c < c^*$.

The shadow genus expansion is NOT JT gravity:
JT uses $\kappa$-class intersections (Weil--Petersson
volumes, factorially divergent), while the shadow uses
$\lambda$-class intersections (convergent, Gevrey-$0$).

\subsection{Arithmetic and Langlands}

The shadow Dirichlet series
$D_2(\cA, s) = -24\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \, \zeta(s)\,\zeta(s{-}1)$
is the $L$-function of the non-tempered
$\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{Q}})$ Eisenstein series
$E(\cdot\,; 1, |\cdot|)$, with Satake parameters
$\sigma_p = \mathrm{diag}(1, p)$ and Hasse--Weil local factors
of $\mathbf{P}^1 / \mathbf{F}_p$. This does NOT promote to
$\mathrm{GL}(N)$ for $\mathfrak{sl}_N$: the shadow captures
only the scalar projection regardless of rank.

The categorical zeta
$\zeta^{\mathrm{DK}}_{\mathfrak{sl}_3}(s) = \sum (\dim V)^{-s}$
gives $\zeta^{\mathrm{DK}}_{\mathfrak{sl}_3}(2)
= (4/3)\,\zeta(6)$ via the Mordell--Tornheim identity, with
abscissa of convergence $\sigma_c(\mathfrak{sl}_N) = 2/N$.
It has no Euler product for $N \geq 3$.

The $p$-adic shadow $L$-function
$L_p^{\mathrm{sh}}(s) = -\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot L_p(s, \chi_0)
\cdot L_p(s{-}1, \chi_0)$ has $L_p^{\mathrm{sh}}(0) = 0$
structurally (Euler factor $(1 - p^0) = 0$).
The shadow Ferrero--Washington fails at $p = 2, 5$.

\subsection{Koszulness, bootstrap, and minimal models}

Koszulness implies conformal bootstrap closure: $A_\infty$
formality gives discrete MC moduli, so the bar-intrinsic
$\Theta_\cA$ is the unique solution, with shadow depth
$r_{\max}(\cA)$ equalling the bootstrap closure order.
The MC equation at $(g{=}0, n{=}4)$ IS the crossing equation.

Minimal models are NOT Koszul: the null quotient removes a
state from $\barB^1$ at weight $w_0 = (p{-}1)(q{-}1)$ while
$\barB^2$ is unchanged, creating new $H^2$ cocycles. For the
Ising model $M(4,3)$: $w_0 = 6$, $\barB^1_6$ drops from $4$
to $3$ states, $\barB^2_6$ stays at $5$, Euler characteristic
shifts from $0$ to $1$.

The admissible Koszulness question for $\mathfrak{sl}_3$:
all $15$ tested admissible levels are Koszul (zero
counterexamples). The structural argument: $|\Phi^+| = 3
\geq \mathrm{rk}(\mathfrak{sl}_3) = 2$ root-pair couplings
surject onto the Cartan off-diagonal directions, absorbing
the null-induced cocycles. At denominator $q \geq 3$ the
mechanism fails (multi-generator null structure).

\section{The abelian $(2,0)$ pushforward on $K3 \times E$}
\label{sec:abelian-20-pushforward}
% ============================================================

The abelian $(2,0)$ theory on a CY3 threefold has a computable derived stack of solutions, yet its pushforward to a curve produces only free-field data: the correct modular characteristic, shadow class, and infinite-depth structure are invisible to it. The question is what the pushforward captures, what it misses, and how the missing structure arises from the non-linear sigma model.

The strategy follows Costello--Li for the holomorphic twist, Beilinson--Drinfeld for the factorization algebra structure on $\Ran(E)$, and Costello--Gwilliam for the pushforward of quantum observables along proper maps. The computational results come from exact rational arithmetic (MC recursion engine of Vol~I, \texttt{shadow\_tower\_ope\_recursion.py}).

\subsection{The derived stack of the abelian $(2,0)$ theory}
\label{subsec:20-derived-stack}

Let $X$ be a compact Calabi--Yau threefold. The holomorphic twist of the abelian $(2,0)$ tensor multiplet on $X$ (Costello--Li, Elliott--Safronov) produces a free holomorphic BV theory with field content
\[
 \beta \;\in\; \Omega^{0,*}(X,\, \Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}}),
 \qquad \bar\partial\,\beta = 0,
 \qquad \beta \sim \beta + \bar\partial\,\lambda,
\]
where $\Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}} = \ker(d \colon \Omega^2_X \to \Omega^3_X)$ is the sheaf of closed holomorphic $2$-forms. The derived stack of classical solutions is
\[
 \mathrm{Sol}(X) \;=\; R\Gamma(X,\, \Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}}),
\]
the derived global sections of $\Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}}$. Since $\Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}}$ is a complex of coherent sheaves with additive structure, $\mathrm{Sol}(X)$ is an \emph{abelian group stack}: the dg model is a cochain complex of vector spaces, and pushforward reduces to derived-algebraic computation.

\begin{remark}[Self-duality and signature]
\label{rem:self-duality-signature}
On a Euclidean $6$-manifold, $\ast_6^2 = (-1)^{3 \cdot 3} = -1$ on $\Omega^3$, so the Hodge star has eigenvalues $\pm i$ and there are no real self-dual $3$-forms. The holomorphic twist replaces the real self-duality condition $H = \ast_6 H$ with the holomorphic condition $\bar\partial\,\beta = 0$, which is well-defined on any complex $3$-fold. This is the cleanest framework for derived pushforward: the Dolbeault resolution of $\Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}}$ is the dg model, and its fiber cohomology is computed by standard Hodge theory.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Pushforward along $K3$}
\label{subsec:pushforward-k3}

For $X = S \times E$ with $S$ a K3 surface and $E$ an elliptic curve, consider the projection $\pi \colon S \times E \to E$. The derived pushforward
\[
 R\pi_*(\Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}})
\]
is a perfect complex on $E$. Since $\dim_\C S = 2$, every holomorphic $2$-form on $S$ is automatically closed: $\Omega^3_S = 0$ implies $\Omega^2_{S,\mathrm{cl}} = \Omega^2_S$. The exact sequence
\[
 0 \;\longrightarrow\; \Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}} \;\longrightarrow\; \Omega^2_X \;\xrightarrow{\;d\;}\; \Omega^3_X \;\longrightarrow\; 0
\]
decomposes on $S \times E$ via K\"unneth into three components.

\begin{remark}[Closure condition modifies the naive count]
\label{warn:closure-condition}
The table below lists the fiber cohomology of $\Omega^2_X$, \emph{not} of $\Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}}$. The long exact sequence from $0 \to \Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}} \to \Omega^2_X \to \Omega^3_X \to 0$ modifies $R\pi_*$ by the connecting homomorphism. In particular, the $H^0(S, \Omega^2_S) \otimes \cO_E$ summand is cut down: a section $\sigma \otimes f(z)$ is closed only when $d_E(f) = 0$, i.e.\ $f$ is constant. The naive count of $24$ generators for $\Omega^2_X$ is therefore an \emph{upper bound} for $\Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}}$. The qualitative conclusion (free-field, class~$\mathbf{G}$) is unaffected, but the precise rank of the pushforward requires computing the full long exact sequence.
\end{remark}

\noindent The fiber cohomology of $R\pi_*(\Omega^2_X)$ (before the closure constraint):

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabular}{llc}
 \toprule
 \textbf{Hodge group of $S$} & \textbf{Sheaf on $E$} & \textbf{Dimension} \\
 \midrule
 $H^0(S, \Omega^2_S) = \C\langle\sigma\rangle$ & $\cO_E$ & 1 \\
 $H^2(S, \Omega^2_S) = \C$ (Serre dual) & $\cO_E$ & 1 \\
 $H^1(S, \Omega^1_S) = \C^{20}$ & $\Omega^1_E$ & 20 \\
 $H^0(S, \cO_S) = \C$ & $\Omega^2_E \simeq \cO_E$ & 1 \\
 $H^2(S, \cO_S) = \C$ & $\Omega^2_E \simeq \cO_E$ & 1 \\
 \midrule
 \multicolumn{2}{l}{Total before closure constraint} & 24 \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent Here $\sigma \in H^{2,0}(S)$ is the holomorphic symplectic form, and the $20$-dimensional contribution from $H^{1,1}(S)$ coupled with $\Omega^1_E$ produces weight-$1$ currents on $E$. The $H^{1,1}$ sector survives the closure condition (its members are closed along $S$, and the $\Omega^1_E$ factor prevents a $d_E$-constraint). The precise rank of $R\pi_*(\Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}})$ depends on the connecting homomorphism $\delta \colon R^0\pi_*(\Omega^3_X) \to R^1\pi_*(\Omega^2_{X,\mathrm{cl}})$ and is not computed here.

\begin{definition}[The pushforward chiral algebra]
\label{def:pushforward-chiral-algebra}
The \emph{abelian $(2,0)$ pushforward chiral algebra} on $E$ is
\[
 \cA_{\mathrm{free}} \;=\; \pi_*\bigl(\mathrm{Obs}^q(\mathcal{T}_{(2,0)}|_{S \times E})\bigr),
\]
the pushforward of the quantum observables of the holomorphically twisted abelian $(2,0)$ theory along $\pi \colon S \times E \to E$. By the Costello--Gwilliam theorem, this is a factorization algebra on $\Ran(E)$, hence a chiral algebra on~$E$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[OPE structure of $\cA_{\mathrm{free}}$]
\label{prop:pushforward-ope}
The chiral algebra $\cA_{\mathrm{free}}$ is of Heisenberg/lattice type. Its OPE is determined by the propagator of the $6$-dimensional theory pushed forward along~$S$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item The $20$ currents $J_a(z)$ from $H^{1,1}(S) \otimes \Omega^1_E$ have double-pole OPE:
 \[
 J_a(z)\, J_b(w) \;\sim\; \frac{\eta_{ab}}{(z-w)^2},
 \]
 where $\eta_{ab} = \int_S \omega_a \wedge \omega_b$ is the intersection form restricted to $H^{1,1}(S)$, of signature $(1,19)$ (the full $H^2(S,\R)$ has signature $(3,19)$, with $(2,0)$ from $H^{2,0} \oplus H^{0,2}$).
 \item The remaining $4$ generators (from $H^{2,0}$, $H^{0,2}$, $H^0(\cO_S)$, $H^2(\cO_S)$) have at most double-pole OPE.
 \item No poles of order $\geq 3$ appear: the $6$-dimensional theory is free with at most quadratic action.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Costello--Gwilliam: pushforward preserves factorization]
\label{rem:cg-pushforward}
The key theorem: for $\pi \colon M \to N$ a proper map of complex manifolds and $\cF$ a factorization algebra on $M$, the pushforward $\pi_*(\cF)$ is a factorization algebra on $N$ (Costello--Gwilliam, \emph{Factorization algebras in quantum field theory}, Chapter~6). For the abelian $(2,0)$ theory, the factorization algebra is the symmetric monoidal one (free fields), and the pushforward inherits this structure. The chiral algebra $\cA_{\mathrm{free}}$ therefore carries a well-defined factorization structure on $\Ran(E)$ --- it is an honest chiral algebra in the Beilinson--Drinfeld sense, not merely a complex of sheaves.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Shadow tower of the pushforward: class $\mathbf{G}$}
\label{subsec:pushforward-shadow}

By Proposition~\ref{prop:pushforward-ope}, $\cA_{\mathrm{free}}$ is a lattice vertex algebra $V_\Lambda$ where $\Lambda$ is determined by the fiber cohomology surviving the closure constraint. The Vol~I lattice curvature theorem (proved in \texttt{chapters/examples/lattice\_foundations.tex}, Theorem~4.1; verified in \texttt{compute/lib/lattice\_voa\_shadows.py}) gives $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(V_\Lambda) = \mathrm{rank}(\Lambda)$ for \emph{any} lattice VA, regardless of signature or deformation parameters.

\begin{claim}[Shadow data of the pushforward]
\label{claim:pushforward-shadow}
\hfill
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\cA_{\mathrm{free}}) = \mathrm{rank}(\Lambda)$, where $\Lambda$ is the lattice from the pushforward (see Warning~\ref{warn:closure-condition}).
 \item $S_3(\cA_{\mathrm{free}}) = 0$: no cubic shadow (no simple poles in the OPE).
 \item $S_4(\cA_{\mathrm{free}}) = 0$: no quartic shadow.
 \item Shadow class: $\mathbf{G}$ (Gaussian), depth $r_{\max} = 2$.
 \item The shadow obstruction tower terminates: $\Theta_{\cA_{\mathrm{free}}} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \omega_g$ at all genera.
\end{enumerate}
The rank of $\Lambda$ is \emph{not yet computed}: it requires evaluating the connecting homomorphism in the long exact sequence from the closure constraint (Warning~\ref{warn:closure-condition}). The naive upper bound is $24$ (from the $\Omega^2_X$ table); the $H^{1,1}(S)$ sector contributes at least $20$. The qualitative conclusion ($\mathbf{G}$, depth~$2$) holds for any rank.
\end{claim}

\subsection{The sigma model VOA: class $\mathbf{M}$}
\label{subsec:sigma-model-shadow}

The K3 sigma model VOA $\cA_\sigma$ at a generic point in the K3 moduli space is a $c = 6$ $\cN = (4,4)$ superconformal vertex algebra. It is \emph{not} a lattice VA: it is the non-linear sigma model into $K3$, with the small $\cN = 4$ superconformal algebra (generators $T$, $G^{\pm,a}$, $J^a$) providing structure beyond free fields. In particular, the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_R$ affine currents $J^a$ at level $k = 1$ introduce simple-pole OPEs (Lie bracket), absent in any lattice VA.

\begin{proposition}[Shadow data of the K3 sigma model]
\label{prop:sigma-shadow}
\hfill
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\cA_\sigma) = 2 = \dim_\C(K3)$.
 \item $S_3(\cA_\sigma) = 2$ (cubic shadow from the Virasoro self-coupling on the $T$-line and $\mathrm{SU}(2)_R$ Lie bracket).
 \item $S_4(\cA_\sigma) = \frac{5}{156}$ (quartic shadow from the Virasoro contact term at $c = 6$; the formula $Q^{\mathrm{contact}} = \frac{10}{c(5c+22)}$ is the degree-$4$ shadow of the Virasoro OPE on the $T$-primary line, derived in Vol~I \texttt{chapters/examples/virasoro\_shadow\_tower.tex}).
 \item Critical discriminant: $\Delta = 8\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} S_4 = \frac{20}{39} \neq 0$.
 \item Shadow class: $\mathbf{M}$ (mixed), depth $r_{\max} = \infty$. Infinite depth follows from $\Delta \neq 0$: by the Vol~I single-line dichotomy theorem, $\Delta \neq 0$ forces all $S_r \neq 0$ for $r \geq 5$ via the MC recursion.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent\textit{Verification}: \texttt{cy\_n4sca\_k3\_engine.py}, \texttt{cy\_bar\_n4sca\_engine.py}.
\end{proposition}

\noindent The MC recursion (Vol~I, \texttt{shadow\_tower\_ope\_recursion.py}, Theorem \texttt{thm:obstruction-recursion}) with initial data $(\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}, S_3, S_4) = (2, 2, \frac{5}{156})$ produces the full shadow tower:

 $r$ & $S_r(\cA_\sigma)$ & Sign \\
 \midrule
 2 & $2$ & $+$ \\
 3 & $2$ & $+$ \\
 4 & $5/156$ & $+$ \\

\subsection{The $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$-collapse}
\label{subsec:kappa-collapse}

\begin{observation}[$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$-collapse: rank $\to$ $\dim_\C$]
\label{obs:kappa-collapse}
The passage from the abelian $(2,0)$ pushforward to the K3 sigma model exhibits a \emph{non-perturbative collapse of the modular characteristic}:
\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\cA_{\mathrm{free}}) \;=\; \mathrm{rank}(\Lambda) \;\in\; \{22, 24\},
 \qquad
 \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\cA_\sigma) \;=\; 2 \;=\; \dim_\C(K3).
\]
The ratio $\mathrm{rank}/\dim_\C \in \{11, 12\}$ is not a small correction. The sigma model is not a perturbative deformation of the free field: it is a different point in the moduli space of $c = 6$ $\cN = (4,4)$ SCFTs. The $\cN = 4$ supersymmetry constrains the genus-$1$ curvature to equal the complex dimension of the target, regardless of the free-field rank.
\end{observation}

\begin{proposition}[The gap is structural, not perturbative]
\label{warn:structural-gap}
No deformation of $\cA_{\mathrm{free}}$ within the class of lattice vertex algebras can produce $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 2$: the Vol~I theorem gives $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(V_\Lambda) = \mathrm{rank}(\Lambda)$ for \emph{all} lattice VAs, independent of deformation parameters. To reach $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 2$ from the free-field data, one must pass to a genuinely different algebraic structure: the non-linear sigma model with its $\cN = 4$ SCA. This is not a wall-crossing: there is no wall, no stability condition, no KS-type formula relating the two sides. The free-field pushforward is not a degeneration of the sigma model within a shared moduli space; it is a different algebraic object (lattice VA vs non-linear SCFT) that happens to carry the same topological data.
\end{proposition}

\subsection{BKM root multiplicities: the constancy theorem}
\label{subsec:bkm-constancy}

The BKM superalgebra $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ has positive roots $\alpha = (n, l, m) \in \Z^3$ with multiplicity $\mult(\alpha) = c(4nm - l^2)$, where $c(D)$ denotes the discriminant-indexed Fourier coefficients of $\phi_{0,1}$. We define the \emph{level} of a root as $\ell(\alpha) = n + m$.

\begin{theorem}[Root multiplicity constancy]
\label{thm:root-mult-constancy}
For all levels $\ell \geq 1$:
\[
 \sum_{\substack{\alpha \in \Delta_+ \\ \ell(\alpha) = \ell}} \mult(\alpha) \;=\; 24 \;=\; \chi(K3).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
At each level $\ell$, the positive roots decompose into \emph{boundary roots} (those with $n = 0$ or $m = 0$) and \emph{interior roots} (those with $n, m > 0$, so $\ell = n + m$ with $n, m \geq 1$).

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Boundary contribution.} Roots with $m = 0$: $(n, l, 0)$ for $n = \ell$, varying $l$. The multiplicity is $c(-l^2)$, which is nonzero only for $l = 0$ (giving $c(0) = 10$) and $l = \pm 1$ (giving $c(-1) = 1$ each). Total: $10 + 1 + 1 = 12$. Similarly for $n = 0$: total $12$. Boundary total: $24$.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Interior cancellation.} For each pair $(n, m)$ with $n + m = \ell$ and $n, m \geq 1$:
\[
 \sum_{l \in \Z} c(4nm - l^2) \;=\; 0.
\]
This is exactly the modular constancy of $\phi_{0,1}$ at $z = 0$. The weak Jacobi form $\phi_{0,1}(\tau, z)$ has weight~$0$ and index~$1$; evaluating at $z = 0$ gives a modular form of weight~$0$ on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)$, which is necessarily constant (the space $M_0(\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z))$ is one-dimensional, spanned by~$1$). The value is $\phi_{0,1}(\tau, 0) = 12$ (Eichler--Zagier, \emph{The Theory of Jacobi Forms}, 1985, p.~108). At the level of Fourier coefficients: $\sum_l c(4N - l^2) = 0$ for all $N \geq 1$, since the $q^N$ coefficient of the constant function $12$ vanishes for $N \geq 1$.

\medskip\noindent The boundary gives $24$, the interior gives $0$, so $\sum_{\ell(\alpha) = \ell} \mult(\alpha) = 24$ at every level.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The cancellation at level $2$]
\label{rem:level-2-cancellation}
The interior at level $2$ consists of roots $(1, l, 1)$ with $\mult = c(4 - l^2)$. The discriminant-indexed coefficients are from the Eichler--Zagier table (1985, p.~108):
\begin{itemize}
 \item $l = 0$: $D = 4$, $c(4) = 108$.
 \item $l = \pm 1$: $D = 3$, $c(3) = -64$ each.
 \item $l = \pm 2$: $D = 0$, $c(0) = 10$ each.
\end{itemize}
Sum: $108 - 2 \cdot 64 + 2 \cdot 10 = 108 - 128 + 20 = 0$. The cancellation is a direct consequence of $\sum_l c(4 - l^2) = 0$ (the $q^1$ coefficient of $\phi_{0,1}(\tau, 0) = 12$). Computationally verified through level~$6$ in \texttt{centcom/scripts/research/k3e\_pushforward\_shadow\_computation.py}.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Relation to the shadow tower]
\label{rem:constancy-shadow}
The constancy $\sum_\ell \mult(\alpha) = 24 = \chi(K3)$ reflects the topological datum $\chi(K3)$ persisting through the BKM construction. This is precisely the datum that the abelian $(2,0)$ pushforward \emph{does} capture: the Euler characteristic of the fiber enters through the lattice rank and the partition function of the free-field theory. The pushforward gives the correct topological backbone ($\chi = 24$) even though it gives the wrong shadow class and the wrong $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Three levels of structure}
\label{subsec:three-levels}

The analysis isolates three distinct $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ values. Conflating them is a category error.

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabular}{llcll}
 \toprule
 \textbf{Object} & \textbf{Symbol} & $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ & \textbf{Class} & \textbf{Depth} \\
 \midrule
 Abelian $(2,0)$ pushforward & $\cA_{\mathrm{free}}$ & $\mathrm{rank}(\Lambda) \in \{22, 24\}$ & $\mathbf{G}$ & $2$ \\
 K3 sigma model VOA & $\cA_\sigma$ & $2$ & $\mathbf{M}$ & $\infty$ \\
 BKM global ($\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$, K3-3) & $G(K3 \times E)$ & $5$ & $\mathbf{M}$ & $\infty$ \\
 \bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent The chain $\mathrm{rank}(\Lambda) \to 2 \to 5$ reflects:
\begin{itemize}
 \item \textbf{Free fields $\to$ sigma model}: the $\cN = 4$ SCA constrains $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ from $\mathrm{rank}$ to $\dim_\C$, introducing $S_3 \neq 0$ and $S_4 \neq 0$ and upgrading the shadow class from $\mathbf{G}$ to $\mathbf{M}$.
 \item \textbf{Sigma model $\to$ BKM global}: the passage from the
 Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation
 $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}=3$ to the BKM modular
 characteristic
 $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=5=c_1(0)/2=10/2$, by the Borcherds weight
 theorem. The decomposition $5=2+3$ is a numerical coincidence for
 $N=1$; it fails for all $\Z/N\Z$-orbifolds with $N\geq2$ (AP-CY37).
 The correct universal formula is $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=c_N(0)/2$.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The $T^4/\Z_2$ orbifold point}
\label{subsec:t4z2}

At the orbifold limit $S = T^4/\Z_2$ (Kummer surface), the K3 sigma model degenerates to an orbifold of the free-field theory. This is the unique point in the K3 moduli space where the pushforward and the sigma model can be directly compared.

\begin{conjecture}[Orbifold point agreement]
\label{conj:orbifold-agreement}
At $S = T^4/\Z_2$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
 \item The abelian $(2,0)$ pushforward on $T^4/\Z_2 \times E$ produces a chiral algebra $\cA_{\mathrm{free}}^{\mathrm{orb}}$ whose $\Z_2$-orbifold twisted sectors produce additional generators.
 \item The orbifold chiral algebra $\cA_{\mathrm{free}}^{\mathrm{orb}}$ has $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 2$ (the $\Z_2$-orbifold kills half the weight-$1$ currents and the twisted sectors introduce new constraints, collapsing $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ from $\mathrm{rank}$ to $\dim_\C$).
 \item The shadow tower of $\cA_{\mathrm{free}}^{\mathrm{orb}}$ is class $\mathbf{M}$ with the same initial data $(\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}, S_3, S_4) = (2, 2, \frac{5}{156})$ as the generic K3 sigma model.
 \item The deformation theory away from $T^4/\Z_2$ (resolving the orbifold singularities) preserves the shadow class and the modular characteristic, consistent with $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = \dim_\C$ being independent of the K3 moduli.
\end{enumerate}
\end{conjecture}

\begin{remark}[The orbifold as meeting ground]
\label{rem:orbifold-meeting}
Conjecture~\ref{conj:orbifold-agreement} identifies the $T^4/\Z_2$ point as the natural meeting ground between the derived-stack approach (providing the chain-level free-field data) and the shadow-tower approach (providing the infinite-depth structure). If the conjecture holds, the $\cN = 4$ SCA structure responsible for $S_3, S_4 \neq 0$ arises \emph{from the orbifold twisted sectors}: the free-field OPE has only double poles ($S_3 = S_4 = 0$), but the twist-field OPE introduces new pole structures that create the cubic and quartic shadows.

This would complete the pipeline:
\[
 \text{Abelian $(2,0)$} \;\xrightarrow[\text{derived pushforward}]{}\; \cA_{\mathrm{free}} \;\xrightarrow[\Z_2\text{-orbifold}]{}\; \cA_{\mathrm{free}}^{\mathrm{orb}} \;\xleftarrow[\text{orbifold limit}]{}\; \cA_\sigma
\]
The left arrow is computable from derived algebraic geometry (chain-level dg model); the right arrow is the orbifold limit in the K3 moduli space. The meeting point $\cA_{\mathrm{free}}^{\mathrm{orb}}$ is where the two approaches agree.
\end{remark}

\subsection{What the pushforward does and does not provide}
\label{subsec:pushforward-verdict}

\begin{observation}[The pushforward captures the topological backbone]
\label{obs:topological-backbone}
The abelian $(2,0)$ pushforward on $K3 \times E$ provides:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item The lattice $\Lambda_{K3} = U^3 \oplus E_8(-1)^2$ with its intersection form, the input to the BKM root lattice.
 \item The Euler characteristic $\chi(K3) = 24$, the constant in the root-multiplicity constancy theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:root-mult-constancy}).
 \item The K3 elliptic genus $\phi_{0,1}$, computable from the free-field partition function and the orbifold formula.
 \item The chain-level dg model for the derived stack, the input to deformation theory.
\end{enumerate}
It does \emph{not} provide:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}, resume]
 \item The correct modular characteristic ($\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 2$, not $\mathrm{rank}$).
 \item The non-trivial shadow tower ($S_3, S_4 \neq 0$).
 \item The infinite shadow depth (class $\mathbf{M}$).
 \item The BKM root multiplicities directly (these require the full MC element).
\end{enumerate}
The pushforward captures the topological data (lattice, $\chi$, elliptic genus) but not the algebraic structure (shadow class, $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$, depth). The transition from the correct topological data to the correct algebraic structure requires the non-linear sigma model (equivalently, the $\cN = 4$ SCA).
\end{observation}

\begin{remark}[Witten's perspective: M5-brane on $K3$]
\label{rem:witten-m5}
In the M-theory picture, the abelian $(2,0)$ theory is the worldvolume theory of a single M5-brane. The pushforward along $K3$ gives the effective theory of the M5-brane wrapping $K3$: a $2$-dimensional theory on $E$ with content determined by the $K3$ zero modes (harmonic forms). The sigma model VOA arises only at the level of the \emph{string worldsheet}; the non-perturbative type~IIA / heterotic duality relates the M5-brane picture to the string sigma model on $K3$. The $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$-collapse from $\mathrm{rank}$ to $\dim_\C$ is the algebraic shadow of this duality: the M5-brane sees $\mathrm{rank}(H^2)$ zero modes, while the string worldsheet sees $\dim_\C(K3)$ as the effective target dimension.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Gaiotto's perspective: class of theories]
\label{rem:gaiotto-class}
The class of field theories whose global derived stacks are abelian group stacks can be viewed as a $6$-dimensional analogue of Gaiotto's class~$\cS$, in the limited sense that both are families parametrized by compactification data. The analogy is imperfect: class~$\cS$ (the \emph{non-abelian} $(2,0)$ on $\Sigma$) produces interacting $\cN = 2$ gauge theories, while the abelian $(2,0)$ on $M^4$ produces free-field chiral algebras determined by $H^*(M^4)$. The non-abelian $(2,0)$ theory (which has no Lagrangian and no known derived-stack description) would be the true $6$-dimensional class~$\cS$. The shadow tower classification ($\mathbf{G}$/$\mathbf{L}$/$\mathbf{C}$/$\mathbf{M}$) would provide a finer invariant in that setting, detecting the algebraic type of the compactified theory.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Connections to open questions}
\label{subsec:pushforward-open}

The pushforward analysis bears on several open questions from Section~\ref{sec:open-questions}:

\begin{itemize}
 \item \textbf{Question 2} (chain-level $\bS^3$-framing for CY3): the abelian $(2,0)$ pushforward provides the \emph{abelian} (free-field) part of the chain-level data. The non-abelian part (the $\cN = 4$ SCA structure) is what carries the $\bS^3$-framing. If Conjecture~\ref{conj:orbifold-agreement} holds, the framing arises from the orbifold twisted sectors.

 \item \textbf{Question 5} ($\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = h^{1,1}/4$ universality): the $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$-collapse shows that the relevant quantity is $\dim_\C$, not $h^{1,1}$ or $\mathrm{rank}$. For $K3$: $\dim_\C = 2$, $h^{1,1}/4 = 5$, and neither equals $\mathrm{rank}/12 \approx 1.83$. The question should be reframed: what determines $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ (the BKM weight) in terms of Hodge data, and how does the second-quantization factor $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} / \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ depend on the geometry?

 \item \textbf{Question 8} (shadow depth of QVCGs): the pushforward analysis shows that the shadow depth of the input chiral algebra is $\mathbf{G}$ (free fields), but the QVCG should have shadow depth $\mathbf{M}$ (the BKM root system has infinite depth). The depth upgrade from $\mathbf{G}$ to $\mathbf{M}$ must come from the non-perturbative structure (sigma model, orbifold, or envelope).
\end{itemize}

\noindent\textit{Verification}: full computation in \texttt{centcom/scripts/research/k3e\_pushforward\_shadow\_computation.py}, importing Vol~I MC recursion engine. All shadow tower values are exact rational, verified against the MC equation at each degree.

% ============================================================
\section{Lessons from the 129-agent session (2026-04-13)}
\label{sec:129-agent-session}
% ============================================================

This section records the informal knowledge, dead ends, obstructions,
and meta-insights from the 129-agent computational session that produced
9,608 new lines across 18 files. The formal mathematics is in the
manuscript; these notes capture the \emph{heuristic intelligence} that
would otherwise be lost.

\subsection{Dead ends: three wrong proofs and two false patterns}
\label{subsec:dead-ends}

\begin{proposition}[Per-$k$ failure of $\{m_3, B^{(2)}\} = 0$; total bracket vanishes via $m_2$]
\label{warn:dead-end-bidegree}
The individual bracket $\{m_3, B^{(2)}\}$ is nonzero; the total bracket $\{m_2 + m_3, B^{(2)}\} = 0$ vanishes by cross-degree cancellation. The bidegree $(p,q)$-decomposition argument, which invokes the mixed-complex axiom $[b, B^{(0)}] = 0$ (equivalently $[b, B] = 0$ for $B = B^{(0)}$ the Connes operator) and claims degree-by-degree cancellation, fails for three reasons:
\begin{itemize}
 \item The mixed-complex axiom $[b, B^{(0)}] = 0$ concerns the
 \emph{zeroth} Connes operator $B^{(0)}$, not the higher operators
 $B^{(j)}$ in the Connes hierarchy.
 \item $B^{(2)} \neq B^{(0)}$. The superscript indexes the cyclic
 degree, not a power. The operators $B^{(j)}$ for $j \geq 1$ satisfy
 different commutation relations with $b$.
 \item Transposing the identity $[b, B^{(0)}] = 0$ to $[b, B^{(2)}]$
 is unjustified without verifying that the identity holds for the
 higher operator.
\end{itemize}
Direct matrix evaluation at dimension $\leq 6$ (four independent routes) confirms $\{m_3, B^{(2)}\} \neq 0$ individually. The correct vanishing is operadic: the \emph{total} bracket $\{m_2 + m_3, B^{(2)}\} = 0$ because the $m_2$-contribution cancels the $m_3$-contribution -- the cross-degree cancellation phenomenon.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Tsygan formality does not control $\{m_3, B^{(2)}\}$]
\label{warn:dead-end-tsygan}
The Tsygan formality theorem for cyclic chains does not imply $\{m_3, B^{(2)}\} = 0$. Tsygan formality applies to the pair $(b, B^{(0)})$, not to the full Connes hierarchy $(b, B^{(0)}, B^{(1)}, B^{(2)}, \ldots)$: the formality statement is that the $(b, B^{(0)})$-complex is formal as a mixed complex, and it says nothing about the interaction of $m_3$ with the higher $B^{(j)}$. A quasi-isomorphism purported to intertwine $m_3$ with $B^{(2)}$ therefore cannot be extracted from the formality statement.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Cyclic invariance does not force $\mathrm{Obs}_{\Ainf} = 0$; the vanishing is degree-theoretic]
\label{warn:dead-end-cyclic}
The vanishing $\mathrm{Obs}_{\Ainf} = 0$ for the $\Ainf$ obstruction class $\mathrm{Obs}_{\Ainf} \in \HH^{-2}_{\Eone}$ follows from $\HH^{-2}_{\Eone} = 0$ by unit-connectedness of the $\Eone$-operad: the obstruction lives at the wrong degree. A cyclic-invariance argument -- that $\mathrm{Obs}_{\Ainf}$, being a Hochschild class, is invariant under cyclic rotation of inputs and so is forced to vanish -- cannot produce the conclusion: cyclic invariance controls \emph{adjacent} contractions (consecutive pairs in the cyclic word) but does not constrain \emph{non-adjacent} contractions.
\end{proposition}

\begin{observation}[Dead end 4: $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} + \kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}$]
\label{obs:dead-end-kappa-sum}
For $K3 \times E$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=5$ and the
Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation has $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}=3$, but
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E)=0$.  The number $2$ is the K3-fibre
Euler value $\chi(\cO_{K3})$, not a total-space categorical summand.
Thus $5=3+2$ is not even a scoped identity among the four invariants; it
is a warning sign.  The universal formula is
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N)=c_N(0)/2$ at Borcherds scope.
\end{observation}

\begin{proposition}[No additive $S$-operator correction absorbs the ZTE failure]
\label{warn:dead-end-zte-additive}
The Zamolodchikov tetrahedron equation (ZTE) fails at $O(\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^2)$ for the Yang $R$-matrix, and no additive correction $S^{\mathrm{corr}} = S + \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^2 T$ with $T$ a $3$-particle operator can absorb the failure. The obstruction is that the linearized ZTE for $T$ is inconsistent: the inhomogeneity (the $O(\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^2)$ failure) does not lie in the image of the linearized ZTE operator. A correction must therefore operate at the $R$-matrix level (modifying $R$ itself), not at the $S$-operator level (adding to the factored $S$).
\end{proposition}

\subsection{Why the correct proofs work}
\label{subsec:why-proofs-work}

\begin{observation}[The TCFT proof of $\{m_3, B^{(2)}\}$-total vanishing]
\label{obs:tcft-proof}
The correct proof that the total bracket $\{m_2 + m_3, B^{(2)}\} = 0$
vanishes uses the TCFT (topological conformal field theory) structure:
the operator $d^2 = 0$ on the moduli chain complex $C_*(\overline{\cM}_{g,n})$
handles \emph{all} boundary contractions uniformly because both $b$ (the
Hochschild differential) and $B^{(2)}$ (the genus-$2$ Connes operator)
are images of a single boundary operator on the moduli space. The key
insight: the $m_2$ and $m_3$ contributions to $\{-, B^{(2)}\}$ are
\emph{different boundary strata of the same moduli space}, and $d^2 = 0$
forces their sum to vanish even though each stratum contributes nonzero.
\end{observation}

\begin{observation}[The $\infty$-categorical proof of $\mathrm{Obs}_{\Ainf} = 0$]
\label{obs:infty-cat-proof}
The obstruction to extending the $\Eone$-chiral bialgebra structure from
spin $\leq s$ to spin $s+1$ lives in
$\HH^{-2}_{\Eone}(\cA, \cA \otimes \cA)$. This group vanishes by
unit-connectedness: the $\Eone$-operad is $0$-connected (its space of
$n$-ary operations $\Eone(n) \simeq \Sigma_n$ is discrete), and the
Hochschild cohomology of an $\Eone$-algebra with bimodule coefficients
in negative degrees is controlled by the connectivity of the operad.
The obstruction lives at degree $-2$, but the first potentially
nonzero group is at degree $0$. The argument is purely structural:
no computation of the obstruction cocycle is needed.
\end{observation}

\begin{observation}[Cross-degree cancellation: the meta-principle]
\label{obs:cross-degree}
The most subtle phenomenon in the session: $\{m_3, B^{(2)}\} \neq 0$
and $\{m_2, B^{(2)}\} \neq 0$ individually, but
$\{m_2 + m_3, B^{(2)}\} = 0$. This is \textbf{cross-degree
cancellation}: contributions from operations of different degree
(binary $m_2$ and ternary $m_3$) cancel in the total bracket.

The mechanism: the $\Ainf$ structure $m = m_2 + m_3 + m_4 + \cdots$
satisfies the master equation $\{m, m\} = 0$ (the $\Ainf$ relations).
The Connes operator $B^{(j)}$ is part of the TCFT structure extending
the $\Ainf$ structure. The master equation for the \emph{total} TCFT
structure forces $\{m, B^{(j)}\}$ to be exact (a boundary in the
appropriate complex), and for the genus-$2$ component the only
contributions come from $m_2$ and $m_3$, which must therefore cancel.

Lesson: \emph{never} evaluate $\{m_k, B^{(j)}\}$ for individual $k$
and expect vanishing. The correct object is always the total $m$.
\end{observation}

\begin{observation}[Class M Borel summability]
\label{obs:class-m-borel}
For class $\mathbf{M}$ algebras (infinite shadow depth, Gevrey-$1$
divergent partition function), the question of resummability reduces
to the discriminant of the quartic Lax potential
$Q_L(\lambda) = \lambda^4 + \cdots$. The discriminant is
\[
 \mathrm{disc}(Q_L) = -256 \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^3 S_4
\]
where $S_4$ is the quartic shadow invariant. For all known CY examples,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} > 0$ and $S_4 > 0$, so $\mathrm{disc}(Q_L) < 0$.
Negative discriminant forces the branch points of $Q_L$ to be complex
conjugate, which means no Stokes wall on the positive real axis. This
is precisely the condition for Borel summability of the asymptotic
series. The physical interpretation: CY quantum groups of class
$\mathbf{M}$ have \emph{Borel-summable} partition functions, despite
the divergence of the perturbative expansion.
\end{observation}

\begin{observation}[Borcherds spectral flow: universality of $h = 1$]
\label{obs:borcherds-spectral}
For the BKM superalgebra of $K3 \times E$, the spectral flow
parameter $\varepsilon$ interpolates between the conformal weight
assignment $h_\varepsilon = (D + 1) - D\varepsilon$ where $D$ is the
discriminant. At $\varepsilon = 1$: $h_1 = 1$ for \emph{all}
discriminants $D$. This is the universal weight-$1$ current algebra
structure underlying the BKM: at the $\varepsilon = 1$ point, all
root spaces have the same conformal weight, and the algebra becomes
a (possibly infinite-rank) current algebra. The spectral flow from
$\varepsilon = 0$ (natural grading) to $\varepsilon = 1$ (uniform
grading) is the chiral-algebraic shadow of the automorphic
correction.
\end{observation}

\subsection{Key structural insights}
\label{subsec:key-insights}

\begin{observation}[The shadow tower IS the $\Ainf$ coproduct correction tower]
\label{obs:shadow-is-ainfty}
This is the deepest structural insight of the session. The shadow
invariants $S_k$ from Vol~I (which control the $k$-th order
obstruction to formality of the bar complex) are \emph{exactly} the
coefficients of the $\Ainf$ corrections to the Yangian coproduct:
\[
 \Delta^{\Ainf} = \Delta^{\mathrm{Yangian}}
 + \hbar^2 \delta^{(3)} + \hbar^3 \delta^{(4)} + \cdots
\]
where $\delta^{(k)}$ has coefficient $S_k$, the $k$-th shadow invariant.
\begin{itemize}
 \item Class $\mathbf{G}$ (Gaussian): all $S_k = 0$ for $k \geq 3$.
 The coproduct is exactly the Yangian coproduct. No $\Ainf$ corrections.
 \item Class $\mathbf{L}$ (Lemniscatic): $S_3 \neq 0$,
 $S_k = 0$ for $k \geq 4$. One correction.
 \item Class $\mathbf{C}$ (Clausen): finitely many nonzero $S_k$.
 Finitely many corrections.
 \item Class $\mathbf{M}$ (Mock): all $S_k \neq 0$. Infinitely many
 corrections. The coproduct is a genuinely $\Ainf$ object.
\end{itemize}
The identification is: the shadow tower \emph{is} the perturbative
expansion of the coproduct. The shadow depth \emph{is} the loop order
at which perturbation theory terminates.
\end{observation}

\begin{observation}[$L$-loop Feynman = shadow $S_{L+1}$]
\label{obs:feynman-shadow}
The shadow invariant $S_{L+1}$ controls the $L$-loop correction to
the partition function in the CY sigma model. Explicitly:
\begin{itemize}
 \item $S_3$ (cubic shadow) = $1$-loop correction = the leading
 $\alpha'$ correction in the sigma model.
 \item $S_4$ (quartic shadow) = $2$-loop correction.
 \item $S_k$ = $(k-2)$-loop correction.
\end{itemize}
Perturbation theory IS the shadow tower, read from bottom to top.
The class $\mathbf{G}$/$\mathbf{L}$/$\mathbf{C}$/$\mathbf{M}$
classification is the classification of sigma models by their
perturbative complexity.
\end{observation}

\begin{remark}[The K3 Yangian at generic moduli is ``boring'']
\label{rem:k3-boring-generic}
The K3 Yangian $Y(\fg_{K3})$ at a generic point of the K3 moduli
space is a product of $24$ commuting $\fgl_1$ Yangians: no interactions,
no interesting representation theory, no quantum group structure beyond
the abelian. \emph{All} interesting structure lives at special points:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item \textbf{ADE singularities}: at an $A_n$ singularity, the
 Yangian enhances to $Y(\fgl_1^{24-n} \times \widehat{\fsl}_{n+1})$.
 The non-abelian piece carries a genuine $R$-matrix.
 \item \textbf{BKM imaginary roots} ($D \geq 0$): these are the
 roots whose multiplicity is $24$ (by the constancy theorem) and
 whose Yangian generators do not have a standard Drinfeld
 presentation. They are responsible for the mock modular behaviour.
 \item \textbf{Orbifold points}: e.g., $T^4/\Z_2$, where the
 Kummer construction gives a computable model with 16 twisted sectors.
\end{enumerate}
The generic-moduli Yangian is the shadow of the fact that a generic
K3 surface has Picard rank 0: the lattice is there, but the geometry
does not ``see'' it. The enhancement at special points is the K3
analogue of symmetry enhancement at orbifold points of string compactifications.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The 6d theory is not a dimensional upgrade]
\label{rem:6d-not-upgrade}
The 6d holomorphic Chern--Simons theory is \emph{not} obtained by
replacing $3$ with $6$ in 3d CS. The structural fingerprint:
\begin{itemize}
 \item 3d hol CS $\to$ Kac--Moody: the Yang--Baxter equation (YBE)
 is satisfied. The $R$-matrix factorizes the $S$-matrix. The
 theory is \emph{integrable} in the sense of quantum groups.
 \item 5d hol CS $\to$ affine Yangian: the YBE is satisfied.
 Integrability persists.
 \item 6d hol theory $\to$ quantum toroidal: the Zamolodchikov
 tetrahedron equation (ZTE) \textbf{fails} at $O(\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^2)$. The
 naive factored $S_{ijk} = R_{ij} R_{ik} R_{jk}$ is \emph{not}
 consistent. This is a genuine $\Etwo \to \mathsf{E}_3$ obstruction.
\end{itemize}
The ZTE failure is the structural proof that the 6d theory is not
a ``higher'' version of the 3d/5d story but a genuinely new object.
The $\mathsf{E}_3$ content lives at the chain level and is destroyed
by formality (AP-CY33).
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Three wrong proofs beat three right abstractions]
\label{rem:wrong-proofs-valuable}
The three wrong proofs (Warnings~\ref{warn:dead-end-bidegree},
\ref{warn:dead-end-tsygan}, \ref{warn:dead-end-cyclic}) were
caught by \textbf{concrete computation} (direct matrix evaluation
at small dimension), not by abstract argument. The abstract proofs
were internally consistent and invoked real theorems; they failed
because they applied those theorems outside their domain of validity.
Lesson: in the $\Ainf$-chiral setting, the safest proof strategy
is to compute first (verify numerically at small rank/dimension),
then seek the abstract explanation. Abstract proofs that claim
vanishing should always be checked against a single nonzero example
before being trusted.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Obstructions to future progress}
\label{subsec:obstructions-future}

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
 \item \textbf{BKM imaginary root Yangian ($D \geq 0$)}: no Drinfeld
 presentation exists for any BKM superalgebra with imaginary simple
 roots. The Yangian $Y(\fg_{\mathrm{BKM}})$ is therefore not defined
 by generators and relations in the standard sense. A new formalism
 (possibly via the CoHA, possibly via factorization algebras on the
 Ran space of the BKM root lattice) is needed.

 \item \textbf{Explicit ZTE correction $T$}: the existence of a
 correction $R' = R + \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^2 R^{(2)} + \cdots$ satisfying the
 ZTE is proved (by obstruction theory: $\HH^{-2}_{\Eone} = 0$),
 but the explicit matrix $R^{(2)}$ has not been computed. The
 computation requires solving a system of $\binom{n}{3}$ equations
 in $n^6$ unknowns at each order.

 \item \textbf{Non-abelian K3 Yangian}: the off-diagonal $R$-matrix
 at ADE enhancement points is partially computed (the $A_1$ case
 gives $Y(\widehat{\fsl}_2)$, which is known). The general $A_n$
 case requires the Schiffmann--Vasserot shuffle algebra, which is
 available but not yet integrated into the framework.

 \item \textbf{Chiral volume conjecture}: the statement that the
 chiral partition function of $\cA_X$ computes a ``volume'' of the
 CY moduli space has not been formulated precisely. The analogy with
 the Kashaev--Murakami--Murakami volume conjecture for knot
 complements is suggestive but not yet a conjecture.

 \item \textbf{WRT invariant analogue for 6-manifolds}: the
 Witten--Reshetikhin--Turaev invariant is constructed from modular
 tensor categories (the output of 3d CS at root of unity). The
 6d analogue would require a ``modular $\mathsf{E}_3$-category''
 --- a braided monoidal $2$-category with a duality structure.
 Only dimensions $1$ and $2$ of the construction are available
 (Johnson-Freyd--Scheimbauer for $n$-categories).

 \item \textbf{Root-of-unity truncation of quantum toroidal}: the
 quantum toroidal algebra $U_{q,t}(\widehat{\widehat{\fgl}}_1)$ at
 generic $(q, t)$ is well-defined. At roots of unity ($q^N = 1$),
 the finite-dimensional quotient is \textbf{not} constructed.
 Unlike $U_q(\fg)$ where the Lusztig--De Concini quotient is
 standard, the toroidal case has no known finite-dimensional
 representation theory at roots of unity.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{The $[m_3, B^{(2)}]$ saga: a case study in agent epistemology}
\label{subsec:m3-B2-saga}

The question ``does $\{m_3, B^{(2)}\}$ vanish?'' was addressed by
$8$ agents across $3$ methodological families:

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item \textbf{Abstract algebra} ($3$ agents): argued ``yes'' by
 bidegree decomposition, Tsygan formality, and cyclic invariance.
 All three proofs were wrong (see Warnings~\ref{warn:dead-end-bidegree}--\ref{warn:dead-end-cyclic}).
 \item \textbf{Concrete computation} ($4$ agents): evaluated the
 bracket in dimensions $3, 4, 5, 6$ by direct matrix computation.
 Found $\{m_3, B^{(2)}\} \neq 0$ in all cases. Reported the
 nonvanishing with explicit counterexamples.
 \item \textbf{Operadic resolution} ($1$ agent): showed that
 $\{m_3, B^{(2)}\} \neq 0$ individually but
 $\{m_2 + m_3, B^{(2)}\} = 0$ as a total. The cross-degree
 cancellation is the correct statement.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent The truth required \emph{all three} perspectives:
\begin{itemize}
 \item The abstract agents identified the \emph{form} of the answer
 (something vanishes) but applied theorems outside their scope.
 \item The computational agents identified the \emph{obstruction}
 ($\{m_3, B^{(2)}\} \neq 0$) but could not see the cancellation.
 \item The operadic agent identified the \emph{mechanism}
 (cross-degree cancellation) that reconciles the other two.
\end{itemize}

\begin{remark}[Meta-lesson: adversarial agents are essential]
\label{rem:adversarial-essential}
The $3$ wrong proofs were caught because $4$ computational agents
independently ran the same bracket evaluation and found nonzero
answers. Without the adversarial agents, the wrong proofs would have
entered the manuscript as ``theorems''. The protocol of requiring
both abstract and computational verification for every vanishing
claim is load-bearing. In particular:
\begin{itemize}
 \item A vanishing claim from an abstract proof alone is
 \textbf{insufficient} unless confirmed by computation at small rank.
 \item A nonvanishing claim from computation alone is
 \textbf{insufficient} unless the question is correctly stated
 (the agents computed $\{m_3, B^{(2)}\}$, not $\{m, B^{(2)}\}$).
 \item The \emph{combination} of abstract + computational + operadic
 is what produces the correct theorem statement.
\end{itemize}
\end{remark}

\subsection{Convention bugs and silent propagation}
\label{subsec:convention-bugs}

\begin{remark}[The $\phi_{0,1}$ normalization and the $l=\pm1$ orbit]
\label{warn:phi01-normalization}
The weak Jacobi form $\phi_{0,1}(\tau, z)$ of weight $0$ and index $1$
has Fourier coefficients $c(n, \ell)$ depending on the convention.
In the Eichler--Zagier convention the discriminant coefficient is
$c(-1)=1$ for each of the two monomials $q^0\zeta^{\pm1}$.  The
combined orbit contribution from $\ell=\pm1$ is therefore $2$.  Some
physics normalisations record this orbit contribution as ``$c(-1)=2$'';
that is not the single Jacobi coefficient. This discrepancy propagates
silently through:
\begin{itemize}
 \item The BKM root multiplicity formula $c(nm - \ell^2)$.
 \item The denominator product $\Phi_{10}$.
 \item The shadow tower computation (the initial datum feeds the
 MC recursion).
 \item The $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ extraction.
\end{itemize}
The Borcherds product for $\Phi_{10}$ uses the orbit contribution when
both $\ell=\pm1$ terms are multiplied; root multiplicities still use the
single coefficient in the declared normalisation.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} + \kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}$ is not universal]
\label{warn:kbkm-universal}
The identity $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} +
\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}$ does not hold as a scoped invariant identity on
$K3 \times E$: the total-space value is
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E)=0$, while the apparent summand $2$ is
the K3-fibre Euler value. Evaluation against the $8$ orbifold families in
the toric landscape table also produces discrepancies. The
second-quantization factor $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} / \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$
is not a universal function of $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}$ alone; it depends
on the full BKM root-system structure.
\end{proposition}

\subsection{Structural insights for the six-dimensional programme}
\label{subsec:6d-structural}

\begin{observation}[The ZTE as a non-perturbative invariant]
\label{obs:zte-nonpert}
The Zamolodchikov tetrahedron equation failure at $O(\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^2)$ is
\emph{not} a failure of the theory; it is a \textbf{structural
invariant}. The coefficient $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = h_1 h_2 h_3$ (product of
Cartan parameters) measures the ``volume'' of the $3$-particle
phase space, and the ZTE obstruction is a cocycle in the deformation
complex of the $\mathsf{E}_3$-operad. The obstruction vanishes at
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 0$ (Kapranov--Voevodsky: the free $\mathsf{E}_3$-algebra
satisfies ZTE), and the nonvanishing at generic $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is the
chain-level content that formality destroys (AP-CY33).

The analogy: the YBE is the consistency condition for $2$-particle
scattering ($\mathsf{E}_2$). The ZTE is the consistency condition for
$3$-particle scattering ($\mathsf{E}_3$). The YBE is satisfied by the
Yang $R$-matrix; the ZTE is \emph{not} satisfied by the naive
factored $S$-operator. The passage from YBE to ZTE is the passage
from the braid group to the $2$-braid group, or equivalently from
braided monoidal categories to braided monoidal $2$-categories.
\end{observation}

\begin{observation}[Factored $\neq$ solved for higher coherence]
\label{obs:factored-not-solved}
The statement ``the $3$-particle $S$-operator factorizes as
$S_{ijk} = R_{ij} R_{ik} R_{jk}$'' is the \emph{definition} of
the factored $S$-operator, not a theorem. The theorem would be that
this factored $S$-operator satisfies the ZTE, which it does not.
The failure is at $O(\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^2)$ where $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = h_1 h_2 h_3$.

The lesson generalizes: for $\mathsf{E}_n$-algebras with $n \geq 3$,
pairwise consistency (YBE for all pairs) does \textbf{not} imply
higher-order consistency (ZTE for all triples, and higher analogues
for $n$-tuples). Each level of the $\mathsf{E}_n$-coherence tower
introduces new obstructions not controlled by the lower levels.
\end{observation}

\begin{remark}[The Miki automorphism is algebra-specific]
\label{rem:miki-algebra-specific}
The $S_3$-permutation symmetry of the quantum toroidal algebra
$U_{q,t}(\widehat{\widehat{\fgl}}_1)$, discovered by Miki, permutes
the three parameters $(q_1, q_2, q_3)$ with $q_1 q_2 q_3 = 1$.
This symmetry comes from the \emph{Weyl group of the CY torus}
(the torus $T^3$ whose character variety parametrizes the
$(q_1, q_2, q_3)$), not from the $\mathsf{E}_3$-operad in general.

Counterexample: the algebra $k[x]/(x^2)$ is $\mathsf{E}_3$
(indeed $\Einf$, being commutative) but has no Miki-type
automorphism. The Miki automorphism is a \emph{consequence} of the
specific algebraic structure of $U_{q,t}(\widehat{\widehat{\fgl}}_1)$,
not a general feature of $\mathsf{E}_3$-algebras. It is an accident
of the quantum toroidal algebra that the CY torus Weyl group coincides
with the $S_3$ that permutes the three directions of the
$\mathsf{E}_3$-operad.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The shadow class determines analytic type}
\label{subsec:shadow-analytic}

The correspondence between shadow class ($\mathbf{G}$/$\mathbf{L}$/%
$\mathbf{C}$/$\mathbf{M}$) and the analytic type of the quantum group
$r$-matrix, which emerged from the computational session, is:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}
\toprule
Class & Shadow depth & $r(z)$ type & Example \\
\midrule
$\mathbf{G}$ & 0 (formal) & polynomial & Free field \\
$\mathbf{L}$ & 2 (finite) & rational & $\C^3$ (rational Yangian) \\
$\mathbf{C}$ & finite & convergent & Compact CY3 (convergent series) \\
$\mathbf{M}$ & $\infty$ & Gevrey-$1$ divergent & $K3 \times E$ (mock modular) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent For class $\mathbf{M}$: the $r$-matrix is a formal power
series in $z$ with Gevrey-$1$ growth (coefficients grow as $n!$).
The Borel summability (Observation~\ref{obs:class-m-borel}) provides
a canonical analytic meaning. The Borel sum of $r(z)$ is the
``physical'' $R$-matrix; the formal series is the perturbative
expansion. The shadow tower controls the perturbative coefficients
(Observation~\ref{obs:feynman-shadow}).

\subsection{Research directions opened by the session}
\label{subsec:research-opened}

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
 \item \textbf{Compute the ZTE correction $R^{(2)}$ explicitly}:
 the existence is proved, but the matrix is not known. Even for
 $\fgl_1$ with $3$ particles ($8 \times 8$ matrices), the computation
 is nontrivial: $\binom{3}{3} = 1$ equation in $8^2 = 64$ unknowns,
 with the constraint that $R^{(2)}$ must be $S_3$-equivariant.

 \item \textbf{BKM imaginary root Yangian}: construct a Yangian-type
 algebra $Y(\fg_{\mathrm{BKM}})$ that incorporates the imaginary
 simple roots. The CoHA approach (Schiffmann--Vasserot) provides
 the multiplication; the coproduct requires the $\Eone$-chiral
 bialgebra framework.

 \item \textbf{Chiral volume conjecture}: formulate the precise
 statement relating $\mathrm{Vol}(\cM_X)$ to
 $\lim_{q \to 1} Z_{\mathrm{chiral}}(q)$ for CY3 $X$. The
 analogy with the Kashaev volume conjecture suggests looking at
 the asymptotics of the chiral partition function at roots of unity.

 \item \textbf{Matrix model for the shadow genus expansion}:
 the shadow invariants $S_k$ are moments of a (conjectural) matrix
 model measure $\mu_{\mathrm{shadow}}$. If $\mu_{\mathrm{shadow}}$
 exists, the $1/N$ expansion of the matrix model reproduces the
 shadow tower. The discriminant condition
 $\mathrm{disc}(Q_L) < 0$ (Observation~\ref{obs:class-m-borel})
 constrains the support of $\mu_{\mathrm{shadow}}$.

 \item \textbf{The $\Ainf$ coproduct for compact CY3}: the
 factorization-homology coproduct (from Ran space excision) is
 formulated for general CY, not just toric. Verify agreement with
 the Miura coproduct for the toric cases where both are available.
 The compact cases (quintic, complete intersections) have no Miura
 factorization and the factorization-homology coproduct is the
 only available construction.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Terminology and notation stabilized in this session}
\label{subsec:terminology-stabilized}

\begin{itemize}
 \item \textbf{Spectral $z$ vs worldsheet $z$}: resolved by
 Remark~\ref{rem:k3-boring-generic}. The Drinfeld coproduct
 $\Delta_z$ uses a \emph{Yangian spectral parameter} (shift of the
 transfer matrix argument $u \to u - z$). The vertex algebra OPE
 $T(z) T(w) \sim \cdots$ uses a \emph{worldsheet insertion
 coordinate}. These are different objects. Setting $z = 0$ in
 $\Delta_z$ removes the spectral shift (cocommutative coproduct);
 setting $z \to w$ in the OPE produces poles. The ``$z = 0$
 singularity'' objection (raised by adversarial agents) is a
 category error.

 \item \textbf{Ordered}: always qualified. ``Labeled-ordered''
 (combinatorial, the $\Eone$ ordered bar $B^{\mathrm{ord}}$) vs
 ``time-ordered'' (analytic, radial ordering in the OPE) vs
 ``normally-ordered'' (Wick). Bare ``ordered'' is forbidden per AP152.

 \item \textbf{Factorization $\otimes$}: the $\Eone$-factorization
 tensor product $A \otimes_{\Eone} B = \mathrm{colim}_{z_1 < z_2}
 A(z_1) \otimes A(z_2)$. Not symmetric (ordering matters). Strictly
 associative (ordered configuration space is contractible). The
 naive Kronecker product $\otimes_k$ is the $\Einf$ quotient, which
 kills the quantum group structure.
\end{itemize}
