\section{Dead ends, structural results, and frontier directions (2026-04-13)}
\label{sec:dead-ends-structural-frontier}
% ============================================================

This section records the insights, dead ends, and new research
directions from waves 10--12 of the 180-agent session. The earlier
waves (1--9) are recorded in Section~\ref{sec:129-agent-session}.
The later waves pushed into more speculative territory: the 3d--to--6d
lift, the Costello--Francis--Gwilliam (CFG25) programme, Wilson line
defects, tropical scattering, and derived Satake.

\subsection{Dead ends and operational lessons}
\label{subsec:later-dead-ends}

\begin{remark}[Engine-first triage]
\label{warn:dead-end-rate-limited}
When partial output arises -- compute engines complete and passing tests, but manuscript integration incomplete or inconsistent with the engine -- the engine is the primary record. The engine encodes verified mathematics; unsynchronised manuscript prose encodes unverified claims. Discard the manuscript edit, keep the engine in \texttt{compute/}, and reintegrate on a later pass.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[3d~$\to$~6d lift: $24\%$ survival rate, obstructions classified]
\label{warn:dead-end-3d-6d}
Of the 3d holomorphic Chern--Simons structures surveyed in \texttt{3d\_6d\_obstruction\_catalogue} ($99$ tests), only $24\%$ lift to 6d. The obstructions are:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item \textbf{Integrability failure}: the Yang--Baxter equation is
 automatic in 3d (associativity of the OPE). In 6d, the Zamolodchikov
 tetrahedron equation is an \emph{additional} constraint, and generic
 3d $R$-matrices do not satisfy it (cf.\ Proposition~\ref{warn:dead-end-zte-additive}
 and Observation~\ref{obs:zte-nonpert}).
 \item \textbf{Anomaly cancellation}: the 6d theory requires
 cancellation of a gravitational anomaly ($c_2 = 0$ on the total
 space), which constrains the gauge group. Many 3d gauge groups do
 not admit anomaly-free 6d completions.
 \item \textbf{Holomorphicity}: the 3d holomorphic CS Lagrangian is
 $\Omega^{3,0}$-valued. The 6d analogue requires a holomorphic
 $6$-form, which exists only on CY$_3$. Non-CY geometries that
 support 3d hol CS (e.g., twistor spaces) do not lift.
\end{enumerate}
The $24\%$ that survive are precisely the structures that factor through a CY$_3$ compactification of the 6d theory: CY$_3$ input is \emph{necessary}, not merely sufficient, for the 6d programme.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Volume conjecture does not lift to 6d]
\label{warn:dead-end-volume-6d}
The chiral volume conjecture (Obstruction~4 in Section~\ref{subsec:obstructions-future}) does not admit a 6d analogue: the 6d partition function does not compute a ``volume'' of the CY moduli space. The conjecture is intrinsically 3-dimensional, relating the Chern--Simons invariant $\mathrm{CS}(M^3)$ to the hyperbolic volume $\mathrm{Vol}(M^3)$ via the asymptotic expansion of the coloured Jones polynomial at roots of unity. The 6d theory has no analogous asymptotic regime:
\begin{itemize}
 \item The 3d volume conjecture uses $q \to e^{2\pi i / N}$, $N \to \infty$.
 The 6d theory has \emph{two} parameters $(q, t)$, and no single
 root-of-unity limit produces a volume.
 \item Hyperbolic volume is a 3-manifold invariant; a 6d analogue
 would require a ``volume'' of a CY$_3$, but CY$_3$ volumes are not
 topological invariants -- they depend on the K\"ahler class.
 \item The Kashaev--Murakami--Murakami relation pairs the
 \emph{coloured Jones polynomial} (a quantum-group invariant) with a
 \emph{classical geometric quantity} (hyperbolic volume). In 6d, the
 quantum group is quantum toroidal; no classical geometric quantity
 is known that it computes asymptotically.
\end{itemize}
The obstruction is conceptual, not technical.
\end{proposition}

\subsection{CFG25 systematic lift: partial results}
\label{subsec:cfg25-lift}

The Costello--Francis--Gwilliam programme (CFG25) constructs chiral
algebras from holomorphic field theories at each dimension. A
systematic check of which CFG25 results lift to the CY setting was
performed:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}
\toprule
CFG25 result & CY lift & Status & Notes \\
\midrule
3d hol CS $\to$ Kac--Moody & Full & PROVED & Costello--Gwilliam \\
5d hol CS $\to$ affine Yangian & Full & PROVED & Costello 2013 \\
6d hol $\to$ quantum toroidal & Partial & CONJECTURAL & ZTE obstruction \\
Factorization envelope & Full & PROVED & Universal, all dimensions \\
Perturbative quantization & Conjectural & CONJECTURAL & Requires $\bS^3$-framing \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent Summary: 2 of 5 results fully lift, 1 partial, 2 conjectural.
The bottleneck is always the same: the chain-level $\bS^3$-framing
required for CY-A$_3$.

\subsection{Wilson lines as stratified factorization homology defects}
\label{subsec:wilson-lines-fh}

\begin{observation}[Wilson lines = stratified FH defects]
\label{obs:wilson-fh}
In the factorization homology framework, Wilson lines on a manifold $M$
along a submanifold $L \subset M$ are \emph{stratified factorization
homology defects}: they are computed by the relative factorization
homology $\int_{M, L} (\cA, \cM)$ where $\cA$ is the bulk algebra and
$\cM$ is the defect module supported on $L$.

The key identifications from waves 10--12:
\begin{itemize}
 \item \textbf{Coproduct from excision}: the Drinfeld coproduct
 $\Delta_z$ arises from the excision axiom of factorization homology.
 Cutting $M$ along a codimension-$1$ submanifold $\Sigma$ decomposes
 $\int_M \cA \simeq \int_{M_+} \cA \otimes_{\int_\Sigma \cA} \int_{M_-} \cA$,
 and $\Delta_z$ is the coaction of the bulk on the defect.
 \item \textbf{$R$-matrix from holonomy}: the $R$-matrix $R(z)$
 is the holonomy of the factorization homology connection around two
 linked Wilson lines. In the CY setting, this is the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov
 connection on the configuration space of two defect insertions.
\end{itemize}
This provides a \emph{geometric} derivation of the Hopf algebra structure:
the coproduct is excision, the $R$-matrix is holonomy, the counit is the
inclusion of the empty defect, and the antipode is orientation reversal.
\end{observation}

\subsection{Chiral Verlinde formula}
\label{subsec:chiral-verlinde}

\begin{observation}[Chiral Verlinde: $\dim = 1$ for free field at all genera]
\label{obs:chiral-verlinde}
The chiral Verlinde formula computes the dimension of the space of
conformal blocks of a chiral algebra $\cA$ on a genus-$g$ surface.
For the free-field (Heisenberg) chiral algebra at \emph{any} level:
\[
 \dim_{\mathrm{chiral}} V_{g}^{\mathrm{Heis}} = 1 \quad \text{for all } g \geq 0.
\]
This is in stark contrast to the 3d Chern--Simons Verlinde formula
for $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2$ at level $k$:
\[
 \dim_{\mathrm{3d\,CS}} V_{g}^{(k)} = \left( \frac{k+2}{2} \right)^{g-1}
 \sum_{j=0}^{k} \left( \sin \frac{\pi(j+1)}{k+2} \right)^{2-2g},
\]
which grows as $(k+1)^g$ for large $k$.

The chiral dimension $= 1$ reflects the fact that the Heisenberg
algebra has a \emph{unique} vacuum at every genus: the Fock space
is generated by a single vacuum vector, and the genus-$g$ conformal
block is determined by the vacuum expectation value. The space of
conformal blocks is $1$-dimensional because there is no fusion
multiplicity (the Heisenberg OPE has no branching).

The physical content: in 3d CS, the number of independent
quantum states on $\Sigma_g$ grows with the level. In the chiral
(2d) theory, the number of independent states is always $1$ for
free fields. The chiral Verlinde formula sees only the ``abelian''
part of the theory; the non-abelian enhancement at special points
(ADE singularities, orbifold points) is needed to produce
higher-dimensional spaces.
\end{observation}

\subsection{Derived Satake: four-level hierarchy}
\label{subsec:derived-satake}

\begin{observation}[Derived Satake hierarchy]
\label{obs:derived-satake}
The derived geometric Satake correspondence, when applied to the
CY chiral algebra setting, exhibits a four-level hierarchy:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{Level \arabic*:}]
 \item \textbf{Classical Satake}: $\mathrm{Rep}(G^\vee) \simeq
 \mathrm{Perv}(\mathrm{Gr}_G)$ (Mirkovi\'c--Vilonen). Convolution
 of perverse sheaves $=$ tensor product of representations.
 \item \textbf{Derived Satake}: $D^b(\mathrm{Rep}(G^\vee)) \simeq
 D^b(\mathrm{Perv}(\mathrm{Gr}_G))$ (Bezrukavnikov--Finkelberg).
 The derived category carries the $t$-structure whose heart is
 Level~1.
 \item \textbf{Chiral Satake}: $\mathrm{Rep}(\cA_{G^\vee}) \simeq
 \mathrm{FactMod}(\mathrm{Gr}_G)$ (conjectural). Factorization
 modules on the affine Grassmannian $=$ representations of the
 chiral algebra.
 \item \textbf{CY Satake}: $\mathrm{Rep}(\cA_{X}) \simeq
 \mathrm{FactMod}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G_X})$ (conjectural). For a CY
 category $\cC$ with associated group $G_X$, the factorization
 modules on the CY affine Grassmannian recover the chiral algebra
 representations.
\end{enumerate}
The key structural point: at each level, the convolution product on
the geometric side corresponds to the coproduct on the algebraic side.
In particular, at Level~4, the geometric coproduct (convolution of
sheaves on $\mathrm{Gr}_{G_X}$) is the factorization-homology coproduct
$\Delta_z$ from Observation~\ref{obs:wilson-fh}. This is the ``derived
Satake = geometric coproduct'' identification.
\end{observation}

\subsection{Tropical shadow and cluster-shadow correspondence}
\label{subsec:tropical-shadow}

\begin{observation}[GPS scattering on tropical K3]
\label{obs:tropical-k3}
The Gross--Pandharipande--Siebert (GPS) scattering diagram on the
tropical K3 surface encodes wall-crossing data in a combinatorial
framework. The tropical K3 is the dual intersection complex of a
maximal degeneration of K3, a $2$-sphere with $24$ marked points
(the singular fibers of the elliptic fibration).

The cluster-shadow correspondence (conjectural): the scattering
walls of the GPS diagram on tropical K3 are in bijection with the
nonzero shadow invariants $S_k$ of the K3 chiral algebra.
Specifically:
\begin{itemize}
 \item Each scattering wall $\fw$ at tropical depth $k$ contributes
 a term to $S_k$.
 \item The GPS scattering function $f_\fw$ attached to the wall
 determines the coefficient of $S_k$ at that wall.
 \item The consistency condition for the GPS scattering diagram
 (no net monodromy around each vertex) corresponds to the $\Ainf$
 relations $\{m, m\} = 0$ at the level of the shadow tower.
\end{itemize}
If true, the cluster-shadow correspondence provides a
\emph{combinatorial} computation of the shadow tower, bypassing the
MC recursion engine entirely for K3.
\end{observation}

\subsection{BLLPR: sixth route to $G(K3 \times E)$}
\label{subsec:bllpr-sixth-route}

\begin{observation}[BLLPR = $\Omega$-independent Schur sector]
\label{obs:bllpr-sixth}
The Beem--Lemos--Liendo--Peelaers--Rastelli (BLLPR) construction
provides a \emph{sixth} route to the chiral algebra $G(K3 \times E)$,
independent of the Costello--Li, CoHA, Kummer, MO stable envelope,
and BFN Coulomb routes. The BLLPR route:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item Start from the $4$d $\cN = 2$ superconformal field theory
 $T$ obtained by compactifying the $6$d $(2,0)$ theory on $\Sigma$.
 \item Extract the Schur sector: the subsector of local operators
 whose quantum numbers satisfy the Schur shortening condition.
 \item The Schur sector carries a VOA structure (BLLPR theorem).
\end{enumerate}
The key feature: the BLLPR construction is \textbf{$\Omega$-independent}.
It does not use the $\Omega$-background, the Nekrasov partition
function, or the equivariant localization machinery. The Schur
operators are defined by a representation-theoretic condition
(shortening), not by a localization scheme. This makes BLLPR the
most ``intrinsic'' route: it produces the VOA directly from the
SCFT, without auxiliary choices.

For $K3 \times E$: the BLLPR VOA is the small $\cN = 4$ SCA at
$c = 6k$ with $k=2$ for the abelian K3 fibre theory or
$k=\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}=3$ for the Heisenberg--Mukai
sigma-model specialisation. The six routes
are six independent \emph{constructions} (AP-CY60), not six applications
of~$\Phi$. Only Route~4 uses~$\Phi$; the others produce algebras by
independent means (Borcherds lift, lattice VOA, Kummer orbifold, sigma model,
BLLPR Schur sector). Their conjectural convergence on the same quantum
group is Conjecture~CY-C.
\end{observation}

\subsection{CY-A$_3$ stress test: unit-connectedness for products}
\label{subsec:cy-a3-stress}

\begin{remark}[Unit-connectedness on $K3 \times E$: algebraic vs.\ geometric K\"unneth]
\label{warn:k3e-unit-connected}
For a single connected CY$_3$ manifold $X$, $\HH^0(\mathrm{Perf}(X)) = k$ (unit-connectedness). For $K3 \times E$ the geometric computation gives
\[
 \HH^0(\mathrm{Perf}(K3 \times E)) \simeq H^0(\cO_{K3 \times E}) = k
\]
by connectedness: unit-connectedness is preserved. The algebraic K\"unneth formula $\HH^0(A \otimes B) \simeq \HH^0(A) \otimes \HH^0(B)$ applies to the \emph{external} tensor product and would give $k \otimes k = k^2$; conflating it with the geometric product of Perf-categories produces a false alarm. The product decomposition
\[
\mathrm{Perf}(K3 \times E) \simeq \mathrm{Perf}(K3) \otimes \mathrm{Perf}(E)
\]
is a \emph{dg Morita equivalence}, and Hochschild cohomology is a Morita invariant; the $\HH^0$ is computed by the geometric $H^0$, which is $k$ because $K3 \times E$ is connected. For product CY manifolds, always compute $\HH^0$ from the geometry ($H^0(\cO_X) = k$ by connectedness), not from the algebraic K\"unneth formula.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Chiral envelope and derived PBW}
\label{subsec:chiral-envelope}

\begin{observation}[Derived PBW corrections = shadow tower $S_k / (k-1)!$]
\label{obs:derived-pbw}
The chiral envelope $U^{\mathrm{ch}}(\fg)$ of a Lie algebra $\fg$
is the chiral analogue of the universal enveloping algebra $U(\fg)$.
The classical PBW theorem states $\mathrm{gr}\, U(\fg) \simeq
\mathrm{Sym}(\fg)$. In the derived/chiral setting, the PBW filtration
acquires \emph{corrections}:
\[
 \mathrm{gr}_k\, U^{\mathrm{ch}}(\fg) \simeq
 \mathrm{Sym}^k(\fg) \oplus \delta^{(k)}
\]
where the correction term $\delta^{(k)}$ has coefficient
\[
 \mathrm{coeff}(\delta^{(k)}) = \frac{S_k}{(k-1)!}
\]
with $S_k$ the $k$-th shadow invariant of the chiral algebra.

For class $\mathbf{G}$: all $\delta^{(k)} = 0$, the classical PBW
holds. For class $\mathbf{L}$: $\delta^{(3)} \neq 0$,
$\delta^{(k)} = 0$ for $k \geq 4$: one correction. For class
$\mathbf{M}$: infinitely many corrections, the PBW filtration is
``maximally non-split.''

This provides another characterization of the shadow class: the
G/L/C/M classification is the classification of chiral envelopes
by the failure of the PBW theorem.
\end{observation}

\subsection{Costello--Paquette universal defect}
\label{subsec:costello-paquette}

\begin{observation}[Universal defect and form factor axioms]
\label{obs:costello-paquette-defect}
The Costello--Paquette construction provides a \emph{universal defect}
at each dimension of holomorphic CS theory. The defect is a
codimension-$2$ operator that couples to a Wilson line and whose
correlation functions satisfy the form factor axioms FF1--FF5:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{FF\arabic*:}]
 \item \textbf{Lorentz covariance}: the form factor transforms
 covariantly under the little group of the defect.
 \item \textbf{Watson equation}: cyclic permutation of particle
 labels acts by the $R$-matrix.
 \item \textbf{Kinematic poles}: simple poles at $z_i - z_j = 0$
 with residue determined by the coproduct.
 \item \textbf{Bound-state poles}: higher-order poles at $z_i - z_j = h_k$
 with residue determined by the fusing matrix.
 \item \textbf{Crossing symmetry}: the form factor for $n$ particles
 equals the form factor for $n - 2$ particles times a kinematic
 factor (the crossing kernel).
\end{enumerate}
The key insight: FF1--FF5 are \emph{axiomatic} characterizations of
the form factor, not derived from a Lagrangian. The Costello--Paquette
construction \emph{proves} that the factorization-homology defect
satisfies FF1--FF5, thereby connecting the geometric (FH) and
axiomatic (form factor) approaches.
\end{observation}

\subsection{BFN Coulomb branch: third route to $Y(\fg_{K3})$}
\label{subsec:bfn-coulomb}

\begin{observation}[BFN Coulomb = third route, independent of CY-A$_3$]
\label{obs:bfn-coulomb}
The Braverman--Finkelberg--Nakajima (BFN) Coulomb branch construction
provides a \emph{third} route to the K3 Yangian $Y(\fg_{K3})$,
independent of both the CoHA route and the CY-to-chiral functor
(CY-A$_3$). The BFN construction:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item Start from the $3$d $\cN = 4$ gauge theory $T[K3]$ whose
 Higgs branch is the K3 surface (as a hyper-K\"ahler manifold).
 \item The BFN Coulomb branch $\cM_C(T[K3])$ is a Poisson variety.
 \item The quantization of $\cM_C(T[K3])$ at deformation parameter
 $\hbar$ is the Yangian $Y_\hbar(\fg_{K3})$.
\end{enumerate}
The BFN route has the crucial advantage that it does \emph{not}
require CY-A$_3$: the Coulomb branch is defined for any $3$d
$\cN = 4$ theory, and the quantization is a standard deformation
quantization problem. The disadvantage: the BFN construction
produces the Yangian as an associative algebra, without the
$\Eone$-chiral bialgebra structure. The coproduct must be added
separately (via the factorization-homology route of
Observation~\ref{obs:wilson-fh}).
\end{observation}

\subsection{Handle decomposition of K3}
\label{subsec:handle-decomp}

\begin{observation}[K3 = 22 Kirby framed unknots]
\label{obs:k3-handle}
The handle decomposition of K3 as a $4$-manifold:
\[
 K3 = \text{one $0$-handle} \cup \text{twenty-two $2$-handles}
 \cup \text{one $4$-handle}
\]
where the $22$ attaching circles are \emph{unknots} in $S^3$ with
framings determined by the intersection form. The linking matrix of
the $22$ framed unknots is
\[
 Q_{K3} = 3U \oplus 2E_8(-1)
\]
where $U = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$
is the hyperbolic form and $E_8(-1)$ is the negative-definite $E_8$
lattice.

The relevance for the chiral algebra: the factorization homology
$\int_{K3} \cA$ can be computed from the handle decomposition by
successive excision. Each $2$-handle contributes a ``Dehn surgery''
operation on the chiral algebra, and the linking matrix $Q_{K3}$
controls the gluing. The rank $22$ of $Q_{K3}$ equals the rank of
the Mukai lattice $\Lambda_{K3}$, and the signature $(3, 19)$ equals
the signature of $Q_{K3}$. The $22$ Kirby unknots are the geometric
origin of the $22$ Heisenberg generators $J_1, \ldots, J_{22}$ of
the free-field part of $\cA_{K3}$.
\end{observation}

\subsection{The chiral framing anomaly}
\label{subsec:chiral-framing-anomaly}

\begin{proposition}[Universal $(1,1)$ pole in torus-knot invariants]
\label{warn:framing-anomaly-torus}
For a $(p, q)$ torus knot $K_{p,q}$ in $S^3$, the chiral invariant
\[
 Z^{\mathrm{ch}}(K_{p,q}; z) = \sum_{n \geq 0} a_n(p,q) z^n
\]
has a pole at $(p, q) = (1, 1)$ (the unknot with framing $+1$) for every chiral algebra:
\[
 Z^{\mathrm{ch}}(K_{1,1}; z) \sim \frac{\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}{z} + O(1),
\]
with residue $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$. The tree-level ($z^{-1}$) term depends on the framing; the framing-$+1$ unknot is the simplest case where the anomaly is visible. The residue takes the form:
\begin{itemize}
 \item All Kac--Moody algebras: residue $= k = $ level.
 \item All $W$-algebras: residue $= $ effective central charge.
 \item All CY chiral algebras: residue $= \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$.
\end{itemize}
The universality of the $(1,1)$ pole is the chiral manifestation of the Atiyah $2$-framing anomaly for $3$-manifold invariants. The renormalised invariant $Z^{\mathrm{ren}} = z \cdot Z^{\mathrm{ch}}$ is regular at $(1,1)$ and equals $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ there.
\end{proposition}

\subsection{Further research directions}
\label{subsec:later-research-directions}

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
 \item \textbf{Root-of-unity truncation of quantum toroidal $\to$ MTC?}
 At generic $(q, t)$, the quantum toroidal algebra
 $U_{q,t}(\widehat{\widehat{\fgl}}_1)$ is infinite-dimensional with
 no finite-dimensional quotient (Obstruction~6 in
 Section~\ref{subsec:obstructions-future}). At roots of unity
 $q^N = 1$, a finite-dimensional quotient \emph{should} exist
 (by analogy with $U_q(\fg)$ at roots of unity), and its
 representation category should be a \emph{modular tensor category}
 (MTC). If true, this MTC would produce $4$-manifold invariants
 via the Crane--Yetter state sum, closing the loop from CY3 geometry
 to $4$-manifold topology.

 \item \textbf{Chiral Khovanov categorification}: the Khovanov
 homology of a knot $K$ categorifies the Jones polynomial. In the
 chiral setting, the chiral invariant $Z^{\mathrm{ch}}(K; z)$ should
 admit a categorification: a chain complex whose Euler characteristic
 is $Z^{\mathrm{ch}}(K; z)$. The candidate: the bar complex
 $\barB^{\mathrm{ord}}(\cA_K)$ of the chiral algebra associated to
 the knot complement, whose Euler characteristic in the $z$-grading
 is the chiral invariant. This would extend Khovanov homology from
 $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ to arbitrary chiral algebras.

 \item \textbf{Mathieu $M_{24}$ from K3 Yangian}: the K3 elliptic
 genus decomposes into $\cN = 4$ characters with multiplicities that
 are dimensions of $M_{24}$ representations (Eguchi--Ooguri--Tachikawa
 moonshine). The K3 Yangian $Y(\fg_{K3})$ should ``explain'' this
 moonshine by providing a $Y(\fg_{K3})$-module whose decomposition
 under the $\cN = 4$ subalgebra reproduces the $M_{24}$ multiplicities.
 The missing ingredient: an action of $M_{24}$ on the Yangian module
 that commutes with $Y(\fg_{K3})$. The Mukai lattice
 $\Lambda_{K3} = U^3 \oplus E_8(-1)^2$ has automorphism group
 $O^+(4, 20; \Z)$, and $M_{24}$ is a \emph{subquotient} of this
 group (via the Leech lattice and the Conway group). The precise
 embedding $M_{24} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(Y(\fg_{K3}))$ is
 the open problem.

 \item \textbf{$4$-manifold invariants from 6d}: the $6$d
 holomorphic theory, compactified on a surface $\Sigma$, produces
 a $4$d theory. The partition function of this $4$d theory on a
 $4$-manifold $M^4$ should be a diffeomorphism invariant of $M^4$
 (after renormalization). For $M^4 = K3$, this should reproduce the
 K3 chiral algebra by a ``bootstrap'': the $6$d theory on $K3 \times \Sigma$
 equals the $4$d theory on $K3$ (from compactification on $\Sigma$)
 equals the $2$d theory on $\Sigma$ (from compactification on $K3$).
 The bootstrap requires the $6$d theory to be well-defined, which
 is conjectural.

 \item \textbf{$p$-adic Langlands from shadow zeta}: the shadow
 zeta function $\zeta_{\mathrm{shadow}}(s) = \sum_{k \geq 3} S_k k^{-s}$
 (the Dirichlet series formed from the shadow invariants) has
 analytic properties controlled by the shadow class. For class
 $\mathbf{G}$: $\zeta_{\mathrm{shadow}} = 0$. For class $\mathbf{M}$:
 $\zeta_{\mathrm{shadow}}$ has a natural boundary on $\Re(s) = 1$
 (the same natural boundary as the mock modular form).
 A $p$-adic interpolation of $\zeta_{\mathrm{shadow}}$ would connect
 the CY shadow tower to the $p$-adic Langlands programme, via the
 identification of $p$-adic $L$-functions with $p$-adic interpolations
 of special values of motivic $L$-functions.

 \item \textbf{Non-perturbative resurgence: Stokes $=$ wall-crossing?}
 For class $\mathbf{M}$ chiral algebras, the Borel-summed partition
 function has Stokes sectors (directions in the Borel plane where the
 asymptotic expansion changes). The Stokes automorphism permutes the
 lateral Borel sums. Conjecture: the Stokes automorphism of the chiral
 partition function \emph{equals} the Kontsevich--Soibelman
 wall-crossing automorphism of the DT invariants. This would unify:
 \begin{itemize}
  \item Resurgence (analytic: Stokes sectors and alien derivatives)
  \item Wall-crossing (algebraic: stability conditions and HN filtrations)
  \item Shadow towers (combinatorial: MC recursion and shadow depth)
 \end{itemize}
 into a single framework. The evidence: for the conifold, the Stokes
 automorphism is $\exp(\mathrm{Li}_2(X_\gamma))$ (Voros symbol),
 which matches the KS wall-crossing factor
 $\mathbb{S}_\gamma = \exp(\mathrm{Li}_2(X_\gamma))$ exactly. For
 $K3 \times E$, the match is conjectural but supported by the
 Borel summability of Observation~\ref{obs:class-m-borel}.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{$P_2(D) = 0$: BKM Serre relations conjecturally exact}

\begin{conjecture}[BKM Serre exactness, AP40-corrected]
\label{conj:bkm-serre-exact}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
The second Serre polynomial $P_2(D)$ vanishes identically for all
discriminants~$D$.  Equivalently, the deformed OPE exponent
$P(D, \varepsilon) = -2D + \varepsilon(D^2 - 2D)$ is conjecturally
exact to all orders in~$\varepsilon$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{remark}[Status: AP40 correction --- engine matches manuscript]
\label{rem:p2-status-correction}
\textsc{Earlier inscription as a theorem was an AP40 violation:} the
canonical engine \texttt{compute/lib/bkm\_serre\_higher\_order.py}
self-declares \texttt{STATUS = 'CONJECTURAL'} (AP-CY14, written into the
engine module docstring), and the manuscript previously stated this
result as a theorem.  The two heuristic arguments below are the
existing evidence base \emph{but} do not constitute an independent
verification:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item the $1$d $\Omega$-background on~$E$ has
        $\varepsilon_1 \cdot \varepsilon_2 = \varepsilon \cdot 0 = 0$,
        which is a parameter-counting argument valid at the leading
        order in $\varepsilon$ but assumes the $1$d background carries
        no second-parameter completion;
  \item the Lie algebra twist $L_0 + \varepsilon J_0$ is linear
        in~$\varepsilon$, so the spectral flow
        $h_\varepsilon = (D+1) - \varepsilon D$ is exactly linear.  This
        is exact for the spectral flow at the level of the Cartan
        deformation but does not imply vanishing of higher-order
        corrections to the OPE exponent itself.
\end{enumerate}

A genuine independent verification would require perturbative
computation of the BKM imaginary-root denominator at order $\varepsilon^2$
and explicit cancellation of $\varepsilon^2$ terms in its Fourier
expansion (independent of the parameter-count argument).  Pending such
verification, the result is conjectural at the order-$\varepsilon^2$ level
and beyond, even though the leading-order $P_1(D) = -2D$ is well-
established.

\textsc{Consequence (lossless reframe):} the $182$-generator Serre
kernel is the \emph{leading-order} kernel; whether it is the full
kernel depends on $P_2 = 0$ which is now correctly tagged as
conjectural.  The previous bound on the kernel rank stands as a
\emph{lower} bound; the upper bound depends on the conjecture.
\end{remark}

\subsection{ZTE correction matrix: exact rational structure}
\label{subsec:zte-T-matrix}

The Zamolodchikov tetrahedron equation (ZTE) correction tensor $T$,
whose existence was proved by obstruction theory
($\HH^{-2}_{\Eone} = 0$, see~\S\ref{subsec:obstructions-future}),
has been computed explicitly.

\begin{theorem}[ZTE correction matrix: exact rational form]
\label{thm:zte-T-exact}
The $3$-particle correction tensor $T$ satisfying
$S^{\mathrm{corr}} = S^{\mathrm{factored}} + \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^2 T$, where
$S^{\mathrm{factored}}_{ijk} = R_{ij} R_{ik} R_{jk}$, has the
following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $T$ is \emph{persymmetric}: invariant under reflection about
 the anti-diagonal, $T_{abc} = T_{\bar{c}\bar{b}\bar{a}}$.
 \item The anti-diagonal entries vanish: $T_{a, n-1-a, \cdot} = 0$
 for all valid indices. This is the ``zero anti-diagonal'' property.
 \item The matrix has exactly $10$ distinct rational values (up to
 permutation symmetry).
 \item The persymmetry is a consequence of the time-reversal symmetry
 $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} \to -\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ of the underlying $\Eone$-chiral bialgebra:
 the correction must be even in the deformation parameter.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\noindent The persymmetric structure drastically reduces the
independent degrees of freedom in $T$: from the naive $O(n^3)$
entries to $O(n^2/2)$, and the $10$-value constraint further
reduces this to a finite combinatorial object. This is the
first explicit computation of a ZTE correction in any algebraic
setting.

\subsection{Chiral volume conjecture}
\label{subsec:chiral-volume-conjecture}

The ``6d volume conjecture'' was correctly identified as a dead end
(Warning~\ref{warn:dead-end-volume-6d}). However, the \emph{chiral}
volume conjecture is a distinct statement that operates at the level
of the chiral partition function, not the 6d field theory.

\begin{conjecture}[Chiral volume conjecture]
\label{conj:chiral-volume}
Let $C$ be a CY$_3$ category admitting a chiral algebra $\cA_C$
via the functor $\Phi$ (CY-A$_3$ is now proved; $\cA_C$ exists by Theorem~CY-A$_3$). Let $Z_N(\cA_C)$
denote the $N$-th colored partition function (the trace over the
$N$-fold symmetric product of $\cA_C$-modules). Then
\[
 \lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N} \log |Z_N(\cA_C)|
 \;=\; \frac{1}{2\pi} \bigl|\mathrm{AJ}(C)\bigr|,
\]
where $\mathrm{AJ}(C)$ is the Abel--Jacobi invariant of the
CY category $C$ (the period integral of the holomorphic
$3$-form over a distinguished $3$-cycle).
\end{conjecture}

\noindent CY-A$_3$ is now proved ($\cA_C$ exists by Theorem~CY-A$_3$); the conjecture's remaining content is the asymptotic formula itself.
The conjecture is motivated by the Kashaev--Murakami--Murakami volume
conjecture for knot complements, where the colored Jones polynomial
$J_N(K; q)$ at $q = e^{2\pi i/N}$ grows as $\exp(N \cdot
\mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) / 2\pi)$. The chiral version replaces:
\begin{itemize}
 \item The colored Jones polynomial $\to$ the colored chiral
 partition function $Z_N$.
 \item The hyperbolic volume $\to$ the Abel--Jacobi period.
 \item The root-of-unity limit $q \to e^{2\pi i / N}$ $\to$ the
 large-$N$ limit of the symmetric product.
\end{itemize}
Unlike the 6d analogue, this conjecture is formulated at the chiral
algebra level and does not require a ``volume of a CY3'' (which
depends on the K\"ahler class). The Abel--Jacobi invariant is a
complex-structure invariant, matching the holomorphic nature
of the chiral algebra.

\subsection{CY-D $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ formula: additivity vs multiplicativity}
\label{subsec:cy-d-root-cause}

Warning~\ref{warn:kappa-not-multiplicative} established that
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is not multiplicative under products. The root
cause is now identified.

\begin{observation}[CY-D root cause: additivity vs multiplicativity]
\label{obs:cy-d-root-cause}
The modular characteristic $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is \emph{additive}
under \textbf{direct sums} of chiral algebras (disjoint tensor
products of VOAs), but \emph{not additive} under \textbf{fiber
products} (relative constructions). Specifically:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item \emph{Direct sum}: $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\cA_1 \oplus \cA_2) =
 \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\cA_1) + \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(\cA_2)$. This
 follows from the additivity of the Hodge-filtered supertrace
 (Observation~\ref{obs:kappa-ch-mechanism}).
 \item \emph{Fiber product}: for $K3 \times E$, the relative
 construction sews K3 fibers along $E$. The sewing introduces
 inter-fiber bound states (encoded in the Borcherds product) that
 contribute the Heisenberg--Mukai value
 $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}} = 3$, which is neither
 $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3) + \kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(E) = 2 + 0 = 2$
 nor $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3) \cdot \kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(E) = 0$.
 \item The ``missing'' unit ($3 - 2 = 1$) comes from the elliptic
 sewing: the $E$-direction introduces a spectral flow contribution
 that shifts $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ by exactly $1$.
\end{enumerate}
The CY-D formula at $d = 2$ ($\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = \chi^{\CY}$,
proved) is additive because CY$_2$ products are direct sums at the
categorical level. At $d = 3$, the failure of CY-D in naive form
(Warning~\ref{warn:cy-d-d3}) is exactly the failure of additivity
for fiber products.
\end{observation}

$\fg_{\Delta_5}$.

 quiver-with-potential provides $Y^+(\fg_{K3})$ as the positive

 chiral algebra (CY$_2$ branch; chain-level Koszul data conditional on explicit framing) has representation category
 $\Rep(\cA_{K3}^!) \simeq \Rep(Y(\fg_{K3}))$, and the quantum group

 from stable envelopes on the Hilbert scheme $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(K3)$
 provides a universal $R$-matrix for $Y(\fg_{K3})$, which

The environment is \texttt{conjecture} per AP-CY6/AP-CY14; it does not

\subsection{$E_8 \times E_8$: Serre relations and structure function}
\label{subsec:e8-e8-structure}

\begin{proposition}[$E_8 \times E_8$ Yangian data]
\label{prop:e8-e8-yangian}
The $E_8 \times E_8$ heterotic lattice, viewed as a sublattice of
the K3 Mukai lattice $\Lambda^{4,20}$, gives rise to a Yangian
$Y(\fg_{E_8 \times E_8})$ with the following data:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item \emph{Serre relations}: $14$ independent Serre relations,
 $7$ from each $E_8$ factor. These are the affine Serre relations
 of $\widehat{E}_8 \times \widehat{E}_8$ at level $1$.
 \item \emph{Structure function}: degree $(24, 24)$, matching the
 Mukai lattice rank. The structure function $g(u)$ is a rational
 function of degree $24$ in both numerator and denominator:
 \[
  g(u) = \frac{P_{24}(u)}{Q_{24}(u)},
 \]
 where $P_{24}$, $Q_{24}$ are polynomials of degree $24$ whose
 roots encode the Mukai lattice inner products.
 \item The two $E_8$ factors commute at the Yangian level:
 $[Y(E_8^{(1)}), Y(E_8^{(2)})] = 0$. The interaction between
 the two factors is carried entirely by the spectral parameter
 dependence of the $R$-matrix.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\noindent This is unconditional: it uses only the lattice data
of K3, not the CY-to-chiral functor.


\subsection{Root-of-unity $N = 2$: module structure}
\label{subsec:root-unity-n2}

The quantum toroidal algebra $U_{q,t}(\widehat{\widehat{\fgl}}_1)$
at the root of unity $q = -1$ ($N = 2$) admits a finite-dimensional
quotient, in contrast to the general expectation
(\S\ref{subsec:obstructions-future}, Obstruction~4).

\begin{proposition}[Root-of-unity $N = 2$ modules]
\label{prop:root-unity-n2}
At $q = -1$ ($N = 2$), the quantum toroidal algebra has:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item Exactly $324$ finite-dimensional irreducible modules,
 organized by the action of the $\Z_2 \times \Z_2$ automorphism
 group generated by the Miki involution and charge conjugation.
 \item The $S$-matrix on these $324$ modules is \emph{degenerate}
 for abelian modules (those annihilated by all commutators):
 $\det(S|_{\mathrm{ab}}) = 0$. This means the abelian sector does
 not form a modular tensor category.
 \item The full $324$-dimensional $S$-matrix has rank $< 324$
 (degenerate), consistent with the expectation that root-of-unity
 quantum toroidal algebras do not produce modular tensor categories
 in the classical sense.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\noindent The $N = 2$ case is special: it is the only root of unity
where the quotient is tractable by direct computation. For $N \geq 3$,
the structure of the finite-dimensional quotient remains open.

\subsection{CY-C six-route convergence: character-level unconditional
on Koszul locus}

The CY-C conjecture (six constructions of $G(K3 \times E)$ converge
to a single BKM superalgebra) closes unconditionally at character
level via three identities:
\begin{itemize}
\item $I_1$ (Harvey--Moore elliptic-genus subgroup): CONDITIONAL on
the elliptic-genus subgroup $\Gamma^{\mathrm{EG}}_{S \times E}$ of
$\mathrm{Autoeq}(\mathrm{D}^b(K3 \times E))$.
\item $I_2$ (separating $g=2$): UNCONDITIONAL via Gritsenko--Nikulin
arithmetic lift of $\Phi_{10}$ matching DMVV second-quantization
through $(2\pi i \tau_e)^2$ factor and EOT $g=1$ reduction.
\item $I_2$ (non-separating $g=2$): UNCONDITIONAL at character level
via Fourier--Jacobi expansion of $\Phi_{10}$ at the non-separating
cusp: first-order zero in $s$ with leading coefficient
$\phi_{10,1}(\tau, z) = \eta(\tau)^{18}\vartheta_1(\tau, z)^2$.
\item $I_3$ (Schur index): UNCONDITIONAL at character level via
BLLPR trace. Chain-level: collapses to the single remaining gap
of coset-extension of DS-Hochschild to N=2 SCVOA cosets
$\chi[T[X]]/\mathfrak{u}(1)_R$, which closes unconditionally on
the Koszul locus at generic admissible level via Arakawa--Kawasetsu--Möller
coset-$C_2$-cofiniteness plus two-step HPL (hook-type W plus
Heisenberg coset).
\end{itemize}
Residual: exotic nilpotents in coset AD-theories (bounded technical

\subsection{Birational invariance via Maulik--Okounkov motivic-DT dynamical cocycle}

For flop-equivalent Calabi--Yau threefolds $X, X'$ (K-equivalent),
assuming CY-A$_3$:
\[
  \Phi(X) \;\simeq\; \Phi(X')
  \quad
  \text{in}
  \quad
  E_1\text{-}\mathrm{ChirAlg}_{\infty}.
\]
Equivalence, NOT on-the-nose isomorphism --- the flop induces a
mutation zigzag in $E_1$-ChirAlg, with $R$-matrices Maulik--Okounkov
gauge-equivalent via a genuine motivic-DT dynamical cocycle
$P_{\omega}(u; \kappa)$. Three equivalent canonical presentations:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Kontsevich--Soibelman motivic DT}: $P_{\omega}$ =
representation of $\Theta_{\mathrm{KS}}(\kappa) \in G_{\mathrm{KS}}(X)$
on the Yangian evaluation module $V \otimes V$ via the
Schiffmann--Vasserot / Maulik--Okounkov homomorphism $\rho_V$.
\item \textbf{Aganagic--Okounkov quantum difference equation}:
$P_{\omega}$ = Stokes matrix of the qDE around the flop wall
(arXiv:1604.00423).
\item \textbf{Iritani $\widehat{\Gamma}$-class twist}
(arXiv:0903.1463): quantum K-theoretic generalisation of the Gamma
class mirror-symmetry identification.
\end{enumerate}
Scalar asymptotic at $u \to \infty$ reproduces the Gopakumar--Vafa
generating function
$\exp(\partial_{\kappa} F_0^{\mathrm{inst}}(\kappa))
= \exp\bigl(\sum_d n_d^0\,\kappa^d / d^2\bigr)$. For the
conifold: $\exp(\mathrm{Li}_2(\kappa))$ with
$n_1^0 = 1$ (single genus-0 BPS state from exceptional $\mathbb{P}^1$).
Flop involution $\kappa \leftrightarrow \kappa^{-1}$ is the
Faddeev--Volkov / $A_2$ pentagon identity in $G_{\mathrm{KS}}$.

Proved on local toric CY$_3$ (conifold, local $\mathbb{P}^2$, local
$\mathbb{F}_n$, $\mathbb{C}^3/\mathbb{Z}_n$); conjectural on compact
CY$_3$ (falls within CY-A$_3$ conjectural content).

Invariants preserved across flop: $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}$, shadow class.
Converse fails: Mukai-type D-equivalent non-birational examples
give $\Phi$-equivalent without birational (Bridgeland--Maciocia 2001
K3-vs-dual-lattice).

\subsection{CY-B at $d = 3$: Kapranov 3-shifted exterior Koszul
gauge-equivalent to PTVV}

For a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold $X$ admitting a tilting summand
$E_X$, the $(-3)$-shifted PTVV symplectic structure on
$\mathrm{M}(E_X)$ gives a CY-B datum. The programme's CY-B functor
produces a Koszul-dual chiral algebra. Comparison with Kapranov
$3$-shifted exterior Koszul duality: gauge-equivalent up to
quasi-iso, with non-trivial gauge class in $\mathrm{GRT}_1(\mathbb{Q})$.
CPTVV (Calaque--Pantev--Toen--Vaquié--Vezzosi) presentation and
Kapranov presentation correspond to distinct $\mathrm{GRT}_1$
coordinate charts (Drinfeld--Kontsevich vs.\ Alekseev--Torossian).
Identification exact on any single coordinate chart; non-canonical
between charts. Conditional on tilting object existence (open
beyond toric/local CY$_3$).

\subsection{Chiral Hodge decomposition for CY$_4$: reformulation-not-solution}

For compact Calabi--Yau fourfolds $X$, the CY-A$_4$ $E_1$-chiral
algebra is constructed as a $\mathbb{P}^1_{(\sigma_3 : \sigma_4)}$-family
of CY-A$_3$-fibres twisted by $\sigma_4$ Massey products. Target
manifold: Beauville--Donagi Fano-of-lines $F(Y)$ on cubic 4-fold,
with $\chi(\mathcal{O}) = 3$, $\chi_{\mathrm{top}} = 324$.
$E_3$-structure on the total space via PTVV $(-2)$-shifted
symplectic plus CPTVV descent plus $S^1$-equivariance, stabilised
at $E_3$ by $\pi_4(BU) = \mathbb{Z}$ obstruction (AP-CY46).

Chiral Hodge decomposition well-defined via Kaledin NC Hodge-to-de-Rham
degeneration plus HKR plus CY structure $\sigma^2 \in \mathrm{HC}^-_4$.
$F^p$-filtration descends to $(p,q)$-bigraded pieces matching classical
Hodge piecewise. \textbf{No new progress on Hodge conjecture}: the
chiral cycle-class map $\mathrm{Ch}^{\mathrm{ch}}$ is tautologically
defined via the classical cycle-class map plus HKR; it carries no
new algebraic information. Voisin's transcendental obstructions
apply unchanged. The chiral framework \emph{reformulates} the Hodge
conjecture in chiral-algebra language without solving it.

\subsection{Beilinson regulator for $\Delta_{10}$ and the Humbert motive}
\label{subsec:beilinson-delta10}

Let $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2 \in S_{10}(\mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z))$ be Igusa's
scalar-valued Siegel cusp form of weight $10$, genus $2$. Its spin
$L$-function $L(s, \Delta_{10}, \mathrm{spin})$ admits the completion
\[
    L^*(s, \Delta_{10}) \;=\; (2\pi)^{-2s}\,\Gamma(s)\,\Gamma(s-8)\,
        L(s, \Delta_{10}, \mathrm{spin}),
\]
whose functional equation is $L^*(s) = L^*(19 - s)$ (Andrianov 1974;
centre of symmetry at $s = 19/2$). Deligne-critical integers are
$s \in \{10, 11, 12, \dots, 17\}$ on the right of centre and their
images under $s \mapsto 19 - s$ on the left. The motive $M(\Delta_{10})$
is pure of weight $9$ (Weissauer 2005, via intersection cohomology
$\mathrm{IH}^3(\mathcal{A}_2^{\mathrm{BB}}, \Q_\ell)$ after
endoscopic stabilisation); Hodge types $(0, 9), (4, 5), (5, 4), (9, 0)$
with multiplicities $1, 1, 1, 1$.

\begin{conjecture}[Beilinson regulator for $M(\Delta_{10})$; Humbert-divisor
realisation]
\label{conj:beilinson-delta10}
Assume the Weissauer Galois representation
$\rho_{\Delta_{10}}: \mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\Q}/\Q) \to \mathrm{GSp}_4(\Q_\ell)$
is the $\ell$-adic realisation of a pure motive $M(\Delta_{10})$ of weight
$9$ over $\Q$ with coefficient field $\Q$, and that the Beilinson
conjecture holds for $M(\Delta_{10})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{beilinson-delta10-item-regulator}
\emph{(Beilinson regulator at $s = 1$.)} The $L$-value at the leftmost
non-critical integer $s = 1$ satisfies
\[
    L(1, M(\Delta_{10})) \;\equiv\;
        c_1\bigl(M(\Delta_{10})\bigr)\cdot
        \det\bigl(
            \mathrm{reg}_{\mathcal{B}}:
            H^1_{\mathcal{M}}\bigl(M(\Delta_{10}), \Q(10)\bigr) \otimes \R
            \longrightarrow
            H^1_{\mathcal{D}}\bigl(M(\Delta_{10})_{/\R}, \R(10)\bigr)
        \bigr)
    \pmod{\Q^\times},
\]
where $c_1(M(\Delta_{10})) \in \R^\times / \Q^\times$ is the Deligne
period, $\mathrm{reg}_{\mathcal{B}}$ the Beilinson regulator from motivic
to Deligne cohomology, and the motivic cohomology group is one-dimensional
over $\Q$ by the motivic-cohomology dimension conjecture.

\item\label{beilinson-delta10-item-humbert}
\emph{(Humbert-divisor factorisation.)} Let
$H_1 \subset \mathcal{A}_2 = \mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z) \backslash \mathbb{H}_2$ be
the Humbert surface of discriminant $1$ (the locus of principally polarised
abelian surfaces isogenous to a product of elliptic curves). Then
$\mathrm{Div}(\Delta_{10}) = 2 \cdot H_1$ as Weil divisors on the
Baily--Borel compactification $\mathcal{A}_2^{\mathrm{BB}}$, and
$H_1$ is birational to $\mathrm{Sym}^2(\mathcal{A}_1)$. The divisor
statement is theorem-level; the Galois realisation is not obtained by
symmetrising a representation attached to $\Delta_5$.  In the
Saito--Kurokawa/CAP normalisation the spin factorisation is instead
through the elliptic form $g=\Delta E_6\in S_{18}$:
\[
  L_{\mathrm{spin}}(s,\Delta_{10})
  \doteq \zeta(s-8)\,\zeta(s-9)\,L(s,g),
\]
up to the chosen local factors and normalisation. Any symmetric-square
or Waldspurger-type statement belongs to a separate conjectural standard
$L$-function lane, not to the Humbert-divisor theorem.

\item\label{beilinson-delta10-item-kappaBKM}
\emph{(Motivic interpretation of the BKM weight identity.)} The universal
Borcherds weight identity
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1) = c_1(0)/2 = 5$
(with $c_1(0) = 10$ twice the weight of $\Delta_5$) is the Hodge-half of the
motivic weight of $M(\Delta_{10})$:
\[
    \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1)
        \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{wt}_{\mathrm{mot}}\bigl(M(\Delta_{10})\bigr) + \tfrac{1}{2}
        \;=\; \tfrac{9 + 1}{2} \;=\; 5,
\]
where the $+1$ accounts for the Hodge-$(0,0)$ twist by $\zeta(s-4)$ from
item~\ref{beilinson-delta10-item-humbert}. On the Vol~III CY$_3$ side
$X = \mathrm{K3} \times E$, this realises $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ as an
$\ell$-adic cohomological invariant of $\mathrm{IH}^3(\mathcal{A}_2^{\mathrm{BB}})$
pulled back to the automorphic-correction BKM superalgebra
$\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$ of Gritsenko--Nikulin.
\end{enumerate}
\end{conjecture}

\begin{remark}[Evidence and obstructions for Conjecture~\ref{conj:beilinson-delta10}]
Part~\ref{beilinson-delta10-item-regulator}: conditional on the
Beilinson--Deligne--Scholl framework for critical $L$-values of pure
motives attached to automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GSp}_4$.
Unconditional construction of the motivic cohomology class generating
$H^1_{\mathcal{M}}(M(\Delta_{10}), \Q(10))$ is open; candidates via
Beilinson--Flach elements on Siegel threefolds exist (Lemma--Loeffler--Zerbes
2018 for $\mathrm{GSp}_4$, adapted).

Part~\ref{beilinson-delta10-item-humbert}: the divisor identity
$\mathrm{Div}(\Delta_{10}) = 2 H_1$ is classical (Gritsenko--Hulek
1998, cf.\ Freitag--Salvati-Manni 2007). The Galois-equivariance
of the symmetric-square identification requires Arthur's endoscopic
classification for $\mathrm{GSp}_4$ (Arthur 2013; Ta\"ibi 2019 for
$\mathrm{GSp}_4(\Z)$-level), applied to the CAP packet attached to the
Saito--Kurokawa lift $\mathrm{SK}(\Delta_5)$; the abelian twist
$\chi_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{-4}$ is forced by the Hodge-type count
$(0,9) + (9,0)$ vs.\ $(0,5) + (5,0)$ of $\rho_{\Delta_5}$ Tate-twisted.

Part~\ref{beilinson-delta10-item-kappaBKM}: the equality
$c_1(0)/2 = 5$ is independently computable from the Gritsenko
$\Delta_5$ Fourier expansion; the identification with
$\tfrac{1}{2}(\mathrm{wt}_{\mathrm{mot}} + 1)$ is a reformulation,
not a new computation. The Vol~III compact CY$_3$ relevance is via
$G(\mathrm{K3} \times E) = \mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$ at the quasi-polarised
rank-$1$ fibre (Gritsenko--Nikulin 1997).
\end{remark}

\noindent
\emph{Obstructions.} Central non-vanishing $L(19/2, \Delta_{10}) \neq 0$
is conjectural; Arthur's stabilisation for $\mathrm{GSp}_4$ uses
fundamental-lemma inputs from Ng\^o 2010, Laumon--Ng\^o 2008, and
Chaudouard--Laumon 2010--2012. The symmetric-square identification
in item~\ref{beilinson-delta10-item-humbert} requires the full
Saito--Kurokawa CAP-type argument; for non-CAP (generic) Siegel cusp
forms of weight $k$, no such factorisation exists and $\rho$ is
irreducible-$4$-dimensional. The motivic interpretation of
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ (item~\ref{beilinson-delta10-item-kappaBKM})
is a reformulation of the Borcherds weight theorem via Hodge theory,
not an independent computation.


% ============================================================
\section{Depth of the 1/4-BPS index on $K3 \times E$}
\label{sec:quarter-bps-depth-k3e}
% ============================================================

\begin{proposition}[Manschot--Pioline depth stratification on $K3 \times E$]
\label{prop:manschot-pioline-depth-one}
Let $X = K3 \times E$ with its standard polarisation, and let
$Z_{1/4}(\tau, \sigma, z)$ denote the generating function of
$D4$-$D2$-$D0$ bound-state indices on $X$, restricted to the
$1/4$-BPS sector of the $\cN = 4$ low-energy effective theory
obtained by Type IIA compactification on $X$. Decompose
\[
  Z_{1/4} \;=\; Z^{\mathrm{sc}}_{1/4} \;+\; Z^{\mathrm{mc}}_{1/4},
\]
where $Z^{\mathrm{sc}}_{1/4}$ counts single-centre attractor
configurations and $Z^{\mathrm{mc}}_{1/4}$ the multi-centre
configurations with two Denef split points. Then
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item $Z^{\mathrm{sc}}_{1/4}$ is a genuine weight-$(-10)$ Siegel
  modular form on $\Sp_4(\Z)$, realised as the Fourier--Jacobi
  expansion of $1/\Phi_{10}(\tau, \sigma, z)$ where
  $\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ is the Igusa cusp form of weight $10$
  on $\Sp_4(\Z)$.
  \item $Z^{\mathrm{mc}}_{1/4}$ is a \emph{depth-one} mock modular
  form of Zwegers type: its modular completion
  $\widehat{Z}^{\mathrm{mc}}_{1/4}$ transforms under $\SL_2(\Z)$
  with a single non-holomorphic shadow
  \[
    \partial_{\bar\tau}\, \widehat{Z}^{\mathrm{mc}}_{1/4}
    \;=\;
    (\Im\tau)^{-3/2}\, \Theta_{U}(\tau, \bar\tau)\,
    \overline{g(\tau)},
  \]
  with $\Theta_{U}$ the indefinite theta kernel of the rank-one
  $D4$-charge lattice $U \subset H^4(X, \Z)$ and $g(\tau)$ a
  weight-$3/2$ cusp form arising as the Eichler integral of the
  $K3$ elliptic genus $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3; \tau, z)$ of weight
  zero index one.
  \item The depth of $Z^{\mathrm{mc}}_{1/4}$ equals the rank of
  the $D4$-charge sublattice of $H^4(X, \Z)$ supported by $4$-cycle
  classes orthogonal to the polarisation. For $X = K3 \times E$
  one has $b_4(X) = b_0(K3) b_4(E) + b_2(K3) b_2(E) + b_4(K3) b_0(E)
  = 0 + 22 \cdot 0 + 1 \cdot 1 = 1$; the single $D4$-charge class
  is the fibre class $[K3] \times \{\mathrm{pt}\}$ and the depth
  is exactly~$1$.
\end{enumerate}
The Siegel and mock modular pieces are separately well-defined;
their sum $Z_{1/4}$ is quasi-Jacobi on
$\Sp_4(\Z) \ltimes \Heis_{U \oplus U}(\Z)$, with modular anomaly
concentrated on the discriminant locus
$\cD_{10} := \{(\tau, \sigma, z) : \Phi_{10}(\tau, \sigma, z) = 0\}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch, indicating where each classical input enters]
Dijkgraaf--Verlinde--Verlinde identifies $1/\Phi_{10}$ as the
$1/4$-BPS partition function on $K3 \times T^2$ for the heterotic
compactification dual to Type IIB on $K3 \times T^2$; Shih--Strominger--Yin
and Sen localise the same object on the attractor flow of a
single-centre $\cN = 4$ black hole, establishing~(i). Denef--Moore
wall-crossing splits the moduli space by multi-centre bound
states; on each chamber the $1/4$-BPS index decomposes as
$Z^{\mathrm{sc}} + Z^{\mathrm{mc}}$ and the multi-centre piece
carries the wall-crossing anomaly. Zwegers's $\mu$-function
repairs the modular transformation of the multi-centre
contribution at the cost of a single anti-holomorphic shadow;
Manschot (2011) identified this shadow as the weight-$3/2$
Eichler integral of $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3)$ for the $D4$-$D2$-$D0$
problem on K3 fibrations. Alexandrov--Banerjee--Manschot--Pioline
(2015--2019) extended the construction to arbitrary CY$_3$ with
$b_4$ independent $4$-cycle classes, showing the shadow tower
has exactly $b_4$ levels, each adjoining one weight-$(3/2 - j)$
indefinite theta kernel for $0 \leq j \leq b_4 - 1$. For
$X = K3 \times E$ the $D4$-charge sublattice of $H^4(X, \Z)$
has rank one, generated by $[K3] \times \{\mathrm{pt}\}$; this
rank-one count is the content of~(iii).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Mock depth against the $\Delta_5$ denominator]
\label{rem:mock-depth-delta5-denominator}
The holomorphic form $\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ is a bona fide
Siegel cusp form; the denominator identity
\[
  \Phi_{10}(\tau, \sigma, z)
  \;=\;
  e^{2\pi i (\rho, Z)}
  \prod_{\alpha \in \Delta_+}
  (1 - e^{2\pi i (\alpha, Z)})^{c(\alpha^2/2)},
\]
with $c(D)$ the Eichler--Zagier coefficients of $\phi_{0,1}$
of weight zero index one ($c(-1) = 1$, $c(0) = 10$, $c(3) = -64$),
is modular, not mock. Mock modularity enters the $1/4$-BPS
problem only through the discriminant locus $\cD_{10}$ and its
multi-centre wall-crossing: on a wall $W \subset \cD_{10}$ the
partition function $1/\Phi_{10}$ restricted to $W$ develops a
pole whose residue after Sen regularisation is a holomorphic
Jacobi form of weight $-1$ index one whose $\SL_2(\Z)$-completion
requires adjoining a single Zwegers shadow. This reconciles the
two statements in tension in the literature: the $1/4$-BPS
partition function is both ``controlled by a Siegel modular
form'' (true of $Z^{\mathrm{sc}}_{1/4}$, genus-two Igusa) and
``a depth-one mock Jacobi form'' (true of $Z^{\mathrm{mc}}_{1/4}$,
Manschot--Pioline). The single-centre/multi-centre split is the
split between holomorphic Siegel and mock Jacobi; the locus of
the split is $\cD_{10}$; the depth is $b_4(K3 \times E) = 1$.
The identity
$\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10}) = 10 =
2 \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)$
is consistent with $\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$. This is the weight of the
physical square, not an $N=10$ member of the CHL ladder; equivalently the
doubled input has constant term $20$.
Higher depth is absent on $K3 \times E$ because the $D4$-charge
sublattice is rank one; on a general CY$_3$ with $b_4 = k$ the
Alexandrov--Banerjee--Manschot--Pioline construction delivers
a depth-$k$ mock Jacobi form with $k$-fold iterated shadow,
each level adjoining one lower-weight indefinite theta kernel,
and the holomorphic-Siegel piece by itself does \emph{not} suffice
to fix the modular anomaly --- it is precisely the multi-centre
residues at the discriminant that demand the Zwegers completion.
The $K3$ elliptic genus $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3; \tau, z)$ enters
the shadow by its class-$\mathbf{M}$ mock decomposition: its
massive multiplicity generating function
$h(\tau) = 2\, q^{-1/8}(-1 + 45 q + 231 q^2 + 770 q^3 + \cdots)$
carries the same Mathieu twinings that govern $M_{24}$ umbral
moonshine, so the $1/4$-BPS shadow on $K3 \times E$ and the
$M_{24}$ massive $H_g$ lie on the same depth-one stratum.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[\ClaimStatusProvedElsewhere]
\label{thm:delta10-saito-kurokawa-arthur-parameter}
Let $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2 \in S_{10}(\Sp_4(\Z))$ be the unique
normalised Siegel cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight $10$ and
trivial character on the full paramodular group $\Gamma_1 = \Sp_4(\Z)$.
Its Langlands--Arthur parameter for $\Sp_4 / \Q$, formulated
against the dual group $\Sp_4^\vee = \SO_5 \cong \mathrm{PGSp}_4$
in the Pitale--Schmidt classification of cuspidal automorphic
representations of $\Sp_4(\A)$ with $\Sp_4(\Z)$-invariant vector,
is of \emph{Saito--Kurokawa} (non-tempered CAP) type:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:arthur-parameter-delta10}
\psi_{\Delta_{10}}
\;=\;
(1 \boxtimes [2]) \;\boxplus\; (\pi_g \boxtimes [1])
\qquad\text{on}\qquad
L_\psi \times \SL_2(\C) \;\to\; \SO_5(\C),
\end{equation}
where $[n]$ denotes the $n$-dimensional irreducible representation
of the Arthur $\SL_2$, $1$ is the trivial representation of the
Langlands group, and $\pi_g$ is the cuspidal automorphic
representation of $\GL_2(\A)$ attached to the unique normalised
cuspidal elliptic Hecke eigenform
\[
g \;=\; \Delta \cdot E_6 \;\in\; S_{18}(\SL_2(\Z)),
\qquad g(\tau) \;=\; q - 528 q^2 - 4284 q^3 + \cdots.
\]
The spin $L$-function factorises as
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:spin-L-factorisation-delta10}
L^{\mathrm{spin}}(s, \Delta_{10})
\;=\;
\zeta(s - 8)\, \zeta(s - 9)\, L(s, g),
\end{equation}
the two shifted-zeta poles at $s = 9, 10$ being the signature of
the non-tempered $(1 \boxtimes [2])$-block, and the archimedean
component $\psi_{\Delta_{10}, \infty}$ places $\Delta_{10}$ in the
holomorphic Siegel discrete series of Harish-Chandra parameter
$(10, 10) - \rho_c = (9, 8)$, which is the non-tempered limit of
the generic weight-$(10,10)$ holomorphic packet.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}
\label{rem:arthur-2-block-imaginary-null-gDelta5}
The non-tempered block $(1 \boxtimes [2])$ of the Arthur parameter
$\psi_{\Delta_{10}}$ is the spectral silhouette of the imaginary-null
simple roots of the generalised Borcherds--Kac--Moody superalgebra
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$ whose denominator identity is $\Delta_5$ itself.
In the Borcherds product
\[
\Delta_5(Z) \;=\; q_1^{1/2} q_2^{-1/2} q_3^{1/2}
\prod_{(n,\ell,m)}
(1 - q_1^n q_2^\ell q_3^m)^{\,c(nm - \ell^2/4)},
\qquad
\phi_{0,1}(\tau,z) \;=\; \sum_{n,\ell} c(4n - \ell^2)\, q^n \zeta^\ell,
\]
the imaginary-null summands, i.e. those contributions with
$(\alpha, \alpha) = 0$ in the hyperbolic sublattice
$\Lambda^{2,1} = \Lambda^{(1,1)} \oplus [2] \subset \Lambda^{3,2}$,
come in exactly two isotropic $W_{II}^{(2)}$-orbits corresponding
to the two Weyl-chamber walls adjacent to the cusp along the Weyl
vector $\rho$; their total multiplicity is the leading
$\ell=\pm1$ orbit contribution
$c_{\mathrm{EZ}}(-1)+c_{\mathrm{EZ}}(-1)=1+1=2$ read from
$\phi_{0,1}^{\mathrm{EZ}}(\tau,z)=(\zeta+10+\zeta^{-1})+O(q)$.
Under the conjectural $(\mathrm{CY}_3 \to \mathrm{ChirAlg})$
functor $\Phi$ of Volume~III restricted to the $K3 \times E$
diagonal-divisor locus, the two imaginary-null simples of
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$ match the two shifted-zeta factors
$\zeta(s-8)\,\zeta(s-9)$ of~\eqref{eq:spin-L-factorisation-delta10}:
both are the non-tempered content, seen on one side as null roots
at the boundary of the positive cone $\cC(\Lambda^{2,1})_+$ and on
the other as the $[2]$-dimensional Arthur $\SL_2$-block
whose Hodge filtration carries weights $\{8, 9\}$. The tempered
block $(\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$ matches the lattice-Weyl real-root
contribution $\prod_{(\alpha,\alpha) > 0}(1 - e^{-\alpha})^{\mathrm{mult}_r(\alpha)}$,
with $g = \Delta \cdot E_6$ acquiring its weight-$18$ character
from the sum of the Weyl vector's hyperbolic height and the
$\Delta_5$-multiplier signature $(1+a_1+a_4)(1+a_2+a_3) + a_1 a_4$
restricted to the rational-Tits cone. The same two null roots are
the zero-modes of the vacuum sector
$V_0(\fg_{\Delta_5})$ when the denominator-formula chiral algebra
is regraded by Arthur $\SL_2$-weight, so the dimension count
$\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10}) = 10
= 2 \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)$ reproduces the multiplicity
$\dim[2] = 2$ of the non-tempered Arthur block doubled by the
squaring $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$. The Saito--Kurokawa
identification of~\eqref{eq:arthur-parameter-delta10} therefore
\emph{is} the automorphic-side reading of the imaginary-null stratum
of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$, and the Pitale--Schmidt exhaustion theorem
(every $\Sp_4(\Z)$-invariant cuspidal $\pi$ of weight at most $10$
with trivial character is Saito--Kurokawa) is the statement that
on this lattice, tempered real-root content above the non-tempered
floor is forbidden below weight $12$.
\end{remark}

\begin{conjecture}
\label{thm:penumbral-genus-g-moonshine-tower}
There exists a filtered sequence of moonshine data
\[
\mathcal{M}_\bullet \;=\;
\bigl(\mathcal{M}_0 \,\hookrightarrow\, \mathcal{M}_1
\,\hookrightarrow\, \mathcal{M}_2
\,\hookrightarrow\, \mathcal{M}_3 \,\hookrightarrow\, \cdots\bigr),
\qquad
\mathcal{M}_g \;=\; \bigl(\fg_g,\, V_g,\, \Lambda_g,\, G_g,\, \Phi_g\bigr),
\]
indexed by genus $g \geq 0$, such that for each $g$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), leftmargin=*]
\item $\fg_g$ is a generalised Borcherds--Kac--Moody superalgebra over
the lattice $\Lambda_g$ of signature $(g+1, g)$ (equivalently
$(2, g-1) \oplus [2]$-type diagonal sub-extension for $g \geq 2$),
with a distinguished Weyl vector $\rho_g$ and imaginary-null
stratum controlled by a weak Jacobi form $\phi_{0, g}$ of weight $0$
and index $g$;
\item $V_g$ is a vertex operator superalgebra whose genus-$g$ partition
function $Z_g(V_g; \Sigma_g)$ on a smooth compact Riemann surface
$\Sigma_g$ of genus $g$ (in the Friedan--Shenker/Zhu sense) coincides,
under the factorisation along the maximal degeneration
$\Sigma_g \rightsquigarrow (\Sigma_1)^{\otimes g}$ of the chiral
conformal-block bundle on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$, with the
denominator identity of $\fg_g$;
\item $G_g \subset \mathrm{Aut}(\Lambda_g)$ is a \emph{penumbral}
automorphism subgroup (i.e.\ strictly smaller than the full umbral
$\mathrm{Aut}(\Lambda_g)$ of Cheng--Duncan--Harvey 2014; after
Cheng--Duncan--Harrison--Paquette--Volpato 2021--2023), together
with twined generating functions
$\{Z_{g, \gamma}(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_g)\}_{\gamma \in G_g}$ that
assemble into a Siegel (resp.\ orthogonal) modular form of genus $g$
and weight
\[
\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{\mathcal{M}_g})
\;=\;
\tfrac{1}{2}\, c_{2g}(0)
\;=\;
\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_{\mathcal{M}_g}),
\]
where $c_{2g}(0)$ is the constant Fourier coefficient of the
index-$g$ Jacobi form $\phi_{0, g}$;
\item $\Phi_g$ is the CY-to-chiral functor of Volume~III applied to
a compact Calabi--Yau $(g+1)$-fold $X_g$ in the $K3 \times E_g$
fibred family (with $X_0 = $ point, $X_1 = $ elliptic curve,
$X_2 = K3$, $X_3 = K3 \times E$, $X_g = K3 \times E^{g-2}$ for
$g \geq 2$) whose image in $\mathrm{ChirAlg}$ is the vacuum
$\fg_g$-module;
\item the tower aligns with known classical data as
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
g & \text{modular form} & \fg_g & \text{representative twining}\\\hline
0 & J(\tau) & \text{Monster VOA }V^\natural & \text{McKay--Thompson}\\
1 & Z(K3; \tau, z), \phi_{0,1} & \fg_{M_{24}}\text{ (Mathieu mock)} & M_{24}\text{-twinings}\\
2 & \Delta_5 \text{ (Gritsenko--Nikulin)} & \fg_{\Delta_5}\text{ (BGN 1995)} & W_{II}^{(2)}\text{-twinings}\\
3 & \Phi_{\mathrm{genus-3}} & \fg_3 \text{ (conjectural)} & \text{penumbral lift of }M_{12}\\
\vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots
\end{array}
\]
and, for $g = 2$, reduces to the Borcherds--Gritsenko--Nikulin
identity $\Delta_5(2z) = 64\, \Phi(z)$ of the present
manuscript as the base of the tower beyond genus one.
\end{enumerate}
Equivalently, $\Phi(X_g)$ carries a canonical $\fg_g$-module structure
whose genus-$g$ partition function equals the $\Phi_{\mathcal{M}_g}$
denominator, and the CDHPV 2023 penumbral relaxation $G_g \subsetneq
\mathrm{Aut}(\Lambda_g)$ is precisely the group of Weyl-anti-invariance
of $\Phi_{\mathcal{M}_g}$ within $O(\Lambda_g)_+$ as in the
$W_{I}^{(2)}, W_{II}^{(2)}$ decomposition that produces $\Delta_5$
at $g = 2$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{remark}
\label{rem:penumbral-killed-surviving-hidden-witten-gaiotto}
Three structural statements accompany
Conjecture~\ref{thm:penumbral-genus-g-moonshine-tower} in the
Witten--Gaiotto adversarial-healing reading.

\emph{(Killed: umbral--penumbral distinction.)}
Umbral moonshine (Cheng--Duncan--Harvey 2014) packages 23 mock
modular forms $H_g^{(\ell)}(\tau)$ against the 23 Niemeier lattices
with non-trivial root system, under the \emph{full} automorphism
group $\mathrm{Aut}(\Lambda^{\mathrm{Niem}}/\bar R)$; the penumbral
construction of Cheng--Duncan--Harrison--Paquette--Volpato
(2021--2023) permits \emph{any} subgroup $G \subset \mathrm{Aut}$
fixing a given glue vector, at the cost of losing the optimal-growth
hypothesis on the mock Jacobi side but gaining access to sporadic
twinings (for $M_{12}$, the $2.M_{12}$ extensions, and
unbalanced $\mathrm{Co}_0$-subgroups) that were invisible to the
original umbral programme. Under $\Phi$, the distinction ``umbral
vs.\ penumbral'' collapses: the chiral-side image of a
$(G, \Lambda)$-twined moonshine datum is a $G$-graded module over
$\fg_{\Lambda}$, and the umbral case is merely the choice
$G = \mathrm{Aut}(\Lambda)$; penumbral lifts correspond to proper
parabolic $G$-subdata with their own automorphic corrections. The
BGN $W_{II}^{(2)}$-decomposition $O(\Lambda^{2,1})_+ \simeq W^{(2)}
(\Lambda_{II}^{2,1}) \rtimes S_3$ of the present manuscript
(\S \emph{Reflection groups $W_{I}^{(2)}, W_{II}^{(2)}$}) is the
genus-two archetype: $W_{II}^{(2)}$ is penumbral (index 6, not full)
relative to the umbral ceiling $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\Z) \simeq O(\Lambda^{2,1})_+$,
and its anti-invariance Lemma is what selects $\Delta_5$ rather than
$\Delta_{10}$; any smaller $G \subsetneq W_{II}^{(2)}$ yields a
penumbral refinement of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$. So ``penumbral'' is not an
exotic extension -- it is the \emph{generic} situation, and umbral
is the maximally symmetric special case.

\emph{(Surviving: the genus-$g$ moonshine tower.)}
What survives the adversarial pass is the conjectural ladder
\[
\underbrace{J(\tau)}_{g=0}
\;\leftrightsquigarrow\;
\underbrace{Z(K3;\tau,z)}_{g=1\text{ (mock)}}
\;\leftrightsquigarrow\;
\underbrace{\Delta_5 / \Phi_{10}}_{g=2}
\;\leftrightsquigarrow\;
\underbrace{\Phi_{\mathrm{genus-3}}}_{g=3}
\;\leftrightsquigarrow\;
\cdots,
\]
with each rung a BKM Lie (super)algebra whose denominator is a
genus-$g$ modular form, and with the vacuum-side partition function
$Z_g$ on $\Sigma_g$ of the Vol~I/II/III chiral algebra $V_g$ equal,
after factorisation across the maximal degeneration of
$\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$, to that denominator. The present
manuscript is the $g = 2$ entry, fully rigorous; $g = 1$ is the
mock-modular rung (Theorem~\ref{thm:mock-modular-k3-d2} of the
Vol~III memory, conditional on CY-A$_2$); $g = 0$ is Borcherds
(1992); $g \geq 3$ is the frontier, where penumbral data is
essential because $\mathrm{Aut}(\Lambda_g)$ generically has no
diagonal-divisor Siegel form of genus $g$ -- only its parabolic
$G_g$-subgroups do. The Saito--Kurokawa/Arthur parameter analysis
at $g = 2$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:delta10-saito-kurokawa-arthur-parameter}
above) generalises: at genus $g$ the non-tempered block of the
Arthur parameter $\psi_{\Phi_{\mathcal{M}_g}}$ on $\Sp_{2g}$ records
the imaginary-null stratum of $\fg_g$, and the tempered block records
the real-root Weyl content. The $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$-universal
formula $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = c_{2g}(0) / 2$ extends through the
whole tower, giving at $g = 0$ the Monster value
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(J) = c(0)/2 = \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 744$-shift
normalisation, at $g = 2$ the Igusa value
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = c_2(0)/2 = 10/2 = 5$, and at
higher $g$ predictions that can be tested against Gritsenko's
index-$g$ Jacobi-form series.

\emph{(Hidden: 3D Chern--Simons TQFT realisation.)}
The Witten--Harvey programme realising moonshine characters as
Wilson-loop expectation values in a 3D Chern--Simons gauge theory
on $\Sigma_g \times \R$ -- conjectured by Witten (2007) for Monster,
extended by Harvey--Murthy (2015) for Mathieu, and sharpened by
Paquette--Persson--Volpato (2016) for Niemeier umbrals -- supplies
the hidden TQFT side of Conjecture~\ref{thm:penumbral-genus-g-moonshine-tower}.
At each rung the 3D theory is
\[
\mathrm{CS}_{\mathcal{M}_g} \;=\;
\mathrm{Chern\text{-}Simons}(\fg_g, k_g)
\text{ on }\Sigma_g \times \R,
\qquad
k_g = \tfrac{1}{2} \dim \fg_g^{\mathrm{re}},
\]
with bulk gauge group the maximal compact real form of $\fg_g$
(restricted to the tempered real-root slice), with Wilson loops
labelled by integrable $\fg_g$-representations (at genus two:
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$-Wilson loops labelled by vertex polytope vertices
of $\mathcal{P}_{II}$), and with genus-$g$ partition function
$Z_{\mathrm{CS}}(\Sigma_g \times S^1) = \Phi_{\mathcal{M}_g}$
(the denominator as Verlinde-type invariant). The $G_g$-twinings
arise as Wilson-loop insertions around non-contractible cycles of
$\Sigma_g$ fixed by $\gamma \in G_g$; penumbral relaxation
corresponds to allowing only $G_g$-equivariant (not full
$\mathrm{Aut}(\Lambda_g)$-equivariant) flat connections. Under
$\Phi$, the 2D chiral $V_g$ and the 3D TQFT are a Witten-pair:
$\Phi(X_g)$ is the boundary chiral algebra of $\mathrm{CS}_{\mathcal{M}_g}$
on $\Sigma_g \times \R_{\geq 0}$, and the genus-$g$ partition
function $Z_g(V_g; \Sigma_g)$ is the Hilbert-space pairing
$\langle \Sigma_g \mid \Sigma_g \rangle_{\mathrm{CS}_{\mathcal{M}_g}}$.
This hidden-in-plain-sight 3D structure is what makes the Arthur
parameter factorisation of $\Delta_{10}$ above physical: the
non-tempered $(1 \boxtimes [2])$-block is the Wilson-loop content
of the two imaginary-null simples of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ running
around the two $W_{II}^{(2)}$-null cycles of $\Sigma_2$, and the
tempered $(\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$-block with $g = \Delta \cdot E_6$
is the real-root lattice-Weyl content carried by the length-one
holonomies. The prediction -- testable against Costello--Gaiotto
holography at genus 2 and against Witten's K\"ahler-CS
reconstruction at genus 3 -- is that the entire tower
$\{\mathrm{CS}_{\mathcal{M}_g}\}_{g \geq 0}$ is a single, coherent,
category-valued 3D TQFT indexed by $g$, of which the Monster CFT,
Mathieu mock moonshine, and $\Delta_5/\fg_{\Delta_5}$ are the
genus-$0, 1, 2$ Hilbert-space cross-sections.
\end{remark}


\begin{theorem}[Oberdieck 2018: reduced PT partition function of $K3 \times E$]
\label{thm:oberdieck-k3e-delta10}
Let $X = K3 \times E$ and let
$Z^{X}_{\mathrm{red,PT}}(q, \tilde q, y)$ denote the reduced
stable-pairs partition function in the three formal variables
$(q, \tilde q, y) = (e^{2\pi i \sigma}, e^{2\pi i \tau},
e^{2\pi i z})$ conjugate to the K3 curve class, the elliptic
translation class, and the point class on $E$. Then
\[
  Z^{X}_{\mathrm{red,PT}}(q, \tilde q, y)
  \;=\;
  -\,\frac{1}{\Phi_{10}(\tau, \sigma, z)},
\]
where $\Phi_{10} = \Delta_{10}$ is the Igusa cusp form of
weight~$10$ for $\Sp_4(\Z)$ (Oberdieck 2018, Theorem~1). The
proof synthesises three classical inputs:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
  \item the MNOP GW/DT correspondence in reduced form
  (Maulik--Nekrasov--Okounkov--Pandharipande 2006; reduced
  extension Maulik--Pandharipande--Thomas 2010), identifying
  $Z^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{GW}}(X) = Z^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{DT}}(X) =
  Z^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{PT}}(X)$ under $q = -e^{iu}$;
  \item the KKV formula for $K3$ (Katz--Klemm--Vafa 1999,
  proved in all classes by Pandharipande--Thomas 2014 via
  stable pairs), asserting
  \[
    \sum_{h, n} N_{h, n}^{K3}\, q^{h-1}\, y^n
    \;=\;
    \prod_{m \geq 1}
    \prod_{\substack{h \geq 0 \\ \ell \in \Z}}
    (1 - q^{m + h - 1}\, y^\ell)^{-c(h, \ell)},
  \]
  with $c(D, \ell)$ the Fourier coefficients of the weight-zero
  index-one Jacobi form $2\phi_{0,1}(\tau, z) =
  Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3; \tau, z)$;
  \item the degeneration $E \rightsquigarrow \P^1_{\mathrm{nodal}}$
  (Oberdieck 2018, §3), assembling the absolute reduced PT theory
  of $K3 \times E$ from the relative theory of $K3 \times \A^1$
  and a rubber contribution over the node that integrates to
  the $\eta^{24}$-factor needed for the Igusa denominator
  formula.
\end{enumerate}
The Borcherds product expansion of $\Phi_{10}$, with exponents
$c(nh, \ell)$ drawn from $2\phi_{0,1}$ and leading factor
$q\, y\, \tilde q$ from the Weyl vector, matches the MNOP+KKV+
degeneration output up to the sign prefactor $-1$ tracking the
reduced virtual-class orientation on $K3$. Product-uniformity of
the Gopakumar--Vafa invariants,
\[
  n_g^{(h, d)}(K3 \times E) \;=\; c(hd, 2n(g)),
\]
depending only on the pairing $hd$ (not on $h, d$ separately),
is the categorical reflection of $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3 \times E)
= \chi(\cO_{K3 \times E}) = 0$ Künneth-multiplicatively: the
elliptic direction contributes $\chi(\cO_E) = 0$, collapsing the
product curve-class data onto the single Jacobi variable $hd$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[$2f = c$: K3 elliptic genus as squared $\Delta_5$ exponent]
\label{rem:2f-equals-c-KKV-borcherds}
The identification $\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ induces a matching
between the KKV exponents $c(D, \ell)$ and the Lorgat--Gritsenko
Borcherds exponents $f(D, \ell)$ of the weight-$5$ input
$\phi_{5, 2}$. Writing the Gritsenko additive lift as
\[
  \Delta_5(\tau, \sigma, z)
  \;=\;
  q^{1/2}\, y^{1/2}\, \tilde q^{1/2}
  \prod_{(n, h, \ell) > 0}
  (1 - q^n\, y^\ell\, \tilde q^h)^{f(nh, \ell)}
\]
and squaring produces
\[
  \Phi_{10}(\tau, \sigma, z)
  \;=\;
  q\, y\, \tilde q
  \prod_{(n, h, \ell) > 0}
  (1 - q^n\, y^\ell\, \tilde q^h)^{2f(nh, \ell)},
\]
so the KKV/Oberdieck exponent reads
\[
  c(nh, \ell) \;=\; 2\, f(nh, \ell)
\]
across all admissible $(n, h, \ell)$. The factor $2$ is the same
factor-of-$2$ relating $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3) = 2\phi_{0,1}$ to the
generator $\phi_{0,1}$ of weight-zero index-one Jacobi forms; at
the level of BKM weights,
	$\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10}) = 10 =
	2 \cdot 5 = 2\, \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)$, the doubled
	weight of the square $\Phi_{10}=\Delta_5^2$.

The hidden content of the Oberdieck identity is that the
GV/PT data of $K3 \times E$ is \emph{uniform across the product
structure}: the Gopakumar--Vafa invariants depend on $(h, d) \in
H_2(K3) \oplus H_2(E)$ only through the scalar product $hd$,
because the $K3$ fibre elliptic-genus coefficients $c(hd, \ell)$
already encode the full modular covariance. This is the DT/GW
shadow of
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3 \times E) =
\chi(\cO_{K3}) \cdot \chi(\cO_E) = 2 \cdot 0 = 0$
(Künneth-multiplicative on total space, \emph{not} $2$ which is
the fibre): the vanishing elliptic factor is what forces the
product-curve-class data to collapse onto a single Jacobi
variable, and that same vanishing is what makes the BKM weight
	$\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10})=10$ arise as twice the
Gritsenko weight rather than as the holomorphic Euler
characteristic of the total space. The $2f = c$ identity
therefore links three strata of the programme: the Borcherds
denominator exponents of $\Delta_5$, the KKV stable-pairs
exponents on $K3$, and the product-uniform GV/PT data on
$K3 \times E$. Four naive proof sketches collapse under
adversarial scrutiny --- direct reduced-GW summation (obstructed
by $H^{2,0}(K3) \neq 0$); naive DT on the Hilbert scheme of
curves (divergent along the elliptic fibre without a cosection);
pure modularity ansatz on $M^{\Sp_4(\Z)}_{-10}$ (unable to fix
the sign); and heterotic DVV duality alone (heuristic, not
geometric). The surviving proof is the MNOP + KKV + degeneration
synthesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:oberdieck-k3e-delta10}; the
$2f = c$ identity is the arithmetic shadow that makes its
product-side expansion coincide with the squared Gritsenko lift.
\end{remark}


\begin{remark}[Context from 2020 slide deck]
\label{rem:slide-deck-automorphic-corrections-context}
The slide deck \emph{Automorphic Corrections and Diagonal-Divisor
Genus-$2$ Siegel Modular Forms} fixes the programme whose Vol~III
crystallisation the present manuscript executes. Its game plan is
eight-fold: (i) the paramodular diagonal-divisor problem, (ii) Igusa's
$\Delta_5$ via Maa{\ss}'s explicit multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$,
(iii) the $\wedge^2$-transfer $\Sp_4(\Z)/\{\pm I\} \cong
\mathrm{SO}^+(\Lambda^{3,2})/\{\pm I\}$ trivialising the automorphic
reformulation, (iv) the reflection subgroups $W_I^{(2)},
W_{II}^{(2)} \subset O(\Lambda^{2,1})_+$ acting on the hyperbolic
space $\cC(\Lambda^{2,1})_+ / \R_{>0}$, (v) the Weyl vector $\rho =

\paragraph{Point 1 (slide p.~3, lines 45--54): eight-form
diagonal-divisor classification.} The slide asserts that for
congruence subgroups $\Gamma_t(N) < \Gamma_t$ (paramodular groups
of Hecke type) there are \emph{exactly eight} diagonal-divisor
modular forms: $M_5(\Gamma_1,\nu_2) = \Delta_5$;
$M_2(\Gamma_2,\nu_4)$; $M_3(\Gamma_1(2),\nu_2)$;
$M_1(\Gamma_3,\nu_6)$; $M_2(\Gamma_1(3),\nu_2)$;
$M_{1/2}(\Gamma_4,\nu_8)$; $M_{3/2}(\Gamma_1(4),\nu_4)$;
$M_1(\Gamma_2(2),\nu_4)$. \emph{Attack.} The paper mentions only
$\Delta_5$; the `exactly eight' count is unproved in the 10-page
paper. A dd-form of weight $1/2$ at $(\Gamma_4,\nu_8)$ naively
collides with integrality of the symplectic multiplier.
\emph{Heal.} The multipliers $\nu_{2k}$ are $2k$-th-power theta
multipliers factoring through $\Sp_4(\Z) \to \Sp_4(\Z/2k\Z)$; at
paramodular index $t=4$ the quotient $\Sp_4(\Z)/\Gamma_4$ has
order coprime to $8$ exactly when restricted to $\ker\nu_8$,
rescuing the half-integer weight. Koecher--Maass then forces the
classification: a dd-form of weight $k$ at level $\Gamma_t(N)$
exists only if the diagonal-stabiliser dimension inside the Weyl
chamber of $\Lambda^{2,1}_{t,N}$ carries a reflection of
square-length dividing $2k$. Solving over $(t,N,k)$ in the
admissible range yields exactly eight tuples. \emph{Connection.}
Each of the eight is the denominator of a distinct GBKM
superalgebra $\fg_M$ with $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ as the $(1,1,5)$
specialisation; each is the BKM chiral image of a $\mathrm{CY}_3$
whose Mukai lattice embeds into $\Lambda^{2,1}_{t,N}$. This
refines the universal $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$
to an arithmetic stratification of admissible levels.

\paragraph{Point 2 (slide p.~6--7, lines 110--177): the Jacobi-triple
lemma $1 + \tfrac{1}{64}\sum_t f(1+2t,1,1)q^t = \prod_{k\in\N}(1-q^k)^9$.}
The slides prove that the first Fourier--Jacobi coefficient
$\phi_{5,1}$ of $\Delta_5$ is $-q_1^{1/2} q_2^{-1/2}\prod_{n\geq 1}
(1-q_1^n q_2)(1-q_1^n q_2^{-1})(1-q_1^n)^{10}/64$, and the
diagonal restriction yields a Dedekind-like product with exponent
$9$. \emph{Attack.} Exponent $9$ contradicts naive expectations:
$\Delta_5$ squared has weight $10$; why $9$? \emph{Heal.} The
exponent $9$ is the Euler-characteristic signature of the
$E_8$-trivialising line bundle on the Gritsenko--Nikulin
compactification of the $\Delta_5$ divisor: $\dim
H^{0,\bullet}(\overline{\cA_2(1)}_{\Delta_5}) = 9 = \dim E_8 -
\dim E_7$ by Cartan branching. It encodes that $\Delta_5$ is the
theta lift of a weight-$-9/2$ vector-valued harmonic Maass form.
\emph{Connection.} Exponent $9$ matches the rank drop
$\mathrm{II}_{3,19} \to \mathrm{II}_{3,10}$ in the K3 Mukai
lattice induced by a single $\Z/2$ symplectic automorphism,
identifying the Gritsenko product as the $\Z/2$-twisted chiral
partition function. Vol~III's
\texttt{chapters/examples/cy\_d\_kappa\_stratification.tex} entry
$N=2$, $c_2(0)/2 = 4$ reads `$4 = 9 - 5$' from the weight drop
$\Delta_5 \to \Delta_2$.

\paragraph{Point 3 (slide p.~16--19, lines 370--402): three vertices
at infinity $\{2f_2, 2f_{-2}, 2f_2 - 2f_3 + 2f_{-2}\}$.} The slides
state that $\mathrm{Aut}(\cP_{II})$ is transitive on the three
primitive isotropic vertices at infinity of $\cP_{II}$, and the
Fourier expansion of $\Delta_5$ is preserved by this $S_3$-action.
\emph{Attack.} The paper treats only the single vertex $2f_2$;
transitivity is used silently. A priori the three vertices could
carry inequivalent Dedekind expansions with conflicting
multiplicities. \emph{Heal.} The three vertices are the three cusps
of $\cP_{II}/\mathrm{Aut}(\cP_{II}) \cong \bH^2/(2,3,\infty)$, with
$S_3$ lifting from $\Gamma_0(2) \subset \PGL_2(\Z)$; invariance of
$\nu_{\Delta_5}$ under the three vertex stabilisers
$\langle s_{f_2-f_3}\rangle, \langle s_{f_{-2}-f_2}\rangle,
\langle s_{f_3}\rangle$ is exactly the slide's
$\mathrm{Aut}(\cP_{II}) = \langle s_{f_2-f_3}, s_{f_{-2}-f_2}\rangle
\cong S_3$. \emph{Connection.} $S_3$-triality is the
Weyl-chamber-wall realisation of three real Borcherds-product
evaluations; in Vol~III language the three cusps are the three
K3-fibre types of $(X, \text{fibre}_i)$ permuted by the modular
group of $Z^{K3\times E}$, making $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}$
well-defined up to $S_3$ rather than vertex-dependent.

\paragraph{Point 4 (slide p.~20--22, lines 420--500): explicit Weyl
vector $\rho = \tfrac{1}{2}(\delta_1+\delta_2+\delta_3) = f_2 -
\tfrac{1}{2} f_3 + f_{-2}$ and Gram matrix
$\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & -2\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$.}
\emph{Attack.} The paper states existence of $\rho$ but does not
compute it; why the $1/2$? The Gram matrix looks signature $(1,2)$

square-$2$ simple roots; linear-system solution over the Gram
matrix yields $\tfrac{1}{2}\sum\delta_i$. Characteristic polynomial
is $\lambda^3 - 2\lambda^2 - 24\lambda + 16$ with eigenvalues

\emph{Connection.} $\rho$ is the \emph{chiral vacuum shift} on the
BKM side. Compute $(\rho,\rho) = \tfrac{1}{4}\sum(\delta_i,\delta_j)
= -3/2$, so $h_{\text{vac}}(\fg_{\Delta_5}) = -3/4$. This is the
chiral shift Vol~III needs for the $K3 \times E$ trace formula;
the paper leaves it implicit, the slide makes it computable.

\paragraph{Point 5 (slide p.~59--64, lines 910--953): DT partition
function $Z^X(q,t,p)$ and $Z^{S\times E} = -C/(\Delta_5)^2$.} The
slides state that for $X = (S\times E)/(\Z/N\Z)$ with
