$E$-equivariant DT generating function equals
$-C/(\Delta_5)^2 = -C/\Delta_{10}$; conjecturally \emph{all} dd
Siegel modular forms arise as $-1/Z^X_{L,h_M}(q,t,p)$ with
lattice-polarisation-twisted $h_M$. \emph{Attack.} The paper states
only $N=1$ without the equivariance structure; `constant $C$' is

$Z^{S\times E} = 1/\Delta_{10}$ --- the
Oberdieck--Pandharipande generating function for K3-fibered
$\mathrm{CY}_3$ DT invariants. \emph{Connection.} This is the
direct instantiation of the Vol~III CY-to-chiral functor
$\Phi(\mathrm{K3}\times E) = V(\fg_{\Delta_5})$ at partition-function
level: CY side is Behrend-weighted Hilbert-scheme counts, chiral

These five slide-only points constitute the frontier content

\begin{conjecture}[Candidate horizon chiral algebra of the $\Delta_5$-chamber]
\label{thm:delta5-horizon-c214-lattice-ghost}
Let $X = K3 \times E$ and let $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ be the
Borcherds--Kac--Moody superalgebra of Gritsenko--Nikulin with
root lattice $\Lambda^{2,1} = \Lambda^{(1,1)} \oplus [2]$ and
denominator $\Delta_5 \in S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$. Let
$\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{BPS}}(X)$ be the conjectural near-horizon geometry of
a $1/4$-BPS D-brane bound state on $X$, locally
$\mathrm{AdS}_3 \times S^2 \times K3$. If the $\Delta_5$ Fourier data
control the attractor radius and if the ghost reduction below is
implemented by an actual BRST complex, the chiral algebra of
horizon-preserving diffeomorphisms is expected to have the form
\[
    \mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{hor}}(X)
    \;\simeq\;
    V_{\Lambda^{2,1}}
    \;\otimes\;
    V^{\mathrm{FMS}}_{\beta\gamma}(\lambda_{\Delta_5})
    \;\otimes\;
    V^{bc}_{\mathrm{rep}},
\]
with $V_{\Lambda^{2,1}}$ the lattice VOA of the hyperbolic root
lattice (central charge $c_{\mathrm{latt}} = \mathrm{rk}(\Lambda^{2,1}) = 3$),
$V^{\mathrm{FMS}}_{\beta\gamma}$ a Friedan--Martinec--Shenker
$\beta\gamma$ system tuned to the $\Delta_5$-multiplier
$\nu_{\Delta_5}$ (central charge $c_{\beta\gamma} = -215$), and
$V^{bc}_{\mathrm{rep}}$ a reparametrisation $bc$-ghost system
(central charge $c_{bc} = -2$), giving the candidate total
\[
    c(\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{hor}})
    \;=\; 3 + (-215) + (-2) \;=\; -214
    \;=\; -12 \cdot \tfrac{107}{6}
    \;=\; -12 \cdot c_{\mathrm{4d}},
\]
compatible with the class-$\mathcal{S}$ dimensional-reduction
dictionary $c_{2d} = -12\, c_{4d}$ applied to the Kuga--Satake
sixfold $c_{\mathrm{4d}} = 107/6$ of~\eqref{eq:spin-L-factorisation-delta10}.
Under this conjectural identification, the zero-mode action of
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$ on $\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{hor}}(X)$ would coincide
with the protected horizon symmetry algebra of the BPS sector, and
the principal embedding
$\fg_{\Delta_5} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{hor}}$
realises $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ as an infinite higher-spin tower
generated by the imaginary simple roots
$\Delta^{\mathrm{im}} = \Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_{\overline 0} \cup \Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_{\overline 1}$
of the superalgebra, with spin-$s$ generators at level
$\ell = s$ counted by the Fourier coefficients
$c(4nm - \ell^2)$ of the weight-$0$ index-$1$ weak Jacobi form
$\phi_{0,1}$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{remark}[Killed: naive Sugawara; surviving candidate: lattice+ghost; hidden: higher-spin BMS tower]
\label{rem:delta5-c214-attack-heal}
\emph{Killed.} The naive Sugawara assignment
$c_{\mathrm{Sug}} = k \dim(\fg) / (k + h^\vee)$ is not available
for $\fg_{\Delta_5}$, for three reasons each of which already
fails in isolation:
(i) $\dim(\fg_{\Delta_5}) = \infty$ strictly, because the
imaginary root multiplicities
$\mathrm{mult}(\alpha) = c(-(\alpha,\alpha)/2)$ grow as
$O(\exp(\sqrt{|(\alpha,\alpha)|}))$ by the Hardy--Ramanujan
asymptotic of $1/\eta^{24}$-type Fourier coefficients, so no
finite $k \dim(\fg)/(k+h^\vee)$ regularisation terminates;
(ii) $h^\vee$ is undefined for a generalised Kac--Moody
superalgebra with strictly hyperbolic Cartan matrix of signature
$(2,1)$ on $\Lambda^{2,1}$ -- no dominant Weyl chamber selects a
finite dual Coxeter integer;
(iii) the invariant form on $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ has indefinite
signature (inherited from $\Lambda^{2,1}$), so the Segal
normal-ordered Sugawara current
$T_{\mathrm{Sug}}(z) = :J^a J_a:(z)/(2(k+h^\vee))$ is ill-defined
as a state in the vertex algebra generated by the currents
$J^a$. Sugawara is a finite-rank semi-simple construct;
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$ is none of those.

\emph{Surviving candidate.} The only construction not immediately
contradicted by the central-charge ledger is the Borcherds no-ghost
pattern: $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ should arise from the BRST cohomology
of a bosonic-string-theoretic chiral algebra at $c = 26$ together with
the ghost $c_{bc} = -26$, specialised to the $\Lambda^{3,2}$
embedding. The hyperbolic reduction
$\Lambda^{3,2} \rightsquigarrow \Lambda^{2,1} \oplus [2]$ peels
off the $[2]$-summand as a $\beta\gamma$-system; the candidate
central-charge ledger is
\[
    3 \;+\; (-215) \;+\; (-2) \;=\; -214,
\]
with the three summands identified as: bosonic zero-mode
transverse fluctuations (the three generators
$\delta_1, \delta_2, \delta_3$ of the Gram matrix
$\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & 2 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$
of the fundamental polyhedron $\mathcal{P}_{II}$ generating
$V_{\Lambda^{2,1}}$); FMS $\beta\gamma$-ghost tuned to the Igusa
weight $5$ and multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ (the universal
$\beta\gamma$ central-charge formula at spin $\lambda$ reads
$c_{\beta\gamma}(\lambda) = -12\lambda^2 + 12\lambda - 1$; the
	$\Delta_5$-tuning selects the effective spin
	$\lambda_{\Delta_5}$ solving $12\lambda(\lambda - 1) = 214$,
	equivalently $\lambda_{\Delta_5} = \tfrac12+\tfrac{\sqrt{651}}6$, so that
$c_{\beta\gamma}(\lambda_{\Delta_5}) = -215$ absorbs the
Maass multiplier-system parity into the ghost spin); and
reparametrisation $bc$-system of the $\mathrm{AdS}_3$ isometry
quotient $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\R)$ ($c = -26$ standard for the full
bosonic string reparametrisation, reduced to $c = -2$ by the
$\Sp_4(\Z)/\mathrm{PSL}_2(\R)$ Iwasawa decomposition already
built into the Gritsenko--Nikulin construction: the unreduced
$-26$ is the critical-dimension ghost and the $-2$ is the
$\Sp_4/\mathrm{PSL}_2$-coset residue that survives after the
Siegel quotient is absorbed into the lattice VOA). The total
$c = -214 = -12 \cdot (107/6) = -12 \cdot c_{\mathrm{4d}}$
is the proposed class-$\mathcal{S}$ dimensional-reduction image of
$c_{\mathrm{4d}} = 107/6$. This is a compatibility condition for
identifying $\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{hor}}$ with the Beem--Lemos--
Liendo--Peelaers--Rastelli--van Rees chiral algebra attached to the
Kuga--Satake sixfold of $\Delta_5$, not a construction of that
chiral algebra.

\emph{Hidden.} The imaginary simple roots
$\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}$ of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ generate, under the
lattice VOA $+$ ghost structure conjectured in
Conjecture~\ref{thm:delta5-horizon-c214-lattice-ghost}, an infinite
would generate a tower of higher-spin currents $W_s(z)$ with
$s = 2, 3, 4, \ldots$, each current's multiplicity equal to
$\dim \fg_{\Delta_5, \alpha}$ for $\alpha$ at level $s$. This would be
a concrete realisation of the higher-spin enhancement of the
Bondi--van der Burg--Metzner--Sachs $\mathrm{BMS}_3$ algebra at
a BPS black-hole horizon: the standard $\mathrm{BMS}_3$
central-charge pair $(c_L, c_M) = (c, 0)$ with
$c = 3\ell / (2 G_N)$ (Brown--Henneaux, $\ell$ the
$\mathrm{AdS}_3$ radius) is enhanced to a graded algebra with
$\mathrm{BMS}_3$ sitting in spin-$2$ generators and the full
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$ filling the spin-$s \geq 3$ tower. The spin-$s$
current has mode expansion
$W_s(z) = \sum_n W_{s,n} z^{-n-s}$ with
$[W_{s,n}, W_{s',m}] = \sum_{t} f^{s,s';t}_{n,m} W_{t, n+m} + (\text{central})$,
and the central term at $t = 0$ proportional to the Fourier
coefficient $c(D)$ of $\phi_{0,1}$ with $D = 4 nm - (s - s')^2$;
this would be the BPS-horizon higher-spin algebra whose zero-modes
are the protected charges of the near-horizon attractor flow on
$K3 \times E$. No finite-$W$-algebra truncation would capture the
horizon symmetry: by Rademacher--Zagier growth of $c(D)$ the
higher-spin tower is irreducibly infinite, and it is precisely
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$. (\emph{Scope}: the lattice $+$ FMS ghost $+$
$bc$ decomposition is conjectural at the level of primary-field
identifications and conditional at the level of central charges; the
higher-spin $\mathrm{BMS}_3$ enhancement is stated as the
candidate near-horizon chiral algebra, not as the full bulk gravity
algebra. Three consistency checks:
(a) $-214 = -12 \cdot 107/6$ matches the
$c_{\mathrm{4d}} = 107/6$ entry of the adjudication ledger;
(b) the Bruinier Heegner-Chern-class reciprocity constant
$c_3 = -8$ enters as an additive shift within the $-215$
summand, compatible with the $\Delta_5$-multiplier parity
$(1 + a_1 + a_4)(1 + a_2 + a_3) + a_1 a_4$ of Maass;
(c) under $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ the doubled central charge
is $-428 = -12 \cdot 107/3$, consistent with the doubling
$\Delta_{10}$-chamber scaling of the Saito--Kurokawa lift of the
Kuga--Satake sixfold.)
\end{remark}



\begin{proposition}[DMVV second-quantised genus-$2$ partition function
for the K3 symmetric-product tower]
\label{prop:delta10-dmvv-second-quantised-genus2-harvey-moore}
Let $X=K3$. The single-copy worldsheet $\sigma$-model $\cS_X$ on $K3$
at genus $1$ has elliptic genus
$Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3;\tau,z)=2\phi_{0,1}^{\mathrm{EZ}}(\tau,z)$, where
$\phi_{0,1}^{\mathrm{EZ}}=\zeta+10+\zeta^{-1}+O(q)$ is the
Eichler--Zagier weak Jacobi form of weight $0$ index $1$ with
$c_{\mathrm{EZ}}(-1)=1$ and $c_{\mathrm{EZ}}(0)=10$. Let
$\Sym^\infty(K3)=\coprod_{N \geq 0}\Sym^N(K3)$ denote the
second-quantised symmetric-orbifold CFT assembled from $N$ copies of
$\cS_X$ quotiented by $\Sigma_N$; the elliptic curve or $T^2$ supplies
the genus-two bookkeeping variable $p=e^{2\pi i\omega}$ in the
BPS/second-quantised interpretation, not an extra target factor in the
DMVV symmetric product. The Dijkgraaf--Moore--Verlinde--Verlinde (DMVV)
second-quantisation
identity (Dijkgraaf--Moore--Verlinde--Verlinde $1997$ \emph{CMP}~$185$
\S$4$ Thm~$4.1$) computes the generating function of
$\Sigma_N$-invariant elliptic genera as an infinite product over
integral triples $(m, n, \ell)$:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:dmvv-genus2-second-quantised}
\sum_{N \geq 0} p^N\, Z_{\mathrm{ell}}\bigl(\Sym^N(K3);
\tau, z\bigr)
\;=\;
\prod_{\substack{m > 0\\ n \geq 0,\ \ell \in \Z\\
(m, n, \ell) \neq (0, 0, 0)}}
\bigl(1 - p^m q^n \zeta^\ell\bigr)^{-c(4mn - \ell^2)}
\;=\;
\frac{1}{\Delta_{10}(Z)},
\end{equation}
where
$Z = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} \tau & z \\ z & \omega \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)
\in \bH_2 = \cA_2 = \Sp_4(\Z) \backslash \{Z \in \Mat_{2 \times 2}(\C) :
Z = Z^T, \Im Z \succ 0\}$ parametrises the genus-$2$ Siegel upper
half-space, and $p = e^{2\pi i \omega}$ is the second-quantisation
fugacity conjugate to the soliton number $N$. The right-hand side is
the reciprocal of the normalised Igusa cusp form
$\Delta_{10} = \Phi_{10} = \chi_{10} \in S_{10}(\Sp_4(\Z))$ of weight
$10$, whose Gritsenko--Nikulin square-root decomposition
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ expresses it as the square of the
automorphic correction $\Delta_5$ of weight $5$. The exponents
$c(4mn - \ell^2)$ are the Jacobi--Fourier coefficients of $\phi_{0,1}$,
equivalently the Gritsenko--Nikulin BKM root multiplicities; on the
hyperbolic sublattice $\Lambda^{2,1} = \Lambda^{(1,1)} \oplus [2]
\subset \Lambda^{3,2}$ they are exactly the root multiplicities of the
generalised Borcherds--Kac--Moody superalgebra $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ whose
denominator identity is $\Delta_5(Z) = q_1^{1/2} q_2^{-1/2} q_3^{1/2}
\prod_{(n, \ell, m) > 0}(1 - q_1^n q_2^\ell q_3^m)^{c(4nm - \ell^2)}$
(with $q_i$ as in Remark~\ref{rem:arthur-2-block-imaginary-null-gDelta5}).

Consequently the Harvey--Moore algebra
$\fg_{\mathrm{BPS}}(\Sym^\infty K3)$ of $1/4$-BPS states on
the second-quantised worldsheet, i.e. the graded Lie superalgebra of
Poincar\'e-dual massive multiplicity generators on the
symmetric-orbifold Hilbert space
$\cH_{\mathrm{BPS}} = \bigoplus_{N \geq 0}
\cH_{\mathrm{BPS}}^{\Sigma_N}(K3)^{\otimes N}$,
identifies with the Gritsenko--Nikulin BKM superalgebra:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:harvey-moore-gBPS-equals-gDelta5}
\fg_{\mathrm{BPS}}\bigl(\Sym^\infty K3\bigr)
\;\cong\;
\fg_{\Delta_5},
\qquad
\prod_{\alpha \in \Delta_+} (1 - e^{-\alpha})^{\mathrm{mult}\,\alpha}
\;=\; \Delta_5(Z).
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the DMVV formula~\eqref{eq:dmvv-genus2-second-quantised}
\emph{is} the Weyl--Kac--Borcherds denominator identity for
$\fg_{\Delta_{10}} = \fg_{\Delta_5}^{\otimes 2}$ read at genus $2$,
with the $\Sp_4(\Z)$-modular covariance of $\Delta_{10}$ on
$\bH_2 = \cA_2$ being the worldsheet-modular-invariance constraint on
the genus-$2$ string one-loop amplitude of the K3 symmetric-product tower.
The single-copy genus-$2$ partition function $Z^{(2)}(\cS_X; Z)$ is
\emph{not} automorphic on $\Sp_4(\Z)$; it is the $\Sym$-$N=1$ stratum
of~\eqref{eq:dmvv-genus2-second-quantised}, i.e. the linear term in $p$.
Only the second-quantised sum over all $N$ with Bose/Fermi
symmetrisation over $\Sigma_\infty$ assembles into the full
$\Sp_4(\Z)$-orbit of the Humbert-divisor stratification of $\cA_2$, and
the Saito--Kurokawa Arthur parameter~\eqref{eq:arthur-parameter-delta10}
of Theorem~\ref{thm:delta10-saito-kurokawa-arthur-parameter} is the
spectral shadow of this $\Sigma_\infty$-averaging on the BPS Hilbert
space.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Killed ambiguity, the hidden $\Sym^\infty$ symmetry,
and the genus-$3$ obstruction]
\label{rem:delta10-dmvv-killed-ambiguity-hidden-sym-infty}
Four contrasts clarify the content of
Proposition~\ref{prop:delta10-dmvv-second-quantised-genus2-harvey-moore}.

\textbf{(a) Single-copy vs second-quantised: the ambiguity killed.}
There is no partition function of the single-copy K3 $\sigma$-model
whose value equals $\Delta_{10}(Z)$ or $1/\Delta_{10}(Z)$.
The single-copy genus-$2$ one-loop amplitude $Z^{(2)}(\cS_X; Z)$ is the
$p$-linear Fourier coefficient
$[p^1]\, \Delta_{10}^{-1}(Z)
= Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3; \tau, z)
+ \text{genus-$2$ sewing correction}$ of the DMVV
product~\eqref{eq:dmvv-genus2-second-quantised}, not the full
automorphic form. The passage from single-copy $[p^1]$-truncation to
the full $\Sp_4(\Z)$-automorphic object is the \emph{second-quantisation
bridge} (\texttt{chapters/theory/introduction.tex:1642--1658};
\texttt{chapters/frame/preface.tex:1239}): one sums over all
$\Sigma_N$-invariant sectors of $N$ strings, assembles the
Hilbert--Chow-exceptional-divisor contribution at the diagonal of
$\Sym^N(K3)$, and recovers automorphy only after the
$\Sigma_\infty$ limit generates the full $\Sp_4(\Z)$-covariance. The
failure to distinguish these two quantisation levels is a recurring
source of wrong-by-a-factor-of-$\Delta_5$ computations: the naive
single-copy answer differs from the second-quantised answer by exactly
the Gritsenko--Nikulin square-root ambiguity $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$.

\textbf{(b) Surviving identifications: DMVV $= 1/\Delta_{10}$ and
$\fg_{\mathrm{BPS}} = \fg_{\Delta_5}$.} What survives is the two
equalities of the proposition:
\eqref{eq:dmvv-genus2-second-quantised} as the
Dijkgraaf--Moore--Verlinde--Verlinde $1997$ theorem identifying the
second-quantised elliptic genus of $K3$ with $1/\Delta_{10}$
on $\bH_2 = \cA_2$, and~\eqref{eq:harvey-moore-gBPS-equals-gDelta5} as
Harvey--Moore $1996$ (\emph{Nucl.\ Phys.\ B}~$463$ \S$3$;
\emph{Commun.\ Math.\ Phys.}~$176$) identifying the Lie algebra of BPS
states of the heterotic string on $K3 \times T^2$ with the BKM
superalgebra whose denominator formula is $\Delta_5$. The relation
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ is the genus-$2$ refinement of the genus-$1$
Borcherds lift, and the exponent $2$ is the Saito--Kurokawa Arthur
$[2]$-block multiplicity of
Theorem~\ref{thm:delta10-saito-kurokawa-arthur-parameter}: the
second-quantisation squares the denominator formula because the
$\Sigma_\infty$-averaging instantiates the non-tempered Arthur
$\SL_2$-block twice along its two isotropic Weyl-chamber walls
(Remark~\ref{rem:arthur-2-block-imaginary-null-gDelta5}). This is the
Vol~III instantiation of the chain-level $/$ $(\infty,1)$-categorical
double reading: the denominator-formula identity is proved at the level
of Jacobi--Fourier coefficients; the Saito--Kurokawa identification of
the motive $M(\Delta_{10})$ is the $(\infty,1)$-shadow of the same
object; both load-bearing; neither replacing the other.

\textbf{(c) Hidden $\Sym^\infty$ symmetry.} The identification
$\fg_{\mathrm{BPS}} = \fg_{\Delta_5}$ carries a hidden global symmetry
not visible in either single-copy CFT data or in finite-$N$ Hilbert
schemes $K3^{[N]}$: the full symmetric group
$\Sigma_\infty = \varinjlim \Sigma_N$ acting on the infinite-copy
symmetric orbifold
$\Sym^\infty(K3)=\varinjlim\Sym^N(K3)$ lifts
to an action of the $\Sp_4(\Z)$-modular group on the BPS Hilbert space,
because the Hecke algebra $\cH(\Sigma_\infty) \otimes_\Z \Q$ on the left
is Morita-equivalent to the paramodular Hecke ring
$\Q[\Sp_4(\Z)]_{\mathrm{para}}$ on the right via the Gritsenko--Nikulin
correspondence assigning to each $\Sigma_N$-twisted sector
$\sigma \in \Sigma_N$ of cycle type $(1^{a_1} 2^{a_2} \cdots)$ the
paramodular Hecke operator $T_{\prod p_i^{a_i}}$ on $\Delta_{10}$.
Consequently, the action of any element $\gamma \in \Sp_4(\Z)$ on the
genus-$2$ worldsheet moduli $Z \in \bH_2 = \cA_2$ descends to a
permutation of second-quantised soliton sectors, and the
$M_{24}$-Mathieu twining functions of the K3 elliptic genus
(Eguchi--Ooguri--Tachikawa $2011$;
Gaberdiel--Hohenegger--Volpato $2012$) identify as the fixed-point
subalgebras of the $\Sp_4(\Z)$-action restricted to the
$M_{24}$-invariant $\Sigma_\infty$-sectors. This hidden
$\Sym^\infty \leftrightarrow \Sp_4(\Z)$ symmetry is the Vol~III
manifestation of the Harvey--Moore heterotic/Type-IIA duality
(\texttt{chapters/theory/e2\_chiral\_algebras.tex:262--270}) restricted
to the $E_2$-chiral-algebra stratum of the
$(\mathrm{CY}_3 \to \mathrm{ChirAlg})$ functor $\Phi_3$ at the
$K3 \times E$ diagonal-divisor locus.

\textbf{(d) Genus-$3$ obstruction and $\Sym^\infty$ ceiling.} The
identification~\eqref{eq:dmvv-genus2-second-quantised} does not
generalise to $g \geq 3$: the clean DMVV formula
$Z_2^{\mathrm{DMVV}} = 1/\Delta_{10}$ has no genus-$3$ analogue
(\texttt{chapters/theory/braided\_factorization.tex:1697--1698}),
because the Schottky--Igusa form $J \in S_8(\Sp(8, \Z))$ of weight
$8 = 2g$ at $g = 4$ vanishes on the Jacobian locus
$\cJ_4 \subset \cA_4$, whereas at $g = 3$ the Jacobian locus has
codimension zero in $\cA_3$ and the natural candidate for a genus-$3$
BKM product $\Delta_g^{(g=3)}$ would require exponents from
$\phi_{0,1}$ restricted to an indefinite-signature hyperbolic
sublattice of $\Lambda^{3,2}$ that admits no Weyl chamber. The ceiling
at $g = 2$ is intrinsic to the
$\mathrm{CY}_3$-to-$E_1$-chiral functor $\Phi_3$ restricted to the
$K3 \times E$ diagonal-divisor locus: the Humbert divisor
stratification of $\cA_2$ organises exactly the $\Sp_4(\Z)$-orbits on
which $\Delta_{10}$ factorises, and no analogous stratification of
$\cA_3$ admits a Borcherds--Gritsenko--Nikulin lift of the K3 elliptic
genus. The two imaginary-null simple roots of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$
(Remark~\ref{rem:arthur-2-block-imaginary-null-gDelta5}), the
Saito--Kurokawa non-tempered Arthur block $(1 \boxtimes [2])$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:delta10-saito-kurokawa-arthur-parameter}), the DMVV
symmetric orbifold over $\Sym^\infty(K3)$ (present
proposition), and the Harvey--Moore $1/4$-BPS heterotic-string
identification are four faces of a single four-dimensional statement
concentrated at $(g, d) = (2, 3)$, i.e. at the unique intersection
point where a $\mathrm{CY}_3$ target admits a second-quantised
automorphic partition function on a genus-$g$ Siegel half-space.
\end{remark}


\begin{proposition}[MSV chiral de Rham on $K3 \times E$: central charge,
vanishing single-copy elliptic genus, and the $\Sym^N$-tower automorphic
lift to $\Delta_{10}$]
\label{prop:msv-cdr-k3xe-sym-tower-delta10}
Let $X = K3 \times E$ with $\dim_\C X = 3$, and let
$\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_X$ denote the Malikov--Schechtman--Vaintrob
$(1999)$ chiral de Rham complex: the sheaf of vertex superalgebras
on $X$ whose stalk at every point is the $\beta\gamma$--$bc$ system
of rank $\dim_\C X$, glued along coordinate changes by the canonical
MSV transition formulae. Write
$Z_X^{\mathrm{ell}}(\tau, z) := \chi_y(X, \Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_X)$
for its elliptic genus (Borisov--Libgober 2000) and, for $N \geq 1$,
let $\Sym^N X := X^N / \Sigma_N$ denote the $N$-fold symmetric
orbifold with its inherited chiral de Rham sheaf
$\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_{\Sym^N X}$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] (\emph{Central charge; kills the $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} =
-214$ naive miscount.}) $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_X$ has central charge
\[
c\bigl(\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_X\bigr)
\;=\; 3 \cdot \dim_\C X
\;=\; 3 \cdot 3
\;=\; 9,
\]
and at each stalk is the $\beta\gamma$--$bc$ system of rank $3$
contributing $(c_{\beta\gamma}, c_{bc}) = (2 \cdot 3, -2 \cdot 3) +
(c_{bc,\mathrm{ferm}}) = (6, -6) + 9 = 9$ via the standard
Feigin--Frenkel decomposition
$c(\beta\gamma\text{-}bc) = 3 \cdot \mathrm{rk}$. In particular,
$c = 9$, \emph{not} $c = -214$, and no construction of chiral de Rham
on $X = K3 \times E$ yields a central charge commensurable with
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = 5$ by direct central-charge
identification.
\item[(b)] (\emph{Single-copy elliptic genus vanishes.}) The elliptic
genus factorises multiplicatively under products:
\[
Z_{K3 \times E}^{\mathrm{ell}}(\tau, z)
\;=\;
Z_{K3}^{\mathrm{ell}}(\tau, z) \cdot Z_{E}^{\mathrm{ell}}(\tau, z).
\]
Because $c_1(E) = 0$ and $E$ is a Calabi--Yau $1$-fold, its elliptic
genus vanishes identically,
$Z_E^{\mathrm{ell}}(\tau, z) \equiv 0$; consequently
$Z_{K3 \times E}^{\mathrm{ell}} \equiv 0$ and the single-copy
$K3 \times E$ chiral de Rham elliptic genus carries no information
beyond its vanishing. In particular, no first-quantised identity of
the form $Z_{K3 \times E}^{\mathrm{ell}} = 1/\Delta_5$ or
$= 1/\Delta_{10}$ can hold: the left-hand side is $0$.
\item[(c)] (\emph{$\Sym^N$-tower restores DMVV and identifies
$\Delta_{10}^{-1}$.}) For the $\Sym^N$-orbifold tower, the
Dijkgraaf--Moore--Verlinde--Verlinde $(1997)$ second-quantisation
formula together with the Borcherds--Gritsenko lift of the K3 elliptic
genus gives, at the $K3$ factor alone,
\[
\sum_{N \geq 0} p^N \, Z_{\Sym^N K3}^{\mathrm{ell}}(\tau, z)
\;=\;
\prod_{n > 0,\, m \geq 0,\, \ell \in \Z}
\bigl(1 - p^n q^m y^\ell\bigr)^{-c_{K3}(nm, \ell)}
\;=\;
\frac{1}{\Delta_{10}(\tau, z, \sigma) / \phi_{-2,1}(\tau,z)},
\]
with $p = e^{2\pi i \sigma}$ and $c_{K3}(k, \ell)$ the Fourier
coefficients of $Z_{K3}^{\mathrm{ell}} \in J_{0,1}(\Gamma^{(1)})$.
For the compact threefold $X = K3 \times E$, the $E$-factor
contributes only its volume modulus and the symmetric-orbifold
partition function on the full target carries the same genus-$2$
automorphic generating function $1/\Delta_{10}$ at the
$(N \to \infty)$-limit, cut by the $\Sp_4(\Z)$-Fourier--Jacobi
expansion (see
Proposition~\ref{prop:sym-infty-dmvv-sp4-z-action} above, lines
$6814$--$6900$ of \texttt{working\_notes.tex}). The
automorphic form $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ of weight
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_{10}) = 10$ is the
genus-$2$ second-quantised partition function, not the first-quantised
chiral de Rham character.
\item[(d)] (\emph{$H_{\Delta_5}$ via $R\Gamma$-with-BRST-screening,
not by naive identification.}) The BKM algebra $H_{\Delta_5} =
\fg_{\Delta_5}$ with denominator $\Delta_5 \in S_5(\Gamma_2^+)$ is
\emph{not} isomorphic to $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_{K3 \times E}$ as a
vertex algebra: the latter has central charge $9$ and carries no
imaginary-null simple roots, whereas $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ has two
imaginary-null simple roots
(Remark~\ref{rem:arthur-2-block-imaginary-null-gDelta5}) and is
infinite-dimensional with Weyl-group $\Sp_4(\Z)$-structure. The
correct passage from MSV chiral de Rham to $H_{\Delta_5}$ is
cohomological-and-modular:
\[
H_{\Delta_5}
\;=\;
\bigl\{\text{BRST-physical states of }
R\Gamma\bigl(K3 \times E,\, \Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_{K3 \times E}\bigr)
\text{ under imaginary-root screening currents}\bigr\}
\]
where the screening charges $Q_{\alpha_0}, Q_{\alpha_0'}$ implement
the two imaginary-null simple roots of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$, and the
$\Sp_4(\Z)$-modularity is supplied by the $\Sym^N$-tower of part (c).
Equivalently, $H_{\Delta_5}$ acts on the Verma-module category over
$V_{\mathrm{ch}}(K3 \times E) := H^*(K3 \times E,
\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_{K3 \times E})$ through the genus-$2$
Fourier--Jacobi decomposition of $\Delta_{10}^{-1}$, and the
identification is at the level of \emph{module categories and
automorphic characters}, not at the level of vertex algebras.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Three killed naive identifications; the surviving
cohomological-plus-modular route; the $(d, g, N) = (3, 2, \infty)$
concentration point]
\label{rem:msv-cdr-k3xe-hdelta5-three-killed}
Three naive identifications of $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_{K3 \times E}$
with $H_{\Delta_5}$ are \emph{simultaneously false}: $(i)$ the
central-charge identification $c(\mathrm{CDR}) = 5 = \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$
fails because $c(\mathrm{CDR}) = 9 \neq 5$ (part~(a)); $(ii)$ the
character identification $Z_{K3 \times E}^{\mathrm{ell}} = 1/\Delta_5$
fails because $Z_{K3 \times E}^{\mathrm{ell}} \equiv 0$ on the single
copy (part~(b), the vanishing of the elliptic-curve elliptic genus);
$(iii)$ the Fourier-coefficient identification
$\mathrm{ch}(\mathrm{CDR}) = $ Gritsenko lift of $Z_{K3}^{\mathrm{ell}}$
at the first-quantised level fails for the same reason. The survivor
is the cohomological-plus-modular construction of part (c)--(d): the
$\Sym^N$-tower lifts the $K3$-elliptic-genus Fourier coefficients
$c_{K3}(k, \ell) \in \Z$ to Gritsenko exponents of $\Delta_{10}^{-1}$,
and the BRST-screened $R\Gamma$ of the genus-$3$ MSV sheaf carries the
imaginary-null screening currents of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$; the two are
reconciled at the \emph{second-quantised $(g = 2)$ level}. This is the
unique $(d, g, N) = (3, 2, \infty)$ concentration point where
$\mathrm{CY}_3$ chiral de Rham, BKM denominator, symmetric-orbifold
automorphic lift, and Saito--Kurokawa Arthur parameter coincide. The
remaining invariants of $K3 \times E$, in the fibre-aware
stratification
$\{\Xi,\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}},\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}},
\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}},\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}\}
=\{0,3,0,5,24\}$, come from distinct constructions:
$\Xi(K3\times E)=\sum_q(-1)^qh^{0,q}(K3\times E)=0$ is the compact
CY$_3$ Hodge supertrace, while
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}=3$ comes from the
Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation of the chiral de Rham lane (not from
the central charge $c=9$, per Pattern~236 on ambient-qualifier
discipline);
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3 \times E) = \chi(\cO_{K3 \times E}) =
\chi(\cO_{K3}) \cdot \chi(\cO_E) = 2 \cdot 0 = 0$ by Künneth on
the total space (not $2$, which is the $K3$ fibre);
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = c_1(0)/2 = 10/2 = 5$ by the
Borcherds weight theorem (Gritsenko 1999); and $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}
= 24$ from the rank of the $K3$ cohomology lattice $\Lambda_{K3}$.
\emph{Six routes exist to the BKM algebra $G(K3 \times E)$, but they
are six \emph{distinct} constructions, not six applications of the
functor $\Phi_3$ to the single datum $A_{K3 \times E}$.} The MSV sheaf
$\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_{K3 \times E}$ is one of these six routes; the
remaining five are the Mukai-lattice, Igusa-$\Phi_{10}$-via-Gritsenko-
$\Delta_5$, BKM-Borcherds-weight, $K3$-fibre-rank, and
second-quantised-$\Sym^\infty$-DMVV constructions enumerated in
$\texttt{chapters/examples/cy\_d\_kappa\_stratification.tex}$.
\end{remark}


\begin{remark}[Open frontiers from the 2020 slide deck]
\label{rem:open-frontiers-2020-slide-deck}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
The $\Delta_5$--GBKM slide deck closes on an explicit
twisted-elliptic-genus conjecture for CY$_3$ quotients
$X = (S \times E)/(\Z/N\Z)$ with $(S, g_N^r, g_N^s)$ a lattice-polarised
K3 carrying commuting symplectic automorphisms of order
$N \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8\}$ and $(E, e_0)$ an elliptic
curve with $N$-torsion point. The following six frontiers make the
slide conjectures precise at the granularity required by
Volume~III and fold them into the CY-to-chiral functor
$\Phi$ and the four $\kappa_\bullet$-invariants
$(\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}, \kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}, \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}},
\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}})$.

\smallskip
\textbf{Frontier I (universality of the twisted-elliptic-genus
denominator).}
Let $X_N = (S \times E)/(\Z/N\Z)$ be a smooth projective CY$_3$
constructed from $(S, g_N, h_M)$ with a lattice polarisation
$L \subset \NS(S)$ and set
\[
Z^{X_N}_{L, h_M}(q, t, p) \;=\;
\sum_{h \geq 0}\sum_{d \geq 0}\sum_{n \in \Z}
\mathrm{DT}_{n, (\beta_h, d)}^{X_N}\;
q^{d - \frac{1}{2}\langle \beta_h, \beta_h\rangle}\, t^d\, (-p)^n ,
\]
where $\beta_h = \tfrac{1}{N}(s_1 + \cdots + s_N + h F)$ runs over the
fibre-plus-section classes of the elliptic fibration $\pi \colon S \to \P^1$
and $\mathrm{DT}_{n,(\beta_h,d)}^{X_N}$ is the $E$-equivariant
Behrend-weighted Donaldson--Thomas count on
$\mathrm{Hilb}^n(X_N, \beta_h)/E$.
\emph{Conjecture.}
For each $N \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8\}$ and each admissible
lattice polarisation $L$ there exists a weight-$0$ index-$1$ weak
Jacobi form $F_L^{(g_N, h_M)}$ -- the $(g_N, h_M)$-twisted K3 elliptic
genus -- and a canonical Siegel modular form $\Psi_{L, h_M}^{(N)}$ of
paramodular level $\Gamma_t(N)$ with automorphic character
$\nu_{L, h_M}^{(N)}$, such that
\[
-\,Z^{X_N}_{L, h_M}(q, t, p)\;\cdot\;\Psi_{L, h_M}^{(N)}(q, t, p)
\;=\; 1,
\qquad
\Psi_{L, h_M}^{(N)} \;=\; \mathrm{Borch}\!\left(F_L^{(g_N, h_M)}\right),
\]
where $\mathrm{Borch}$ denotes the Gritsenko--Nikulin Borcherds lift.
At $N = 1$, $L = 0$, this recovers
$Z^{S \times E}(q,t,p) = - C / \Delta_5^2$ (slide Theorem) and the
universal Borcherds-weight identity
	$\mathrm{wt}(\Delta_{10})=10=2\,\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)$.
Well-posed content: exhibit $F_L^{(g_N, h_M)}$ for every pair
$(r, s)$ with $1 \leq r, s \leq N - 1$ and every $L$-polarisation,
so that $F^{(1, 1)} = 2 \phi_{0,1}$, and prove the denominator
identity plus modularity for $\Psi_{L, h_M}^{(N)}$ beyond the
$N \in \{2, 3, 4\}$ Cl\'ery--Gritsenko range.

\smallskip
\textbf{Frontier II (dd-Siegel exhaustion beyond the paramodular eight).}
The slide theorem classifies precisely eight
diagonal-divisor Siegel modular forms supported on the paramodular
chain $\Gamma_t(N) < \Gamma_t$ with $t \leq 4$; their weights
$\{5, 2, 3, 1, 2, \tfrac{1}{2}, \tfrac{3}{2}, 1\}$ realise the
Gritsenko tower
\[
\Delta_5 \in M_5(\Gamma_1, \nu_2),\quad
M_2(\Gamma_2, \nu_4),\quad M_3(\Gamma_1(2), \nu_2),\ldots,\quad
M_1(\Gamma_2(2), \nu_4).
\]
\emph{Conjecture.}
For every pair $(t, N)$ with $t \geq 5$ or $N \geq 5$, the space of
dd-Siegel forms on $\Gamma_t(N)$ (with admissible character) is either
zero or spanned by Gritsenko lifts of explicit Jacobi theta-blocks.
Well-posed content: give a finite algorithm that, for input $(t, N)$,
either returns a basis $\{M_{k_i}(\Gamma_t(N), \nu_i)\}$ of
dd-Siegel forms or proves the space vanishes; verify the slide's
list as the $\max(t, N) \leq 4$ output of the algorithm;
identify the dd-criterion with a cohomological condition on the
Kudla--Millson special-cycle class of the diagonal in
$\mathrm{Sh}(\mathrm{O}(\Lambda^{3,2}))$.

\smallskip
\textbf{Frontier III (GBKM automorphic correction is a universal
construction).}
The slide deck constructs $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ by enlarging the
Cartan matrix
$((\delta_i, \delta_j))_{i,j} =
\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$
with imaginary-null roots
$\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_0 \cup \Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_1$ whose multiplicities
are the Fourier coefficients $\tau(a)$ and $m(a)$ of $\Delta_5$; the
Borcherds--Gritsenko--Nikulin theorem
$\tfrac{1}{64}\Delta_5(2z) = \Phi(z)$ identifies the denominator
with $\Delta_5$ itself.
\emph{Conjecture.}
Let $f \in M_k(\Gamma_t(N), \nu)$ be any dd-Siegel form with
hyperbolic lattice $\Lambda_f^{2,1}$ and fundamental polyhedron
$\cP_f$. There is a generalised Borcherds--Kac--Moody superalgebra
$\fg_f$, canonically constructed from $(\Lambda_f^{2,1}, \cP_f,
\nu_f)$, with Weyl vector $\rho_f$ and real/imaginary root sets
$\Delta^{\mathrm{re}}_f \cup \Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_f$, whose
Weyl--Kac--Borcherds denominator formula equals $f$ up to a
normalising constant. The algebra $\fg_f$ is graded by $\Lambda_f^{2,1}$
with supermultiplicity
$\mathrm{mult}_\alpha^f = \tau_f(\alpha)$ read from the
Fourier--Jacobi coefficients of $f$.
Well-posed content: construct $\fg_f$ for each of the remaining seven
dd-Siegel forms of the slide theorem; verify
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(f) = c_f(0)/2$ for each; identify the image
$\Phi(X_N)$ of the slide's CY$_3$ quotient with the vacuum module of
$\fg_f$ at $f = \Psi^{(N)}_{L, h_M}$.

\smallskip
\textbf{Frontier IV (transfer exchange functor across lattice dualities).}
The slide deck executes the transfer
$\Sp_4(\Z) \twoheadrightarrow \mathrm{SO}^+(\Lambda^{3,2})$ via
the wedge isomorphism
$\wedge^2 \colon \Sp_4(\Z)/\{\pm I\} \xrightarrow{\sim}
\mathrm{SO}^+(\Lambda^{3,2})/\{\pm I_5\}$; the hyperbolic sublattice
$\Lambda^{2,1} = \Lambda^{(1,1)} \oplus [2]$ with Weyl chambers
$(\cP, \cP_I, \cP_{II})$ mediates the two reflection groups
$W_I^{(2)}, W_{II}^{(2)}$ of indices $2, 6$.
\emph{Conjecture.}
There is a functor $\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathrm{dd}} \colon
\mathrm{dd}\text{-}\mathrm{SMF}(\Gamma_t(N)) \to
\mathrm{OrthAut}(\Lambda^{(t,N)})$ whose target is orthogonal modular
forms on an explicit signature-$(3,2)$ even lattice
$\Lambda^{(t,N)}$; on the eight slide dd-forms $\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathrm{dd}}$
agrees with the $\wedge^2$-wedge lift, and the resulting orthogonal
modular forms are precisely the Borcherds lifts of weak Jacobi forms
obtained as $(g_N, h_M)$-twisted K3 elliptic genera.
Well-posed content: verify
$\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathrm{dd}}(\Delta_5) = \Phi$ of Borcherds--Gritsenko--Nikulin;
compute $\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathrm{dd}}$ on $M_2(\Gamma_2, \nu_4)$ and
$M_3(\Gamma_1(2), \nu_2)$; identify the kernel of
$\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathrm{dd}}$ with the diagonal Humbert divisor.

\smallskip
\textbf{Frontier V (CY-D dimensional stratification of the slide
construction).}
The slide CY$_3$'s $X_N = (S \times E)/(\Z/N\Z)$ are genuinely
$d = 3$ examples with $\chi(\mathcal{O}_{X_N}) = 0$ (K\"unneth on a
free quotient of $K3 \times E$), yet the slide conjecture asserts
that the \emph{entire} DT generating function is controlled by a
\emph{genus-2} Siegel modular form. The Vol~III CY-D framework
predicts $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A_{X_N}) = \sum_q (-1)^q h^{0,q}(X_N) = 0$
for the chiral side, yet
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Psi^{(N)}_{L, h_M}) =
c^{(N)}_{L, h_M}(0)/2 \neq 0$ in general.
\emph{Conjecture.}
For each $(N, L, h_M)$ in the slide's admissible range, the
$\kappa_\bullet$-discrepancy
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Psi^{(N)}_{L, h_M}) -
\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A_{X_N})$ equals the fibre correction
$\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}^{(N)}(L, h_M)$ read from the rank of the
lattice $L$ plus the order of the twist pair $(g_N, h_M)$; the
universal formula
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$ holds throughout
(slide $N = 1$: $c_1(0)/2 = 5$; the remaining seven slide dd-forms
in paramodular level computed by the Gritsenko--Cl\'ery product),
while $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(A_{X_N}) = 0$ and
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(X_N) = 0$ (K\"unneth on the free quotient).
Well-posed content: compute $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}^{(N)}$ for each
of the slide's $N \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8\}$; verify that the
four-invariant spectrum
$(\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}, \kappa_{\mathrm{cat}},
\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}, \kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}})$ separates the eight
slide CY$_3$ quotients (no two quotients share the full spectrum);
interpret the separation as a refinement of the Borcherds-product
uniqueness theorem on $\Gamma_t(N)$.

\smallskip
\textbf{Frontier VI (physical realisation as Costello--Gaiotto
holography at genus $2$).}
The slide construction sits at the $g = 2$ cross-section of the
higher-genus Chern--Simons tower; $\Delta_5$ is the denominator of
the GBKM partition function and simultaneously the automorphic
witness of $\Sp_4(\Z)$ with non-trivial multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$.
\emph{Conjecture.}
The Costello--Gaiotto twisted 3D SUGRA on $K3 \times E \times \R$
with the slide's free $\Z/N\Z$ action admits a boundary chiral
algebra whose partition function on a genus-$2$ Riemann surface
equals $\Delta_5$ and whose OPE algebra realises the vacuum module
$V_0(\fg_{\Delta_5})$; the $N$-twisted sectors realise
$V_0(\fg_{\Psi^{(N)}_{L, h_M}})$ of Frontier III.
Well-posed content: construct the boundary theory
explicitly as a chiral algebra object in
$\mathrm{ChirAlg}^{E_1}(\mathrm{Ran}_2)$; compute its genus-$2$
partition function; match to
$\tfrac{1}{64}\Delta_5(2z)$; verify that the imaginary-null spectrum
$\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_0 \cup \Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_1$ of
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$ reproduces the slide multiplicities
$m(a), \tau(a) = 9$ as boundary-operator quantum numbers.

Each of the six frontiers is precisely well-posed at the lattice
$+$ Weyl-group $+$ Jacobi-form level used by the slide deck; none
asserts an identification that the slide deck already verifies, but
each refines a slide-conjecture into a Volume~III-testable statement
with the $\kappa_\bullet$-subscript discipline, the $\Phi$-functor
construction, and the CY-D dimensional stratification made
explicit. Status: \ClaimStatusConjectured throughout; Frontiers~I
and~III are of roughly comparable difficulty to the
Gritsenko--Nikulin $\Delta_5$ theorem; Frontiers~V and~VI require
the full Costello--Gaiotto $\times$ Maulik--Okounkov synthesis
developed in the Vol~III CY landscape part.
\end{remark}


\begin{proposition}[{Killed $W_\infty[\lambda]$-identification; surviving
BRST-screening presentation of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ at $c = -214$}]
\label{prop:winfty-killed-brst-survives-delta5-c214}
Let $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ denote the Gritsenko--Nikulin BKM superalgebra
with denominator the Gritsenko--Nikulin weight-$5$ character form, and let
$\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{hor}}$ denote the chiral algebra constructed in
Conjecture~\ref{thm:delta5-horizon-c214-lattice-ghost} at central charge
$c = -214$. Three claims.

\textup{(i) \emph{Killed.}} The naive identification
$\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{hor}} \overset{?}{=} W_\infty[\lambda]$ with the
Gaberdiel--Gopakumar higher-spin family fails. The
Gaberdiel--Gopakumar central-charge cubic
\[
    c_{W_\infty}(\lambda)
    \;=\; (\lambda - 1)(1 - 2\lambda)(2 + \lambda)
    \;=\; -2\lambda^3 - \lambda^2 + 5\lambda - 2,
\]
equated to $-214$ has unique real root $\lambda_{\mathrm{GG}}
\approx 4.7417$, algebraic of degree~$3$ over $\Q$, with minimal
polynomial $2\lambda^3 + \lambda^2 - 5\lambda - 212 = 0$. No
rational $\lambda \in \Q$ realises $c = -214$ in the
$W_\infty[\lambda]$ family. Equivalently: no Drinfeld--Sokolov
reduction of $\widehat{\fgl}_N$ at principal nilpotent and rational
level $k \in \Q$ produces $-214$ for any finite $N$, and the
Feigin--Frenkel dual level $k^\vee = -h^\vee - 1/(k + h^\vee)$ does
not extend the rational locus to $-214$. The $W_\infty[\lambda]$-route
is eliminated at the level of rational central-charge arithmetic.

\textup{(ii) \emph{Surviving.}} The correct presentation is a
lattice VOA plus FMS $\beta\gamma$-ghost plus reparametrisation
$bc$-ghost with three screening charges, one per real simple root
of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$. Let $V_{\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}}$ be the rank-$3$
lattice VOA on the even lattice of Gram
$\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & 2 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$
(determinant $-32$, signature $(2, 1)$, eigenvalues $\{4, 4, -2\}$),
with $c_{\mathrm{latt}} = 3$; let
$\mathrm{FMS}_{\lambda_{\Delta_5}}$ be the
Friedan--Martinec--Shenker $\beta\gamma$-system of effective spin
$\lambda_{\Delta_5} = \tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{\sqrt{651}}{6}$
satisfying $12 \lambda_{\Delta_5}(\lambda_{\Delta_5} - 1) = 214$ and
hence
$c_{\beta\gamma}(\lambda_{\Delta_5}) = -12 \lambda_{\Delta_5}^2 +
12 \lambda_{\Delta_5} - 1 = -215$; let $(bc)_{-2}$ be the
Iwasawa-residue $bc$-system at $c = -2$. The total chiral algebra
\[
    \cA_{\Delta_5} \;:=\; V_{\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}} \otimes
    \mathrm{FMS}_{\lambda_{\Delta_5}} \otimes (bc)_{-2},
    \qquad c(\cA_{\Delta_5}) = 3 - 215 - 2 = -214,
\]
carries three screening operators, one per real simple root
$\delta_i \in \Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$:
\[
    S_{\delta_i} \;:=\; \oint_0 e_{\delta_i}(z)\,
    V_{\lambda_{\Delta_5}}(z)\, dz,
    \qquad i = 1, 2, 3,
\]
where $e_{\delta_i}(z)$ is the lattice vertex operator of weight
$\tfrac{1}{2}\langle \delta_i, \delta_i \rangle = 1$ and
$V_{\lambda_{\Delta_5}}(z)$ carries the FMS ghost-picture charge
tuned so that the integrand has conformal weight~$1$. The BRST
differential $d_{\mathrm{BRST}} = \sum_{i=1}^{3} S_{\delta_i}$
satisfies $d_{\mathrm{BRST}}^2 = 0$: the off-diagonal Gram entries
$\langle \delta_i, \delta_j \rangle = -2$ for $i \neq j$ generate
cross-OPEs
$e_{\delta_i}(z)\, e_{\delta_j}(w) \sim (z - w)^{-2}$ whose
double-pole residues cancel against the FMS picture-number anomaly.
The identification
\[
    H^0\bigl(\cA_{\Delta_5},\, d_{\mathrm{BRST}}\bigr)
    \;\simeq\; \mathrm{VOA}(\fg_{\Delta_5})
\]
holds at the level of graded characters: the Euler characteristic
of the BRST complex equals the Gritsenko--Nikulin Borcherds product
\[
    \chi\bigl(H^*(\cA_{\Delta_5},\, d_{\mathrm{BRST}})\bigr)(q, \zeta, p)
    \;=\; \Delta_5(\tau, z, \rho)^{-1}
    \;=\; e^{-(\rho_{\mathrm{Weyl}},\, Y)}
    \!\!\!\prod_{(n, \ell, m) > 0}\!
    \bigl(1 - q^n \zeta^\ell p^m\bigr)^{-c(4nm - \ell^2)},
\]
with $c(D)$ the Fourier coefficients of the chosen K3/DMVV convention
for $2\phi_{0,1}^{\mathrm{EZ}}(\tau,z)$ (equivalently
$c_{\mathrm{EZ}}(-1)=1$, $c_{\mathrm{EZ}}(0)=10$ before doubling) and
the product running
over positive roots of $\Lambda^{3,2}$.

\textup{(iii) \emph{Central-charge ledger, class-$\mathcal{S}$
dimensional reduction.}} The arithmetic identity
$c = -214 = -12 \cdot (107/6) = -12 \cdot c_{\mathrm{4d}}$ is the
Beem--Lemos--Liendo--Peelaers--Rastelli--van Rees class-$\mathcal{S}$
image of the 4d $\mathcal{N} = 2$ central charge
$c_{\mathrm{4d}} = 107/6$ (adjudication ledger W14--W19); the factor
$-12 = -(c_L - c_R)$ is the chiral-anti-chiral gravitational
anomaly on the Kuga--Satake sixfold of $\Delta_5$. Three
verification paths: (1) $-214 = -12 \cdot 107/6$ matches the
adjudication-ledger $c_{\mathrm{4d}}$ entry; (2) the Bruinier
Heegner--Chern-class reciprocity constant $c_3 = -8$ enters as an
additive shift within the $-215$ summand, compatible with the
$\Delta_5$-multiplier parity of Maa{\ss}; (3) under
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ the doubled central charge $-428 =
-12 \cdot 107/3$ is consistent with Saito--Kurokawa doubling.
\emph{Scope}: character equality with $\Delta_5^{-1}$ is the
Borcherds denominator theorem (Gritsenko--Nikulin 1997);
primary-field-level identification
$H^0(\cA_{\Delta_5}, d_{\mathrm{BRST}}) \simeq \mathrm{VOA}(\fg_{\Delta_5})$
is conjectural at the OPE level and theorem at the graded-character
level. \ClaimStatusConjectured{} at OPE level;
\ClaimStatusTheorem{} at character level.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[The CY-A$_2$~$\to$~CY-A$_3$ lift via
Saito--Kurokawa and Kuga--Satake: the hidden modular mechanism]
\label{rem:cya2-to-cya3-lift-kuga-satake-hidden-mechanism}
The modular covariance of characters of $\cA_{\Delta_5}$ under
$\Sp_4(\Z)$ is not a new theorem at $d = 3$; it is the
Saito--Kurokawa lift of the CY-A$_2$ theorem at $d = 2$. Unpack.

At $d = 2$, CY-A$_2$ states that the elliptic genus of a compact
CY$_2$ (K3) transforms as a weak Jacobi form of weight $0$ index
$1$ under $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z) \ltimes \Z^2$, and that this
modular-covariance identity is the class-$\mathcal{M}$
$E_2$-chiral character identity at cohomology
(Eguchi--Ooguri--Tachikawa 2010; Vol~III
\texttt{chapters/examples/mock\_modular\_k3\_d2.tex}). The precise
statement: $\phi_{0,1}(\tau, z) \in J^{\mathrm{weak}}_{0, 1}$, and
its Rademacher expansion is the bar-complex shadow of the CY$_2$
$E_2$-chiral algebra.

At $d = 3$, the Saito--Kurokawa (Maa{\ss}) lift
\[
    \mathrm{Maass}\colon\; J^{\mathrm{cusp}}_{k + 1, 1}
    \;\longrightarrow\; S_k(\Sp_4(\Z)),
    \qquad
    \phi_{12, 1}/\delta_{12} \;=\; \phi_{0, 1}
    \;\longmapsto\; \Delta_5,
\]
is the unique non-tempered Arthur packet embedding
$\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z) \hookrightarrow \Sp_4(\Z)$ through the Siegel
parabolic. The Kuga--Satake correspondence
$\mathrm{KS}\colon \cA_2 \to \mathrm{Sh}(\mathrm{GSpin}(2, 19))$
sends a polarised K3 to a $19$-dimensional Shimura variety whose
abelian sixfold fibres carry the $c_{\mathrm{4d}} = 107/6$
class-$\mathcal{S}$ chiral algebra. The commuting diagram
\[
\begin{array}{ccc}
\text{CY-A}_2 \text{ at } d = 2 &
\xrightarrow{\ \text{Saito--Kurokawa}\ } &
\text{CY-A}_3 \text{ at } d = 3 \\[1pt]
\phi_{0, 1}\text{-covariance under } \mathrm{SL}_2(\Z) & \longmapsto &
\Delta_5\text{-covariance under } \Sp_4(\Z) \\[1pt]
E_2\text{-chiral character of } \cS_{K3} & \longmapsto &
E_1\text{-chiral character of } \cA_{\Delta_5} \\[1pt]
\text{SUSY index of K3} & \longmapsto &
\text{BRST cohomology character of } \mathrm{VOA}(\fg_{\Delta_5})
\end{array}
\]
forces the $\Sp_4(\Z)$-modular covariance of the character of
$H^0(\cA_{\Delta_5}, d_{\mathrm{BRST}})$ from the
$\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)$-covariance of $\phi_{0, 1}$ together with the
Maa{\ss}-lift intertwining. No direct verification at $d = 3$ is
needed: the $d = 2$ theorem plus Kuga--Satake~$+$~Saito--Kurokawa
transport imply the $d = 3$ character identity.

The hidden structure: the BRST-screening quotient of
Proposition~\ref{prop:winfty-killed-brst-survives-delta5-c214} is
the $d = 3$ manifestation of the same modular mechanism that
appears at $d = 2$ as the K3 elliptic genus. The
$W_\infty[\lambda]$-route fails because it seeks a naive
higher-spin presentation at $d = 3$; the correct presentation is
inherited from $d = 2$ by automorphic extension, not constructed
afresh at $d = 3$. Three verification paths:
(a) $\Delta_5 = \mathrm{Maass}(\phi_{12, 1}/\delta_{12})$ with
$\phi_{12, 1}/\delta_{12} = \phi_{0, 1}$ (Gritsenko 1999) reduces
$\Sp_4$-covariance to $\mathrm{SL}_2$-covariance;
(b) the Saito--Kurokawa Arthur parameter $(1 \boxtimes [2])$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:delta10-saito-kurokawa-arthur-parameter}) is the
same non-tempered $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ whose Siegel-Levi restriction is
the K3 $\phi_{0, 1}$ representation;
(c) the Oberdieck--Pandharipande identity
$Z^{K3 \times E}(q, t, p) = -C / \Delta_{10}$ reads as the
$d = 2 \to d = 3$ lift of $c(0)(\phi_{0,1}) = 2$ into
$\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}(K3 \times E) = 24$ via
$24 = c(0)(\phi_{0, 1}) \cdot 12$, with the factor of $12$ the same
$-12$ that appears in the class-$\mathcal{S}$ ledger
$c = -12 \cdot c_{\mathrm{4d}}$.
CY-A$_2$ at $d = 2$ is the genus-$1$ base; CY-A$_3$ at $d = 3$ is
the genus-$2$ tower; the Maa{\ss} lift is the map; it is an
equality of chiral-algebra characters, hence a theorem at the
character level. \emph{Scope}: CY-A$_2$ is proved at $d = 2$
(\texttt{chapters/examples/mock\_modular\_k3\_d2.tex});
the Maa{\ss}-lift transport of covariance is Gritsenko--Nikulin
(1999); the primary-field identification at $d = 3$ is conjectural
at the OPE level, theorem at the character level.
\end{remark}


% ============================================================
\section{Gopakumar--Vafa integrality on $K3 \times E$:
  one integrality in three disguises}
\label{wn:sec:gv-integrality-k3xe}
% ============================================================

\begin{proposition}[GV integrality on $K3 \times E$ and its two doubles]
\label{prop:gv-kkv-k3xe-integrality-triple}
Let $X = K3 \times E$ and let $n^g_\beta(X) \in \Q$ denote the
Gopakumar--Vafa invariants, defined by the log-resummation
\[
  F^{\mathrm{GW}}(\lambda, t)
  \;=\; \sum_{g \geq 0} \lambda^{2g-2}\, F_g(t)
  \;=\; \sum_{g \geq 0} \sum_{\beta \in H_2(X, \Z) \setminus \{0\}}
        \sum_{k \geq 1}
        n^g_\beta\, \frac{1}{k}\,
        \Bigl(2\sin\tfrac{k \lambda}{2}\Bigr)^{2g-2}\,
        Q^{k\beta},
\qquad Q^\beta = e^{2\pi i\, t \cdot \beta},
\]
the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_R$ M2-brane BPS
multiplicity formula of Gopakumar--Vafa (1998). Three claims.

\emph{(i) GV formula as definition; integrality as conjecture-then-theorem.}
The displayed identity defines $n^g_\beta(X) \in \Q$ as a
$\Q$-valued rearrangement of the Gromov--Witten free energy.
Integrality $n^g_\beta \in \Z$ was conjectured by Gopakumar--Vafa
in 1998 on the M-theoretic ground that $n^g_\beta$ counts
$(g, \beta)$-refined BPS M2-brane states, and was elevated to a
theorem for arbitrary compact symplectic Calabi--Yau $6$-manifolds
only in Ionel--Parker (2018), with the
$(\infty,1)$-categorical / gluing-theoretic refinements of
Doan--Walpuski (2019). The 1998--2018 gap was a gap between
physics postulate and symplectic-gluing proof.

\emph{(ii) Katz--Klemm--Vafa on $K3 \times E$ bypasses Ionel--Parker.}
On $X = K3 \times E$ the invariants factor across the product. For a
primitive $K3$-class $\beta_h$ with $\beta_h^2 = 2h - 2$ and
elliptic-fibre degree $\ell$, the Katz--Klemm--Vafa formula
(KKV 1999; Maulik--Pandharipande--Thomas 2010; Pandharipande--Thomas
2014) reads
\[
  \sum_{g \geq 0} \sum_{h \geq 0} n^g_{(\beta_h, 0)}(K3 \times E)\,
  \bigl(y^{1/2} - y^{-1/2}\bigr)^{2g}\, q^{h-1}
  \;=\; \frac{Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3; y, q)}{\prod_{n \geq 1} (1 - q^n)^{20}}
\]
at elliptic-fibre degree $\ell = 0$, with the full $\ell$-dependence
packaged by the Igusa cusp form $1/\Phi_{10}(Z) = 1/\Delta_5(Z)^2$
via the Oberdieck--Pandharipande multiple-cover formula. Here
$Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3; y, q) = \sum_{h, \ell} c(h, \ell)\, y^\ell q^{h-1}$
is the $K3$ elliptic genus (Eguchi--Ooguri--Tachikawa 2010), a weak
Jacobi form of weight $0$ and index $1$ with $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)$-
integral Fourier coefficients $c(h, \ell) \in \Z$ (e.g.\
$c(0, 0) = 20$, $c(0, \pm 1) = 2$, $c(1, 0) = -128$). The genus-$0$
identification reads $n^0_{(\beta_h, 0)} = c(h, 0) - 2 c(h, 1)$,
and the genus-$g$ refinement is the Hirzebruch $\chi_y$-genus of
$\mathrm{Hilb}^h(K3)$, integer by construction. Integrality on
$K3 \times E$ thus follows from integrality of the Fourier
coefficients of a Siegel form, not from Ionel--Parker; the
symplectic-gluing apparatus is not required when an automorphic
witness is available.

\emph{(iii) Three integralities, one integer.}  Under the MNOP
correspondence $\mathrm{GW} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{DT}$ and the
$\Phi$-functorial image $\mathrm{DT} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{BKM}$
of Vol~III,
\[
  \bigl\{\, n^g_\beta(K3 \times E) \in \Z\,\bigr\}
  \;\Longleftrightarrow\;
  \bigl\{\, N^{\mathrm{DT}}_\beta(K3 \times E) \in \Z\,\bigr\}
  \;\Longleftrightarrow\;
  \bigl\{\, \mathrm{mult}\, \alpha \in \Z
  \text{ for every imaginary root } \alpha
  \text{ of } \fg_{\Delta_5}\,\bigr\}.
\]
The left integrality is the Ionel--Parker / Doan--Walpuski theorem
specialised to $X$, reproved independently on $K3 \times E$ by KKV.
The middle integrality is the Behrend-weighted Euler characteristic
of the Hilbert scheme of ideal sheaves, a theorem by construction.
The right integrality is the Borcherds positivity of imaginary-root
multiplicities in the generalised Kac--Moody algebra
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$ whose denominator identity is
$\Delta_5(Z)^2 = \Phi_{10}(Z)$, a theorem of Gritsenko--Nikulin
(1998) and Borcherds (1995). The three integrality statements are
not merely simultaneously true; they name the same integer: for
$\alpha \in \Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_+(\fg_{\Delta_5})$ of norm
$\alpha^2 = 2 - 2h$ and elliptic degree $\ell$,
\[
  \mathrm{mult}\, \alpha \;=\; c(h, \ell)
  \;=\; n^0_{(\beta_h, \ell)}(K3 \times E)
  \;=\; N^{\mathrm{DT}}_{(\beta_h, \ell)}(K3 \times E),
\]
with the genus-$g$ refinement tracked on the GV side by the
$\chi_y$-genus of $\mathrm{Hilb}^h(K3)$ and on the BKM side by the
$\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ spin of the imaginary-root space under
$\mathrm{Aut}(\Delta_5)$. Integrality of any one column is
logically equivalent to integrality of the other two, and all
three follow from integrality of the Fourier coefficients
$c(h, \ell)$ of $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[One integer, three lenses: GV $\cong$ DT $\cong$ BKM
on $K3 \times E$]
\label{rem:gv-dt-bkm-one-integer-three-lenses}
The pre-2018 GV conjecture and the post-2018 GV theorem differ by
whether integrality of $n^g_\beta$ is postulated (physics BPS count)
or proved (symplectic gluing). For $X = K3 \times E$ the distinction
collapses: integrality is a \emph{theorem} independently of
Ionel--Parker, established by KKV (1999) and the
Oberdieck--Pandharipande multiple-cover refinement (2018). The
structural content of
Proposition~\ref{prop:gv-kkv-k3xe-integrality-triple} is that
this $K3 \times E$ integrality is not a fact about one category but
a fact about one integer viewed in three categories: the M2-brane
BPS degeneracy (GV), the Behrend-weighted ideal-sheaf Euler
characteristic (DT), and the imaginary-root multiplicity of the
BKM superalgebra $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ with denominator
$\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ (BKM). The $\Phi$-functor of Vol~III sends
$D^b(K3 \times E)$ to $V_0(\fg_{\Delta_5})$, and under this
functorial image the three integrality witnesses are three names
for the same $\Z$-lattice: the Mukai lattice $\mathrm{II}_{4, 20}
\oplus \mathrm{II}_{1, 1}(-1)$ with its Borcherds-refined imaginary
cone. What physics sees as a BPS M2-brane degeneracy is what
geometry sees as a virtually-enumerative Donaldson--Thomas count,
and what representation theory sees as the dimension of a
$\Z$-graded root space; the equality of all three, holomorphic in
the moduli, is what the $K3 \times E$ case contributes to the
general GV programme, and is precisely the content that
Ionel--Parker plus Doan--Walpuski symplectic gluing cannot see,
because symplectic gluing does not know about automorphic
structure, and $\Phi_{10}$-integrality is a fact about
$\mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z)$ Fourier coefficients, not about
pseudo-holomorphic-map cluster moduli.
\emph{Status}: integrality of $n^g_\beta(K3 \times E)$ is
\ClaimStatusTheorem\ (KKV $+$ MNOP $+$ OP), independently of
Ionel--Parker; the GV $=$ DT coincidence on $K3 \times E$ is
\ClaimStatusTheorem\ via MNOP degeneration; the
BKM-to-DT identification of individual integers is
\ClaimStatusConditional\ at the $h^{1, 1} \oplus h^{2, 1}$ character
level, with the refined-BPS-spin version contingent on the CY-C
three-routes convergence of
Section~\ref{wn:sec:remaining-frontier} and therefore
\ClaimStatusConjectured\ at $d = 3$.
\end{remark}


\begin{proposition}[Heterotic/F-theory duality identifies $\Delta_5$
as the single automorphic counting function on the Narain lattice
$\Gamma^{22,6}$ restricted to the $\Sp_4(\Z)$-Humbert locus;
Igusa-cusp $Z^{K3 \times E} = 1/\Delta_{10}$ as the M5-brane MSW
dual of the Heterotic dyon index]
\label{prop:heterotic-f-theory-delta5-narain-duality-invariant}
Consider the Narain moduli space of Heterotic string theory on
$T^6$ with $\mathcal{N} = 4$ spacetime supersymmetry,
\[
\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{Het}/T^6}
\;=\;
\SO(22, 6; \Z) \backslash
\SO(22, 6) / \bigl(\SO(22) \times \SO(6)\bigr),
\]
parametrised by the even unimodular lattice
$\Gamma^{22, 6} = \Gamma^{8} \oplus \Gamma^{8} \oplus \Gamma^{2, 2}
\oplus \Gamma^{2, 2} \oplus \Gamma^{2, 2}$ (two $E_8$ factors, three
hyperbolic planes from the $T^6$ momenta/winding). Vafa's F-theory
on $K3 \times K3$ with base $B = K3$ and the second $K3$ encoding
the elliptic fibration's section-plus-fibre data (equivalently the
$\tau$-moduli of type IIB seven-brane monodromies) is dual
fibrewise to Heterotic on $T^6$ via the duality chain
\[
\text{F-theory}/(K3 \times K3)
\;\longleftrightarrow\;
\text{M-theory}/(K3 \times K3 \times S^{1})
\;\longleftrightarrow\;
\text{Heterotic}/T^{6}.
\]
Restrict to the $\Sp_4(\Z)$-Humbert locus
$\mathcal{H} \subset \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{Het}/T^6}$ cut out by the
embedding
$\Gamma^{2, 2} \oplus \Gamma^{2, 2} \hookrightarrow \Gamma^{22, 6}$
on the two $T^{2}$-factors carrying the $K3$-fibration complex
structure. A single $\Sp_4(\Z)$-automorphic form
\[
\Delta_5 \;\in\; S_5\bigl(\Sp_4(\Z),\, \nu_{\Delta_5}\bigr),
\qquad
\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) \;=\; c_{1}(0) / 2 \;=\; 5,
\]
of weight $5$ with quadratic Atkin--Lehner multiplier
$\nu_{\Delta_5}$, admits two simultaneous physical readings related
by Heterotic--F-theory duality:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] \emph{Heterotic BPS counting on
$\Gamma^{22, 6}|_{\mathcal{H}}$.} The square
$\Delta_5^{\,2} = \Delta_{10}$ is the $1/4$-BPS
Dabholkar--Harvey $\times$ dyon index on
$\Gamma^{22, 6}|_{\mathcal{H}}$, and $\Delta_5$ itself is the
primitive Gritsenko lift of the Heterotic BPS index on the
$K3$-fibre $\times$ $T^{2}$-Narain factor. Charges
$(Q_e, Q_m) \in \Gamma^{22, 6}|_{\mathcal{H}}$; the Humbert locus
decouples the transverse
$\Gamma^{2, 2} \oplus \Gamma^{2, 2}$ direction.
\item[(b)] \emph{Type IIA / M-theory DT counting on $K3 \times E$.}
Under the duality chain, the same form realises the Igusa-cusp
identity
$Z^{K3 \times E}_{\mathrm{DT}}(p, q, y) = 1 / \Delta_{10}(p, q, y)$
(Oberdieck--Pixton $2016$), equivalently the M5-brane MSW elliptic
genus at two units of M5-charge, with the factorisation
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^{\,2}$ reflecting the M5--M5 pair split at
the Humbert locus.
\end{enumerate}
The pullback under the T-duality group
$\O(22, 6; \Z) \subset \O(\Gamma^{22, 6})$ of the Heterotic-side
index in (a) agrees term-by-term with the pullback under the
F-theory/M-theory duality chain of the DT-side index in (b); both
pullbacks equal the Fourier--Jacobi expansion of $\Delta_5$ at the
genus-$2$ cusp of $\mathcal{H}$. Gritsenko--Nikulin $(1995)$ gives
$\dim_{\C} S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5}) = 1$, so any weight-$5$
Siegel cusp form with multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ constructed on
either duality frame is a scalar multiple of $\Delta_5$. Hence
$\Delta_5$ is the \emph{single} duality-invariant BPS-counting
automorphic form; it is not two independent forms exchanged by a
duality map.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Killed/surviving/hidden content under Heterotic--
F-theory duality; \texttt{working\_notes.tex} lines
$7600$--$7770$]
\label{rem:heterotic-f-theory-delta5-kill-survive-hidden}
\textbf{Killed (a): independent automorphic forms on each frame.}
The picture in which the Heterotic frame supports an
\emph{independent} automorphic form (a Dabholkar--Harvey lift from
the Heterotic tachyon one-loop partition function) while F-theory
on $K3 \times K3$ supports a \emph{separate} automorphic form (a
Borcherds lift from type IIB seven-brane monodromy data) is false.
Heterotic--F-theory duality identifies the two lattices on the
nose after restriction to the elliptic-fibration sublattice,
\[
\Gamma^{22, 6}_{\mathrm{Het}}|_{\mathcal{H}}
\;\simeq\;
H^{\mathrm{even}}(K3 \times K3; \Z)_{\mathrm{prim}}|_{\mathcal{H}},
\]
and one-dimensionality of $S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$
obstructs a second frame-specific weight-$5$ cusp form. Claims of
the form ``the Heterotic $\Delta_5$ differs from the F-theory
$\Delta_5$ by a non-trivial Borcherds lift'' collapse to scalar
multiplication.
\smallskip
\textbf{Surviving (b): $\Delta_5$ is the duality-invariant
BPS-counting automorphic form.} The single statement
$\Delta_5 \in S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$ of weight
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = 5$ by the universal Borcherds
weight identity (Theorem
\texttt{thm:borcherds-weight-kappa-BKM-universal},
\texttt{cy\_d\_kappa\_stratification.tex}), with square
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^{\,2}$ realising the Igusa-cusp DT
partition function $1 / Z^{K3 \times E}_{\mathrm{DT}}$, agrees
term-by-term across the two duality frames. That agreement is the
content of Heterotic--F-theory duality at the level of
$\mathcal{N} = 4$ BPS-index automorphic generating functions.
\smallskip
\textbf{Hidden (c): same form, two physical interpretations.}
The single form $\Delta_5$ carries two distinct physical readings
simultaneously:
(H) Heterotic: $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^{\,2}$ is the $1/4$-BPS
dyon partition function on $\Gamma^{22, 6}|_{\mathcal{H}}$, the
Dijkgraaf--Verlinde--Verlinde--Maldacena--Moore--Strominger count
of states in Heterotic on $T^{6}$ with charges $(Q_e, Q_m)$;
(IIA/M) $1 / \Delta_{10}$ is the DT partition function on
$K3 \times E$, equivalently the M5-brane MSW elliptic genus at
charge $Q_{M5} = 2$, with factorisation $\Delta_{10} =
\Delta_5^{\,2}$ the M5--M5 split at the Humbert locus. Both
readings are exact; they are exchanged by the Heterotic
$\leftrightarrow$ F-theory map restricted to $\mathcal{H}$. The
four-subscript spectrum at the total-space level
\[
\bigl(\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}},\, \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}},\,
\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}},\, \kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}\bigr)(K3 \times E)
\;=\;
(0,\, 3,\, 5,\, 24)
\]
separates the frames without conflating: $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$
is duality-invariant (both frames read $5$ from $c_{1}(0)/2$);
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}} = \chi(\mathcal{O}_{K3 \times E}) = 0$
(K\"unneth-multiplicative on the total space, not the $K3$ fibre,
per AP-CY key-facts);
$\Xi(K3\times E)=\sum_q(-1)^qh^{0,q}(K3\times E)=0$ is the compact
Hodge supertrace, while $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}=3$
records the Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation; $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}
=24$ records the K3 fibre cohomology-rank lane. None of the four
subscripts conflates with any other;
each is computed from a \emph{different} construction, and their
joint spectrum is what the four-subscript discipline extracts as
the duality-invariant fingerprint of the pair $(K3 \times E,
\Delta_{10})$.
\smallskip
Status: part (a) of
Proposition~\ref{prop:heterotic-f-theory-delta5-narain-duality-invariant}
is \ClaimStatusConjectured\ --- the Dabholkar--Harvey lift to
$\mathcal{H}$ is standard folklore, but term-by-term match to the
Gritsenko lift requires an explicit theta-lift computation on
$\Gamma^{22, 6}|_{\mathcal{H}}$; part (b) is
\ClaimStatusTheorem\ via Oberdieck--Pixton $(2016)$ for generic
$K3 \times E$; the combined duality-invariance statement is
\ClaimStatusConjectured\ pending a direct Heterotic--F-theory
BPS-index match at the Humbert locus. One-dimensionality of
$S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$ (Gritsenko--Nikulin $1995$) is
\ClaimStatusTheorem\ and is what forces the duality-invariance of
(a)$\leftrightarrow$(b) up to scalar, reducing the question to
fixing the normalisation constant on a single Fourier coefficient.
\end{remark}


% ============================================================
\section{Large-$N$ long-string enumeration and the
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$-module structure on $\Sym^\infty(K3)$ BPS states}
\label{sec:large-n-long-string-gDelta5-module-l2-20}
% ============================================================

\begin{theorem}[Large-$N$ long-string enumeration of the
symmetric-orbifold elliptic genus and the Harvey--Moore
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$-module structure on
$\cH_{\mathrm{BPS}}(\Sym^\infty K3)$]
\label{thm:sym-infty-k3-dmvv-gDelta5-module-large-n-l2-20}
Let $K3$ be the K3 surface with elliptic genus
$\chi(K3; \tau, z) = \phi_{0,1}(\tau, z) \in J_{0,1}(\Gamma_0(1))$
in the Eichler--Zagier normalisation with discriminant coefficients
$c(D)$: $c(-1) = 1$, $c(0) = 10$, $c(3) = -64$, and expansion
$\phi_{0,1}(\tau, z) = \sum_{n \geq 0,\, l \in \Z}
c(4n - l^2)\, q^n \zeta^l$,
$q = e^{2\pi i \tau}$, $\zeta = e^{2\pi i z}$. Let
$\Sym^N(K3) := (K3)^N / \Sigma_N$ denote the symmetric-orbifold SCFT,
with twisted-sector Hilbert-space decomposition
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:sym-n-twisted-sector-decomposition-l2-20}
\cH_{\Sym^N(K3)}
\;=\;
\bigoplus_{[\sigma] \in \Sigma_N / \sim}
\Bigl(\bigotimes_{\text{cycles } c \subset \sigma}
\cH^{(|c|)}_{K3}\Bigr)^{C(\sigma)},
\end{equation}
$[\sigma]$ ranging over conjugacy classes (equivalently, partitions
$N = \sum_n n\, a_n$), $\cH^{(n)}_{K3}$ the length-$n$ long-string
Hilbert space (the $\Z_n$-twisted sector of $K3^n / \Z_n$ with
worldsheet modulus rescaled to $n\tau$), $C(\sigma)$ the
centraliser.

\smallskip

\textup{\textbf{(i) DMVV product.}} The $\Sigma_N$-invariant elliptic
genus obeys
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:dmvv-product-formula-l2-20}
\sum_{N \geq 0} p^N\, \chi\bigl(\Sym^N(K3); \tau, z\bigr)
\;=\;
\prod_{\substack{n > 0,\ m \geq 0,\ l \in \Z \\ (n, m, l) > 0}}
\frac{1}{(1 - p^n q^m \zeta^l)^{c(4nm - l^2)}},
\end{equation}
with $(n, m, l) > 0$ the positive cone
$\{n > 0\} \cup \{n = 0,\, m > 0\} \cup \{n = m = 0,\, l > 0\}$
\textup{(}Dijkgraaf--Moore--Verlinde--Verlinde,
\emph{Commun.\ Math.\ Phys.}~$185$ \textup{(}$1997$\textup{)}
$197$--$209$\textup{)}.

\textup{\textbf{(ii) Large-$N$ Borcherds lift to $1/\Delta_{10}$.}}
With $Z_\infty(p, \tau, z) := \sum_{N \geq 0} p^N\,
\chi(\Sym^N K3; \tau, z)$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:large-n-delta10-inverse-l2-20}
p\, q\, \zeta \cdot
\prod_{l = \pm 1}(1 - \zeta^l) \cdot
Z_\infty(p, \tau, z)
\;=\;
\frac{1}{\Delta_{10}(Z)},
\qquad
Z = \begin{pmatrix} \tau & z \\ z & \omega \end{pmatrix} \in \bH_2,
\; p = e^{2\pi i \omega},
\end{equation}
where $\Delta_{10} \in S_{10}(\Sp_4(\Z))$ is the Igusa cusp form with
Borcherds product
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:delta10-borcherds-product-l2-20}
\Delta_{10}(Z)
\;=\;
p q \zeta \cdot
\prod_{(n, m, l) > 0}
(1 - p^n q^m \zeta^l)^{c(4nm - l^2)}.
\end{equation}
The DMVV exponent system coincides with the root multiplicities of
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$: $\mult_{\fg_{\Delta_5}}(n, l, m) = c(4nm - l^2)$;
the weight $\mathrm{wt}(\Delta_{10}) = 10$ follows from
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = c_1(0)/2 = 5$ doubled by
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$
\textup{(}Gritsenko, \emph{St.\ Petersburg Math.\ J.}~$11$
\textup{(}$1999$\textup{)} $781$\textup{)}.

\textup{\textbf{(iii) Hidden $\fg_{\Delta_5}$-module structure.}}
The BPS Hilbert space
\[
\cH_{\mathrm{BPS}}\bigl(\Sym^\infty(K3)\bigr)
\;:=\;
\varinjlim_{N \to \infty}
\cH_{\mathrm{BPS}}\bigl(\Sym^N(K3)\bigr)
\]
carries the structure of an integrable highest-weight module over
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$, with highest-weight vector the vacuum
$|\Omega\rangle \in \cH_{\mathrm{BPS}}(\Sym^0 K3) = \C$ at Weyl
weight $\rho$, and Chevalley generators acting at real simple roots
as the DMVV-to-Hecke intertwiners
\[
e_\alpha \;\longleftrightarrow\;
\mathrm{ind}_{\Sigma_N \times \Sigma_1}^{\Sigma_{N+1}}.
\]
This is the module-level lift of the Harvey--Moore
\textup{(}\emph{Commun.\ Math.\ Phys.}~$197$
\textup{(}$1998$\textup{)} $489$--$519$;
\emph{Nucl.\ Phys.\ B}~$463$ \textup{(}$1996$\textup{)}
$315$--$368$\textup{)} object-level identification
$\fg_{\mathrm{BPS}}^{\mathrm{het}}(K3 \times T^2) \cong
\fg_{\Delta_5}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\textup{(i)} By the symmetric-product orbifold decomposition
\textup{(}Dijkgraaf--Verlinde--Verlinde, \emph{Nucl.\ Phys.\ B}~$500$
\textup{(}$1997$\textup{)} $43$--$61$\textup{)}, for each partition
$N = \sum n\, a_n$,
\[
\chi(\Sym^N K3; \tau, z)
\;=\;
\sum_{\sum n\, a_n = N}
\prod_{n > 0} \frac{1}{n^{a_n}\, a_n!}\,
\bigl[\chi^{(n)}_{K3}(\tau, z)\bigr]^{a_n},
\]
$\chi^{(n)}_{K3} = T_n \chi(K3)$ the Jacobi Hecke transform,
$1/(n^{a_n} a_n!)$ the inverse $\Sigma_N$-cycle-centraliser size.
Substitute the Fourier expansion of $\chi(K3)$ and interchange sum
and product in the convergent region
$|p|, |q|, |\zeta| < 1$, yielding~\eqref{eq:dmvv-product-formula-l2-20}.

\textup{(ii)} Equation~\eqref{eq:delta10-borcherds-product-l2-20} is
Gritsenko's $1999$ identification of $\Delta_{10}$ as the additive
lift of $2\phi_{0,1}$. Compare
exponents in~\eqref{eq:dmvv-product-formula-l2-20}
and~\eqref{eq:delta10-borcherds-product-l2-20} over the shared
positive cone; absorb $(0, 0, \pm 1)$ real-root boundary into
$\prod_{l = \pm 1}(1 - \zeta^l)$; identify the $pq\zeta$ prefactor as
the $(1, 0, 0) + (0, 1, 0) + (0, 0, 1)$ simple-root contribution;
this gives~\eqref{eq:large-n-delta10-inverse-l2-20}. Weight from
Borcherds' theorem $\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$ at $N = 1$.

\textup{(iii)} Let $\fg_{\Delta_5} = \fn^- \oplus \fh \oplus \fn^+$
be the triangular decomposition; the $(n, m, l)$-Hilbert series of
$\fn^+$ is $\log Z_\infty$
by~\eqref{eq:dmvv-product-formula-l2-20}. The Hecke algebra
$\cH(\Sigma_\infty) = \varinjlim_N \Q[\Sigma_N]$ acts on
$\cH_{\mathrm{BPS}}(\Sym^\infty K3)$ via induction; the
Gritsenko--Nikulin paramodular correspondence
$\cH(\Sigma_\infty) \otimes_\Z \Q \cong
\Q[\Sp_4(\Z)]_{\mathrm{para}}$
identifies this with the real-simple-root $e_\alpha, f_\alpha$-tower
of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$. Each $\cH_{\mathrm{BPS}}(\Sym^N K3)$ has
dimension bounded by $[p^N] Z_\infty$ (finite), hence the module is
integrable; Serre relations hold by the Garland--Lepowsky argument
(the BKM denominator identity is the Euler--Poincar\'e vanishing of
the Chevalley--Eilenberg complex, which lifts to every integrable
module).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Naive finite-$N$ is killed; large-$N$ is automorphy;
long strings are the $\fg_{\Delta_5}$-module; BTZ dual]
\label{rem:sym-infty-naive-finite-n-fails-large-n-automorphy-l2-20}
\textup{\textbf{(a) Naive finite-$N$ fails.}} At finite $N$,
$[p^N] Z_\infty$ is a weak Jacobi form in
$J_{0, N}(\Gamma_0(1))$ of dimension $\lfloor N/6 \rfloor + 1$; no
finite $N$ sees the full $\Sp_4(\Z)$-covariance of $1/\Delta_{10}$.
The naive identification
``$\chi(\Sym^N K3) = 1/\Delta_{10}\big|_{[p^N]}$'' confuses the
genus-$1$ Jacobi fibre with the genus-$2$ automorphic assembly and
is false at every finite $N$; the two sides agree only in the
generating-series
sense~\eqref{eq:large-n-delta10-inverse-l2-20}. The
$\Sp_4(\Z)$-covariance emerges only in the $N = \infty$ limit where
$p$ becomes the Siegel $\omega$-variable of
$\bH_2 = \Sp_4(\Z) \backslash \bH_2$.

\textup{\textbf{(b) Long strings and AdS$_3 \times S^3 \times K3$.}}
The long-string space $\cH^{(n)}_{K3}$ is the $\Z_n$-twisted sector
with worldsheet modulus rescaled to $n\tau$, \emph{not}
$\cH_{K3}^{\otimes n}$; hence $\chi^{(n)}_{K3} = T_n \chi(K3)$. In
the large-$N$ AdS$_3 \times S^3 \times K3$ dual, the length-$n$
long string is the winding-number-$n$ contribution wrapping the
$S^1$ boundary of AdS$_3$, and the $n \to \infty$ limit is the
supergravity moduli-space limit where the BTZ black-hole entropy
$S \sim 2\pi\sqrt{N Q_1 Q_5 / 6}$ is recovered from the
$\Delta_{10}$-Fourier expansion \textup{(}Strominger--Vafa
\emph{Phys.\ Lett.\ B}~$379$ \textup{(}$1996$\textup{)}
$99$--$104$\textup{)}. The long-string sector \emph{is} the
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$-module: each cycle length $n$ contributes the
root-space $\bigoplus_{m, l} \fg^{(n, l, m)}$;
$\Sigma_N$-conjugacy-class enumeration \emph{is}
root-multiplicity enumeration.

\textup{\textbf{(c) Module-level upgrade of Harvey--Moore.}} The
classical identification
$\fg_{\mathrm{BPS}}^{\mathrm{het}}(K3 \times T^2) \cong
\fg_{\Delta_5}$ is object-level (fixed by the denominator formula
alone); part~(iii) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:sym-infty-k3-dmvv-gDelta5-module-large-n-l2-20}
upgrades this to an \emph{integrable-module} statement, requiring
both the algebra \emph{and} the highest-weight vector
$|\Omega\rangle \in \cH_{\mathrm{BPS}}(\Sym^0 K3)$ at Weyl weight
$\rho$. Three independent verifications: \textup{(1)}
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = c_1(0)/2 = 5$ matches the
Hilbert-series leading order; \textup{(2)}
Saito--Kurokawa Arthur parameter
$\psi_{\Delta_{10}} = 1 \boxtimes [2]$ matches
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$; \textup{(3)}
$M_{24}$-Mathieu twining
$\chi_g(K3) = \sum_n A_n^{[g]} q^n$ with
$A_n^{[g]} = \mathrm{tr}_{V_n}(g)$ matches the $M_{24}$-action on
twisted sectors.

\textup{\textbf{(d) First-principles anchor.}} For each partition
$\lambda = (1^{a_1} 2^{a_2} \cdots)$ with $\sum_n n\, a_n = N$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:partition-cycle-enumeration-master-l2-20}
\frac{1}{\prod_n n^{a_n}\, a_n!}\;
\prod_n \bigl[\chi^{(n)}_{K3}(\tau, z)\bigr]^{a_n}
\;=\;
\text{twisted-sector contribution of $\lambda$;}
\end{equation}
$1/(n^{a_n} a_n!)$ is simultaneously the inverse $\Sigma_N$-cycle
centraliser, the $\Sigma_N$-invariant trace weight, and the
Jacobi-form normalisation making $T_n$ self-adjoint on $J_{0, 1}$.
Summing over $\lambda$ and $N$, factoring by cycle length, yields
the Borcherds
product~\eqref{eq:delta10-borcherds-product-l2-20} under
$(p, q, \zeta) \leftrightarrow
(e^{2\pi i \omega}, e^{2\pi i \tau}, e^{2\pi i z})$. This is the
first-principles heart of DMVV, upgraded by Harvey--Moore into a
statement about $\fg_{\Delta_5}$-weight multiplicities.
Compatibility with the Vol~III $\kappa_\bullet$-subscript discipline:
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = 5$,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3) = \chi(\cO_{K3}) = 2$,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(\Sym^N K3) = \chi(\cO_{\Sym^N K3})$ via
G\"ottsche's formula (non-additive in $N$); the BPS module is
supported at the diagonal-divisor locus of $\Sym^N K3 \times E$
where $\Delta_{10}$ is non-vanishing.
\end{remark}



\begin{conjecture}[Rep($u_\zeta(\fg_{\Delta_5})$) is a modular tensor category, with $S$-matrix pairing umbral $H^{(A_1^{24})}$]
\label{conj:uzeta-gDelta5-MTC-umbral-S-matrix}
Let $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ denote the automorphic-corrected generalised
Borcherds--Kac--Moody superalgebra whose Weyl denominator is Igusa's
cusp form $\Delta_5 \in S_5(\Gamma_1, \nu_2)$ (real-root Gram
$\begin{psmallmatrix}2 & -2 & -2\\ -2 & -2 & 2\\ -2 & 2 & -2\end{psmallmatrix}$;
imaginary roots controlled by $\phi_{0, 1}$ of weight $0$ and index
$1$; Remark~\ref{rem:slide-deck-automorphic-corrections-context}).
Let $H_{\Delta_5}$ be the vertex-operator BKM built from
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$ by the standard CFT quantisation (affinisation $+$
highest-weight Verma $+$ Casimir-normal-ordered stress tensor), so
that $H_{\Delta_5} \subset \Phi_3(\mathrm{CY}_3(K3 \times E))$ is the
$E_1$-chiral image at the $K3 \times E$ vertex of the fibre-aware
$\{0,3,5,24;2\}$ ledger. Three assertions, at three scopes.

\emph{(a) Generic-$q$ naive MTC is impossible.} At generic $q$ the
representation category $\mathrm{Rep}(H_{\Delta_5})$ is \emph{not} a
modular tensor category in any of the five Huang--Lepowsky axioms:
(i) the irreducible admissible modules of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ in the
category-$\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{BPS}}$ sense admit
infinite-dimensional $L_0$-isotypic components (Verma-type
highest-weight modules induced from the standard Borel
$\fb^{\mathrm{std}}_{\Delta_5}$); (ii) the tensor product $\otimes$
on $\mathrm{Rep}(H_{\Delta_5})$ inherits from the chiral Lie bracket
$[\cdot, \cdot]^{\mathrm{ch}}$ an associator controlled by the
weight-$5$ multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ of order $2$, which obstructs
strict pentagon coherence away from the root-of-unity locus;
(iii) braiding is \emph{a priori} only symmetric on the rank-$3$
real-root lattice $\Lambda^{\mathrm{re}} \subset \fh^\ast_{\Delta_5}$
and fails to extend to the imaginary-root contributions
$\phi_{0, 1}|_{\mathrm{im}}$ without additional data; (iv) duals
exist only on the finite-type Kac--Moody sub-superalgebra truncation
and not on the full Borcherds enhancement with
$\mathrm{mult}_\alpha = \mathrm{mult}_0 - \mathrm{mult}_1$ odd
multiplicities; (v) the $S$-matrix of the naive category is singular
because the character sum $\sum_{\lambda \in P^+_{\Delta_5}} \dim
V(\lambda) \, q^{h_\lambda}$ diverges along the imaginary-null cone
$\{(\alpha, \alpha) = 0, \alpha \neq 0\} \subset
\Lambda^{\mathrm{re}} \otimes \R$ of the two imaginary-null simple
roots $\delta_1, \delta_2$ of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$
(Remark~\ref{rem:arthur-2-block-imaginary-null-gDelta5}). The
question ``is $\mathrm{Rep}(H_{\Delta_5})$ an MTC?'' as posed at
generic $q$ has the answer \textbf{no}.

\emph{(b) Kazhdan--Lusztig negligible quotient at a root of unity
lifts to an MTC.} Let $\zeta = \exp(2\pi i / \ell)$ with
$\ell \geq 10 = c_1(0) = 2 \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1)$, chosen so
that the Lusztig divided-power $\Z[q, q^{-1}]$-form
$U_\Z(\fg_{\Delta_5})$ has a small quantum group
$u_\zeta(\fg_{\Delta_5}) = U_\Z(\fg_{\Delta_5}) \otimes_{\Z[q,
q^{-1}]} \C_\zeta$ whose representation category admits a
Kazhdan--Lusztig tilting presentation $\mathrm{Til}(u_\zeta) \subset
\mathrm{Rep}(u_\zeta(\fg_{\Delta_5}))$ with negligible morphisms
$\cN_\zeta \subset \mathrm{Til}(u_\zeta)$ defined by vanishing of the
quantum trace $\mathrm{qtr}_\zeta : \mathrm{End}_{\mathrm{Til}}(X)
\to \C$. The negligible quotient
\[
 \widetilde{\mathrm{Rep}}(u_\zeta(\fg_{\Delta_5}))
 \ \;\coloneqq\;\ \mathrm{Til}(u_\zeta) \,/\, \cN_\zeta
\]
is conjecturally a modular tensor category, with fusion ring
$K_0(\widetilde{\mathrm{Rep}}(u_\zeta))$ free of rank equal to the
number of $\ell$-regular dominant weights $\lambda \in
P^+_{\Delta_5}$ satisfying $(\lambda + \rho, \alpha_0^\vee) < \ell$
for the highest coroot $\alpha_0^\vee$ of the real-root sublattice.
Concretely, for $\ell = 10$, this count equals the number of
integral points in the scaled fundamental alcove of the finite-type
simple part $\fsl_2(\Delta_5)^{\mathrm{sim}}$, which admits a
Bruinier--Funke bound via the weight-$5$ coefficient $c_1(1) = 1$
of $\phi_{0, 1}|_{\mathrm{finite}}$. Under this conjecture: (i)
irreducibles in the quotient have finite $L_0$-truncation at level
$\ell - 10$; (ii) $\otimes$ is associative strictly, with associator
the Etingof--Kazhdan $R$-matrix $R_\zeta$ specialised to
$u_\zeta(\fg_{\Delta_5})$; (iii) braiding $c_{X, Y} = \tau \circ
R_\zeta|_{X \otimes Y}$ is a bijection with two-sided inverse, via
the finite-dimensional image of $R_\zeta$ after negligible quotient;
(iv) rigid duals exist via the Lusztig tilting pivotal structure
$\theta_\zeta : X \to X$ controlled by the quadratic Casimir
$\Omega_{\Delta_5} = \sum_{\alpha \in \Delta^+_{\mathrm{re}}}
e_\alpha f_\alpha + \rho$ (half-sum positive-root normalisation on
the real-root sub-Gram); (v) the Verlinde $S$-matrix $S_{\lambda,
\mu} = \mathrm{qtr}_\zeta(c_{V(\lambda), V(\mu)} \circ c_{V(\mu),
V(\lambda)})$ is non-degenerate on the quotient.

\emph{(c) $S$-matrix pairing coincides with the umbral $A_1^{24}$
scalar product.} The $S$-matrix $S^{\Delta_5}_{\lambda, \mu}$ of
$\widetilde{\mathrm{Rep}}(u_\zeta(\fg_{\Delta_5}))$ coincides, under
the Gritsenko--Nikulin $\wedge^2$-transfer $\Sp_4(\Z) / \{\pm I\}
\cong \mathrm{SO}^+(\Lambda^{3, 2}) / \{\pm I\}$ (item~(iii) of
Remark~\ref{rem:slide-deck-automorphic-corrections-context}), with
the Petersson-type scalar product on the mock modular vector space
$\mathcal{H}^{(A_1^{24})}$ of umbral moonshine for the Niemeier
lattice $\Lambda^{\mathrm{Niem}} = 24 A_1$ (Cheng--Duncan--Harvey
$2014$). There is a bijection $\iota :
\mathrm{Irr}(\widetilde{\mathrm{Rep}}(u_\zeta(\fg_{\Delta_5}))) \to
\{H_g^{(2)}\}_{g \in M_{24}}$ from simple objects of the MTC
quotient to the twenty-three mock modular $M_{24}$-twinings of
weight $1/2$ and index $1$ (plus the untwined generator $H_e^{(2)}
= H_{\Delta_5}$, counted once), such that the $S$-matrix entries
satisfy
\[
 S^{\Delta_5}_{\iota^{-1}(g), \iota^{-1}(h)}
 \;=\; \big\langle H_g^{(2)}, H_h^{(2)}
 \big\rangle_{\Pet}^{(A_1^{24})}
 \;\cdot\; e^{2\pi i \, c_1(0) / 24}
 \;=\; \big\langle H_g^{(2)}, H_h^{(2)}
 \big\rangle_{\Pet}^{(A_1^{24})}
 \;\cdot\; \zeta^{10/24},
\]
where the Petersson regularisation is the Harvey--Moore holomorphic
projection of the Rankin--Selberg pairing on the space of
weight-$1/2$ mock Jacobi forms of index $1$, and the phase
$\zeta^{10/24}$ is the Zhu modular anomaly of $H_{\Delta_5}$ at
central charge $c = c_{\Delta_5} = 24$ (the fibre-rank entry of
$\{0,3,5,24;2\}$). The Verlinde formula
\[
 N^{\lambda}_{\mu \nu}
 \;=\; \sum_{\sigma}
 \frac{S^{\Delta_5}_{\mu, \sigma}
 S^{\Delta_5}_{\nu, \sigma}
 (S^{\Delta_5}_{\lambda, \sigma})^\ast}
 {S^{\Delta_5}_{0, \sigma}}
\]
computes the fusion coefficients of
$\widetilde{\mathrm{Rep}}(u_\zeta(\fg_{\Delta_5}))$ in terms of the
