umbral mock Jacobi pairing, identifying the BKM MTC fusion ring
with the $M_{24}$-equivariant part of the mock modular
multiplication on $\mathcal{H}^{(A_1^{24})}$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{remark}[Attack--heal cycle: naive MTC killed, KL quotient healed, umbral $S$-matrix as hidden witness]
\label{rem:attack-heal-uzeta-gDelta5-MTC-umbral}
The three scopes of
Conjecture~\ref{conj:uzeta-gDelta5-MTC-umbral-S-matrix} record a
completed adversarial-healing cycle whose hidden output is a
first-principles bridge between the Igusa--Gritsenko side
$(\Delta_5, \fg_{\Delta_5})$ and the mock-modular umbral side
$(\mathcal{H}^{(A_1^{24})}, M_{24})$ of the $K3 \times E$ landscape,
distinct from the quantum-toroidal obstruction recorded at
Section~\ref{subsec:rectification-pass} and from the heuristic
$M_{24}$-Yangian moonshine of
Section~\ref{subsec:later-research-directions}.

\emph{Attack on (a).} A reader carrying Huang--Lepowsky MTC axioms
(finite-dimensional irreducibles, rigid associative $\otimes$,
braided, dualisable, modular $S$) reaches for the obvious answer:
``yes, the chiral category of $H_{\Delta_5}$ should be an MTC just
like any rational vertex algebra.'' The attack kills this in five
lines. Borcherds imaginary-root Vermas are infinite-dimensional;
$\phi_{0, 1}$ generates infinitely many imaginary roots at every
positive level; the character sum diverges along the null cone of
$\delta_1, \delta_2$; the associator fails pentagon coherence
because the weight-$5$ multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ has order $2$,
not $1$, so fusion is projective and not strict; and the
$S$-transformation on the Siegel upper half-plane $\bH_2$
intertwines $\Delta_5$ with a non-holomorphic shadow unless
regularised. Status at generic $q$: \textbf{killed}.

\emph{Heal via Kazhdan--Lusztig negligible quotient.} The surviving
mathematics is not ``$\mathrm{Rep}(H_{\Delta_5})$ is an MTC'' but
``$\widetilde{\mathrm{Rep}}(u_\zeta(\fg_{\Delta_5})) \coloneqq
\mathrm{Til}(u_\zeta(\fg_{\Delta_5})) / \cN_\zeta$ is an MTC,'' and
this distinction is load-bearing. The Lusztig divided-power
$\Z[q, q^{-1}]$-form of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ is non-standard because
imaginary-root generators lack finite quantum Serre relations (the
BKM Serre presentation uses weak Jacobi coefficients of
$\phi_{0, 1}$, not Chevalley constants), but the real-root sub-Gram
$\begin{psmallmatrix}2 & -2 & -2\\ -2 & -2 & 2\\ -2 & 2 & -2\end{psmallmatrix}$
supports a Lusztig form on its finite-type Weyl group
$W(\Lambda^{\mathrm{re}})$, and the imaginary-root extension is
handled by Kashiwara's crystal-level tensor product for BKMs. The
negligible quotient collapses the infinite-dimensional Verma to a
finite-dimensional tilting equivalence class. Status at $\zeta^\ell
= 1$ with $\ell \geq 10$: \textbf{MTC conjecture}
(\ClaimStatusConjectured), \emph{not} an established theorem,
because: (i) the Lusztig integral form for Borcherds superalgebras
with automorphic corrections is not fully constructed; (ii) the
pentagon-hexagon compatibility of $R_\zeta$ with the
$\phi_{0, 1}$-imaginary-root contributions requires a
Kazhdan--Lusztig tensor product for BKMs with mock-modular
correction, which remains open.

\emph{Hidden witness: umbral $H^{(A_1^{24})}$ pairing.} The
genuinely new content is the identification of the (conjectural)
MTC $S$-matrix $S^{\Delta_5}$ with the Petersson pairing on the
umbral mock modular space $\mathcal{H}^{(A_1^{24})}$ for the
Niemeier lattice $\Lambda^{\mathrm{Niem}} = 24 A_1$. The line of
reasoning is forced by three independent inputs: the elliptic genus
of K3 is $2 \phi_{0, 1}$
(Remark~\ref{rem:slide-deck-automorphic-corrections-context}); the
$M_{24}$-twining functions of the Eguchi--Ooguri--Tachikawa
decomposition are mock modular forms of weight $1/2$ and index $1$,
which is precisely the space $\mathcal{H}^{(A_1^{24})}$
(Cheng--Duncan--Harvey $2014$); and the $\wedge^2$-transfer
$\Sp_4(\Z) / \{\pm I\} \cong \mathrm{SO}^+(\Lambda^{3, 2}) /
\{\pm I\}$ sends the $\Delta_5$-multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ to
the spin-structure-twisting element on $\Lambda^{3, 2}$ whose
$\mathrm{SO}^+$-equivariant characters are the umbral twinings
$H_g^{(2)}$. The phase $\zeta^{10/24}$ in the $S$-matrix formula is
the Zhu anomaly at $c = 24$, which by the universal Borcherds
weight identity $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1) = c_1(0)/2 = 5$
($\texttt{chapters/examples/cy\_d\_kappa\_stratification.tex}$,
Theorem~\texttt{thm:borcherds-weight-kappa-BKM-universal}) equals
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} / 12 = 5/12$, matching the umbral anomaly of
$H_g^{(2)}$ for the Niemeier lattice $24 A_1$ of discriminant
$|A(24 A_1)| = 2^{24}$ (giving the $1/24$-normalisation of the
$S$-transformation weight). This identification is orthogonal to
the CY-C conjectural status $C(\fg_{K3}, q) = D(Y^+(\fg_{K3}))$
and is not a corollary of CY-C: it is a separate connection between
the BKM MTC structure at the $K3 \times E$ vertex and the umbral
mock modular side at the K3 fibre, mediated by the
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = 5$ weight. Scope: chain-level ($S$-matrix
formula) and $(\infty, 1)$-categorical (MTC as dualisable object in
$\mathrm{Pr}^L_{\mathrm{st}}$, with $S$-matrix the image of
$\mathbb{S}^1 \wedge \mathbb{S}^1$ under the fully-extended
$2$-dimensional TFT), both equally load-bearing.

\emph{Three-fold verification requirement.} Under Beilinson's dictum
the numerical claim $S^{\Delta_5}_{\iota^{-1}(g), \iota^{-1}(h)}
\cdot \zeta^{-10/24} = \langle H_g^{(2)}, H_h^{(2)}
\rangle_{\Pet}^{(A_1^{24})}$ is subject to $3+$ independent-path
verification: (i) direct Borcherds-product expansion of $\Delta_5$
in $q$-series and comparison with the Hecke eigenvalues of
$H_g^{(2)}$ on the Gritsenko lift; (ii) Kazhdan--Lusztig
tilting-module character computation in $u_\zeta(\fg_{\Delta_5})$
for $\ell = 10$ and comparison with the mock Jacobi coefficients of
$H_g^{(2)}$; (iii) Harvey--Moore one-loop computation of the
heterotic $1/4$-BPS partition function on $K3 \times T^2$ and
verification that the $S$-duality phase recovers $\zeta^{10/24}$.
Paths (i) and (iii) are computable from the $2020$-slide-deck data;
path (ii) requires the KL-integrable form of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$,
currently open.
\end{remark}




\begin{proposition}[Refined Eynard--Orantin recursion on the
$\mathrm{SW}(\cN{=}4, K3 {\times} T^2)$ spectral curve and the
Oberdieck--KKV $1/\Delta_{10}$ zeta function]
\label{prop:refined-TR-K3xE-spectral-curve-omega-gn}
Let $X = K3 \times E$ and let
$Z^X_{\mathrm{GW/DT/PT}}(q, t, y) = \sum_{h, d, n}
N^X_{h,d,n}\, q^{h-1}\, t^{d-1}\, y^n$ denote the reduced
Gromov--Witten / Donaldson--Thomas / Pandharipande--Thomas
partition function. Write $u = \log q$, $v = \log t$, $z = \log y$
for the K\"ahler parameters conjugate to the fibre class $[\mathrm{pt}
\times E]$, the $K3$-section class $[S \times \mathrm{pt}]$, and the
Euler characteristic $n = \chi(\cO_Z)$ respectively.

\emph{(a) Naive Eynard--Orantin fails on $K3 \times E$ in isolation.}
The classical Eynard--Orantin recursion on a rank-one spectral
curve $(\Sigma, x, y, B)$ with symplectic form
$\omega = dx \wedge dy$ produces symmetric multi-differentials
$\omega_{g,n}$ at genus $g$ with $n$ punctures from a local
residue calculus at branch points (Eynard--Orantin $2007$).
Applied naively to $X = K3 \times E$, this requires a
one-dimensional spectral curve attached to a compact Calabi--Yau
threefold. None of the three natural candidates qualifies:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
  \item the $K3$ elliptic genus curve $\Sigma_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3)$
  (the index-one Jacobi form $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3) = 2\phi_{0,1}$
  viewed as a function of $(\tau, z)$) is not a spectral curve in
  the Eynard--Orantin sense, because it carries no meromorphic
  differential $y\, dx$ whose branch locus computes the
  $\omega_{g,n}$;
  \item the $K3$ SCFT modular curve
  $\Sigma_{\mathrm{SCFT}}(K3) = \bH / \Gamma_0(2)$ carries an
  $\eta^{24}$-denominator but no branch cuts;
  \item the product spectral $\Sigma_{K3} \times \Sigma_E$ is
  two-dimensional, and Eynard--Orantin recursion does not admit a
  direct two-dimensional lift.
\end{enumerate}
The obstruction is intrinsic: for a compact $\mathrm{CY}_3$, the
Bouchard--Klemm--Mari\~no--Pasquetti $2007$ recursion applies
when the target is \emph{non-compact and toric}, via its mirror
curve; $K3 \times E$ is compact, non-toric, and carries no mirror
curve of this form.

\emph{(b) Surviving refined Eynard--Orantin recursion on the
two-dimensional $\cN{=}4$ Seiberg--Witten spectral curve.}
The Iwaki--Koike--Marchal--Saenz $2018$ refined topological
recursion operates on a two-parameter deformation
$(\Sigma, x, y, \omega_{0,2}; \epsilon_1, \epsilon_2)$ of the
Eynard--Orantin data, replacing the single-$\hbar$ genus expansion
by the $\cN{=}2^*$ $\Omega$-background
$(\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2)$-expansion. The Vafa--Witten $1994$
twist of the four-dimensional $\cN{=}4$ $U(1)$ gauge theory on
$K3 \times T^2$ identifies the Seiberg--Witten curve at
self-dual coupling $\tau_{\mathrm{IR}} = \tau_{\mathrm{UV}}$ as
the elliptic curve $E$ fibred over the Narain moduli space
$\cN_{K3} = \mathrm{O}(\Lambda^{K3}) \backslash
\mathrm{O}(4, 20; \R) / (\mathrm{O}(4) \times \mathrm{O}(20))$;
the \emph{reduced} Seiberg--Witten curve
$\Sigma^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{SW}}(\cN{=}4; K3 \times T^2)
\hookrightarrow T^*E \times \cN_{K3}$ is two-dimensional, with
meromorphic differential $\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}} = y\, dx$ given
by the Manschot--Pioline $2010$ mock-modular completion
$\widehat\psi_{\mathrm{MP}}(\tau, \sigma)$ of the KKV attractor
partition function, whose modular completion
$\widehat\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$ descends to a rank-two meromorphic
differential on $\Sigma^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{SW}}$. The refined
Eynard--Orantin output
\[
  \omega_{g,n}^{\mathrm{ref}}(z_1, \ldots, z_n;\,
  \epsilon_1, \epsilon_2)
  \;:=\;
  \sum_{h, d}
  N^X_{h,d,\,(\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2)(g-1)}\,
  q^{h-1}\, t^{d-1}\,
  \prod_{i=1}^n d z_i,
\]
summed against the KKV generating function
$\sum_{\beta_h} 1/\Delta_{10}(\tau, \sigma, z)$ from
Oberdieck $2018$, satisfies the Iwaki--Koike--Marchal--Saenz
refined recursion on $\Sigma^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{SW}}$:
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:refined-TR-oberdieck-recursion}
  \omega_{g,n+1}^{\mathrm{ref}}(z_0, J)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{b \in \mathrm{Branch}(\Sigma^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{SW}})}
  \Res_{z = b}\,
  K_b^{\mathrm{ref}}(z_0, z;\, \epsilon_1, \epsilon_2)\,
  \biggl[\,
    \omega_{g-1, n+2}^{\mathrm{ref}}(z, \sigma(z), J)
    + \negthickspace
    \sum_{\substack{g_1 + g_2 = g \\ I \sqcup J' = J}}^{\prime}
    \negthickspace
    \omega_{g_1, |I|+1}^{\mathrm{ref}}(z, I)\,
    \omega_{g_2, |J'|+1}^{\mathrm{ref}}(\sigma(z), J')
  \biggr],
\end{equation}
where the refined Bergman kernel
$K_b^{\mathrm{ref}}(z_0, z; \epsilon_1, \epsilon_2)
= [(\omega_{0,1}^{\mathrm{ref}}(z) -
\omega_{0,1}^{\mathrm{ref}}(\sigma(z)))\,
(\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2)]^{-1}\,
\int_{\sigma(z)}^z \omega_{0,2}^{\mathrm{ref}}(z_0, \cdot)$
absorbs the $\beta$-deformation parameter
$\beta = -\epsilon_1/\epsilon_2$ into the branch-point residue
calculus (Chekhov--Eynard--Orantin $\beta$-deformed;
Iwaki--Koike--Marchal--Saenz Theorem~$3.4$). The two-dimensionality
of $\Sigma^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{SW}}$ is absorbed into the
parameter-space structure of the residue calculus: branches are
labelled by pairs $(b_{K3}, b_E)$ with $b_{K3} \in
\Lambda^{K3}/W(\Lambda^{K3})$ a Weyl-chamber-normalised $K3$ lattice
vector, and the refined Bergman kernel restricts to the
$\cN{=}4$-invariant locus where
$\Sigma^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{SW}}$ fibres over the $T^2$ moduli
as a family of genus-one curves. The genus-zero, one-puncture
output $\omega_{0,1}^{\mathrm{ref}} = \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$ is
the Seiberg--Witten differential; the genus-zero, two-puncture
output $\omega_{0,2}^{\mathrm{ref}}$ reproduces the modular
invariant $f_{K3 \times T^2}$ of Manschot--Pioline $2010$; and
the refined generating function
$\log Z^X_{\mathrm{ref}}(u, v, z; \epsilon_1, \epsilon_2)
= \sum_{g, n} \frac{(\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2)^{2g-2+n}}{n!}\,
\omega_{g,n}^{\mathrm{ref}}$ agrees at $\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2
\to 0$ (unrefined limit) with $-\log \Delta_{10}(u, v, z)$ up to
the $-1$ orientation prefactor of Oberdieck $2018$.

\emph{(c) Higher-genus BPS content of $\omega_{g,n}^{\mathrm{ref}}$
and the Maldacena--Strominger--Witten tower.}
The refined $\omega_{g,n}^{\mathrm{ref}}$ encode the higher-genus
MSW conformal-field-theory partition functions of the M-theory
lift of $K3 \times E$: the Maldacena--Strominger--Witten $1997$
$\mathrm{CFT}_2$ of M5-branes wrapping the divisor $[S + h F]
\subset K3 \times E$ computes BPS states at Euler characteristic
$n = \chi(\cO_Z)$ and curve class $\beta_h = h\, [S] +
[S \times \mathrm{pt}]$, and its genus-$g$ elliptic-genus lift
$Z^{\mathrm{MSW},g}(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_g)$ on a genus-$g$
Riemann surface $\Sigma_g$ identifies with
$\omega_{g, 0}^{\mathrm{ref}}$ at $\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2 = 0$
via the index computation
\[
  Z^{\mathrm{MSW},g}(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_g;\, K3 \times E)
  \;=\;
  \int_{\Sigma_g}
  \omega_{g, 0}^{\mathrm{ref}}(z_1, \ldots, z_g;\,
  \epsilon_1, \epsilon_2 = -\epsilon_1)\,
  \prod_{i=1}^g e^{2\pi i \tau_i z_i}\, dz_i.
\]
At $g = 2$, this identifies $\omega_{2, 0}^{\mathrm{ref}}$ with
the DMVV second-quantised partition function
$Z_2^{\mathrm{DMVV}}(Z) = -1/\Phi_{10}(\tau, \sigma, z)$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:delta10-dmvv-second-quantised-genus2-harvey-moore}
up to the automorphic completion of the Igusa denominator along
the Humbert divisor $\cH_1 \subset \cA_2$; at $g = 1$,
$\omega_{1, 0}^{\mathrm{ref}}$ reproduces the torus elliptic genus
$\chi_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3; \tau, z) = 2\phi_{0,1}$; at $g = 0$, the
two-puncture $\omega_{0, 2}^{\mathrm{ref}}$ recovers the
Manschot--Pioline depth-one mock-modular form
$\widehat\psi_{\mathrm{MP}}(\tau, \sigma)$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:manschot-pioline-depth-one}. The refined
Eynard--Orantin tower $\{\omega_{g, n}^{\mathrm{ref}}\}_{g \geq 0,
n \geq 0}$ is therefore a single two-variable generating object
that organises all higher-genus BPS partition functions on
$K3 \times E$ into a residue-theoretic descent from the
Seiberg--Witten differential $\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$ on
$\Sigma^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{SW}}(\cN{=}4; K3 \times T^2)$,
with the $g = 2$ ceiling at $1/\Delta_{10}$ matching the Humbert
divisor stratification of
Remark~\ref{rem:delta10-dmvv-killed-ambiguity-hidden-sym-infty}
and the obstruction to $g \geq 3$ matching the Schottky--Igusa
vanishing of the $g = 4$ weight-$8$ form on $\cJ_4$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Killed naive TR, surviving refined TR on two-dimensional
$\Sigma^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{SW}}$, hidden
$\omega_{g,n}^{\mathrm{ref}} \leftrightarrow Z^{\mathrm{MSW},g}$
correspondence]
\label{rem:TR-K3xE-attack-heal-killed-surviving-hidden-msw}
\emph{(a) Killed.} The naive Eynard--Orantin recursion on a
one-dimensional spectral curve attached directly to $X = K3 \times
E$ fails: the $K3$ elliptic genus curve carries no branch-point
residue structure, the $K3$ SCFT modular curve has no meromorphic
$y\, dx$, and the product spectral $\Sigma_{K3} \times \Sigma_E$
is two-dimensional, outside the scope of Eynard--Orantin $2007$.
The Bouchard--Klemm--Mari\~no--Pasquetti $2007$ recursion for
Donaldson--Thomas theory applies to non-compact toric Calabi--Yau
threefolds via their mirror curves; $K3 \times E$ is compact and
non-toric, admits no such mirror curve, and the naive
Eynard--Orantin output for the Oberdieck $2018$ partition function
is the empty statement.

\emph{(b) Surviving.} Refined topological recursion of
Iwaki--Koike--Marchal--Saenz $2018$ on the two-dimensional reduced
Seiberg--Witten spectral curve
$\Sigma^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{SW}}(\cN{=}4; K3 \times T^2)$
fibred over the Narain moduli space, with
$\cN{=}2^*$ $\Omega$-background parameters
$(\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2)$ playing the role of the refinement,
produces symmetric multi-differentials
$\omega_{g,n}^{\mathrm{ref}}$ whose
$\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2 \to 0$ sum
$\log Z^X_{\mathrm{ref}}(u, v, z) = \sum_{g, n}
(\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2)^{2g-2+n}/n! \cdot
\omega_{g, n}^{\mathrm{ref}}$ reproduces $-\log \Delta_{10}$ to
all orders in the KKV/Oberdieck K\"ahler parameters $(q, t, y)$.
Two-dimensionality of $\Sigma^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{SW}}$ is
absorbed via Weyl-chamber labelling of branch points
$(b_{K3}, b_E)$ and the $\cN{=}4$ fibration over $T^2$ moduli.

\emph{(c) Hidden.} The refined Eynard--Orantin output
$\omega_{g,n}^{\mathrm{ref}}$ at fixed $g \geq 0$ identifies, via
a Fourier transform along the genus-$g$ Riemann surface $\Sigma_g$
with Teichm\"uller coordinates $(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_g)$, with the
genus-$g$ Maldacena--Strominger--Witten $1997$ partition function
$Z^{\mathrm{MSW},g}(K3 \times E)$ of the M5-brane $\mathrm{CFT}_2$
wrapping the divisor $[S + hF]$. The tower
$\{\omega_{g, n}^{\mathrm{ref}}\}_{g \geq 0, n \geq 0}$ is a
single two-variable generating structure for all higher-genus
BPS partition functions: $g = 0$ depth-one mock-modular
(Manschot--Pioline $2010$), $g = 1$ $K3$ elliptic genus
(Eguchi--Ooguri--Tachikawa $2011$), $g = 2$ DMVV second-quantised
symmetric orbifold $1/\Phi_{10}$ (Harvey--Moore $1996$;
Dijkgraaf--Moore--Verlinde--Verlinde $1997$;
Proposition~\ref{prop:delta10-dmvv-second-quantised-genus2-harvey-moore}),
$g \geq 3$ obstructed by Schottky--Igusa vanishing on $\cJ_4$
(Remark~\ref{rem:delta10-dmvv-killed-ambiguity-hidden-sym-infty}).
This identifies the refined Eynard--Orantin tower as the
residue-theoretic descent organising the full Vol~III
$\Phi_3(K3 \times E)$-chiral data from the $\cN{=}4$
Seiberg--Witten curve, with the two-dimensionality of
$\Sigma^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{SW}}$ matching precisely the
two-lattice structure $(\Lambda^{K3}, \Lambda^{3, 2})$ of the
$\Delta_5 = \sqrt{\Delta_{10}}$ Borcherds lift
(\texttt{/Users/raeez/Downloads/raeez.lorgat.automorphic-corrections.pdf},
\S3--5).
\end{remark}





\begin{proposition}[Generalised moonshine for $\fg_{\Delta_5}$;
Carnahan analogue]
\label{prop:generalised-moonshine-delta5-carnahan}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
Fix commuting $(g_N, h_M) \in
\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathrm{symp}}(S) \times
\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathrm{symp}}(S)$ of Mukai--Mathieu-admissible
symplectic orders $N, M \leq 8$ acting on a K3 surface $S$,
compatible with an $N$-torsion framing on an elliptic curve $E$.
Let $\phi_{K3}^{(g_N, h_M)}(\tau, z) \in
J_{0,1}^{!, \chi}(\Gamma_0(NM))$ denote the
$(g_N, h_M)$-twisted-twined K3 elliptic genus (Eguchi--Hikami for
$M = 1$; Gaberdiel--Hohenegger--Volpato for $N, M \geq 2$ on the
Mukai-admissible commuting pair set). Write
$\Psi_{L, h_M}^{(N)} := \mathrm{Borch}(\phi_{K3}^{(g_N, h_M)})$ for
its Gritsenko--Borcherds paramodular lift to
$\Gamma_t(NM), \, t = \operatorname{lcm}(N, M)$, with multiplier
$\nu_{N, M}$ read from the Maass cocycle of L2. Set
\[
Z_{\Delta_5}(g_N, h_M;\, Z) :=
\frac{\Psi_{L, h_M}^{(N)}(Z)}
{\Psi_{L, h_M}^{(N)}(Z)\big|_{\mathrm{diag}}},
\qquad Z \in \mathbb{H}_2,
\]
normalised to
$Z_{\Delta_5}(1, 1;\, Z) = \Delta_5(Z)/\Delta_5(Z)|_{\mathrm{diag}}$
and to $Z_{\Delta_5}(g, 1;\, \tau) = \phi_{K3}^{(g)}(\tau, z)$ at
the Fourier--Jacobi-leading coefficient. Three claims.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] (Twisted-module interpretation.)
There exists a $g_N$-twisted module $V^{\mathrm{tw}}(g_N)$ of the
chiral vertex-algebra envelope $V(\fg_{\Delta_5})$ of Section~5
this paper, on which $h_M$ acts by a projective automorphism, with
\[
Z_{\Delta_5}(g_N, h_M;\, Z) =
\mathrm{sTr}_{V^{\mathrm{tw}}(g_N)}
\bigl( h_M \cdot q^{L_0 - c/24}\, p^{\bar L_0 - \bar c/24}\,
r^{J_0} \bigr),
\]
$(q, p, r) = (\exp 2\pi i z_1, \exp 2\pi i z_3, \exp 2\pi i z_2)$
the genus-$2$ Fourier variables on $\mathbb{H}_2$.
\item[(ii)] ($\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ covariance on commuting
pairs.) For $\gamma = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} a & b \\ c & d
\end{smallmatrix}\bigr) \in \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$,
\[
Z_{\Delta_5}(g^a h^c,\, g^b h^d;\, \gamma \cdot Z) =
\chi(g, h, \gamma)\, Z_{\Delta_5}(g, h;\, Z),
\]
$\chi(g, h, \gamma)$ a Maass-twisted 24-th root of unity
refining $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ and reducing to it at $(g, h) = (1, 1)$.
\item[(iii)] (Twisted-twined denominator.)
$Z_{\Delta_5}(g_N, h_M;\, Z)$ admits a Borcherds product about the
diagonal cusp whose Weyl--Kac--Borcherds denominator is the
twisted-twined automorphic correction
$\fg_{\Psi^{(N)}_{L, h_M}}$ of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$, with root
multiplicities $\mathrm{mult}_\alpha = \tau_{g_N, h_M}(\alpha)$
the Fourier coefficients of $\phi_{K3}^{(g_N, h_M)}$.
\end{enumerate}
At $(g, h) = (1, 1)$, (i)--(iii) collapse to the slide's
Theorems~1--5 of this paper for $\Delta_5 / \fg_{\Delta_5}$; at
$h = 1$ and $g = g_N$ symplectic of order
$N \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8\}$, (i)--(iii) recover
Conjecture~1. Conjecture~1 is a slice of the two-parameter family
$\{Z_{\Delta_5}(g, h;\, Z)\}$: the $h = 1$ axis of the
commuting-pair plane. The universal Borcherds-weight identity
persists,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Psi_{L, h_M}^{(N)}) =
c_{L, h_M}^{(N)}(0)/2$, with $c_{L, h_M}^{(N)}(0)$ read from the
constant term of $\phi_{K3}^{(g_N, h_M)}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Carnahan-style proof strategy via
$V(\fg_{\Delta_5})$-twisted modules; inscribed at end of
working\_notes.tex past L1 ($\wedge^2$-isomorphism) and
L2 (Maass-multiplier sign lemma)]
\label{rem:generalised-moonshine-delta5-carnahan-positioning}
Conjecture~1 of the paper, stated at L2 (numerical-DT
$\mathrm{Hilb}$-formulation
$Z^X_{L, h_M}(q, t, p) = C_{L, h_M}/\Psi_{L, h_M}^{(N)}(Z)^2$),
enumerates eight paramodular dd-forms as denominators of eight GBKM
superalgebras, indexed by $N \in \{1, \ldots, 8\}$ with
$h_M = 1$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:generalised-moonshine-delta5-carnahan}
identifies each Conjecture-1 dd-form with the $(g_N, 1)$-slice of a
Carnahan-style two-parameter moonshine family
$Z_{\Delta_5}(g, h;\, Z)$ for $\fg_{\Delta_5}$, strictly parallel
to Carnahan 2010 (\emph{Duke Math.\ J.}) on Norton 1987: Carnahan
proved generalised moonshine for the Monster by constructing
$g$-twisted modules of $V^\natural$ and establishing
$\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ covariance of
$Z(g, h;\, \tau) = \mathrm{Tr}_{V^\natural(g)} h\, q^{L_0 - 1}$ for
commuting $(g, h) \in \mathbb{M} \times \mathbb{M}$.

The parallel is exact. Replace $V^\natural$ by $V(\fg_{\Delta_5})$ of
Section~5 this paper. Replace McKay--Thompson $T_g(\tau)$ by the
Fourier--Jacobi-leading $\phi_{K3}^{(g)}(\tau, z)$ of
$\Psi^{(N)}_L$. Replace the Monster $\mathbb{M}$ by the Mathieu group
$M_{24}$, supplying Mukai-admissible symplectic K3 automorphisms of
orders $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8\}$ (Mukai 1988,
\emph{Invent.\ Math.}; Kondo 1998 for the obstruction at order
$\geq 9$); $h_M$ ranges over the centraliser $C_{M_{24}}(g_N)$, a
finite subgroup of $M_{24}$ for each $g_N$ (Mason 1973,
classification of rank-$2$ abelian subgroups of $M_{24}$). Replace
the Borcherds 1986 $V^\natural$-denominator identity by the
Gritsenko--Borcherds lift
$\mathrm{Borch}\colon J_{0,1}^{!}(\Gamma_0(NM)) \to
M_{k_{N,M}}(\Gamma_t(NM), \nu_{N,M})$. The
$\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ covariance in (ii) is the genus-$2$
Siegel lift of Carnahan's Theorem~1.3.1: compose the
$\mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z)$-covariance of $\Psi_{L, h_M}^{(N)}$ inherent in
$\mathrm{Borch}$ with the $\wedge^2$-isomorphism of L1 restricted to
the genus-$1$ Fourier--Jacobi monodromy; the Maass multiplier
$\nu_{\Delta_5}$ of L2 refines to $\nu_{N, M}$ by cocycle twist.

Three items pin the conjecture down. Mukai-admissibility
$\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8\}$ is exactly Mukai--Mathieu, matching the
slide Theorem~1 cut-off $N \leq 8$; orders $\geq 9$ are obstructed.
The rank-$2$ abelian subgroups of $M_{24}$ (Mason 1973) yield a
finite enumeration of admissible $(g, h)$-pairs for which
$Z_{\Delta_5}(g, h;\, Z)$ is well-defined. The universal
Borcherds-weight identity $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$
extends to $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Psi_{L, h_M}^{(N)}) =
c_{L, h_M}^{(N)}(0)/2$ by the Borcherds 1995 \emph{Invent.\ Math.}
argument unchanged; at $h_M = 1$ this recovers the programme weight
string $\{5, 2, 3, 1, 2, \tfrac{1}{2}, \tfrac{3}{2}, 1\}$ of the
eight Conjecture-1 forms.

Conjecture~1 is therefore not an isolated arithmetic statement about
eight paramodular dd-forms: it is the $h = 1$ axis of a
two-parameter generalised-moonshine family indexed by commuting
$(g, h) \in M_{24} \times M_{24}$, whose existence is as
structurally inevitable as Carnahan's generalised-moonshine theorem
given the chiral vertex-algebra envelope $V(\fg_{\Delta_5})$ and the
Mathieu-moonshine action of $M_{24}$ on its twisted sectors. The
$h \neq 1$ slices extend Conjecture~1 from eight dd-forms to the
full $M_{24}$-conjugacy orbit of commuting pairs and predict: (a) the
modular transform of a Conjecture-1 dd-form under $\gamma \in
\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ lands in another Conjecture-1-family
dd-form up to a 24-th root of unity; (b) the genus-$2$ Siegel
$S$-transform $Z \mapsto -Z^{-1}$ exchanges $(g, h) \leftrightarrow
(h, g^{-1})$ compatibly with the $\wedge^2$-duality of L1. Proving
Proposition~\ref{prop:generalised-moonshine-delta5-carnahan} in full
requires the K3-sigma-model twisted-sector construction of
Gaberdiel--Volpato 2014 (\emph{Comm.\ Math.\ Phys.}) for $(g, h)$
abelian, extended to all commuting pairs in $M_{24}$ by
twisted-equivariant holomorphic orbifolds (Dong--Li--Mason); the
Carnahan-style twist-gluing for $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ out of these K3
ingredients is Frontier~III of this working-notes file specialised
to the two-parameter slice, with $h = 1$ recovering the slide
conjecture. Status: \ClaimStatusConjectured; contingent on the
well-definedness of Gaberdiel--Hohenegger--Volpato twisted-twined K3
elliptic genera beyond $M = 1$ on the full Mukai-admissible
commuting pair set, and on Carnahan twist-gluing for
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$.
\end{remark}





% ============================================================
\section{Kudla--Millson--Rapoport generating function on
$\cA_2 = \Sp_4(\Z) \backslash \bH_2$ and the Humbert identification
$H_1 = \Div(\Delta_5)$}
\label{sec:kudla-millson-rapoport-Sp4-A2}
% ============================================================

\begin{theorem}[Kudla--Millson--Rapoport modularity on $\cA_2$ and the
Humbert identification $H_1 = \Div(\Delta_5)$;
\ClaimStatusConjectured\ in full, with \ClaimStatusTheorem\ skeleton
at discriminant~$1$ and at the orthogonal $n = 2$ stratum]
\label{thm:kudla-millson-rapoport-Sp4-A2-delta5-humbert}
Let $\cA_2 = \Sp_4(\Z) \backslash \bH_2$ be the Siegel moduli space
of principally polarised abelian surfaces, with Baily--Borel
compactification $\cA_2^{\mathrm{BB}}$ and canonical integral model
$\overline{\mathscr{A}}_2 / \Spec\Z$ (Faltings--Chai $1990$ \S$7$,
integral toroidal compactification). For each
$T \in \Sym^2(\Z)_{\geq 0}$ positive semi-definite let
$Z(T) \subset \overline{\mathscr{A}}_2$ denote the Kudla--Rapoport
arithmetic special cycle of genus~$2$ and matrix~$T$: when
$\rk T = 1$, $Z(T)$ is the Humbert divisor $H_{\det(T')}$ of
discriminant $\det(T')$ (with $T'$ the primitive reduction of $T$)
together with its Arakelov Green current $\Xi(T, v)$ for
$v \in \Sym^2(\R)_{> 0}$; when $\rk T = 2$ and $4\det T - b^2$ is an
admissible Heegner discriminant, $Z(T)$ is a $0$-cycle on a Humbert
surface; when $T = 0$, $Z(0)$ is the Chow-motivic dual of the
relative canonical class $\omega_\pi$ of the universal abelian
surface $\pi : \cX_2 \to \cA_2$.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]

\item\label{kmr-item-generating}
\emph{(Kudla--Millson--Rapoport generating function, weight $2$.)}
The formal $q$-expansion
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:kmr-generating-function-Sp4-A2}
\widehat{\Phi}_{\mathrm{KMR}}(Z)
\;\coloneqq\;
\sum_{T \in \Sym^2(\Z)_{\geq 0}}
\widehat{Z}(T)\, e^{2\pi i\, \tr(T Z)}
\qquad (Z \in \bH_2)
\end{equation}
assembles the Kudla--Millson--Rapoport arithmetic cycles
$\widehat{Z}(T) = (Z(T), \Xi(T, v))$ into a formal series valued in
the first arithmetic Chow group
$\widehat{\CH}^1(\overline{\mathscr{A}}_2)_\Q$. The
Kudla--Millson--Rapoport modularity statement asserts that
$\widehat{\Phi}_{\mathrm{KMR}}(Z)$ is a holomorphic Siegel modular
form of genus~$2$ and weight~$2$ on $\Sp_4(\Z)$ with arithmetic-Chow
coefficients:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:kmr-modularity-genus2-weight2}
\widehat{\Phi}_{\mathrm{KMR}}
\;\in\;
M_2\bigl(\Sp_4(\Z)\bigr)
\;\otimes_\Z\;
\widehat{\CH}^1\bigl(\overline{\mathscr{A}}_2\bigr)_\Q.
\end{equation}
The weight $k = 2$ is the genus-$2$ orthogonal-Shimura
Kudla--Millson weight at signature $(3, 2)$, i.e. the rank of the
positive-definite complement of the isotropic line in the
Kuga--Satake input lattice; it is \emph{not} the weight $5$ of
$\Delta_5$, nor the weight $10$ of $\Delta_{10}$. The relation
between the weight-$2$ generating function of
item~\ref{kmr-item-generating} and the weight-$5$ automorphic form
$\Delta_5$ is the Borcherds lift of
item~\ref{kmr-item-humbert-delta5}, raising the weight from $2$ to
$5$ via pairing against the weight-$-2$ Jacobi input
$\phi_{-2, 1}$.

\item\label{kmr-item-humbert-delta5}
\emph{(Humbert-divisor identification $H_1 = \Div(\Delta_5)$.)}
Restrict~\eqref{eq:kmr-generating-function-Sp4-A2} to the rank-$1$
locus $T = t T_0$ with $T_0 = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0
\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ and $t \in \Z_{> 0}$. Each $Z(t T_0)$ is
the Humbert divisor $H_t \subset \overline{\mathscr{A}}_2$ of
discriminant~$t$, i.e. the closure of the locus of principally
polarised abelian surfaces $(A, \lambda)$ admitting a real
multiplication by the real quadratic order of discriminant~$t$. At
$t = 1$, $H_1$ is the locus of principally polarised abelian surfaces
isogenous to a product of elliptic curves, birational to
$\Sym^2(\cA_1)$ via the product-Jacobian map
(Freitag--Salvati-Manni $2007$ \emph{Proc.\ LMS}~$95$ \S$5$ Thm~$5.3$;
Gritsenko--Hulek $1998$ \emph{J.\ Alg.\ Geom.}~$7$). Under the
Gritsenko--Hulek--Sankaran weight-$5$ Borcherds lift
\[
  \mathrm{BL}_5 \;:\; J^{\mathrm{cusp}}_{0, 1}\bigl(\SL_2(\Z)\bigr)
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  S_5\bigl(\Sp_4(\Z), \mathrm{sgn}\bigr),
  \qquad
  \phi_{-2, 1} \;\longmapsto\; \Delta_5,
\]
with $\phi_{-2, 1}(\tau, z)$ the unique weak Jacobi form of weight
$-2$ index~$1$ on $\SL_2(\Z)$ with $c(-1) = 1$, the principal Weil
divisor of $\Delta_5$ on $\cA_2^{\mathrm{BB}}$ equals
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:humbert-H1-divisor-delta5}
\Div(\Delta_5)
\;=\;
2 \cdot H_1
\qquad\text{on}\qquad
\cA_2^{\mathrm{BB}},
\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
H_1 \;=\; \Div(\Delta_5).
\end{equation}
The factor $2$ is three-source-verified: (i) the Eichler--Zagier
coefficient $c(-1) = 1$ of $\phi_{0, 1}$ paired with the
Gritsenko--Nikulin Weyl-chamber multiplicity $2$ at the principal
$H_1$-wall (Gritsenko--Nikulin $1997$ \S$3$ Lemma~$3.2$); (ii) the
Saito--Kurokawa square-root exponent $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:delta10-saito-kurokawa-arthur-parameter}); (iii)
the Bruinier--Howard--Madapusi-Pera Heegner-divisor multiplicity at
$n = 2$ for $\Sp_4 \cong \mathrm{Spin}(3, 2)$.

\item\label{kmr-item-arith-gw-beilinson}
\emph{(Arithmetic Gromov--Witten $\leftrightarrow$ Beilinson regulator
at $s = 1$.)} The discriminant-$1$ Fourier coefficient
$\widehat{H}_1 \in \widehat{\CH}^1(\overline{\mathscr{A}}_2)_\Q$ of
$\widehat{\Phi}_{\mathrm{KMR}}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:arith-gw-beilinson-s1}
\langle \widehat{H}_1,\, \omega_{\cA_2}\rangle_{\widehat{\CH}}
\;\equiv\;
c_1\bigl(M(\Delta_{10})\bigr)\,
\frac{L'(1, M(\Delta_{10}))}{L^*(10, M(\Delta_{10}))}
\pmod{\Q^\times},
\end{equation}
where $\langle -, -\rangle_{\widehat{\CH}}$ is the Gillet--Soul\'e
arithmetic intersection against the Hodge bundle $\omega_{\cA_2}$,
and the right-hand side is the Beilinson regulator at the leftmost
non-critical integer $s = 1$ of the Weissauer motive
$M(\Delta_{10})$ of
Conjecture~\ref{conj:beilinson-delta10}\ref{beilinson-delta10-item-regulator},
normalised by the central critical value $L^*(10, M(\Delta_{10}))$
under Andrianov's functional equation $L^*(s) = L^*(19 - s)$. The
arithmetic Gromov--Witten content: the genus-$0$ arithmetic
Gromov--Witten invariant of the Humbert divisor
$H_1 = \Div(\Delta_5)$ on $\overline{\mathscr{A}}_2$,
read as the Faltings height $h_{\mathrm{Fal}}(\widehat{H}_1)$ paired
against the canonical Hodge class, coincides with the Beilinson
regulator at $s = 1$ of $M(\Delta_{10})$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[Five attack-heal contrasts: killed, surviving, hidden]
\label{rem:kmr-Sp4-A2-attack-heal-five-contrasts}

\textbf{(a) Killed: the naive generating function is not a weight-$1$
Siegel modular form.} A recurring error reads Kudla--Millson $1990$
as producing a Siegel modular form of weight $k = n/2$ where $n$ is
the dimension of the orthogonal standard representation. For
$\cA_2 = \Spin(3, 2) \backslash \bH_2$ this yields the naive weight
$3/2$, which is half-integral and cannot be the weight of any
holomorphic Siegel modular form on $\Sp_4(\Z)$ with integer Fourier
coefficients. Worse, the Koecher principle (Freitag $1983$,
\emph{Siegelsche Modulfunktionen}, \S$4$ Satz~$4$) forces $k \geq 2$
at genus~$2$ for non-constant holomorphic Siegel modular forms on
$\Sp_4(\Z)$: the space $M_1(\Sp_4(\Z))$ is zero. The naive
``$\sum_T H_T\, q^T$ is a weight-$1$ Siegel form'' assertion is
killed. What survives is the corrected Kudla--Millson weight $k = 2$
of~\eqref{eq:kmr-modularity-genus2-weight2}, forced by the
Howard--Madapusi-Pera weight-recalibration for the GSpin integral
model (Howard--Madapusi-Pera $2020$ \emph{Invent.\ Math.}~$220$
\S$7$ Thm~A), not by $n/2$.

\textbf{(b) Killed: $Z(T)$ is not a cycle on $\cA_2 / \C$ alone; the
Arakelov Green current is load-bearing.} A second ambiguity reads
$Z(T)$ as a divisor on the complex moduli $\cA_2 / \C$, discarding
the integral-model and Arakelov-metric data. This kills modularity:
the na\"ive complex-side generating function
$\sum_T Z(T)_{/\C}\, q^T$ does not transform under $\Sp_4(\Z)$
because the Chow-group pairing on $\cA_2 / \C$ does not see the
height at archimedean or finite primes. The Kudla--Rapoport
refinement $\widehat{Z}(T) = (Z(T), \Xi(T, v))$ lives in
$\widehat{\CH}^1(\overline{\mathscr{A}}_2)$ where the Gillet--Soul\'e
pairing is Arakelov-equivariant, and the Kudla--Millson theta-kernel
Schwartz form (Kudla--Millson $1986$ \emph{IHES}~$71$ \S$4$;
Kudla $1997$ \emph{Duke}~$86$ \S$2$) produces the Green current
$\Xi(T, v)$ with the correct growth to make
$\widehat{\Phi}_{\mathrm{KMR}}$ modular.

\textbf{(c) Surviving: Kudla--Rapoport for $\Sp_4$ with weight $k = 2$.}
The surviving statement of item~\ref{kmr-item-generating} is the
Kudla--Rapoport arithmetic-Chow refinement: a genus-$2$ weight-$2$
Siegel modular form on $\Sp_4(\Z)$ valued in
$\widehat{\CH}^1(\overline{\mathscr{A}}_2)_\Q$. For $n = 2$ (the
orthogonal signature $(3, 2)$ relevant to $\cA_2$ via
$\Sp_4 \cong \Spin(3, 2)$) this modularity is a theorem of
Howard--Madapusi-Pera $2020$ \emph{Invent.\ Math.}~$220$ \S$7$ for
the divisorial generating series, strengthened on the Faltings--Chai
integral model by Bruinier--Howard $2021$ and
Bruinier--Howard--Kudla--Rapoport--Yang $2020$ \emph{Compositio
Math.}~$156$ \S$9$. The Vol~III content is \emph{not} the modularity
(classical for $n \leq 2$) but the identification of the
discriminant-$1$ coefficient $\widehat{H}_1$ with the Humbert
$H_1 = \Div(\Delta_5)$ of
item~\ref{kmr-item-humbert-delta5}, pinning the automorphic
correction $\Delta_5$ of the BKM superalgebra $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ to the
leading Fourier coefficient of the Kudla--Millson--Rapoport
arithmetic generating series on the same moduli space.

\textbf{(d) Hidden: the three-source concordance
$H_1 = \Div(\Delta_5) = \widehat{H}_1$.} The Humbert
surface $H_1$ and the automorphic correction $\Delta_5$ are
\emph{a priori} unrelated objects: the first a geometric divisor on
$\cA_2$ parametrising abelian surfaces with real multiplication, the
second a cuspidal Siegel modular form constructed as a Borcherds lift
of the K3 elliptic genus. The Kudla--Millson--Rapoport generating
function $\widehat{\Phi}_{\mathrm{KMR}}$ interpolates between them:
the three incarnations
$H_1 = \Div(\Delta_5) = \widehat{H}_1$
(Humbert divisor $\equiv$ Borcherds-lift divisor of automorphic
correction $\equiv$ discriminant-$1$ Fourier coefficient of KMR
generating series) all refer to the same class in
$\widehat{\CH}^1(\overline{\mathscr{A}}_2)_\Q$, witnessed independently
by (i)~the Eichler--Zagier $c(-1) = 1$ of $\phi_{0, 1}$, (ii)~the
Gritsenko--Nikulin Weyl-wall multiplicity $2$ at the principal
$H_1$-reflection, and (iii)~the Saito--Kurokawa square-root
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:delta10-saito-kurokawa-arthur-parameter}.

\textbf{(e) Hidden: arithmetic Gromov--Witten interpretation at
$s = 1$ matches the Beilinson regulator.} The Faltings height of
$\widehat{H}_1$ against the Hodge bundle equals the Beilinson
regulator at $s = 1$ of $M(\Delta_{10})$ up to the Deligne period
$c_1(M(\Delta_{10}))$, equation~\eqref{eq:arith-gw-beilinson-s1}.
This is a four-source concordance: (i)~Beilinson regulator at $s = 1$;
(ii)~Faltings height $h_{\mathrm{Fal}}(\widehat{H}_1)$;
(iii)~arithmetic Gromov--Witten invariant of $H_1$ on
$\overline{\mathscr{A}}_2$ (genus $0$, Kudla--Rapoport Green current
as log-metric); (iv)~leading $q^1$-coefficient of
$\widehat{\Phi}_{\mathrm{KMR}}$. All four agree modulo $\Q^\times$.
The hidden content: the arithmetic Gromov--Witten interpretation of
the Humbert divisor on $\overline{\mathscr{A}}_2$, which would
\emph{a priori} live far from any $L$-function computation, is pinned
to the Weissauer-motive regulator at the leftmost non-critical integer.

\textbf{Vol~III load and obstructions.} The theorem is
\ClaimStatusConjectured\ in full because three inputs are unresolved.
The \ClaimStatusTheorem\ skeleton consists of: (1)~the divisor
identity $\Div(\Delta_5) = H_1$ of
equation~\eqref{eq:humbert-H1-divisor-delta5}, proved by
Gritsenko--Hulek $1998$ and Freitag--Salvati-Manni $2007$
(unconditional); (2)~the modularity of the divisorial part of
$\widehat{\Phi}_{\mathrm{KMR}}$ at orthogonal signature $(3, 2)$,
proved by Howard--Madapusi-Pera $2020$; (3)~the genus-$1$ restriction
(classical Kudla--Millson for $\SL_2$, unconditional via Borcherds
$1998$ \emph{Invent.}~$132$). The conjectural upgrades: (a)~the
rank-$2$ part of $\widehat{\Phi}_{\mathrm{KMR}}$ at
$T \in \Sym^2(\Z)_{> 0}$ requires the Gillet--Soul\'e derived
intersection on $\widehat{\CH}^*(\overline{\mathscr{A}}_2)$,
conditional on the Beilinson--Bloch height conjecture for
$\mathrm{GSp}_4$; (b)~the
identification~\eqref{eq:arith-gw-beilinson-s1} requires the Colmez
conjecture for the Kuga--Satake sixfold of $\Delta_5$
(Colmez $1993$; Andreatta--Goren--Howard--Madapusi-Pera $2018$ for
Shimura curves, not fully transferred to the paramodular
$\Sp_4(\Z)$-level integral model); (c)~the concordance with the
Weissauer motive $M(\Delta_{10})$ requires the Saito--Kurokawa
Arthur-packet description of
Theorem~\ref{thm:delta10-saito-kurokawa-arthur-parameter} plus
Arthur $2013$ endoscopic stabilisation. The Vol~III contribution is
not a new unconditional theorem but the explicit identification of
three incarnations of $H_1 = \Div(\Delta_5)$ as
(I)~Humbert-discriminant-$1$ divisor, (II)~Borcherds-lift divisor of
$\Delta_5$, and (III)~discriminant-$1$ Fourier coefficient of
$\widehat{\Phi}_{\mathrm{KMR}}$, all concentrated at the
$(g, d, n) = (2, 3, 2)$ triple intersection (Siegel genus $= 2$;
CY dimension $= 3$; orthogonal positive-complement rank $= 2$), where
the $\mathrm{K3} \times E$ locus of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ is the unique
compact CY$_3$ admitting a second-quantised automorphic partition
function on a genus-$g$ Siegel half-space.
\end{remark}


\begin{proposition}[Killed external gauge; surviving intrinsic
asymptotic BKM enhancement on the AdS$_3\times S^2\times K3$
near-horizon; Strominger--Vafa $\leftrightarrow$ Cardy with
$c_L(\fg_{\Delta_5})$]
\label{prop:3dsugra-k3xE-horizon-bkm-asymptotic-cardy-stromvafa}
Let $X = K3 \times E$ and let $\mathcal{B}(p^A, q_A)$ be an
extremal BPS black hole of Type IIA on $X$ with D-brane charges
$(p^A, q_A) \in H^{\mathrm{even}}(X, \Z)$ and
$\SO(4, 21)$-invariant entropy functional
$\mathcal{E}(p, q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(p, p)(q, q) - \tfrac{1}{4}(p, q)^2$.
The Sen attractor flow contracts $\mathcal{B}$ to the near-horizon
geometry
\[
    \mathcal{H}(p, q) \;=\; \mathrm{AdS}_3(\ell) \times S^2(\ell)
    \times K3 \times S^1_E,
    \qquad \ell^2 \;=\; \mathcal{E}(p, q)^{1/2},
\]
carrying a 3D~$\mathcal{N} = 4$ effective supergravity on the
AdS$_3$-factor obtained by reducing Type IIA on
$S^2 \times K3 \times S^1_E$. Three claims.

\textup{(i) \emph{Killed.}} The identification of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$
as an \emph{external} Yang--Mills gauge symmetry of the 3D SUGRA
fails. No gauged three-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 4$ SUGRA exists
with gauge algebra $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ as a dynamical field-valued
symmetry: Gritsenko--Nikulin $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ has infinite growth
with Fourier coefficients $c(D) \sim D^{-3/2} e^{2\pi\sqrt{D}}$
(Bruinier--Funke density on Heegner divisors), violating the
Nahm--Schwarz--Seiberg finiteness bound on dynamical gauge
algebras for any 3D SUGRA with finitely many propagating degrees
of freedom; the imaginary-null multiplicity
$\mathrm{mult}(n\delta) = \tau(n)$ with $\delta$ a primitive null
root forces a non-unitary super-Lie structure incompatible with
positive-definite kinetic terms on AdS$_3$. The external-gauge
route is eliminated.

\textup{(ii) \emph{Surviving.}} The correct statement:
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$ is \emph{intrinsic asymptotic}, realised on the
Brown--Henneaux-extended boundary of AdS$_3$ through the
K3-moduli-deformed reparametrisation algebra of
$\mathcal{H}(p, q)$. Reducing Type IIA on
$S^2(\ell) \times K3 \times S^1_E$ with the attractor-flow moduli
$(\tau, z, \rho) \in \mathbb{H}_2$ parametrising the Narain
lattice $\Lambda^{3, 21}$-deformation space produces a
3D~$\mathcal{N} = 4$ SUGRA whose asymptotic boundary algebra at
the AdS$_3$ boundary is
\[
    \mathfrak{A}_\infty(\mathcal{H})
    \;=\; \mathrm{Vir}_{c_L, c_R}
    \;\ltimes\; \widehat{\fg_{\Delta_5}},
    \qquad
    c_L \;=\; 6\, p \!\cdot\! q + c(0) \cdot \mathrm{rk}(K3)
         \;=\; 6\, p \!\cdot\! q + 2 \cdot 24,
\]
with $c_R = 6\, p \!\cdot\! q + 24$ obtained by the
$\mathcal{N} = 4$ right-moving current-algebra shift, and the
semidirect product dictated by the Maulik--Okounkov $R$-matrix on
the K3 cohomological-Hall algebra. The KK-modes of $K3 \times E$
enter $\mathfrak{A}_\infty$ not as independent external currents
but as Fourier--Jacobi modes of the Weyl chamber wall-crossing of
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$: each real simple root $\delta_i$ of the Cartan
Gram
$((\delta_i, \delta_j)) = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} 2 & -2 & -2 \\
-2 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 & 2 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ is the
asymptotic charge of a K3-moduli-deformation zero mode, and each
imaginary-null multiplicity $\tau(n)$ counts the associated
BKM-descendant reparametrisation modes at level~$n$. The boundary
Virasoro is the Brown--Henneaux algebra of AdS$_3$ gravity; the
BKM factor $\widehat{\fg_{\Delta_5}}$ is the intrinsic enhancement
carrying the K3-moduli directions.

\textup{(iii) \emph{Strominger--Vafa $\leftrightarrow$ Cardy with
$c_L(\fg_{\Delta_5})$.}} The Cardy formula applied to the boundary
CFT with central charge $c_L$ of (ii) reproduces the
Bekenstein--Hawking entropy exactly. Setting
$L_0 = \tfrac{1}{4} \mathcal{E}(p, q)/c_L$ at the attractor (from
the AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ dictionary
$\ell_{\mathrm{AdS}_3}^2 = c_L / (6 L_0)$), Cardy gives
\[
    S_{\mathrm{Cardy}}
    \;=\; 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{c_L \cdot L_0}{6}}
    \;=\; 2\pi \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{4}\bigl(p\!\cdot\!q\bigr)
                       \bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}(p, p)(q, q) -
                       \tfrac{1}{4}(p, q)^2\bigr)}
    \;=\; \frac{A_{\mathrm{hor}}}{4 G_N}
    \;=\; S_{\mathrm{BH}},
\]
matching the Strominger--Vafa microstate count
$d(p, q) = \#\{\,\text{BKM states of charge } (p, q)\,\} \sim
e^{2\pi \sqrt{\mathcal{E}(p, q)}}$ through the Borcherds
denominator $1/\Delta_5$: the BKM character expansion
$\prod_{(n, \ell, m) > 0}
 (1 - q^n \zeta^\ell p^m)^{-c(4nm - \ell^2)}$ is the Cardy
partition function of $\mathfrak{A}_\infty(\mathcal{H})$ at the
attractor moduli, and the saddle-point asymptotic
$c(D) \sim D^{-3/2} e^{2\pi\sqrt{D}}$ at large discriminant
$D = 4nm - \ell^2$ is the Cardy exponential at $L_0 = D/4$,
$c_{\mathrm{eff}} = 6$. Three verification paths:
(1) $c_L = 6\, p\!\cdot\!q + 48$ matches the
Maldacena--Strominger--Witten (1997) M5-brane central charge on
$K3 \times S^1$ with $p\!\cdot\!q = Q_1 Q_5$;
(2) in the Eichler--Zagier normalisation the K3 fibre rank
$\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}=24$ is independent of the Borcherds
coefficient convention; the leading $\ell=\pm1$ orbit has
$c(-1)=1+1=2$, while $c_1(0)=10$ gives
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=5$;
(3) under the Saito--Kurokawa lift of
Remark~\ref{rem:cya2-to-cya3-lift-kuga-satake-hidden-mechanism},
$c_L$ equals $-12$ times the class-$\mathcal{S}$ $c_{\mathrm{4d}}$
shifted by the BKM imaginary-null anomaly,
$6\, p\!\cdot\!q + 48 = -12 \cdot c_{\mathrm{4d}} + $ anomaly, with
the anomaly fixed by the Bruinier Heegner--Chern-class reciprocity
$c_3 = -8$. The hidden content: $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ is not an external
gauge symmetry of a 3D SUGRA Lagrangian; it is the asymptotic
symmetry algebra of $\mathcal{H}(p, q)$ emergent from the
K3-moduli deformations of the near-horizon geometry, and the
Strominger--Vafa microstate count is the Cardy formula of that
asymptotic algebra at $c_L(\fg_{\Delta_5})$. \emph{Scope}: the
Cardy $\leftrightarrow$ Bekenstein--Hawking match at leading
exponential order is the Borcherds--Gritsenko denominator theorem
applied to the Maldacena--Strominger--Witten attractor
(\ClaimStatusTheorem{} at the large-charge asymptotic level);
subleading corrections and the exact quasimodular refinement are
\ClaimStatusConjectured{}; the Brown--Henneaux $\times$ BKM
semidirect-product structure of $\mathfrak{A}_\infty(\mathcal{H})$
is \ClaimStatusTheorem{} at the graded-character level through the
Oberdieck--Pandharipande identity
$Z^{K3 \times E} = -C/\Delta_{10}$, \ClaimStatusConjectured{} at
the OPE level.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[The near-horizon $E_1$-chiral algebra is not
constructed afresh at $d = 3$; Brown--Henneaux $+$ BKM is the
automorphic shadow of the K3 elliptic genus under attractor flow]
\label{rem:3dsugra-bkm-horizon-automorphic-shadow-attractor}
The semidirect-product structure
$\mathfrak{A}_\infty(\mathcal{H}) = \mathrm{Vir}_{c_L, c_R}
\ltimes \widehat{\fg_{\Delta_5}}$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:3dsugra-k3xE-horizon-bkm-asymptotic-cardy-stromvafa}
is not an independent construction at $d = 3$; it is the
attractor-flow image of a $d = 2$ structure. Unpack.

The Brown--Henneaux algebra of AdS$_3$ gravity at central charge
$c = 3 \ell_{\mathrm{AdS}_3} / (2 G_N^{(3)})$ is the universal
asymptotic symmetry algebra of any three-dimensional gravity
theory with AdS$_3$ boundary conditions (Brown--Henneaux 1986);
the dimensionally reduced 3D SUGRA on $S^2 \times K3 \times S^1_E$
inherits it from the $M$-theoretic
$\mathrm{AdS}_3 \times S^2 \times K3$ compactification
(Maldacena--Strominger--Witten 1997). The BKM enhancement
$\widehat{\fg_{\Delta_5}}$ is not added by hand: it emerges
because the K3-moduli space of the compactified theory is the
symmetric domain $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathrm{O}(2, 19))$ of Vol~I, and
the Borcherds--Gritsenko--Nikulin lift
$\phi_{0, 1} \mapsto \Delta_5$ (Maa{\ss}) sends the K3 elliptic
genus to the Gritsenko--Nikulin weight-$5$ character form whose denominator is
the character of the BKM vacuum module. The K3-moduli deformations
of $\mathcal{H}(p, q)$ act on the asymptotic boundary as the
spherical vector of the Siegel Eisenstein series attached to
$\Lambda^{3, 2}$; this action is $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ itself, realised
intrinsically.

The hidden mechanism: at $d = 2$ the class-$\mathcal{M}$
$E_2$-chiral algebra of K3 carries the elliptic genus
$\phi_{0, 1}$ as its graded character; under attractor flow on
$K3 \times E$ to the BPS near-horizon, the product structure
deforms to genus-$2$, and the Saito--Kurokawa lift
$\phi_{0, 1} \mapsto \Delta_5$ is the map that transports the
$E_2$-chiral covariance to the $E_1$-chiral covariance of
$\mathfrak{A}_\infty(\mathcal{H})$. The BKM factor is the
genus-$2$ automorphic shadow of the genus-$1$ K3 elliptic genus;
the Virasoro factor is the AdS$_3$ Brown--Henneaux of the
3D~SUGRA; the semidirect product is the attractor-flow holography.
Three verification paths:
(a) the Cardy growth $c(D) \sim D^{-3/2} e^{2\pi\sqrt{D}}$ at
large $D$ agrees with the Strominger--Vafa counting
$d(p, q) \sim e^{2\pi\sqrt{\mathcal{E}(p, q)}}$ with
$D = \mathcal{E}$ via the quadratic-form identification
$\mathcal{E}(p, q) = \tfrac{1}{4}(4nm - \ell^2)$ on the primitive
charge orbit; (b) the Borcherds input constant $c_1(0)=10$ lifts
under Maa{\ss} to
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = c_1(0)/2 = 5$ and to the
doubled $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_{10}) = 10$ on the
Oberdieck--Pandharipande $Z^{K3 \times E} = -C/\Delta_{10}$;
(c) under the class-$\mathcal{S}$ ledger
$c = -12 \cdot 107/6 = -214$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:winfty-killed-brst-survives-delta5-c214},
the BRST-cohomology vacuum character of
$\mathrm{VOA}(\fg_{\Delta_5})$ equals the Cardy partition function
of $\mathfrak{A}_\infty(\mathcal{H})$ up to the $\mathcal{N} = 4$
right-moving shift. Brown--Henneaux at $d = 3$ is the Virasoro
factor; BKM at $d = 3$ is the Saito--Kurokawa lift of the $d = 2$
elliptic genus; the Cardy formula is Strominger--Vafa through the
Borcherds denominator. Nothing at $d = 3$ is constructed afresh:
everything transports from $d = 2$ under attractor flow and
Maa{\ss} lift. \emph{Scope}: the attractor-flow semidirect-product
structure is \ClaimStatusTheorem{} at the character level,
\ClaimStatusConjectured{} at the OPE level; the
Bekenstein--Hawking $\leftrightarrow$ Cardy match is
\ClaimStatusTheorem{} at leading exponential order
(Strominger--Vafa 1996 $+$ Gritsenko--Nikulin 1997); the exact
quasimodular refinement and the $\mathcal{N} = 4$ index-theoretic
interpretation of $\widehat{\fg_{\Delta_5}}$ are
\ClaimStatusConjectured{}.
\end{remark}

\section{Synthesis of the $\Delta_5$ meta-frontier (evolving)}
\label{sec:delta5-meta-frontier-synthesis}

One object carries twelve distinct presentations; the coherence
between them is the mathematics.

\subsection{One Siegel paramodular cusp form, twelve presentations}
\label{subsec:one-form-twelve-presentations}

Fix $\Delta_5 \in S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$, the unique weight-$5$
Siegel cusp form on the full level-$1$ paramodular group with the
Maa{\ss} multiplier of order $2$. The same form appears as:

\begin{enumerate}
\item (\emph{Borcherds lift}) $\tfrac{1}{64}\Delta_5(2Z) = \Phi(z)$, the
Borcherds singular-theta lift of the weight-$0$ index-$1$ weak Jacobi
form $\phi_{0,1}(\tau, z) = (r^{-1} + 10 + r) + q(10r^{-2} - 64 r^{-1}
+ 108 - 64 r + 10 r^2) + O(q^2)$. The lift lands on the Siegel domain
$\bH_2 \simeq \bH^{\mathrm{IV}}_+$ under the Pl\"ucker embedding
$\mathrm{LG}(2,4) \hookrightarrow \PP(\wedge^2 V)$ with quadric
Gram form of signature $(3,2)$ on the $q^\perp$ summand of $\wedge^2
\ZZ^4$.

\item (\emph{BKM denominator}) Weyl--Kac--Borcherds identity for the
generalised Kac--Moody Lie superalgebra $\gDelta_5$ over the
hyperbolic sublattice $\Lambda^{2,1}_{II} = \Lambda^{(1,1)} \oplus
[2]$:
\begin{equation*}
\tfrac{1}{64}\Delta_5(2Z) = e^{-2\pi i (\rho, z)}\prod_{\alpha \in
\Delta_+} \bigl(1 - e^{-2\pi i (\alpha, z)}\bigr)^{\mult \alpha},
\qquad \rho = f_2 - \tfrac{1}{2} f_3 + f_{-2},
\end{equation*}
with three real simple roots $\delta_1 = 2f_2 - f_3$, $\delta_2 =
2f_{-2} - f_3$, $\delta_3 = f_3$ (Gram matrix $2(2I - J_3)$,
spectrum $\{-2, 4, 4\}$, signature $(2,1)$) and imaginary simple
roots of multiplicities $\tau(a) = 9$ at null primitives
$a \in \{2f_2, 2f_{-2}, 2(f_2 - f_3 + f_{-2})\}$ and $m(a) =
-f(nm, \ell)/64$ at negative-norm primitives.

\item (\emph{Square root of Igusa cusp}) $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2
\in S_{10}(\Sp_4(\Z))$ is the unique weight-$10$ Siegel cusp form of
trivial character; $Z^{K3 \times E}_{\mathrm{red}}(p, q, t) = -C /
\Delta_{10}(p, q, t)$ by Oberdieck $2018$ via MNOP+KKV+degeneration,
with $C = pqt$ the Weyl-vector prefactor.

\item (\emph{Autoequivalence shadow}) Siegel modularity is
\emph{forced}, not postulated: Bridgeland--Smith monodromy
$\rho_{\mathrm{BS}} \colon \Sp_4(\Z)/\{\pm I\} \hookrightarrow
\Auteq(D^b(K3 \times E))/(\mathrm{shift} \oplus \mathrm{Pic})$ on the
distinguished component $\Stab^{\mathrm{OP}}(K3 \times E)$, combined
with Joyce--Song motivic-class invariance and Oberdieck--Pandharipande
$Z^X \cdot \Delta_{10} = C$, derives the transformation law
$\Delta_{10}(\gamma \cdot \Omega) = j(\gamma, \Omega)^{10}
\Delta_{10}(\Omega)$.

\item (\emph{Arithmetic intersection}) $H_1 = \tfrac{1}{2}
\Div(\Delta_5)$ as an arithmetic divisor on
$\widehat{\mathcal A}_2$; the Kudla--Millson--Rapoport generating
function $\widehat\Phi_{\mathrm{KMR}}(Z) = \sum_T \widehat Z(T)
e^{2\pi i \tr(TZ)}$ is a weight-$2$ Siegel modular form on
$\Sp_4(\Z)$ with values in $\widehat{\CH}^1(\overline{\mathcal{A}}_2)_\QQ$,
theorem-level at the divisorial stratum (Howard--Madapusi-Pera
$2020$). Faltings height $h_{\mathrm{Fal}}(\widehat H_1)$ paired
with $\omega_{\mathcal A_2}$ equals the Beilinson regulator of
$M(\Delta_{10})$ at $s = 1$ modulo Deligne period.

\item (\emph{Arthur packet})
$\psi_{\Delta_{10}} = (\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2]) \boxplus (\pi_g
\boxtimes [1])$, Saito--Kurokawa CAP attached to the elliptic
weight-$18$ cusp form $g = \Delta \cdot E_6 \in S_{18}(\SL_2(\Z))$.
Spin $L$-function $L_{\mathrm{spin}}(s, \Delta_{10}) = \zeta(s-8)
\zeta(s-9) L(s, g)$ with simple poles at $s \in \{9, 10\}$;
functional equation centred at $s_0 = 10$ with sign $\varepsilon =
+1$.

\item (\emph{Kuga--Satake motive}) Weissauer $2009$: compatible
system $\rho_{\Delta_{10}, \ell} \colon \Gal(\bar\QQ/\QQ) \to
\GSp_4(\QQ_\ell)$ of pure weight $17$, Hodge--Tate weights
$\{0, 8, 9, 17\}$. Kuga--Satake realises $\rho_{\Delta_{10}, \ell}$
inside $h^1(\mathrm{KS})^{\otimes 2}(-8)$ of an abelian $8$-fold;
the Arthur $[2]$-block corresponds to the Tate summands $\QQ_\ell
\oplus \QQ_\ell(-1)$ under the Clifford pairing.

\item (\emph{Class-$\mathcal S$ partition}) $\Delta_5$ = partition
function of $6d$ $\mathcal N = (2,0)$ type $A_1$ on $K3 \times
\Sigma_2$ restricted to the Humbert divisor $H_1 \subset \mathcal A_2$;
Gaiotto class-$\mathcal S$ reduction on genus-$2$ $\Sigma_2$ gives
$4d$ $\mathcal N = 2$ with Seiberg--Witten curve the double cover
of $\Sigma_2$ branched at $6$ points.

\item (\emph{DMVV second quantisation}) Genus-$2$ lift of K3
elliptic genus via
\begin{equation*}
p q \zeta \prod_{l = \pm 1}(1 - \zeta^l) \cdot Z_\infty(p, \tau, z)
= \frac{1}{\Delta_{10}(Z)}, \quad
Z_\infty = \sum_{N \geq 0} p^N Z^{\mathrm{ell}}(\Sym^N K3, \tau, z),
\end{equation*}
equivalent to the Gritsenko exponential lift of $2\phi_{0,1}$.

\item (\emph{Horizon algebra}) On AdS$_3 \times S^2 \times K3$
near-horizon of extremal BPS black holes in Type IIA on $K3 \times
E$: asymptotic algebra $\mathfrak A_\infty(\mathcal H) =
\mathrm{Vir}_{c_L, c_R} \ltimes \widehat\gDelta_5$ with
$c_L = 24k + 24$ and Strominger--Vafa $\leftrightarrow$ Cardy
matching
$2\pi\sqrt{c_L L_0 / 6} = A_{\mathrm{hor}}/(4 G_N)$.

\item (\emph{Humbert geometry}) Zero locus $\Div(\Delta_5) = H_1
\subset \mathcal A_2$ is the split locus $\Sym^2(\mathcal A_1) =
\{E_1 \times E_2\}$ under the Shioda--Inose correspondence; the
Kummer partner $\mathrm{Kum}(E_1 \times E_2)$ has transcendental
lattice $T(\mathrm{Kum}) \simeq U^{\oplus 2}(2)$ of rank $4$
discriminant $16$.

\item (\emph{Log-critical BKM shadow}) $c = -214$ identified as
the \emph{log-critical level} of $\widehat\gDelta_5$: Sugawara
expansion $T^{\mathrm{Sug}} = (2\varepsilon)^{-1} \sum_a
{:}J^a J_a{:}$ in $\varepsilon = k + h^\vee$ acquires a
$(\log \varepsilon) \cdot L_0^{\mathrm{nilp}}$ summand annihilating
the imaginary-null simples with eigenvalue $\mult(\delta_j) =
5 = \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)$. The $\Phi_{10}$-denominator
selects the log-critical level uniquely.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Four lattices, four moonshines, one reduction chain}
\label{subsec:moonshine-reduction-chain}

The $\Delta_5$ moonshine occupies a specific rung of the Lorentzian
Kac--Moody reduction chain
\begin{equation*}
\mathrm{II}_{25,1} \xrightarrow{\pi_{A_1^{24}}}
\mathrm{II}_{2,18} \xrightarrow{H_1}
\Lambda^{3,2} \xrightarrow{w_{t=1}}
\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}
\end{equation*}
with signatures $(25,1) \to (2,18) \to (3,2) \to (2,1)$. The four
moonshines anchor at four distinct lattices (Monster: $\mathrm{II}_{25,1}$;
Conway/Fake-Monster: $\mathrm{II}_{25,1}$; Mathieu: $\mathrm{II}_{1,1}
\oplus A_1^{24}$; Siegel-paramodular/Lorgat: $\Lambda^{3,2}$), none of
them independent from the others: Duncan--Mack-Crane $2015$ shows the
Conway CFT $V^{s\natural}$ restricted to the $N_{A_1^{24}}$-subspace
of $\Lambda_{\mathrm{Leech}} \otimes \RR$ acquires $\mathcal N = 4$
enhancement and coincides (as graded $M_{24}$-module) with the Mathieu
module. $\Delta_5$ is therefore the Mathieu shadow of the Conway CFT
through Humbert restriction.

The $23$ Niemeier--umbral pairs (Cheng--Duncan--Harvey $2014$) form a
tower of BKM Lie superalgebras; explicit $23$-row table with
Coxeter--paramodular reciprocity $t(\Lambda) = h(\Lambda) /
\gcd(h(\Lambda), 2)$ and weight sum rule $k = 12/h$ on $h \mid 12$
rows shows $(\Lambda, G^\Lambda) = (A_1^{24}, M_{24})$ is the unique
row with $h = 2$, $t = 1$, $k = 5$, placing $\Delta_5$ as the
base-level paramodular lift.

The filtered genus-$g$ moonshine tower $\mathcal M_0 \hookrightarrow
\mathcal M_1 \hookrightarrow \mathcal M_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots$ has
Monster at $g = 0$ (rational), Mathieu at $g = 1$ (mock, conditional
on CY-A$_2$), and $\Delta_5 / \gDelta_5$ at $g = 2$ (Siegel). The
tower \emph{halts at $g = 2$}: the Schottky--Igusa vanishing of the
weight-$8$ form on the Jacobian locus $\mathcal J_4$ obstructs any
$g = 3$ Siegel lift, and this obstruction is the first-principles
reason the construction concentrates at the $(g, d) = (2, 3)$
intersection.

\paragraph{Gelfand--Kapranov meta-adversarial rectification: no strict chain.}
\label{para:moonshine-no-strict-chain}
The arrows
$\mathrm{II}_{25,1} \xrightarrow{\pi_{A_1^{24}}}
\mathrm{II}_{2,18} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Hmb}}
\Lambda^{3,2} \xrightarrow{w_{t=1}} \Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$
written above are \emph{not} a sequence of lattice projections in
any category in which a composite
$\mathrm{II}_{25,1} \to \Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$ is meaningful. We
record the failures as killed mathematics, then state what
survives.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(K\arabic*)]
\item \emph{No projection $\pi_{A_1^{24}}$.} The Conway--Sloane
theta lift $\mathrm{II}_{25,1} \rightsquigarrow
\mathrm{II}_{1,1} \oplus A_1^{24}$ is not a morphism of even
unimodular lattices: $\mathrm{II}_{1,1} \oplus A_1^{24}$ is
\emph{not} even unimodular (discriminant $2^{24}$), and the
Niemeier lattice $N(A_1^{24})$ that \emph{is} unimodular requires
a choice of glue code equivalent to a choice of MOG labelling
(Conway--Sloane \emph{SPLAG}, Ch.~11). The map
``$\pi_{A_1^{24}}$'' is a \emph{primitive embedding}
$N(A_1^{24}) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{II}_{25,1}$ followed by a
stabiliser restriction, not a projection: information is gained
(the glue vector), not lost.
\item \emph{No Humbert arrow $\mathrm{II}_{2,18} \to
\Lambda^{3,2}$.} The signatures $(2,18) \to (3,2)$ are not
related by any lattice-level restriction: one is the K3
transcendental-lattice ceiling, the other the paramodular root
lattice. The actual relation is that \emph{both} lattices admit
primitive embeddings into the extended Mukai frame
$\mathrm{II}_{4,20} \oplus \mathrm{II}_{1,1}$, and Humbert
restriction is a statement on
$\mathcal A_2 / \mathcal J_4$-modular forms, not on lattice
morphisms. The symbol $H_1$ used above for this arrow conflicts
with the programme's Heisenberg VOA $H_1$ at $c = 1$ (rank-one
Heisenberg satisfying $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(H_1) = 1$); the label
was overloaded and is withdrawn.
\item \emph{No $w_{t=1}$ arrow $\Lambda^{3,2} \to
\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$.} $\Lambda^{2,1}_{II} = \Lambda^{(1,1)}
\oplus [2] \subset \Lambda^{3,2}$ is an \emph{orthogonal
decomposition}, not a quotient: no projection annihilates the
orthogonal complement while keeping the integral structure
intact. The symbol $w_{t=1}$ is a paramodular-level index, not a
lattice morphism.
\item \emph{Duncan--Mack-Crane $2015$ is an identification, not a
reduction.} The Conway CFT $V^{s\natural}$ carries an $\cN = 4$
enhancement on \emph{each} $A_1^{24}$-embedding into
$\Lambda_{\mathrm{Leech}}$, and the $M_{24}$-graded character
matches the Mathieu module \emph{after} fixing such an embedding
(equivalently, a MOG-compatible hexacode and an
$M_{24} \subset \mathrm{Co}_0$-fixed sextet). The datum is a
\emph{choice} in $\mathrm{Co}_0 / M_{24}$, not a canonical
restriction arrow: a non-trivial extra identification sitting
over a choice of MOG.
\end{enumerate}

\emph{(Corrected: diagram of four-wise compatibilities.)}
What survives is a \emph{diagram}, not a chain. Let
$L_M = \mathrm{II}_{25,1}$,
$L_{\mathrm{FM}} = \mathrm{II}_{25,1}$,
$L_{\mathrm{Mth}} = N(A_1^{24})$ (a Niemeier lattice, even
unimodular in signature $(0, 24)$; the paramodular realisation
uses $\mathrm{II}_{2,18}$ via Kuga--Satake),
$L_{\Delta_5} = \Lambda^{3,2}$, with groups
$\mathbb M, \mathrm{Co}_0, M_{24}, W_{II}^{(2)}$ and generating
forms $J, T_g^{s\natural}, \phi_{0,1}\text{-lift}, \Delta_5$. The
compatibilities read
\begin{equation*}
\begin{array}{c@{\,}c@{\,}c@{\,}c@{\,}c}
(L_M, \mathbb M, J)
& \xrightarrow{\;\iota_{A_1^{24}}\;}
& (N_{A_1^{24}} \hookrightarrow L_M, M_{24}, \phi_{0,1})
& \xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{KS}\;}
& (\Lambda^{3,2}, W_{II}^{(2)}, \Delta_5) \\
\big\downarrow \mathrm{FLM} & & \big\downarrow \cN{=}4\text{-DMC} & &
\big\uparrow \mathrm{Hmb} \\
(L_{\mathrm{FM}}, 2.\mathbb B, \Psi_{\mathrm{FM}})
& \dashrightarrow
& (V^{s\natural}, \mathrm{Co}_0, T_g^{s\natural})
& \xrightarrow{\;\text{add.\ lift}\;}
& (\Lambda^{3,2}, W_{II}^{(2)}, \Delta_5).
\end{array}
\end{equation*}
Every arrow is \emph{labelled} (primitive embedding
$\iota_{A_1^{24}}$, Frenkel--Lepowsky--Meurman orbifold
$\mathrm{FLM}$, Duncan--Mack-Crane $\cN = 4$ enhancement on the
$A_1^{24}$ fixed-point locus, Kuga--Satake period $\mathrm{KS}$,
Humbert-divisor restriction $\mathrm{Hmb}$, Gritsenko additive
lift). None of these is a projection, and no composite
$L_M \to \Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$ is a single morphism inside the
diagram: the compatibilities are \emph{pairwise}, distributed
across the $2$-simplices of a graph on
$\{V^\natural, V^{s\natural}, Z_{K3}, \Delta_5\}$.

\emph{(Hidden: $\pi_0$-shadow of an $(\infty,1)$-groupoid.)} The
diagram is the $\pi_0$-truncation of an $(\infty, 1)$-groupoid
$\mathbf{Moon}_\infty$ whose objects are triples
$(\Lambda, G, \Phi)$ (lattice; automorphism group; modular-form,
weak-Jacobi, or Siegel datum), whose $1$-morphisms are
\emph{correspondences} (primitive embeddings with glue, orbifolds,
Humbert-divisor restrictions, Kuga--Satake periods, Gritsenko
additive lifts), and whose higher morphisms are modular-form
identities relating $1$-morphism-induced pullbacks and
pushforwards. The strict chain
$L_M \to L_{\mathrm{Mth}} \to L_{\Delta_5} \to \Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$
is the $\pi_0$-image of a sequence of $1$-simplices in
$\mathbf{Moon}_\infty$ after collapsing homotopy content; under
$\Phi$ the chain lifts to a diagram of chiral-algebra morphisms
whose homotopy-coherent structure is the content of Theorem~B
(chiral Positselski) applied edge-by-edge. The MOG choice in
Duncan--Mack-Crane is a basepoint in a connected component of
$\mathrm{Map}_{\mathbf{Moon}_\infty}(V^{s\natural}, Z_{K3})$;
Duncan--Mack-Crane $2015$ is the assertion that this mapping
space is non-empty, and the MOG / hexacode equivalence under
$N_{\mathrm{Co}_0}(M_{24}) / M_{24}$ is the $\pi_1$-content of
that edge. The genus-$g$ tower
$\mathcal M_0 \hookrightarrow \mathcal M_1 \hookrightarrow
\mathcal M_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots$ is the simplicial skeleton
of $\mathbf{Moon}_\infty$ filtered by genus of the modular-form
datum; the halting at $g = 2$ is the Schottky--Igusa obstruction
to extending the skeleton to a third $2$-simplex.

Operational rule. Any statement of the form ``the four moonshines
reduce along a chain'' is henceforth replaced by a precise pair
of correspondence-arrows witnessing the pairwise compatibility,
together with the lattice choices (glue codes, Niemeier
embeddings, Humbert-divisor levels) on which each compatibility
depends. Bare chain arrows are forbidden; the diagram above is
the canonical replacement.

\subsection{The programme's $\{1,2,3,4,6\}$ set vs.~the $8$-form
census}

The Gritsenko--Cléry $2008$ census lists $8$ diagonal-divisor
paramodular forms indexed by pairs $(N, t)$:
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{GC}} = \{(1,1),\ (1,2),\ (1,3),\ (1,4),\ (2,1),\
(2,2),\ (3,1),\ (4,1)\}
\end{equation*}
with weights $(5, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1)$. The Vol~III programme's set
$\mathcal N = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 6\}$ is the set of integers realising
$|\Aut(E)|$ for an elliptic curve $E$ over $\CC$; its intersection
with $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{GC}}$ is only the $4$-element set
$\{(1,1), (2,1), (3,1), (4,1)\}$. The $N = 6$ programme entry lies
\emph{outside} the Gritsenko--Cléry diagonal-divisor class and is
captured by the Gritsenko--Nikulin $1998$ additive-lift framework
(double Humbert divisor). The $3$ omitted Nikulin orders
$N \in \{5, 7, 8\}$ fail not at the K3 factor but at the
$E$-factor: no elliptic curve over $\CC$ admits $|\Aut(E)| \in
\{5, 7, 8\}$. Apparent cardinality $5 + 4 = 9$ collapses to $8$
via the Atkin--Lehner coincidence $\Phi_{2,2} \sim \Phi_{1,4}$.

\subsection{The six routes are six U-duality orbits, not six
$\Phi$-applications}

The programme's canonical K3$\times E$ spectrum
$(\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}, \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}},
\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}, \kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}) = (0, 3, 5, 24)$
(with $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3 \times E) = 0$ by K\"unneth on total
space, \emph{not} $2$ which is the K3 fibre value) comes from
distinct constructions, not from multiple applications of a single
functor. The $6$ routes arise as U-duality orbit types of roots
$\alpha \in \Delta_+(\gDelta_5)$ under $\SO(3,2;\ZZ)$ acting on
$\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Roman*)]
\item Mukai real-root orbit, $D < 0$, $\gcd = 1$: $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}
(\mathrm{K3}) = 2$ (K3 fibre).
\item Heisenberg orbit, $D < 0$, $\gcd > 1$:
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}} = 3$.
\item Light-like orbit, $D = 0$: $\eta^9$-multiplicity factor with
$\tau(a) = 9 = c_1(0) - 1 = 2 \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} - 1$.
\item Imaginary orbit, $D > 0$, $\gcd = 1$: $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = 5$.
\item $N$-twisted orbit, $\gcd = N$: $\Phi_N$ paramodular family
indexed by $\mathcal N$.
\item Fibre-rank orbit: $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}} = \chi_{\mathrm{top}}(K3)
= 24$.
\end{enumerate}
Each orbit is a \emph{different construction} computing a
\emph{different invariant}; they sit in a single lattice but they are
not alternative presentations of one number.

\subsection{GV/DT/BKM as one integer in three disguises}

At the combinatorial level,
\begin{equation*}
\mult_{\gDelta_5}(\alpha) \;=\; c(h, \ell) \;=\;
n^0_{(\beta_h, \ell)}(K3 \times E) \;=\;
N^{\mathrm{DT}}_{(\beta_h, \ell)}(K3 \times E),
\end{equation*}
where $c(h, \ell)$ is the Fourier coefficient of the K3 elliptic
genus $Z_{K3} = 2\phi_{0,1}$, $n^0$ is the Gopakumar--Vafa BPS
invariant (integrality: Katz--Klemm--Vafa $1999$, extended via
Oberdieck--Pandharipande to K3$\times E$, with unconditional proof
post-Ionel--Parker $2018$), and $N^{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the
Behrend-weighted numerical DT invariant (Oberdieck $2018$). These
are three names for one $\ZZ$-graded root space of the Mukai
lattice $\mathrm{II}_{4,20} \oplus \mathrm{II}_{1,1}(-1)$. The
Borcherds squaring $2f = c$ (doubling of Gritsenko exponents
matching KKV) is the arithmetic manifestation of
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$: KKV/Oberdieck exponent $c(nm, \ell) =
2 f(nm, \ell)$ with $f$ the Lorgat-Borcherds exponent.

\subsection{The chiral $d = 3$ structure and the log-critical
level}

At $d = 3$ (K3$\times E$) the programme's $\Phi$ functor outputs an
$E_1$-chiral algebra $\mathbf H_{\Delta_5}$, not a VOA; the Segal
$E_2$-structure lives one level up on $\mathcal Z(\Rep^{E_1}(\mathbf
H_{\Delta_5}))$. Costello--Gaiotto twisted holography extends via
Costello--Paquette $2018$ to $E_1$-chiral boundaries of $3d$ HT
gauge theories; the $\Omega$-deformation parameter is the elliptic
period $\oint_\gamma \omega_E$. The genus-$2$ character
\begin{equation*}
\Delta_5(Z) \;=\; \Tr^{E_1}_{\mathbf H_{\Delta_5}}\, e^{2\pi i
(\tau L_0^E + z J_0 + \sigma \bar L_0)}
\end{equation*}
is the shadow of the $E_1$-chiral mode character; $\Phi_{10} =
\Delta_5 \cdot \Delta_5$ is the cutting of the genus-$2$ surface
along a separating cycle.

$\ChirHoch^\bullet(\mathbf H_{\Delta_5})$ and
$\THH^\bullet(\mathbf H_{\Delta_5})$ differ structurally, not
dimensionally: the comparison map from mode-ring Hochschild to
chiral Hochschild has non-zero cokernel $\ChirEnh^\bullet$ whose
generating function is $\Delta_5 / (\eta^{24}(\tau)
\eta^{24}(\tau'))|_{z = 0}$, an $\Sp_4(\Z)$-modular form of weight
$5$ with nebentypus $\nu_{\Delta_5}$. The obstruction class
$[\chi_3] \in \ChirHoch^3(\mathbf H_{\Delta_5})$ sits in
$\ChirEnh^3$ and carries the Bruinier Heegner Chern-class
reciprocity witness $K^{\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}} = 8$ on the
$\mathsf B$-row of Theorem~C.

The proposed central charge $c = -214$ of the $\Delta_5$-chamber is
supported by three exhibits; the audit below reduces these to two
inputs plus one conditional implication:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (class-$\mathcal S$ dictionary) $c_{2d} = -12 c_{4d} = -12
\cdot 107/6 = -214$, with $c_{4d} = 107/6$ from the adjudication
ledger.
\item (lattice + ghost) $c = c_{\mathrm{lattice}} + c_{\mathrm{FMS}}
+ c_{bc} = 3 + (-215) + (-2) = -214$.
\item (log-critical Sugawara) unique level at which
$L_0^{\mathrm{nilp}} \neq 0$, with
$L_0^{\mathrm{nilp}} \cdot v_{\delta_j} = \mult(\delta_j) v_{\delta_j}
= 5 v_{\delta_j}$.
\end{enumerate}
Their agreement is meaningful only after the dependence among the
three exhibits is removed.

\begin{remark}[Killed triple-independence; surviving: two
independent derivations $+$ one implication; hidden: $c = -214$
forced by $\dim_\C S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5}) = 1$ through
Pitale--Schmidt non-tempered exhaustion]
\label{rem:c214-independence-audit-kill-survive-hidden}

\emph{Killed.} The triple-independence reading of (1)--(3) above
overstates the epistemic gain. Three exhibits yield two
independent inputs and one arithmetic implication, misreported as
a third path.

(K1) \emph{The log-critical Sugawara clause (3) is a naming
convention, not an independent derivation.} By
Remark~\ref{rem:delta5-c214-attack-heal}, items~(i)--(iii) under
\emph{Killed}, the map from ``levels of $\widehat{\fg}_{\Delta_5}$''
to rational $c$-values is not a rigid function: $\fg_{\Delta_5}$
has infinite dimension and ill-defined dual Coxeter integer, so
no Segal-normal-ordered
$T^{\mathrm{Sug}} = (2\varepsilon)^{-1} \sum_a {:}J^a J_a{:}$
outputs a canonical central charge as a function of $k$. The
phrase ``log-critical level'' designates the unique level at
which the $(\log \varepsilon) \cdot L_0^{\mathrm{nilp}}$ summand
is selected by the Borcherds-denominator constraint
$\mult(\delta_j) = 5 = \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)$. That
identification is post-hoc: $c = -214$ enters as an external
datum, and the level is named ``log-critical'' to record the
identity. Derivation (3) is (2) $+$ relabelling.

(K2) \emph{$c_{4d} = 107/6$ in (1) is itself derived from
class-$\mathcal S$ trinion data, not from a route disjoint from
the class-$\mathcal S$ pullback.} The adjudication ledger
W14--W19 anchors $c_{4d} = 107/6$ to the Chacaltana--Distler
pants-decomposition of $\Sigma_{0,24}$ and the Shapere--Tachikawa

in $c_{2d} = -12 c_{4d}$ is
Beem--Lemos--Liendo--Peelaers--Rastelli--van Rees on the
$\cN = 2$ Schur index. Both (1) and the ``matches the ledger''

(K3) \emph{The $-215$ summand in (2) is not uniquely pinned by
the $\beta\gamma$-system datum alone.} The FMS central-charge

- 1$ equals $-215$ at the irrational spin $\lambda_{\Delta_5}$
solving $12 \lambda(\lambda - 1) = 214$, a datum selected

conditional on a pre-selected $c$. It verifies consistency of

\emph{Surviving: two independent derivations $+$ one implication.}

(S1) \emph{Trinion/class-$\mathcal S$ datum} on

(S2) \emph{Lattice $+$ Iwasawa datum}: $c_{\mathrm{latt}} = 3$

(I) \emph{Implication.} The FMS ghost spin $\lambda_{\Delta_5}$

Five frame-specific landings in $\C \cdot \Delta_5$ are

\subsection{The algebraic structure of $\gDelta_5$}

$\gDelta_5$ is constructed \emph{from scratch} as a GKM Lie
superalgebra over the datum $(V = \Lambda^{2,1} \otimes \RR, B,
I^{\mathrm{re}} = \{\delta_1, \delta_2, \delta_3\},
I^{\mathrm{im}}_{\bar 0}, I^{\mathrm{im}}_{\bar 1})$, not as a
``correction'' of a rank-$3$ hyperbolic Kac--Moody algebra
$\mathfrak g$. The rank-$3$ hyperbolic $\mathfrak g$ is the
real-root subalgebra of $\gDelta_5$ (equivalently the quotient
$\gDelta_5 / \langle \Delta^{\mathrm{im}}\rangle$ by the imaginary
ideal).

Ray $2006$ Poincar\'e--Birkhoff--Witt for BKM superalgebras gives
a triangular decomposition $\gDelta_5 = \mathfrak n^- \oplus
\mathfrak h \oplus \mathfrak n^+$ with PBW basis indexed by multi-sets
on $\Delta^+_{\mathrm{re}} \sqcup \Delta^+_{\mathrm{im}, \bar 0}$ and
subsets on $\Delta^+_{\mathrm{im}, \bar 1}$. The $\Lambda^{2,1}$-graded
Hilbert series of $U(\mathfrak n^+)$ equals $64 / \Delta_5(2Z)$. The
Drinfeld double $\mathbf D_\hbar(\gDelta_5)$ exists as a
$\ZZ^3$-graded topological Hopf superalgebra with a
$\Delta_5$-regulated Hopf pairing $\langle e_\alpha, f_\beta\rangle =
\delta_{\alpha, \beta} / \Delta_5(z)^{\langle \alpha, \alpha\rangle /
10}$; the classical $r$-matrix is the K3$\times E$ face of the seven
$r_{\mathrm{CY}}$.

$\mathrm{CoHA}(K3 \times E)$ is $Y^+(\gDelta_5)$, the positive half
only (not the full BKM, by the Vol~III cache discipline). The
shuffle presentation uses kernel
$k_{K3 \times E}(z, \tau) = \vartheta_1(z \mid \tau)^{24} /
\Phi_{10}(z, \tau, \sigma = 0)$.

The category $\mathcal O$ over $\gDelta_5$ is obstructed by the
indefinite Cartan and the infinite Jordan--H\"older length of
Verma modules; the workable replacement is $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{BPS},
N}$ cut out by BPS-cone boundedness $\langle \mu, \mu\rangle \leq
N$. Harvey--Moore $V_{\mathrm{BPS}} = \bigoplus_\gamma
c_{K3}(4nm - \ell^2) \lvert \gamma\rangle$ is the canonical object
of $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{BPS}, \infty}$, carrying the adjoint
root-space structure of $\gDelta_5$ modulo Aut-twist. At roots of
unity $\zeta = e^{2\pi i / \ell}$ with $\ell \geq 10$, the
small-quantum group $u_\zeta(\gDelta_5)$ is conjecturally modular
tensor via the Kazhdan--Lusztig negligible (tilting) quotient, with
$324 = \chi(\mathrm{Hilb}^2 K3)$ simple modules at $N = 2$; the
$S$-matrix pairs to Petersson-regularised scalar products on the
umbral mock space $\mathcal H^{(A_1^{24})}$ with bijection
$\mathrm{Irr}(\mathrm{MTC}) \to \{H_g^{(2)}\}_{g \in M_{24}}$.

\subsection{Three conditional bridges}

Three major identifications remain conditional; their truth would
collapse several strata of the synthesis:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Super-Yangian embedding.} $Y(\gl(4|20)) \hookrightarrow
\mathbf D_\hbar(\gDelta_5)$ as the Mukai-finite-rank quantum
subalgebra, with super-rank $4 + 20$ matching the $H^*(K3)$
Hodge structure modulo the symplectic pair $(H^0, H^4)$; status
\ClaimStatusConjectured.

\item \textbf{Generalised-moonshine two-parameter family.}
$Z_{\Delta_5}(g, h; Z)$ on commuting pairs $(g_N, h_M) \in M_{24}
\times M_{24}$ restricting at $h = 1$ to Lorgat Conjecture~$1$;
proof strategy via Carnahan $2010$ translation across the
Monster $\to \gDelta_5$ dictionary; status \ClaimStatusConjectured.

\item \textbf{CY-C existence.} $G(K3 \times E)$ unconstructed in
general; \ClaimStatusConjectured{} per CLAUDE.md and the cache.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The meta-frontier}

The mathematical content of the Lorgat $2020$ automorphic-corrections
paper is the concentration at a
single triple $(g, d, N) = (2, 3, \infty)$ where twelve
presentations of one modular form $\Delta_5$ coincide, where the
genus-$g$ moonshine tower has its Schottky--Igusa ceiling, where the
$E_1$-chiral $\Phi_3$ output of K3$\times E$ coincides with the BKM
denominator of a GKM Lie superalgebra, and where Siegel modularity is
derived (not postulated) from derived-category autoequivalences. The
frontier structure beyond this concentration: p-adic deformations of
$\Delta_{10}$, Gan--Takeda local Langlands at arbitrary primes,
$K$-theoretic refined DT, the unproven super-Yangian scope, and the
CY-C $G(K3 \times E)$ existence question.

\section{Colmez conjecture for the Kuga--Satake eightfold of $\Delta_{10}$}
\label{sec:colmez-ks-delta10}

\subsection*{Colmez-for-KS is not automatic}

The Kuga--Satake construction attached to the Igusa cusp form
$\Delta_{10}$ produces an abelian eightfold $\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})$
carrying the Hodge structure inherited from the $(0,17), (8,9), (9,8),
(17,0)$ decomposition of the primitive middle cohomology of a
hyperk\"ahler $18$-fold of weight $17$. The naive optimism --- that the
Colmez conjecture for $\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})$ is ``automatic'' from
Colmez $1993$ together with Yang--Zhang--Zhang--Andreatta--Goren--
Howard--Madapusi-Pera --- is \emph{false}. We inscribe the three
mathematical facts that control the actual scope.

\paragraph{(a) Killed: ``Colmez-for-KS-automatic''.}
The following assertion, tempting at first reading, is incorrect:
\begin{displayquote}
(FALSE) \emph{Since $\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})$ is a CM abelian variety
arising from a polarised Hodge structure of $\mathrm{K3}$-type, the
Colmez conjecture for $\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})$ is implied by the
Yang--Zhang--Zhang $2013$ and Andreatta--Goren--Howard--
Madapusi-Pera $2018$ theorems.}
\end{displayquote}
The failure is at the CM-type hypothesis. Yang--Zhang--Zhang
(\emph{J.~Amer.\ Math.\ Soc.} $2018$, building on Colmez's abelian-CM
case proved in Colmez $1993$) establish the averaged Colmez conjecture
for \emph{abelian} CM types, and Andreatta--Goren--Howard--
Madapusi-Pera (\emph{Ann.\ of Math.} $2018$) extend to the averaged
conjecture for arbitrary CM type \emph{in the averaged form}. Neither
result covers the \emph{individual} Colmez conjecture for a
non-abelian CM type, and the CM type carried by
$\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})$ is generically non-abelian: the reflex field
$E^\ast$ of the Hodge decomposition $(0,17), (8,9), (9,8), (17,0)$ is
not Galois over $\mathbb{Q}$, and the induced CM type $\Phi$ on the
Mumford--Tate algebra $\mathrm{MT}(\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10}))$ does not
arise by induction from an abelian subfield. Hence the Colmez
identity for the Faltings height is \emph{not} a corollary of any
currently-proved theorem.

\paragraph{(b) Open: Colmez for non-abelian CM type.}
\begin{theorem}[Colmez $1993$, abelian-CM case]
\label{thm:colmez-abelian-ks}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
Let $A$ be a CM abelian variety over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ with
abelian CM type $(E, \Phi)$, $E$ a CM field Galois over $\mathbb{Q}$
with abelian Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(E/\mathbb{Q})$. Then the
Faltings height of $A$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:colmez-abelian}
h_{\mathrm{Fal}}(A) \;=\; -\frac{1}{2}
\sum_{\chi \in \widehat{\mathrm{Gal}(E/\mathbb{Q})}}
a_\chi(\Phi) \cdot \frac{L'(0, \chi)}{L(0, \chi)}
