\;-\; \frac{1}{4} \sum_\chi a_\chi(\Phi) \log f_\chi,
\end{equation}
where $a_\chi(\Phi)$ are rational coefficients determined by $\Phi$
and $f_\chi$ the Artin conductor.
\end{theorem}

\begin{conjecture}[Colmez, non-abelian-CM version for $\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})$]
\label{conj:colmez-nonabelian-ks-delta10}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
Let $A = \mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})$, a CM abelian eightfold with
non-abelian CM type $(E^\ast, \Phi_{\mathrm{KS}})$ where $E^\ast$ is
the reflex field of the $(0,17), (8,9), (9,8), (17,0)$ decomposition
of the Mukai--Kuga--Satake $H^{17}$. Then
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:colmez-nonabelian-ks}
h_{\mathrm{Fal}}(\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})) \;=\;
-\frac{1}{2} \sum_{\rho \in \widehat{\mathrm{Gal}(\widetilde{E^\ast}/\mathbb{Q})}^{\mathrm{irr}}}
m_\rho(\Phi_{\mathrm{KS}}) \cdot \frac{L'(0, \rho)}{L(0, \rho)}
\;-\; \frac{1}{4} \sum_\rho m_\rho(\Phi_{\mathrm{KS}}) \log f_\rho,
\end{equation}
where the sum runs over irreducible Artin representations of
$\mathrm{Gal}(\widetilde{E^\ast}/\mathbb{Q})$ with $\widetilde{E^\ast}$
the Galois closure, and $m_\rho(\Phi_{\mathrm{KS}}) \in \mathbb{Q}$
are the non-abelian multiplicity coefficients of the Colmez invariant.
\end{conjecture}

The conjecture is \emph{open}; the averaged form
$\sum_\Phi h_{\mathrm{Fal}}(A_\Phi)$ over the orbit of CM types under
$\mathrm{Gal}(\widetilde{E^\ast}/\mathbb{Q})$ is implied by
Andreatta--Goren--Howard--Madapusi-Pera, but the individual height
$h_{\mathrm{Fal}}(\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10}))$ at the specific CM type
$\Phi_{\mathrm{KS}}$ requires the non-abelian refinement.

\paragraph{(c) Hidden theorem: $L'(0,\rho)$ as KS-height formula.}
\begin{conjecture}[Transcendental numerical prediction]
\label{conj:ks-height-transcendental-numerics}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
Conditional on \Cref{conj:colmez-nonabelian-ks-delta10}, the Faltings
height of $\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})$ decomposes as a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear
combination of transcendental numbers
$\{L'(0, \rho) : \rho \in \widehat{\mathrm{Gal}(\widetilde{E^\ast}/\mathbb{Q})}^{\mathrm{irr}}\}$
that arise as \emph{arithmetic-intersection periods} on the Kuga--Satake
Shimura variety $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathrm{GSpin}(2, 17))$:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:ks-height-arith-intersection}
h_{\mathrm{Fal}}(\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})) \;=\;
\langle \widehat{\mathcal{Z}}(\Delta_{10}), \widehat{\omega} \rangle_{\mathrm{Arak}},
\end{equation}
where $\widehat{\mathcal{Z}}(\Delta_{10})$ is the arithmetic special
divisor on the integral model of $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathrm{GSpin}(2,17))$
cut out by the Heegner divisor attached to $\Delta_{10}$, and
$\widehat{\omega}$ is the arithmetic Hodge line bundle with Petersson
metric. The right side is the $\mathrm{GSpin}(2, 17)$-analogue of the
Gross--Zagier--Kudla--Yuan arithmetic-intersection formula; its
computation in the $\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})$ case would yield
explicit transcendental numerical predictions for the individual
$L'(0, \rho)$ values, obstructed at present by the non-abelian CM
scope.
\end{conjecture}

\subsection*{Scope and frontier structure}

The chain-level obstruction to proving
\Cref{conj:colmez-nonabelian-ks-delta10} is the absence of an explicit
$q$-expansion for the Gritsenko lift of $\Delta_{10}$ against the
Kudla--Millson theta kernel on $\mathrm{SO}(2, 17)$ at the reflex CM
points; the $(\infty, 1)$-categorical obstruction is the
non-abelian-CM Artin $L$-function factorisation (outside the
Andreatta--Goren--Howard--Madapusi-Pera averaged-case scope). The
chiral-side image of $\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})$ under the Vol III
functor $\Phi$ does \emph{not} manifestly compute this height; the
direct integral-model arithmetic-intersection route via
$\mathrm{GSpin}(2, 17)$ Shimura variety is the first-principles
approach, independent of the Vol III $\Phi$ functor, and its
$(\infty, 1)$-categorical shadow on the derived Shimura stack is the
lane in which a future proof would live. All three assertions
$(a), (b), (c)$ are inscribed at scope \ClaimStatusConjectured{} for
(b) and (c); (a) is the killed claim and thus correctly negative.

\section{The Hida--Skinner $p$-adic family of $\Delta_{10}$ and the
$p$-adic Oberdieck zeta}
\label{sec:hida-skinner-delta10}

\subsection*{Non-ordinarity of $\Delta_{10}$ and Klingen half-ordinarity}

Ordinarity for a Siegel genus-$2$ eigenform at a prime $p$ asks
that the Hecke operators $U_{p,1}, U_{p,2}$ of the Borel parabolic
$B \subset \Sp_4(\Z_p)$ act on a $p$-stabilised new vector with
$p$-adic-unit eigenvalues: $v_p(\alpha_{p,i}) = 0$ for $i = 1, 2$
where $\alpha_{p,1}, \alpha_{p,2}$ are the two Iwahori Hecke
eigenvalues of the Borel stabilisation. This is the Hida $1988$
hypothesis under which the Iwasawa control theorem deforms the
eigensystem along the Borel eigenvariety.

The Arthur parameter of $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ at weight
$(k_1, k_2) = (10, 10)$ with trivial central character is
Saito--Kurokawa non-tempered CAP of the form
\[
 \psi_{\Delta_{10}} \;=\; (\chi_{\mathrm{triv}} \boxtimes S[2])
  \ \boxplus\ (\pi_g \boxtimes S[1]),
\]
where $\pi_g$ is the Saito--Kurokawa elliptic constituent
$g=\Delta E_6\in S_{18}(\SL_2(\Z))$, not a weight-$11$ Ramanujan
form. The Langlands $L$-group side
$\widehat{\mathrm{GSp}}_4 = \mathrm{GSpin}_5$ reads the Satake
parameters at every prime $p \nmid 11$ as the multiset
\[
  \mathrm{Sat}_p(\Delta_{10}) \;=\;
 \bigl\{\,\alpha_p,\ \beta_p,\ p^{8} \alpha_p^{-1},\ p^{9} \beta_p^{-1}\,\bigr\},
\qquad \alpha_p \beta_p = a_p(g)
\]
with $a_p(g)$ the coefficient of $g=\Delta E_6$. The
Newton polygon has slopes $\{0, 0, 8, 9\}$: $U_{p,2}$ acts with
$p$-adic slope $\geq 8$ on every $p$-stabilisation. $\Delta_{10}$
is \emph{non-ordinary} at every prime $p \nmid 11$, and the naive
Hida $1988$ Borel-ordinary deformation is vacuous.

The healing is the Klingen parabolic $P_{\mathrm{Kl}} \subset
\mathrm{GSp}_4$ with Levi $\mathrm{GL}_2 \times \mathrm{GL}_1$.
Tilouine--Urban $1999$ define a Klingen-ordinary eigenvariety
$\cE^{\mathrm{Kl}}_{\mathrm{GSp}_4}$ on which only the slope-zero
direction of the Satake parameters is imposed. For
$\Delta_{10}$ the slope-zero direction is precisely the Jacobi
block $(\pi_g \boxtimes S[1])$ with Satake parameters
$\{\alpha_p, p^9 \beta_p^{-1}\}$ restricted to $\alpha_p$ of
slope $0$; the Klingen-ordinary stabilisation selects $\alpha_p$
as the $U_{p,1}$-eigenvalue of a new vector and the
$U_{p,2}$-eigenvalue drops out of the ordinarity condition.
$\Delta_{10}$ is expected to lie on a Klingen-nearly-ordinary branch at
primes satisfying the relevant parabolic ordinarity and residual
hypotheses.  This is not a direct consequence of the Lehmer
non-vanishing locus, and Skinner--Urban $2014$ Theorem~B for ordinary
$\GL_2$ forms does not by itself furnish a $\GSp_4$ Klingen-family
Iwasawa Main Conjecture for $\Delta_{10}$.

\begin{conjecture}[Klingen-ordinary deformation of the Saito--Kurokawa point
interpolating the Oberdieck $K3 \times E$ zeta,
\ClaimStatusConjectured]
\label{thm:hida-skinner-delta10-oberdieck}
Let $\Delta_{10}=\chi_{10}$ be the Saito--Kurokawa lift attached to
$g=\Delta E_6\in S_{18}(\SL_2(\Z))$.  At a prime $p$ for which the
$p$-stabilisation satisfies the relevant Klingen-nearly-ordinary and
residual hypotheses, one expects a rigid-analytic Klingen-ordinary family
\[
\bigl\{\Delta_{10}[\kappa]\bigr\}_{\kappa \in \cW_p}
\ \subset\ \cE^{\mathrm{Kl}}_{\mathrm{GSp}_4, p}
\]
over a two-dimensional weight-space neighbourhood $\cW_p \subset
\Spec(\Lambda_p)$ with Iwasawa algebra $\Lambda_p = \Z_p[[T_1,
T_2]]$, such that the classical specialisation at $\kappa = (10, 10)$
equals the Borcherds--Gritsenko cusp form $\Delta_{10}$. For every
classical point $\kappa \in \cW_p \cap \Z_{\geq 10}^2$ the
Arthur parameter of $\Delta_{10}[\kappa]$ is
$(\chi_\kappa \boxtimes S[2]) \boxplus (\pi_g[\kappa] \boxtimes
S[1])$ with $\pi_g[\kappa]$ a Hida-family deformation of the
weight-$18$ constituent $g$ when the required ordinary hypotheses hold.
The associated $p$-adic $L$-function $L_p(\Delta_{10}[\kappa],s)$ is
expected to satisfy a Klingen-Selmer divisibility
\[
  \mathrm{char}_{\Lambda_p}\bigl(X_{\mathrm{Sel}}
    (\Delta_{10}[\kappa])\bigr) \ \Big|\ L_p(\Delta_{10}[\kappa], s),
\]
with $X_{\mathrm{Sel}}$ the Pontryagin dual of the Klingen-Selmer
group. The reciprocal specialisation equals the $p$-adic Oberdieck
zeta of $K3 \times E$: for every classical weight $\kappa =
(k, k) \in \cW_p \cap \Z_{\geq 10}^2$,
\[
  \Delta_{10}[\kappa](q, t, p)^{-1} \ =\ Z^{K3 \times E}_{p, k}(q, t, p),
\]
the $p$-adic Pandharipande--Thomas partition function of
$K3 \times E$ at level-$(k, k)$ weight. The universal Borcherds
identity $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N[\kappa]) = c_{N, \kappa}(0)
/ 2$ persists $p$-adically for all $N \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 6\}$ with
$c_{N, \kappa}$ the $p$-adic interpolation of the Fourier
coefficients of the Gritsenko--Igusa series. The
$r_{\mathrm{CY}}$-face at $K3 \times E$ admits a $\Lambda_p$-linear
lift $r_{\mathrm{CY}, p}(\kappa) \in \mathbf D_\hbar(\gDelta_5)
\mathbin{\hat\otimes}_{\Z_p} \Lambda_p$ whose specialisation at
$\kappa = (10, 10)$ is the Borcherds--Gritsenko denominator
formula $1 / \Delta_5(2Z) = \Phi(z) / 64$ of the GKM
superalgebra $\gDelta_5$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{remark}
The parabolic ordinary and residual hypotheses at $p$ are load-bearing in
three places. First, it selects the Klingen-ordinary
stabilisation of $\Delta_{10}$ at $p$: without it, both
$U_{p,1}$-eigenvalues of the Klingen stabilisation would carry
positive slope and the Klingen eigenvariety would miss
$\Delta_{10}$ at $p$. Second, it ensures the associated Galois
representation $\rho_{\Delta_{10}, p}: \Gal(\overline\Q / \Q) \to
\mathrm{GSp}_4(\overline{\Z}_p)$ is residually absolutely
irreducible, the Clozel--Harris--Taylor input to the Taylor--Wiles
patching on the Klingen deformation ring. Third, it is the
condition under which Liu--Zhu $2019$ construct the $p$-adic
$L$-function at non-Iwahoric level without the Coleman
$\theta$-operator obstruction.

The DT-geometric content is that classical specialisations
$\Delta_{10}[\kappa]$ at $\kappa = (k, k)$ produce weight-$k$
Borcherds--Gritsenko cusp forms $\Delta_{2k}$ (Gritsenko lift of
$\Delta_{2k-1}$ elliptic cusp form, with $\Delta_{2 \cdot 10} =
\Delta_{20}$ and $\Delta_{20}^{-1}$ the weight-$20$ genus-$2$
partition function of K\"ahler moduli of $K3 \times E$). These
are not classical Oberdieck partition functions, which live only
at $k = 10$; the $p$-adic family packages the higher-weight
Siegel modular forms as a rigid-analytic fibration over $\cW_p$
whose fibre at $\kappa = (10, 10)$ is the Oberdieck PT zeta of
$K3 \times E$, and whose generic fibre parametrises higher-rank
refined DT partition functions indexed by $p$-adic weights. This
is the Coleman--Mazur eigencurve construction in the
$\mathrm{GSp}_4$ setting with coherent-sheaf-theoretic
$K3 \times E$ incarnation.

Two bridges to Vol III canonical infrastructure extend
$p$-adically. (a) The universal Borcherds weight identity
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0) / 2$ at $N \in \{1, 2, 3,
4, 6\}$ extends because $\Phi_N$ is a Borcherds product of
$\vartheta$-quotients whose Fourier coefficients are interpolated
by the Hida family along the orthogonal Shimura variety
$\mathrm{Sh}_{\mathrm{SO}(2, N+1)}$. (b) The CY-D dimensional
stratification $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3 \times E) = 0 =
\chi(\cO_{K3 \times E})$ (K\"unneth-multiplicative on the total
space, never the fibre $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3) = 2$) is
geometric, insensitive to the weight deformation, and preserved
under the $p$-adic Kuga--Satake correspondence on
$\mathrm{Hilb}^{[n]}(K3)$ and $\mathrm{Sh}_{\mathrm{SO}(3, 2)}$.

Three obstructions remain. First, the existence of the relevant
$p$-adic $L$-function at non-Iwahoric/Klingen level is not supplied by
the preceding discussion; it must be constructed for the
Saito--Kurokawa constituent $g=\Delta E_6$ with the correct parabolic
ordinary hypotheses. Second, the full Iwasawa divisibility upgrade to
equality requires Euler-system
input from Heegner points on the Humbert surface
$\mathrm{Hum}_d \subset \mathrm{Sh}_{\mathrm{SO}(3, 2)}$, which
is open at interior weights $\kappa \neq (10, 10)$. Third, the
compatibility of the $\Lambda_p$-linear $r$-matrix $r_{\mathrm{CY},
p}(\kappa)$ with the $\hbar$-quantisation of the BKM Drinfeld
double $\mathbf D_\hbar(\gDelta_5)$ requires a $p$-adic
Etingof--Kazhdan quantisation theorem, conjectural for BKM
superalgebras even in the classical case (Etingof--Kazhdan $1996$
is proven for symmetrisable Kac--Moody, not for
GKM-indefinite-Cartan).
\end{remark}

\section{Tate conjecture for $\mathcal{A}_2$ at the Humbert divisor $H_1$}
\label{sec:tate-humbert-delta-5-witness}

\subsection*{Deligne--Tate channel}

The moduli $\mathcal{A}_2 = \mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z) \backslash \mathbb{H}_2$
of principally polarised abelian surfaces is a three-dimensional
Shimura variety. Tate's $1965$ conjecture asserts: for $X$ smooth
projective over a finitely-generated field $F$, every
$\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{F}/F)$-invariant class in
$H^{2i}_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(X_{\overline{F}}, \Q_\ell(i))$ is a
$\Q_\ell$-linear combination of algebraic cycle classes. At
codimension one on $\mathcal{A}_2$ the statement acquires a sharp
refined form controlled by Humbert loci, and the Gritsenko cusp form
$\Delta_5$ realises this refinement directly.

\subsection{The killed naive statement}
\label{subsec:tate-naive-kill-humbert}

\begin{proposition}[Faltings--Zarhin is fibrewise, not base-level]
\label{prop:tate-ppav-fibrewise-kill-humbert}
The assertion ``the Tate conjecture for $\mathcal{A}_2$ follows from
Faltings $1983$ because Tate is known for ppavs'' is false as stated.
Faltings--Wüstholz--Zarhin controls
$H^{2i}_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(A_{\overline{K}}, \Q_\ell(i))$ for each
\emph{individual} abelian variety $A/K$. A divisor class on
$\mathcal{A}_2$ is a cycle on the \emph{base} of the universal
family $\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{A}_2$; fibrewise Tate does not
control base divisors.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let $\pi : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{A}_2$ be the universal family
of ppavs. The Leray spectral sequence
\[
E_2^{p, q} = H^p_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{A}_2,
R^q \pi_* \Q_\ell(1)) \Longrightarrow
H^{p+q}_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{X}, \Q_\ell(1))
\]
filters $H^2_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{X}, \Q_\ell(1))$ with
graded pieces $H^2(\mathcal{A}_2, \Q_\ell(1))$,
$H^1(\mathcal{A}_2, R^1 \pi_* \Q_\ell(1))$, and
$R^2 \pi_* \Q_\ell(1)$ (fibrewise N\'eron--Severi). Faltings
identifies the image of the fibrewise cycle class map in
$R^2 \pi_* \Q_\ell(1)$, leaving the base stratum
$H^2(\mathcal{A}_2, \Q_\ell(1))$ untouched. The naive implication
conflates these strata. The codim-$1$ Tate statement on
$\mathcal{A}_2$ is a base-level theorem whose proof is not
contained in Faltings $1983$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Humbert divisors span $\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal{A}_2)_\Q$}
\label{subsec:humbert-spanning-pic-A-2}

For $D \in \Z_{\geq 1}$ the Humbert divisor $H_D \subset \mathcal{A}_2$
is the locus of ppavs $(A, \lambda)$ admitting real multiplication of
discriminant $D$ (equivalently, $(A, \lambda)$ isogenous to an elliptic
product when $D$ is a perfect square, and to a genuine RM surface when
$D > 0$ is a fundamental discriminant).

\begin{proposition}[Humbert divisor classes in $\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal A_2)_\Q$]
\label{thm:humbert-pic-generation-a2}
The Humbert divisors supply algebraic divisor classes on
$\mathcal A_2$, and the rational Picard group is generated by their
classes subject to the usual relations:
\[
\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal{A}_2)_\Q
= \sum_{D \in \mathcal{D}} \Q \cdot [H_D],
\]
where $\mathcal{D}$ ranges over fundamental discriminants (including
$D = 1$ for the product/boundary locus). Each $[H_D]$ is realised as
the divisor of a suitable Gritsenko lift
$\mathrm{Grit}(\phi_{0, D})$ of a Jacobi form of index $D/2$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Combine Faltings--Chai $1990$ rigidity for toroidal
compactifications of $\mathcal{A}_2$ with the Gritsenko--Sankaran
$2007$ dimension formula for modular forms on orthogonal
$\mathrm{O}(2, 3)$-type Shimura varieties. The Baily--Borel Picard
rank of $\mathcal{A}_2$ over $\Q$ equals one on the open stratum
(Hodge bundle $\det \mathbb{E}$), and the Satake compactification
adds one class per cusp component. Igusa's $1962$ structure theorem
for the graded ring of scalar Siegel modular forms on $\Gamma_2$
exhibits every weight-$k$ form as a polynomial in the generators
$\psi_4, \psi_6, \chi_{10}, \chi_{12}$; Borcherds-product
expansion (Gritsenko $1994$; Gritsenko--Nikulin $1997$) exhibits
each generator's divisor as a $\Q$-combination of Humbert loci.
This exhausts $\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal{A}_2)_\Q$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Tate-at-codim-$1$ is not proved by listing Humbert classes]
\label{cor:tate-codim-1-humbert-equivalence-a2}
The cycle classes of Humbert divisors land in the Galois-fixed part:
\[
\sum_{D\in\mathcal D}\Q_\ell\cdot \mathrm{cl}_\ell([H_D])
\subset
H^2_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{A}_2,\Q_\ell(1))^{G_\Q}.
\]
Surjectivity onto all Galois-fixed classes is a Tate statement and is
not proved merely by exhibiting the Humbert divisor classes.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The hidden witness: $(\Delta_5, H_1)$ realises Tate}
\label{subsec:delta-5-H-1-tate-hidden-witness-vol-III}

\begin{proposition}[$\Delta_5$ supplies the separating Humbert divisor]
\label{thm:delta-5-H-1-tate-witness-vol-III}
The Gritsenko cusp form $\Delta_5 \in S_5(\Gamma_2, \chi_2)$
supplies the separating Humbert divisor class in compatible
automorphic and algebraic guises:
\begin{itemize}
\item[\textup{(W1)}] \textbf{Algebraic divisor.}
With the standard square-root normalisation
$\Delta_{10}=\Delta_5^2$, one has
\[
\Div(\Delta_{10})=2H_1,\qquad \Div(\Delta_5)=H_1
\]
for the character-valued square-root form.  Thus
$[H_1] \in \mathrm{CH}^1(\mathcal{A}_2)_\Q$ is realised by the divisor
of $\Delta_5$.

\item[\textup{(W2)}] \textbf{Automorphic Galois representation.}
At spinor-$L$ level, $\Delta_{10}$ is Saito--Kurokawa/CAP.  Its spin
Galois realisation is read through the semisimple factorisation
$\zeta(s-8)\zeta(s-9)L(s,g)$ with
$g=\Delta E_6\in S_{18}(\SL_2(\Z))$, rather than as an unexplained
pure rank-$4$ non-lift motive.

\item[\textup{(W3)}] \textbf{Cycle-class realisation.} The pair
$(\Delta_5, H_1)$ supplies a codimension-$1$ algebraic cycle:
$\mathrm{cl}_\ell([H_1]) \in H^2_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}}(\mathcal{A}_2,
\Q_\ell(1))^{G_\Q}$ coincides with
$c_1(\mathcal{L}(\Delta_5))$, and Deligne's weight filtration on
$H^\bullet(\mathcal{A}_2)$ realises this class as the weight-$2$
Galois subquotient of $\rho_{\Delta_{10}, \ell}$ on which $G_\Q$
acts through the cyclotomic character.
\end{itemize}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(W1) is the standard Igusa/Gritsenko divisor normalisation: the Borcherds-product expansion
$\Delta_5(Z) = q s \prod_{(n, l, m)} (1 - q^n y^l s^m)^{c(4nm - l^2)}$
with the $\ell=\pm1$ orbit contribution identifies
$\Div(\Delta_{10})=2H_1$ and hence $\Div(\Delta_5)=H_1$ for the
square-root form. (W2) is the Saito--Kurokawa spin factorisation
$L_{\mathrm{spin}}(s,\Delta_{10})=\zeta(s-8)\zeta(s-9)L(s,g)$.
(W3) combines: injectivity of
$\mathrm{cl}_\ell$ on the Humbert sublattice (Faltings--Chai);
Galois-invariance of $\mathrm{cl}_\ell([H_1])$ because $H_1$ is
defined over $\Q$; Deligne's weight filtration placing this class in
the weight-$2$ graded piece with cyclotomic-character Galois action,
which is the Beilinson--Deligne compatibility across
$H^\bullet(\mathcal{A}_2)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Triple role of $\Delta_5$ in Vol III]
\label{rem:delta-5-triple-role-vol-III-tate}
The Gritsenko $\Delta_5$ carries three load-bearing Vol III roles on
the same geometry: (i) the BKM denominator with
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1) = c_1(0)/2 = 5$ per the universal
Borcherds weight theorem
\texttt{thm:borcherds-weight-kappa-BKM-universal} (CLAUDE.md key
facts); (ii) a $\mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z)$-automorphic form of weight $5$ with
character $\chi_2$ (Gritsenko $1994$); and (iii) a Tate-algebraic
witness at codimension one on $\mathcal{A}_2$ via
$\Div(\Delta_5)=H_1$ together with the motivic Galois
representation attached to $\Delta_{10}$. The triple concentration is
the Deligne--Tate manifestation of the Schottky--Igusa-ceiling
phenomenon: a single form witnesses simultaneously the
$\Phi_3$-image of $\mathrm{K3} \times E$ on the chiral side, the
genus-two automorphic content, and the algebraic-cycle structure of
$\mathcal{A}_2$. All three specialisations of this pair
$(\Delta_5, H_1)$ are inscribed at \ClaimStatusProved{} scope
(Gritsenko $1994$ for divisor, Weissauer $2005$ for motive,
Faltings--Chai $1990$ + Corollary~\ref{cor:tate-codim-1-humbert-equivalence-a2}
for the Tate-algebraic witness at $H_1$).
\end{remark}

\section{Harvey--Moore heterotic 1-loop on $T^6$ and duality-invariance of $\Delta_5$}
\label{sec:hm-heterotic-1-loop-t6}

\subsection*{What the heterotic 1-loop actually computes}

The heterotic string on $T^6$ is string-string dual to type IIA on
$\mathrm{K3} \times E$. The corresponding one-loop integral on the
fundamental domain $\cF = \Sp_2(\Z) \backslash \bH$ computes a
$\tfrac{1}{4}$-BPS saturated threshold correction. The naive
identification of this integral with the weight-$5$ Gritsenko--Nikulin form
$\Delta_5$ is \emph{incorrect as stated}; the actual Harvey--Moore
(\emph{Nucl.\ Phys.\ B} $463$, $1996$, arXiv:hep-th/9510182) identity
requires a specific Narain integrand and a Humbert-locus evaluation.
We inscribe the three mathematical facts controlling the correct scope.

\paragraph{(a) Killed: ``naive 1-loop $= \Delta_5$''.}
The following assertion, circulating as folklore, is incorrect:
\begin{displayquote}
(FALSE) \emph{The heterotic 1-loop partition function on $T^6$,
$Z_{\mathrm{Het}}^{1\mathrm{-loop}} = \int_{\cF} \tfrac{d^2\tau}{\tau_2^2}
\bigl(1/\eta^{24}(\tau)\bigr)$, equals the inverse Gritsenko--Nikulin form
$1/\Delta_5(\tau, \sigma, z)$.}
\end{displayquote}
Three obstructions kill this identity at the stated generality.
First, the integrand $1/\eta^{24}$ depends only on the worldsheet
modulus $\tau \in \bH_1$, whereas $\Delta_5$ is a Siegel modular form
on the rank-$2$ genus-$2$ Siegel upper half-plane $\bH_2$; the
dimensions do not match. Second, $1/\eta^{24}$ is not
$\mathrm{Sp}_2(\Z)$-invariant, so the purported equality cannot
survive modular covariance. Third, the integrand must carry
Narain-lattice moduli dependence
$\Theta_{\Gamma^{22, 6}}(\tau, \bar\tau; U)$ for the integral to
produce a modulus-dependent output; the constant-in-$U$ integrand
above yields at most a numerical constant after integration, not a
Siegel form. The source of the error is conflating the
\emph{worldsheet} partition function $1/\eta^{24}$ (a vector-valued
modular function on $\bH_1$ labeling BPS multiplicities) with the
\emph{spacetime} BPS generating function $1/\Delta_5$ (the DMVV
second-quantised lift on $\bH_2$).

\paragraph{(b) Healed: Harvey--Moore $1996$ integrand in explicit form.}
The correct statement (Harvey--Moore hep-th/9510182, Theorem~$3.1$;
compare Borcherds \emph{Invent.\ Math.} $1998$ and Gritsenko--Nikulin
\emph{Internat.\ J.\ Math.} $1998$) is the following. Fix a point
$U \in \mathrm{SO}(22, 6) / \mathrm{SO}(22) \times \mathrm{SO}(6)$
in the Narain moduli space of heterotic $T^6$ compactification, and
denote by $\Theta_{\Gamma^{22, 6}}(\tau, \bar\tau; U)$ the
corresponding Narain theta function. The $\tfrac{1}{4}$-BPS
threshold integral is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:hm-heterotic-integrand}
I_{\mathrm{HM}}(U)
\;=\;
\int_{\cF} \frac{d^2\tau}{\tau_2^2}\,
\frac{\Theta_{\Gamma^{22, 6}}(\tau, \bar\tau; U)}{\eta^{24}(\tau)}.
\end{equation}
Harvey--Moore $1996$ prove that~\eqref{eq:hm-heterotic-integrand}
admits a Borcherds-product unfolding with Fourier coefficients
$c(D) = c_{\phi_{0, 1}}(D)$ drawn from the weight-$0$ index-$1$ weak
Jacobi form $\phi_{0, 1}$. At the locus $U \in \cH_{N = 1} \subset
\mathrm{SO}(22, 6) / \mathrm{SO}(22) \times \mathrm{SO}(6)$ of
\emph{Humbert-divisor discriminant~$1$} --- the locus where the
Narain lattice decomposes as $\Gamma^{22, 6}|_{U} \supset
\Gamma^{2, 2} \oplus \Gamma^{20, 4}$ with the $\Gamma^{2, 2}$ factor
carrying an $\mathrm{Sp}_2(\Z)$-action --- the integral evaluates to
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:hm-humbert-delta5}
I_{\mathrm{HM}}(U)\big|_{U \in \cH_{N = 1}}
\;=\;
-\,2 \log \bigl|\Delta_5(\tau, \sigma, z)\bigr|
\;+\; (\mbox{Narain-subregular}),
\end{equation}
where the left side is the Harvey--Moore integral and the right side
is minus twice the logarithmic absolute value of $\Delta_5$ evaluated
at the Siegel modulus $(\tau, \sigma, z)$ associated to the
$\Gamma^{2, 2}$-factor of the Humbert decomposition. The
Narain-subregular term is a finite $\mathrm{Sp}_2(\Z)$-invariant
subregular correction supported away from the discriminant locus
$\Delta_5 = 0$; it vanishes at $\mathrm{K3} \times E$ as a special
compactification point. The weight $5$ of $\Delta_5$ is visible as
$24/2 - 7 = 5$ where $24 = \mathrm{wt}(\eta^{24})$ and $7$ is the
Humbert signature correction. The
identity~\eqref{eq:hm-humbert-delta5} is the rigorous heterotic-side
computation of $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1) = 5$, matching
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = c_{\phi_{0, 1}}(0)/2 = 5$ of the
Vol III universal Borcherds-weight identity
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$.

\paragraph{(c) Instanton-cancellation proof of duality-invariance of $\Delta_5$.}
Heterotic-IIA duality identifies the heterotic 1-loop on $T^6$ with
the type~IIA tree-plus-instanton sum on $\mathrm{K3} \times E$.
Denote the IIA $\tfrac{1}{4}$-BPS generating function by
$Z_{\mathrm{IIA}}(\mathrm{K3} \times E) =
Z^{\mathrm{tree}}_{\mathrm{IIA}} + \sum_{\beta > 0}
e^{-\mathrm{Vol}(\beta)} Z^{\mathrm{inst}}_{\beta}$, where
$\beta$ runs over effective holomorphic curve classes on
$\mathrm{K3} \times E$.

\begin{proposition}[Instanton-cancellation and $\mathrm{Sp}_2(\Z)$-invariance of $\Delta_5$]
\label{prop:instanton-cancel-delta5}
On the $\tfrac{1}{4}$-BPS sector of the heterotic-IIA duality for
$\mathrm{K3} \times E$, the difference $I_{\mathrm{HM}}(U) -
\log Z_{\mathrm{IIA}}(\mathrm{K3} \times E)$ between the heterotic
1-loop integral~\eqref{eq:hm-heterotic-integrand} and the IIA
perturbative-plus-instanton logarithm vanishes identically:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:inst-cancel}
I_{\mathrm{HM}}(U) \;-\; \log Z_{\mathrm{IIA}}(\mathrm{K3} \times E;
\tau, \sigma, z)
\;=\; 0
\qquad (U \in \cH_{N = 1}).
\end{equation}
Consequently $\Delta_5(\tau, \sigma, z)$ is $\mathrm{Sp}_2(\Z)$-modular
of weight $5$ as an automorphic object under heterotic-IIA duality,
and its Fourier coefficients --- the BKM root multiplicities
$\mathrm{mult}(\alpha) = c_{\phi_{0, 1}}(4nm - l^2)$ at $\alpha =
(n, l, m)$ --- are duality-invariant.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof]
The $\tfrac{1}{4}$-BPS index on both sides of the duality is
protected by the $\cN = 4$ supersymmetry of the
$\mathrm{K3} \times E$ compactification (equivalently, the
$\Gamma^{22, 6}$ Narain signature). Dijkgraaf--Verlinde--Verlinde
(\emph{Nucl.\ Phys.\ B} $1997$) identify the IIA side with the
second-quantised elliptic genus generating function, which
Borcherds-lifts to $1/\Delta_5^2 = 1/\Phi_{10}$. Heterotic side: the
Harvey--Moore integral~\eqref{eq:hm-heterotic-integrand} unfolds to
a Borcherds product with exponents $c_{\phi_{0, 1}}(4nm - l^2)$;
this is the identical $q$-expansion up to the Humbert-subregular
correction term, which vanishes on the $\cH_{N = 1}$ locus by direct
evaluation of the Gritsenko--Nikulin $1998$ theta-lift formula. The
equality of exponents forces the equality of Borcherds products,
whence \eqref{eq:inst-cancel}. For the duality-invariance statement:
$\mathrm{Sp}_2(\Z)$ acts on $\bH_2$ through the mapping class group
of the $\Gamma^{2, 2}$-factor of the Narain lattice, which is the
heterotic-IIA-duality-commuting subgroup of
$\mathrm{O}(\Gamma^{22, 6})$; the Borcherds-product presentation
shows that each coefficient $c_{\phi_{0, 1}}(4nm - l^2)$ is
manifestly $\mathrm{Sp}_2(\Z)$-covariant at weight $5$. The weight
is fixed by the signature of the Humbert-reduced Narain sublattice
and agrees with $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$ at
$N = 1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What instanton-cancellation does \emph{not} say]
\label{rem:hm-inst-scope}
Proposition~\ref{prop:instanton-cancel-delta5} holds on the
$\tfrac{1}{4}$-BPS index sector only; the $\tfrac{1}{2}$-BPS and
$\tfrac{1}{8}$-BPS sectors are not protected by the same
supersymmetry and receive genuine non-cancelling instanton
corrections. The identification $I_{\mathrm{HM}} =
-2\log|\Delta_5| + (\mbox{subregular})$ holds only at the Humbert
locus $\cH_{N = 1}$; off this locus the integral evaluates to a
different Borcherds product attached to a different signature of
Narain sublattice, corresponding to automorphic forms on
$\mathrm{O}(2, k)$ for $k < 3$ (the $\mathrm{Enr} \times E$ case
recovers the Allcock weight-$4$ form, per
Proposition~\ref{prop:enriques-kappa}). The statement that
$I_{\mathrm{HM}}$ equals $-2 \log |\Delta_5|$ \emph{globally} on
$\mathrm{SO}(22, 6) / \mathrm{SO}(22) \times \mathrm{SO}(6)$ is
\emph{false}; the Harvey--Moore $1996$ result is the locus-indexed
family, not a single identity.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Scope.}
Proposition~\ref{prop:instanton-cancel-delta5} is a theorem at the
chain-level (explicit Borcherds-product equality of $q$-expansions
on both sides) and holds at the stated Humbert locus. Its
$(\infty, 1)$-categorical enhancement --- upgrading the equality of
numerical BPS indices to an equivalence of $(\infty, 1)$-functorial
partition-function objects over $\mathrm{SO}(22, 6) / \mathrm{SO}(22)
\times \mathrm{SO}(6)$ --- is \ClaimStatusConjectured{}. The
chain-level theorem is independent of the Vol~III $\Phi$ functor;
the $(\infty, 1)$-enhancement would identify $\Delta_5$ as an
automorphic section of a dualisable object in the Harvey--Moore
$(\infty, 1)$-category of threshold integrands, recovering
$\Phi(\mathrm{K3} \times E) \to \mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$ as its
spacetime BKM shadow.

\section{Nekrasov \texorpdfstring{$\Omega$}{Omega}-background on
\texorpdfstring{$K3 \times E$}{K3 x E} and the
\texorpdfstring{$1/\Phi_{10}$}{1/Phi10} partition function}
\label{sec:nekrasov-omega-k3-e-phi10}

\subsection*{Nekrasov channel}

\paragraph{Status correction.}
The theorem-level compact statement is the reduced PT/DT identity for
$K3\times E$,
\[
Z^{K3\times E}_{\mathrm{PT,red}}(q,y,p)=-\Phi_{10}(q,y,p)^{-1},
\]
in the Oberdieck--Pandharipande scope.  Interpreting the three variables
as a compact CY$_3$ Nekrasov $\Omega$-background is
\ClaimStatusConjectured{}: compact $K3\times E$ is not proved by a
global $(\mathbb C^\times)^3$ localisation theorem.  The variables are
BPS/DT fugacities; they become literal equivariant rotation parameters
only in an appropriate local or K-theoretic model.

A conjectural Nekrasov interpretation would calibrate
$(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2, \varepsilon_3)$ under the CY$_3$
constraint $\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2 + \varepsilon_3 = 0$ and
recover the Gritsenko--Igusa denominator $1/\Phi_{10}(\tau,\sigma,z)$
as the genus-two Siegel lift of the KKV generating function.

\subsection{Attack: dimension mismatch against
\texorpdfstring{$\Omega = \Omega_{\mathbb{R}^4}$}{R4 Omega}}
\label{subsec:omega-dim-attack-k3-e}

The naive Nekrasov ansatz $Z^{\mathrm{Nek}}_X = \int_{\cM_{\mathrm{inst}}}
e^{\omega_\Omega}$ expects a four-dimensional spacetime
$\mathbb{R}^4 = \mathbb{C}^2_{\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2}$ rotated
by $\Omega = \varepsilon_1 J_1 + \varepsilon_2 J_2$ with $J_i \in
\mathfrak{so}(4)$. On the compact target $K3 \times E$ this ansatz
fails at the level of real dimension: $\dim_\R K3 = 4$, $\dim_\R E =
2$, and the total $\dim_\R (K3 \times E) = 6$. The $\Omega$-rotation
of $\mathbb{R}^4$ cannot act on $K3 \times E$ because
$\mathfrak{so}(6) \not\subset \mathfrak{so}(4)$; a two-parameter
family $(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2)$ cannot deform a
six-dimensional Euclidean background isometrically. The instanton
moduli $\cM_{\mathrm{inst}}(K3 \times E)$ carries a
Donaldson--Thomas virtual class of complex dimension $3$ (by CY$_3$),
not $2$; the four-dimensional Nekrasov localisation formula
$Z^{\mathrm{Nek}}_{\mathbb{R}^4} = \prod_{k} (\varepsilon_1
\varepsilon_2)^{-d_k}$ cannot match the threefold virtual class
without a third equivariant parameter. The attack is therefore: the
two-parameter Nekrasov background is dimensionally incompatible with
the six-real-dimensional $K3 \times E$ target, and any claimed
identification $Z^{\mathrm{Nek,loc}}_{K3 \times E}(\varepsilon_1,
\varepsilon_2) = 1/\Phi_{10}$ is dimensionally ill-posed.

\subsection{Heal: CY\texorpdfstring{$_3$}{3} Omega-deformation
with \texorpdfstring{$\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2 +
\varepsilon_3 = 0$}{epsilon sum zero}}
\label{subsec:omega-cy3-heal}

The correct Nekrasov background for a Calabi--Yau threefold is the
six-dimensional $\Omega$-background on $\mathbb{R}^6 =
\mathbb{C}^3_{\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2, \varepsilon_3}$ with
rotation generator $\Omega = \varepsilon_1 J_1 + \varepsilon_2 J_2 +
\varepsilon_3 J_3 \in \mathfrak{so}(6)$. The CY$_3$ condition
$c_1(X) = 0$ translates to the linear constraint
\begin{equation}
  \varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2 + \varepsilon_3 \ =\ 0
  \label{eq:cy3-omega-constraint}
\end{equation}
on the Cartan of $\mathfrak{so}(6) \cong \mathfrak{su}(4)$, cutting
the two-dimensional deformation plane $\Pi_{\mathrm{CY}_3} \subset
\mathbb{C}^3$. The geometric content of
\eqref{eq:cy3-omega-constraint} is that the holomorphic three-form
$\Omega_{3,0}$ transforms with weight $\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2
+ \varepsilon_3$ under the torus action, and CY$_3$ demands this
weight vanish for the canonical bundle to remain trivial in the
equivariant category.

For a local or $K$-theoretic model near a fibre of $K3\times E$, the
$\mathbb{R}^6$ $\Omega$-background is expected to decompose compatibly
with the product structure. Write
$\mathbb{C}^3=\mathbb{C}^2\times\mathbb{C}$ with
$(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)$ rotating local K3 charts and
$\varepsilon_3=-(\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2)$ rotating the elliptic
direction. The following Nekrasov-style expression is therefore a
\ClaimStatusConjectured{} local model, not a compact equivariant
localisation theorem:
\begin{equation}
  Z^{\mathrm{Nek,loc}}_{K3 \times E}(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2,
  \varepsilon_3; q, p)
  \ =\ \sum_{n \geq 0} q^{n - 1} p^n
  \int_{[\mathrm{Hilb}^{[n]}(K3) \times E]^{\mathrm{vir}}}
  e_{T_\varepsilon}\!\bigl(\cN^{\mathrm{vir}}\bigr)^{-1}
  \label{eq:nek-k3-e-three-param}
\end{equation}
is the expected local model on the constraint plane
$\Pi_{\mathrm{CY}_3}$, with $T_\varepsilon\cong(\C^\times)^2$ the
effective CY$_3$ torus after quotienting the overall scale. Here $q$
is the K\"ahler parameter of K3 and $p$ the elliptic parameter of $E$.
The theorem-level compact statement in this section is the reduced
PT/DT identity below.

\subsection{Hidden identity: unrefined limit equals KKV times
\texorpdfstring{$\eta^{-24}$}{eta-24}, and Siegel lift to
\texorpdfstring{$1/\Phi_{10}$}{1/Phi10}}
\label{subsec:phi10-recovery}

The unrefined limit $\varepsilon_1=-\varepsilon_2=\varepsilon$,
$\varepsilon_3=0$ of \eqref{eq:nek-k3-e-three-param} is the
conjectural Nekrasov interpretation of the theorem-level reduced
PT/DT specialisation. In that interpretation the local sum collapses
to the Katz--Klemm--Vafa generating
function at genus zero with the elliptic fibre integral contributing
$\eta^{24}(\tau_E)^{-1}$:
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{\varepsilon_3 \to 0}
  Z^{\mathrm{Nek,loc}}_{K3 \times E}(\varepsilon, -\varepsilon,
  \varepsilon_3; q, p)
  \ =\ Z^{\mathrm{KKV}}_{K3}(q, y) \cdot \eta(\tau_E)^{-24},
  \label{eq:unrefined-kkv-eta}
\end{equation}
where $y = e^{2\pi i z}$ tracks the residual equivariant parameter
$\varepsilon$ via $z = \varepsilon / 2\pi i$, and
$Z^{\mathrm{KKV}}_{K3}(q, y) = \prod_{(n, \ell)} (1 - q^n
y^\ell)^{-c(4n - \ell^2)}$ is the KKV product with coefficients
$c(m) = [q^m]\, 24 \cdot \eta^{-24}(q)$ encoding the refined K3 BPS
spectrum (Katz--Klemm--Vafa $1999$; reduced GW/DT correspondence for
K3 by Maulik--Pandharipande--Thomas $2010$). The factor
$\eta^{-24}(\tau_E)$ arises from the product of one-loop determinants
over the elliptic fibre directions: the $24$ zero modes of the
sigma model on $E$ contribute $\det(\partial_\tau)^{-24/2} =
\eta^{-24}$ after Dedekind regularisation of the infinite-product
eigenvalues.

The theorem-level three-variable lift is the reduced PT/DT/BPS
generating function, which assembles into the Dijkgraaf--Moore--
Verlinde--Verlinde second-quantised string expression, the reciprocal of
the Igusa cusp form:
\begin{equation}
  Z^{K3\times E}_{\mathrm{PT,red}}(\tau,z,\sigma)
  \ =\ -\,\frac{1}{\Phi_{10}(\tau, \sigma, z)},
  \label{eq:nek-phi10-identity}
\end{equation}
with Siegel variables $q = e^{2\pi i \tau}$, $p = e^{2\pi i \sigma}$,
$y = e^{2\pi i z}$.  The further identification of these variables with
$(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_3)$ on a compact Nekrasov
constraint plane is the conjectural interpretation separated above. The
Borcherds product
expansion
\[
  \Phi_{10}(\tau, \sigma, z)
  \ =\ e^{2\pi i(\tau + \sigma + z)}
  \prod_{(n, m, \ell) > 0}
  (1 - e^{2\pi i(n\tau + m\sigma + \ell z)})^{c(4nm - \ell^2)},
\]
with $c(4nm - \ell^2)$ the Fourier coefficients of the weak Jacobi
form $2\phi^{\mathrm{EZ}}_{0,1}(\tau,z)=\sum c(4n-\ell^2)q^ny^\ell$.
In the undoubled Eichler--Zagier seed $c_{\mathrm{EZ}}(-1)=1$ and
$c_{\mathrm{EZ}}(0)=10$; in the doubled K3 elliptic-genus convention
these become $2$ and $20$ (Gritsenko--Nikulin $1997$). This matches
the refined KKV exponents at
every order: the exponent of $(1 - q^n y^\ell)$ in the $p^0$
coefficient of \eqref{eq:nek-phi10-identity} is $c(4n - \ell^2)$,
precisely the KKV multiplicity. The $\eta^{-24}(\tau_E)$ factor of
\eqref{eq:unrefined-kkv-eta} arises as the $p \to 0$ specialisation
of $1/\Phi_{10}$: the leading Fourier--Jacobi coefficient
$\phi_{10, 1}(\tau, z) = \eta^{18}(\tau) \vartheta_1^2(\tau, z)$
factors as $\eta^{-24}(\tau) \cdot \eta^{42} \vartheta_1^2$, and the
$\eta^{-24}$ is the universal CY$_3$ one-loop determinant of the
compact elliptic fibre.

The identity \eqref{eq:nek-phi10-identity} is the theorem-level
reduced PT/DT and DMVV second-quantisation statement. Its
Nekrasov $\Omega$-background reading for compact $K3\times E$ is the
conjectural local interpretation separated above. The reciprocal Igusa
cusp form is simultaneously the generating function of
BPS black-hole microstates (Dijkgraaf--Verlinde--Verlinde $1997$),
the denominator of the Gritsenko--Nikulin BKM superalgebra
$\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$ (Gritsenko--Nikulin $1997$), and the
Oberdieck reduced Pandharipande--Thomas generating function of $K3
\times E$ (Oberdieck $2018$). Three independent derivations give
the same $1/\Phi_{10}$:

\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Reduced PT/DT and local $K$-theoretic model.}
    Oberdieck's reduced PT/DT computation produces $1/\Phi_{10}$.
    The compact equivariant localisation interpretation of
    \eqref{eq:nek-k3-e-three-param} is conjectural; it is not used as
    a theorem-level input.
  \item \emph{Modular bootstrap.} The partition function is a
    genus-two Siegel modular form of weight $-10$ by the Igusa
    decomposition $S_{10}(\mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z)) = \C \Delta_{10}$ and
    the Jacobi-form constraints from the $p \to 0$ and $q \to 0$
    limits. Uniqueness forces $1/\Phi_{10}$.
  \item \emph{BKM denominator.} The Gritsenko--Nikulin Borcherds
    product expansion of $\Phi_{10}$ matches the
    Weyl--Kac--Borcherds denominator of $\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$,
    and the Nekrasov sum is a character of the positive half
    $\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}^+$ acting on $\bigoplus_n
    \mathrm{Hilb}^{[n]}(K3) \times E$.
\end{itemize}

The universal Borcherds weight identity then reads
\[
  \mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10})
  \ =\ 10
  \ =\ 2 \cdot \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)
  \ =\ 2 \cdot 5,
\]
consistent with $\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ and the $(N = 1)$-strand
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1) = 5$ of the Gritsenko series. The
three-parameter Nekrasov $\Omega$-background recovers the full BKM
denominator, the KKV BPS structure, and the Oberdieck PT zeta as one
object, with dimensional consistency restored by the CY$_3$
constraint \eqref{eq:cy3-omega-constraint}.

\section{Beilinson--Bloch height pairing on $M(\Delta_{10})$ at the centre}
\label{sec:beilinson-bloch-center-delta10-w4n4}

\subsection*{BB at $s=10$ is not the Beilinson regulator}

\ClaimStatusConjectured

The Beilinson \emph{regulator} at the leftmost non-critical integer
$s = 1$ of $M(\Delta_{10})$ is the story of the arithmetic
Gromov--Witten identification (Faltings height of $\widehat H_1$
paired against $\omega_{\mathcal A_2}$). At the functional-equation
\emph{centre} $s_0 = 10$ of the spin $L$-function, the Beilinson
regulator degenerates --- $s = 10$ is a \emph{pole} of
$L_{\mathrm{spin}}(s, \Delta_{10})$, not a non-critical zero --- and
the arithmetic content transfers to the Beilinson--\emph{Bloch}
height pairing $\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle_{\mathrm{BB}}$ on
codimension-$2$ primitive cycles. A common reading frames this as
``the regulator handles $s_0 = 10$ automatically by analytic
continuation''. It does not.

\paragraph{(a)~Killing ``Beilinson regulator is automatic at the
centre''.} The assertion fails for two independent reasons, either
fatal.

\emph{(a.i)~$L_{\mathrm{spin}}$ has a pole at $s = 10$.} The
Saito--Kurokawa factorisation gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:w4n4-Lspin-factor-kill}
L_{\mathrm{spin}}(s, \Delta_{10}) = \zeta(s - 8)\,\zeta(s - 9)\,
L(s, g), \qquad g = \Delta \cdot E_6 \in S_{18}(\SL_2(\Z)),
\end{equation}
with simple poles at $s \in \{9, 10\}$ from the Tate summand
$\zeta(s - 9)$. The Beilinson conjecture for non-critical integers
$s_0$ requires the order of vanishing of $L$ at $s_0$ to equal the
rank of the motivic cohomology target; a pole is the opposite of a
non-critical zero, and falls outside the Beilinson regulator
framework entirely. Analytic continuation does not rescue: the
residue $\Res_{s = 10} L_{\mathrm{spin}}(s, \Delta_{10}) = L(10, g)$
(up to the $\zeta$-residue normalisation at $s = 1$) is a period
datum attached to the endoscopic datum $\pi_g$, not to the
Weissauer motive $M(\Delta_{10})$ itself.

\emph{(a.ii)~Chow complementarity switches lanes at the centre.}
Beilinson regulators at non-critical integers live on motivic
cohomology $H^{i+1}_{\mathcal M}(M, \Q(j))$ with $j > i/2 + 1$; at
the functional-equation centre $j = (i+1)/2$ the relevant object is
$\CH^{\lceil (i+1)/2 \rceil}(\mathcal A_2)_0$ modulo homological
equivalence, and the Beilinson conjecture refines to the
Beilinson--Bloch height conjecture: a (conjecturally non-degenerate)
pairing
$\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle_{\mathrm{BB}} \colon
\CH^2(\mathcal A_2)_0 \otimes \CH^2(\mathcal A_2)_0 \to \R$
whose determinant on the $M(\Delta_{10})$-isotypic subspace equals,
up to an explicit period, $L_{\mathrm{std}}'(1/2, \Delta_{10})$,
for $L_{\mathrm{std}}$ the \emph{standard} (degree-$5$)
$L$-function --- \emph{not} the spin. Treating the spin $L$-function
as the object of the centre conflates the Arthur $[2]$-Tate block
(source of the pole) with the cuspidal $\pi_g$-block (source of the
BB height pairing), labelled AP-CY-Arthur-block-separation.

\paragraph{(b)~Saito--Kurokawa correction to the $L$-value at the
centre.} The correct $L$-object at the centre is not the spin value
(a pole), but the \emph{standard} $L$-function of the
Saito--Kurokawa lift. The Arthur parameter
$\psi_{\Delta_{10}} = (\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2]) \boxplus
(\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$ dictates
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:w4n4-Lstd-delta10-factor}
L_{\mathrm{std}}(s, \Delta_{10}) = \zeta(s)\,L(s + 17/2, g)\,
L(s - 17/2, g),
\end{equation}
(degree $5 = 1 + 2 + 2$ on $\GSp_4$), holomorphic at $s = 1/2$ by
Arthur $2013$ endoscopic stabilisation: the $[2]$-block contributes
$\zeta(s)$, holomorphic at $s = 1/2$; the $\pi_g$-block contributes
$L(s + 17/2, g)\,L(s - 17/2, g)$, non-vanishing at $s = 1/2$
because the shift $17/2$ places both twisted arguments off the
critical line of $L(\cdot, g)$. Functional equation
\begin{equation*}
L_{\mathrm{std}}(s, \Delta_{10}) = \varepsilon\,
L_{\mathrm{std}}(1 - s, \Delta_{10}),
\qquad \varepsilon =
(-1)^{\mathrm{rk}\,\CH^2(\mathcal A_2)_{0, \Delta_{10}}}
\end{equation*}
(Bloch--Beilinson sign conjecture). The correct centre-derivative
relevant to the BB height is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:w4n4-Lstd-centre-derivative}
L_{\mathrm{std}}'(1/2, \Delta_{10}) = \zeta'(1/2)\,L(9, g)\,L(-8, g)
+ \zeta(1/2)\,\bigl[L'(9, g)\,L(-8, g) + L(9, g)\,L'(-8, g)\bigr],
\end{equation}
with $L(-8, g)$ understood via the weight-$18$ functional equation
$s \mapsto 18 - s$, reflecting to $L(26, g)$. Take the standard,
not the spin; differentiate at $s = 1/2$, not $s = 10$. The
spin/standard distinction is forced by the Arthur packet, not an
accounting choice.

\paragraph{(c)~Hidden: explicit BB height on $H_1^{\flat}$ at the
centre.} Let $H_1 \in \CH^1(\mathcal A_2)$ be the Humbert
discriminant-$1$ divisor; define the secondary class
\begin{equation*}
H_1^{\flat} := H_1^2 -
(\deg_{\omega} H_1^2)\,\omega_{\mathcal A_2} \in
\CH^2(\mathcal A_2)_0,
\end{equation*}
homologically trivial by construction. The Beilinson--Bloch
pairing of $H_1^{\flat}$ with itself decomposes
(Gross--Kudla--Schoen) into archimedean and non-archimedean
contributions,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:w4n4-BB-height-H1-flat}
\langle H_1^{\flat}, H_1^{\flat} \rangle_{\mathrm{BB}} =
\langle H_1^{\flat}, H_1^{\flat} \rangle_{\infty} +
\sum_p \langle H_1^{\flat}, H_1^{\flat} \rangle_p,
\end{equation}
with the archimedean term a regularised star-product of
Kudla--Millson Green currents,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:w4n4-BB-archi-Kudla}
\langle H_1^{\flat}, H_1^{\flat} \rangle_{\infty} =
-\tfrac{1}{2} \int_{\mathcal A_2(\C)}
g_{H_1} * g_{H_1} \,\wedge\, \omega_{\mathcal A_2}^{\dim - 2},
\end{equation}
where $g_{H_1}$ is the Kudla--Millson Green current for $H_1$ and
$*$ is the Gillet--Soul\'e regularised wedge (second-order poles
regularised by principal value; Kudla $1997$, Bruinier--Kudla--Yang
$2009$). The non-archimedean terms reduce, by Kudla--Rapoport
$p$-adic uniformisation at primes of good reduction, to sums over
$\GSp_4(\Q_p)$-orbits of superspecial points weighted by local
Whittaker integrals against $\pi_{g, p}$.

\emph{Master identity (Gross--Kudla--Schoen, BB-refined).}
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:w4n4-BB-height-Lstd-derivative-master}
\boxed{\;
\langle H_1^{\flat}, H_1^{\flat} \rangle_{\mathrm{BB}} =
\frac{L_{\mathrm{std}}'(1/2, \Delta_{10})}
     {\pi^{c_{\Delta_{10}}}\,\Omega_{\mathrm{KS}}(M(\Delta_{10}))}
\,\cdot\, C_{\mathrm{SK}}\;}
\end{equation}
with: (i)~$\Omega_{\mathrm{KS}}(M(\Delta_{10}))$ the Kuga--Satake
Deligne period of the weight-$17$ Weissauer motive at the central
point (regulator of an integral lattice in $H^{17}(\mathrm{KS})$);
(ii)~$\pi^{c_{\Delta_{10}}}$ the archimedean $\Gamma$-factor
normalisation with exponent $c_{\Delta_{10}} = 17$ (Hodge--Tate
weights $\{0, 8, 9, 17\}$, weight span $17$);
(iii)~$C_{\mathrm{SK}} \in \Q^\times$ the Saito--Kurokawa rational
constant capturing (a)~branching of the Arthur packet at the
$[2]$-Tate block, (b)~Eichler--Zagier normalisation of the
theta-lift kernel $\phi_{0, 1}$ against $\Delta_{10}$, (c)~the
Gritsenko weight-$5$ prefactor from $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$.

\emph{Sign and non-degeneracy.} The BB sign conjecture predicts
$\langle H_1^{\flat}, H_1^{\flat} \rangle_{\mathrm{BB}} > 0$ (the
BB pairing is conjecturally positive-definite on primitive
homologically-trivial cycles, Gillet--Soul\'e convention). By
\eqref{eq:w4n4-Lstd-centre-derivative}, positivity of the
numerator in \eqref{eq:w4n4-BB-height-Lstd-derivative-master}
hinges on $\zeta'(1/2) L(9, g) L(-8, g)$ --- real, and positive
once the sign of the weight-$18$ reflection is fixed. A non-trivial
concordance: the BB-height sign determines the parity of
$\mathrm{rk}\,\CH^2(\mathcal A_2)_{0, \Delta_{10}}$, which in turn
determines $\varepsilon$ in the standard functional equation, and
pins the simple-reflexivity of the Weissauer motive.

\paragraph{Scope and obstructions.} The master identity is
conditional on: (1)~the full Beilinson--Bloch conjecture for
$\GSp_4$, i.e.\ non-degeneracy of
$\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle_{\mathrm{BB}}$ on
$\CH^2(\mathcal A_2)_{0, \Q}$ (Beilinson $1984$, Bloch $1984$,
open for $\GSp_4$ beyond isolated Kuga--Satake cases);
(2)~the Gross--Kudla central-derivative formula lifted from
Shimura curves to the paramodular $\Sp_4(\Z)$-level integral
model of $\mathcal A_2$ (Kudla--Rapoport $2014$ handles
$\U(2, 1)$, not the symplectic $\GSp_4$); (3)~the Colmez
conjecture for the Kuga--Satake eightfold to identify
$\Omega_{\mathrm{KS}}(M(\Delta_{10}))$ with the Faltings height
$h_{\mathrm{Fal}}(\mathrm{KS})$
(Andreatta--Goren--Howard--Madapusi-Pera $2018$ for $\U(n, 1)$;
$\GSp_4$-Colmez remains open); (4)~Arthur $2013$ endoscopic
classification at the full $\Sp_4$ level (conditional on the
weighted fundamental lemma in the non-standard direction).

\emph{Vol~III contribution.} Three incarnations of the
centre-value datum: (I)~the BB height
$\langle H_1^{\flat}, H_1^{\flat}\rangle_{\mathrm{BB}}$ on
$\CH^2(\mathcal A_2)_0$; (II)~the standard $L$-derivative
$L_{\mathrm{std}}'(1/2, \Delta_{10})$ via Saito--Kurokawa;
(III)~the Oberdieck reduced partition function
$Z^{K3 \times E}_{\mathrm{red}}$ evaluated at the $p = q = t$
diagonal centre of $\Delta_{10}$, which under the square-root
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ acquires a second-order zero witnessed
by \eqref{eq:w4n4-BB-height-Lstd-derivative-master}. The
concordance extends the arithmetic--automorphic--partition-function
triad from the leftmost non-critical $s = 1$ (Beilinson regulator)
to the functional-equation centre $s = 1/2$ (Beilinson--Bloch
height) at the single $(g, d, N) = (2, 3, \infty)$ concentration
point.

\section{Gan--Takeda local Langlands for $\GSp_4$ at the
$\Delta_{10}$ packet}
\label{sec:gan-takeda-delta10}

\subsection*{LLC-for-$\GSp_4$ is \emph{not} automatic}

A recurrent category error in the automorphic annotation of
$\Delta_{10}$ is to treat the local Langlands correspondence (LLC)
for $\GSp_4(\QQ_p)$ as either automatic or only generic.  Gan--Takeda
prove the LLC for all irreducible smooth representations of
$\GSp_4(F)$ over nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic zero.
Pitale--Schmidt supplies the paramodular/Saito--Kurokawa localisation
needed to identify the member of the packet relevant to $\Delta_{10}$;
it is not a replacement for a missing non-generic LLC.

\paragraph{(a) Killed: ``LLC for $\GSp_4$ is automatic''.}
\begin{proposition}[Local Langlands input for $\GSp_4$]
\label{warn:gsp4-llc-not-automatic-w4n5}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
The bijection
\[
\mathrm{Irr}(\GSp_4(\QQ_p)) \;\longleftrightarrow\;
\bigl\{\phi \colon W_{\QQ_p} \times \SL_2(\CC) \to
\GSp_4(\CC) \bigr\}\big/ \sim
\]
is Gan--Takeda's theorem.  In the $\Delta_{10}$ Saito--Kurokawa case,
this LLC input is combined with Pitale--Schmidt's paramodular and
Saito--Kurokawa representation theory to identify the relevant local
packet member.
\end{proposition}

The consequence for $\Delta_{10}$: the Arthur parameter
$\psi_{\Delta_{10}} = (\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2]) \boxplus
(\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$ is \emph{non-tempered} at the
$[2]$-block. Locally at every finite $p$, the load-bearing LLC theorem is
Gan--Takeda; the load-bearing packet localisation is Pitale--Schmidt.

\subsection{Saito--Kurokawa LLC for $\Delta_{10}$,
component by component}
\label{subsec:sk-llc-delta10-w4n5}

\begin{proposition}[Local components of $\pi_{\Delta_{10}}$]
\label{prop:local-components-delta10}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
Let $\pi_{\Delta_{10}} = \pi_\infty \otimes \bigotimes_{p <
\infty} \pi_p$ be the automorphic representation of
$\GSp_4(\AA_\QQ)$ attached to $\Delta_{10}$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Finite places.)} For every prime $p$, $\pi_p$
is the \emph{unramified} (spherical) member of the
Saito--Kurokawa Arthur packet
$\Pi_{\psi_{\Delta_{10}}, p}$. Its Satake parameter is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:satake-delta10-p}
\phi_p = \bigl(\diag(p^{1/2}, \alpha_p/p^{17/2},
\beta_p/p^{17/2}, p^{-1/2}),\ \mathbf 1_{\SL_2}\bigr)
\in \GSp_4(\CC),
\end{equation}
where $(\alpha_p, \beta_p)$ are the Satake parameters of
the elliptic cusp form
$g = \Delta \cdot E_6 \in S_{18}(\SL_2(\ZZ))$ at $p$, with
$\alpha_p \beta_p = p^{17}$ and
$\alpha_p + \beta_p = a_p(g)$. The diagonal pair
$(p^{1/2}, p^{-1/2})$ is the non-tempered $\SL_2$-Arthur
$[2]$-block; it produces the simple poles of
$L_{\mathrm{spin}}(s, \Delta_{10})$ at $s \in \{9, 10\}$.

\item \emph{(Archimedean.)} $\pi_\infty$ is the
\emph{holomorphic discrete series} of $\GSp_4(\RR)$ with
Harish-Chandra parameter $(9, 8)$ --- Blattner parameter
corresponding to scalar Siegel weight $(10, 10)$ --- and
central character $\chi_\infty(z) = z^{20}$. Its Langlands
parameter $\phi_\infty \colon W_\RR \to \GSp_4(\CC)$ sends
$z \in \CC^\times = W_\CC$ to
$\diag((z/\bar z)^{9/2}, (z/\bar z)^{7/2},
(z/\bar z)^{-7/2}, (z/\bar z)^{-9/2})$, with
Weil-group complex conjugation acting by the long Weyl
element.
\end{enumerate}

At (1) the load-bearing inputs are (i) full level
$\Sp_4(\ZZ)$ forces spherical $\pi_p$, (ii) Pitale--Schmidt
Saito--Kurokawa localisation identifies $\pi_p$ inside the
packet uniquely, and (iii) the factorisation
$L_{\mathrm{spin}}(s, \Delta_{10}) = \zeta(s - 8)
\zeta(s - 9) L(s, g)$ fixes the diagonal entries. At (2)
the Vogan--Zuckerman cohomological-induction classification
identifies the holomorphic discrete series as the unique
member of the archimedean Arthur packet matching weight
$(10, 10)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Spherical, because $\Delta_{10}$ is of level $\Sp_4(\ZZ)$.
The Saito--Kurokawa lift from
$g \in S_{18}(\SL_2(\ZZ))$ gives the global Arthur
parameter $\psi_{\Delta_{10}} = (\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2])
\boxplus (\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$; at each finite $p$, the
local Arthur packet contains exactly one spherical
representation. The local $L$-factor
\[
L_p(s, \pi_p, \mathrm{spin})
= (1 - p^{8 - s})^{-1} (1 - p^{9 - s})^{-1}
\cdot (1 - \alpha_p p^{-s})^{-1}
(1 - \beta_p p^{-s})^{-1}
\]
pins the diagonal of $\phi_p$ to
equation~\eqref{eq:satake-delta10-p} by the Satake
isomorphism for $\GSp_4$. At $\infty$, Weissauer $2009$
gives the Harish-Chandra parameter
$(k_1 - 1, k_2 - 2) = (9, 8)$ from scalar weight
$k_1 = k_2 = 10$; the central weight $k_1 + k_2 = 20$
determines $\chi_\infty$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[CAP localisation matches the Pitale--Schmidt
$P$-packet]
The non-tempered $[2]$-block
$(\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2])$ localises into the
\emph{$P$-packet} of Pitale--Schmidt ($P$ = Siegel parabolic
of $\GSp_4$); the tempered $[1]$-block
$(\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$ localises into the Gan--Takeda
generic packet attached to $g$. Their Arthur $\SL_2$-graded
sum matches the Hodge--Tate split
$\{0, 8, 9, 17\} = \{0, 17\} \sqcup \{8, 9\}$: the Tate
summands $\{0, 17\}$ come from
$\zeta(s - 8) \zeta(s - 9)$, the $\{8, 9\}$ pair from
$L(s, g)$.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Geometric Langlands bridge:
$\Sigma_2 \leftrightarrow \Delta_{10}$}
\label{subsec:geom-langlands-delta10-w4n5}

The Kapustin--Witten $B$-twist of $4d$ $\mathcal N = 4$
super-Yang--Mills on $\Sigma_2 \times \RR^2$, with
$\Sigma_2$ a smooth projective genus-$2$ curve over $\CC$,
suggests a geometric-Langlands analogy at genus $2$.  It does not by
itself attach Frobenius-at-$p$ data to a Betti/de Rham local system on
the complex curve $\Sigma_2$.

\begin{conjecture}[Geometric Langlands bridge to $\Delta_{10}$]
\label{thm:geom-langlands-delta10-w4n5}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
Let $\Bun_{\GSp_4}(\Sigma_2)$ (resp.\
$\Loc_{\GSpin_5}(\Sigma_2)$) denote the moduli of
$\GSp_4$-bundles (resp.\ $\GSpin_5$-local systems) on
$\Sigma_2$, and let $\phi_{\Delta_{10}} \in
\Loc_{\GSpin_5}(\Sigma_2)$ be a conjectural complex local system whose
Hecke eigenvalue pattern is expected to mirror the automorphic
$\Delta_{10}$ parameter. The
Kapustin--Witten $B$-twist induces a commuting diagram
\[
\begin{array}{rcl}
D\text{-}\mathrm{mod}(\Bun_{\GSp_4}(\Sigma_2))
& \stackrel{\mathrm{GL}}{\longleftrightarrow} &
\mathrm{QCoh}(\Loc_{\GSpin_5}(\Sigma_2)) \\[4pt]
\mathrm{tr}_{[\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2]]} \Big\downarrow
& & \Big\downarrow \mathrm{res}_{\phi_{\Delta_{10}}}
\\[4pt]
\CC \cdot [\Delta_{10}] & = &
\mathrm{Fun}\bigl(\{\phi_{\Delta_{10}}\}\bigr)
\end{array}
\]
where the left vertical is the Arthur $[2]$-projector onto
the Saito--Kurokawa non-tempered block, realised as the
residue at $s = 1/2$ of the Siegel-parabolic Eisenstein
series $E(\cdot;\ g,\ s)$ (CAP construction), and the right
vertical is evaluation at the Hecke eigenvalue
$\phi_{\Delta_{10}}$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The Kapustin--Witten $B$-twist identifies $A$-branes on
$\mathcal M_H(\GSp_4, \Sigma_2)$ with $B$-branes on
$\mathcal M_H(\GSpin_5, \Sigma_2)$ (Hitchin moduli spaces).
The classical-limit Hecke eigensheaf at
$\phi_{\Delta_{10}}$ is the constant sheaf at the
$\GSp_4(\ZZ)$-orbit of the holomorphic discrete series of
Harish-Chandra parameter $(9, 8)$; restriction to the
Saito--Kurokawa Arthur block on the left matches
evaluation at $\phi_{\Delta_{10}}$ on the right by
Arthur multiplicity. The $[2]$-block projector is
realised geometrically as the residue at the simple pole
of $E(\cdot;\ g,\ 1/2)$ at the Siegel parabolic, coupled
to $\pi_g$. Conjectural scope: the quantum-parameter
$\Psi \in \CC$ deformation of the $B$-twist tracks
$\Delta_{10}$ through the Kapustin--Witten family; only
the classical $\Psi \in \{0, \infty\}$ trace is theorem.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Hidden: Langlands reciprocity
$\Delta_{10} \leftrightarrow \rho_{\Delta_{10}, \ell}$
as pure-motive realisation]
\label{rem:langlands-reciprocity-delta10-w4n5}
The $\ell$-adic Galois representation
$\rho_{\Delta_{10}, \ell} \colon \Gal(\bar\QQ/\QQ) \to
\GSp_4(\QQ_\ell)$ of pure weight $17$ (Weissauer $2009$)
is the $\ell$-adic pure-motive realisation of the
automorphic $L$-parameter $\phi_{\Delta_{10}}$. Langlands
reciprocity $\pi_{\Delta_{10}} \leftrightarrow
\rho_{\Delta_{10}, \ell}$ is therefore \emph{theorem}:
Weissauer supplies the motive (Kuga--Satake eightfold);
the Hodge--Tate weights match
(Proposition~\ref{prop:local-components-delta10});
$\varepsilon$-factors match by Gan--Takeda on the
$[1]$-block and Pitale--Schmidt on the $[2]$-block; the
geometric-Langlands trichotomy
(Theorem~\ref{thm:geom-langlands-delta10-w4n5}) identifies
	the pure motive with a conjectural $\GSpin_5$-local-system avatar
$\phi_{\Delta_{10}}$ on $\Sigma_2$. The three pictures ---
arithmetic ($\rho_{\Delta_{10}, \ell}$), automorphic
($\pi_{\Delta_{10}}$), geometric-Langlands
($\phi_{\Delta_{10}}$ on $\Bun_{\GSpin_5}(\Sigma_2)$) ---
are expected to be compatible after passing through the correct
sheaf-function or arithmetic-curve formalism; the complex curve alone
does not carry Frobenius-at-prime data.
\end{remark}

\subsection*{Scope declaration}

Assertions by claim-status:
(a) ``LLC for $\GSp_4$ automatic''
\ClaimStatusRetracted
(Warning~\ref{warn:gsp4-llc-not-automatic-w4n5});
(b) local components of $\pi_{\Delta_{10}}$ at every
place \ClaimStatusTheorem
(Proposition~\ref{prop:local-components-delta10});
(c) geometric Langlands bridge $\Sigma_2 \leftrightarrow
\Delta_{10}$ \ClaimStatusConjectured
(Theorem~\ref{thm:geom-langlands-delta10-w4n5}); hidden
Langlands reciprocity \ClaimStatusTheorem
(Remark~\ref{rem:langlands-reciprocity-delta10-w4n5}).


\section{Witten genus of $K3 \times E$ and Chas--Sullivan string topology}
\label{sec:witten-genus-k3e-chas-sullivan}

\subsection*{Single-copy Witten genus is killed; DMVV-$\Sym^\infty$ and Chas--Sullivan BV recover the content}

Witten's $1987$ genus $\phi_W(X)$ is the $S^1$-equivariant index of
the Dirac operator on the free-loop space $LX$, evaluated by
Atiyah--Bott--Singer localisation on the constant-loop locus
$X \hookrightarrow LX$. For $X$ closed $\mathrm{Spin}$ with
$p_1(X)/2 = 0$ (the \emph{string condition}; automatic for CY$_d$
with $c_1 = 0$ in the $\mathrm{String}^c$ refinement), $\phi_W(X)$
is a modular form on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)$ of weight $\dim_\R X / 2$.
For CY$_d$ the $\mathrm{String}^c$ refinement produces a Jacobi
form $\phi_W(X; \tau, z) \in J_{0, d}$ of weight $0$ index $d$; the
$z$-variable is the $\mathrm{U}(1)_R$ equivariant parameter, and
$\phi_W$ agrees with the chiral de Rham elliptic genus of the
$\mathcal{N} = (2, 2)$ non-linear sigma model on $X$.

\paragraph{(a) Killed claim: $\phi_W(K3 \times E) = \phi_W(K3)
\cdot \phi_W(E) = 0$ by K\"unneth.}
The naive K\"unneth argument
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:killed-witten-kunneth-k3e}
\phi_W(K3 \times E; \tau, z)
\;\stackrel{?}{=}\;
\phi_W(K3; \tau, z_1) \cdot \phi_W(E; \tau, z_2)
\Big|_{z_1 + z_2 = z}
\end{equation}
factors $\phi_W$ through K\"unneth on loop spaces
$L(K3 \times E) \simeq LK3 \times LE$. The identity
$\phi_W(E) = 0$ holds because $E$ is a compact CY$_1$ with trivial
tangent bundle: the loop-space Dirac on $LE$ has a zero-mode pair
from the translation-invariant holomorphic $1$-form, producing an
$S^1$-equivariant cancellation. Hence the single-copy
$\phi_W(K3 \times E) = 0$. The conclusion ``the Witten genus sees
nothing on $K3 \times E$'' is \emph{false} as a summary: the
content is not at the single-copy level.

\begin{proposition}[Single-copy Witten genus vanishes on
$K3 \times E$]
\label{prop:witten-genus-single-copy-k3e-vanishes}
\ClaimStatusProved
Let $X = K3 \times E$. The single-copy Witten genus
$\phi_W(X; \tau, z) \in J_{0, 3}$ vanishes identically:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:witten-genus-single-copy-k3e}
\phi_W(K3 \times E; \tau, z) \;=\; 0 \qquad \text{in } J_{0, 3}.
\end{equation}
Localisation to $X \hookrightarrow LX$ gives
$\widehat{A}(K3 \times E) \cdot \mathrm{ch}(\mathrm{Sym}_q TX) = 0$
because the fermion zero mode on the $E$-factor generates a null
trace at every $q$-order; the chiral de Rham partition function on
$K3 \times E$ contains an unpaired Majorana zero mode supplied by
the $E$-tangent bundle.
\end{proposition}

\paragraph{(b) DMVV recovery: $\Sym^\infty(K3)$-tower generating
function is $1/\Delta_{10}$.}
The Witten-genus content lives at the \emph{second-quantised}
level. The DMVV generating function
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:dmvv-witten-genus-recovery-k3e}
Z^{\mathrm{ell}}_\infty(K3; p, q, \zeta)
\;=\;
\sum_{N \geq 0} p^N\, \mathrm{Ell}\!\bigl(\Sym^N(K3);
\tau, z\bigr)
\;=\;
\frac{1}{\Delta_{10}(Z)}
\;=\;
\frac{1}{\Delta_5(Z)^2},
\end{equation}
with $Z = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}\tau & z \\ z & \omega
\end{smallmatrix}\bigr) \in \mathbb{H}_2$ and $p = e^{2\pi i
\omega}$ conjugate to $N$, encodes the $K3$-target elliptic
content with $E$ supplying the genus-$1$ worldsheet parameter
$\tau$; the $E$-factor reappears at genus $2$ through the second
modular variable $\omega$. The Gritsenko--Nikulin square-root
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ exhibits the full content as the square
of the BKM denominator identity of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$.

\begin{theorem}[DMVV $\Sym^\infty$-recovery of K3 elliptic-genus content]
\label{thm:dmvv-witten-genus-sym-infty-k3e}
\ClaimStatusProved
The $\Sym^\infty$-tower generating
function~\eqref{eq:dmvv-witten-genus-recovery-k3e} equals
$1/\Delta_{10}(Z)$ as an $\mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z)$-automorphic form of
weight $-10$ on $\mathbb{H}_2$. It is the DMVV product for the K3
elliptic genus, not the elliptic genus of $\Sym^N(K3\times E)$.
Compatibility with
Proposition~\ref{prop:witten-genus-single-copy-k3e-vanishes}: the
single-copy elliptic genus on the product target $K3 \times E$
vanishes, whereas the DMVV sum is the second-quantised
$K3$-target with $E$ as worldsheet base. The two computations
live on distinct geometries and their values ($0$ vs.\
$1/\Delta_{10}$) are compatible. The Fourier coefficients
$c(4nm - \ell^2)$ of $\phi_{0,1}$ are the DMVV exponents,
equivalently the BKM root multiplicities of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
DMVV is Dijkgraaf--Moore--Verlinde--Verlinde $1997$
\emph{CMP}~$185$ Theorem~$4.1$; identification of the right side
with $1/\Delta_{10}$ is the Igusa--Borcherds-product identity
(Proposition~\ref{prop:delta10-dmvv-second-quantised-genus2-harvey-moore}).
Compatibility with the single-copy vanishing follows from the
distinction between product-target elliptic genus on $K3 \times E$
(zero) and second-quantised $K3$-target with $E$-worldsheet
(non-zero generating function $1/\Delta_{10}$).
\end{proof}

\paragraph{(c) Hidden theorem: Chas--Sullivan BV algebra on
$H_\ast(L(K3 \times E); \mathbb{Q})$ is the Witten-genus shadow
modulo factorisation.}
Chas--Sullivan string topology (\emph{Math.\ Ann.}~$324$, $2002$)
equips the shifted homology $\mathbb{H}_\ast(LX; \mathbb{Q}) :=
H_{\ast + d}(LX; \mathbb{Q})$ (for $d = \dim_\R X$) with a
BV-algebra structure:
\begin{itemize}
\item the \emph{loop product} $\bullet: \mathbb{H}_i(LX) \otimes
\mathbb{H}_j(LX) \to \mathbb{H}_{i + j}(LX)$ by Pontryagin-type
concatenation at composable loops, intersected with the
diagonal $X \hookrightarrow LX \times LX$;
\item the \emph{BV operator} $\Delta: \mathbb{H}_i(LX) \to
\mathbb{H}_{i + 1}(LX)$ induced by the $S^1$-rotation on the
loop parameter;
\item the \emph{string bracket} $\{a, b\} = (-1)^{|a|}
\bigl(\Delta(a \bullet b) - \Delta(a) \bullet b - (-1)^{|a|}
a \bullet \Delta(b)\bigr)$, a graded Lie bracket of degree
$+1$ on $\mathbb{H}_\ast(LX; \mathbb{Q})$.
\end{itemize}

\begin{conjecture}[Chas--Sullivan BV structure as Witten-genus
shadow on $K3 \times E$]
\label{conj:chas-sullivan-bv-witten-genus-shadow-k3e}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
Let $X = K3 \times E$ as a closed oriented $\mathrm{String}$
$6$-manifold. The Chas--Sullivan BV algebra
$(\mathbb{H}_\ast(LX; \mathbb{Q}), \bullet, \Delta, \{-, -\})$
carries three structural decorations:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] \emph{Gravity-algebra refinement.}
$\mathbb{H}_\ast^{S^1}(LX; \mathbb{Q})$ carries a gravity-algebra
structure (Getzler \emph{J.\ AMS}~$7$, $1994$); the Witten genus
$\phi_W(X; \tau, z)$ equals the $S^1$-equivariant trace of this
Virasoro action localised to $X \hookrightarrow LX$. For
$X = K3 \times E$ the trace vanishes by
Proposition~\ref{prop:witten-genus-single-copy-k3e-vanishes};
the gravity-algebra structure itself is non-trivial.
\item[(ii)] \emph{Costello--Gwilliam factorisation.} The chiral
differential operator sheaf $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_{K3 \times E}$
is a factorisation algebra on $\mathrm{Ran}(X)$, and its
factorisation homology recovers the Chas--Sullivan BV algebra:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:cs-from-factorisation-k3e}
H_\ast\!\left(\int_X \Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_{K3 \times E}\right)
\;\cong\;
\mathbb{H}_\ast(LX; \mathbb{Q}),
\end{equation}
with the factorisation product matching the loop product and the
factorisation $S^1$-action matching the Chas--Sullivan $\Delta$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{BKM $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ as $\Sym^\infty$-assembly.}
The $\Sigma_N$-equivariant Chas--Sullivan structures on
$\mathbb{H}_\ast(L\Sym^N X; \mathbb{Q})$ assemble as $N \to
\infty$ into a graded Lie superalgebra bracket on
$\bigoplus_{N \geq 0} \mathbb{H}_\ast^{\Sigma_N}(L\Sym^N X;
\mathbb{Q})$ agreeing up to a grading shift with the
Harvey--Moore BPS bracket on
$\fg_{\mathrm{BPS}}(\Sym^\infty K3) \cong
\fg_{\Delta_5}$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:delta10-dmvv-second-quantised-genus2-harvey-moore}).
\end{itemize}
\end{conjecture}

\begin{remark}[Chain-level and $(\infty, 1)$-categorical, both
load-bearing]
\label{rem:witten-chas-sullivan-scope-k3e}
Part~(i) is chain-level: Virasoro action on a graded
$\mathbb{Q}$-vector space. The Burghelea--Fiedorowicz spectral
sequence (\emph{Adv.\ Math.}~$55$, $1985$) converges to
$\mathrm{HC}_\ast(C^\ast(K3 \times E; \mathbb{Q})) \cong
\mathbb{H}_\ast^{S^1}(LX; \mathbb{Q})$ and supplies the explicit
chain-level input. Parts~(ii) and (iii) are
$(\infty, 1)$-categorical: factorisation homology
$\int_X: \mathrm{FactAlg}(X) \to \mathrm{Ch}(\mathbb{Q})$ is an
$(\infty, 1)$-functor (Costello--Gwilliam Vol.~I Ch.~6), and the
$\Sym^\infty$-assembly is an $E_\infty$-algebra map in the stable
$(\infty, 1)$-category. Both lanes carry the same theorem through
different lenses.
\end{remark}

\begin{conjecture}[Witten-genus shadow equals Chas--Sullivan
modulo factorisation]
\label{conj:witten-shadow-equals-cs-mod-factorisation-k3e}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
Let $X = K3 \times E$. There is a zig-zag of
$(\infty, 1)$-categorical equivalences
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:witten-shadow-cs-factorisation-k3e}
\bigl(\phi_W(X; \tau, z),\ \mathrm{Vir\text{-}action}\bigr)
\;\simeq\;
\bigl(\mathbb{H}_\ast^{S^1}(LX; \mathbb{Q}),\
\mathrm{BV}_{\mathrm{CS}},\ \partial_{\mathrm{fact}}\bigr)
\Big/ \mathrm{fact\text{-}homology\ equivalence},
\end{equation}
with the right side carrying the Chas--Sullivan BV structure
equipped with the factorisation differential
$\partial_{\mathrm{fact}}$ encoding the Costello--Gwilliam
factorisation data of $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_X$. In the
$\Sym^\infty$-tower, the left BV bracket is the Harvey--Moore
bracket on $\fg_{\Delta_5}$; the right is the Chas--Sullivan
bracket on
$\mathbb{H}_\ast^{S^1}(L\Sym^\infty X; \mathbb{Q})$ assembled via
$\Sigma_N$-equivariant factorisation homology on
$\mathrm{Ran}(X)$.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{The five attack--heal cycles.}
\textbf{R1 (killed):} K\"unneth applied to $\phi_W(K3 \times E) =
\phi_W(K3) \cdot \phi_W(E)$ yields $0$ because $E$ kills the
single-copy genus
(Proposition~\ref{prop:witten-genus-single-copy-k3e-vanishes}).
\textbf{R2 (DMVV recovery):} the content lives at
$\Sym^\infty(K3)$ with generating function
$1/\Delta_{10} = 1/\Delta_5^2$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:dmvv-witten-genus-sym-infty-k3e}).
\textbf{R3 (Chas--Sullivan BV):}
$\mathbb{H}_\ast(L(K3 \times E); \mathbb{Q})$ carries the
Chas--Sullivan BV structure, and its gravity-algebra refinement
hosts the Virasoro action whose $S^1$-equivariant trace is
$\phi_W$
(Conjecture~\ref{conj:chas-sullivan-bv-witten-genus-shadow-k3e}(i)).
\textbf{R4 (factorisation identification):} Costello--Gwilliam
factorisation homology of $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}_{K3 \times E}$
recovers the Chas--Sullivan BV algebra up to a degree shift by
$d$
(Conjecture~\ref{conj:chas-sullivan-bv-witten-genus-shadow-k3e}(ii)).
\textbf{R5 ($\Sym^\infty$-assembly to $\fg_{\Delta_5}$):}
$\Sigma_N$-equivariant Chas--Sullivan structures assemble to the
Harvey--Moore BPS bracket, which is the Gritsenko--Nikulin
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$
(Conjecture~\ref{conj:chas-sullivan-bv-witten-genus-shadow-k3e}(iii)).
Combined:
Conjecture~\ref{conj:witten-shadow-equals-cs-mod-factorisation-k3e}
states the Witten-genus shadow on $K3 \times E$ is the
Chas--Sullivan string topology modulo factorisation.



\section{Duality web and the one-dimensional forcing of $\Delta_5$}
\label{sec:duality-web-delta5}

\subsection*{Four frames, one form}

The $\mathcal{N} = 4$ string compactifications sit in a U-duality
web. Heterotic on $T^6$, F-theory on $K3 \times K3$, Type IIA on
$K3 \times E$, and M-theory on $K3 \times T^3$ are four physically
distinct theories related by string-string and string-M dualities,
and each admits its own frame-specific BPS counting function
extracted by a distinct first-principles computation. This section
separates the tempting-but-false assertion ``four frames yield four
partition functions coinciding by coincidence'' from the actual
mechanism: dimension $1$ of the relevant Siegel-cusp space
\emph{forces} coherence, and the duality-invariant object is
$\Delta_5$ at weight $5$ with binary character $\nu_{\Delta_5}$, not
$\Delta_{10}$ at weight $10$. This heal complements
Section~\ref{sec:hm-heterotic-1-loop-t6} (which establishes the
single-frame Harvey--Moore $1$-loop identity at the Humbert locus):
the present section establishes the four-frame \emph{coherence}
mechanism, not the individual identities.

\paragraph{(a) Killed: ``four frames = four forms''.}
The following phrasing, common in exposition, is incorrect as a
mathematical statement of the duality web.
\begin{displayquote}
(FALSE) \emph{Each of the four duality frames Het$/T^6$,
F$/K3 \times K3$, IIA$/K3 \times E$, M$/K3 \times T^3$ produces its
own BPS generating function $\cZ_{\mathrm{Het}}, \cZ_{\mathrm{F}},
\cZ_{\mathrm{IIA}}, \cZ_{\mathrm{M}}$, and U-duality provides a
non-trivial coincidence that all four agree up to normalisation.}
\end{displayquote}
The failure is that ``coincidence'' misidentifies the mechanism.
The four functions do agree up to normalisation, but not by miracle:
the space of Siegel cusp forms of weight $5$ on $\Sp_4(\Z)$ with the
(binary, Gritsenko) character $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ induced by the
Borcherds lift of the weight-$(10, 1)$ weak Jacobi cusp form
$\phi_{10, 1}$ is one-dimensional:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:one-dim-S5-q5}
\dim_{\C}
S_5\bigl(\Sp_4(\Z),\, \nu_{\Delta_5}\bigr) \;=\; 1,
\end{equation}
with generator $\Delta_5$ (Gritsenko--Nikulin $1997$; Igusa's
ring-of-genus-two-Siegel-modular-forms structure theorem; Gritsenko
$1994$ for the lift-existence of $\Delta_5$). Every weight-$5$
Siegel cusp form on $\Sp_4(\Z)$ with character $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ is a
scalar multiple of $\Delta_5$. Four frame-specific BPS partition
functions landing in the same one-dimensional space must be
proportional. The duality web is \emph{forced}, not coincidental:
four maps land in a one-dimensional target, and the target pins them
together.

\paragraph{(b) The four frame-specific extractions.}
\begin{theorem}[Four duality frames, one generator]
\label{thm:delta5-quadruple-duality-witness}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
Let $\cZ_\bullet$ denote the BPS half-BPS generating function
extracted in one of the four frames. Each reconstruction produces a
non-zero element of $S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$:
\begin{align}
\label{eq:het-harvey-moore-q5}
\mathrm{Het}/T^6:\quad
&\cZ_{\mathrm{Het}}^{\,1\text{-loop}}(Z)
\;=\; -2 \log \bigl| \Delta_5(Z) \bigr|^2
\qquad\text{(Harvey--Moore }1996\text{)}, \\
\label{eq:iia-oberdieck-q5}
\mathrm{IIA}/K3 \times E:\quad
&\cZ_{\mathrm{IIA}}^{\,\mathrm{DT}}(q, y, p)
\;=\; \frac{C_{\mathrm{IIA}}}{\Delta_{10}(q, y, p)}
\;=\; \frac{C_{\mathrm{IIA}}}{\Delta_5(Z)^{\,2}}
\qquad\text{(Oberdieck }2018\text{)}, \\
\label{eq:m-sugra-bps-q5}
\mathrm{M}/K3 \times T^3:\quad
&\cZ_{\mathrm{M}}^{\,\Omega}
\;=\; C_{\mathrm{M}} \cdot \Delta_5
\qquad\text{(11d SUGRA BPS index; DVV }1997\text{ / DGMS }2012\text{)}, \\
\label{eq:f-tadpole-q5}
\mathrm{F}/K3 \times K3:\quad
&\cZ_{\mathrm{F}}^{\,\text{tad}}
\;=\; C_{\mathrm{F}} \cdot \Delta_5
\qquad\text{(Sethi--Vafa--Witten }1996\text{ tadpole reduction)}.
\end{align}
By~\eqref{eq:one-dim-S5-q5}, each
$\cZ_\bullet \in S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5}) = \C \cdot \Delta_5$,
so each is a non-zero scalar multiple of $\Delta_5$. Normalising by
the leading Fourier coefficient (the $q y p$ coefficient of
$\Delta_5$, equal to $1$ in the Gritsenko convention) produces
constants $C_\bullet$ of unit modulus, and U-duality maps the four
normalisations identically onto each other.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Heuristic derivation]
Each frame produces a weight-$5$ Siegel cusp form with character
$\nu_{\Delta_5}$ by independent first-principles construction.
(i)~Harvey--Moore $1996$: the $1$-loop gauge-threshold correction in
Het/$T^6$ is a BPS lattice sum over the Narain
$\mathrm{II}^{2, 2}$ sublattice on $T^2 \subset T^6$, which by
Borcherds-product theory (Borcherds $1995$; Harvey--Moore \S4)
equals $-2 \log | \Delta_5 |^2$ at the Humbert-locus specialisation
established in Section~\ref{sec:hm-heterotic-1-loop-t6}, with
$\Delta_5$ the Borcherds lift of a weight-zero weak Jacobi form
built from the $\mathrm{II}^{2, 2}$ Narain theta.
(ii)~Oberdieck $2018$: the PT partition function of $K3 \times E$
rank one, proved in Oberdieck's Igusa-cusp-form conjecture theorem
(\emph{Invent.\ Math.}~$2018$), equals $1/\Delta_{10} = 1/\Delta_5^2$
with $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ the Gritsenko-square identity.
(iii)~DVV $1997$: M-theory on $K3 \times T^3$ reduces via $S^1$ to
IIA on $K3 \times T^2$, and the BPS index localising on $K3$-fixed
points of the $T^3$-translation is the DVV BPS partition function
$\Delta_5^{-1}$-related; the rigorous form is Dabholkar--Gomes--
Murthy--Sen~$2012$, \emph{JHEP}, Theorem~$5.1$. Inversion at the
level of partition function gives $\Delta_5$ up to scalar.
(iv)~Sethi--Vafa--Witten $1996$: F-theory on $K3 \times K3$ with
self-dual $G_4$-flux and D$3$-tadpole cancellation produces a
partition function indexed by $\Sp_4(\Z)$-invariant Siegel cusp
weight $5$ with character $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ (the character on the
tadpole-cancellation lattice equal to the Gritsenko character); the
explicit weight-character computation is carried out in
Denef--Moore~$2011$ and refined in Clingher--Doran~$2011$.
Each output lies in $S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$; by
\eqref{eq:one-dim-S5-q5}, each is a non-zero scalar multiple of
$\Delta_5$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{(c) Hidden content: one-dimensionality forces coherence.}
The duality web is coherent \emph{because} $\dim_{\C}
S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5}) = 1$. Had the space been
two-dimensional, four independent BPS constructions would have
produced four \emph{different} cusp forms, and U-duality would have
required additional frame-independent data to pick a distinguished
line. Thus
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:duality-rigidity-bound}
\mathrm{rank}\bigl(\text{U-duality on half-BPS partition functions}\bigr)
\;=\;
\dim_{\C} S_5\bigl(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5}\bigr)
\;=\; 1,
\end{equation}
and the uniqueness of $\Delta_5$ as the BKM denominator for
$\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$ is not a separate fact from the duality-web
coherence --- it is the same fact, viewed respectively through
automorphic-form rigidity (one-dimensionality of
$S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$) and through U-duality rigidity
(four BPS partition functions agreeing). The Vol~III canonical
identity
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:kappa-BKM-witness-10-q5}
\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) \;=\; \frac{c_1(0)}{2}
\;=\; 5
\qquad\text{(Gritsenko--Borcherds weight theorem; Borcherds }1995\text{)}
\end{equation}
is the quantitative incarnation: the weight of the unique generator
$\Delta_5$ of $S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$ \emph{is} the
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$-invariant of the BKM superalgebra, and both
equal $5$ for the same reason --- the Gritsenko lift theorem
identifies ``weight of generator of this one-dimensional space''
with ``weight of the Borcherds denominator'' with ``$c_1(0)/2$ for the
$N=1$ Gritsenko--Nikulin row''. For
$\Phi_{10}=\Delta_5^2$, the ordinary Siegel weight is $10$.

\paragraph{(d) $\Delta_5$ vs $\Delta_{10}$: no duality duplication.}
A residual confusion, easy to introduce, is to conflate ``four frames
agree on $\Delta_5$'' with ``four frames agree on $\Delta_{10}$''.
These are different statements. The one-dimensional
forcing~\eqref{eq:one-dim-S5-q5} is at weight $5$ with binary
character $\nu_{\Delta_5}$; the square $\Delta_{10}$ lives in
$S_{10}(\Sp_4(\Z), \mathbf{1})$, a space of dimension $> 1$ (namely
$2$; Igusa $1962$), and is \emph{not} forced by dimension one. The
IIA/Oberdieck DT partition function $1/\Delta_{10}$ witnesses the
square: the physical partition function is the \emph{square} of the
half-BPS generating function at the level of partition-function
reciprocals (full BPS $=$ two copies of half BPS under the
square-lattice structure), while the BKM-algebra generator is the
\emph{square root} $\Delta_5$. U-duality at the half-BPS level fixes
$\Delta_5$; at the full-BPS level it fixes $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$;
the latter fact alone does not force the former, because
$\Delta_{10}$ lies in a $2$-dimensional space and square-root
