extraction from $\Delta_{10}$ is not unique. The one-dimensional
space $S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5}) = \C \cdot \Delta_5$ is the
duality-invariant of the web; $\Delta_{10}$ is its physical-frame
image at the level of full-BPS partition-function counting.

\paragraph{(e) Scope and three open edges.}
Three items remain open. First, F-theory on $K3 \times K3$
in~\eqref{eq:f-tadpole-q5} is established at the level of the BPS
index by Sethi--Vafa--Witten $1996$, and the identification with
$\Delta_5$ requires the Donagi--Grassi--Witten $1996$
F-theory-heterotic duality fibre-by-fibre, which is rigorously proven
only on the attractor locus; away from the attractor locus, what we
actually prove is $\cZ_{\mathrm{F}}^{\,\text{tad}} \in
S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$, so by~\eqref{eq:one-dim-S5-q5} it is
a scalar multiple of $\Delta_5$, but the specific scalar
$C_{\mathrm{F}} \in U(1)$ is identified physically only at the
attractor locus. Second, the M-theory/$K3 \times T^3$
frame~\eqref{eq:m-sugra-bps-q5} uses the Dabholkar--Gomes--
Murthy--Sen $2012$ form of the $11$-d SUGRA BPS index; the full
non-perturbative $11$-d computation without the Dijkgraaf--Verlinde
--Verlinde $1997$ ansatz is open. Third, the four
$\kappa_\bullet$-values on $K3 \times E$, namely
$\{\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}=0,
\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}=3,
\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=5,\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}=24\}$, correspond to
\emph{four distinct
constructions} (K\"unneth on total space $\chi(\cO_{K3 \times E})
= 0$; Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation $3$, while the compact Hodge
supertrace is $\Xi(K3\times E)=0$; Gritsenko--Borcherds weight
$c_1(0)/2=5$; Mukai lattice rank
$\mathrm{rk}\, \widetilde{\Lambda}_{K3} = 24$). The dimension-one
rigidity~\eqref{eq:one-dim-S5-q5} at weight $5$ applies to and
controls \emph{only} the $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ construction; the
other three have their own rigidity statements (K\"unneth
multiplicativity, Hodge symmetry, Mukai-lattice uniqueness) which
are independent. The duality-web argument of this section does not
collapse four constructions into one; it forces coherence within the
single $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ lane.


\subsection*{Dim-$1$ alone does not force, character-matching plus non-vanishing is the theorem}
\label{subsec:dim1-alone-does-not-force}

The paragraphs above (a)--(e) state that $\dim_{\C} S_5(\Sp_4(\Z),
\nu_{\Delta_5}) = 1$ forces the four duality frames into the same
line $\C \cdot \Delta_5$. Read carelessly, that slogan elides two
lemmas entirely separate from the linear-algebraic
one-dimensionality statement, whose proofs constitute the
\emph{physical} content of the duality web. The correct
decomposition follows.

\paragraph{(a) Killed: ``$\dim = 1$ alone forces all four frames to
agree''.} The following reading is false.
\begin{displayquote}
(FALSE) \emph{Because $\dim_{\C} S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5}) = 1$,
any automorphic function produced by any of the four duality frames
$\{\mathrm{Het}/T^6, \mathrm{F}/K3 \times K3, \mathrm{IIA}/K3 \times E,
\mathrm{M}/K3 \times T^3\}$ must equal $\Delta_5$ up to scalar. The
linear-algebraic dimension count is a theorem of
Gritsenko--Nikulin~$1997$, and that is the end of the forcing
argument.}
\end{displayquote}
Two obstructions, each fatal.

\emph{Obstruction $1$ (character-matching).} The cited
one-dimensionality statement applies to weight-$5$ Siegel cusp forms
on $\Sp_4(\Z)$ \emph{with the specific binary Maa{\ss} multiplier
$\nu_{\Delta_5}$}. The order-$2$ character $\nu_{\Delta_5}$
(Gritsenko's sign multiplier) differs from the trivial character
$\mathbf{1}$ on $\Sp_4(\Z)$, and both are available targets for a
weight-$5$ Siegel form. A frame-specific BPS construction on
$\Sp_4(\Z)$ need not, a priori, land on the
$\nu_{\Delta_5}$-eigenline; it may equally produce a weight-$5$ form
with trivial character or, more subtly, a form with a different
order-$2$ character differing from $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ by the sign
character of $\Sp_4(\Z)$. For any such alternative,
\[
S_5\bigl(\Sp_4(\Z),\, \mathrm{sgn}\bigr),
\qquad
S_5\bigl(\Sp_4(\Z),\, \mathbf{1}\bigr)
\]
are \emph{separate} $\C$-vector spaces, and lying in one of them
does not force proportionality to $\Delta_5$.

\emph{Obstruction $2$ (non-vanishing).} Even on the
$\nu_{\Delta_5}$-eigenspace, landing in a one-dimensional line does
not force a match: the zero vector also lies in that line. A
frame-specific construction producing the zero Siegel form is a
weight-$5$ $\nu_{\Delta_5}$-form, and it is a scalar multiple of
$\Delta_5$ (the scalar being $0$); nothing is said about matching
any other non-zero frame-specific construction. Linear-algebra
forcing proves coincidence up to scalar, vacuous when the scalar
can be zero. The physical claim is that the four scalars are all
non-zero; this is a separate theorem from $\dim = 1$.

\paragraph{(b) Corrected: dim-$1$ $+$ character-matching $+$
non-vanishing.} The correct forcing theorem decomposes into three
logically independent inputs.

\begin{theorem}[Forced coherence of the four duality frames on
$\Delta_5$ requires three ingredients]
\label{thm:delta5-forcing-three-ingredients}
\ClaimStatusTheorem\
For $\star \in \{\mathrm{Het}/T^6,\, \mathrm{F}/K3 \times K3,\,
\mathrm{IIA}/K3 \times E,\, \mathrm{M}/K3 \times T^3\}$, let
$\cZ_\star(Z) \in \mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{hol}}(\bH_2)$ denote the
weight-$5$ half-BPS generating function extracted from frame $\star$
by first-principles lattice-sum and Borcherds-lift construction.
The identification $\cZ_\star = C_\star \cdot \Delta_5$ with
$C_\star \in \C^\times$ holds \emph{iff} all three of the following
hold for each $\star$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(I)] \emph{Dimension:}
$\dim_{\C} S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5}) = 1$
(Gritsenko--Nikulin $1997$; linear-algebraic).
\item[(II)] \emph{Character-matching:}
$\cZ_\star \in S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$,
i.e.\ $\cZ_\star$ transforms under $\Sp_4(\Z)$ with precisely the
Maa{\ss} multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ and not with $\mathbf{1}$, with
$\mathrm{sgn}$, or with any other element of
$\Hom(\Sp_4(\Z), \C^\times)$.
\item[(III)] \emph{Non-vanishing:} $\cZ_\star \neq 0$ as a function
on $\bH_2$.
\end{enumerate}
Each of $(I), (II), (III)$ is necessary; none follows from either
of the others. Omitting any one leaves the four frames free to
disagree.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\emph{Necessity of $(I)$.} If $\dim S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})
\geq 2$, four frame-specific constructions can produce four linearly
independent weight-$5$ $\nu_{\Delta_5}$-forms, and coherence becomes
a separate coincidence rather than a forced identity.

\emph{Necessity of $(II)$.} A weight-$5$ Siegel cusp form with
character $\chi \neq \nu_{\Delta_5}$ lives in a disjoint $\C$-vector
space; there is no non-zero scalar making it equal to $\Delta_5$.
Non-matching character means no forcing, even if the non-matching
space happened to be one-dimensional.

\emph{Necessity of $(III)$.} The zero vector lies in every character
eigenspace. If $\cZ_\star = 0$, then $\cZ_\star = 0 \cdot \Delta_5$
vacuously, but gives no relationship to any other non-zero
$\cZ_{\star'}$.

\emph{Sufficiency (all three).} Under $(I), (II), (III)$: by $(II)$,
each $\cZ_\star \in S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5}) = \C \cdot
\Delta_5$ (using $(I)$). Hence $\cZ_\star = C_\star \Delta_5$ for
some $C_\star \in \C$. By $(III)$, $C_\star \neq 0$. Each frame
lands on a non-zero scalar multiple of the same generator
$\Delta_5$, and U-duality of the underlying physical theories
identifies the four non-zero scalars $\{C_\mathrm{Het},
C_\mathrm{F}, C_\mathrm{IIA}, C_\mathrm{M}\}$ up to the BPS
normalisation fixed by the leading Fourier coefficient.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{(c) Hidden: $(II)$ is the non-trivial step;
Harvey--Moore $1/4$-BPS cancellation is its proof.} The three
ingredients are not equally hard.

$(I)$ is a $1997$ linear-algebra fact in Gritsenko--Nikulin, provable
by explicit Fourier-expansion matching against the Igusa ring
structure: the $\nu_{\Delta_5}$-isotypic piece of
$M_*(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$ at weight $5$ is spanned by
$\Delta_5$ alone.

$(III)$ is elementary for each frame: the leading Fourier
coefficient of each $\cZ_\star$ is computed directly from the
BPS-counting lattice sum. For instance $\cZ_{\mathrm{Het}}$ has
non-zero $(qyp)^2$-coefficient $c_{10}(1)/2$ by the Borcherds-weight
identity, witnessing $\cZ_{\mathrm{Het}} \neq 0$.

$(II)$ is the non-trivial step. Each frame produces some weight-$5$
automorphic function on $\Sp_4(\Z)$; the question is which character
of $\Sp_4(\Z)$ the function carries. The \emph{Harvey--Moore
$1/4$-BPS cancellation} (Harvey--Moore \emph{Nucl.\ Phys.\
B}~$463$~[1996] $315$, \S$4$--$5$; refined in Harvey--Moore
\emph{Commun.\ Math.\ Phys.}~$197$~[1998] $489$) is the physical
argument that fixes $(II)$: cancellations between $1/2$-BPS and
$1/4$-BPS contributions in the Heterotic $1$-loop integral conspire
to leave precisely the $\nu_{\Delta_5}$-transformation behaviour and
not a $\mathbf{1}$- or $\mathrm{sgn}$-behaviour. The character
$\nu_{\Delta_5}$ is determined on each $\gamma \in \Sp_4(\Z)$ as a
quadratic refinement of the intersection form on $H^1(T^4; \Z/2)$
induced by $\gamma$ via its action on the Heterotic $\Gamma^{2, 2}$
lattice. That $\nu_{\Delta_5}$-transformation emerges from the
Heterotic $1/4$-BPS lattice sum is the content of Harvey--Moore's
cancellation theorem; without it, one would write down a weight-$5$
Siegel form with \emph{some} character, and dim-$1$ on the
$\nu_{\Delta_5}$-space would provide no constraint.

The analogous character-matching for the other three frames requires
separate proofs:
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{IIA/$K3 \times E$:} The Oberdieck--Pixton $2016$
Igusa-cusp theorem identifies the DT generating function with
$1/\Delta_{10} = 1/\Delta_5^2$; character-matching at weight~$5$ is
inherited via square-root on the $\nu_{\Delta_5}$-eigenspace.

\item \emph{M-theory/$K3 \times T^3$:} Character-matching is
inherited from the IIA frame via the $S^1$-reduction of M-theory to
IIA, an isomorphism of automorphic outputs at the level of
characters.

\item \emph{F-theory/$K3 \times K3$:} Character-matching requires
the Sethi--Vafa--Witten tadpole lattice to carry precisely the
$\nu_{\Delta_5}$ quadratic refinement, verified in
Denef--Moore~$2011$ by explicit Heegner-divisor theta-lift
computation on the $\O(2, 18)$-moduli space.
\end{itemize}
Each of these is a physical cancellation theorem at the character
level, logically independent of one-dimensionality.

\paragraph{(d) Could a frame produce zero?} In principle, yes. If
the Heterotic lattice sum at the Humbert locus were organised so
that $1/2$-BPS and $1/4$-BPS contributions cancelled \emph{completely}
(not just into a Maa{\ss}-character eigenspace), the Heterotic frame
would produce the zero form, which lies in every character eigenspace
and gives no constraint. That this does \emph{not} happen is
Harvey--Moore's non-vanishing statement: the subleading Fourier
coefficient is non-zero (equal to $c_{10}(1)/2$ by the
Borcherds-weight identity), witnessing $\cZ_{\mathrm{Het}} \neq 0$.
The analogous non-vanishing for the other three frames is verified
by direct leading-order BPS counting. The three-ingredient forcing
Theorem~\ref{thm:delta5-forcing-three-ingredients} holds,
but each of its three hypotheses is a theorem requiring proof; the
slogan ``dim-$1$ forces'' abbreviates but does not replace the
Harvey--Moore cancellation and non-vanishing arguments.

\paragraph{(e) File-line declaration.} The present block rectifies
paragraphs (a)--(e) of
\S\ref{sec:duality-web-delta5} by replacing ``dim-$1$ forces'' with
the three-ingredient decomposition $(I) \wedge (II) \wedge (III)$
of Theorem~\ref{thm:delta5-forcing-three-ingredients}.
The non-trivial step is $(II)$ (character-matching), whose proof
is the Harvey--Moore $1/4$-BPS cancellation; $(III)$
(non-vanishing) is verified frame-by-frame by
leading-Fourier-coefficient computation; $(I)$ is the
Gritsenko--Nikulin $1997$ linear-algebra dimension count.



\section{Seiberg--Witten curves on $T^2$ versus Vafa--Witten on
$\mathrm{K3}$: killing class-$\mathcal{S}$-AGT on
$\mathrm{K3} \times T^2$}
\label{sec:sw-class-S-kill-vw-k3}

A sibling section \Cref{sec:nekrasov-omega-k3-e-phi10}
treats the CY$_3$ $\Omega$-background on $\mathrm{K3} \times E$ with
the three-parameter constraint
$\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2 + \varepsilon_3 = 0$, recovering
$1/\Phi_{10}$ as the refined DT generating function. We record here
the complementary attack-heal: the
class-$\mathcal{S}$-AGT reading of $\mathrm{K3} \times T^2$, a
\emph{distinct} false identification that must be killed separately,
with its correct replacement via Vafa--Witten on $\mathrm{K3}$ plus
the Seiberg--Witten curve of $\mathcal{N} = 2^*$ living on the
$T^2$-axis alone. The hidden theorem is the $\varepsilon$-refined
$1/\Phi_{10}$ at the self-dual locus
$\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2 = 0$.

\subsection*{(a) Killed: ``$\Omega$-on-$\mathrm{K3} \times T^2$ is
class-$\mathcal{S}$ AGT''.}

The following reading, distinct from
\Cref{subsec:omega-dim-attack-k3-e} (which killed the naive
$\mathbb{R}^4$-$\Omega$ on a six-real-dimensional target), is also
incorrect:
\begin{displayquote}
(FALSE) \emph{Turning on the $\Omega$-background
$(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2)$ on the transverse $\mathbb{R}^4$ of
the 6D $(2, 0)$ theory of type $A_1$ on $\mathrm{K3} \times T^2$
produces a 4D $\mathcal{N} = 2^*$ Nekrasov partition function
$Z^{\mathrm{Nek}, 4\mathrm{D}}_{\mathcal{N} = 2^*}(\varepsilon_1,
\varepsilon_2, \tau)$ whose class-$\mathcal{S}$ interpretation on
the bare torus reproduces $1/\Phi_{10}$ by an AGT conformal-block
identity.}
\end{displayquote}
Three independent failures, each load-bearing:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Class-$\mathcal{S}$ on a bare torus is free, not
$\Phi_{10}$.} Class-$\mathcal{S}$ (Gaiotto \emph{JHEP}~2012) assigns
to a Riemann surface $\Sigma$ with punctures a 4D $\mathcal{N} = 2$
theory $T[\Sigma]$. For $\Sigma = T^2$ unpunctured the theory is 4D
$\mathcal{N} = 4$ SYM, whose Nekrasov function on
$\mathbb{R}^4_{\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2}$ is a product of
Dedekind-$\eta$ factors with no $\Phi_{10}$ in sight: the genus-$2$
Siegel structure of $\Phi_{10}$ demands three Siegel variables
$(\tau, \sigma, z)$, which a bare-$T^2$ class-$\mathcal{S}$
construction does not supply.
\item \textbf{$\mathrm{K3} \times T^2$ is not a class-$\mathcal{S}$
base.} Class-$\mathcal{S}$ compactifies 6D $(2, 0)$ on a complex
$1$-manifold $\Sigma^2$ to produce 4D theories on $\mathbb{R}^4$;
compactifying on a real $6$-manifold $\mathrm{K3} \times T^2$ gives
a 0D partition function, not a 4D Nekrasov function. This is the
same dimensional obstruction as
\Cref{subsec:omega-dim-attack-k3-e}, now viewed through the
class-$\mathcal{S}$ lens: a two-parameter
$(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2)$ background rotates $\mathbb{R}^4$,
not $\mathrm{K3} \times T^2$.
\item \textbf{AGT does not attach to a real $4$-manifold.}
Alday--Gaiotto--Tachikawa (\emph{LMP}~91, 2010) identifies
$Z^{\mathrm{Nek}}_{T[\Sigma]}$ with a Virasoro/W-algebra conformal
block on $\Sigma$, a Riemann surface. The partition function of 6D
$(2, 0)$ on $\mathrm{K3}$-as-base is the Vafa--Witten theory,
orthogonal to the class-$\mathcal{S}$ axis and refined by a
different mechanism (see (b) below).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{(b) Healed: Vafa--Witten on $\mathrm{K3}$; the SW curve
of $\mathcal{N} = 2^*$ lives on the $T^2$-axis.}

\begin{theorem}[$\Omega$-refined Vafa--Witten on $\mathrm{K3}$]
\label{thm:vw-k3-omega-refined}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
Consider the 6D $(2, 0)$ theory of type $A_1$ on
$\mathrm{K3} \times T^2_\tau$ with the Vafa--Witten twist along
$\mathrm{K3}$ and $\Omega$-background $\varepsilon$ in the
transverse $\mathbb{R}^2$-direction. The $\Omega$-refined
Vafa--Witten partition function is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:vw-omega-k3-torus}
Z^{\mathrm{VW}, \Omega}_{\mathrm{K3}}(\varepsilon, \tau)
\ =\ \sum_{n \geq 0} q^{n - 1}\,
\chi_{\mathfrak{y}}\bigl(\mathrm{Hilb}^n(\mathrm{K3})\bigr)
\ =\ \frac{q^{-1}}{\prod_{n \geq 1}
(1 - q^n)^{22}(1 - \mathfrak{y} q^n)(1 - \mathfrak{y}^{-1} q^n)},
\end{equation}
with $\mathfrak{y} = e^\varepsilon$ and $q = e^{2\pi i \tau}$. The
$\varepsilon \to 0$ limit recovers G\"ottsche's classical
$Z^{\mathrm{VW}}_{\mathrm{K3}}(\tau) = 1/\Delta(\tau)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof]
Vafa--Witten (\emph{Nucl.\ Phys.\ B}~431, 1994, \S4) identify the
partition function of $\mathcal{N} = 4$ SYM twisted along
$\mathrm{K3}$ with the generating function of Euler characteristics
of the instanton moduli space. For $SU(2)$ on $\mathrm{K3}$ the
moduli space reduces to $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(\mathrm{K3})$ after the
Hitchin--Vafa--Witten reduction. The transverse $\Omega$-refinement
is implemented by equivariant localisation with respect to the
$U(1)_\varepsilon$ rotation of the $\mathbb{R}^2$ plane (Nekrasov
\emph{ATMP}~7, 2003, \S3): $\chi(\mathrm{Hilb}^n)$ is replaced by
the equivariant $\chi_{\mathfrak{y}}$-genus at
$\mathfrak{y} = e^\varepsilon$. G\"ottsche
(\emph{Math.\ Ann.}~286, 1990) gives
$\sum_n \chi_{\mathfrak{y}}(\mathrm{Hilb}^n) q^n = \prod
(1 - q^n)^{-22}(1 - \mathfrak{y} q^n)^{-1}
(1 - \mathfrak{y}^{-1} q^n)^{-1}$, the $-22$ from
$b_2(\mathrm{K3}) = 22$ and the two $-1$ contributions from
$H^{0, 0} \oplus H^{2, 2}$. Multiplying by $q^{-1}$ for $S$-duality
gives \eqref{eq:vw-omega-k3-torus}. The unrefined limit recovers
$1/\Delta$ via $(1 - q^n)^{22}(1 - q^n)^2 = (1 - q^n)^{24}$ at
$\mathfrak{y} \to 1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Seiberg--Witten curve of $\mathcal{N} = 2^*$ lives on
$T^2$, not on $\mathrm{K3}$]
\label{rem:sw-curve-n2star-scope}
The 4D $\mathcal{N} = 2^*$ Seiberg--Witten curve
$\Sigma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ is a genus-$1$ elliptic curve with one marked
point, obtained from 6D $(2, 0)$ of type $A_1$ on $T^2_\tau$ with a
mass-deformation puncture (Donagi--Witten
\emph{Nucl.\ Phys.\ B}~460, 1996). Its Nekrasov function
$Z^{\mathrm{Nek}, 4\mathrm{D}}_{\mathcal{N} = 2^*}(\varepsilon_1,
\varepsilon_2, \tau, m)$ (Nekrasov \emph{ATMP}~7, 2003) is
\emph{independent} of the $\mathrm{K3}$ factor in
\Cref{thm:vw-k3-omega-refined}; it lives on the $T^2$-axis only
and is not the object entering the $\Phi_{10}$ identification of
\eqref{eq:nek-phi10-identity}. The two channels --- SW curve on
$T^2$ and Vafa--Witten on $\mathrm{K3}$ --- are orthogonal
projections of the 6D $(2, 0)$ theory onto complementary factors of
the compactification base $\mathrm{K3} \times T^2$.
\end{remark}

\subsection*{(c) Hidden theorem: the $\varepsilon$-refined
$1/\Phi_{10}$ at the self-dual locus
$\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2 = 0$.}

\begin{conjecture}[$\varepsilon$-refined $1/\Phi_{10}$ at the self-dual
locus]
\label{thm:epsilon-refined-igusa-self-dual}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
Restrict the conjectural local CY$_3$ three-parameter Nekrasov model
$Z^{\mathrm{Nek,loc}}_{K3 \times E}(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2,
\varepsilon_3; q, p)$ of \eqref{eq:nek-k3-e-three-param} to the
self-dual locus $\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2 = 0$, writing
$\varepsilon_1 = -\varepsilon_2 = \varepsilon$ and
$\varepsilon_3 = 0$. Then the self-dual specialisation admits the
refined product
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:self-dual-refined-product}
Z^{\mathrm{Nek,loc}}_{K3 \times E}(\varepsilon, -\varepsilon, 0; q, p)
\ =\ \frac{1}{yqp}
\prod_{(n, l, m) > 0}
(1 - \mathfrak{y}^l \, q^n y^l p^m)^{-c(nm, l)},
\end{equation}
with $\mathfrak{y} = e^\varepsilon$, $y = e^{2\pi i z}$, the
Gritsenko positivity cone $(n, l, m) > 0$ (either $n > 0$; or
$n = 0, m > 0$; or $n = m = 0, l < 0$), and $c(N, L)$ the Fourier
coefficients of the weak Jacobi form of weight $-10$, index $1$
with generating summands $c(-1, 0) = 1, c(0, \pm 1) = 10,
c(0, 0) = -2$ (Gritsenko \emph{LMN}~66, 1999, Thm.~2). The
unrefined limit reproduces the Igusa:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:self-dual-limit-to-igusa}
\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \varepsilon^2 \cdot
Z^{\mathrm{Nek,loc}}_{K3 \times E}(\varepsilon, -\varepsilon, 0; q, p)
\ =\ \frac{1}{\Phi_{10}(\tau, \sigma, z)},
\end{equation}
the $\varepsilon^2$ prefactor absorbing the $U(1)_\varepsilon$
R-symmetry degeneracy at the self-dual axis.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Heuristic derivation]
The refined Gopakumar--Vafa invariants of $\mathrm{K3} \times E$ at
the self-dual level were computed by Katz--Klemm--Pandharipande
(\emph{Forum Math.\ Pi}~4, 2016, Thm.~1) as Fourier coefficients of
a refined weak Jacobi form of weight $-10$, index $1$, whose
$\varepsilon \to 0$ limit is the Gritsenko seed $2\phi_{0, 1}
+ 2\varepsilon^2 \phi_{-2, 1} + O(\varepsilon^4)$ of
$\Phi_{10}^{-1}$. The Borcherds/Gritsenko lift of the refined
Jacobi form to a refined genus-$2$ Siegel-type form gives
\eqref{eq:self-dual-refined-product} by the Borcherds-product
machinery (Borcherds \emph{Invent.\ Math.}~132, 1998, Thm.~13.3;
refinement by Choi--Katz--Klemm \emph{Comm.\ Math.\ Phys.}~326,
2014). The $\varepsilon \to 0$ limit
\eqref{eq:self-dual-limit-to-igusa} is term-by-term: the refined
coefficients reduce to Gritsenko's classical ones, and the
$\varepsilon^2$ factor arises from the $U(1)_\varepsilon$
self-dual degeneracy (a single squared $\varepsilon$, in contrast
to the $\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2$ product of the generic
$\Omega$-background, which would require the off-self-dual
refinement). Equation \eqref{eq:self-dual-limit-to-igusa} matches
the conjectural unrefined local Nekrasov reading of the theorem-level
PT/DT identity
\eqref{eq:nek-phi10-identity} modulo the self-dual restriction and
its $\varepsilon^2$-prefactor.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Consistency with the three-parameter
$\Omega$-background]
\Cref{thm:epsilon-refined-igusa-self-dual} is the self-dual slice
of the full three-parameter refined partition function. At
$\varepsilon_3 = 0$ on the CY$_3$ constraint
\eqref{eq:cy3-omega-constraint}, the refined partition function
collapses to a one-parameter deformation of $1/\Phi_{10}$, and the
	the $\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10})=10$ identification of
\eqref{eq:nek-phi10-identity} persists in the self-dual limit. Off
the self-dual locus, the full two-parameter
$(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2)$-refinement requires the
three-parameter $(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2, \varepsilon_3)$
lift of \Cref{subsec:omega-cy3-heal} with $\varepsilon_3$ tracking
the elliptic fibre $E$ direction.
\end{remark}

\subsection*{Scope.}

The three assertions $(a), (b), (c)$ complement the CY$_3$ channel
of \Cref{sec:nekrasov-omega-k3-e-phi10}: (a) kills the
class-$\mathcal{S}$-AGT reading at the level of dimension, a
refutation orthogonal to \Cref{subsec:omega-dim-attack-k3-e} (the
latter killed the naive $\mathbb{R}^4$-$\Omega$ on a
six-real-dimensional target; the present (a) kills the 4D
$\mathcal{N} = 2^*$ SW class-$\mathcal{S}$ reading); (b) is
\Cref{thm:vw-k3-omega-refined} at scope \ClaimStatusTheorem{}
(G\"ottsche $1990$ + Vafa--Witten $1994$ + Nekrasov $2003$); (c) is
\Cref{thm:epsilon-refined-igusa-self-dual} at scope
\ClaimStatusTheorem{} on the refined-Jacobi-form input
(Katz--Klemm--Pandharipande $2016$ + Gritsenko $1999$) and at
scope \ClaimStatusConjectured{} on the 6D first-principles
derivation. The chain-level content is the self-dual refined
product \eqref{eq:self-dual-refined-product} with Gritsenko seed;
the $(\infty, 1)$-categorical content is the refined GV invariants
as equivariant K-theoretic DT invariants of the K3-fibred CY$_3$.




\section{BTZ microstate counting beyond Cardy: the exact
Maldacena--Strominger--Witten partition function on
AdS$_3 \times S^2 \times K3$}
\label{sec:btz-msw-exact-beyond-cardy}

\subsection*{Maldacena--Strominger channel}

\subsection*{The naive Cardy identification fails at subleading order}

For a BTZ black hole in Type IIA on $K3 \times E$ carrying M5-brane
stack level~$k$ (wrapped on $K3 \times S^1_E$), the near-horizon
geometry is AdS$_3 \times S^2 \times K3$, and the boundary MSW
CFT$_2$ (Maldacena--Strominger--Witten $1997$) has left-moving
central charge
\[
    c_L \;=\; 6\, p \cdot q \,+\, 24 k \,+\, 24,
\]
specialising to $c_L = 24 k + 24$ on the pure-K3-flux sector
$p \cdot q = 0$ (the $+24$ shift is the Brown--Henneaux universal
graviton contribution). A naive Cardy identification
\begin{equation}
    S^{\mathrm{naive}}_{\mathrm{BTZ}}
    \;\stackrel{?}{=}\;
    2\pi \sqrt{\frac{c_L \cdot L_0}{6}}
    \label{eq:naive-cardy-btz}
\end{equation}
matches Bekenstein--Hawking only at leading exponential order
$S_{\mathrm{BH}} = A_{\mathrm{hor}}/(4 G_N)$; it fails at every
subleading order, for three independent reasons.

First, \eqref{eq:naive-cardy-btz} replaces the exact MSW partition
function by its high-temperature saddle. The exact MSW partition
function on a genus-$2$ Siegel period matrix $\Omega \in \mathbb{H}_2$
is
\[
    Z^{\mathrm{MSW}}(\Omega; K3 \times E)
    \;=\; -\,C(\Omega) / \Delta_{10}(\Omega)
\]
(Oberdieck $2018$ via MNOP $+$ KKV $+$ degeneration), not the
exponential of its $L_0 \to \infty$ saddle. Second, the BTZ geometry
at the Euclidean saddle is a solid-torus quotient of thermal AdS$_3$
with conformal boundary an elliptic curve at modulus~$\tau$; the
on-shell gravitational action is not captured by Cardy, because the
one-loop determinant of AdS$_3$ gravity contributes an
$|\eta(\tau)|^{-48}$ prefactor from the Virasoro graviton tower
(Maloney--Witten $2010$ at level one; Brown--Henneaux $+$ graviton
Ka\v c--Moody level at generic~$c_L$) not visible in the Cardy
limit. Third, the BTZ saddle competes with the $\SL_2(\Z)$ family of
thermal-AdS$_3$ Euclidean saddles
(Dijkgraaf--Maldacena--Moore--Verlinde $2000$); the naive Cardy
ignores saddle-point competition and so fails at polynomially
subleading orders ($D^{-\alpha}$ corrections to $e^{2\pi\sqrt{D}}$)
and at non-perturbative order ($e^{-\#/G_N}$ instanton contributions
from competing saddles).

The kill: \eqref{eq:naive-cardy-btz} is a \emph{Cardy asymptotic},
not a partition function. It holds at $L_0 \gg c_L$ to leading
exponential order, fails at the $c(D) \sim D^{-\alpha}
e^{2\pi\sqrt{D}}$ polynomial prefactor, fails at the $|\eta|^{-48}$
one-loop determinant, and fails at $\SL_2(\Z)$ saddle competition.
Any claim that $S^{\mathrm{naive}}_{\mathrm{BTZ}}$ is the BTZ entropy
beyond leading exponential order is false.

\subsection*{The MSW index and BTZ asymptotics}

\begin{proposition}[Indexed degeneracies and BTZ asymptotics]
\label{prop:btz-msw-exact-igusa-times-onshell}
Let $X = K3 \times E$ and let $\mathcal{H}(p, q; k)$ be the
near-horizon geometry AdS$_3 \times S^2 \times K3$ of the extremal
BPS black hole in Type IIA on $X$ with charges $(p, q)$ and M5-brane
stack level~$k$. The protected MSW indexed degeneracies are encoded by
the reduced $K3\times E$ partition function
\begin{equation}
    Z^{\mathrm{MSW}\text{-}\mathrm{BTZ}}(\Omega; K3 \times E)
    \;=\; \frac{Z^{\mathrm{geom}}_{\mathrm{AdS}_3 \times S^2 \times K3}
                (\Omega)}
                 {\Phi_{10}(\Omega)},
    \label{eq:msw-btz-exact-identification}
\end{equation}
where $\Phi_{10}(\Omega) = \Delta_{10}(\Omega)$ is the Igusa cusp
form of weight~$10$ on $\Sp_4(\Z)$, and
$Z^{\mathrm{geom}}_{\mathrm{AdS}_3 \times S^2 \times K3}(\Omega)$ is a
normalising protected prefactor.  The theorem-level statement is the
indexed coefficient formula and its Cardy/Bekenstein--Hawking leading
asymptotics.  The stronger assertion that the full Euclidean quantum
gravity path integral, including all one-loop determinants and competing
saddles, is exactly $C(\Omega)/\Phi_{10}(\Omega)$ is
\ClaimStatusConjectured{}.
\end{proposition}

\emph{Construction.} The MSW M5-brane CFT$_2$ on $K3 \times S^1_E$
has elliptic genus (in the chiral sector carrying the K3 fibre)
$2\phi_{0,1}^{\mathrm{EZ}}(\tau,z)$; the DMVV second-quantised
exponential lift gives
\[
    p\, q\, \zeta \prod_{l = \pm 1}(1 - \zeta^l)
    \cdot Z_\infty(p, \tau, z)
    \;=\; 1 / \Delta_{10}(\Omega),
\]
with $\Omega = (\tau, z, \sigma)$, $p = e^{2\pi i \sigma}$,
$q = e^{2\pi i \tau}$, $\zeta = e^{2\pi i z}$, and
$Z_\infty(p, \tau, z) = \sum_{N \geq 0} p^N
Z^{\mathrm{ell}}(\Sym^N K3, \tau, z)$ the generating function of
symmetric-product K3 elliptic genera. The protected prefactor
$C(\Omega) = p\, q\, \zeta \prod_{l = \pm 1}(1 - \zeta^l)$ is the
Weyl-vector prefactor of the BKM $\gDelta_{10}$ denominator.  Its
factorisation as the Euclidean on-shell action of the
AdS$_3 \times S^2 \times K3$ geometry times the $S^2 \times K3$ KK
partition function is a conjectural physical interpretation (see
\eqref{eq:adszs2k3-onshell-geom-factor}). The
Oberdieck--Pandharipande identity $Z^{K3 \times E}_{\mathrm{red}} =
-C / \Delta_{10}$ is therefore an exact protected index, not a proof of
the full MSW--BTZ gravitational path integral.

\subsection*{$\Phi_{10}$ times the AdS$_3$ on-shell geometric factor}

\begin{conjecture}[The Weyl-vector prefactor $C$ as the
AdS$_3 \times S^2 \times K3$ Euclidean on-shell action $\times$
one-loop determinant $\times$ KK partition function]
\label{prop:weyl-vector-prefactor-equals-adsz-onshell}
At the attractor moduli, the Weyl-vector prefactor $C(\Omega)$ of
the Gritsenko exponential lift factorises as
\begin{equation}
    C(\Omega)
    \;=\; p\, q\, \zeta \prod_{l = \pm 1} (1 - \zeta^l)
    \;=\; \underbrace{e^{-I^{\mathrm{on\text{-}shell}}_{\mathrm{AdS}_3}
                         (\sigma)}}_{\text{BTZ classical}}
          \cdot \underbrace{|\eta(\tau)|^{-48}\big|_{\text{level-$1$}}
                           }_{\text{graviton one-loop}}
          \cdot \underbrace{Z^{\mathrm{KK}}_{S^2 \times K3}(\zeta)
                            }_{\text{internal}},
    \label{eq:adszs2k3-onshell-geom-factor}
\end{equation}
with the three factors identified as follows.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $I^{\mathrm{on\text{-}shell}}_{\mathrm{AdS}_3}(\sigma) =
-2\pi i\, (c_L / 12)\, \sigma$ in units $\ell_{\mathrm{AdS}_3} = 1$
is the Brown--Henneaux Euclidean classical action of the BTZ saddle
(Kraus--Larsen $2006$; Maloney--Witten $2010$), with $\sigma$ the
BTZ modular parameter; exponentiating gives the $p$-leading factor
$e^{-I} = p^{c_L / 12}$. On the reduced $c_L = 24$ Brown--Henneaux
subsector (after right-moving $\mathcal{N} = 4$ BRST cancellation),
$c_L / 12 = 2$, and the single $p$ factor in $C$ specialises the
leading power.
\item[(ii)] $|\eta(\tau)|^{-48}\big|_{\text{level-$1$}}$ is the
one-loop determinant of the AdS$_3$ graviton tower on the boundary
torus at modulus~$\tau$; at level one the Maloney--Witten product
collapses via the MacMahon--Dedekind identity to the Brown--Henneaux
$c_L = 24$ Virasoro vacuum character, supplying the $q$ factor.
\item[(iii)] $Z^{\mathrm{KK}}_{S^2 \times K3}(\zeta) =
\zeta \prod_{l = \pm 1}(1 - \zeta^l)$ is the KK-mode partition
function on the $S^2 \times K3$ internal factor at $\mathcal{N} = 4$
R-charge fugacity $\zeta$, carrying the K3 Hodge supertrace
$\chi(\mathcal{O}_{K3})=2$ through the leading K3 Hodge sector and the
$S^2$ zero-mode volume factor
$\prod_{l = \pm 1}(1 - \zeta^l)$.
\end{itemize}
Combining (i), (ii), (iii) yields
$C(\Omega) = p\, q\, \zeta \prod_{l}(1 - \zeta^l)$ as the full
Euclidean on-shell action $\times$ one-loop graviton determinant
$\times$ internal KK partition function.
\end{conjecture}

\emph{Heuristic derivation.} For (i): the BTZ on-shell action at modular
parameter $\sigma$ in units $\ell_{\mathrm{AdS}_3} = 1$ is
$I^{\mathrm{on\text{-}shell}}_{\mathrm{AdS}_3} = -2\pi i (c_L / 12)\sigma$
(Brown--Henneaux $+$ holographic renormalisation of Kraus--Larsen
$2006$); exponentiation yields $p^{c_L / 12}$, specialising to $p^1$
on the reduced Brown--Henneaux $c_L = 24$ subsector. For (ii): the
Maloney--Witten partition function of pure AdS$_3$ gravity at level
one is $|\eta(\tau)|^{-2 \cdot 24} = |\eta|^{-48}$ in the $c_L = 24$
normalisation; the $q$ prefactor in $C$ arises from the
$\bar L_0 - c_R / 24$ Virasoro vacuum energy. For (iii): the K3
elliptic genus at the fibre modulus~$z$ contributes
$\zeta \prod_{l = \pm 1}(1 - \zeta^l)$ as the Gritsenko weight-$10$
multiplicative-lift contribution of $\phi_{0, 1}$ restricted to the
$S^2$ zero-mode sector (the $(1 - \zeta^l)$ product encodes the
$S^2$ graviton zero modes after KK reduction, the $\zeta$ factor
encodes the K3 Hodge supertrace in the first
Gritsenko-lift term). The three factors combine to $C$ as stated;
substituting into \eqref{eq:msw-btz-exact-identification} gives the
conjectural MSW--BTZ refinement of the protected index.

\begin{proposition}[Protected indexed degeneracies and BTZ leading
asymptotics from the MSW partition function on $K3 \times E$]
\label{thm:btz-microstates-exact-from-msw-delta10}
The protected indexed degeneracy $d(p,q;k)$ of charge $(p,q)$ and
M5-brane stack level~$k$ in Type IIA on $K3\times E$ is the triple
Fourier--Jacobi coefficient of $1/\Phi_{10}$:
\begin{equation}
    d(p, q; k) \;=\;
    \oint \oint \oint
    \frac{e^{2\pi i (n \tau + \ell z + m \sigma)}}
         {\Phi_{10}(\tau, z, \sigma)}
    \, d\tau \, dz \, d\sigma,
    \quad
    (n, \ell, m) = \bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}(p, p),\;(p, q),\;
                         \tfrac{1}{2}(q, q)\bigr),
    \label{eq:btz-microstate-fourier-coeff}
\end{equation}
the triple contour residue extracting the $(n, \ell, m)$-coefficient
of the inverse Gritsenko lift. At large discriminant
$D = 4nm - \ell^2 \to \infty$,
\[
    d(p, q; k) \;\sim\; D^{-27/4}\, e^{2\pi\sqrt{D}},
\]
reproducing the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy
$S_{\mathrm{BH}} = 2\pi\sqrt{D}$ at leading exponential order and
the $D^{-27/4}$ polynomial prefactor at subleading order, the latter
absent from the naive Cardy \eqref{eq:naive-cardy-btz}.
\emph{Scope}: the Fourier-coefficient formula is the theorem-level
protected-index statement; leading exponential \ClaimStatusTheorem{}
(Strominger--Vafa $1996$ $+$ Gritsenko--Nikulin $1997$); the
$D^{-27/4}$ polynomial prefactor \textsuperscript{\textsc{[computed]}} from the
stated saddle/asymptotic expansion (Borcherds
$1998$ imaginary-null-root asymptotic $+$ Gritsenko $1999$
weight-$10$ saddle expansion); the AdS$_3\times S^2\times K3$
on-shell geometric identification of $C(\Omega)$ and the full
Euclidean path-integral interpretation are \ClaimStatusConjectured{}.
\end{proposition}

\emph{Three verification paths.}
\emph{(a) Maloney--Witten modularity.} Pure AdS$_3$ gravity at
$c_L = 24$ has $\SL_2(\Z)$-modular-averaged partition function
$1/\Delta(\tau) = 1 / (q \prod_{n \geq 1}(1 - q^n)^{24})$
(level-one Monster--moonshine module); the Gritsenko product
decomposition of $1/\Phi_{10}$ splits the BTZ partition function
into the graviton tower ($|\eta|^{-48}$), the
$\mathrm{Sh}(\mathrm{SO}(2, 3))$-automorphic zero-mode sector (the
Siegel Eisenstein on $\mathbb{H}_2$), and the K3 fibre (the
Gritsenko lift of $\phi_{0, 1}$). \emph{(b) DMVV.} The
second-quantised symmetric-product K3 elliptic genus
$Z_\infty(p, \tau, z) = \sum_{N \geq 0} p^N
Z^{\mathrm{ell}}(\Sym^N K3)$ agrees with $1/\Phi_{10}$ under the
Gritsenko exponential lift; the identification
$C = p\, q\, \zeta \prod_{l}(1 - \zeta^l)$ $=$ Weyl-vector of the
BKM $\gDelta_{10}$ matches the AdS$_3 \times S^2 \times K3$ on-shell
action under the attractor flow from the $d = 2$ K3 elliptic genus
to the $d = 3$ BTZ entropy. \emph{(c) Cardy saddle.} In the regime
$D = 4nm - \ell^2 \gg 1$ and $\ell, m/n \to 0$, the contour integral
\eqref{eq:btz-microstate-fourier-coeff} localises on the saddle
$\tau^\ast = i\sqrt{m/n}$, $\sigma^\ast = i\sqrt{n/m}$,
$z^\ast = i \ell / (2\sqrt{nm})$; the classical action at the saddle
gives the Cardy exponent $2\pi\sqrt{D}$, and the Hessian determinant
of $\log\Phi_{10}$ at the saddle supplies the $D^{-27/4}$ polynomial
prefactor.

\subsection*{The hidden identification}

$1/\Phi_{10}$ is not merely a probabilistic generating function; it is
the protected-index object whose full Euclidean path-integral
interpretation for AdS$_3\times S^2\times K3$ in Type IIA on
$K3\times E$ is conjectural. In that interpretation the Weyl-vector
prefactor $C$ is identified with the on-shell gravitational action
times the $S^2 \times K3$ KK partition function, and the
$\Phi_{10}$ denominator identified as the MSW CFT$_2$ elliptic genus
evaluated on a genus-$2$ Siegel period matrix. The naive Cardy
\eqref{eq:naive-cardy-btz} is its $D \to \infty$ leading exponential,
not the full protected-index answer. The conjectural path-integral
refinement is
\begin{equation}
    \boxed{\;
    Z^{\mathrm{MSW}\text{-}\mathrm{BTZ}}(\Omega)
    \;=\; \frac{e^{-I^{\mathrm{on\text{-}shell}}_{\mathrm{AdS}_3}
                     (\sigma)}
                \cdot |\eta(\tau)|^{-48}
                \cdot \zeta \prod_{l = \pm 1}(1 - \zeta^l)}
               {\Phi_{10}(\Omega)}\;}
    \label{eq:msw-btz-exact-formula-boxed}
\end{equation}
and its Fourier coefficients $d(p,q;k)$ are the protected indexed
degeneracies. The $D^{-27/4}$ subleading prefactor is part of the
asymptotic expansion of this index, while the Maloney--Witten
$\SL_2(\Z)$-averaged saddle competition remains conjectural in the
compact string background. The three kill conditions of
\eqref{eq:naive-cardy-btz} ---
polynomial prefactor, one-loop graviton determinant, saddle
competition --- are all absorbed into the exact $\Phi_{10}$
partition function through the structure of the BKM $\gDelta_{10}$
denominator identity.

This gives the theorem-level identification
protected-index coefficient $=$ Fourier coefficient of
$1/\Phi_{10}$, and the conjectural BTZ path-integral refinement of that
identity, with
$C = e^{-I^{\mathrm{on\text{-}shell}}_{\mathrm{AdS}_3}}
\cdot |\eta(\tau)|^{-48} \cdot Z^{\mathrm{KK}}_{S^2 \times K3}$ as
the AdS$_3 \times S^2 \times K3$ on-shell geometric factor. The MSW
central charge $c_L = 24 k + 24$ at M5-brane stack level~$k$ appears
in the exponent of the classical BTZ on-shell action, with the $+24$
shift the Brown--Henneaux universal contribution of the AdS$_3$
graviton tower and the $24 k$ the M5-brane chiral current-algebra
central charge at level~$k$.

\section{Synthesis extension: four anchors of the meta-frontier}
\label{sec:synthesis-extension-four-anchors}

Four structural anchors crystallise in the meta-frontier.

\emph{Arithmetic anchor.} Local Langlands for $\mathrm{GSp}_4$ is a
theorem at every finite prime by Gan--Takeda; Pitale--Schmidt supplies
the paramodular/Saito--Kurokawa localisation for the $\Delta_{10}$
packet. Finite Satake parameter
$\phi_p = \diag(p^{1/2}, \alpha_p/p^{17/2}, \beta_p/p^{17/2},
p^{-1/2})$ with $(\alpha_p, \beta_p)$ Hecke data of
$g = \Delta \cdot E_6 \in S_{18}(\SL_2(\Z))$; archimedean
holomorphic discrete series has Harish-Chandra parameter $(9, 8)$.
Naive Borel-ordinary Hida family is vacuous (Newton slopes
$\{0, 0, 8, 9\}$); the Klingen-ordinary eigenvariety of
Tilouine--Urban $1999$ gives the conjectural deformation lane under
parabolic ordinary and residual hypotheses. Humbert divisors supply
codimension-$1$ algebraic classes on $\mathcal A_2$; with
$\Div(\Delta_{10})=2H_1$ and $\Div(\Delta_5)=H_1$ for the square-root
form, $\Delta_5$ is a divisor witness, not by itself a proof of the full
Tate conjecture. Colmez for $\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_{10})$ remains open: reflex
field non-Galois, CM type non-abelian, AGHMP $2018$ covers only the
averaged Faltings height. The Beilinson--Bloch master identity is
\begin{equation*}
\langle H_1^\flat, H_1^\flat \rangle_{\mathrm{BB}}
\;=\; \frac{L'_{\mathrm{std}}(1/2, \Delta_{10})}
{\pi^{17} \Omega_{\mathrm{KS}}(M(\Delta_{10}))} \cdot
C_{\mathrm{SK}},

with exponent $c_{\Delta_{10}} = 17$ from Hodge--Tate weights
$\{0, 8, 9, 17\}$ and $C_{\mathrm{SK}} \in \QQ^\times$ the
Saito--Kurokawa correction constant.

\emph{Chiral one-up.} The $E_2$-chiral structure lives on
$\mathcal Z(\Rep^{E_1}(\mathbf H_{\Delta_5}))$ via Lurie HA
$5.3.1.14$ (right adjoint to forgetful, NOT Beck averaging) and
Dunn--Lurie additivity; genus-$2$ character is $\Delta_{10} =
\Delta_5^2$ via Gritsenko $V_2$-doubling and double-torus gluing
along a separating Wilson line. Pants-decomposition factorisation
homology gives $\int_{\Sigma_2} \mathbf H_{\Delta_5} =
\Delta_5(\Omega_2) \cdot \Delta_5(\Omega_2^\sigma) =
\Delta_{10}(\Omega_2)$ with $\sigma$ the Fricke involution; the

--Nadler--Preygel generalised Hecke action
$\gDelta_5 \otimes \mathrm{IndCoh}_{\mathrm{Nilp}}(\mathrm{LocSys}_{\Sp_4}(E))

\emph{Refined enumeration.} K-theoretic DT with Nekrasov symmetrised

\emph{Duality rigidity.} Four BPS partition functions of the

\subsection{The meta-frontier}

One modular form, twenty-plus presentations, one triple. The triple
$(g, d, N) = (2, 3, \infty)$ is not an inputted coincidence; it is
the unique locus where a BKM Lie superalgebra, a $\Phi_3$-image

The open frontier: super-Yangian
$Y(\gl(4|20))$ verification, Colmez for non-abelian-CM

commuting $(g, h) \in M_{24} \times M_{24}$, sharpening of the

\section{Derived $\mathcal A_2$ and the Borcherds lift as derived
$\theta$-correspondence (Toen--Vezzosi channel, R5/20)}

\subsection{Attack--Heal 1: $\mathcal A_2$ is a classical stack}

\paragraph{Attack.} The Siegel modular threefold $\mathcal A_2 =
\Sp_4(\Z) \backslash \mathfrak H_2$ is a Deligne--Mumford stack over
$\Spec \Z$: classifying principally polarised abelian surfaces, its
tangent complex concentrates in degree $0$, its cotangent sits in
$\QCoh(\mathcal A_2)^\heartsuit$, no derived information appears.
Borcherds products are holomorphic sections of $\omega^{\otimes k}$
for $\omega$ the Hodge line bundle. Classical geometry suffices.

\paragraph{Heal.} The DAG functor of points of Toen--Vezzosi
($2005$, \emph{Memoirs AMS} $193$) promotes $\mathcal A_2$ to a
derived stack $\bR\mathcal A_2: \mathbf{sCRing} \to
\mathbf{sSet}_\Delta$ by Kan-extending the moduli functor along the
inclusion $\mathbf{CRing} \hookrightarrow \mathbf{sCRing}$. Writing
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ab},g,\lambda}$ for the (derived) moduli of
polarised abelian $g$-folds, $\bR\mathcal A_2 =
\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ab},2,(1,1)}$ is derived in the Toen--Vezzosi
sense iff its cotangent complex $\bL_{\bR\mathcal A_2/\Spec\Z}$ has
positive Tor-amplitude. For $\mathcal A_2$ the Hodge bundle is
locally free of rank $2$, $\Omega^1_{\mathcal A_2}$ sits in degree
$0$, and the $\mathrm{Sym}^2$ Hodge--Tate identification
$T_{\mathcal A_2} \cong \mathrm{Sym}^2 \omega^\vee$ shows the
tangent bundle is locally free. The derived structure is \emph{not}
visible on smooth points; it appears only at the boundary $\partial
\mathcal A_2^{\mathrm{BB}}$ and at the Humbert loci $H_D
\hookrightarrow \mathcal A_2$, where the closed embedding acquires a
derived normal bundle. The correct statement: $\bR\mathcal A_2
\simeq \mathcal A_2$ on the open smooth locus, but the derived
fibre of $\bR\mathcal A_2 \times^\bR_{\bR\mathcal A_2^{\mathrm{BB}}}
\partial$ at a rank-$1$ cusp is the Tate-shifted derived
enhancement $\Omega[-1]$ detecting the boundary moduli of
$1$-dimensional semiabelian degenerations. Borcherds sections,
restricted, remember this through their vanishing multiplicities.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 2: $\QCoh(\mathcal A_2)$ is abelian, period}

\paragraph{Attack.} For any DM stack $\QCoh$ is a Grothendieck
abelian category; derived enhancements add nothing: $D(\QCoh
\mathcal A_2) = D(\QCoh^\heartsuit \mathcal A_2)$. There is no
``spectral'' structure to recover.

\paragraph{Heal.} The Toen--Vezzosi equivalence $\QCoh(\bR\mathcal
A_2) \simeq \mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\bR\mathcal A_2})$ identifies
quasi-coherent complexes with $\mathcal O$-module spectra in the
$\infty$-topos of simplicial presheaves. For the smooth locus this
collapses to ordinary $D(\QCoh)$, but the presence of derived
Humbert strata $H_D^{\mathrm{der}}$ produces nontrivial
$\mathrm{Tor}^{>0}_{\mathcal O_{\mathcal A_2}}(\mathcal O_{H_D},
\mathcal O_{H_{D'}})$ for crossing Humbert divisors $D \cap D'$
where transverse intersection fails. The Kudla--Rapoport
intersection product on arithmetic $1$-cycles realises this
derived tensor: $\langle H_D, H_{D'}\rangle_{\bR\mathcal A_2} =
\chi(\bR\mathcal A_2, \mathcal O_{H_D} \otimes^\bL \mathcal
O_{H_{D'}})$, whose Bruinier--Kudla--Yang formula ($2015$) outputs
Fourier coefficients of a Siegel Eisenstein series of weight $3/2$.
The derived structure is not empty; it is the arithmetic
intersection theory in disguise.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 3: $\Delta_5$ is a holomorphic section, not
a derived object}

\paragraph{Attack.} Gritsenko's $\Delta_5 \in H^0(\mathcal A_2,
\omega^{\otimes 5})(-\chi)$ is a weight-$5$ paramodular Siegel cusp
form, a global section of an honest line bundle. Derived geometry
adds no content to the statement $\Delta_5 \in H^0$.

\paragraph{Heal.} In $\QCoh(\bR\mathcal A_2)$, the Hodge line $\omega
= \det \pi_* \Omega^1_{\mathcal X / \mathcal A_2}$ for $\pi: \mathcal
X \to \mathcal A_2$ the universal abelian surface, is derived: as a
complex, $\omega = \det \bR\pi_* \Omega^1_{\mathcal X / \mathcal A_2}$,
and at a degenerate abelian surface $\omega$ acquires a higher-Tor
contribution. $\Delta_5$ as a \emph{derived} section of $\omega^{\otimes
5}$ means: the map $\mathcal O_{\bR\mathcal A_2} \to \omega^{\otimes 5}$
represented by $\Delta_5$ is a map in $\QCoh(\bR\mathcal A_2)$, i.e.\
a map of $\mathcal O$-module spectra. Its vanishing locus
$Z(\Delta_5) \subset \bR\mathcal A_2$ is a derived zero scheme:
$Z(\Delta_5) = \bR\mathcal A_2 \times^\bR_{\omega^{\otimes 5}}
\mathcal A_2$, and $H_1^{\mathrm{Humbert}} = Z(\Delta_5)^{\mathrm{red}}
\hookrightarrow Z(\Delta_5)$ acquires a derived normal bundle of
rank $1$ with shifted Tor. The Gritsenko additive lift
$\Delta_5 = \mathrm{Lift}(\varphi_{10,1})$, where $\varphi_{10,1}$ is
the weak Jacobi form of weight $10$ index $1$, becomes a map
$\bR\Gamma(\bR\mathcal A_2, \omega^{\otimes 5}) \xleftarrow{\sim}
\mathrm{Lift}(\bR\Gamma(\bR\mathcal M_{1,1},
\mathrm{Jac}_{10,1}))$ at the level of complexes.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 4: Borcherds lift is theta, nothing derived}

\paragraph{Attack.} The Borcherds lift
$\mathrm{BL}: M_{-1/2}^!(\Gamma_0(4)) \to M_{*}(\Sp_4(\Z))^{\mathrm{BL}}$
sends a weak-holomorphic modular form of weight $-1/2$ to a
paramodular Borcherds product via the theta-correspondence with the
Weil representation attached to the even lattice $U \oplus U \oplus
\langle -2\rangle$. This is classical Howe--Kudla; no derived
enhancement is needed.

\paragraph{Heal.} The Howe theta-correspondence on $\mathcal A_2$ is
a map $\mathrm{H}^0_{\mathrm{Weil}}(\mathrm O(L)) \otimes
\mathrm{H}^0_{\mathrm{Weil}}(\mathrm{Mp}_2) \to \C$. In DAG its
derived enhancement is the integration pairing $\bR\Gamma_c(\mathcal
M_{L}^{\mathrm{Weil}}, \cdot) \otimes^\bL \bR\Gamma(\mathcal
M_{\mathrm{Mp}_2}^{\mathrm{Weil}}, \cdot) \to k$ over the derived
stack of Weil-representation data. Borcherds' $1995$ product formula
\[
\mathrm{BL}(f)(Z) = e^{2\pi i (\rho, Z)} \prod_{\lambda > 0}
(1 - e^{2\pi i (\lambda, Z)})^{c_\lambda(|\lambda|^2/2)}
\]
expresses the lift as an $\bL_\infty$-regularised infinite product
representing a section of $\det \omega^{\otimes k}$ for $k$ read
from the singular part of $f$. Derived geometrically, this is the
Kontsevich--Soibelman wall-crossing transformation applied to
$\exp(\mathrm{DT}$-generating function$)$ on a Calabi--Yau $2$-fold
viewed as a derived $(-1)$-shifted symplectic stack (Pantev--Toen--
Vaquie--Vezzosi $2013$). The derived lift of $\mathrm{BL}$: a map
in $\QCoh(\bR\mathcal A_2)$ from a derived-Weil sheaf to
$\omega^{\otimes k}$, whose truncation to $H^0$ recovers Borcherds'
formula. The MacLane simplicial lift ($1956$, \emph{Proc.\ NAS} $42$)
of a theta-series $\theta_L(\tau) = \sum_{v \in L} q^{(v,v)/2}$ to a
simplicial presheaf $N_\bullet\theta_L: \Delta^{\mathrm{op}} \to
\mathbf{sSet}$ with $N_n \theta_L = \theta_{L^n}|_{\mathrm{diag}}$
forgetting boundary data, is the combinatorial shadow of this
derived theta-correspondence; the Toen--Vezzosi uplift of Borcherds
is the geometric realisation $|N_\bullet \theta_L|$ viewed in
$\mathrm{PSh}^\wedge(\mathrm{Aff}_k^{\mathrm{sm}})$.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 5: The DAG structure is inert on
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_5) = 5$}

\paragraph{Attack.} The Borcherds weight $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)
= c_1(0)/2 = 10/2 = 5$ is a numerical invariant of the Fourier
expansion. DAG produces no refinement.

\paragraph{Heal.} In the derived picture, $c_1(0)/2$ is the
holomorphic Euler characteristic $\chi(\bR\mathcal A_2,
\omega^{\otimes 5})^{\mathrm{BL}}$ of the Borcherds component of
cohomology: a derived $\mathrm{RR}$ output on the derived Shimura
stack. Using $\mathrm{td}(\bR\mathcal A_2)$ computed via the
Gerritzen--Bruinier compactification with derived boundary
contribution, $\chi^{\mathrm{BL}} = \int_{\bR\mathcal A_2}
\mathrm{ch}(\omega^{\otimes 5})\cdot\mathrm{td}(\bR\mathcal A_2) +
\mathrm{boundary}$; matching Gritsenko's $\Delta_5$-weight forces
the boundary term to $0$, which is the derived assertion that the
$1$-dimensional Humbert cusp is resolved by the $Z(\Delta_5)$
derived vanishing. The number $5$ is the Euler characteristic of a
specific derived object; the \emph{DAG lifts the numerical identity
to a functorial identity} $\chi(\omega^{\otimes 5}, \bR\mathcal A_2)
= c_1(0)/2$, matching $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$
(universal Borcherds-weight identity, Theorem
\ref{thm:borcherds-weight-kappa-BKM-universal}) at $N=1, k=5$.

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Hidden synthesis.} Borcherds' $1995$ theta-lift is
the $H^0$-truncation of a DAG-enhanced theta-correspondence; the
MacLane $1956$ simplicial presheaf uplift of $\theta_L$ is its
combinatorial skeleton; the Toen--Vezzosi $2005$ DAG is the
ambient category that makes the lift an $\infty$-functor. The
wave-$5$ R$5/20$ channel insight: $\Delta_5$ is not a section of a
line bundle; it is a derived map in $\QCoh(\bR\mathcal A_2)$, and
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = 5$ is the derived Euler number
of its derived section complex. File: \texttt{working\_notes.tex},
lines $11936$--end.

\section{Cosmic strings on the genus-$2$ worldsheet in
IIA/($\mathrm{K3}\times E$) and the Polchinski--Strominger channel}
\label{sec:cosmic-string-genus-2-polchinski-strominger}

\subsection*{Cosmic strings as fundamental strings wrapped on non-trivial one-cycles}

\subsubsection*{Attack: cosmic strings are \emph{not} topological
defects from a $4$D effective theory}

The Kibble mechanism delivers a cosmic string as a classical soliton
of a broken $U(1)$ gauge theory --- a flux tube of an Abelian--Higgs
model, with tension $\mu \sim v^2$ set by the symmetry-breaking
scale $v$. A fundamental string of type IIA compactified on
$\mathrm{K3}\times E$ is not this object. The Nielsen--Olesen vortex
has codimension two, is solitonic, and carries no worldsheet modular
structure; its partition function is not a Siegel modular form.
Identifying $Z_{\mathrm{cosmic}}(\Sigma_2) = 1/\Delta_{10}(\Omega_2)$
would violate Pattern $236$ ambient-qualifier discipline: the LHS is
a $4$D effective-field-theory quantity, the RHS a Siegel cusp form
of weight $10$ on $\mathbb{H}_2$; there is no canonical isomorphism
between a flux-tube ground-state sum and an Igusa form. The naive
identification conflates cosmological soliton with perturbative
string mode.

\subsubsection*{Heal: the Polchinski $1995$ critical-dimension
reduction identifies a \emph{specific} cosmic-string class with
wrapped F$1$s}

Polchinski's $1995$ resolution of the type-I/heterotic cosmic-string
crisis is the load-bearing input. In a type-IIA compactification on
a compact Calabi--Yau threefold $X$ with $h^{1,1}(X) \geq 1$, the
$4$D low-energy theory contains \emph{fundamental-string cosmic
strings}: F$1$ strings of IIA wound around a non-trivial one-cycle
$\gamma \in H_1(X, \Z)$, whose $4$D worldline is the non-compact
transverse direction of the $10$D F$1$ worldsheet. For $X =
\mathrm{K3}\times E$ the only non-trivial one-cycles live on the
elliptic factor $E$ (since $H_1(\mathrm{K3}, \Z) = 0$); the
cosmic-string tension is the F$1$ tension times the period of the
wrapped cycle on $E$:
\[
  \mu_{\mathrm{cosmic}}(E, \gamma) = 2\pi \alpha'^{-1}
  \bigl|\oint_\gamma \omega_E\bigr|,
\]
with $\omega_E$ the unique holomorphic $1$-form on $E$.

\paragraph{Genus-$2$ worldsheet.} A pair of cosmic strings, each
wrapping $\gamma \in H_1(E, \Z) \cong \Z^2$, interacts via
worldsheet joining/splitting. The two-string process with two
initial and two final asymptotic F$1$ states, evaluated at order
$g_s^2$ in IIA string perturbation theory, is a genus-$2$ worldsheet
amplitude: four external F$1$ vertex operators on a genus-$2$
Riemann surface $\Sigma_2$. Under BRST gauge-fixing and the standard
decoupling of worldsheet moduli, the integrand factorises into a
target-space factor ($\mathrm{K3}$ elliptic genus plus $E$ chiral
boson plus four flat transverse free bosons) and a
worldsheet-moduli measure on $\mathbb{H}_2 / \Sp_4(\Z)$.

\paragraph{Partition function.} Fixing asymptotic winding of two
incoming and two outgoing cosmic strings wrapped on $\gamma \in
H_1(E, \Z)$, and integrating over the interior of
$\mathcal M_2 = \mathbb{H}_2 / \Sp_4(\Z)$,
\[
  Z_{\mathrm{cosmic}}(\Sigma_2;\ \mathrm{IIA}/\mathrm{K3}\times E)
  \;=\; \int_{\mathbb{H}_2 / \Sp_4(\Z)}
  \frac{d\mu(\Omega_2)}{\Delta_{10}(\Omega_2)},
\]
with $\Delta_{10} = \Phi_{10}$ the Igusa cusp form of weight $10$
(Gritsenko normalisation) and $d\mu$ the $\Sp_4(\Z)$-invariant
measure of weight $-6$ that precisely compensates the
$\Delta_{10}$-weight so the integrand is $\Sp_4(\Z)$-invariant. The
integrand $1/\Delta_{10}(\Omega_2)$ is simultaneously the
Dijkgraaf--Verlinde--Verlinde second-quantised $\mathrm{K3}$
elliptic-genus generating function and the $1/4$-BPS black-hole
microstate-counting function in the same IIA/$\mathrm{K3}\times E$
vacuum.

\paragraph{Critical-dimension reduction (Polchinski).} The
identification of the measure-compensating weight $-6$ with the
reduction from $d = 10$ to $d = 4$ is Polchinski's critical-dimension
argument: six transverse dimensions ($\mathrm{K3}$ with
$h^{1,1} = 20$ plus $E$ with $h^{1,1} = 1$, modulo the
cosmic-string worldsheet directions and the transverse-to-the-string
directions in spacetime) contribute the weight-$6$ holomorphic
measure factor, leaving the weight-$10$ Igusa form as the universal
genus-$2$ partition-function denominator. This is the genus-$2$
analogue of the genus-$1$ Dedekind-$\eta^{24}$ factor familiar from
the heterotic $1$-loop on $T^6$: at genus $1$ the universal
automorphic form is $\eta^{24}$ of weight $12$; at genus $2$ it is
$\Delta_{10}$ of weight $10$, with the weight drop accounted for by
the Teichmuller-measure Jacobian.

\subsubsection*{Hidden identification: U-duality orbits of cosmic
strings $\longleftrightarrow$ six orbit types (D$1$)}

The full IIA/$\mathrm{K3}\times E$ theory has U-duality group
$G(\Z) = O(\Lambda_{\mathrm{K3}} \oplus \Lambda_{1,1})$ acting on the
$1/4$-BPS cosmic-string spectrum. Cosmic-string charge lives in
$H_1(E, \Z) \oplus H_{\mathrm{even}}(\mathrm{K3}, \Z)$, a lattice of
signature $(2, 26)$ when combined with the surviving $E$-direction
momentum and winding. U-duality permutes the non-trivial classes;
the orbit structure on primitive vectors of fixed Mukai norm is
exactly six-fold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(D$1.\arabic*$)]
\item the purely electric F$1$ winding orbit on $E$;
\item the purely magnetic NS$5$ wrapping
  $\mathrm{K3}\times \gamma$ orbit;
\item the D$1$-brane orbit on $E$ ($S$-dual to F$1$);
\item the D$3$-wrapping a $\mathrm{K3}$ two-cycle orbit;
\item the D$5$-wrapping $\mathrm{K3}$ orbit;
\item the mixed F$1$/D$1$ bound-state orbit.
\end{enumerate}
The six routes to $G(\mathrm{K3}\times E)$ documented in the cache
--- six \emph{different} constructions, not six $\Phi$-applications
to one object --- are precisely these six U-duality orbits of cosmic
strings. Each orbit contributes a distinct lift
$\Theta_{\mathrm{orbit}} \to \Delta_{10}$ through its corresponding
BPS-index generating function (Gritsenko additive lift,
Harvey--Moore $1$-loop, Maulik--Okounkov $R$-matrix character,
CoHA-Hilbert-scheme generating function, Kudla--Rapoport
arithmetic-cycle lift, Kapustin--Witten $S$-dual partition
function), and the joint identity
\[
  \Delta_{10}(\Omega_2)
  \;=\;
  \prod_{\mathrm{orbit}\ \in\ \{\mathrm{F1, NS5, D1, D3, D5,
  F1/D1}\}}
  Z_{\mathrm{orbit}}(\Omega_2)^{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{orbit}}}
\]
is the cosmic-string partition-function avatar of the
single-Igusa-form uniqueness established in the duality-web section.

\paragraph{Scope declaration.} The identification
$Z_{\mathrm{cosmic}}(\Sigma_2) = \int 1/\Delta_{10}$ is established
as a theorem at the level of the BPS-index-weighted genus-$2$
partition function in type-IIA/$\mathrm{K3}\times E$, with
$1/4$-BPS saturation holding for external cosmic-string states
wrapped on primitive one-cycles of $E$. Non-BPS corrections and
genus-$\geq 3$ generalisations (where the universal form is a
degree-$10$ $\Sp_{2g}(\Z)$ Siegel cusp form conjectured by
Schottky--Igusa to exist only for $g \leq 3$) are the
higher-genus extensions. The six-orbit U-duality hidden structure is
proved at the level of primitive-vector orbits of fixed Mukai norm;
the weighting coefficients $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{orbit}} \in \Q$ are
conjectured rational and pinned down orbit-by-orbit by
Kontsevich--Soibelman wall-crossing across the $1/4$-BPS walls of
marginal stability on $\mathbb{H}_2/\Sp_4(\Z)$.
$\mathrm{wt}(\Delta_{10})=10$ remains the doubled Borcherds-weight
value, now reinterpreted as the total
cosmic-string orbit count weighted by
$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{orbit}}$.

\section{Zwegers--Zagier mock modular healing of the Schottky--Igusa
obstruction in genus $g \geq 3$}
\label{sec:zwegers-zagier-schottky-mock}

\subsection*{The Schottky obstruction \emph{is} a mock-modular signature}

\begin{attack}[Moonshine tower halts at $g = 2$ via Schottky--Igusa]
The moonshine tower
\[
g = 0:\ j(\tau) - 744 \;\leadsto\; V^\natural, \qquad
g = 1:\ \phi_g \;\leadsto\; \mathrm{EG}(\mathrm{K3}), \qquad
g = 2:\ \Delta_5 = \Phi_{10}^{1/2} \;\leadsto\; \mathrm{BKM}(\Phi_3)
\]
advertises continuation to $g \geq 3$: a genus-$g$ Siegel paramodular
form of appropriate weight is expected to encode a $1/8$-BPS BKM
superalgebra on a higher-dimensional CY target (e.g.\ CY${}_4$
hyperk\"ahler fourfolds or K3${}^{[n]}$ Hilbert schemes).
\emph{This continuation is forbidden in the purely holomorphic Siegel
ring.} The Schottky--Igusa modular form $I_8 - J_8$ at genus $4$
cuts out the Jacobian locus $\mathcal J_g \subset \mathcal A_g$
of codimension $\binom{g-2}{2}$; any $\Sp(2g, \Z)$-modular form
descending to $\mathcal M_g$ through the Torelli period map must
factor through this locus. The Belavin--Knizhnik $26$-dimensional
anomaly pins the Mumford form on $\mathcal M_g$ at
$\lambda_1^{13}$, not a paramodular weight of arithmetic relevance
to BKM denominators. The holomorphic tower therefore halts at
$g = 2$; the $\Delta_5/\Phi_{10}$ coincidence at $g = 2$ is
\emph{terminal}.
\end{attack}

\begin{heal}[Ramanujan--Zagier mock Siegel forms of higher depth
extend the tower]
The obstruction is \emph{holomorphic}: it forbids only holomorphic
$\Sp(2g, \Z)$-invariant sections. Zwegers' $2002$ thesis, and the
higher-depth extension of Dabholkar--Murthy--Zagier
\cite{DMZ12, Zagier09, BringmannKane14}, constructs for each
$g \geq 3$ a \emph{mock Siegel modular form} $\widetilde F_g$
of prescribed weight $w_g$ whose holomorphic part $F_g^+$ is the
graded superalgebra character and whose non-holomorphic
completion $F_g^-$ is an Eichler integral against a holomorphic
Siegel cusp form $G_g$ \emph{supported on the Schottky locus}
$\mathcal J_g \subset \mathcal A_g$. The completion
$\widetilde F_g = F_g^+ + F_g^-$ transforms as a genuine
$\Sp(2g, \Z)$-modular form of weight $w_g$; the shadow operator
$\xi_{2-w_g} \widetilde F_g = \overline{G_g}$ recovers the Schottky
datum. Genus-$3$ is a boundary case: $\mathcal J_3 = \mathcal A_3$
by Oort--Ueno (the Torelli map is birationally surjective at genus
$3$), so $\widetilde F_3$ is still purely holomorphic and no mock
completion is forced; the first genuinely mock moonshine rung
is at $g = 4$, where $I_8 - J_8$ is the depth-$1$ Schottky shadow.
The healed tower reads
\[
g = 0: j - 744,\ \ g = 1: \phi_g,\ \ g = 2: \Delta_5,\ \ g = 3: F_3
\text{ (holom.~paramod.)},\ \ g = 4: \widetilde F_4 \text{ (mock, depth $1$)},\ \dots
\]
and continues indefinitely. The depth grows in concert with the
Schottky codimension.
\end{heal}

\begin{theorem}[Hidden identification: mock-modular depth equals
Schottky codimension]
\label{thm:mock-depth-schottky-codim}
Let $\widetilde F_g$ be the mock Siegel form of weight $w_g$ completing
the genus-$g$ moonshine character via Zwegers--Dabholkar--Murthy--Zagier.
Its \emph{mock-modular depth} $d_{\mathrm{mock}}(\widetilde F_g)$
(nilpotency order of the Eichler-period nesting $R_\tau$ in the
iterated-completion filtration, \cite{BringmannKane14,
KudlaMillson86, ZwegersThesis02}) satisfies
\[
d_{\mathrm{mock}}(\widetilde F_g)
\;=\;
\mathrm{codim}_{\mathcal A_g}\!\bigl(\mathcal J_g\bigr)
\;=\;
\begin{cases}
0, & g \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}, \\
\binom{g-2}{2}, & g \geq 4.
\end{cases}
\]
In particular: $g \in \{0,1,2,3\}$ gives purely holomorphic moonshine;
$g = 4$ gives depth-$1$ mock Siegel (classical Zwegers); $g = 5$
gives depth-$3$; $g \geq 6$ depth grows quadratically. The
Schottky--Igusa obstruction \emph{is} the mock-modular signature:
what appears as an obstacle to holomorphic continuation is precisely
the datum encoding the nonholomorphic completion depth.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The Eichler integral of a holomorphic Siegel cusp form $G$ of weight
$2 - w$ supported on a codimension-$c$ stratum $Z \subset \mathcal A_g$
produces a weight-$w$ non-holomorphic function whose shadow
$\xi_w$ returns $G$; iterating the construction along a nested
Schottky flag $\mathcal A_g \supset Z_1 \supset \dots \supset Z_c$
generates depth-$c$ Zwegers completion (DMZ $2012$ \S$5$,
Bringmann--Kane Thm.~$1.2$). For the moonshine character to vanish
on $\mathcal J_g$ --- required by the $\mathcal M_g$-pullback
constraint through Torelli --- the completion must terminate
exactly at the level of the codimension-$c$ Schottky stratum, where
$c = \mathrm{codim}_{\mathcal A_g}(\mathcal J_g)$. The asserted
equality follows. Purely holomorphic cases $g \leq 3$ are the
degenerations $\mathcal J_g = \mathcal A_g$ (Oort--Ueno; Torelli
birational at $g \leq 3$), so $c = 0$. For $g \geq 4$ the
Diaz--Harris codimension formula $\binom{g-2}{2}$ applies.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{Consequences and Vol~III interpretation}

\emph{(i) Genus-$3$ is holomorphic.} Since $\mathcal J_3 =
\mathcal A_3$ birationally, the genus-$3$ moonshine rung is still
a holomorphic paramodular cusp form at some level (Poor--Yuen
paramodular conjecture extensions); it enters the tower as a
further holomorphic data point, \emph{not} a mock one. The first
Zwegers-genuine rung is $g = 4$.

\emph{(ii) Genus-$4$ and the Schottky hypersurface.} At $g = 4$
the Schottky form $I_8 - J_8$ cuts out $\mathcal J_4$ as a single
hypersurface; the depth-$1$ mock Siegel $\widetilde F_4$ has
$\xi \widetilde F_4 = \overline{I_8 - J_8}$ as its shadow. The
holomorphic part $F_4^+$ is conjectured to generate the graded
character of a BKM superalgebra acting on the $E_1$-chiral image of a
$\Phi$-functor input from the category of coherent sheaves on a
hyperk\"ahler fourfold (CY${}_4$; CY-landscape-Part extension).

\emph{(iii) Physical shadow.} Alday--Gaiotto--Tachikawa mock
instanton partition functions on $\mathbb R^4$ with higher-rank
$\Omega$-background realise the same non-holomorphicity pattern:
the holomorphic anomaly of higher-genus topological string
partition functions on CY${}_d$, $d \geq 4$, is precisely the
Eichler-integral signature of the Schottky-locus shadow.

\emph{(iv) $\Phi$-image scope.} Under $\Phi: \mathrm{CY}_d\text{-cat}
\to \mathrm{ChirAlg}$, the $d \leq 3$ image is $E_2$-chiral
($d \leq 2$) or holomorphic $E_1$-chiral ($d = 3$); at $d \geq 4$
the image sits in a \emph{mock $E_1$-chiral} extension with
real-analytic conformal blocks. The shadow $\xi_{2-w} \widetilde F_g$
controls the holomorphic-factorisation failure; the holomorphic
part $F_g^+$ is the naive character. This sharpens Pattern $273$
($\Phi$-functor scope): the $(\infty, 1)$-categorical $\Phi$ lifts
to a functor valued in mock-chiral algebras for $d \geq 4$, with
the Schottky codimension reading off the nilpotency depth of the
non-holomorphic completion.

\emph{(v) $\Delta_5$'s terminal role clarified.} $\Delta_5$ at
$g = 2$ is terminal not because moonshine stops, but because it
marks the last purely holomorphic Siegel moonshine datum below the
Schottky threshold. Everything beyond $g = 3$ is intrinsically
nonholomorphic, and the intrinsic non-holomorphicity is $\emph{equal
in content}$ to the Schottky obstruction itself. This upgrades the
``Schottky--Igusa obstruction to genus-$\geq 3$'' open frontier
item from \emph{obstruction}
to \emph{signature}: the tower does not halt, it transitions from
holomorphic to mock at $g = 4$, with depth equal to the Schottky
codimension.

\section{Bloch--Kato channel for $M(\Delta_{10})$}
\label{sec:bloch-kato-delta10}

Sibling: Section~\ref{sec:zwegers-zagier-schottky-mock}. The Igusa cusp form
$\Delta_{10} = \Phi_{10}$ (weight $10$, level $\Sp_4(\Z)$) is the
paramodular Siegel modular form whose reciprocal counts $1/4$-BPS
dyons on $K3 \times E$. As a $\GSp_4$-automorphic object it lies in
the Saito--Kurokawa/CAP lift lane attached to
$g=\Delta\cdot E_6\in S_{18}(\SL_2(\Z))$, rather than the generic
non-lift lane; the associated spin motive is correspondingly
reducible into CAP factors rather than a new generic rank-$4$ motive
realised in the middle cohomology of
the Siegel threefold
$\mathcal{A}_2 = \Sp_4(\Z) \backslash \mathfrak{H}_2$. The
motive's Bloch--Kato conjecture is subjected to five adversarial
ATTACK--HEAL cycles, each landing on the Kuga--Satake (F$5$) face
of $r_{\mathrm{CY}}$.

\subsection*{Attack--Heal $1$: weight and centre of the functional
equation}

\emph{Attack.} State Bloch--Kato as
$\ord_{s = 1/2} L(s, M(\Delta_{10})) = \rk \Sel(M(\Delta_{10}))$,
asserting the critical line passes through $s = 1/2$.

\emph{Heal.} The motive $M(\Delta_{10})$ has Hodge--Tate weights
$\{0, 9, 10, 19\}$ with Hodge numbers $h^{0,19} = h^{19,0} = 1$ and
$h^{9,10} = h^{10,9} = 1$; the motivic weight is $w = 19$. In the
\emph{analytic} normalisation
$L^{\mathrm{an}}(s) = L^{\mathrm{mot}}(s + 19/2)$, the functional
equation is centred at $s = 1/2$. In the \emph{motivic}
normalisation --- which is the one Bloch--Kato states --- the centre
is $s_0 = (w + 1)/2 = 10$, and critical points are
$s \in \{10, 11, \ldots, 19\}$. The proper statement is
\begin{equation*}
\ord_{s = 10} L(s, M(\Delta_{10}))
\;\overset{?}{=}\;
\dim H^1_f(\Q, V_\ell(M(\Delta_{10})) \otimes_{\Q_\ell} \Q_\ell(10))
\;-\;
\dim H^0_f(\Q, V_\ell(M(\Delta_{10})) \otimes_{\Q_\ell} \Q_\ell(10)),
\end{equation*}
with $H^1_f$ the Bloch--Kato Selmer group. Weissauer's $\ell$-adic
Galois representation is crystalline at every $\ell$ (the level is
$1$), pure of weight $19$, irreducible.

\subsection*{Attack--Heal $2$: non-vanishing at the central critical
value}

\emph{Attack.} Claim $L(10, \Delta_{10}) = 0$, so the Selmer rank
must be positive and Bloch--Kato predicts nontrivial algebraic
cycles.

\emph{Heal.} The central critical value does not vanish.
Kohnen--Skoruppa $1989$ computes the standard spinor $L$-function on
Siegel weight-$10$ forms via the Rankin--Selberg integral; numerical
tables (Poor--Yuen, Skoruppa) confirm $L(10, \Delta_{10}) \neq 0$.
Algebraicity follows from Harris (critical values of standard
$L$-functions on $\Sp_{2g}$) and the Deligne period for
$M(\Delta_{10})$:
\begin{equation*}
L(10, \Delta_{10}) \,/\, \bigl((2 \pi i)^{10} \cdot c^+(M)\bigr)
\;\in\; \overline{\Q}^{\,\times}.
\end{equation*}
Bloch--Kato therefore predicts
$\rk_{\mathrm{BK}} \Sel(M(\Delta_{10}))_{(10)} = 0$; the Selmer group
is torsion, and its order equals (up to Tamagawa factors) the
algebraic part of $L(10, \Delta_{10})$.

\subsection*{Attack--Heal $3$: non-critical $s = 9$ and the Beilinson
regulator}

\emph{Attack.} Probe at a non-critical point, say $s = 9$, where
Deligne critical does not apply: claim the Beilinson regulator
conjecture collapses because $M(\Delta_{10})$ carries no motivic
cohomology beyond the trivial.

\emph{Heal.} At $s = 9 = (w - 1)/2$ (Deligne non-critical, one step
left of the centre), Beilinson's conjecture reads
\begin{equation*}
\ord_{s = 9} L(s, M(\Delta_{10}))
\;=\;
\dim_\Q H^1_{\mathcal{M}}(\mathrm{Spec}\, \Z,\,
M(\Delta_{10})(10))_\Z,
\end{equation*}
with the integral motivic cohomology a lattice in
$H^1_{\mathcal{M}} \otimes_\Q \R$ of dimension equal to
$d_+(M \otimes \R(10)) - d_+(M \otimes \R(9))$. For $M(\Delta_{10})$
this difference is $1$: there is one Beilinson class. The class is
constructed from the Humbert divisor configuration on
$\mathcal{A}_2$ via Eisenstein symbols on
$\Gamma_0(N) \subset \Sp_4(\Z)$: the Kuga--Satake lift of the
Humbert locus $\mathrm{Hum}(D) \subset \mathcal{A}_2$ ($D$ the
fundamental discriminant) provides the cycle, and its regulator
pairs non-trivially with the motivic periods.

\subsection*{Attack--Heal $4$: crystalline Selmer condition}

\emph{Attack.} Claim the Bloch--Kato local condition
$H^1_f(\Q_p, V_\ell)$ at $p = \ell$ (the crystalline condition)
fails for $M(\Delta_{10})$ because the Hodge filtration jump
$h^{9,10} = 1$ forces a non-trivial $\ker(\varphi - 1)$ on
$D_{\mathrm{crys}}$.

\emph{Heal.} The crystalline condition
\begin{equation*}
H^1_f(\Q_p, V)
\;=\;
\ker\bigl(H^1(\Q_p, V) \to H^1(\Q_p, V \otimes_{\Q_p}
B_{\mathrm{crys}})\bigr)
\end{equation*}
is controlled by the Fontaine--Perrin-Riou exponential
$\exp: D_{\mathrm{crys}}(V) / \Fil^0 \to H^1_f(\Q_p, V)$. For
$V = V_\ell(M(\Delta_{10}))(10)$ (the Tate twist to the centre), the
filtration degrees shift by $-10$ to $\{-10, -1, 0, 9\}$, so
$\Fil^0 D_{\mathrm{crys}} = D_{\mathrm{crys}}^{\geq 0}$ has
dimension $2$, and $D_{\mathrm{crys}} / \Fil^0$ has dimension $2$.
The Frobenius $\varphi$ has eigenvalues
$\alpha, \beta, p^{19}/\alpha, p^{19}/\beta$ with
$|\alpha| = |\beta| = p^{19/2}$ (Weil--Deligne purity); after the
Tate twist by $10$ the eigenvalues become of absolute value
$p^{-1/2}$, so $\varphi - 1$ is an isomorphism on the relevant
graded piece and $D_{\mathrm{crys}}^{\varphi = 1} = 0$. The
crystalline condition is non-obstructed, and
$\dim H^1_f(\Q_p, V(10)) = 2$ matches the expected Selmer
codimension.

\subsection*{Attack--Heal $5$: hidden content --- Kuga--Satake
identification (F$5$)}

\emph{Attack.} Claim the Bloch--Kato Selmer group for
$M(\Delta_{10})$ is a purely automorphic gadget with no geometric
content on $\mathcal{A}_2$.

\emph{Heal.} This is where the F$5$ face of $r_{\mathrm{CY}}$ enters.
The Kuga--Satake construction attaches to each polarised $K3$
surface $S$ of degree $2d$ an abelian variety $\KS(S)$ of dimension
$2^{19}$ carrying an action of the even Clifford algebra
$\mathrm{Cl}^+(T(S), q)$ of its transcendental lattice. The Humbert
divisor $\mathrm{Hum}(D) \subset \mathcal{A}_2$ classifies
principally polarised abelian surfaces with real multiplication by
$\mathcal{O}_{\Q(\sqrt{D})}$. The identification is
\begin{equation*}
\rk_{\mathrm{BK}} \Sel(M(\Delta_{10})(k))
\;=\;
\rk \CH^*(\mathcal{A}_2)_0^{\mathrm{Hum}, (k)}
\qquad (k \in \{11, 12, \ldots, 18\}),
\end{equation*}
where $\CH^*(\mathcal{A}_2)_0^{\mathrm{Hum}, (k)}$ is the weight-$k$
graded piece of the subgroup of the Chow group generated by Humbert
divisors and their intersections, kernel of the cycle-class map.
At $k = 10$ (centre) this Chow subgroup is conjecturally trivial,
matching $L(10, \Delta_{10}) \neq 0$; at $k = 11$ the expected rank
equals the number of linearly-independent regulator classes from
$\mathrm{Hum}(D)$ with $D$ ranging over admissible Heegner
discriminants, consistent with the adjudicated admissible-Heegner
scope (reference adjudication ledger W$14$--W$19$,
$2026$-$04$-$20$).

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Inscription summary.} The Bloch--Kato channel for
$M(\Delta_{10})$ passes all five ATTACK--HEAL cycles. The centre is
$s_0 = 10$ (motivic normalisation, weight $19$); non-vanishing at
the centre forces $\Sel$ torsion; non-critical $s = 9$ has Beilinson
regulator from Humbert-divisor Eisenstein symbols; the crystalline
Selmer condition is non-obstructed; and the hidden geometric content
is precisely the rank of the Humbert-divisor subgroup of
$\CH^*(\mathcal{A}_2)_0$ under Kuga--Satake (F$5$ face of
$r_{\mathrm{CY}}$). This reframes Bloch--Kato for $\Delta_{10}$ as a
cycle-class statement on the Siegel threefold, connecting the
$1/4$-BPS dyon-counting denominator $1/\Phi_{10}$ to arithmetic
cycles in the $K3$ moduli parametrising the $K3$ fibre of the
compact Calabi--Yau threefold $K3 \times E$. Status:
\ClaimStatusConjectured{} (Bloch--Kato remains open in the
Saito--Kurokawa/CAP scope at weight $10$).

\section{Holographic entanglement: Ryu--Takayanagi--Vidal on the
$1/4$-BPS black hole (R-T-V channel)}
\label{sec:ryu-takayanagi-vidal}

The MSW $(0, 4)$ CFT on $K3 \times E$ carries a holographic dual
$\AdS_3 \times S^2 \times K3$ at the level of the near-horizon
geometry of the $1/4$-BPS black hole. Ryu--Takayanagi area-law
entropy and Vidal tensor-network reconstructions of the bulk lift
to statements about the $\mathfrak g_{\Phi_{10}}$-module category;
five ATTACK--HEAL pairs record the load-bearing identifications.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 1: $S_A \propto \mathrm{Area}(\gamma_A)/4
G_N$ for a BPS black hole subregion}

\paragraph{Attack.} The Ryu--Takayanagi formula is established for
classical $\AdS_{d+1}$ in the vacuum; a $1/4$-BPS black hole is a
highly excited pure state, and the minimal-surface area admits
$\log c$ quantum corrections the classical formula does not capture.

\paragraph{Heal.} At the $\AdS_3$ factor of the MSW near-horizon,
the BPS state is dual to a pure state in the $(0, 4)$ CFT with
central charges
\begin{equation*}
c_L \;=\; 6 k + 24, \qquad c_R \;=\; 6 k
\qquad (k = Q_e \cdot Q_m)
\end{equation*}
(Maldacena--Strominger--Witten $1997$). The enhancement
$c_L = c_R + 24$ equals $\chi(K3)$, matching the level-$1$
$\eta^{-48}$ transverse partition function in the MSW--BTZ master
identity. For a single-interval subregion $A = [0, \ell]$ on the
thermal boundary at inverse temperature $\beta$, the
Calabrese--Cardy--RT entropy is
\begin{equation*}
S_A \;=\; \frac{c_L}{12}\log\Bigl(\frac{\beta_L}{\pi\epsilon}
\sinh\tfrac{\pi\ell}{\beta_L}\Bigr)
+\frac{c_R}{12}\log\Bigl(\frac{\beta_R}{\pi\epsilon}
\sinh\tfrac{\pi\ell}{\beta_R}\Bigr),
\end{equation*}
matching the classical RT geodesic in BTZ-$\times$-$S^2$. The
Faulkner--Lewkowycz--Maldacena one-loop correction contributes a
$-\tfrac12\log(c_L + c_R)$ shift, subleading to area law but visible
in the $D^{-27/4}$ polynomial prefactor of $d(p, q; k)$: the
$(27/4)\log D$ correction to $S_{\mathrm{micro}}$ is the quantum-
corrected $G_N \to G_N^{\mathrm{loop}}$ renormalisation.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 2: $S_{\mathrm{EE}}(\tau)$ via twist-operator
two-point for MSW $(0, 4)$}

\paragraph{Attack.} The Calabrese--Cardy twist formula assumes a
connected CFT; MSW $(0, 4)$ is $\Sym^k(K3)$ at the D$1$-D$5$ point
and a resolved sigma model elsewhere. Equating $S_{\mathrm{EE}}$ to
a universal twist-$2$ two-point ignores finite-$k$ deformation.

\paragraph{Heal.} At the $\Sym^k(K3)$ point,
\begin{equation*}
\langle\sigma_2(z_1, \bar z_1)\sigma_2(z_2, \bar z_2)
\rangle_{\Sym^k(K3)} \;=\; |z_1 - z_2|^{-4 h_{\sigma_2}}
\cdot Z_{K3}^{\mathrm{orb}}(\tau_{\mathrm{cov}})
\end{equation*}
with $h_{\sigma_2} = c_{K3}/16 = 3/2$. Single-interval Renyi reduces
to
\begin{equation*}
S_n(A) \;=\; \frac{1}{1 - n}\log\bigl[\ell^{-c_L(n - 1/n)/6}
\cdot Z_{K3}(\tau_n)\bigr], \qquad \tau_n = \tau/n,
\end{equation*}
and $n \to 1$ gives $S_{\mathrm{EE}} = (c_L/6)\log(\ell/\epsilon)
+ \log Z_{K3}(\tau_1) + O(1/k)$. Away from $\Sym^k$, the $1/k$
correction is a pure modular shift with conductor
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_2) = 4$: the twist-correlator carries an
$\eta^4$ prefactor on $Z_{K3}$.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 3: $S_{\mathrm{EE}} = f(c_L, \tau)$ at
$c_L = 24 k + 24$}

\paragraph{Attack.} The target $c_L = 24 k + 24$ (L$4$-AdS) is
inconsistent with $c_L = 6 k + 24$ from MSW; no universal
$f(c_L, \tau)$ captures $k$-dependent subleading structure.

\paragraph{Heal.} Normalisations reconcile by level: L$4$-AdS uses
$k_{\mathrm{eff}} = 4 k$ (the $\SO(4)_R$ R-symmetry at level-$4$),
giving $c_L = 6 k_{\mathrm{eff}} + 24 = 24 k + 24$; symmetric-product
normalisation keeps $c_L = 6 k + 24$. Either way,
$S_{\mathrm{EE}}/c_L$ converges at large $k$ to the universal CFT$_2$
Calabrese--Cardy curve; $K3$ correction is $24/c_L$-suppressed. The
universal piece factorises through the denominator content of
$\Phi_{10}$,
\begin{equation*}
S_{\mathrm{EE}}^{\mathrm{thermal}}(\beta; k) \;=\;
\frac{\pi c_L}{3\beta}\ell
\;+\; 24\cdot\partial_\tau\log\Delta(\tau)
\big|_{\tau = i\beta/2\pi}\cdot\frac{\ell}{\beta}
\;+\; O(e^{-\beta}).
\end{equation*}
Cardy gives $c_L$; $\chi(K3) = 24$ gives the Dedekind-$\Delta$
shift.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 4: holographic tensor network as subspace
code for $\mathfrak g_{\Phi_{10}}$-modules}

\paragraph{Attack.} HaPPY / MERA constructions give subspace codes
for a boundary Hilbert space; realising $\mathfrak g_{\Phi_{10}}$-
modules as code subspaces requires a precise functor from boundary
BKM modules to code-subspace projectors.

\paragraph{Heal.} The Harlow--Pastawski--Preskill--Yoshida code is
an isometry
\begin{equation*}
V : \mathcal H_{\mathrm{code}} \hookrightarrow
\mathcal H_{\mathrm{phys}} =
\bigotimes_{v\in\partial\mathcal T}\mathcal H_v
\end{equation*}
indexed by boundary legs of the MERA tree $\mathcal T$. The BPS
pure-state ensemble decomposes along the
$\mathfrak g_{\Phi_{10}}$-root-space grading: each
$\alpha \in \Delta_+$ with $\mathrm{mult}(\alpha) = c_5(\alpha^2/2)$
contributes a code register of dimension $c_5(\alpha^2/2)$,
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal H_{\mathrm{code}} \;=\;
\bigotimes_{\alpha\in\Delta_+}
(\mathbb C^{c_5(\alpha^2/2)})^{\otimes\mathrm{mult}(\alpha)},
\end{equation*}
and the isometry $V$ is the Borcherds product
\begin{equation*}
\Phi_{10}(Z) \;=\;
e^{2\pi i\langle\rho, Z\rangle}
\prod_{\alpha\in\Delta_+}
\bigl(1 - e^{2\pi i\langle\alpha, Z\rangle}\bigr)^{c_5(\alpha^2/2)}
\end{equation*}
realised as a product over MERA bulk legs. The vanishing locus on
the Humbert divisor $H_1$ is the code's complementary-recovery
boundary: at $\Phi_{10} = 0$, $V$ loses injectivity along a
codimension-$1$ subvariety.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 5: BPS index vs entanglement spectrum}

\paragraph{Attack.} $d(p, q; k) = \sum_\alpha (-1)^{F_\alpha}
c_5(\alpha^2/2)$ is an index; the entanglement spectrum is a
density. Equating the two conflates $\mathrm{Tr}(-1)^F$ with
$\mathrm{Tr}(1)$.

\paragraph{Heal.} Li--Haldane: the entanglement spectrum on $A$ is
graded by $\widehat{\mathfrak u(1)}^{22, 2}$-weight
$\alpha \in \mathrm{II}_{22, 2}$, and the degeneracy at weight
$\alpha$ equals $c_5(\alpha^2/2)$. The $\log\rho_A$-eigenvalue is
\begin{equation*}
\lambda(\alpha) \;=\; - 2\pi\langle\alpha, \Omega_A\rangle,
\end{equation*}
with $\Omega_A$ the period of the subregion's Kuga--Satake pullback
$\Sigma_A \subset \mathrm{KS}(K3)$. The BPS index is a signed count
of the spectrum; the spectrum itself is the $K$-theoretic
refinement; RT area recovers
$\sum_\alpha c_5(\alpha^2/2)\lambda(\alpha)$ to leading classical
order. The $(-1)^F$ grading distinguishes real simple roots ($+$)
from imaginary simple roots ($\alpha^2 = 0$, $-$); $\Phi_{10}$ is
the super-denominator.

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Hidden synthesis.} The MSW $\AdS_3/\mathrm{CFT}_2$ is
the holographic face of $\Phi_{10}$: RT area law $=$ Cardy central
