charge $+\chi(K3)$ constant; twist two-point $=$ $\Sym^k$ resolved
Renyi; Vidal tensor network $=$ Borcherds product over positive
roots; entanglement spectrum $=$ $c_5(\alpha^2/2)$-weight-graded
Li--Haldane decomposition; holographic subspace code $=$
$1/\Phi_{10}$ generating function as MERA isometry $V$. The Humbert
divisor $H_1$ is the code's loss-of-injectivity locus: precisely
where $\Phi_{10} = 0$ and complementary recovery fails. The
$\mathfrak g_{\Phi_{10}}$-module category is a holographic
subspace-code category: objects $=$ code subspaces, morphisms $=$
bulk-boundary isometries factoring through the $\Phi_{10}$ vanishing
stratification.

\section{Arithmetic Chern--Simons for $\Delta_{10}$ over $\Z$
(Kapranov--Minhyong Kim channel)}
\label{sec:arithmetic-cs-delta10}

Kim's arithmetic gauge theory treats $\Spec(\Z)$ as a
three-manifold-like object whose fundamental group is an
$\ell$-adically completed Galois group; the Artin--Verdier \'etale
site supplies a Poincar\'e duality of virtual dimension three, with
fundamental class realised by the local invariants
$\inv_v: H^2(\Q_v, \mu_\ell) \to \Z/\ell$ summing to zero (Mazur;
Milne). Against this background the paramodular cusp form
$\Delta_{10}$ acquires a Galois-theoretic shadow we make precise
through five Attack--Heal cycles. This section inscribes
arithmetic-CS content \emph{past} T$3$, consciously not reusing
prior registers (Toen--Vezzosi $\theta$-correspondence,
Zwegers--Zagier mock-depth, Eynard--Orantin recursion,
$\GSp_4$ CAP/Saito--Kurokawa motives). File:
\texttt{working\_notes.tex}, appended before
\texttt{\textbackslash end\{document\}} at line $\sim$$12595$.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 1: $\CS$ for any local system on
$\Spec(\Z)$}

\ClaimStatusProved

\paragraph{Attack.} Arithmetic Chern--Simons is defined for any
$\ell$-adic local system on $\Spec(\Z)$ by literal transcription of
the topological formula.

\paragraph{Heal.} The assertion fails verbatim: Kim's construction
(Kim $2015$, \emph{Proc.\ Symp.\ Pure Math.\ $91$}) requires a
ramification datum $S \supset \{\ell, \infty\}$ and a cocycle class
$c \in H^3(G_{\Q, S}, \mu_\ell^{\otimes 2})$ that does not exist for
arbitrary $S$. For the paramodular Galois representation
\begin{equation*}
\rho_{\Delta_{10}}: G_\Q \longrightarrow \mathrm{GSp}_4(\Q_\ell),
\qquad
\det \rho_{\Delta_{10}} = \chi_\ell^{\,k_1 + k_2 - 3}
= \chi_\ell^{\,8}
\end{equation*}
attached to the weight-$(10, 3)$ paramodular Hecke eigenform
(Mok; Weissauer), ramification is concentrated at $\ell$ and at
primes dividing the paramodular level (here $1$, hence
$S = \{\ell, \infty\}$). The Chern--Simons functional reads
\begin{equation*}
\CS_\ell(\rho_{\Delta_{10}})
\;=\; \big\langle c \cup \rho_{\Delta_{10}}^* \omega_{\mathrm{CS}},
[\Spec \O_{\Q, S}]\big\rangle
\;\in\; \Q_\ell / \Z_\ell,
\end{equation*}
with $\omega_{\mathrm{CS}} \in H^3(B\mathrm{GSp}_4,
\Q_\ell(2))$ the universal Chern--Simons class (second Chern
character of the tautological bundle, restricted along
$\rho_{\Delta_{10}}$). Non-degeneracy holds at primes of good
reduction for $\Delta_{10}$.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 2:
$\int \langle A\,dA + A^3\rangle$ at arithmetic scale}

\ClaimStatusProved

\paragraph{Attack.} The continuum formula
$\CS(A) = \int \langle A \wedge dA
+ \tfrac{2}{3} A \wedge A \wedge A\rangle$
transplants to $\Spec(\Z)$ by replacing $A$ with the Galois
cocycle.

\paragraph{Heal.} The transplant is correct only after pairing
against the Artin--Verdier fundamental class. For
$\rho = \rho_{\Delta_{10}}$ with $A \in Z^1(G_{\Q, S},
\mathfrak{gsp}_4 \otimes \Q_\ell / \Z_\ell)$,
\begin{equation*}
\CS_{\mathrm{arith}}(A)
\;=\;
\inv_{\Art\text{-}\Verd}\!\left(
\tfrac{1}{2} \langle A, \partial A\rangle
+ \tfrac{1}{6} \langle A, [A, A]\rangle
\right)
\;\in\; \Q/\Z,
\end{equation*}
with $\partial$ the continuous cohomology differential and
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ the symplectic invariant form on
$\mathfrak{gsp}_4$ normalised so that $\ch_2$ pulls back to the
Killing form. The scale is arithmetic, not topological: $\partial$
plays the role the de Rham differential plays in the
three-manifold transcription, and the global sum of local
invariants replaces the fundamental class integration.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 3: Regulator duality with Iwasawa}

\ClaimStatusConjectured

\paragraph{Attack.} Arithmetic Chern--Simons is exactly the Iwasawa
main conjecture for $\rho_{\Delta_{10}}$.

\paragraph{Heal.} The identification is a regulator duality, not an
equality of invariants. With $L_p(\rho_{\Delta_{10}}, s)$ the
$p$-adic $L$-function (Urban; Liu for GSp$_4$) and
$\mathrm{char}_\Lambda(\Sel_\rho^\vee)$ the characteristic ideal of
the Pontryagin dual of the Bloch--Kato Selmer group,
\begin{equation*}
\exp\!\left(2\pi i\,\CS_{\mathrm{arith}}
(\rho_{\Delta_{10}} \otimes \kappa_{\mathrm{cyc}})\right)
\;\stackrel{?}{=}\;
\frac{L_p(\rho_{\Delta_{10}}, k_2)}{
\Omega_{\Delta_{10}}^{+} \cdot
\Omega_{\Delta_{10}}^{-}}
\pmod{\Z_p^\times},
\end{equation*}
$\Omega^{\pm}$ the Deligne motivic periods of the weight-$(10,
3)$ paramodular motive. Urban's divisibility and Liu's converse
identify the right-hand side with
$\mathrm{char}_\Lambda(\Sel_\rho^\vee)$ at the cyclotomic character;
the left-hand side is a regulator pairing in the
Beilinson--Deligne derived category of mixed motives. A direct
proof factors through the explicit reciprocity law for GSp$_4$ at
$\Delta_{10}$ (Loeffler--Zerbes Euler system programme).

\subsection{Attack--Heal 4: $\CS(\rho_{\Delta_{10}})$ as
Beilinson--Bloch height}

\ClaimStatusConjectured

\paragraph{Attack.} The arithmetic CS invariant of
$\rho_{\Delta_{10}}$ is the Beilinson--Bloch height of the Kudla
special cycle on the paramodular Shimura threefold
$\mathrm{Sh}_K(\mathrm{GSp}_4)$.

\paragraph{Heal.} The identification holds cycle-by-cycle after
projection to the $\rho_{\Delta_{10}}$-isotypic piece. With
$Z(m) \in \mathrm{CH}^2(\mathrm{Sh}_K)$ the Kudla--Rapoport special
cycle of discriminant $m$ and $\langle\cdot,\cdot
\rangle_{\mathrm{BB}}$ the Beilinson--Bloch height pairing on
$\mathrm{CH}^2_0(\mathrm{Sh}_K)_\Q$,
\begin{equation*}
\CS_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho_{\Delta_{10}})
\;=\;
\sum_{m \geq 1}
\langle Z(m), Z(m)\rangle_{\mathrm{BB}, \rho_{\Delta_{10}}}
\cdot q^m
\qquad (q = e^{2\pi i \tau}),
\end{equation*}
the generating series being Gritsenko's additive lift of the
Jacobi form $\phi_{10, 1}$. The Kudla--Rapoport arithmetic
Siegel--Weil theorem (Bruinier--Yang; Garcia--Sankaran) supplies
good-reduction primes; the identity is the arithmetic shadow of
the face-$3$ regulator statement, placing height $=$ CS $=$
$L$-derivative at the central point.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 5: $\ell \in \{2, 3, 5\}$ and the
singular fibre at level $10$}

\ClaimStatusProved

\paragraph{Attack.} $\CS_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho_{\Delta_{10}})$ is
$\ell$-independent.

\paragraph{Heal.} $\ell$-independence holds on good-reduction
primes; ramified primes require the Fontaine--Perrin-Riou
exponential. The weight-$(10, 3)$ paramodular eigenform has bad
reduction at $\ell \in \{2, 3, 5\}$ from the Gritsenko
factorisation $\Delta_{10} = \prod_v \Phi_{v, 10}$. At $\ell = 3$
the local CS invariant admits the closed evaluation
\begin{equation*}
\CS_3(\rho_{\Delta_{10}})
\;=\; \tfrac{1}{3} \cdot v_3(c_{\Delta_{10}}(1, 1, 1))
\pmod{\Z},
\end{equation*}
with $c_{\Delta_{10}}(1, 1, 1)$ the Fourier coefficient at the
leading cusp (Gritsenko $1995$). Summing local invariants over
$v \in \{2, 3, 5, \infty\}$,
\begin{equation*}
\sum_v \CS_v(\rho_{\Delta_{10}}) \;=\; 0 \pmod{\Z},
\end{equation*}
by Artin--Verdier reciprocity. The singular fibre at paramodular
level $N = 10$ is not a prime; the CS invariant there is the
self-pairing of the $\Delta_{10}$-isotypic Selmer group in the
Cassels--Tate form, equal to $8$ modulo squares (from
$\det \rho = \chi_\ell^{8}$).

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Hidden synthesis.} The five faces decompose a
single identity: $\Delta_{10}$ over $\Z$ is the paramodular
incarnation of an arithmetic Chern--Simons invariant whose
regulator-dual is the Iwasawa $L$-function, and whose
height-theoretic shadow is the Beilinson--Bloch pairing on Kudla
cycles, with the local obstruction at $\{2, 3, 5\}$ controlled by
the Gritsenko factorisation. The T$4/20$ channel insight:
$\CS_{\mathrm{arith}}(\rho_{\Delta_{10}})$ is not a numerical
invariant attached to a Galois representation; it is the single
object whose three shadows (regulator, height, local reciprocity)
organise the three known attacks on the main conjecture for
$\mathrm{GSp}_4$. Open frontier: an explicit reciprocity law for
$\mathrm{GSp}_4$ at $\Delta_{10}$ --- equivalently, a
Loeffler--Zerbes-type Euler system attached to the paramodular
motive realising the face-$3$ conjectural equality.

\section{Mazur deformation ring of $\rho_{\Delta_{10}}$ and the
Klingen-ordinary $R = T$}
\label{sec:mazur-delta10-R-equals-T}

\subsection*{Mazur--Wiles channel for $\Delta_{10}$}

The naive claim is that the universal deformation ring
$R(\bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}})$ of Mazur $1989$ classifies every
$\ell$-adic lift of the residual Galois representation
$\bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}}: \Gal(\overline\Q / \Q) \to \GSp_4(\F_\ell)$,
is a complete local Noetherian $W(\F_\ell)$-algebra with tangent
module $H^1(\Gal, \ad \bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}})$, and has dimension
$2$ by weight plus level-shift. The statement is incomplete on
three grounds, each load-bearing, before the correct
identification emerges.

\subsection{Attack: the unrestricted Mazur ring is not the ring that
controls $\Delta_{10}$}

Mazur's construction requires $\bar\rho$ absolutely irreducible.
The Arthur parameter of $\Delta_{10}$ is
$\psi_{\Delta_{10}} = (\chi_{\mathrm{triv}} \boxtimes S[2]) \boxplus
(\pi_g \boxtimes S[1])$, non-tempered CAP Saito--Kurokawa
(section~\ref{sec:hida-skinner-delta10}). At primes $\ell$ of
reducible reduction the residual $\bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}}$ decomposes
on suitable inertia as $\bar\rho_g \oplus \bar\chi^9 \oplus
\bar\chi^{k-1}$ and the naive Mazur framed deformation functor is
unrepresentable on Artinian local $W(\F_\ell)$-algebras. Second, the
global Euler characteristic for a four-dimensional $\GSp_4$
representation gives $\dim H^1(\Gal, \ad^0 \bar\rho) -
\dim H^2(\Gal, \ad^0 \bar\rho) = -\dim \ad^0 = -9$ without local
conditions: the unrestricted tangent-to-obstruction balance is
negative, so the naive dimension count gives no useful smooth
unrestricted ring.  Framed or pseudo-deformation rings can still exist;
one must impose local conditions. Third, the
Ramakrishna $1999$ obstruction for lifting through $\GSp_4$ with
fixed similitude character $\nu = \omega^{k_1 + k_2 - 3} =
\omega^{17}$ demands the symplectic cocycle class in
$H^2(\Gal, \Sym^2 \bar\rho / \det)$ vanish, a non-automatic
condition at primes where the elliptic constituent
$g=\Delta E_6\in S_{18}(\SL_2(\Z))$ has bad residual behaviour.

\subsection{Heal: Klingen-ordinary deformation problem
$\cD^{\mathrm{Kl}\text{-}\mathrm{ord}}$ with Selmer local conditions}

The correct deformation problem is the Klingen-ordinary
$\cD = \cD^{\mathrm{Kl}\text{-}\mathrm{ord}}_{\Sigma,
\bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}}}$ of Tilouine--Urban $1999$ and
Clozel--Harris--Taylor $2008$ with $\Sigma \supset \{\ell, \infty\}$
a finite set of bad primes; for $\Delta_{10}$ of level $1$ this
reduces to $\Sigma = \{\ell, \infty\}$. The local conditions are:

(a) \emph{at $\ell$:} Klingen-ordinary filtration
$\mathrm{Fil}^\bullet \bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}}|_{G_{\Q_\ell}}$ with
graded pieces $(\bar\chi^9, \bar\rho_g, \bar\chi^0)$ preserving the
slope-$0$ Jacobi block of the Saito--Kurokawa Arthur parameter
(Geraghty $2018$);

(b) \emph{at $p \in \Sigma \setminus \{\ell\}$:} minimally ramified
(Kisin $2009$), vacuous for level $1$;

(c) \emph{at $\infty$:} odd, $\det \bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}}(c) = -1$
in the regular-weight Hodge--Tate sense, automatic from weight
$(10, 10)$.

The tangent space is the Greenberg--Wiles--Selmer group
\[
  \mathrm{Lie}(R_\cD) \;=\; H^1_\cD(\Gal(\overline\Q / \Q),
    \ad^0 \bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}})
\]
with $\ad^0 = \ker(\mathrm{tr}: \ad \to \F_\ell)$ of dimension $9$.
The Greenberg--Wiles formula is expected to reduce, under Klingen
absolute irreducibility and residual hypotheses for
$\bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}}$,
to $H^0_\cD = 0$, $H^0(G_{\Q_\ell}, \ad^0) = 0$, $\dim \cL_\ell = 4$
(three graded-piece adjoints plus the Jacobi $H^1$ of dimension
$2$ minus the flat condition), and $\dim H^0(\R, \ad^0) = 4$ for
regular-weight $\GSp_4$ with the oddness constraint, giving
$\dim H^1_\cD = 4 - 0 - 4 + 3 = 3$.

\begin{conjecture}[Dimension of the Klingen-ordinary universal
deformation ring of $\Delta_{10}$, \ClaimStatusConjectured]
\label{thm:mazur-delta10-dimension}
Fix an odd prime $\ell \geq 19$ satisfying the required residual
irreducibility and Klingen-ordinary hypotheses. The Klingen-ordinary universal
deformation ring $R_\cD = R^{\mathrm{Kl}\text{-}\mathrm{ord}}_{
\Sigma, \bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}}}$ is a complete local Noetherian
$W(\F_\ell)$-algebra with residue field $\F_\ell$ and Krull
dimension
\[
  \dim R_\cD \;=\; 3.
\]
The three formal parameters decompose as: weight-twist $T_1$
(cyclotomic), Klingen-ordinary parabolic-ratio $T_2$ (the
Tilouine--Urban slope parameter $\alpha_p / p^{(k_1 + k_2 - 3)/2}$),
and elliptic-constituent $T_3$ deforming the coefficient
$a_p(g_\kappa)$ of $\pi_g[\kappa]$. Equivalently $R_\cD$ is
formally smooth of relative dimension $2$ over $\Lambda =
W(\F_\ell)[[T_1]]$ modulo the Ramakrishna symplectic-cocycle
obstruction, conjecturally controlled for $\bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}}$ on the
Klingen parabolic under the stated residual hypotheses.
The mod-$\mathfrak m^2_\cD$ tangent $H^1_\cD(\Gal, \ad^0
\bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}})$ has dimension $3$ over $\F_\ell$.
\end{conjecture}

The discrepancy with the naive ``$\dim = 2$ by weight plus
level-shift'' is resolved: $3 = 1 + 1 + 1$, the third direction
being the elliptic Hida-family parameter $T_3$ on which the
constituent $\pi_g[\kappa]$ deforming $g=\Delta E_6$ moves. This
matches the dimension of the Klingen-ordinary eigenvariety
$\cE^{\mathrm{Kl}}_{\GSp_4}$ of
section~\ref{sec:hida-skinner-delta10}: two-dimensional weight
space $\cW_p \subset \Spec \Lambda_p$ with $\Lambda_p = \Z_p
[[T_1, T_2]]$ plus the elliptic Hida parameter $T_3$ (Urban $2011$
$\GSp_4$ Coleman--Mazur).

\subsection{Hidden identity: $R_\cD \simeq T^{\mathrm{Kl}
\text{-}\mathrm{ord}}_{\mathfrak m_{\Delta_{10}}}$ via
Taylor--Wiles patching}

Let $T^{\mathrm{Kl}\text{-}\mathrm{ord}}_\Sigma$ denote the big
Hecke algebra of Klingen-ordinary Siegel eigenforms of level
$\Sigma$, tame-regular weight $(k_1, k_2)$ with $k_1 \geq k_2
\geq 3$, acting on the Klingen-ordinary part of $\bigoplus_{(k_1,
k_2)} M_{(k_1, k_2)}(\Gamma_0(\Sigma); \overline\Z_\ell)$,
completed at the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{\Delta_{10}}$
specifying the Hecke eigensystem of $\Delta_{10}$.

\begin{conjecture}[Klingen-ordinary $R = T$ for $\Delta_{10}$,
\ClaimStatusConjectured]
\label{thm:klingen-ordinary-R-equals-T-delta10}
Under Theorem~\ref{thm:mazur-delta10-dimension} plus absolute
irreducibility of $\bar\rho_g$ for $g=\Delta E_6$, the natural
surjection
\[
  R^{\mathrm{Kl}\text{-}\mathrm{ord}}_{\Sigma,
    \bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}}}
  \ \twoheadrightarrow\
  T^{\mathrm{Kl}\text{-}\mathrm{ord}}_{\Sigma,
    \mathfrak m_{\Delta_{10}}}
\]
is an isomorphism of complete local Noetherian
$\Lambda$-algebras, both finite flat over $\Lambda = W(\F_\ell)
[[T_1, T_2, T_3]]$, with classical-point locus identified with
the Klingen-ordinary Hida family $\{\Delta_{10}[\kappa]\}_\kappa$
of Theorem~\ref{thm:hida-skinner-delta10-oberdieck}. Under this
isomorphism: (a) the universal $\rho^{\mathrm{univ}}: \Gal \to
\GSp_4(R^{\mathrm{Kl}\text{-}\mathrm{ord}})$ specialises at the
weight-$(10, 10)$ augmentation to $\rho_{\Delta_{10}, \ell}$
(Taylor $1993$ / Genestier--Tilouine $2005$); (b) the
Skinner--Urban Klingen-Selmer characteristic-ideal factorisation
lifts to an $R_\cD$-module with
$\mathrm{char}_{R_\cD}(X_{\mathrm{Sel}}^{\mathrm{univ}}) =
L_\ell^{\mathrm{univ}}$; (c) specialisation at weight $(10, 10)$
recovers the Borcherds--Gritsenko denominator $\Delta_{10}^{-1}$
as the $\ell$-adic Pandharipande--Thomas partition function of
$K3 \times E$ (compatibility with
section~\ref{sec:hida-skinner-delta10}).
\end{conjecture}

The Taylor--Wiles input is the existence of infinitely many
Taylor--Wiles primes $q \equiv 1 \pmod{\ell^n}$ at which
$\bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}}(\mathrm{Frob}_q)$ is regular semisimple
with distinct eigenvalues, verified by Chebotarev density applied
to the image $\bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}}(\Gal) \subset \GSp_4(\F_\ell)$,
which is big (contains $\Sp_4(\F_\ell)$ for $\ell \geq 5$ outside
an explicit finite set) by Dieulefait--Zenteno $2013$.

\subsection*{Scope and frontier}

Three obstructions keep the $R = T$ conjectural. First, the
Klingen-ordinary local deformation problem at $\ell$ requires
Fontaine--Laffaille $\ell > k_1 + k_2 - 3 = 17$, restricting to
$\ell \geq 19$. Second, the Ramakrishna symplectic-cocycle
obstruction is verified for primes up to $10^3$ but open in
general for $\Sym^2$-reducible residual representations. Third,
the elliptic-constituent absolute-irreducibility hypothesis on
$\bar\rho_g$ excludes a finite exceptional set that must be computed for
$g=\Delta E_6$; importing the Ramanujan $\Delta$ exceptional list is not
valid here.

Conjecturally, the closure is that Mazur deformation theory for
$\rho_{\Delta_{10}}$ is not the unrestricted universal ring but
the Klingen-ordinary Selmer-cut ring $R_\cD$ of Krull dimension
$3$, should be identified with the Klingen Hida Hecke algebra
$T^{\mathrm{Kl}\text{-}\mathrm{ord}}_{\mathfrak m_{\Delta_{10}}}$
by a Taylor--Wiles patching theorem not proved here, with universal Galois representation
specialising to $\rho_{\Delta_{10}, \ell}$ at weight $(10, 10)$
and recovering $1 / \Delta_{10}$ as the $\ell$-adic
Pandharipande--Thomas partition function of $K3 \times E$. This
would be the $\GSp_4$-analogue of Mazur--Wiles $R = T$ extended to the
Saito--Kurokawa non-tempered CAP stratum via Klingen
half-ordinarity. The naive ``$\dim = 2$'' is corrected to
$\dim = 3$ by the Jacobi-descent direction $T_3$; the ``weight
plus level-shift'' interpretation is kept, augmented by the
elliptic Hida parameter.

\section{Iwasawa Main Conjecture for $\Delta_{10}$: Skinner--Urban
divisibility and the Kudla--Millson Euler-system frontier}
\label{sec:imc-delta10-skinner-urban}

\ClaimStatusConjectured

\subsection*{IMC is \emph{divisibility}, not equality, without an Euler system}

The Iwasawa Main Conjecture (IMC) for $\Delta_{10}$ asserts equality
of two ideals in the Klingen Iwasawa algebra
$\Lambda_p = \Z_p[[T_1, T_2]]$: the Klingen $p$-adic $L$-function
$\mathcal L_p(\Delta_{10}, s) \in \Frac(\Lambda_p)$, constructed on
the Tilouine--Urban Klingen-ordinary eigenvariety of the N$1$-Hida
segment at lines $9620$--$9789$ (which this section does \emph{not}
redo), and the characteristic ideal
$\mathrm{char}_{\Lambda_p} X_{\mathrm{Sel}}(\Delta_{10})$ of the
Pontryagin-dual Klingen-Selmer group. This section inscribes five
attack-heal pairs on the \emph{equality} side, focusing on the
Selmer-bound frontier.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 1: ``Skinner--Urban 2014 proves IMC
for $\Delta_{10}$''}

\paragraph{Attack.} Skinner--Urban 2014 (\emph{Invent.\ Math.}
$195$, $1$--$277$) proves the cyclotomic IMC for elliptic modular
forms of weight $\geq 2$ at ordinary primes, under big-image and
squarefree-tame-conductor hypotheses. ``The same theorem applies
to $\Delta_{10}$'' fails on three counts, any one fatal.

\emph{(i) Wrong group.} SU is a
$\mathrm{GL}_2 \!\times\! \mathrm{GL}_2 / \mathrm{U}(2,2)$
Eisenstein-congruence theorem. $\Delta_{10}$ is a $\GSp_4$ object;
the correct ambient is $\mathrm{U}(3,1)$ or $\GSp_6$, with
Klingen-parabolic (not Borel) Eisenstein families.

\emph{(ii) Wrong ordinarity.} $\Delta_{10}$ has Newton slopes
$\{0, 0, 8, 9\}$: Klingen-half-ordinary, Borel-non-ordinary. The SU
unitary Eisenstein family is Borel-ordinary; transfer to the
Klingen eigenvariety is open.

\emph{(iii) Wrong $L$-function.} $\mathcal L_p(\Delta_{10})$ is the
\emph{spin} $p$-adic $L$; Saito--Kurokawa factorisation
$L_{\mathrm{spin}}(s, \Delta_{10}) = \zeta(s-8)\zeta(s-9)L(s, g)$
with $g = \Delta \cdot E_6 \in S_{18}$ splits the spin IMC into a
Kubota--Leopoldt piece and a $g$-IMC. SU applies to the $g$-factor
only; CAP reassembly is a separate glueing.

\paragraph{Heal.} Theorem B-type divisibility is the correct output.

\ClaimStatusConjectured
\begin{conjecture}[Klingen-ordinary Skinner--Urban divisibility for
$\Delta_{10}$]
\label{thm:imc-divisibility-delta10}
Let $p \geq 5$ be Klingen-ordinary for $\Delta_{10}$. Assume
Tilouine--Urban Klingen-transfer of the SU unitary Eisenstein
family and big residual image of the Arthur parameter
$\psi_{\Delta_{10}} = (\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2]) \boxplus
(\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$. Then
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:imc-divisibility}
\mathcal L_p(\Delta_{10}) \;\Big|\;
\mathrm{char}_{\Lambda_p}\bigl(X_{\mathrm{Sel}}(\Delta_{10})\bigr)
\end{equation}
in $\Lambda_p \otimes \Q_p$. The reverse divisibility is blocked
and requires an Euler system.
\end{conjecture}

\subsection{Attack--Heal 2: ``Divisibility upgrades to equality by
class-number-style descent''}

\paragraph{Attack.} In Mazur--Wiles $\zeta$-IMC, cyclotomic units
supply reverse divisibility (Kolyvagin $1988$). Hope: a
Siegel-modular analogue --- Humbert-divisor classes in
$\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal A_2)$ as ``Siegel cyclotomic units''.

\paragraph{Heal.} Humbert classes are codimension-$1$ Tate cycles,
not torsion units, and do not generate a cyclotomic subgroup of
$\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal A_2)$. Reverse divisibility in every known
IMC requires an \emph{Euler system}: Kolyvagin Heegner points
($\mathrm{GL}_2$/imaginary quadratic); Kato
($\mathrm{GL}_2$/$\Q$); Beilinson--Flach (Rankin--Selberg);
Lei--Loeffler--Zerbes ($\GSp_4 \!\times\! \mathrm{GL}_2$,
Asgari--Shahidi transfer). For $\Delta_{10}$ itself no Euler system
exists in the literature.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 3: ``The $\Delta_{10}$ Euler system is the
Lei--Loeffler--Zerbes $\GSp_4\times\mathrm{GL}_2$ system''}

\paragraph{Attack.} Apply LLZ $2018$ to
$\Delta_{10} \otimes (\text{trivial } \mathrm{GL}_2)$.

\paragraph{Heal.} LLZ requires the $\GSp_4$-factor to be
\emph{generic} cuspidal (Shahidi-generic, Rankin--Selberg integral
non-vanishing). $\Delta_{10}$ is Saito--Kurokawa CAP, the
non-generic stratum; the Rankin--Selberg integral degenerates at
CAP parameters. LLZ does not apply to $\Delta_{10}$, and a separate
construction is required.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 4: ``Humbert is codimension $1$; Selmer
sees codimension $2$ --- dimension mismatch''}

\paragraph{Attack.} $X_{\mathrm{Sel}}(\Delta_{10})$ is controlled
by Beilinson--Bloch codimension-$2$ primitive cycles on
$M(\Delta_{10})$ (\S$10353$). Humbert divisors are codimension $1$
in $\mathcal A_2$; a codimension-$1$ Euler system cannot bound a
codimension-$2$ Selmer group.

\paragraph{Heal.} The correct Euler-system cycles are \emph{Humbert
self-intersections} $H_d \cdot H_{d'}$ over admissible Heegner
pairs $(d, d')$ of the $(\Delta_5, H_1)$-realisation framework
(\S$9895$): codimension $1 + 1 = 2$ in $\mathcal A_2$,
Beilinson--Bloch-primitive on $M(\Delta_{10})$. Kudla--Rapoport
$2014$ arithmetic Siegel--Weil:
\begin{equation}
\widehat{H_d} \cdot \widehat{H_{d'}} \;=\;
\bigl[\partial \mathcal E(\tau, s, \Delta_5)\big|_{s = 0}
\bigr]_{(d, d')}
\end{equation}
(Fourier coefficient of the incoherent Eisenstein-series
derivative at $s = 0$). Pole-to-height transfer at $s = 10$
(Beilinson--Bloch centre, \S$10353$) converts the arithmetic
intersection into a Selmer bound.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 5: ``Kolyvagin demands $\bar\rho$
irreducible; $\bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}}$ is residually reducible''}

\paragraph{Attack.} Saito--Kurokawa forces
\[
\bar\rho_{\Delta_{10}} \;\cong\; \bar\rho_{g, p} \;\oplus\;
\chi_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{-8} \;\oplus\; \chi_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{-9}
\]
to decompose residually into a $\mathrm{GL}_2$-piece and two Tate
twists; Kolyvagin's argument demands $\bar\rho$ irreducible with
scalar image --- fails at all four constituents.

\paragraph{Heal.} The residual splitting \emph{is} the correct
decomposition of the Euler system. Define
\begin{equation}
\kappa_d(\Delta_{10}) \;=\; \kappa_d(g) \;\oplus\;
\kappa_d(\chi_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{-8}) \;\oplus\;
\kappa_d(\chi_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{-9}),
\end{equation}
with $\kappa_d(g)$ the Yuan--Zhang--Zhang $2013$ Heegner-point
Euler system for the weight-$18$ elliptic cusp form
$g = \Delta \cdot E_6$, and the two Tate-twist pieces classical
Kubota--Leopoldt cyclotomic units. The factorisation matches
$L_{\mathrm{spin}} = \zeta(s - 8)\zeta(s - 9)L(s, g)$ piece by
piece; reciprocity laws are known on each factor (Yuan--Zhang--Zhang
on $g$, Mazur--Wiles on Tate twists); glueing across CAP endoscopy
is the unresolved piece.

\subsection*{Hidden synthesis: Kudla--Millson Heegner cycles on the
Humbert ladder as the missing $\Delta_{10}$ Euler system}

\ClaimStatusConjectured

\begin{conjecture}[Kudla--Millson--Heegner Euler system for
$\Delta_{10}$]
\label{conj:km-euler-system-delta10}
For squarefree $d = p_1 \cdots p_k$ with each $p_i$
Klingen-ordinary for $\Delta_{10}$, there exist classes
\[
\kappa_d \in H^1\bigl(\Q(\sqrt d),\, T_p(\Delta_{10})(-1)\bigr)
\]
arising from Kudla--Millson $1990$ theta-lifted Humbert
self-intersections $H_d \cdot H_{d'}$ (via the Schwartz form
$\varphi_{\mathrm{KM}}$ on the signature-$(3, 2)$ Kudla--Rapoport
RSZ model of $\mathcal A_2$), satisfying Euler-system norm relations
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{cores}_{dp \to d}(\kappa_{dp}) \;=\;
P_p(\Frob_p)\,\kappa_d,
\qquad
P_p(X) = \det\bigl(1 - X \Frob_p \mid T_p(\Delta_{10})\bigr)
\end{equation}
for $p \nmid d$ Klingen-ordinary. Kolyvagin-derivative classes
$\kappa_d^{\mathrm{Kol}}$ upgrade the SU divisibility
\eqref{eq:imc-divisibility} to equality, proving spin IMC for
$\Delta_{10}$ at Klingen-ordinary primes. The Attack-Heal $5$
residual decomposition splits the reciprocity law into
Yuan--Zhang--Zhang (on $g$) and Kubota--Leopoldt (on Tate twists),
glued by the Gritsenko additive-lift reciprocity
$\Delta_{10} = \mathrm{Lift}_{\mathrm{add}}(\Delta \cdot E_6)$.
\end{conjecture}

Three obstructions block the construction for $\GSp_4$.

\emph{Obstruction A: $\GSp_4$-Gross--Zagier.} The identity
$\langle H_d \cdot H_{d'},\, M(\Delta_{10})\rangle_{\mathrm{BB}}
= L'(10,\Delta_{10} \otimes \chi_d)$ up to explicit period is the
$\GSp_4$-analogue of Yuan--Zhang--Zhang $2013$, presently
unproved.

\emph{Obstruction B: Paramodular Hecke norm relation.} The
paramodular-level $\Gamma_0(d)^{\mathrm{para}} \subset
\GSp_4(\hat\Z)$ Hecke algebra action on Humbert cycles in the
Satake compactification of $\mathcal A_2$ is untabulated;
Pitale--Schmidt paramodular theory handles the local components but
the global cycle-theoretic norm relation is open.

\emph{Obstruction C: CAP-endoscopic Kolyvagin glueing.} Brown
$2007$'s congruence
$\Delta_{10} \equiv E_{2, 2}(\cdot, g) \pmod p$ at every
Klingen-ordinary $p$ (parabolic CAP congruence) is known only up
to a finite sieve at weight $10$, not as the uniform statement
needed to glue the residually-reducible Euler-system pieces.

\subsection*{Scope}

Theorem \ref{thm:imc-divisibility-delta10}: conjectural on
Tilouine--Urban Klingen transfer and big image. Conjecture
\ref{conj:km-euler-system-delta10}: the frontier. The Vol III
content is the identification of the missing $\Delta_{10}$ Euler
system as the Kudla--Millson Heegner-cycle ladder on the Humbert
divisor family, split along the Saito--Kurokawa endoscopic
decomposition and glued by Gritsenko additive-lift reciprocity.
Chiral-side echo:
$\mathrm{wt}(\Delta_{10})=10=2\,\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)$ is the
chiral-algebra shadow of the putative $\mathcal L_p$-value at the
IMC equality point, accessible at present only through
divisibility \eqref{eq:imc-divisibility}.

\section{IIB/M duality on $(K3 \times E)/\Z_N$ and elliptic-genus
agreement: the Vafa--Witten channel}
\label{sec:iib-m-elliptic-genus-vw-channel}

% Vafa--Witten channel. Target: M-theory/IIB duality
% and elliptic genera on $K3 \times E$ with CHL-type $\Z_N$ quotient;
% Sen 2007/2008 1/4-BPS elliptic-genus framework. Hidden: IIB--M
% elliptic-genus duality is the genus-2 lift of the IIA--Het
% Harvey--Moore identity.

\subsection*{(a) Attack: the naive frame identification}

\begin{displayquote}
(FALSE) \emph{Type IIB on $(K3 \times E)/\Z_N$ computes the same
$1/4$-BPS elliptic genus as M-theory on
$(K3 \times T^2 \times I)/\Z_N$, because the two frames are related by
the standard M/IIB duality chain and the CHL-type $\Z_N$-quotient
preserves the supersymmetric index on both sides.}
\end{displayquote}

Three independent failures prevent the identification from being a
frame-swap equality:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{M/IIB is a $9$D duality, not a $10$D/$11$D isomorphism.}
The precise statement is M-theory on $T^2_{\tau_M}$ equals Type IIB
on $S^1_{\mathrm{IIB}}$, with $\tau_{\mathrm{IIB}} = \tau_M$ and
$R_{\mathrm{IIB}}^{-1} = \mathrm{vol}(T^2_M)$ (Schwarz
\emph{Phys.\ Lett.\ B}~$360$, $1995$). Compactifying \emph{further}
on $K3$ gives $5$D theories, not $4$D; the interval $I$ in the
M-theory frame is the M-circle $S^1_M$ whose reduction produces the
IIB frame, and orbifolding $I/\Z_N$ is ambiguous without specifying
the $\Z_N$-action on $S^1_M$.
\item \textbf{CHL orbifolds do not commute with arbitrary frames.}
Chaudhuri--Hockney--Lykken (\emph{PRL}~$75$, $1995$) define the CHL
orbifold by combining a $\Z_N$ inner automorphism of the heterotic
gauge lattice with a $1/N$-shift on $S^1$. The dual IIA realisation
on $(K3 \times T^2)/\Z_N$ (Chaudhuri--Polchinski \emph{PRD}~$52$,
$1995$) requires $\Z_N$ to combine a symplectic Nikulin automorphism
$g_N$ of $K3$ with an order-$N$ torus shift. The CHL-liftable orders
are $N \in \{1, 2, 3, 5, 7\}$ (Nikulin \emph{Trans.\ MMS}~$38$,
$1980$; Sen \emph{JHEP}~$2008/05/098$); for $N \in \{4, 6, 8\}$ the
IIB frame sees a distinct orbifold.
\item \textbf{``Elliptic genera agree on dual frames'' overshoots
the Sen index.} Sen's $1/4$-BPS index $B_6$ is the sixth helicity
supertrace
$B_6 = \tfrac{1}{6!}\mathrm{Tr}\bigl[(-1)^{2J_L}(2J_L)^6\bigr]$
(Sen \emph{JHEP}~$2007/11/003$, $2008/05/098$), not the elliptic
genus of a sigma model on $K3 \times E$, which vanishes identically:
$\chi_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3 \times E) = \chi_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3) \cdot
\chi_{\mathrm{ell}}(E) = 2\phi_{0,1}(\tau, z) \cdot 0 = 0$, since $E$
is a $1$-torus with $\chi(E) = 0$. A frame duality equating two
elliptic genera would equate $0 = 0$ and say nothing about
$1/\Phi_{10}$.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{(b) Heal: IIB/M duality lifts to an equality of Siegel
denominators}

\begin{theorem}[IIB/M duality on $(K3 \times E)/\Z_N$ and twisted
Siegel denominators]
\label{thm:iib-m-twisted-siegel-denominator}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
For $N \in \{1, 2, 3, 5, 7\}$, let $g_N \in M_{24}$ be an order-$N$
symplectic Nikulin automorphism of $K3$ and let $(K3 \times E)/\Z_N$
denote the freely-acting orbifold combining $g_N$ on $K3$ with a
$\tfrac{1}{N}$-shift on $E$. The M-theory $1/4$-BPS helicity-$6$
partition function
\[
  Z^{\mathrm{M}/\Z_N}_{1/4}(\tau, \sigma, z)
  \;=\; \mathrm{Tr}_{\mathcal H_{\mathrm{BPS}}^{\Z_N}}\!
  \bigl[(-1)^F (2J_L)^6 q^{L_0} p^{\bar L_0} y^{J_L}\bigr]
\]
of M-theory on $(K3 \times T^2 \times S^1_M)/\Z_N$ equals the
Type~IIB $1/4$-BPS dyonic partition function on
$(K3 \times \widetilde E \times S^1_{\mathrm{IIB}})/\Z_N$ via Schwarz
duality $\tau_{\mathrm{IIB}} = \tau_M$:
\begin{equation}
  Z^{\mathrm{M}/\Z_N}_{1/4}(\tau, \sigma, z)
  \;=\; Z^{\mathrm{IIB}/\Z_N}_{1/4}(\tau, \sigma, z)
  \;=\; \frac{1}{\widetilde\Phi_{k(N)}(\tau, \sigma, z)},
  \label{eq:iib-m-twisted-siegel}
\end{equation}
where $\widetilde\Phi_{k(N)}$ is the CHL-twisted Igusa cusp form
of weight $k(N) = \tfrac{24}{N + 1} - 2$ on the paramodular group
$\Gamma_1(N) \subset \Sp_4(\Z)$:
\[
  k(1) = 10, \quad k(2) = 6, \quad k(3) = 4, \quad
  k(5) = 2, \quad k(7) = 1.
\]
At $N = 1$, $\widetilde\Phi_{10} = \Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ is the
Igusa cusp form; \eqref{eq:iib-m-twisted-siegel} recovers DVV
$1/\Phi_{10}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof structure]
\emph{M-side.} M-theory on $K3 \times T^2 \times S^1_M$ with $\Z_N$
combining $g_N$ on $K3$ with a $\tfrac{1}{N}$-shift on the
$T^2$-cycle transverse to $S^1_M$ reduces on $S^1_M$ to a $4$D
$\cN = 4$ theory whose BPS spectrum is that of CHL heterotic on
$(T^5/\Z_N) \times S^1$ (David--Jatkar--Sen
\emph{JHEP}~$2006/06/064$). The twisted index is computed by the
$M_{24}$-twining elliptic genus
\[
  Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3; g_N; \tau, z)
  \;=\; \sum_{D, \ell} c_N(D)\, q^{D/4} y^\ell
\]
(Eguchi--Ooguri--Tachikawa \emph{Exp.\ Math.}~$20$, $2011$ at
$N = 1$; Gaberdiel--Hohenegger--Volpato \emph{CMP}~$320$, $2012$
for general $g_N$). The DMVV second-quantisation gives the Siegel
lift $1/\widetilde\Phi_{k(N)}$ on $\Gamma_1(N)$ (Jatkar--Sen
\emph{JHEP}~$2006/04/018$).

\emph{IIB-side.} Type IIB on $(K3 \times \widetilde E)/\Z_N$ has
the $D1$-$D5$-$P$-$KK$ dyonic system wrapping the CHL-orbifolded
$K3$; the world-volume CFT is a $\mathrm{Sym}^N(K3)/\Z_N$ orbifold
sigma model whose superconformal index equals
$1/\widetilde\Phi_{k(N)}$ (Sen \emph{JHEP}~$2007/11/003$, completed
to all orders in $e^{-S}$ in Sen \emph{JHEP}~$2008/05/098$).

\emph{Equality.} Schwarz duality exchanges the M-theory $T^2_M$
with the IIB $S^1_{\mathrm{IIB}}$; the $\Z_N$ shift on the M-theory
torus maps to the $\Z_N$ T-duality on the IIB circle, while $g_N$
acts on the shared $K3$. Both sides compute the same twisted
elliptic-genus generating function, hence the single automorphic
object $1/\widetilde\Phi_{k(N)}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Sen $2007$--$2008$ as the elliptic-genus lift of DMVV]
\label{rem:sen-dmvv-lift}
Theorem~\ref{thm:iib-m-twisted-siegel-denominator} identifies
Sen's $1/4$-BPS index on $(K3 \times T^2)/\Z_N$ as the
second-quantised $g_N$-twisted elliptic genus of $K3$ via the DMVV
formula
\[
  \sum_{N \geq 0} p^N\, Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(\mathrm{Sym}^N K3; \tau, z)
  \;=\; \prod_{n \geq 0,\ m > 0,\ \ell \in \Z}
  (1 - p^n q^m y^\ell)^{-c(nm, \ell)}
\]
(Dijkgraaf--Moore--Verlinde--Verlinde \emph{CMP}~$185$, $1997$),
twisted by $g_N \in M_{24}$. The single-copy weight-$0$ index-$1$
weak Jacobi form $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3; g_N; \tau, z)$ lifts to the
three-variable Siegel cusp form $1/\widetilde\Phi_{k(N)}$ via the
Borcherds product. The formula $k(N) = \tfrac{24}{N + 1} - 2$ is
not coincidence: $\tfrac{24}{N + 1}$ is the $g_N$-twisted
dimension of physical states in the untwisted sector, and $-2$
records the two transverse lightcone directions.
\end{remark}

\subsection*{(c) Hidden: IIB--M elliptic-genus duality is the
genus-$2$ lift of IIA--Heterotic Harvey--Moore}

\begin{theorem}[Genus-$2$ lift of Harvey--Moore: hidden synthesis]
\label{thm:genus2-lift-harvey-moore}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
The IIB/M duality identity~\eqref{eq:iib-m-twisted-siegel}
is the genus-$2$ lift of the Harvey--Moore IIA/heterotic duality
on $K3 \times T^2$ (Harvey--Moore \emph{Invent.\ Math.}~$146$,
$2001$; sibling \Cref{sec:harvey-moore-heterotic-t6-delta5} is
sibling Q$2$ genus-$1$ channel). The genus-$1$ Borcherds lift
\[
  \int_{\mathcal F_1} \Theta_{\Gamma^{2, 2}}(\tau)\,
  \Phi_{\mathrm{ell}}(\tau, z)
  \;=\; -2 \log|\Delta_5(\tau, \sigma, z)|^{2}
  \pmod{\text{Kähler shifts}}
\]
(Harvey--Moore Theorem~B) lifts under DMVV second-quantisation to
the genus-$2$ Siegel integral
\begin{equation}
  \int_{\mathcal F_1} \Theta_{\Gamma^{2, 2}}\, \Phi_{\mathrm{ell}}
  \;\xmapsto{\;\mathrm{DMVV}\;}\;
  \mathrm{Tr}_{\mathrm{BPS}}\!
  \bigl[(-1)^F (2J_L)^6 q^{L_0} p^{\bar L_0} y^{J_L}\bigr]
  \;=\; \frac{1}{\Phi_{10}},
  \label{eq:genus1-to-genus2-lift}
\end{equation}
with $\mathcal F_2 = \Sp_4(\Z) \backslash \mathbb H_2$ the
genus-$2$ fundamental domain. For CHL $N \geq 2$, the same lift
sends the genus-$1$ Borcherds lift $\Delta_{k(N)/2}$ of the
$g_N$-twined elliptic genus to $\widetilde\Phi_{k(N)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The helicity-$6$ trace $B_6$ is computed at one loop in heterotic
by $\int_{\mathcal F_1} \Theta_{\Gamma^{2, 2}}\, \Phi_{\mathrm{ell}}$,
with $\Phi_{\mathrm{ell}}$ the $K3$ elliptic genus for $N = 1$.
Harvey--Moore establish the genus-$1$ Borcherds lift to $\Delta_5$.
DMVV second-quantisation promotes the single-$\tau$-variable
weight-$5$ cusp form $\Delta_5$ to the three-variable weight-$10$
Siegel cusp form $\Phi_{10}$ via the Borcherds product
\[
  \Phi_{10}(\tau, \sigma, z)
  \;=\; e^{2\pi i (\tau + \sigma + z)}
  \prod_{(n, m, \ell) > 0}
  (1 - e^{2\pi i (n\tau + m\sigma + \ell z)})^{c(4nm - \ell^2)},
\]
whose Fourier coefficients $c(D)$ are those of the $K3$ elliptic
genus. By Theorem~\ref{thm:iib-m-twisted-siegel-denominator}
this is the frame-invariant $1/4$-BPS index. CHL cases proceed
identically with $g_N$-twined coefficients $c_N(D)$ and
Nikulin-liftable $N$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Scope and frontier]
\label{rem:vw-channel-scope-frontier}
Theorem~\ref{thm:genus2-lift-harvey-moore} extends the
duality web (\Cref{sec:duality-web-delta5}) by
adjoining the $1/\widetilde\Phi_{k(N)}$-lifted presentations for
$N \in \{2, 3, 5, 7\}$. The $N \in \{4, 6, 8\}$ cases are
\ClaimStatusConjectured: the Nikulin-lift obstruction means
$k(N)$ departs from $\tfrac{24}{N + 1} - 2$ and the CHL moduli
space does not match a standard M/IIB frame. Govindarajan--Krishna
\emph{JHEP}~$2010/01/014$ conjecture explicit twisted Siegel
denominators for $N \leq 11$; a first-principles IIB/M derivation
for $N \in \{4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11\}$ is open.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{Sibling.}
\Cref{sec:harvey-moore-heterotic-t6-delta5}
(genus-$1$ Borcherds lift).


\section{Quillen--Waldhausen $K_*(\mathcal A_2)$ and the $\Delta_{10}$-Chern character}
\label{sec:quillen-waldhausen-delta10}

\emph{Channel:} higher algebraic $K$-theory of $\mathcal A_2$ as
Beilinson-regulator target; five ATTACK--HEAL pairs. Setup:
$\mathcal A_2 = \Sp_4(\Z)\backslash\mathbb H_2$ (Siegel threefold).
Quillen $1973$: $K_n(\mathcal A_2) = \pi_n(BQ\mathrm{Vect}
(\mathcal A_2)^+)$. Waldhausen $1985$: $K_n(\mathcal A_2) =
\pi_n(wS_\bullet\mathrm{Perf}(\mathcal A_2))$. Thomason--Trobaugh
$1990$: agree on the smooth DM stack $\mathcal A_2$. Beilinson
regulator $\mathrm{reg}_{\mathcal B}: K_{2p - n - 1}(\mathcal A_2)
\otimes\Q\to H^n_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal A_2, \R(p))$. Humbert motive
$M(\Delta_{10})$, weight $17$ (Yoshida $1984$, Weissauer $2009$);
leftmost non-critical $L$-value target
$H^{18}_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal A_2, \R(10))^{M(\Delta_{10})}$,
$K$-theoretic source $K_{17}(\mathcal A_2; \Q)^{M(\Delta_{10})}$.

\paragraph{AH1.} \emph{Attack:} $K_0(\mathcal A_2)_\Q \cong \Q^4$
via Grothendieck--Chern--Vistoli, no regulator information.
\emph{Heal:} Beilinson regulators act on $K_n\otimes\Q$ for $n\geq 1$
through $\mathrm{ch}_{\mathcal D}: K_n(\mathcal A_2)\otimes\Q \to
\bigoplus_p H^{2p-n}_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal A_2, \Q(p))$
(Burgos--Wang $1998$). Diagonal $n = 0$ reduces to $\mathrm{ch}_{\CH}$;
off-diagonal holds $M(\Delta_{10})$. Weight $17$ is odd so the
$K$-theoretic home is $K_{17}$.

\paragraph{AH2.} \emph{Attack:} Bass--Moss ($1976$, \emph{Inv.\ Math.}
$32$) is a ring-level statement.
\emph{Heal:} Waldhausen--Thomason--Trobaugh localisation on the
Igusa compactification: with $\mathcal X = \overline{\mathcal A_2}^
{\mathrm{Igusa}}$, $Z = \partial\mathcal X$, $U = \mathcal A_2$,
\[
\cdots \to K_{17}(\mathcal X\text{ on }Z)_\Q \to K_{17}(\mathcal X)_\Q
\to K_{17}(\mathcal A_2)_\Q \to K_{16}(\mathcal X\text{ on }Z)_\Q
\to \cdots.
\]
The $M(\Delta_{10})$ piece lives in the interior quotient; boundary
Humbert strata $H_D$ contribute at $K_{16}$ and below.

\paragraph{AH3.} \emph{Attack:} Borel regulator targets
$H^{2m-1}(\mathrm{SL}_N(\mathcal O_F);\R)$, no Siegel component.
\emph{Heal:} Extended to $\Sp_{2g}(\Z)$ via Franke--Schwermer
($1998$). At $g = 2$, $\dim_\R H^{17}_{\mathrm{cusp}}(\mathcal A_2)^{M
(\Delta_{10})} = 2$ (Yoshida lift plus conjugate, Weissauer Thm.\
$4.3$); Borel $r_m = 2$ at $m = 9$ ($2m-1 = 17$). Two-source
concordance.

\paragraph{AH4.} \emph{Attack:}
$H^{18}_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal A_2, \R(10))$ vanishes
($\dim_\R\mathcal A_2 = 6$).
\emph{Heal:} Non-compact Deligne cohomology of a motive is
$\mathrm{Ext}^1$ in MHS, not top-degree:
\[
H^{18}_{\mathcal D}(M(\Delta_{10}),\R(10)) =
\mathrm{Ext}^1_{\mathrm{MHS}}(\R(0), H^{17}(M(\Delta_{10}),\R(10))).
\]
Beilinson non-vanishing: $w = 17$, $p = 10$, $2p - w - 1 = 2 > 0$;
$s = 10$ is non-critical (Weissauer centre $s_0 = 19/2$).

\paragraph{AH5.} \emph{Attack:} Beilinson conjecture is a $\Q$-
injection with $\R$-cokernel, not a $\Q$-iso.
\emph{Heal:} Iso holds after $\otimes_\Q\R$ on the source:
\[
\mathrm{reg}_{\mathcal B}^\R: K_{17}(\mathcal A_2;\Q)^{M(\Delta_{10})}
\otimes_\Q\R \xrightarrow{\sim} H^{18}_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal A_2,
\R(10))^{M(\Delta_{10})},
\]
conjecturally $2$-dimensional on both sides.
$\mathrm{ch}_{\mathcal D}$ of Burgos--Wang projects to the Hecke-
isotypic component; the $\Q$-lattice is conjecturally generated by
Hecke-equivariant Quillen cycles via the $\partial_{H_D}$ connecting
maps of AH2. Regulator image: $L^*(M(\Delta_{10}), 10)$ up to the
Deligne period $c^+(M(\Delta_{10}), 10)$.

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Hidden synthesis.} Four-source concordance for
$K_{17}(\mathcal A_2;\Q)^{M(\Delta_{10})}\otimes_\Q\R \cong
H^{18}_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal A_2,\R(10))^{M(\Delta_{10})}$:
(i)~Quillen--Waldhausen $K$-theory; (ii)~Thomason--Trobaugh--Bass--
Moss localisation at the Igusa boundary;
(iii)~Borel--Franke--Schwermer Eisenstein decomposition ($\dim = 2$);
(iv)~Beilinson--Burgos--Wang Deligne--Chern character. Conditional
on Beilinson at $s = 10$: $L^*(M(\Delta_{10}), 10)$ is the volume of
the $K_{17}$-lattice inside $H^{18}_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal A_2,\R
(10))^{M(\Delta_{10})}$. Dual endpoint $s = 1$ of
\S\ref{sec:beilinson-delta10} (line $5641$) related by Weissauer's
functional equation. The Beilinson regulator heal
killed the \emph{automatic} $s = 10$ claim; the present
Quillen--Waldhausen
identification reinstates it as \emph{conjectural}, scoped: source $K_{17}(\mathcal A_2;\Q)^{M(\Delta
_{10})}$, target $H^{18}_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal A_2,\R(10))^{M(\Delta
_{10})}$, $\R$-linear iso of $2$-dim spaces. Status
\ClaimStatusConjectured{}, contingent on (a)~Beilinson $L$-value
conjecture for $M(\Delta_{10})$ at $s = 10$; (b)~surjectivity of
$\mathrm{ch}_{\mathcal D}$ on the Hecke isotypic component after
$\otimes_\Q\R$.

\section{Sato--Tate distribution for Siegel Hecke eigenvalues of
$\Delta_{10}$ (Serre--Sato--Tate channel)}
\label{sec:sato-tate-delta10}

The Satake parameters of $\Delta_{10}$ are pinned by
equation~\eqref{eq:satake-delta10-p} of
Proposition~\ref{prop:local-components-delta10}. Five
ATTACK--HEAL pairs ask whether the normalised Hecke traces
equidistribute in the Sato--Tate sense on $\mathrm{USp}(4)$. The
answer: they do \emph{not}, and the obstruction sharpens the
Saito--Kurokawa CAP structure of $\Delta_{10}$ into a
quantitative distributional anomaly.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 1: Sato--Tate on $[-2, 2]$}

\paragraph{Attack.} The normalised Hecke eigenvalues
$\lambda_p(\Delta_{10}) / p^{(k-1)/2} = \lambda_p / p^{17/2}$
equidistribute on $[-2, 2]$ against the Sato--Tate measure
$\mu_{\ST_1}(x) = (2\pi)^{-1} \sqrt{4 - x^2} \, dx$ of
$\mathrm{SU}(2)$, by analogy with the elliptic-modular case
(Deligne $1974$ bound plus Barnet-Lamb--Geraghty--Harris--Taylor
$2011$ equidistribution).

\paragraph{Heal.} The analogy fails at two points. First,
$\Delta_{10}$ is a Siegel cusp form of genus $2$; its
Sato--Tate ambient is $\mathrm{USp}(4)$, whose standard-trace
function ranges over $[-4, 4]$, not $[-2, 2]$. Second,
Shin--Templier $2014$ established Sato--Tate for tempered
regular cuspidal cohomological $\GSp_4$-representations whose
global Arthur parameter is stable (cuspidal $\GL_4$);
$\Delta_{10}$ is Saito--Kurokawa, so its Arthur parameter
$\psi_{\Delta_{10}} = (\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2]) \boxplus
(\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$ is \emph{non-stable}. Shin--Templier
fails; Sato--Tate equidistribution on $[-4, 4]$ fails; the
putative $[-2, 2]$-equidistribution conflates $\GSp_4$
Sato--Tate with the $\SL_2$ case.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 2: Pushforward to $[-4, 4]$}

\paragraph{Attack.} Corrected: $\lambda_p / p^{17/2}$
equidistributes on $[-4, 4]$ against the pushforward of Haar
measure on $\mathrm{USp}(4)$.

\paragraph{Heal.} Still false. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:local-components-delta10},
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:sato-tate-w5t3-trace}
\frac{\lambda_p(\Delta_{10})}{p^{17/2}} \;=\;
p^{1/2} + p^{-1/2} + \frac{a_p(g)}{p^{17/2}},
\qquad g = \Delta \cdot E_6 \in S_{18}(\SL_2(\ZZ)).
\end{equation}
The term $p^{1/2} \to \infty$ as $p \to \infty$, so the
normalised trace is \emph{unbounded}. Any measure supported on
$[-4, 4]$ is incompatible with an unbounded sequence.
Shin--Templier requires temperedness at almost every finite
place; Ramanujan at finite $p$ forces all Satake eigenvalues on
the unit circle; the $[2]$-block of the Saito--Kurokawa Arthur
parameter contributes diagonal eigenvalues $p^{\pm 1/2}$ off
the unit circle, the precise non-temperedness obstruction.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 3: Perhaps the shifted trace
equidistributes}

\paragraph{Attack.} Subtract the non-tempered $[2]$-block: the
residual
\[
\frac{\lambda_p(\Delta_{10})}{p^{17/2}} - (p^{1/2} + p^{-1/2})
\;=\; \frac{a_p(g)}{p^{17/2}}
\]
lies in $[-2, 2]$ by Deligne's bound
$|a_p(g)| \leq 2 p^{17/2}$ for the weight-$18$ cusp form $g$,
and should equidistribute on $[-2, 2]$ against
$\mu_{\ST_1}$.

\paragraph{Heal.} The shifted statement is \emph{true} but
identifies the \emph{correct} Sato--Tate group as a proper
factor. Barnet-Lamb--Geraghty--Harris--Taylor $2011$ gives
Sato--Tate for the cuspidal elliptic form
$g = \Delta \cdot E_6$ (holomorphic of weight $18$, level $1$).
Equidistribution of $a_p(g) / p^{17/2}$ on $[-2, 2]$ against
$\mu_{\ST_1}$ follows. This is Sato--Tate of the
\emph{elliptic factor} $\pi_g$, not of the Siegel form
$\Delta_{10}$ itself. The non-tempered $[2]$-block contributes
a rigid $\SL_2$-factor whose Satake parameters
$(p^{1/2}, p^{-1/2})$ do not equidistribute at all --- they
follow the deterministic Arthur-$\SL_2$ embedding.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 4: Sato--Tate group as proper Levi}

\paragraph{Attack.} The Sato--Tate group of $\Delta_{10}$ is
$\mathrm{USp}(4)$, and empirical failure of equidistribution is
a level or Ramanujan-violation artefact.

\paragraph{Heal.} The compact Sato--Tate group is not
$\mathrm{USp}(4)$ for the unshifted Siegel trace.  More precisely, the
failure is an Arthur-parameter diagnostic:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:sato-tate-group-delta10}
\psi_{\Delta_{10}}
\;=\;(\mathbf 1\boxtimes[2])\boxplus(\pi_g\boxtimes[1]),
\end{equation}
where the non-tempered Arthur $[2]$-block contributes the deterministic
Tate terms $(p^{1/2},p^{-1/2})$, while the compact $\mathrm{SU}(2)$
Sato--Tate law applies only to the shifted elliptic constituent
$g=\Delta E_6$.  Writing an actual Sato--Tate group as
$\mathrm{SL}_2\times\mathrm{SU}(2)$ would be wrong: Sato--Tate groups
are compact.

\subsection{Attack--Heal 5: Spin $L$-function from Sato--Tate}

\paragraph{Attack.} From the Sato--Tate data one recovers
$L_{\mathrm{spin}}(s, \Delta_{10}) = \prod_p \det(1 - p^{-s}
\phi_p \mid V)^{-1}$, $V$ the standard $4$-dimensional
$\mathrm{USp}(4)$-representation.

\paragraph{Heal.} The Euler form is correct, but its
factorisation records non-temperedness visibly:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:spin-L-factor-w5t3}
L_{\mathrm{spin}}(s, \Delta_{10}) \;=\; \zeta(s - 8)\,
\zeta(s - 9)\, L(s, g),
\end{equation}
with simple poles at $s = 9, 10$ from the two zeta factors.
The poles are the analytic signature of the non-tempered
$[2]$-block; a tempered $\GSp_4$-form has $L_{\mathrm{spin}}$
holomorphic in $\Re(s) > (k_1 + k_2 - 1)/2$. Sato--Tate
equidistribution of normalised traces is equivalent (Serre
$1968$, $1997$) to analytic non-vanishing of all
symmetric-power $L$-functions in the Euler-product region;
poles at $s = 9, 10$ in $L_{\mathrm{spin}}$ break this
non-vanishing and detect the Arthur-parameter reduction
equation~\eqref{eq:sato-tate-group-delta10}.

\subsection{Synthesis: CAP detector from Hecke distribution}

\begin{theorem}[Non-temperedness visible in Sato--Tate]
\label{thm:nontempered-detector-w5t3}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
Let $F$ be a cuspidal $\GSp_4$-Hecke eigenform of weight
$(k_1, k_2)$ and full level $\Sp_4(\ZZ)$. The following are
equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is a Saito--Kurokawa lift (CAP form), i.e.\ its
global Arthur parameter has a non-trivial $\SL_2$-block.
\item The normalised Hecke trace
$\lambda_p(F) / p^{(k_1 + k_2 - 3)/2}$ is unbounded in $p$.
\item The unshifted trace is governed by a non-tempered Arthur block
rather than a compact $\mathrm{USp}(4)$ Sato--Tate law.
\item The spin $L$-function $L_{\mathrm{spin}}(s, F)$ has a
pole in the right half-plane
$\Re(s) > (k_1 + k_2 - 1)/2$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
$(1) \Rightarrow (2)$: the non-tempered $[2]$-block contributes
a diagonal Satake entry $p^{1/2}$, so $\lambda_p /
p^{(k_1 + k_2 - 3)/2}$ contains the term $p^{1/2}$, unbounded.
$(2) \Leftrightarrow (3)$: an unbounded trace sequence cannot
equidistribute on a compact Sato--Tate group; by Arthur's classification
the obstruction is the non-tempered $[2]$ block. $(3) \Leftrightarrow
(4)$: poles of $L_{\mathrm{spin}}$ record the Tate factors contributed
by that block. $(4) \Rightarrow (1)$:
Weissauer $2009$ classification of Arthur packets for
$\GSp_4(\ZZ)$ cuspidal forms.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Hidden content.} The non-temperedness of
Saito--Kurokawa is detectable purely from the
\emph{distribution} of Hecke eigenvalues: no arithmetic or
cohomological input is needed. Computing $\lambda_p$ for
$p \leq 100$ from Poor--Yuen data and plotting
$\lambda_p / p^{17/2}$ against $p$ yields a sequence escaping
to $+\infty$ along the $p^{1/2}$-trajectory; the residual
$(\lambda_p / p^{17/2}) - (p^{1/2} + p^{-1/2}) = a_p(g) /
p^{17/2}$ tightly tracks the weight-$18$ $\SL_2$-Sato--Tate
semicircle on $[-2, 2]$. The Sato--Tate distributional
anomaly is the coarsest-possible CAP detector for genus-$2$
Siegel eigenforms --- coarser than $L$-function factorisation,
coarser than Arthur-packet localisation, coarser than
Galois-representation reducibility --- and agrees with each of
them on $\Delta_{10}$.

\paragraph{Vol III consequence.} In the $K3 \times E$
landscape, $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ is the DT
partition-function denominator (Oberdieck $2018$); its
Saito--Kurokawa structure is the chiral-side marker that
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1) = c_1(0)/2 = 5$ comes from a
Gritsenko additive lift rather than a multiplicative
Borcherds product: $\Delta_5$ is additive-lifted from the
Jacobi form of weight $10$, index $1$, and this additivity is
the $\SL_2$-Arthur $[2]$-block. The non-temperedness is not
an Arthur-packet curiosity; it is the \emph{mechanism} by
which the Gritsenko additive lift produces a modular form
whose BKM-weight output $c_1(0)/2 = 5$ has no transcendental
components. The Sato--Tate reduction
equation~\eqref{eq:sato-tate-group-delta10} is the
Langlands-dual shadow of the additive-lift mechanism.

\section{Test for a unifying functor $\Phi^{\mathrm{gen}}$ and the
$(\infty, 2)$-groupoid of U-duality orbits}
\label{sec:unifying-functor-test}

\subsection*{Target of attack}

The cache rule ``six routes to $G(\mathrm{K3}\times E)$ are six
\emph{different} constructions, NOT six $\Phi$-applications'' is
Vol~III orthodoxy. The K3~$\times$~E spectrum $\{0, 3, 5, 24\}$ ---
the four scalars $\{\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}},
\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}, \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}},
\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}\}$, with $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3 \times E)
= 0$ on the total space by K\"unneth multiplicativity, \emph{not}
$2$ which is the K3 fibre value --- is the four-valued projection of
the six orbit strata $(\mathrm{I})\ldots(\mathrm{VI})$ of
\S~\ref{subsec:six-routes-six-u-duality-orbits}. The attack asks:
is there a generalised functor
$\Phi^{\mathrm{gen}}: \mathrm{CY\text{-}cat}_d \to \mathrm{StratOut}$
whose single categorical output encodes all four $\kappa_\bullet$
simultaneously as strata of one object?

\subsection*{Test: does $\Phi^{\mathrm{gen}}$ exist?}

\textbf{Partial fail at the $1$-categorical level, partial succeed
at the $(\infty, 2)$-categorical level.} Precisely:

\begin{proposition}[Obstruction to a single-target
$1$-functor]\label{prop:no-single-functor-unification}
No symmetric-monoidal functor
$\Phi^{\mathrm{gen}}: \mathrm{CY\text{-}cat}_3 \to \mathrm{Alg}$
into a single $1$-category of algebras has scalar shadow that
simultaneously computes all four of $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}$,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}$. The obstruction is
\emph{multiplicativity type}:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(X \times Y) = \kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(X)
\cdot \kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(Y)$ (K\"unneth-multiplicative);
\item $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}(\pi: X \to B)$ is the topological
Euler characteristic of the \emph{fibre}, not the total space
(neither additive nor multiplicative under products);
\item $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$ is the constant
Fourier coefficient of the $N$-th paramodular form, additive under
Borcherds tensor product;
\item $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}$ is the Heisenberg
central charge, invariant under Borcherds tensor product.
\end{itemize}
A single symmetric-monoidal functor has one product rule, hence one
multiplicativity type, hence captures at most one $\kappa_\bullet$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Suppose $\Phi^{\mathrm{gen}}$ is symmetric monoidal with scalar
shadow $f$ satisfying $f(A \boxtimes A') = f(A) \ast f(A')$ for a
fixed binary operation $\ast$. Apply to $A = \cA_{K3}$, $A' =
\cA_E$: $f = \kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}$ forces $\ast = \cdot$ with
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3) \cdot \kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(E) = 2 \cdot
0 = 0 = \kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3 \times E)$, consistent; $f =
\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}$ demands $24 = 24 \ast
\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}(E)$, but $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}$ is not
defined on generic CY$_1$ factors, nor does any $\ast$ with
reasonable neutral return $24$; $f = \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ demands
$5 = \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(K3) \ast \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(E)$, but
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ is only defined on BKM-algebraic outputs,
not on individual CY factors. No single $\ast$ reconciles these
four requirements.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[Stratified-target unifying functor at
$(\infty, 2)$]\label{thm:stratified-unifying-functor}
There should exist a unifying functor
\[
\Phi^{\mathrm{gen}}: \mathrm{CY\text{-}cat}_3 \longrightarrow
\mathrm{Strat}_{(\infty, 2)}\bigl(\mathrm{UDual}\bigr)
\]
into the $(\infty, 2)$-category of U-duality-stratified algebraic
outputs, defined by
\[
\Phi^{\mathrm{gen}}(\cA_X) \;=\;
\bigl\{\, \Phi^{(\mathrm{I})}(\cA_X),\, \Phi^{(\mathrm{II})}(\cA_X),
\,\ldots,\, \Phi^{(\mathrm{VI})}(\cA_X) \,\bigr\},
\]
with $\Phi^{(i)}$ the restriction of the BPS root-space sheaf to
the $i$-th U-duality orbit of primitive Mukai vectors
($(\mathrm{I})\ldots(\mathrm{VI})$ per
\S~\ref{subsec:six-routes-six-u-duality-orbits}). For
$X = K3 \times E$ the functor recovers the full $\{0, 3, 5, 24\}$
spectrum via the orbit-collision map
\[
\mathsf{coll}: \{\mathrm{I},\ldots,\mathrm{VI}\} \twoheadrightarrow
\{\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}, \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}, \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}},
\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}\},
\]
orbits $(\mathrm{I})$ and $(\mathrm{VI})$ distinguished by
K3-fibre vs.\ fibre-rank, orbits $(\mathrm{III})$ and $(\mathrm{V})$
collapsed into the $\Phi_N$-paramodular family, orbits
$(\mathrm{II})$, $(\mathrm{IV})$ the $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ and
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ poles.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Heuristic construction]
The Narain lattice $\Lambda_{\mathrm{Nar}} = \mathrm{II}_{4,20}
\oplus \mathrm{II}_{1,1}(-1)$ carries the
$O(\Lambda_{\mathrm{Nar}})$ U-duality action. Primitive vectors of
fixed Mukai norm fall into exactly six orbit types
$(\mathrm{I})\ldots(\mathrm{VI})$
(cf.~\S~\ref{subsec:six-routes-six-u-duality-orbits} and the
cosmic-string decomposition D$1.1$--D$1.6$ of
\S~\ref{sec:cosmic-strings-g2}). The BPS root-space sheaf
$\cR_{\mathrm{BPS}} \to \mathrm{Narain}/O(\Lambda)$ restricts to
each orbit yielding a distinct algebraic invariant. The
$(\infty, 2)$-groupoid structure: $1$-morphisms are
Kontsevich--Soibelman BPS wall-crossing isomorphisms; $2$-morphisms
are U-duality isotopies. The functor $\Phi^{\mathrm{gen}}$ takes a
CY$_3$ category to its six-stratum BPS-root-space diagram.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{Corrected cache-discipline statement}

\begin{corollary}[Sharpened ``six routes'' cache
discipline]\label{cor:sharpened-six-routes-discipline}
The rule ``six routes to $G(\mathrm{K3}\times E)$ are six different
constructions, not six $\Phi$-applications'' is \emph{conservative
but true within its scope}:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Strict, $1$-categorical.) No symmetric-monoidal $1$-functor
      $\Phi: \mathrm{CY\text{-}cat}_3 \to \mathrm{Alg}$ has scalar
      shadow computing all four $\kappa_\bullet$. The rule holds
      verbatim.
      \textsc{(Proposition~\ref{prop:no-single-functor-unification}.)}
\item (Sharpened, $(\infty, 2)$-categorical.) There exists a
      unifying $\Phi^{\mathrm{gen}}: \mathrm{CY\text{-}cat}_3 \to
      \mathrm{Strat}_{(\infty, 2)}(\mathrm{UDual})$; its single
      output on $\cA_{K3 \times E}$ contains all four
      $\kappa_\bullet$ as scalar shadows of its six orbit strata.
      The six orbit types are $0$-cells of an
      $(\infty, 2)$-groupoid $\zeta = \zeta_{\mathrm{UDual}(K3
      \times E)}$.
      \textsc{(Conjecture~\ref{thm:stratified-unifying-functor}.)}
\item (Master $\kappa$.) Define
      $\kappa^{\mathrm{mast}}(\cA_X) := \sum_i \varepsilon_i\,
      \kappa^{(i)}\bigl(\Phi^{(i)}(\cA_X)\bigr)$ with
      $\varepsilon_i$ the Kontsevich--Soibelman wall-crossing
      weights. The naked sum $\sum_{\mathrm{route}}
      \kappa_{\mathrm{route}} = 0 + 3 + 5 + 24 = 32$ has no
      intrinsic significance. With $\varepsilon_i$ fixed by the
      Igusa-$\Delta_{10}$ denominator-formula multiplicity
      assignment, $\kappa^{\mathrm{mast}}(\cA_{K3 \times E}) =
      \mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10})=10$ recovers the doubled
      Borcherds-weight identity for $\Phi_{10}=\Delta_5^2$
      (Theorem~\ref{thm:borcherds-weight-kappa-BKM-universal}). The
      weighted master is the Borcherds weight; the naked sum is
      not.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\subsection*{Hidden identification: six orbit types $=$ orbits of
$\zeta \in (\infty, 2)\text{-}\mathrm{grpd}$ of U-duality}

The six orbit types $(\mathrm{I})\ldots(\mathrm{VI})$ are orbits of
a single point
$\zeta \in \pi_0\bigl(\mathrm{UDual}_{(\infty, 2)}(K3 \times
E)\bigr)$. Concretely, $\zeta$ is the Narain-moduli germ at the
generic Picard-rank-$3$ K3 attractor point equipped with the
$O(\Lambda_{\mathrm{Nar}})$-action. The orbit-stabiliser structure
on primitive Mukai vectors of fixed norm organises the cosmic-string
D$1.1$--D$1.6$ decomposition of
\S~\ref{sec:cosmic-strings-g2} into six $1$-cell
isomorphism classes, with $2$-cells given by
Kontsevich--Soibelman wall-crossing. ``Six different
constructions'' are six $1$-cells of this $(\infty, 2)$-groupoid;
``one unifying $\Phi^{\mathrm{gen}}$-output'' is the
$(\infty, 2)$-groupoid itself. The hidden identification is
orbit-stabiliser duality:
\begin{equation*}
\{\,\text{six distinct constructions}\,\}
\;=\;
\mathrm{Orb}\bigl(O(\Lambda_{\mathrm{Nar}}) \curvearrowright
\mathrm{Prim}_{(2, 26)}\bigr)
\;=\;
\pi_0(\zeta / \mathrm{UDual}).
\end{equation*}

\subsection*{Reconciliation}

The cache rule survives intact at the $1$-categorical level
(Proposition~\ref{prop:no-single-functor-unification}): no
single monoidal functor collects all four $\kappa_\bullet$. It is
simultaneously sharpened at the $(\infty, 2)$-categorical level
(Conjecture~\ref{thm:stratified-unifying-functor}): the six
``different constructions'' are the six orbit strata of a single
$(\infty, 2)$-groupoid output $\Phi^{\mathrm{gen}}(\cA_{K3 \times
E})$. The naive master scalar
$\sum_{\mathrm{route}}\kappa_{\mathrm{route}} = 32$ is meaningless;
the Borcherds-weighted master is
$\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10})=10=2\,\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)$.

\section{The crystal metaphor is wrong: $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ as the correct $(\infty,1)$-groupoid of moonshine data}
\label{sec:crystal-metaphor-killed}

\subsection*{(a) Killing ``crystal''}

The governing metaphor threaded through the manuscript --- $\Delta_{10}$
(and related objects $\Delta_5, \Phi_N, \Omega_g$) as a \emph{single
crystal refracted through different lenses} (GV/DT/BKM ``three lenses''
at line~$7558$; $\Phi$/CoHA/derived-category ``different lenses'' at
line~$2963$; four $\kappa_\bullet$ ``like a crystal's symmetry group,
Bravais lattice, band structure, free energy'' at line~$2700$; ``four
faces of a single four-dimensional statement'' at line~$6896$; the
``pinhole camera'' of \textsc{Lorgat}~$2020$ at
\texttt{chapters/frame/preface.tex:1239}) --- is mathematically
misleading in four specific ways.

\emph{(C1) Finite faceting is a category error.} A crystal has finitely
many flat faces related by a finite point group. The moonshine data in
Vol~III has non-discrete automorphisms: $O^+(II_{2,26})$ acting on
$\Delta_{\mathrm{Mon}}$, $\Sp_4(\Z)$ acting on $\Delta_{10}$, the
continuous Maulik--Okounkov $R(z)$ deformation, and the Hida-family
variation on $\Delta_{10}[\kappa]$. One cannot face-count a variety
with a positive-dimensional automorphism group.

\emph{(C2) ``Refraction of the same object'' conflates $\pi_0$ with
$\pi_1$.} The claim ``GV $=$ DT $=$ BKM counts the same integer
through three lenses'' is a $\pi_0$-statement; but MNOP wall-crossing,
DT/PT flop, Gopakumar--Vafa refinement, and the BKM Borcherds product
carry non-trivial \emph{homotopies between the lenses} (MNOP
change-of-variable, Joyce--Song wall-crossing, Bridgeland stability
chambers). These homotopies are not refractions; they are $\pi_1$-data
of the ambient groupoid and are invisible in the crystal picture.

\emph{(C3) ``Twelve faces'' is not a face count; it is a $\pi_0$
census.} The seven faces of $r_{\mathrm{CY}}$, the four
$\kappa_\bullet$, the CY-A/B/C/D stratification, the
Schiffmann--Vasserot / Maulik--Okounkov / Nakajima trio: twelve
\emph{non-isomorphic but compatibly linked} objects. ``Faces of one
crystal'' suggests a shared interior they all bound; there is no
interior. The compatibilities are morphisms, not boundaries.

\emph{(C4) ``Pinhole camera'' understates.} \textsc{Lorgat}~$2020$ is
not a 2D projection of a 3D crystal; it is a distinguished
\emph{basepoint} equipped with a preferred self-equivalence (the
$\Delta_5 \mapsto \Delta_5 \cdot \Delta_5$ genus-2 cutting,
line~$9372$). A pinhole loses information; a basepoint does not.

\subsection*{(b) Correction: the $(\infty,1)$-groupoid $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$
of moonshine data}

\begin{definition}[Groupoid of moonshine data]
\label{def:cG-moonshine}
Let $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ be the $(\infty,1)$-groupoid whose
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{objects} are quadruples $(L, \Theta, \Psi, \iota)$ with
$L$ an even lattice of signature $(p,q)$, $\Theta$ a Siegel/orthogonal
modular form on the symmetric domain $\cD_L = O(L \otimes \R)/K$ of
weight $w(\Theta) \in \tfrac12 \Z$, $\Psi$ a Borcherds multiplicative
lift $\Theta = \Psi(F)$ of a vector-valued modular form
$F \in M^{!}_{1 - p/2}(\rho_L)$, and $\iota$ the compatibility datum
\[
\iota \;:\; \mathrm{Denom}(\Theta) \;=\; e^{-\rho}
\prod_{\alpha \in \Delta^+(L)} (1 - e^{-\alpha})^{\mathrm{mult}(\alpha)}
\]
with a generalised Kac--Moody Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{g}(L)$ of
BKM type, root system $\Delta(L) \subset L$, root multiplicities
$c_F(\alpha^2/2)$;

\item \emph{1-morphisms} $(L, \Theta, \Psi, \iota) \to (L', \Theta',
\Psi', \iota')$ are triples $(\varphi, \beta, \gamma)$ with
$\varphi: L \hookrightarrow L'$ a primitive lattice embedding,
$\beta$ the pullback compatibility $\varphi^* \Theta' = \Theta \cdot
\Theta^{\perp}_{\varphi}$, and $\gamma: \mathfrak{g}(L)
\hookrightarrow \mathfrak{g}(L')$ a BKM subalgebra map intertwining
$\iota, \iota'$;

\item \emph{higher morphisms}: 2-cells are lattice-theoretic
conjugations (change of polarisation, Fricke/Atkin--Lehner
involution), 3-cells are pentagon/hexagon coherences of Borcherds
products under iterated pullback.
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[$\pi_0$ of $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$]
\label{prop:pi0-cG-moonshine}
$\pi_0(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$ contains the isomorphism classes of:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $[\Delta_5]$: Gritsenko weight-$5$ form on Siegel $\cA_2$ with
$L = 2U \oplus 2E_8(-1)$, $\mathfrak{g}(L) = \mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$;
\item $[\Delta_{10}]$: Igusa weight-$10$ cusp form $= \Delta_5^2$
on $\cA_2$, with $\mathfrak{g}(\Delta_{10}) = \mathrm{Sym}^2
\mathfrak{g}(\Delta_5)$ suitably folded;
\item $[\Phi_N], N \in \{1,2,3,4,6\}$: Gritsenko $\Phi_N$-family,
$w(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = w(\Phi_N)$;
\item $[\Delta_{\mathrm{Mon}}]$: $L = II_{1,25}$,
$\Delta_{\mathrm{Mon}}$ the Borcherds Monster denominator,
$\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{m}$;
\item $[\Omega_g], g \in M_{24}$: Mathieu twining classes lifted to
BKM data via $K3$ elliptic genus.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Moduli problem.} $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ represents the functor
$S \mapsto \{\text{$S$-families of $(L, \Theta, \Psi, \iota)$ up to
lattice-Borcherds equivalence}\}$ on smooth schemes over
$\Spec \Z[1/N_{\mathrm{bad}}]$. Homotopy groups:
$\pi_1(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}, [\Delta_5]) \supset \mathrm{Aut}(L)
= O^+(2U \oplus 2E_8(-1)) \supset \Sp_4(\Z)$; $\pi_2$ encodes
Fricke-involution coherence.
\end{proposition}

\subsection*{(c) Hidden structure: \textsc{Lorgat}~$2020$ as basepoint,
wave findings as $\mathrm{Hom}_{\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}}$}

\begin{theorem}[Findings realised as hom-spaces]
\label{thm:moonshine-findings-as-homs}
The pinhole camera of \textsc{Lorgat}~$2020$ is the object
$\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5} := ((2U \oplus 2E_8(-1)), \Delta_5,
\Psi_{\mathrm{Grit}}, \iota_{\Delta_5}) \in \cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$,
a distinguished object with preferred self-equivalence
$\sigma: \mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5} \to \mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$ realising
$\Delta_5 \mapsto \Delta_5 \cdot \Delta_5$ (line~$9372$). The
findings across the programme reorganise as mapping spaces:
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{Map}(\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}, [\Delta_{10}])
&\ni \{\text{Hida--Skinner Klingen family, Saito--Kurokawa lift}\}, \\
\mathrm{Map}(\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}, [\Phi_1])
&\ni \{\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = 5, c_1(0)/2\text{ identity}\}, \\
\mathrm{Map}(\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}, [\Delta_{\mathrm{Mon}}])
&\ni \{\text{Leech-no-roots}/K3\text{-no-}{-}2\text{-curves, line } 2862\}, \\
\mathrm{Map}(\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}, [\Omega_g])
&\ni \{\text{Mathieu twining class attached to } g \in M_{24}\}.
\end{align*}
The six routes to $G(K3 \times E)$ are six 1-morphisms with distinct
targets --- not six endomorphisms of one object --- and their parallel
compatibility is a single $6$-simplex in the nerve
$N(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$. ``Twelve faces'' $=$ twelve distinguished
$\pi_0$-classes plus connecting hom-spaces; ``refraction'' $=$
morphism in $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$; the pinhole camera $=$ basepoint
$\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$, which loses no information. The manuscript
studies the connected component $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}^{\circ} \subset
\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ reachable from $\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$ by
finite-length zigzags of 1-morphisms.
\end{theorem}

\section{Uniqueness of $(g, d, N) = (2, 3, \infty)$ as a universal property}
\label{sec:uniqueness-triple}

The synthesis
(line $\approx 11918$) and meta-frontier (line $\approx 9476$)
name $(g, d, N) = (2, 3, \infty)$ as the ``unique locus where
twelve presentations of $\Delta_5$ coincide.'' Kazhdan--Polyakov
adversarial demand: is the triple actually unique, or is every
genus-$g$ a locally-unique convergence point of its own
eight-to-twelve lenses?

\subsection*{Attack. Naive uniqueness is false; every genus has
its own convergence.}

The assertion ``$(2, 3, \infty)$ is the unique $(g, d, N)$ where
many structures coincide'' admits three immediate counterexamples.

\emph{Counterexample~$1$ (Monstrous moonshine at $g = 0$).} At
$(g, d, N) = (0, 1, \infty)$ the $j$-invariant
$j(\tau) - 744 = \sum_{n \geq -1} c_n q^n$ with $c_1 = 196884$
is simultaneously: (i) the graded character of the Monster
moonshine module $V^\natural$ (Frenkel--Lepowsky--Meurman
$1988$); (ii) the Hauptmodul for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)$ on
$\mathbb H$; (iii) the denominator of the Monster Lie algebra
$\fm$ (Borcherds $1992$); (iv) the chiral partition function
of the bosonic string on $\mathbb R^{24}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{Leech}}$;
(v) the arithmetic Chern character of the Tate module of the
CM elliptic curve with $j = 0$; (vi) the reciprocal of
$\eta^{24}$ up to Rademacher sums. Six lenses converge at
$(0, 1, \infty)$.

\emph{Counterexample~$2$ (Mathieu moonshine at $g = 1$).} At
$(g, d, N) = (1, 2, \infty)$, the K3 elliptic genus
$\mathrm{EG}(K3; \tau, z) = 8 \sum_{i=2}^4 \theta_i(\tau, z)^2
/ \theta_i(\tau, 0)^2$ is simultaneously: (i) a weak Jacobi
form of weight $0$ index $1$; (ii) the graded character of
the Eguchi--Ooguri--Tachikawa $M_{24}$-module with $K_1 =
45 + \overline{45}$ (EOT $2010$); (iii) a mock-modular
completion $\tilde H(\tau)$ matching $M_{24}$ reps across
all $26$ conjugacy classes (Gannon $2016$); (iv) the
Gritsenko seed $\phi_{0, 1}$ for the additive lift to
$\Delta_5$. Four lenses converge at $(1, 2, \infty)$.

\emph{Counterexample~$3$ (Schottky ceiling at $g = 4$).} At
$(g, d, N) = (4, 5, \infty)$ the Schottky--Igusa form $J_8 -
I_8 \in S_8(\Sp_8(\Z))$ vanishes on $\cJ_4 \subset \cA_4$.
Lenses: (i) the first Siegel cusp form detecting the Schottky
locus; (ii) the genus-$4$ theta relation; (iii) the
D'Hoker--Phong $2002$ superstring measure ambiguity;
(iv) the boundary of $R^*(\overline{\cM}_4) \hookrightarrow
R^*(\cA_4)$. Four lenses converge at $(4, 5, \infty)$.

Every genus-$g$ has its own convergence. ``Uniqueness of $(2,
3, \infty)$'' as a point-count is \emph{false}: it misreads a
universal property as a coincidence.

\subsection*{Heal. The universal property in the
$(\infty, 1)$-category $\ModRigidD$ of moonshine-rigid data.}

Define $\ModRigidD$ with objects tuples $(\cC, \fg, \Phi, Z)$
where: (a) $\cC$ a Kontsevich--Soibelman $(\infty, 1)$-CY
category of dimension $d$; (b) $\fg$ a BKM Lie superalgebra
whose denominator is a genus-$g$ paramodular Siegel form;
(c) $\Phi: \CYcat_d \to \ChirAlg$ the CY-to-chiral functor
producing an $E_n$-chiral algebra at $n = \min(2, 3 - d)$;
(d) $Z$ a DT partition function on $\cC$ representable as the
reciprocal of a weight-$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ paramodular form
on $\mathfrak H_g$. Morphisms are coherent $\infty$-
equivalences; the $\infty$-structure is the Joyal--Lurie
enhancement making $\Phi$ a lax $(\infty, 1)$-functor. At
$N = \infty$ the $\mathrm{Sym}^\infty$ second-quantisation
produces the DMVV genus-$g$ partition function.

\begin{conjecture}[Universal property of $(g, d, N) = (2, 3,
\infty)$ in $\ModRigidD$]
\label{thm:universal-property-triple}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
The tuple labelled by $(\cC, \fg, \Phi, Z) = (\Db(K3 \times E),
\fg_{\Delta_5}, \Phi^{K3 \times E}, 1/\Delta_{10})$ is the
unique object of $\ModRigidD$ (up to contractible choice in the
$(\infty, 1)$-sense) where three conditions hold
simultaneously:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(P1)}] \emph{Paramodular-Siegel representability}:
$\fg$ has denominator a paramodular cusp form on
$\Sp_{2g}(\Z)$, genus $g = d - 1 \geq 2$.
\item[\textup{(P2)}] \emph{Compact-CY$_3$ realisation}:
$\cC = \Db(X)$ with $X$ a compact Calabi--Yau threefold,
$\chi(\cO_X) = 0$, carrying a K3$\times$(elliptic) fibre
structure.
\item[\textup{(P3)}] \emph{$\mathrm{Sym}^\infty$ second-
quantisation matching}: the paramodular form is the DMVV
$\mathrm{Sym}^\infty$ lift of a weak Jacobi form of
weight $0$ index $1$ matching the K3 elliptic genus.
\end{enumerate}
Failures at sister triples:
$(0, 1, \infty)$: (P1), (P2) fail (Hauptmodul not paramodular;
$d = 1$ not CY$_3$).
$(1, 2, \infty)$: (P1) fails (Jacobi not paramodular); the
Gritsenko lift promotes to $g = 2$, so this triple is the
\emph{seed}, not the convergence point.
$(3, 4, \infty)$: (P2) fails (no compact CY$_4$ carrying the
K3$\times E$ fibre structure with $\chi(\cO) = 0$).
$(4, 5, \infty)$: (P3) fails catastrophically --- Schottky--
Igusa $J_8 - I_8$ vanishes on $\cJ_4$, so the DMVV lift lands
inside the Schottky ideal, $1/Z$ has poles on all of $\cJ_4$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Heuristic sketch]
(i) $g = d - 1$ with $g \geq 2$ forces $d \geq 3$. (ii) The
compact-CY$_3$ constraint $d = 3$ plus $\chi(\cO) = 0$ plus
K3$\times$(elliptic) fibre is, up to isogeny, $K3 \times E$
(Huybrechts K3 classification + elliptic rigidity). (iii) The
DMVV lift of a weak Jacobi form of weight $0$ index $1$
produces a genus-$2$ paramodular cusp form of weight $10$
(Dijkgraaf--Moore--Verlinde--Verlinde $1997$), which
Gritsenko--Nikulin $1998$ classify under the standard
normalisation as $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$.
$(\infty, 1)$-coherence: contractible choice in
$\mathrm{Aut}^0(\Db(K3 \times E))$.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{Hidden content: three simultaneous matchings.}

$(g, d, N) = (2, 3, \infty)$ is the unique triple where three
matchings hold at once:
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Paramodular-Siegel $\leftrightarrow$ CY$_3$}:
$\mathfrak H_2$ parametrises pairs of elliptic curves with
coupling, and the off-diagonal entry $z$ in $Z =
\left(\begin{smallmatrix} \tau & z \\ z & \omega
\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is the K3-fibre to $E$-base
coupling on $K3 \times E$.
\item \emph{CY$_3$ $\leftrightarrow$ $\mathrm{Sym}^\infty$
second-quantisation}: DMVV gives $\sum_n Q^n Z(\mathrm{Sym}^n
(K3 \times T^2)) = 1/\prod(1 - Q^a p^b q^c)^{c(4ab - c^2)} =
1/\Delta_{10}$, which is the $\Phi$-image on the CY$_3$
derived category.
\item \emph{$\mathrm{Sym}^\infty$ $\leftrightarrow$
paramodular}: Gritsenko's additive lift $J_{0, 1} \to
M_5(\Sp_4(\Z))$ sends $\phi_{0, 1}$ to $\Delta_5$, and the
exponential lift gives $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ as the
$\mathrm{Sym}^\infty$ generating function.
\end{itemize}

These form a $2$-out-of-$3$ obstruction: at $g = 0$ the second
fails (no CY$_3$); at $g = 1$ the first fails (no paramodular);
at $g = 3$ the second fails (no compact CY$_4$); at $g \geq 4$
the third fails (Schottky--Igusa). Only at $g = 2$ all three
match.

\subsection*{Reframing the counterexamples as sister initial
objects.}

\begin{itemize}
\item $(0, 1, \infty)$: initial of the $\SL_2$-modular
Hauptmodul subcategory. Degenerate-(P1), fails (P2), (P3).
\item $(1, 2, \infty)$: initial of the Jacobi subcategory.
Degenerate-(P1) (Jacobi not Siegel), degenerate-(P2)
($d = 2$, K3 not CY$_3$), partial-(P3).
\item $(2, 3, \infty)$: initial of the \emph{full}
subcategory where (P1), (P2), (P3) all hold non-
trivially. The Gritsenko--Borcherds--DMVV triangulation
point.
\item $(3, 4, \infty)$: (P2) fails; no compact CY$_4$
carrying the required fibre structure.
\item $(4, 5, \infty)$: Schottky--Igusa \emph{obstructs}
(rather than merely complicates) because the DMVV lift
lands \emph{inside} the Schottky ideal, not transverse to
it; $1/Z$ has poles on all of $\cJ_4$, so the DT partition
function cannot pull back to $\cM_4$. This eliminates the
Calabi--Yau manifold realisation and sharpens the
obstruction into a representability failure.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{Metamathematical upshot.}

$(g, d, N) = (2, 3, \infty)$ is not where ``many things happen
to coincide''; it is the unique object of $\ModRigidD$
satisfying the universal property of
Theorem~\ref{thm:universal-property-triple}. Other
genera are sister initial objects of subcategories of
$\ModRigidD$ with their own convergences, not the
triangulation point of (P1), (P2), (P3) simultaneously. The
``twelve presentations of $\Delta_5$'' are the twelve
functorial images of these three matchings under derived,
chiral, automorphic, motivic, $L$-theoretic, Kudla--Rapoport,
Kapustin--Witten, Bridgeland--Smith, Harvey--Moore,
Saito--Kurokawa, Carnahan-twist, and Borcherds-product-
coefficient functors.

Open frontier: explicit
construction of $\ModRigidD$ as a genuine $(\infty, 1)$-
category with Theorem~\ref{thm:universal-property-triple}
formalised in derived algebraic geometry, plus
$(\infty, 1)$-categorical coherence of morphisms between
tuples $(\cC, \fg, \Phi, Z)$. Status:
\ClaimStatusConjectured.



\section{Meta-adversarial on the frontier list:
the three-problem stamp reconsidered}
\label{sec:frontier-meta-adversarial}

\subsection*{(a) Killed: the three-problem synthesis}

The stamp at lines \textbf{$9450$--$9486$} and
\textbf{$11929$--$11934$} publishes the prior end-state as
``three conditional bridges'' (super-Yangian $Y(\gl(4|20))$,
generalised-moonshine $(g, h)$-family, CY-C existence) and
``five open edges'' appended as a coda. Meta-adversarially these
are \emph{not} the frontier-defining questions of the
$r_{\mathrm{CY}}$ programme; they are the three questions most
visible from the $K3 \times E$ specialisation the waves have hit,
mistaken for the frontier itself.

Three load-bearing corrections.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{CY-C is not about $K3 \times E$; it is about $\Phi_3$
morphism-preservation on $\CY_3$-cat.} Line~$183$ reads
``$\Phi_3$ constructs the $\Eone$-chiral algebra, but the braided
($\Etwo$) quantum group structure requires additional data'', and
lines~$12387$--$12397$ document the $\Phi$-functor scope as an
$(\infty, 1)$-categorical lift whose \emph{morphism-preservation}
status is precisely what distinguishes the object-level statement
(proved, CY-A$_3$) from the functor-level statement (open).
Specialising to $K3 \times E$ makes the question look
lattice-specific ($\gDelta_5$, $M_{24}$); it is category-theoretic.

\item \textbf{Super-Yangian $Y(\gl(4|20)) \hookrightarrow
\mathbf D_\hbar(\gDelta_5)$ is \emph{not} residually conjectural at
the character level, and is \emph{provable} via stable-envelope
comparison} (line~$717$ onwards, $\S$\ref{sec:e2-braiding}). The
Maulik--Okounkov $R$-matrix on $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(K3 \times E)$
(line~$1310$, Proposition~\ref{prop:k3e-mo-rmatrix}, $72$ tests)
computes the Yang--Baxter structure function $g(u)$ exactly; the
super-rank $(4, 20) = (h^{\mathrm{even}}, h^{\mathrm{odd}})$-split
of Mukai $\widetilde\Lambda_{K3}$ is forced by the sign $\pm 1$ of
Mukai vector components. The conjectural tag is residual
caution, not a mathematical gap: the embedding factors through
stable-envelope equivariant $K$-theory exactly as
Schiffmann--Vasserot ($\emph{Ann.\ ENS}$ $2017$, \S$5$--$6$)
proved the $\C^2$ case.

\item \textbf{The $(g, h)$-family is genus-$1$ moonshine carried to
the Siegel axis; it is programmatic (Carnahan translation at
lines~$8553$--$8628$), not a frontier.} The actual
number-theoretic frontier obstructing $\Delta_{10}$-IMC equality
(T$1$/$20$, line~$13179$ onward) is the Kudla--Millson
Heegner-cycle Euler system, which upgrades Skinner--Urban
divisibility to equality; this is strictly deeper than the
Carnahan translate.
\end{enumerate}
