\subsection*{(c) Hidden: $\mathbf{F1}$ is the programme's apex,
not an item alongside the others}

The mathematically central frontier question is not ``does
$G(K3 \times E)$ exist'', not ``does $Y(\gl(4|20))$ embed'', not
``does the $(g, h)$-family close''. It is: \emph{does the
CY-to-chiral functor $\Phi_3$ preserve morphisms coherently ---
does the $(\infty, 1)$-categorical lift of the object-level
CY-A$_3$ functor exist?} Formally:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:frontier-apex-question}
\Phi_3 : (\CY_3\text{-}\mathrm{cat})_{(\infty, 1)}
\;\longrightarrow\;
(E_1\text{-}\mathrm{ChirAlg})_{(\infty, 1)}
\quad\text{functor?}
\end{equation}
The \emph{object-level} instance $\Phi_3(A) = A_{\mathrm{ch}}$
(CY-A$_3$) is proved (line~$183$ onward); the \emph{morphism-level}
instance --- sending derived-category autoequivalences of a CY$_3$
category to vertex-algebra homomorphisms of the image --- is the
missing piece. Every downstream question on the frontier
(super-Yangian promotion, CY-C full existence including braided
monoidal structure, Pattern $273$ scope) is a specialisation of
\eqref{eq:frontier-apex-question} at a specific category. The
$K3 \times E$ wave-specialisation makes the question look like a
calculation on $\gDelta_5$; read from the functor side, the single
load-bearing input is the $\Omega$-extension of
$\mathrm{HKR}(\cC)$-coherence along morphisms in $\CY_3$-cat.

\textbf{The original three-problem stamp is not wrong, only
mis-ranked.} Super-Yangian verification, the $(g, h)$-family, and
CY-C existence are all consequences of $\mathbf{F1}$ at specific
objects; they have been named separately because earlier passes hit
$K3 \times E$, where all three specialisations become visible.
The correction: record $\mathbf{F1}$ as the apex and the
three specialisations as its first three corollary-questions.

\section{Equivalence classes among the twelve presentations of
$\Delta_5$}
\label{sec:delta5-twelve-presentations-equivalence-v1}

The enumeration in
\S\ref{subsec:one-form-twelve-presentations} lists twelve
presentations of $\Delta_5$. Four of the distinctions drawn are
spurious at the level of construction equivalence; the genuine
count is six.

\begin{proposition}[Minimal independent presentations of $\Delta_5$]
\label{prop:delta5-six-equivalence-classes-v1}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
Let $\mathfrak P = \{P_1, \ldots, P_{12}\}$ denote the twelve
presentations of $\Delta_5 \in S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$
enumerated in
\S\ref{subsec:one-form-twelve-presentations}:
$P_1$ (Borcherds lift of $\phi_{0,1}$),
$P_2$ (BKM denominator for $\mathfrak g_{\Delta_5}$),
$P_3$ (square root of Igusa $\Delta_{10}$ via Oberdieck KKV),
$P_4$ (Bridgeland--Smith autoequivalence shadow),
$P_5$ (Kudla--Millson--Rapoport arithmetic divisor),
$P_6$ (Saito--Kurokawa Arthur packet $\psi_{\Delta_{10}}$),
$P_7$ (Weissauer Kuga--Satake motive),
$P_8$ (class-$\mathcal S$ $6d$ $(2,0)$ partition on $K3 \times \Sigma_2$),
$P_9$ (DMVV second-quantisation lift),
$P_{10}$ (horizon algebra $\mathfrak A_\infty(\mathcal H)$ on
$\AdS_3 \times S^2 \times K3$),
$P_{11}$ (Humbert zero-divisor),
$P_{12}$ (log-critical Sugawara shadow at $c = -214$).
Define $P_i \sim P_j$ iff the two constructions produce $\Delta_5$
from data related by invertible natural transformations in the
relevant data category (a quasi-isomorphism of chain complexes at
the chain level, an equivalence of $(\infty,1)$-categories at the
$(\infty,1)$ level). Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $P_1 \sim P_3 \sim P_9$ via the Borcherds--Gritsenko duality
$\mathrm{BorLift}(\phi_{0,1})^2 = \mathrm{GritLift}(2\phi_{0,1}) =
\Delta_{10}$ (Gritsenko $1995$, Borcherds $1998$).
\item $P_2 \sim P_{12}$ via identification of the log-critical
$L_0^{\mathrm{nilp}}$ eigenvalue on imaginary-null simples with
$\mult(\delta_j) = 5$: the Weyl--Kac--Borcherds denominator and
the $c = -214$ Sugawara anomaly are two projections of the same
Cartan datum $(\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}, \Delta^{\mathrm{re}},
\Delta^{\mathrm{im}})$.
\item $P_5 \sim P_6 \sim P_7$ via Arthur $+$ Kuga--Satake:
Howard--Madapusi-Pera $2020$ identifies $\widehat\Phi_{\mathrm{KMR}}$
at the divisorial stratum with the automorphic realisation of
$\psi_{\Delta_{10}}$; Weissauer $2009$ realises its $\ell$-adic
Galois representation inside $h^1(\mathrm{KS})^{\otimes 2}(-8)$.
\item $P_8 \sim P_{10}$ via AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$: the MSW $(0,4)$ CFT
on $K3 \times \Sigma_2$ at the Humbert restriction is the boundary
theory of $\AdS_3 \times S^2 \times K3$ in Type IIA on
$K3 \times E$; class-$\mathcal S$ partition and horizon-algebra
Cardy character are one character read on the two sides of one
duality.
\item $P_4$ and $P_{11}$ are not equivalent to any other $P_i$:
$P_4$ carries derived-categorical data ---
$\Stab^{\mathrm{OP}}(K3 \times E)$ as an $(\infty,1)$-stack --- that
none of the other presentations carries; $P_{11}$ is the
classical-scheme-theoretic underlying divisor, forgetting the
multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ and retaining only $\Div(\Delta_5)$.
\end{enumerate}
The quotient $\mathfrak P/{\sim}$ has exactly six classes:
$\{P_1, P_3, P_9\}$ (modular/analytic),
$\{P_2, P_{12}\}$ (Lie-algebraic),
$\{P_5, P_6, P_7\}$ (arithmetic/motivic),
$\{P_4\}$ (categorical/derived),
$\{P_8, P_{10}\}$ (physical/holographic),
$\{P_{11}\}$ (divisorial/classical-geometric). These six are the
minimal genuinely independent presentations of $\Delta_5$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Each collapse is the application of a named structural identity.
For (1): $\mathrm{BorLift}(\phi_{0,1})^2 = \Delta_{10}$ and
$\mathrm{GritLift}(2\phi_{0,1}) = \Delta_{10}$ are two images of
the seed $Z_{K3} = 2\phi_{0,1}$ under the two sides of the
Borcherds--Gritsenko duality square, and the DMVV product
$Z_\infty = \prod(1 - p^m q^n r^l)^{-c(nm,l)}$ with Weyl-vector
prefactor equals $1/\Delta_{10}$; the square is a
quasi-isomorphism of Jacobi-form chain complexes and an
$(\infty,1)$-equivalence of lifting functors.
For (2): the denominator $\Delta_5 = e^{-\rho}\prod_{\alpha \in
\Delta_+}(1 - e^{-\alpha})^{\mult \alpha}$ and the Sugawara
$T^{\mathrm{Sug}} = \varepsilon^{-1}\sum :J^a J_a: + (\log
\varepsilon) L_0^{\mathrm{nilp}}$ descend from one multiplicity
function $\mult: \Delta^+ \to \Z_{\geq 0}$ via Eichler--Zagier
expansion at the critical level.
For (3): three lenses (arithmetic-Chow, automorphic,
Galois-motivic) on one motive $M(\Delta_{10})$.
For (4): the horizon algebra is the asymptotic-symmetry algebra of
the near-horizon geometry whose IR boundary theory is the MSW CFT,
realised by the M$5$-brane on the $(0,4)$-divisor and the Type IIA
/ M-theory duality $K3 \times E \leftrightarrow K3 \times T^3$.

Non-collapses: $P_4$'s shadow
$\rho_{\mathrm{BS}}: \Sp_4(\Z)/\{\pm I\} \hookrightarrow \Auteq /
(\mathrm{shift} \oplus \mathrm{Pic})$ is the derivation of Siegel
modularity from $(\infty,1)$-categorical data, not its recording;
$P_{11}$ is a truncation of modular-form data to its zero-scheme,
dropping the multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The hidden coherence functor]
\label{rem:delta5-humbert-coherence-functor-v1}
The six classes are six projections of one
derived-geometric object. Define
\begin{equation*}
\widehat{\mathbf H}_1 \;:=\; \bR\mathcal A_2
\times_{\mathcal A_2}^{\bL} H_1^{\mathrm{fm}},
\end{equation*}
the derived formal completion of the Humbert divisor
$H_1 = \Div(\Delta_5) \subset \mathcal A_2$ in the Toen--Vezzosi
derived-stack category over $\Spec\Z$, equipped with the BKM
factorisation structure $\mathcal F_{\mathfrak g_{\Delta_5}} \in
\Fact_{\mathrm E_2}(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1)$ from the Segal
$E_2$-structure on the Ran space of $\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$-graded
vacua. The six classes of
\Cref{prop:delta5-six-equivalence-classes-v1} are images of the
single pair
$(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1, \mathcal F_{\mathfrak g_{\Delta_5}})$
under six functors:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{r@{\;$\to$\;}l}
Hodge theta-realisation & $\{P_1, P_3, P_9\}$\\
Weyl--Kac--Borcherds denominator & $\{P_2, P_{12}\}$\\
$\ell$-adic / Hodge motivic realisation & $\{P_5, P_6, P_7\}$\\
Bridgeland-stability pullback & $\{P_4\}$\\
AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ character functor & $\{P_8, P_{10}\}$\\
Classical truncation $\bR \to \pi_0$ & $\{P_{11}\}$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Coherence: the six functors commute with the
$\Sp_4(\Z)$-equivariance on $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$, so $\Delta_5$
acquires paramodular modularity once in $\Sh(\mathrm{GSpin}(3,2))$
and distributes to all six lanes. The ``twenty-plus'' phrasing of
\S\ref{sec:delta5-meta-frontier-synthesis} collapses to
\emph{six} presentations with multiplicities $(3, 2, 3, 1, 2, 1)$.
The asymmetric distribution reflects the literature, not the
object: the motivic class has three independent lines
(Howard--Madapusi-Pera / Arthur / Weissauer), the derived class
one (Bridgeland--Smith). Closing the asymmetry --- a second
genuinely independent derived presentation --- is open; candidates
are the Maulik--Okounkov $R$-matrix on the Hilbert-scheme side and
a Kapustin--Rozansky--Saulina $3d$ gauge-theoretic realisation,
neither carried out at $(g,d,N) = (2,3,\infty)$. Scope: the
six-class reduction is \ClaimStatusTheorem{} at the level of
construction equivalence spelled out in the proof; the coherence
functor $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1 \rightsquigarrow \{\text{six lanes}\}$
factoring through a single derived stack is
\ClaimStatusConjectured, with two of the $\binom{6}{2} = 15$
commuting squares (Toen--Vezzosi / $\ell$-adic realisation) in the
literature, and the remaining thirteen open.
\end{remark}

\section{Nekrasov--Kontsevich meta-adversarial V3/10: the four-way
identity is \emph{not} on-the-nose}
\label{sec:nk-meta-v3-four-way-identity}

\subsection{Claim under scrutiny}

Proposition~\ref{prop:gv-kkv-k3xe-integrality-triple}
(line~$\approx 7545$) and the subsection ``GV/DT/BKM as one
integer in three disguises'' (line~$\approx 9336$) assert, for
$\alpha \in \Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_+(\fg_{\Delta_5})$ of norm
$\alpha^2 = 2h - 2$ and elliptic degree $\ell$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:nk-naive-four-way}
\mult_{\fg_{\Delta_5}}(\alpha)
\;\stackrel{?}{=}\;
c_{K3}(h, \ell)
\;\stackrel{?}{=}\;
n^0_{(\beta_h, \ell)}(K3 \times E)
\;\stackrel{?}{=}\;
N^{\mathrm{DT}}_{(\beta_h, \ell)}(K3 \times E).
\end{equation}
Adversarial test at $(h, \ell) = (1, 1)$.

\subsection{(a) On-the-nose reading is false at $(1, 1)$}

\emph{EZ coefficient.} $D = 4h - \ell^2 = 3$, so $c_\phi(3) = -64$
(Eichler--Zagier 1985, p.~108; line~$\approx 1240$, $3750$).
Under $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3) = 2\phi_{0,1}$ (line~$\approx 2748$,
$6223$, $7506$),
\(
c_{K3}(1, 1) = 2 \cdot c_\phi(3) = -128,
\)
consistent with $c_{K3}(1, 0) = -128$ (line~$\approx 7510$).

\emph{Gritsenko exponent.} $\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ doubles
Borcherds exponents (Gritsenko--Nikulin 1998;
Remark~\ref{rem:2f-equals-c-KKV-borcherds}): $c_{K3}(nh, \ell) =
2 f(nh, \ell)$, so $f(1, 1) = -64$.

\emph{BKM imaginary-root multiplicity.} At $h = 1$ the root
$\alpha$ has $\alpha^2 = 0$: lightlike. Lightlike multiplicities
are governed by the $\eta^9$-multiplier sector
(Gritsenko--Nikulin 1998 Cor.~3.3; line~$\approx 9324$:
$\tau(a) = 9 = 2 \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} - 1$), not bare $c_{K3}$.
Naive $\mult(\alpha) = -128$ fails because
(i) BKM multiplicities are non-negative;
(ii) Borcherds denominator attaches $f = -64$, not $c = -128$,
to $\Delta_5$;
(iii) BKM superalgebra convention
$\mult_{\bar 0}(\alpha) - \mult_{\bar 1}(\alpha) = f(h, \ell)$,
so $f = -64 < 0$ signals fermionic dominance at $D = 3$
(line~$\approx 1244$).

\emph{Gopakumar--Vafa.} $n^0_{1, 1} = -44$ (line~$\approx 795$)
contradicts both $c_{K3}(1, 1) = -128$ and $f(1, 1) = -64$: GV is
a multi-cover-subtracted reduced BPS count. KKV packages GV into
$\prod_m (1 - q^{m + h - 1} y^\ell)^{-c(h, \ell)}$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:oberdieck-k3e-delta10}); extracting $n^0$
requires $\chi_y(\mathrm{Hilb}^h K3)$, not bare Fourier readout.
At $h = 1$: $n^0_{(\beta_1, 0)} = c(1, 0) - 2 c(1, 1)$
(line~$\approx 7511$) gives $-128 - 2(-128) = 128$ in
$Z_{K3} = 2\phi_{0,1}$ (or $64$ in bare EZ).

\emph{Donaldson--Thomas.} $N^{\mathrm{DT}}$ is Behrend-weighted;
on $K3 \times E$ reduced normalisation forces a $-1$ orientation
prefactor (line~$\approx 6235$). Behrend DT differs from Euler
DT by $\nu_B$; they agree only on smooth moduli, failing for
Hilbert schemes of curves on $K3 \times E$ above minimum degree.

\subsection{(b) Corrected identity with explicit constants}

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:nk-healed-four-way}
\boxed{\;
\begin{aligned}
\mult_{\fg_{\Delta_5}}(\alpha)
&\;=\; f(h, \ell) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\, c_{K3}(h, \ell)
\quad\text{(Gritsenko squaring, }\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2\text{)},\\
n^0_{(\beta_h, 0)}(K3 \times E)
&\;=\; c_{K3}(h, 0) - 2\, c_{K3}(h, 1)
\quad\text{(KKV genus-}0\text{, }
\chi_y(\mathrm{Hilb}^h K3)\text{)},\\
N^{\mathrm{DT}}_{(\beta_h, \ell)}(K3 \times E)
&\;=\; -\, n^{\mathrm{PT}}_{(\beta_h, \ell)}(K3 \times E)
\quad\text{(MNOP reduced; Oberdieck 2018 sign)},
\end{aligned}\;}
\end{equation}
with normalisation constants
$\kappa_1 = \tfrac{1}{2},\ \kappa_2 = (c \mapsto c_0 - 2 c_1),\
\kappa_3 = -1,\ \kappa_4 = \nu_B$. At $(h, \ell) = (1, 1)$:
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.12}
\begin{tabular}{l r l}
\hline
Object & Value at $(1, 1)$ & Convention\\
\hline
$c_\phi(3)$ & $-64$ & EZ\\
$c_{K3}(1, 1)$ & $-128$ & $Z_{K3} = 2\phi_{0,1}$\\
$f(1, 1) = c_{K3} / 2$ & $-64$ & $\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$\\
$\mult_{\fg_{\Delta_5}}(\alpha)$, $\alpha^2 = 0$ &
\emph{lightlike, $\eta^9$-sector} & Borcherds denominator\\
$n^0_{(\beta_1, 0)}$ & $128$ ($Z_{K3}$) / $64$ (EZ) &
KKV linear $c_0 - 2 c_1$\\
$n^0_{1, 1}$ & $-44$ & reduced GV, $K3 \times E$\\
$N^{\mathrm{DT}}_{(\beta_1, 1)}$ & $+44$ & MNOP reduced,
Oberdieck\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
No two coincide on-the-nose. Constant graph:
$c_\phi \xrightarrow{\times 2} c_{K3} \xrightarrow{\div 2}
f = \mult\text{(real sector)} \xrightarrow{c_0 - 2 c_1}
n^0 \xrightarrow{-\nu_B} N^{\mathrm{DT}}.$

\subsection{(c) The constants \emph{are} the 4-way naturality data}

$(\tfrac{1}{2},\ c \mapsto c_0 - 2 c_1,\ -1,\ \nu_B)$ is the
naturality data of $\Phi$ on $K3 \times E$, recording how $\Phi$
intertwines four distinct categorical structures.
$\kappa_1 = \tfrac{1}{2}$ is the
$\mathrm{Aut}(\Phi_{10})$-to-$\mathrm{Aut}(\Delta_5)$ double cover
squaring in $M_*(\Sp_4(\Z))$.
$\kappa_2 = (c \mapsto c_0 - 2 c_1)$ is the
$\chi_y(\mathrm{Hilb}^h K3)$ Hodge-theoretic linearisation of KKV
(Göttsche 1990).
$\kappa_3 = -1$ is the reduced virtual-class orientation
(Oberdieck 2018).
$\kappa_4 = \nu_B$ is Behrend's microlocal function.
The mod-$64$ integrality $|f(1, 1)| = 64$ is exactly $\Phi_{10} =
\Delta_5^2$ applied to $c_{K3}(1, 1) = -128$: $|f| = 64$ is the
$\Delta_5$-exponent; the $2$-to-$1$ match to $|c_{K3}| = 128$ is
$\kappa_1 = \tfrac{1}{2}$.

``One integer in three disguises'' (line~$\approx 7568$, $9336$)
now reads: \emph{the four normalisation-corrected integers, once
$(\tfrac{1}{2}, c_0 - 2c_1, -1, \nu_B)$ are applied, parametrise
one $\Z$-graded root space of
$\mathrm{II}_{4, 20} \oplus \mathrm{II}_{1, 1}(-1)$}. The root
space is categorical; the integers counting it are
normalisation-dependent. Naive
Proposition~\ref{prop:gv-kkv-k3xe-integrality-triple} is
downgraded to \ClaimStatusConditional\ at character level; the
constant-corrected~\eqref{eq:nk-healed-four-way} is
\ClaimStatusTheorem\ via KKV $+$ MNOP $+$ OP $+$
Gritsenko--Nikulin assembled in
Theorem~\ref{thm:oberdieck-k3e-delta10}.

\section{BCOV channel: topological string on $K3\times E$, $\Delta_{10}$, and genus-$2$ Siegel automorphy}
\label{wn:sec:bcov-k3xe-siegel}

\subsection{BCOV equation on $K3\times E$ as modular-anomaly $E_2$-derivative}

On a compact CY$_3$ the BCOV holomorphic anomaly equation is
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:bcov-master}
\bar\partial_{\bar\imath} F_g = \tfrac12 \bar C^{jk}_{\bar\imath}
\Bigl(D_j D_k F_{g-1} + \sum_{r=1}^{g-1} D_j F_r D_k F_{g-r}\Bigr),
\qquad \bar C^{jk}_{\bar\imath} = e^{2K}\overline{C_{ijk}} G^{j\bar\jmath} G^{k\bar k}.
\end{equation}
For $X = K3\times E$ the complex moduli factorise,
$\cM_{\mathrm{cs}} = \cM_{\mathrm{cs}}(K3)\times \bH/\SL_2(\Z)$, with the K3
factor Griffiths-flat by holomorphic symplecticity and the $E$ factor supplying
the quasi-modular Eisenstein $E_2$. The Yukawa coupling factorises
$C_{ijk} = C^{K3}_{ij}\partial_{t_E}\tau_E + \text{cyclic}$, and the anomaly
reduces to a modular anomaly equation
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:bcov-modular-anomaly}
\Bigl(\partial_{\bar\tau_E} - \tfrac{1}{8\pi\,\mathrm{Im}\,\tau_E}
\partial_{E_2}\Bigr) Z_{\mathrm{top}}^{K3\times E} = 0,
\qquad E_2 = 1 - 24\sum_{n\ge 1}\sigma_1(n)q^n.
\end{equation}

\subsection{Conjectural solution via $1/\Delta_{10}$: genus-$g$ amplitudes as Humbert residues}

The proposed all-genus topological string partition function on $K3\times E$,
refined by the M-theory circle and $U(1)_R$ chemical potential, is
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:bcov-ztop-solution}
Z_{\mathrm{top}}^{K3\times E}(\Omega;\lambda,\bar t)
= \frac{\Theta_{K3}(\Omega;\lambda)}{\Delta_{10}(\Omega)}
= \frac{\Theta_{K3}(\Omega;\lambda)}{\Delta_5(\Omega)^2},
\end{equation}
with $\Omega = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}\tau_E & z\\ z & \sigma\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)
\in\bH_2$, $\sigma$ the wrapped-M$2$ modulus, $z$ the $U(1)_R$/class-$j$
potential, and $\Theta_{K3}$ a $\Sp_4(\Z)$-theta kernel from the Mukai
lattice. $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ is the Gritsenko--Nikulin doubling:
$\Delta_5$ is the BKM denominator of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ and its square is the
Igusa cusp form realising the denominator piece of the protected
DT/BPS partition function. The conjectural genus-$g$ amplitudes are
triple contour residues
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:genus-g-residue}
F_g^{K3\times E}(\lambda) = \oint_{\cC_g}
\frac{\Theta_{K3}(\Omega;\lambda)}{\Delta_{10}(\Omega)}
\lambda^{2g-2} d^3\Omega,
\end{equation}
with $\cC_g$ the Rankin--Selberg contour encircling the Humbert divisor
$H_1\subset\cA_2$ to order $2g-2$. Since
$\mathrm{ord}_{H_1}(\Delta_{10}) = 2$, the anomaly equation closes at all
genera with only a leading Humbert pole.

\begin{conjecture}[BCOV $=$ Humbert residue]
\label{wn:prop:bcov-humbert-residue}
\eqref{wn:eq:bcov-master} on $K3\times E$ is solved by~\eqref{wn:eq:bcov-ztop-solution}:
the anomaly operator $(\partial_{\bar\tau_E}
-\frac{1}{8\pi\mathrm{Im}\tau_E}\partial_{E_2})$ annihilates $1/\Delta_{10}$
up to a $\bar\partial$-exact term supported on $H_1$, and the residue
formula~\eqref{wn:eq:genus-g-residue} extracts $F_g$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Heuristic]
$\bH_2$ admits the Kodaira--Spencer splitting
$T_\Omega\bH_2 = T_{\tau_E}\bH\oplus T_\sigma\bH\oplus T_z\C$; $\Delta_{10}$
is holomorphic on $\bH_2$ with first-order vanishing on
$H_1 = \{z=0\}\cup\text{transl.}$ (Gritsenko--Nikulin, Igusa). The BCOV
anomaly pulls back to $\partial_{\bar\tau_E}\log\Delta_{10}$ which by the
Gritsenko additive-lift equals $24\cdot G_2^*(\tau_E) + \text{(BKM-imaginary)}$,
with $G_2^*$ the almost-holomorphic Eisenstein completion. The $24$ is the
K3 fibre-rank $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}$; this matches~\eqref{wn:eq:bcov-modular-anomaly}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Mirror map $T_E\leftrightarrow\tau_E$: hidden Siegel automorphy}

The BCOV partition function carries a hidden $\Sp_4(\Z)$-automorphy
invisible from the IIA complex-structure side. The mirror map is
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:mirror-map-bcov}
T_E\leftrightarrow\tau_E,\qquad T_{K3}\leftrightarrow\sigma,
\qquad (\text{heterotic Wilson line})\leftrightarrow z,
\end{equation}
with LHS K\"ahler moduli (IIA on $K3\times E$) and RHS Siegel periods
(IIB on the mirror). $(T_E,T_{K3},W)\mapsto\Omega\in\bH_2$ lifts the
$T$-duality $T_E\to -1/T_E$ together with the Wilson-line
$\OO(\Gamma^{2,2})$ action to the full paramodular $\Sp_4(\Z)$ action,
yielding the genus-$2$ automorphy
\begin{equation}
Z_{\mathrm{top}}^{K3\times E}(\gamma\cdot\Omega)
= \det(C\Omega+D)^{10}\, Z_{\mathrm{top}}^{K3\times E}(\Omega),
\qquad \gamma\in\Sp_4(\Z),
\end{equation}
of weight $10 = \mathrm{wt}(\Delta_{10})$ matching the doubled BKM weight
$\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10})=2\,\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)$.

\begin{conjecture}[BCOV--Siegel correspondence on $K3\times E$]
\label{wn:thm:bcov-siegel-k3-e}
$\{F_g^{K3\times E}\}_{g\ge 0}$ assemble into the Igusa
ratio~\eqref{wn:eq:bcov-ztop-solution}, a meromorphic Siegel modular form
of weight $-10$ with a double pole on $H_1\subset\cA_2$. The BCOV
anomaly~\eqref{wn:eq:bcov-master} is equivalent, under the mirror
map~\eqref{wn:eq:mirror-map-bcov}, to
$\partial_{\bar\Omega}\log\Delta_{10} = \mathrm{Sym}^2(\partial_{\bar\tau}\log\Delta_5)$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{corollary}[Four $\kappa_\bullet$ at four Siegel degenerations]
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E)=0$ at the cusp $\sigma\to i\infty$
(K\"unneth-multiplicative);
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}=3$ at the $E$-diagonal
boundary, while the compact Hodge supertrace is $\Xi=0$;
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=5$ at $H_1$ as
$\mathrm{ord}_{H_1}\Delta_5 = 1$; $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}} = 24$ from
the K3 fibre-rank in the $G_2^*$ anomaly term. The bare-$\chi/24$
false identity $F_g^{\mathrm{BCOV}} = \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}\lambda_g^{\mathrm{FP}}$
is corrected to $F_g^{K3\times E} =
\mathrm{Res}_{H_1}(\Theta_{K3}/\Delta_{10})\cdot\lambda^{2g-2}$.
\end{corollary}

\section{Beilinson--Drinfeld channel: constructibility
of $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ as a derived Shimura stack}
\label{wn:sec:cG-mn-constructibility}

\subsection*{(a) Attack: is $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ constructible?}

Definition~\ref{def:cG-moonshine} exhibits
$\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ as an $(\infty,1)$-groupoid but stops at the
$\pi_0/\pi_1$ census of
Proposition~\ref{prop:pi0-cG-moonshine}, leaving open whether
the moduli functor
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:cG-mn-moduli-functor}
\mathscr{F}_{\mathrm{mn}}:\;\mathrm{CAlg}^{\mathrm{cn}}_{\Z[1/N_{\mathrm{bad}}]}
\;\longrightarrow\;\mathcal{S},\qquad
R \;\longmapsto\; \bigl\{R\text{-families of }(L,\Theta,\Psi,\iota)\bigr\}
\end{equation}
is representable by a (derived) geometric stack. Four obstructions
block na\"ive representability and drive the attack.

\emph{(A1) Lattice component is discrete but unbounded.} $L$ ranges
over even lattices of varying signature $(p,q)$, $p+q\le 26$, so
$\pi_0(\mathscr{F}_{\mathrm{mn}})$ is an infinite discrete set. No
single affine scheme can parametrise all $L$; one is forced into an
infinite disjoint union indexed by genera in the Nikulin sense.

\emph{(A2) Modular-form component is infinite-dimensional.} For fixed
$L$, the data $\Theta$ of weight $w$ with character $\chi$ ranges over
$M_w(O^+(L),\chi)$, whose dimension grows $\sim C\cdot w^{p+q-1}$
(Hirzebruch--Mumford). Without bounding $w$, the fibre of
$\mathscr{F}_{\mathrm{mn}} \to \{L\}$ is not even a scheme of
finite type.

\emph{(A3) Borcherds-lift component is not a scheme map.} The input
$F \in M^{!}_{1-p/2}(\rho_L)$ is a vector-valued weakly holomorphic
modular form with \emph{integer} Fourier coefficients $c_F(m,\mu)$ at
negative indices; $\Psi$ depends on $F$ through a transcendental
infinite product
$\Psi(F) = e^{((\rho,Z))}\prod_{\lambda>0}\prod_\mu
(1 - e^{((\lambda,Z))+(\mu,\cdot)})^{c_F(-\lambda^2/2,\mu)}$.
The assignment $F\mapsto\Psi(F)$ is a $\Z$-linear map on Fourier
coefficients but its target is a section of a line bundle on
$\cD_L / O^+(L)$; representability requires the target line bundle to
be coherent over the base.

\emph{(A4) BKM-identification $\iota$ is not a property; it is
structure.} The Weyl--Kac denominator identity
$\mathrm{Denom}(\Theta) = e^{-\rho}\prod_{\alpha\in\Delta^+(L)}
(1-e^{-\alpha})^{\mathrm{mult}(\alpha)}$
is a \emph{chosen} isomorphism between the Borcherds product and a
BKM denominator, not a condition automatically satisfied. The space
of such isomorphisms is a torsor under the automorphism group of
the BKM, i.e.~$O^+(L)$ acting on root data; thus $\iota$ contributes
a 1-stack level.

The four obstructions are additive; their resolution forces a
\emph{derived geometric stack} of countably many components, with
each component a derived Shimura-type stack. We construct this stack
below and identify its tangent complex with period data.

\subsection*{(b) Healed construction: $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ as a derived
Shimura stack glued from per-lattice Siegel moduli}

\begin{definition}[Per-lattice derived Shimura stack]
\label{wn:def:RShim-L}
For an even lattice $L$ of signature $(p,q)$ with $q\in\{2,3\}$ (the
range covering $\Delta_5,\Delta_{10},\Phi_N,\Delta_{\mathrm{Mon}},
\Omega_g$), let
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:RShim-L-def}
\bR\mathrm{Shim}_L \;:=\; \bigl[\,
(\cD_L)^{\mathrm{der}} \,/\, O^+(L)\,\bigr]
\;\in\; \mathrm{dSt}_{\infty}
\end{equation}
be the derived quotient stack of the complexified symmetric domain
$\cD_L = O(L\otimes\R)/K_L$ (a Hermitian symmetric domain of
non-compact type) by the discrete group $O^+(L)$ acting properly
discontinuously. The derived enhancement takes $\cD_L$ as an analytic
derived scheme with structure sheaf $\Omega^\bullet_{\cD_L}$ and
$O^+(L)$ acting by derived-equivalences. At $L = 2U\oplus 2E_8(-1)$
this is the derived Siegel stack $\bR\cA_2$; at
$L = \mathrm{II}_{1,25}$ this is the derived Baily--Borel locally
symmetric space of the Leech lattice.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Modular-form fibration]
\label{wn:def:modular-form-fibration}
Over $\bR\mathrm{Shim}_L$ sits the tower
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:modular-form-tower}
\bR\mathrm{ModForm}_L
\;:=\; \bigsqcup_{w\in\tfrac12\Z}\bigsqcup_{\chi}
\bR\Gamma\bigl(\bR\mathrm{Shim}_L;\,\cL_{w,\chi}\bigr),
\end{equation}
with $\cL_{w,\chi}$ the automorphic line bundle of weight $w$ and
character $\chi$ (the Hodge bundle $\lambda^{\otimes w}$ twisted by
$\chi$). Each summand is a perfect complex over the affine base of
$\bR\mathrm{Shim}_L$; the tower is countable but each term is finite-
dimensional by the Hirzebruch--Mumford vanishing
$H^{>0}(\cL_{w,\chi}) = 0$ for $w\gg 0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Borcherds section]
\label{wn:def:borcherds-section}
The Borcherds lift is a map of derived stacks
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:borcherds-derived-map}
\Psi_L:\;\bR M^{!}_{1-p/2}(\rho_L)^{\Z} \;\longrightarrow\;
\bR\mathrm{ModForm}_L,\qquad
F \;\longmapsto\; \Psi_L(F),
\end{equation}
where the domain is the derived scheme of vector-valued weakly
holomorphic modular forms with $\Z$-integer singular Fourier
coefficients (a countable union of affine lines indexed by principal
parts). The map $\Psi_L$ is a closed immersion onto its image: its
tangent at $F$ is the Kudla--Millson theta kernel
$\Theta_{\mathrm{KM}}(F)$ viewed as an element of
$H^{p,q}(\cD_L,\cL_{w(F)})$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[BKM-identification stack]
\label{wn:def:iota-stack}
Let $\bR\mathrm{BKM}_L$ be the derived stack of BKM Lie superalgebra
structures with root datum $(L,\Delta(L),\mathrm{mult})$. An object
is $(\mathfrak{g},\{e_\alpha,f_\alpha,h_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\Delta})$,
modulo the $O^+(L)$-action on root data. The $\iota$-datum is an
isomorphism $\iota: \mathrm{Denom}(\Theta) \xrightarrow{\sim}
\mathrm{Denom}_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\mathfrak{g})$ of formal power series
in $e^{-\alpha}$; the space of such isomorphisms is an
$O^+(L)$-torsor, making $\bR\mathrm{BKM}_L$ a gerbe over its coarse
space banded by $O^+(L)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Constructibility of $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$]
\label{wn:thm:cG-mn-constructibility}
The moduli functor~\eqref{wn:eq:cG-mn-moduli-functor} is representable
in $\mathrm{DAG}_\infty$ by the derived geometric stack
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:cG-mn-representing-stack}
\cG_{\mathrm{mn}} \;=\; \bigsqcup_{[L]\in\mathrm{Gen}(p,q)}
\bigl(\Psi_L \times_{\bR\mathrm{ModForm}_L} \bR\mathrm{BKM}_L\bigr),
\end{equation}
the disjoint union over Nikulin genera $[L]$ of even lattices with
$p+q\le 26$ of the fibre products of the Borcherds
section~\eqref{wn:eq:borcherds-derived-map} with the BKM-identification
gerbe of Definition~\ref{wn:def:iota-stack} over the
modular-form tower~\eqref{wn:eq:modular-form-tower}. Each component
is a derived Artin stack locally of finite type over $\Z[1/N_{\mathrm{bad}}]$.
The gluing across genera is via primitive-embedding correspondences:
for $L\hookrightarrow L'$ primitive, the pullback $\varphi^*$
induces a derived morphism $\bR\mathrm{Shim}_{L'}\dashrightarrow
\bR\mathrm{Shim}_L \times_{} \bR\mathrm{Shim}_{L'/\varphi(L)^\perp}$
(Kudla--Rapoport special cycle), and the full
$\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$-nerve is the colimit over this category of
primitive embeddings.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
(A1) is resolved by the disjoint union over $\mathrm{Gen}(p,q)$:
each Nikulin genus is a finite set (Nikulin finiteness), and
$p+q\le 26$ truncates to finitely many genera per signature.
(A2) is resolved fibrewise: each $\cL_{w,\chi}$ on
$\bR\mathrm{Shim}_L$ has finite-dimensional cohomology by
Hirzebruch--Mumford proportionality, and the tower
$\bR\mathrm{ModForm}_L$ is a derived scheme locally of
finite presentation.
(A3) is the content of Borcherds' embedding theorem: the image
of $\Psi_L$ is cut out by the Borcherds product identities, which
on Fourier-coefficient level are polynomial in $c_F(m,\mu)$.
Pullback of sections along the closed immersion
$\Psi_L$~\eqref{wn:eq:borcherds-derived-map} preserves perfectness.
(A4) is absorbed into the gerbe structure of
Definition~\ref{wn:def:iota-stack}: the band is
$O^+(L)$, the Artin-stack structure is standard
(Laumon--Moret-Bailly).
Gluing across genera uses Kudla--Rapoport's derived special-cycle
formalism: a primitive embedding $\varphi:L\hookrightarrow L'$
defines a Hecke correspondence between $\bR\mathrm{Shim}_{L'}$ and
$\bR\mathrm{Shim}_L\times\bR\mathrm{Shim}_{L^\perp}$, and the
Borcherds product $\Psi_{L'}(F')$ pulls back to
$\Psi_L(\varphi^*F')\cdot\Psi_{L^\perp}(F'^\perp)$ (Borcherds
pullback identity). The colimit of this primitive-embedding diagram
in $\mathrm{dSt}_\infty$ is $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{(c) Tangent complex $=$ period data}

\begin{theorem}[Tangent complex at $\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$]
\label{wn:thm:tangent-complex}
At the basepoint $\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5} = (2U\oplus 2E_8(-1),
\Delta_5,\Psi_{\mathrm{Grit}},\iota_{\Delta_5})$ the tangent complex
of $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ is
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:tangent-complex-delta5}
\bT_{\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}}\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}
\;\simeq\;
\underbrace{\mathfrak{sp}_4(\R)/\mathfrak{k}}_{\text{degree }0,\;
\text{Siegel period}}
\;\oplus\;
\underbrace{\mathrm{PrincPart}(F_5)}_{\text{degree }0,\;
\text{Borcherds input}}
\;\oplus\;
\underbrace{H^1(\bR\mathrm{BKM}_{\Lambda^{3,2}},\mathrm{ad})[-1]}_{\text{degree }1,\;
\iota\text{-deformation}}.
\end{equation}
The degree-$0$ summand is the tangent to the Siegel moduli space
$\cA_2 = \bH_2/\Sp_4(\Z)$ at the period of $\Delta_5$ (paramodular
lattice $\Lambda^{3,2}$ per
Theorem~$3$ of \textsc{Lorgat}~$2020$); the Borcherds-input summand
is the finite-dimensional principal-part
space of $F_5 \in M^{!}_{-1/2}(\rho_{\Lambda^{3,2}})$;
the degree-$1$ summand encodes Fricke-involution and
$O^+(\Lambda^{3,2})$-equivariance deformations of the
BKM-identification.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Differentiate~\eqref{wn:eq:cG-mn-representing-stack} at
$\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$. The per-lattice factor contributes
$\bT\bR\mathrm{Shim}_{\Lambda^{3,2}} \simeq \mathfrak{sp}_4(\R)/\mathfrak{k}$
(Harish-Chandra decomposition at the Siegel upper half-plane);
this is the period data of $\Delta_5$ (the Hodge structure on
$H^3(X,\Q)$ for $X$ the $\mathrm{CY}_3$ with $\Delta_5$-BKM symmetry,
per \textsc{Lorgat}~$2020$~\S$1$). The Borcherds section
$\Psi_{\Lambda^{3,2}}$ is a closed immersion, so its differential is
the inclusion of the principal part of $F_5$ (negative Fourier
coefficients $f(1,1,1) = 64$ and the ten theta-constant principal
parts controlling $\Delta_5 = \prod v_{a,b}$). The gerbe
$\bR\mathrm{BKM}_{\Lambda^{3,2}}$ contributes
$H^1(\mathrm{BO}^+(\Lambda^{3,2}),\mathrm{ad}\,\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5})$
in degree $1$, by standard gerbe-tangent computation
(Laumon--Moret-Bailly Thm $8.1$). The direct sum is orthogonal because
the three factors are transverse in
$\Psi_{L}\times_{\bR\mathrm{ModForm}_L}\bR\mathrm{BKM}_L$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Relation to $\bR\cA_g$]
\label{wn:cor:cG-mn-vs-R-A-g}
The first summand of~\eqref{wn:eq:tangent-complex-delta5} identifies
$\bT_{\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}}\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ with
$\bT_{[\Delta_5]}\bR\cA_2$ up to the Borcherds-input and
$\iota$-deformation corrections; there is a forgetful morphism
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:forgetful-to-RAg}
u: \cG_{\mathrm{mn}} \;\longrightarrow\;
\bigsqcup_{g\ge 1} \bR\cA_g,\qquad
(L,\Theta,\Psi,\iota)\mapsto \text{Siegel domain of }\Theta,
\end{equation}
realising $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ as a Borcherds-lifted enhancement of
the derived Siegel moduli tower. The fibre of $u$ over
$[\Delta_5]\in\bR\cA_2$ is $\Psi_{\Lambda^{3,2}}^{-1}(\Delta_5)
\times\bR\mathrm{BKM}_{\Lambda^{3,2}}$: the discrete set of
Borcherds-preimages (principal parts mapping to $\Delta_5$) times
the $O^+(\Lambda^{3,2})$-banded gerbe of BKM-identifications.
\end{corollary}

\section{Toen--Beilinson channel: reconciliation of
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ and $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ as completion and
ambient groupoid}
\label{sec:toen-beilinson-hath1-vs-Gmn}

Two objects appear at neighbouring frontier entries.
Remark~\ref{rem:delta5-humbert-coherence-functor-v1}
introduces the derived formal completion
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1 := \bR\cA_2 \times^{\bL}_{\cA_2} H_1^{\mathrm{fm}}$
of the Humbert divisor $H_1 = \Div(\Delta_5) \subset \cA_2$ in the
Toen--Vezzosi derived-stack category. Definition
\ref{def:cG-moonshine} introduces the
$(\infty,1)$-groupoid $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ of moonshine data with
basepoint $\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5} = ((2U \oplus 2E_8(-1)), \Delta_5,
\Psi_{\mathrm{Grit}}, \iota_{\Delta_5})$. The adversarial question:
are $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ and $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ the same object
viewed through two lenses, different facets of a larger structure,
or distinct mathematical objects standing in a precise functorial
relation?

\subsection*{(a) They are not the same object}

\begin{proposition}[Dimension and $\pi_0$ distinguish
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ from $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$]
\label{prop:hath1-ne-Gmn}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ and $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ are not equivalent
as derived stacks / $(\infty,1)$-groupoids:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\pi_0(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1)$ is a single point (the formal
neighbourhood of $H_1$ in $\cA_2$ has connected classical support
$H_1 \subset \cA_2$, itself an irreducible divisor of dimension
$2$); $\pi_0(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$ contains at least the five classes
$\{[\Delta_5], [\Delta_{10}], [\Phi_N]_{N \in \{1,2,3,4,6\}},
[\Delta_{\mathrm{Mon}}], [\Omega_g]_{g \in M_{24}}\}$ of
Proposition~\ref{prop:pi0-cG-moonshine}, pairwise
non-equivalent (different underlying lattices $L$: signature
$(3,2)$ for $\Delta_5$, signature $(2, 26)$ for
$\Delta_{\mathrm{Mon}}$, signature $(1, 25)$ for Monster Leech,
etc.).
\item Dimension: $\dim H_1 = 2$, so $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ has
classical dimension $2$ with derived corrections from normal-bundle
conormal intersection; $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ has positive-dimensional
$\pi_1$ at $[\Delta_5]$ of rank $\geq \mathrm{rk}(\Sp_4(\Z)) \cdot
\mathrm{rk}(\mathrm{Aut}(2U \oplus 2E_8(-1)))$, and ranges across
lattices of signature up to $(2, 26)$ and ambient-dimension up to
$26$.
\item Ambient category: $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1 \in
\mathrm{dSt}_{\mathrm{TV}}/\Spec\Z$ is a derived stack;
$\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ is an $(\infty,1)$-groupoid in the
Kan-complex/quasi-category sense. The two ambient categories embed
via Toen--Vezzosi $\mathrm{dSt} \to \mathrm{dSt}(\mathrm{Spc})$ but
not identically.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For (1): objects in $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ are quadruples
$(L, \Theta, \Psi, \iota)$ with $L$ varying over even lattices of
all signatures admitting a Borcherds lift. Two objects with
non-isomorphic $L$ lie in different components of $\pi_0$ because a
$1$-morphism $(\varphi, \beta, \gamma)$ requires a primitive
lattice embedding $\varphi: L \hookrightarrow L'$ (or the reverse);
$L = 2U \oplus 2E_8(-1)$ of signature $(3, 2)$ does not embed
primitively into $L' = II_{2, 26}$ of signature $(2, 26)$ with
compatible Borcherds lift (the signatures are incompatible at the
Weyl-vector level: Gritsenko $\Delta_5$-Weyl vector has
$\rho^2 = 5/6$ under normalisation, Monster Weyl vector has
$\rho^2 = -1/2$; the discriminant forms on
$\mathrm{disc}(2U \oplus 2E_8(-1)) = \{0\}$ and
$\mathrm{disc}(II_{2, 26}) = \{0\}$ are both trivial, but the
orthogonal $L'/\varphi(L)$ would require an $II_{-1, 24}$ factor
with a Gritsenko-compatible Borcherds Weyl-vector shift, which is
the Borcherds--Leech identification of
Theorem~\ref{thm:delta10-saito-kurokawa-arthur-parameter}: one
direction only, and only at the level of Heegner-divisor
restriction, not as a lattice embedding of the full
$(L, \Theta, \Psi, \iota)$-quadruple).
For (2): $H_1 \subset \cA_2 = \Sp_4(\Z) \backslash \bH_2$ is the
Humbert surface of discriminant $1$, a closed substack of
dimension $\dim \cA_2 - 1 = 2$; its derived formal completion in
the Toen--Vezzosi sense keeps the same classical dimension and
adds finite derived corrections in negative cohomological degree.
For (3): Toen--Vezzosi derived stacks and $(\infty,1)$-groupoids
are distinct ambient categories; the former has affine replacements
$\mathrm{cdga}_{\geq 0}$-valued, the latter Kan-complex-valued.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{(b) They stand in a precise relation: $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1
= \Omega_{\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}}\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$ at the
tangent-complex level}

\begin{theorem}[Basepoint relation]
\label{thm:hath1-as-tangent-complex}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
Let $\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$ denote the connected component of
$\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ reachable from $\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$ by finite
zigzags of $1$-morphisms (the moonshine-connected moduli;
Theorem~\ref{thm:moonshine-findings-as-homs}). Then
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:hath1-tangent-complex}
\widehat{\mathbf H}_1 \;\simeq\;
\mathrm{Spec}\bigl(\bR \mathrm{Sym}^{\bullet}_{\cO_{\cA_2}}
\mathbb T_{\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}}[\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}]^{\vee}[-1]\bigr)
\end{equation}
as derived formal neighbourhoods of the classical point
$[\Delta_5] \in H_1 \subset \cA_2$, where
$\mathbb T_{\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}}[\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}]$ is
the Toen--Vezzosi tangent complex of $\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$ at
the basepoint, and the right-hand side is the formal-neighbourhood
spectrum of its shifted Koszul--Sym dg-algebra.
Equivalently, $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ is the derived formal
completion of $\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$ at the basepoint
$\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$ pulled back along the classifying
morphism $\kappa_{\Delta_5}: \cA_2 \to \cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$
sending $[A] \in \cA_2$ to $[(A, \Theta_A, \Psi_A, \iota_A)]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The classifying morphism $\kappa_{\Delta_5}: \cA_2 \to
\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$ exists by the universal property of the
moduli stack $\cA_2$ of principally polarised abelian surfaces:
each $[A]$ determines $(L_A, \Theta_A, \Psi_A, \iota_A)$ where
$L_A$ is the Mukai-like lattice $H^{\mathrm{even}}(A, \Z)$ twisted
by the polarisation, $\Theta_A$ is the restriction of
$\Delta_5$-data to $[A]$, and $\iota_A$ is the BKM tautological
datum. At the basepoint $[\Delta_5]$ on the Humbert locus
$H_1 \subset \cA_2$, the classifying morphism has fibre
$\kappa_{\Delta_5}^{-1}(\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}) = H_1$ by
construction (the Humbert discriminant-$1$ divisor is precisely
the locus where the abelian-surface fibre sees the
$\Delta_5$-modular-form datum). Derived formal completion commutes
with pullback along smooth morphisms
(Toen--Vezzosi \emph{HAG II} \S$2.2$, or Gaitsgory--Rozenblyum
\emph{A Study in Derived Algebraic Geometry} Vol I, \S II.7), so
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1 \simeq \cA_2 \times^{\bL}_{\cG^{\circ}_{
\mathrm{mn}}} \widehat{\mathbf{1}}_{\Delta_5}$ where
$\widehat{\mathbf{1}}_{\Delta_5}$ is the formal completion of
$\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$ at the basepoint. The tangent-complex
identification \eqref{eq:hath1-tangent-complex} follows from the
standard Toen--Vezzosi identification of the derived formal
completion with the formal spectrum of the Chevalley--Eilenberg /
shifted Koszul dg-algebra of the tangent Lie algebra at the
basepoint (Pridham, Lurie \emph{DAG X}).
\end{proof}

\subsection*{(c) Mnemonic and scope}

The relation answers the adversarial question directly:
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ is neither the same object as
$\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ nor a disjoint one. It is the
\emph{derived formal completion of $\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$ at
the basepoint $\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$, pulled back to $\cA_2$} along
the classifying morphism. At the tangent-complex level
(first-order derived geometry), $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ \emph{is}
the formal-spectrum avatar of the tangent Lie algebra
$\mathbb T_{\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}} \cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$. This
is stronger than ``tangent space''. The shifted Koszul
identification makes
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ a derived scheme with classical support
$H_1$, while $\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$ is a positive-dimensional
ambient groupoid. The six functors of
Remark~\ref{rem:delta5-humbert-coherence-functor-v1} factor through
the completion: they are images under tangent-complex realisations
of six natural functors on $\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$ evaluated at
$\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$.

Equivalently: ``V1'' and ``V9'' do not compete. V1 zooms into the
infinitesimal neighbourhood of $\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$ in the
Toen--Vezzosi derived category, where the BKM factorisation
$\cF_{\fg_{\Delta_5}}$ lives as an $E_2$-algebra structure on the
cotangent deformation theory. V9 stands back to exhibit the
ambient moduli groupoid whose hom-spaces organise the wave findings.
The relation is completion to ambient, tangent-complex avatar to
total groupoid.

\subsection*{(d) Scope and caveats}

\textbf{Scope.} Proposition~\ref{prop:hath1-ne-Gmn} is
\ClaimStatusTheorem{} because $\pi_0$, dimension, and ambient
category are checkable invariants. Theorem~\ref{thm:hath1-as-tangent-complex}
is \ClaimStatusConjectured{} because the classifying morphism
$\kappa_{\Delta_5}: \cA_2 \to \cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$ has only
been constructed at the level of $\pi_0$ (assigning each point
$[A] \in \cA_2$ its Mukai-lattice quadruple); the higher-coherence
$(\infty,1)$-functoriality (pentagon coherence across Fricke
involutions $\in$ $\pi_2(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$) remains open. What is
unconditional on the classical part: $H_1 \subset \cA_2$ is the
pullback of the basepoint under the set-theoretic $\kappa_{\Delta_5,
0}$ at the level of $\pi_0$, by Gritsenko--Hulek $1998$
$\Div(\Delta_5)=H_1$ and Bruinier--Howard--Kudla--Rapoport--Yang
$2020$ Heegner-divisor reciprocity.

\textbf{Caveat.} The identification
\eqref{eq:hath1-tangent-complex} is at the formal / infinitesimal
level. The global classifying morphism $\kappa_{\Delta_5}$ is
\emph{not} an equivalence of stacks: $\cA_2$ has dimension $3$,
$\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$ has positive-dimensional automorphism
groups and higher homotopy. The basepoint $\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$
is the unique preimage of $H_1$; other components of
$\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$ (e.g.\ $[\Phi_N]$) are not in the
image of $\kappa_{\Delta_5}$.

\textbf{Chain-level vs $(\infty,1)$-categorical parity.} Both
lanes apply:
(i)~chain-level: $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ as the Koszul--Sym shifted
dg-algebra on the tangent complex is computed by explicit
Chevalley--Eilenberg coresolution of the BKM Lie superalgebra
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$ truncated to its imaginary-root generators at
norm $0$ (Borcherds superalgebra structure of
Theorem~\ref{thm:borcherds-weight-kappa-BKM-universal});
(ii)~$(\infty,1)$-categorical: the tangent-complex identification
is an equivalence of pro-dgla's in the sense of
Pridham--Lurie, and the completion statement lives in
$\mathrm{dSt}_{\mathrm{TV}}(\Spec\Z)$.

\textbf{Cross-reference.} The six-coherence-functor statement
of Remark~\ref{rem:delta5-humbert-coherence-functor-v1} is
the \emph{image} of the five hom-space statement of
Theorem~\ref{thm:moonshine-findings-as-homs} under the
tangent-complex realisation at the basepoint: each hom-space
$\mathrm{Map}_{\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}}(\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5},
[-])$ produces, via infinitesimal completion, a derived-pullback
sheaf on $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$, whose six distinct realisation
functors (Hodge theta, Weyl--Kac--Borcherds denominator, $\ell$-adic
Galois-motivic, Bridgeland-stability, AdS/CFT, classical
truncation) are the six projections of
Remark~\ref{rem:delta5-humbert-coherence-functor-v1}.

\section{Kontsevich--Costello channel:
$\mathbf{F1}$ as one framing of a derived-Borcherds correspondence,
not the apex}
\label{wn:sec:kc-f1-framings}

\subsection*{Target}

The meta-adversarial pass (\S\ref{sec:frontier-meta-adversarial},
lines~$15061$, $15087$--$15129$) declared
$\mathbf{F1} = \{\Phi_3$ morphism-preservation on $\CY_3$-cat$\}$
the ``category-theoretic apex''.
Three alternatives present:
\begin{align}
\label{wn:eq:f1-alt-framings}
\mathbf{F1}\phantom{'''}
&:\; \Phi_3: (\CY_3\text{-cat})_{(\infty,1)} \to
(E_1\text{-}\ChirAlg)_{(\infty,1)} \text{ is an }
(\infty,1)\text{-functor}, \\
\mathbf{F1'}\phantom{''}
&:\; \exists\,\bR\BorLift :
\D(J_{0,1}^{\mathrm{wk}})_{(\infty,1)} \to
\D(\mathrm{Sg}_5)_{(\infty,1)}, \\
\mathbf{F1''}\phantom{'}
&:\; \exists\,\cF: \CY_3\text{-cat} \to
\Fact_{E_2}(\mathrm{Sg}), \text{ a BKM-factorisation functor}, \\
\mathbf{F1'''}
&:\; \widehat{\mathbf H}_1 \rightsquigarrow \{\text{six-projection
data}\} \text{ of Remark~\ref{rem:delta5-humbert-coherence-functor-v1}}.
\end{align}
$J_{0,1}^{\mathrm{wk}}$ is the category of weak Jacobi forms of
index~$1$, $\mathrm{Sg}_5 \subset S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$ the
paramodular slice, $\Fact_{E_2}(\mathrm{Sg})$ the Segal category of
$E_2$-factorisation algebras. Adversarial attack: is $\mathbf{F1}$
genuinely apex, or one of four equivalent specialisations?

\subsection*{(a) Alternatives analysed}

\paragraph{$\mathbf{F1}$ (Vol~III native).} Domain: smooth proper
CY$_3$-categories (Kontsevich--Soibelman). Codomain: $E_1$-chiral
algebras (Costello--Gwilliam). Object-level $\Phi_3(A) = A_{\mathrm{ch}}$
is proved (CY-A$_3$, line~$183$); what is open is coherence along
$1$-morphisms. The obstruction lives in $\HH^{-2}_{E_1}$ \emph{along}
morphisms, not on objects: at objects the vanishing is proved.

\paragraph{$\mathbf{F1'}$ (Borcherds--Gritsenko native).}
$\bR\BorLift$ is the derived enhancement of
$\BorLift: J_{0,1}^{\mathrm{wk}} \to M_*^{\mathrm{mer}}(\Sp_4(\Z))$.
Classical $\BorLift$ is set-theoretic; the derived enhancement is
forced by monoidal structure --- $\BorLift(\phi \cdot \psi) =
\BorLift(\phi) \cdot \BorLift(\psi)$ up to Gritsenko squaring
$\BorLift(\phi_{0,1})^2 = \Delta_{10}$ (line~$15187$) --- and
promotes to a symmetric-monoidal $(\infty,1)$-functor on the stable
$(\infty,1)$-category of Jacobi-form chain complexes (mock/quasi
included, per Zwegers--Bringmann).

\paragraph{$\mathbf{F1''}$ (Costello--Gwilliam native).} $\cF$ is the
factorisation upgrade: CY$_3$-category to $E_2$-Segal factorisation
algebra on a Siegel base. $E_2$-structure is forced because at
$d = 3$ the chiral-algebra target has an $E_2$ centre (line~$183$:
``$E_2$ lives on $Z(\Rep(A))$''). This is the factorisation
incarnation of $\Phi_3$ at functor level.

\paragraph{$\mathbf{F1'''}$ (Humbert coherence).}
Remark~\ref{rem:delta5-humbert-coherence-functor-v1}: the six
equivalence classes are images of
$(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1, \cF_{\fg_{\Delta_5}})$ under six named
coherence functors; coherence $=$ $\Sp_4(\Z)$-equivariant
commutativity.

\subsection*{(b) Equivalences proved / contested}

\begin{proposition}[F$1 \Leftrightarrow$ F$1''$]
\label{wn:prop:f1-f1pp-equivalence}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
$\mathbf{F1}$ implies $\mathbf{F1''}$, and $\mathbf{F1''}$ implies
$\mathbf{F1}$ via the forgetful functor $\Fact_{E_2}(\mathrm{Sg})
\to E_1\text{-}\ChirAlg$ extracting the $E_1$ underlying the
factorisation $E_2$-structure.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
$\mathbf{F1} \Rightarrow \mathbf{F1''}$: the Costello--Gwilliam
factorisation envelope applied to $\Phi_3(A)$ produces a factorisation
algebra; the $E_2$ refinement is $Z(\Rep(\Phi_3(A)))$ carrying the
$E_2$-operad action by Lurie--Francis. Conversely, $\Fact_{E_2}$-%
objects forget to $E_1$ via $E_1 \hookrightarrow E_2$. Functoriality
in $\CY_3$-cat is preserved: both envelope and forgetful are
$(\infty,1)$-continuous.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[F$1' \Leftrightarrow$ F$1'''$]
\label{wn:prop:f1p-f1ppp-equivalence}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
$\mathbf{F1'}$ is the Hodge theta-realisation projection of
$\mathbf{F1'''}$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The Hodge theta-realisation functor $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1 \to
\{P_1, P_3, P_9\}$ of
Remark~\ref{rem:delta5-humbert-coherence-functor-v1} factors through
$(J_{0,1}^{\mathrm{wk}})_{(\infty,1)} \to (S_5(\Sp_4(\Z),
\nu_{\Delta_5}))_{(\infty,1)}$, sending a weak Jacobi form $\phi_{0,1}$
to its $(\BorLift, \GritLift, \mathrm{DMVV})$ triple image --- a
single class per
Proposition~\ref{prop:delta5-six-equivalence-classes-v1}(1). Closing
the square with $\Sp_4(\Z)$-equivariance reproduces $\bR\BorLift$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[F$1 \Leftrightarrow$ F$1'$: Kontsevich--Costello
correspondence]
\label{wn:prop:f1-f1p-kc-correspondence}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
$\mathbf{F1} \Leftrightarrow \mathbf{F1'}$ holds modulo the
Kontsevich--Costello correspondence: every elliptic-genus-carrying
CY$_3$-category $A$ determines, via its periods,
$\phi_A(\tau, z) = \mathrm{Tr}_A(q^{L_0 - c/24} y^{J_0}) \in
J_{0,1}^{\mathrm{wk}}$, and $\Phi_3(A)$ is realised on the
Borcherds-lifted Siegel side. Morphism-preservation of $\mathbf{F1}$
is equivalent to the derived enhancement of $\mathbf{F1'}$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Scope / contested]
On $K3 \times E$: direct. $\phi_{K3} = 2\phi_{0,1}$,
$\Phi_3(K3 \times E)$ contains $H_{\Delta_5}$,
$\BorLift(\phi_{0,1})$ generates $\Delta_5$. Off $K3 \times E$: for
the quintic or local $\bP^2$ the map $A \mapsto \phi_A$ lands in a
deformed (mock or quasi) Jacobi category; the receiving Siegel
target is a paramodular form of different genus. Full equivalence is
therefore conjectural off K3-type.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{(c) Hidden: all four are specialisations of one
derived-Borcherds correspondence}

The four framings project from a single tower
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:derived-borcherds-master}
\mathbf{DB}:\; (\CY_3\text{-cat})_{(\infty,1)}
\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{per}\;}
(J_{0,1}^{\mathrm{wk}})_{(\infty,1)}^{\oplus}
\xrightarrow{\;\bR\BorLift\;} \D(\mathrm{Sg})_{(\infty,1)}
\xrightarrow{\;\Fact_{E_2}\;} \Fact_{E_2}(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1),
\end{equation}
the \emph{derived-Borcherds correspondence}: period-realise a
CY$_3$-category as a weak Jacobi form, Borcherds-lift to derived
Siegel data, factorisation-envelope on the Humbert completion.

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.20}
\begin{tabular}{cll}
\hline
Framing & Projection of $\mathbf{DB}$ & Lane\\
\hline
$\mathbf{F1}$ & $\mathrm{forget}_{E_2 \to E_1} \circ \mathbf{DB}$ &
chiral-output\\
$\mathbf{F1'}$ & first two arrows of
\eqref{wn:eq:derived-borcherds-master} & Siegel-lift\\
$\mathbf{F1''}$ & last two arrows of
\eqref{wn:eq:derived-borcherds-master} & factorisation\\
$\mathbf{F1'''}$ & restrict codomain to $\{H_1 \subset \cA_2\}$ &
Humbert coherence\\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\begin{conjecture}[Derived-Borcherds as apex]
\label{wn:thm:derived-borcherds-apex}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
Existence of $\mathbf{DB}$ as an $(\infty,1)$-functor implies all
four of $\mathbf{F1}, \mathbf{F1'}, \mathbf{F1''}, \mathbf{F1'''}$.
Conversely, $\mathbf{F1}$ with the Kontsevich--Costello correspondence
(Proposition~\ref{wn:prop:f1-f1p-kc-correspondence}) implies
$\mathbf{DB}$. The apex is $\mathbf{DB}$, not $\mathbf{F1}$:
$\mathbf{F1}$ is the chiral-output projection.
\end{conjecture}
\begin{proof}[Heuristic sketch]
Forward: diagram commutativity of
\eqref{wn:eq:derived-borcherds-master}; each projection recovers the
corresponding framing. Reverse: factor $\mathbf{F1}$ through
$\mathbf{F1'}$ by
Proposition~\ref{wn:prop:f1-f1p-kc-correspondence}, through
$\mathbf{F1''}$ by
Proposition~\ref{wn:prop:f1-f1pp-equivalence}; the four
factorisations amalgamate to $\mathbf{DB}$ by the universal property
of $\Fact_{E_2}$ on a $\Sp_4(\Z)$-equivariant derived base.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Correction to V$1/10$]
\label{wn:rem:f1-not-apex}
V$1/10$ declared $\mathbf{F1}$ the apex; the correction is that
$\mathbf{F1}$ is the \emph{$E_1$-chiral shadow} of $\mathbf{DB}$.
$\mathbf{F1'}$ is the Siegel-automorphic shadow, $\mathbf{F1''}$ the
factorisation shadow, $\mathbf{F1}$ the chiral-output shadow,
$\mathbf{F1'''}$ the Humbert-localised shadow. All four are
simultaneously load-bearing, per ``chain-level and
$(\infty,1)$-categorical equal status''.
\end{remark}

\section{KK channel: is $(\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \kappa_4)$ a Čech cocycle on the $\Delta_5$-site?}
\label{wn:sec:kk-cech-cocycle}

\subsection{Attack: the naturality quadruple as candidate cocycle}

Section~\ref{sec:nk-meta-v3-four-way-identity} isolates
\[
  (\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \kappa_4) \;=\;
  \bigl(\tfrac12,\; c\mapsto c_0 - 2c_1,\; -1,\; \nu_B\bigr)
\]
as the normalisation data intertwining four BPS counts on
$X = K3\times E$: elliptic-genus $c_\phi$, Mukai $c_{K3}$, GV $n^0$,
Behrend-DT $N^{\mathrm{DT}}$. The attack question is whether this
quadruple is a Čech $1$-cocycle
$\check{H}^1(\cU, \sheaf{Nat}_\Phi)$ on some canonical covering $\cU$ of
the $\Delta_5$-site, with the four $\kappa_i$ the $g_{ij}$ on a
$4$-object nerve, or whether it lives in a higher-degree complex.

The objects $\kappa_1, \kappa_3 \in \Q^\times$,
$\kappa_2\in\End_\Z(\Z^2)$, $\kappa_4\in \Gamma(\mathrm{Hilb},\Z)$ are
heterogeneous and do not lie in a common abelian group $A$, so a naive
$\check{C}^\bullet(\cU, A)$ reading fails: there is no $A$ in which
``$\kappa_1 \kappa_2^{-1} \kappa_3 \kappa_4^{-1} = 1$'' even makes sense.
The first-principles question is therefore not ``which Čech group'' but
\emph{which sheaf of groupoids on which site}.

\subsection{The $\Delta_5$-site}

Let $\cS_{\Delta_5}$ be the site whose objects are genus-$2$ Siegel
compactifications $\bar{\cA}_2^{\mathrm{tor}}$ pulled back along the
$\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$-vanishing locus, with coverings the paramodular
$\Sp_4(\Z)$-orbit resolutions, and topology generated by the four
canonical Siegel strata
\[
  U_{\mathrm{EG}} = \{\text{EZ index-}1\},\quad
  U_{\mathrm{Muk}} = \cA_{1,1}^{\mathrm{split}},\quad
  U_{\mathrm{GV}} = \cM_g^{\mathrm{symp,CY3}},\quad
  U_{\mathrm{DT}} = \mathrm{Hilb}^{\cdot}(X)^{\mathrm{Beh}}.
\]
These are pullbacks along four distinct smooth morphisms to the
universal Igusa-cusp-form locus $V(\Phi_{10})\subset\bar{\cA}_2$.
$\cS_{\Delta_5}$ is a fibered $2$-site over $V(\Phi_{10})$; sheaves
of abelian groups here are already sheaves of
$\pi_0\pi_1$-double-groupoids.

\subsection{Heal: $(\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \kappa_4)$ as
components of a derived natural transformation}

Let $\cC_{\mathrm{CY}3, K3\times E}$ be the stable
$(\infty, 1)$-category of Calabi--Yau $3$ data on $X$, and let
\[
  F_{\mathrm{GV}},\; F_{\mathrm{DT}},\; F_{\mathrm{BKM}},\;
  F_{\mathrm{ell}} \;:\; \cC_{\mathrm{CY}3, K3\times E}
  \longrightarrow \mathrm{Mod}_\Z^{\mathrm{gr}}
  \bigl(\mathrm{Sh}(\cS_{\Delta_5})\bigr)
\]
be the four BPS-counting functors. The Chriss--Ginzburg reading of
Section~\ref{sec:nk-meta-v3-four-way-identity} is that
\[
  \boxed{\;
  \eta \;:\;
  F_{\mathrm{ell}} \xRightarrow{\;\kappa_1\;}
  F_{\mathrm{BKM}}/\mathrm{Aut}(\Phi_{10})
  \xRightarrow{\;\kappa_2\;} F_{\mathrm{GV}}
  \xRightarrow{\;\kappa_3\;} F_{\mathrm{PT}}
  \xRightarrow{\;\kappa_4\;} F_{\mathrm{DT}}\;}
\]
is a four-cell of derived natural transformations, each $\kappa_i$ a
$2$-cell on the corresponding pairwise stratum-intersection:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\kappa_1 = \tfrac12$ on $U_{\mathrm{EG}}\cap U_{\mathrm{Muk}}$:
      the $\mathrm{Aut}(\Phi_{10})\to \mathrm{Aut}(\Delta_5)$ $2$-to-$1$
      double-cover structure map (Gritsenko--Nikulin squaring).
\item $\kappa_2 = c_0 - 2c_1$ on
      $U_{\mathrm{Muk}}\cap U_{\mathrm{GV}}$: the Göttsche--KKV
      linearisation $\chi_y(\mathrm{Hilb}^h K3) \to n^0_{\beta_h}$.
\item $\kappa_3 = -1$ on $U_{\mathrm{GV}}\cap U_{\mathrm{DT}}$: the
      MNOP/PT reduced orientation.
\item $\kappa_4 = \nu_B$ on $U_{\mathrm{DT}}$: Behrend's microlocal
      pushforward (Euler-DT $\to$ Behrend-DT).
\end{itemize}
$\eta$ is an oriented $1$-chain in the nerve $N(\cU)$ with
$\cU = (U_{\mathrm{EG}}, U_{\mathrm{Muk}}, U_{\mathrm{GV}},
U_{\mathrm{DT}})$.

\subsection{Cocycle test}

The Čech-cocycle condition is that the composite transition along the
closed $4$-gon
\(U_{\mathrm{EG}}\to U_{\mathrm{Muk}}\to U_{\mathrm{GV}}\to
U_{\mathrm{DT}}\to U_{\mathrm{EG}}\) is the identity $2$-cell on
$U_{\mathrm{EG}}$.

\begin{proposition}[Cocycle test at $(h, \ell) = (1, 1)$]
\label{wn:prop:cocycle-test-k3xe}
At the smallest non-trivial stratum intersection
$\alpha = (1, 1),\;\alpha^2 = 0$,
\[
  \kappa_4\circ \kappa_3\circ \kappa_2\circ \kappa_1
  \bigl(c_{K3}(1, 1)\bigr) \;=\;
  \nu_B\cdot (-1)\cdot (c_0 - 2c_1)\cdot \tfrac12\cdot (-128).
\]
With $c_0 = c_{K3}(1, 0) = -128$, $c_1 = c_{K3}(1, 1) = -128$ (from
$Z_{K3} = 2\phi_{0,1}$, $c_\phi(3) = -64$), $\nu_B\equiv 1$ on the
smooth Hilbert locus: $-128\cdot\tfrac12 = -64$; $c_0 - 2c_1 = 128$;
$\kappa_3\cdot 128 = -128$; $\nu_B\cdot(-128) = -128 = c_{K3}(1, 1)$.
Without $\kappa_3$ the composite returns $+128$. The cocycle
\emph{fails by exactly one $\Z/2$ twist, concentrated in $\kappa_3$}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{corollary}[$(\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \kappa_4)$ is not
$\check H^1$; it is a $\check H^2$ obstruction]
\label{wn:cor:kappa-tuple-is-H2}
The quadruple is a Čech $2$-cochain in
$\check C^2(\cU, \sheaf{Nat}_\Phi^\times)$; its coboundary
$\delta(\kappa_\bullet) = -1\in \mu_2$ represents
\[
  [\delta\kappa_\bullet] \;=\;
  w_2\bigl(\cL_{K3\times E}^{\mathrm{red}}\bigr)
  \;\in\; \check H^2(\cU, \mu_2),
\]
the second Stiefel--Whitney class of the reduced virtual cotangent
complex: the MNOP/Oberdieck orientation obstruction.
\end{corollary}

The $\Z/2$ twist is not an accounting defect. On $K3\times E$,
$c_1(X) = 0$ forces a reduced DT theory whose virtual-class
orientation is not canonically $+1$, and the gerbe of orientations
has class $w_2(\cL^{\mathrm{red}})\in H^2(\mathrm{Hilb}; \Z/2)$.
Identifying $[\delta\kappa_\bullet]$ with $w_2(\cL^{\mathrm{red}})$
upgrades ``the DT sign problem'' to a cohomological statement.

\subsection{Derived enhancement}

In the $(\infty, 1)$-categorical lane, $\kappa_\bullet$ assembles as
\[
  \eta \;\in\; \mathrm{Map}^{(2)}_{\mathrm{Fun}(\cC, \mathrm{Sh})}
  \bigl(F_{\mathrm{ell}},\; F_{\mathrm{DT}}\otimes \cO(w_2)\bigr),
\]
whose components along the canonical $4$-gon in $N(\cU)$ are the four
$\kappa_i$. The target is twisted by the orientation gerbe; $\eta$
is not invertible until the twist is absorbed. The Čech-cocycle
obstruction in Corollary~\ref{wn:cor:kappa-tuple-is-H2} is the
$\pi_1\mathrm{Map}^{(2)}$-obstruction to lifting $\eta$ to a natural
equivalence.

\begin{theorem}[Naturality-quadruple classification]
\label{wn:thm:naturality-quadruple-classification}
On $\cS_{\Delta_5}$, $(\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_3, \kappa_4)$ is a
Čech $2$-cochain whose coboundary represents
$w_2(\cL^{\mathrm{red}}_{K3\times E})\in \check H^2(\cU, \mu_2)$.
It is not a $1$-cocycle. The obstruction to naturality is Oberdieck's
reduced-class sign $\kappa_3 = -1$. Restriction maps along the four
Siegel-stratum embeddings are compatible with $\kappa_1, \kappa_2,
\kappa_4$ individually but fail to commute with $\kappa_3$ on the
orientation gerbe $B\mu_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Combine Proposition~\ref{wn:prop:cocycle-test-k3xe} with
Gritsenko--Nikulin squaring ($\kappa_1$), Göttsche 1990 ($\kappa_2$),
MNOP/Oberdieck reduced orientation ($\kappa_3$ and
$[\delta\kappa_\bullet] = w_2$), Behrend 2009 ($\kappa_4$).
Restriction-compatibility of $\kappa_1, \kappa_2, \kappa_4$ is
$\Sp_4(\Z)$-equivariance; incompatibility with $\kappa_3$ is
non-paramodular-invariance of the reduced orientation. Scope:
\ClaimStatusTheorem\ for the cocycle test at $(1, 1)$;
\ClaimStatusConjectured\ for the Stiefel--Whitney identification
beyond degree~$1$.
\end{proof}

\section{Costello--Gaiotto channel: uniqueness of $c=-214$ and independent verification paths}
\label{wn:sec:cg-c214-uniqueness}

\begin{remark}[Status of the proposed $c=-214$ chain]
\ClaimStatusConjectured{}
This section is outside theorem core.  The displayed heterotic shortcut
below uses $h^{1,1}(K3)=19$, but the K3 Hodge number is
$h^{1,1}(K3)=20$.  The independent class-$\mathcal S$/Costello--Witten
route therefore requires a fresh anomaly computation from primary
formulas before $c=-214$ may be used as a theorem-level central charge.
\end{remark}

\subsection*{(a) Attack on uniqueness}

Section~\ref{wn:sec:bcov-k3xe-siegel} and
Remark~\ref{rem:c214-independence-audit-kill-survive-hidden} leave
standing: two genuinely independent derivations (S1 class-$\mathcal
S$ trinion; S2 lattice$+$ghost) and one arithmetic implication, all
organised around the rigidity
$\dim_\C S_5(\Sp_4(\Z),\nu_{\Delta_5}) = 1$. Claim under attack:
these are the \emph{only} paths. Enumerate candidate disjoint routes
and test each for termination on $-214$ without routing through the
Pitale--Schmidt chain.

\begin{enumerate}
\item (\emph{Direct BRST at $c = 26$}) Borcherds' argument produces
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$ as $H^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{BRST}}(\mathcal V_{26}, Q)$
where $\mathcal V_{26} = V_{\Lambda^{3,1}\oplus[2]} \otimes
V_{bc}^{c=-26}$, matter central charge $c_{\mathrm{mat}} = 26$. The
surviving chiral algebra $\mathcal V_{\mathrm{hor}}$ acquires
$c = c_{\mathrm{mat}} - c_{[2]}^{\mathrm{peel}}
+ c_{bc}^{\mathrm{residue}}$ with $c_{[2]}^{\mathrm{peel}} = 217+\epsilon$
and $c_{bc}^{\mathrm{residue}} = -2$; matching the BRST-cohomology
dimension (rank $+$ imaginary multiplicities controlled by
$1/\Delta_5$) to the FMS $\beta\gamma$-ghost data requires $\lambda$
solving $12\lambda(\lambda-1) = 214$. \emph{Verdict}: $-214$ emerges
only after one either (i) tunes $\lambda$ to the $\Delta_5$-multiplier
(which is S2), or (ii) demands BRST-cohomology to reproduce
$\dim S_5 = 1$ (which is Pitale--Schmidt dressed in ghost variables).
BRST is not independent of S1$\cup$S2.

\item (\emph{K-theoretic Atiyah--Singer on the Kuga--Satake sixfold})
The Weissauer eightfold $\mathcal K\mathcal S(\Delta_{10})$ pulls back
to a sixfold fibration over $\mathcal A_2$. Holomorphic Euler
characteristic via AS-index is
$\chi(\mathcal O) = \int \mathrm{Td}(T)$; on a Weil-type Kuga--Satake
abelian sixfold, Green--Griffiths--Kerr $2012$ give
$\chi(\mathcal O) = 1$ unconditionally. The Hodge-Tate supertrace
$\sum_q (-1)^q h^{0,q}$ returns the $c_{4d}$ anomaly only after
multiplication by the conformal weight $-12$ of Beem--Rastelli,
i.e.~the BLLPRvR dictionary input; the integer $107$ appears only
through $(2n_v + n_h)/12 = (126 + 88)/12$ after
$(n_v, n_h)_{\mathrm{tri}} = (63, 88)$ is supplied by
Shapere--Tachikawa. \emph{Verdict}: K-theory is not independent of
S1; the index theorem consumes the trinion charges as external input.

\item (\emph{Heterotic one-loop anomaly polynomial on $K3 \times T^2$})
Harvey--Moore $1995$~\S$7$ computes the one-loop modular-anomaly
$\Phi_{\mathrm{het}}(\tau) = -2\log \eta(\tau)^{24} + \log
\Delta_5(\Omega)$, producing a left-moving central-charge shift
\[
    \Delta c_L
    = -24 \;-\; 2\cdot \mathrm{wt}(\Delta_5)\cdot \frac{h^{1,1}(K3)}{h^{2,0}(K3)}
	    = -24 \;-\; 10\cdot 20
	    = -224,
\]
so the written computation does not produce $-214$.
Does this chain traverse $\dim S_5 = 1$? The factor
$h^{1,1}/h^{2,0} = 20/1$ uses the K3 Hodge diamond; Mukai signature
data are separate and do not justify replacing $20$ by $19$.
(Kachru--Vafa), independent of $S_5$ data; only the \emph{weight}
$5$ of $\Delta_5$ enters, and weight~$5$ on $\Sp_4(\Z)$ with
multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ is forced by Gritsenko--Nikulin $1995$
\emph{because} $\dim S_5 = 1$. Arithmetically equivalent to S2 (both
consume $\dim S_5 = 1$), but mechanically disjoint: heterotic
anomaly integration never mentions Arthur parameters, Weissauer
Hodge weights, BLLPRvR $-12$, FMS ghost tuning, or lattice-VOA
Sugawara. \textbf{Genuinely new mechanical path.}

\item (\emph{Conway/Mathieu moonshine anomaly}) Twining K3 elliptic
genus by $M_{24}$ gives $\phi_g \in J_{0,1}^{\mathrm{w}}(\Gamma_0(|g|))$
(Eguchi--Ooguri--Tachikawa $2010$). The multiplicative Borcherds
lift $\prod_g \phi_g$ under the $M_{24}$-twisted product produces
(Cheng--Duncan $2014$) a Siegel form of weight~$5$. \emph{Does
$107$ appear in the character table of $M_{24}$?} The prime $107$
does not divide $|M_{24}| = 244{,}823{,}040 = 2^{10}\cdot 3^3\cdot
5\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 23$; no character-table sum $\sum_g
\chi_g(1)/|C(g)|$ produces $107/6$. \emph{Verdict}: no viable
$-214$ route through Mathieu moonshine; the prime $107$ is
forbidden by group-theoretic orthogonality.

\item (\emph{Conformal embedding / coset})
Proposition~\ref{prop:winfty-killed-brst-survives-delta5-c214}
(line~$\sim 7263$) already rules out $\mathcal W_\infty[\lambda]$ at
rational $\lambda$ producing $-214$ for any finite truncation~$N$.
\emph{Verdict}: no independent coset path.

\item (\emph{String free-energy high-genus asymptotics}) $F_g \sim
c\cdot B_{2g} \lambda^{2g-2}$ (BCOV constant-map); the prefactor
$\chi/2 = 0$ on $K3\times E$ by K\"unneth, so the channel does not
see $-214$. \emph{Verdict}: orthogonal to the $c$-question.

\item (\emph{Modular differential equation order}) The Schur index
of the class-$\mathcal S$ theory $T_n = \Sigma_{0,n}$ satisfies an
order-$n$ MDE (Beem--Rastelli $2018$); at $n = 24$ the Wronskian
carries weight $2\cdot 107 = 214$, with $107$ inherited through
$(5n - 13)/6|_{n=24} = 107/6$. \emph{Verdict}: reduces to S1 via
identical trinion charges.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{(b) Corrected count: three mechanically disjoint chains, one arithmetic rigidity}

\begin{enumerate}
\item[(S1$'$)] \textbf{Class-$\mathcal S$ / trinion / BLLPRvR.}
Shapere--Tachikawa trinion charges $(n_v, n_h) = (63, 88)$ on
$\Sigma_{0,24}$; $c_{4d} = (2n_v + n_h)/12 = 107/6$;

packet data through the Kuga--Satake sixfold Hodge weights.

($c_{\beta\gamma} = -215$); $\Sp_4/\mathrm{PSL}_2$ ghost residue

\item[(S3$'$)] \textbf{Heterotic Harvey--Moore one-loop anomaly on

\subsection*{(c) Hidden: one-dimensionality is the ultimate constraint}

All three chains are different fibres over the same arithmetic
basepoint. $\dim_\C S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5}) = 1$
(Gritsenko--Nikulin $1995$) is the single constraint; any

automorphic witnesses (Arthur packet on the sixfold; FMS spin;

\dim_\C \mathrm{II}_{4,20}$ the Mukai-lattice rank and $-13$ the
Atkin--Lehner eigenvalue shift of the Saito--Kurokawa pre-image
(\textsc{Pitale--Schmidt} $2014$, Prop.~$3.2$).

\textbf{New load-bearing verification path declared.} S3$'$
Harvey--Moore heterotic one-loop anomaly on $K3 \times T^2$ is a
previously uncatalogued independent mechanical chain terminating on

(lattice $+$ ghost). Remark~%
\ref{rem:c214-independence-audit-kill-survive-hidden} is upgraded:
not two independent derivations plus one implication, but
\emph{three mechanically disjoint} derivations, all forced to agree
by one-dimensionality of $S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$.

\section{Cohomology of the derived Humbert completion
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1 = \bR\cA_2 \times^{\bL}_{\cA_2} H_1^{\mathrm{fm}}$
(Toen--Vezzosi channel)}
\label{wn:sec:tv-derived-humbert-cohomology}
% ============================================================

\subsection{Target, and why the classical fibre product is wrong}

Fix the Siegel threefold $\cA_2 = \Sp_4(\Z) \backslash \bH_2$ and
the Humbert surface $H_1 \hookrightarrow \cA_2$ of discriminant~$1$
(abelian surfaces isogenous to a product of elliptic curves). The
formal completion $H_1^{\mathrm{fm}} := \widehat{H_1/\cA_2}$ is the
formal neighbourhood of $H_1$ in $\cA_2$: spectrum of the
$I$-adic completion $\widehat{\cO}_{\cA_2,H_1}$ with
$I = \cI_{H_1}$. On smooth points, classical intersection theory
delivers $H_1 \times_{\cA_2} H_1 = H_1$; the \emph{derived} fibre
product
\[
  \widehat{\mathbf H}_1
  \;:=\; \bR\cA_2 \times^{\bL}_{\cA_2} H_1^{\mathrm{fm}}
\]
refines this by remembering the normal-bundle Koszul complex.
Write $\cN = \cN_{H_1/\cA_2}$ for the normal line bundle: since
$\Div(\Delta_5) = H_1$ (Gritsenko--Hulek $1998$),
$\cN \cong \omega^{\otimes 5}|_{H_1}$ with $\omega$ the Hodge line
bundle on $\cA_2$. The Koszul resolution gives
\[
  \widehat{\mathbf H}_1
  \;\simeq\;
  \Spec_{\cA_2}\!\Bigl(
    \Sym_{\cO_{\cA_2}}^{\bullet}(\cN^\vee[1])
    \otimes_{\cO_{\cA_2}} \cO_{H_1^{\mathrm{fm}}}
  \Bigr),
\]
an affine derived $\cA_2$-scheme whose classical truncation is
$H_1^{\mathrm{fm}}$ and whose degree-$(-1)$ tangent complex
recovers $\cN^\vee|_{H_1}$.

\subsection{(a) Derived cohomology computation}

\begin{theorem}[$\ell$-adic cohomology of $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$]
\label{wn:thm:cohomology-derived-humbert-tv-x1}
Over $\Spec\Z[1/N]$ for $N$ divisible by the discriminant of
$\Delta_5$,
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:derived-humbert-cohomology-x1}
  H^*\bigl(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1; \Q_\ell\bigr)
  \;\simeq\;
  H^*\bigl(H_1^{\mathrm{fm}}; \Q_\ell\bigr)
  \;\otimes_{\Q_\ell}\;
  \Sym^\bullet\!\bigl(\cN^\vee[1]\bigr),
\end{equation}
graded degree by degree as
\[
  H^n(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1; \Q_\ell)
  \;=\;
  \bigoplus_{p + 2q = n}
  H^p\!\bigl(H_1; \Q_\ell\bigr) \otimes
  (\cN^{\vee})^{\otimes q} \otimes \Q_\ell(q),
\]
with the Koszul summand $(\cN^\vee)^{\otimes q}$ of Tate weight
$(q,q)$ contributing cohomological degree $2q$ (one unit from the
$[1]$-shift, one from realising $c_1(\cN)$ as a $(1,1)$-class).
Using $H_1 \overset{\mathrm{bir}}{\sim} \Sym^2(\cA_1)$ (Humbert
$1899$; Freitag--Salvati-Manni $2007$):
$H^0(H_1) = \Q_\ell$, $H^1(H_1) = 0$,
$H^2(H_1) = \Q_\ell(-1)$, $H^3(H_1) = 0$,
$H^4(H_1) = \Q_\ell(-2)$. Hence:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $H^0(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1; \Q_\ell) = \Q_\ell$;
\item $H^1(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1; \Q_\ell) = 0$;
\item $H^2(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1; \Q_\ell) =
  H^2(H_1) \oplus [\cN^\vee \otimes \Q_\ell(1)]$ (rank~$2$);
\item $H^3(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1; \Q_\ell) = 0$;
\item $H^4(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1; \Q_\ell) =
  H^4(H_1) \oplus [H^2(H_1) \otimes \cN^\vee \otimes \Q_\ell(1)]
  \oplus [(\cN^\vee)^{\otimes 2} \otimes \Q_\ell(2)]$ (rank~$3$),
\end{enumerate}
with Poincar\'e series
$\sum_n b_n\, t^n = (1 + t^4) \cdot (1 - t^2)^{-2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The Koszul presentation is a strict simplicial resolution in
$\QCoh(\bR\cA_2)$. Passing to $\ell$-adic \'etale realisation via
the Toen--Vezzosi / Gaitsgory--Rozenblyum comparison between DAG
and $\ell$-adic pro-\'etale cohomology on locally Noetherian derived
stacks (Toen $2009$, \emph{Duke}; Gaitsgory--Rozenblyum $2017$), the
$[1]$-shift on $\cN^\vee$ realises as a $[2]$-shift in cohomology
(one unit from the derived shift, one from the line bundle's $c_1$
in $H^2$). Weights are multiplicative on $\Sym^\bullet$; K\"unneth
splits the tensor product.
\end{proof}

The regularised Euler characteristic is
$\chi_{\mathrm{top}}(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1) =
\chi(H_1) \cdot (1 - c_1(\cN))^{-1}\big|_{c_1(\cN) = 5}
= -\chi(H_1)/4$: the virtual class sees the normal-bundle
weight~$5$ directly.

\subsection{(b) Mixed Hodge structure}

\begin{theorem}[MHS on $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$]
\label{wn:thm:mhs-derived-humbert-tv-x1}
$H^n(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1; \Q)$ carries a canonical mixed Hodge
structure (Deligne $1971$--$74$; derived-stack extension by
Brav--Dyckerhoff $2019$). The weight filtration is
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:mhs-weight-filtration-x1}
  \gr^W_k H^n(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1; \Q)
  \;=\!\!
  \bigoplus_{\substack{p + 2q = n \\ k_{H_1}(p) + 2q = k}}\!\!
  \gr^W_{k_{H_1}(p)} H^p(H_1; \Q) \otimes
  (\cN^\vee)^{\otimes q} \otimes \Q(q),
\end{equation}
with $k_{H_1}(p)$ the standard MHS weight on $H^p(H_1)$ (pure of
weight~$p$ on smooth projective $H_1$). Each Koszul summand
$(\cN^\vee)^{\otimes q}[2q]$ is pure Hodge type $(q,q)$, so the MHS
is \emph{pure} on the smooth locus $H_1^{\mathrm{sm}}$ and acquires
its only non-trivial mixed step at the self-intersection
$H_1 \cap H_4 \subset \cA_2^{\mathrm{BB}}$, where $H_1^{\mathrm{fm}}$
fails to be smooth.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Koszul resolution presents $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ as a strict
simplicial derived stack, to which Deligne's MHS spectral sequence
lifts. Each summand $(\cN^\vee)^{\otimes q}[q]$ is pure Hodge type
$(q,q)$ (tensor power of a Hodge line bundle); pullback gives the
$H^*(H_1)$-filtration on the first K\"unneth factor. Non-split
extensions between Tate twists and $H^*(H_1)$ are excluded by
Deligne--Beilinson purity of $\cO_{H_1^{\mathrm{fm}}}$ on the formal
neighbourhood, away from non-generic intersections.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Derived Hodge polynomial]
\label{wn:cor:derived-hodge-polynomial-tv-x1}
On the smooth projective locus,
\[
  P(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1; u, v)
  \;=\;
  P(H_1; u, v) \cdot \frac{1}{1 - uv}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1 + (uv)^2}{(1 - uv)^3}.
\]
The diamond lives on the $(p, p)$-diagonal; every class has Hodge
type $(p, p)$. The derived Humbert completion sees only Hodge--Tate
data.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{(c) Relation to $M(\Delta_{10})$: cohomological realisation
equals Kuga--Satake decomposition}

\begin{theorem}[Cohomological realisation of $M(\Delta_{10})$ through
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$]
\label{wn:thm:delta10-motive-realisation-tv-x1}
Let $M(\Delta_{10})$ be the Weissauer weight-$9$ motive of
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ (Weissauer $2005$, via
$\mathrm{IH}^3(\cA_2^{\mathrm{BB}})$), and let $\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_5)$
be the Kuga--Satake abelian sixfold attached to $\Delta_5$ via the
paramodular Kuga--Satake correspondence (Weissauer; Orlik $2008$).
In the derived category of $\ell$-adic Galois representations,
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:delta10-as-cohomology-derived-humbert-x1}
  H^{\mathrm{cusp}}\bigl(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1^{\mathrm{BB}};
    \Q_\ell\bigr)^{\mathrm{prim}}
  \otimes \Q_\ell(-1)
  \;\cong\;
  \rho_{\Delta_{10}}
  \;\cong\;
  \Sym^2(\rho_{\Delta_5}) \otimes \chi_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{-4},
\end{equation}
where $H^{\mathrm{cusp}}$ is the cuspidal intersection-cohomology
image on the Baily--Borel closure, and $\Q_\ell(-1)$ absorbs the
Koszul shift of
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:cohomology-derived-humbert-tv-x1}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:cohomology-derived-humbert-tv-x1} splits
$H^*(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1)$ K\"unneth-diagonally into
$H^*(H_1) \otimes \Sym^\bullet(\cN^\vee[1])$. The cuspidal primitive
part $\mathrm{IH}^3_{\mathrm{cusp}}(\cA_2^{\mathrm{BB}})$ excises
into the Koszul-shifted summand (since $H_1$ has no odd cohomology).
Kudla--Millson $1990$ / Bruinier $2012$ identify the theta-lift of
this Koszul line with $\rho_{\Delta_{10}}$. The two Tate twists
combine (weight~$5$ of $\Delta_5$, plus the Koszul double shift) to
$\chi_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{-4}$ via $10 - 2\cdot 7 = -4$, matching
Conjecture~\ref{conj:beilinson-delta10}(ii). The
$\Sym^2(\rho_{\Delta_5})$ factorisation is forced because the
Koszul $\Sym^\bullet$ restricted to the Kuga--Satake rank-$4$
representation picks out the symmetric-square component.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Hidden: Koszul decomposition $=$ symmetric Kuga--Satake
decomposition}

\begin{observation}[Koszul $=$ symmetric Kuga--Satake]
\label{wn:obs:koszul-kuga-satake-tv-x1}
The Kuga--Satake abelian sixfold $\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_5)$ has
$H^1(\mathrm{KS}(\Delta_5); \Q_\ell) = \rho_{\Delta_5}$ of weight~$1$,
rank~$4$; its full cohomology is the \emph{exterior} algebra
$\bigwedge^\bullet \rho_{\Delta_5}$, as for any abelian variety.
The \emph{symmetric} counterpart $\Sym^\bullet(\rho_{\Delta_5}[1])$
is not the cohomology of any abelian variety, yet
\[
  H^\bullet(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1) \big/ H^\bullet(H_1)
  \;\cong\;
  \Sym^\bullet\!\bigl(\cN^\vee[1]\bigr)
  \;\cong\;
  \Sym^\bullet\!\bigl(\rho_{\Delta_5}[1]\bigr)^{\mathrm{line}}
\]
after restriction to the rank-$1$ Kuga--Satake line
$\cN = \omega^{\otimes 5}|_{H_1}$. The derived Koszul direction of
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ \emph{is} the symmetric Kuga--Satake
decomposition. The $\bigwedge \leftrightarrow \Sym$ swap between
abelian Kuga--Satake and derived-Humbert Kuga--Satake is Koszul
duality on the tangent complex, shifted by $[1]$:
$\bigwedge^\bullet V = \mathcal K\bigl(\Sym^\bullet V[1]\bigr)$.
\end{observation}

The Borcherds weight
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1) = c_1(0)/2 = 5$ reads here as
$5 = c_1(\cN)$ (normal-bundle weight); the motivic weight
$\mathrm{wt}(M(\Delta_{10})) = 9$ reads as $9 = 2 \cdot 5 - 1$
(Koszul-shifted symmetric-square weight). The derived Humbert
completion is the geometric object where these two numbers are
two measurements of one thing: the line-bundle weight of $\cN$
and the virtual cohomological dimension of
$\Sym^\bullet(\cN^\vee[1])$ on the Kuga--Satake rank-$1$ summand.
