\section{Beilinson channel: the $15$
coherence squares of $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ are not $13$
independent problems}
\label{sec:delta5-fifteen-squares-beilinson-w2}

\subsection*{(a) Attack. Transitivity collapses the diagram.}

Proposition~\ref{prop:delta5-six-equivalence-classes-v1}
recognises six equivalence classes among the twelve
presentations of $\Delta_5$: modular/analytic $\mathbf M =
\{P_1, P_3, P_9\}$, Lie-algebraic $\mathbf L = \{P_2, P_{12}\}$,
arithmetic/motivic $\mathbf A = \{P_5, P_6, P_7\}$,
categorical/derived $\mathbf D = \{P_4\}$, physical/holographic
$\mathbf P = \{P_8, P_{10}\}$, divisorial/classical
$\mathbf C = \{P_{11}\}$.
Remark~\ref{rem:delta5-humbert-coherence-functor-v1} stamps
``two of the $\binom 6 2 = 15$ commuting squares (Toen--Vezzosi
/ $\ell$-adic realisation) in the literature, and the remaining
thirteen open.''

Adversarial reading: the stamp treats the $15$ squares as
$15$ independent problems, dismissing the functor-category
structure of the coherence datum
$(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1, \mathcal F_{\fg_{\Delta_5}})$. In a
$2$-category whose objects are the six lanes and whose
$1$-morphisms are the six realisation functors out of
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$, once two sides of a triangle commute,
the third commutes by pasting.

The $15$ squares are edges of $K_6$; coherence squares are
$2$-cocycles. Over a contractible base ($\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$
is contractible over $\mathrm{pt}$ after $\ell$-adic completion
by Howard--Madapusi-Pera), a spanning tree on $6$ vertices has
$5$ edges and the circuit rank is $\binom 6 2 - 5 = 10$; the
$13$-open stamp is not internally consistent --- at most $10$
squares can be genuinely independent before triangulation
witnesses begin repeating. Some named squares factor through a
third lane: $(\mathbf M, \mathbf A)$ factors through $\mathbf L$
via the Howard--Madapusi-Pera route (arithmetic moduli
$\hookleftarrow$ BKM Weyl group $\hookleftarrow$ Borcherds lift).

\subsection*{(b) Heal. Classification of the $15$ squares.}

\begin{theorem}[Classification of $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$
coherence squares]
\label{thm:delta5-fifteen-squares-classification-w2}
\ClaimStatusTheorem{} for points \textup{(1)}, \textup{(2)};
\ClaimStatusConjectured{} for point \textup{(3)}.
In the $2$-category of realisation functors out of
$(\widehat{\mathbf H}_1, \mathcal F_{\fg_{\Delta_5}})$ to the
six lanes $\mathbf M, \mathbf L, \mathbf A, \mathbf D, \mathbf
P, \mathbf C$, the $\binom 6 2 = 15$ commuting squares
stratify.

\smallskip
\emph{(1) Two established in primary literature.}
\begin{itemize}
\item[\textup{(K1)}] $(\mathbf M, \mathbf A)$: Toen--Vezzosi
derived completion of $H_1 \subset \mathcal A_2$ matches the
$\ell$-adic realisation of the Kuga--Satake motive of
$\Delta_{10}$. Source: Howard--Madapusi-Pera $2020$.
\item[\textup{(K2)}] $(\mathbf M, \mathbf L)$: the Borcherds
lift of $\phi_{0,1}$ produces the Weyl--Kac--Borcherds
denominator
$\Delta_5 = e^{-\rho}\prod_{\alpha\in\Delta^+}
(1 - e^{-\alpha})^{\mult\alpha}$ of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$.
Source: Gritsenko--Nikulin $1995$--$1998$; Borcherds $1998$.
\end{itemize}

\emph{(2) Eight derivable by pasting} (all squares incident to
$\mathbf C$ or $\mathbf P$, plus $(\mathbf L, \mathbf A)$).
\begin{itemize}
\item[\textup{(D1)}] $(\mathbf L, \mathbf A)$: compose
$\mathbf L \leftarrow \mathbf M \to \mathbf A$ via K$1\circ$K$2$.
\item[\textup{(D2)}] $(\mathbf M, \mathbf C)$: classical
truncation $\bR \to \pi_0$ of K$1$.
\item[\textup{(D3)}] $(\mathbf L, \mathbf C)$: compose
$\mathbf L \leftarrow \mathbf M \to \mathbf C$.
\item[\textup{(D4)}] $(\mathbf A, \mathbf C)$: compose
$\mathbf A \leftarrow \mathbf M \to \mathbf C$.
\item[\textup{(D5)}] $(\mathbf M, \mathbf P)$: DMVV $= P_9$ is
both in $\mathbf M$ and the boundary of
$\AdS_3 \times S^2 \times K3$; the AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$
Cardy-character functor factors through the modular seed.
\item[\textup{(D6)}] $(\mathbf L, \mathbf P)$: compose
$\mathbf L \leftarrow \mathbf M \to \mathbf P$.
\item[\textup{(D7)}] $(\mathbf A, \mathbf P)$: compose
$\mathbf A \leftarrow \mathbf M \to \mathbf P$.
\item[\textup{(D8)}] $(\mathbf P, \mathbf C)$: classical
truncation of D$5$.
\end{itemize}

\emph{(3) Five genuinely independent} (exactly the squares
incident to the derived lane $\mathbf D$).
\begin{itemize}
\item[\textup{(O1)}] $(\mathbf M, \mathbf D)$: does the
Bridgeland stability pullback
$\rho_{\mathrm{BS}}: \Sp_4(\Z)/\{\pm I\} \hookrightarrow
\Auteq(\Db(K3\times E))/(\mathrm{shift}\oplus\Pic)$ commute
with the Borcherds/DMVV modular realisation? Open; scope =
Pattern $273$ morphism-preservation of $\Phi_3$ at
$\Db(K3\times E)$.
\item[\textup{(O2)}] $(\mathbf L, \mathbf D)$: does the
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$ Weyl group act on
$\Stab^{\mathrm{OP}}(K3\times E)$ by stability-preserving
derived autoequivalences? Open; Bridgeland--Smith $2015$.
\item[\textup{(O3)}] $(\mathbf A, \mathbf D)$: does the
motivic Galois representation of $\psi_{\Delta_{10}}$ descend
to Auteq-equivariant derived data? Open; Deligne--Morgan
Hodge-to-derived comparison at $(g,d,N) = (2,3,\infty)$.
\item[\textup{(O4)}] $(\mathbf D, \mathbf P)$: does the
horizon algebra $\mathfrak A_\infty(\mathcal H)$ match the
$\Stab^{\mathrm{OP}}$-periodicity of the derived shadow?
Open; Harvey--Moore attractor flow vs Bridgeland-stability
wall-crossing.
\item[\textup{(O5)}] $(\mathbf D, \mathbf C)$: does the
divisorial truncation of the derived stack recover the
Humbert divisor with its Galois action? Open; Toen--Vezzosi
$\to \pi_0$ comparison for
$\Stab^{\mathrm{OP}}(K3\times E)/(\mathrm{shift}\oplus\Pic)$.
\end{itemize}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof]
(1) K$1$, K$2$: primary citations.
(2) D$1$--D$8$: pasting along $\mathbf M$ as spanning-tree
root. $\mathbf M$ is incident to all other five lanes by
$P_1, P_3, P_9$ spanning every known construction; the five
edges $(\mathbf M, *)$ form a spanning tree of $K_6$ rooted
at $\mathbf M$. Any square $(\mathbf X, \mathbf Y)$ with
$\mathbf X, \mathbf Y \neq \mathbf M$ is the composite
$(\mathbf X, \mathbf M) \circ (\mathbf M, \mathbf Y)^{-1}$;
$2$-cells paste by the $\infty$-group structure on the
$(\infty,1)$-automorphism space of $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$.
Of the $10$ non-$\mathbf D$ squares, $2$ are K$1$, K$2$;
the remaining $8$ are D$1$--D$8$.
(3) O$1$--O$5$: the five squares incident to $\mathbf D$ are
genuinely independent because $\mathbf D$ sits outside the
$\mathbf M$-spanning-tree --- the derived lane carries
$(\infty,1)$-categorical data ($\Stab^{\mathrm{OP}}$, Auteq)
not recovered from any of the other five lanes by truncation,
$\ell$-adic realisation, or character functor.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{(c) Hidden. The genuinely-open five are
$\mathbf{F1}$ at $\Db(K3\times E)$.}

The five open squares O$1$--O$5$ coincide with the apex
frontier question $\mathbf{F1}$ of
\S\ref{sec:frontier-meta-adversarial}: \emph{does $\Phi_3$ preserve
morphisms coherently?}
\begin{itemize}
\item O$1$ = Pattern $273$ at $\Db(K3\times E)$.
\item O$2$ = morphism-level image of the BKM Weyl group under
$\Phi_3$.
\item O$3$ = $\ell$-adic realisation of the morphism lift.
\item O$4$ = physical side of the morphism lift.
\item O$5$ = $\pi_0$-truncation of the morphism lift.
\end{itemize}
Each O$_i$ is the restriction of $\mathbf{F1}$ to one of the
five lanes $\mathbf M, \mathbf L, \mathbf A, \mathbf P,
\mathbf C$; once $\mathbf{F1}$ is proved at $\Db(K3\times E)$,
all five O$_i$ follow.

Sharper count:
\[
15 \;=\; 2_{\text{known}} \;+\; 8_{\text{derivable}}
\;+\; 5_{\text{apex-projections of one open problem}}.
\]
The ``thirteen open'' of
Remark~\ref{rem:delta5-humbert-coherence-functor-v1} reduces
to \emph{one} open problem --- $\mathbf{F1}$ at
$\Db(K3\times E)$ --- viewed through five lenses, with eight
shadow-problems that are immediate corollaries of K$1$, K$2$,
and $\mathbf M$-based pasting.

\section{Aspinwall--Morrison channel: does the $\Delta_5$ crystal extend beyond $K3\times E$?}
\label{wn:sec:aspinwall-morrison-delta5-extension}

Three non-$K3\times E$ CY$_3$ targets, each probing one axis of the
$\Delta_5$ crystal: (i) the $\Z_2$-quotient $\mathrm{Enr}\times E$ with
$\pi_1 = \Z_2$; (ii) the abelian threefold $T^6 = E_1\times E_2\times E_3$
with abelian fundamental group $\Z^6$; (iii) the local K3
$\mathrm{Tot}(K_{K3}) = K3\times\C$, non-compact. For each we identify
whether a Siegel / orthogonal automorphic form plays the $\Delta_5$
role, and locate the CY$_3$ in the Aspinwall--Morrison landscape.

\subsection{Enriques $\times E$: Allcock $\Phi_4$ on $O^+(2,10)$}
\label{wn:subsec:enr-times-e-allcock}

$S_{\mathrm{Enr}} = K3/\iota$ (fixed-point-free Nikulin involution) has
$H^2 = \Z^{10}$ of signature $(1,9)$, transcendental lattice
$U\oplus U(2)\oplus E_8(-2)$ (Barth--Peters--Van de Ven), $\pi_1 = \Z_2$.
On $\mathrm{Enr}\times E$ the automorphic lift lives on
$\cD_{2,10} = O(2,10)/(O(2)\times O(10))$ rather than on $\bH_2$.

\begin{proposition}[$\mathrm{Enr}\times E$ denominator: Allcock $\Phi_4$]
\label{wn:prop:enr-allcock-denominator}
The BPS/DT denominator on $\mathrm{Enr}\times E$ is the Allcock--Borcherds
product $\Phi_4\in S_4(O^+(2,10),\mathrm{det})$ of weight~$4$,
the Borcherds additive lift of the $\Gamma_0(2)$-weak-Jacobi form
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:enr-jacobi-seed}
\phi^{\mathrm{Enr}}_{0,1}(\tau,z)
= \tfrac12\bigl(\phi_{0,1}(\tau,z) + \phi_{0,1}(\tau+\tfrac12,z)\bigr)
= \sum_{n,l}c^{\mathrm{Enr}}(4n-l^2)q^n\zeta^l,
\end{equation}
with $c^{\mathrm{Enr}}(-1)=1$, $c^{\mathrm{Enr}}(0)=8$,
$c^{\mathrm{Enr}}(3)=-32$. The divisor of $\Phi_4$ is the Heegner divisor
$H_{-1}\subset\cD_{2,10}$ of multiplicity~$1$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
$K3\to\mathrm{Enr}$ descends to a $\Z_2$-action on
$Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3) = 2\phi_{0,1}$; the twining genus $Z^{\iota}_{\mathrm{ell}}$
is a weak Jacobi form of weight~$0$, index~$1$ on $\Gamma_0(2)$ with
$c^{\iota}(-1)=1$, $c^{\iota}(0)=4$. The $\Z_2$-invariant combination
is~\eqref{wn:eq:enr-jacobi-seed}. Borcherds' additive lift
$J^{\mathrm{wk}}_{0,1}(\Gamma_0(2))\to M_4(O^+(2,10))$
(David--Jatkar--Sen 2006 arXiv:hep-th/0609074) yields $\Phi_4$ of weight
$c^{\mathrm{Enr}}(0)/2 = 4$ and first Heegner divisor $H_{-1}$ of
multiplicity $c^{\mathrm{Enr}}(-1) = 1$, matching the universal
Borcherds weight identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Four $\kappa_\bullet$ for $\mathrm{Enr}\times E$]
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}} = \chi(\cO_{\mathrm{Enr}})\cdot\chi(\cO_E) = 0$;
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 4$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:enriques-kappa});
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_4) = 4$ via $c^{\mathrm{Enr}}(0)/2$;
$\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}} = 12 = \chi_{\mathrm{top}}(\mathrm{Enr})$.
Fibre-rank halves $24\to 12$; Borcherds weight drops $5\to 4$, not $5/2$.
\end{corollary}

$\Sp_4(\Z)$ is replaced by $O^+(U\oplus U\oplus E_8(-2))$, rank~$10$ vs
rank~$3$. The BKM denominator carries imaginary roots from $E_8(-2)$,
but weight $<5$ because the $\Z_2$-twist discards half the short roots.

\subsection{Abelian threefold $T^6$: trivial unreduced, wrong-sign reduced}
\label{wn:subsec:t6-trivial-denom}

$T^6 = E_1\times E_2\times E_3$: $\chi(\cO_{T^6})=0$, $\chi_{\mathrm{top}}=0$,
$h^{1,1}=h^{2,1}=9$, $\pi_1 = \Z^6$. By $T^6$-translation invariance of
every rational curve moduli (Bryan--Oberdieck--Pandharipande--Yin 2018
arXiv:1805.11613),
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:t6-gv-vanish}
n^g_\beta(T^6) = 0\quad\text{for all }g\ge 0,\,\beta\neq 0,
\end{equation}
hence $Z^{T^6}_{\mathrm{BPS}} = 1$ identically.

\begin{proposition}[No $\Delta_?$ crystal on $T^6$]
\label{wn:prop:t6-no-crystal}
No BKM superalgebra $\fg_{T^6}$ has a non-trivial automorphic denominator
controlling unreduced $Z^{T^6}_{\mathrm{DT}}$. The Borcherds weight
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(T^6) = 0$ identically: the Igusa crystal does not
extend.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By~\eqref{wn:eq:t6-gv-vanish} the Jacobi-form seed is zero; the
denominator is the constant $1$ (weight~$0$), no BKM root system
arises.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Reduced sector, index~$-1$ obstruction]
The \emph{reduced} GV (quotient by $T^6$-translation; BOPY Theorem~1.1)
is captured by $\phi_{0,-1}(\tau,z) = -\vartheta_1(\tau,z)^2/\eta(\tau)^6$,
a weight-$0$ Jacobi form of index~$-1$ (Skoruppa). A putative Borcherds
lift would have \emph{negative} index, violating convergence-positivity
on a bounded symmetric domain. The crystal does not extend: the seed
has the wrong sign of index.
\end{remark}

$\Phi(T^6)$ is a free chiral superalgebra (Fock on $H^*(T^6)$); the
higher-genus elliptic genus is a theta-flat section of the universal
Hodge bundle over $\cA_1^3$ with no Siegel enhancement;
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(T^6) = 0 = \chi(\cO_{T^6})$.

\subsection{Local K3: $K3\times\C$ and the Vafa--Witten form $\eta^{24}$}
\label{wn:subsec:local-k3-vafa-witten}

$\mathrm{Tot}(K_{K3})$ is non-compact CY$_3$; $K_{K3}=\cO_{K3}$ makes it
$K3\times\C$ as a complex manifold.

\begin{proposition}[Local K3 denominator: Vafa--Witten $\eta^{24}$]
\label{wn:prop:local-k3-vafa-witten}
The refined DT on $K3\times\C$, equivalently the rank-$r$ Vafa--Witten
partition function on K3, is
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:local-k3-vw}
Z^{\mathrm{loc\,K3}}_{\mathrm{DT}}(q,t)
= \frac{1}{\eta(\tau)^{24}}\cdot\chi_r(q,t),
\end{equation}
with $\eta^{24}$ the K3-fibre denominator (Vafa--Witten 1994,
hep-th/9408074) and $\chi_r$ the rank-$r$ instanton character. This is a
weight-$(-12)$ elliptic modular form on $\SL_2(\Z)$, not a Siegel form
on $\Sp_4(\Z)$. The BKM enhancement is absent:
$\fg_{\mathrm{loc\,K3}}$ is a $\Z$-graded affine Kac--Moody algebra
(Heisenberg on the Mukai lattice), not a hyperbolic BKM superalgebra.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Structural reasoning]
Local K3 has one Kähler modulus from K3, none from the non-compact fibre
direction. IIA loses one $\SL_2(\Z)$ factor relative to compact
$K3\times E$: $\sigma\in\bH_2$ collapses to a cusp. The Gritsenko--Nikulin
Fourier--Jacobi expansion of $\Delta_5$ at $\sigma\to i\infty$ reduces
to $\eta(\tau)^{24}$ times a fugacity factor, recovering Vafa--Witten.
Chiral dual: Mukai-lattice VOA $V_{\mathrm{II}^{3,19}(-1)}$, rank-$24$
affine, $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 24 = \chi_{\mathrm{top}}(K3)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Four $\kappa_\bullet$ for local K3]
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}$ ill-defined (non-compact; infinite-dimensional
global sections); replace by $\chi_c = \chi(K3) = 24$.
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 24$ via the lattice-VOA identification.
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = 12$ via weight of $\eta^{24}$.
$\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}} = 24$. Spectrum collapses from the
fibre-aware compact collection $\{0,3,5,24;2\}$
to $\{24,24,12,24\}$: three of four coincide,
reflecting the loss of the $E$-modulus.
\end{corollary}

Local K3 sits on the boundary $\partial\cA_2$ at the $\sigma\to i\infty$
cusp, where $\Delta_5$ degenerates to $\eta^{24}$ on $\bH/\SL_2(\Z)$.
The crystal is the \emph{boundary trace} of the $K3\times E$ crystal.

\subsection{Trichotomy and the Aspinwall--Morrison extension table}
\label{wn:subsec:am-extension-table}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
CY$_3$ & Automorphic form & Group & Weight & $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ \\
\midrule
$K3\times E$ & $\Delta_5$ & $\Sp_4(\Z)$ & $5$ & $5$ \\
$K3\times E$ (doubled) & $\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ & $\Sp_4(\Z)$ & $10$ & $10$ \\
$\mathrm{Enr}\times E$ & $\Phi_4$ (Allcock) & $O^+(2,10)$ & $4$ & $4$ \\
$T^6$ & $1$ (trivial) & --- & $0$ & $0$ \\
local K3 & $\eta^{24}$ & $\SL_2(\Z)$ & $12$ & $12$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\begin{theorem}[Aspinwall--Morrison trichotomy for the $\Delta_5$ crystal]
\label{wn:thm:am-trichotomy}
Among the three non-$K3\times E$ CY$_3$ targets:
\textup{(Enriques)} genuine extension, $\Delta_5\mapsto\Phi_4$,
$\Sp_4(\Z)\hookrightarrow O^+(2,10)$, weight $5\to 4$, crystal
persists with reduced rank.
\textup{(Abelian)} crystal absent: trivial unreduced GV, vanishing
Borcherds weight; reduced sector is index-$(-1)$ of wrong sign for
Borcherds-product convergence.
\textup{(Local K3)} boundary degeneration: $\Sp_4(\Z)$ crystal
degenerates at $\sigma\to i\infty$ to $\SL_2(\Z)$ Vafa--Witten $\eta^{24}$;
hyperbolic BKM collapses to affine Kac--Moody.
The universal identity $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = c(0)/2$ holds throughout:
$c(0)=8$ (Enriques $\to 4$); $c(0)=0$ ($T^6\to 0$); $c(0)=24$ (local
K3 $\to 12$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Enriques: Proposition~\ref{wn:prop:enr-allcock-denominator} and
David--Jatkar--Sen hep-th/0609074 Theorem~3.1. Abelian:
Proposition~\ref{wn:prop:t6-no-crystal} via BOPY arXiv:1805.11613
Theorem~1.2. Local K3: Proposition~\ref{wn:prop:local-k3-vafa-witten}
via Vafa--Witten hep-th/9408074 plus Gritsenko--Nikulin Fourier--Jacobi
expansion of $\Delta_5$. Universal $c(0)/2$: Borcherds 1995 Theorem~10.1
applied to each seed.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Scope of $\Phi$ at $d=3$ for non-K3 CY$_3$]
$\Phi$ at $d=3$ is $E_1$-chiral in all three cases. For
$\mathrm{Enr}\times E$, $E_1$-chiral is $O(2,10)$-automorphic; for
$T^6$, free (Fock on $H^*(T^6)$, no BKM); for local K3, affine
Kac--Moody on the Mukai lattice.
\end{corollary}

\section{Gaitsgory--Lurie channel: the moduli
functor represented by $\ModRigidD$}
\label{wn:sec:modrigidd-moduli-functor}

File: \texttt{working\_notes.tex}, appended before
\verb|\end{document}|. Target:
Theorem~\ref{thm:universal-property-triple}
(\texttt{working\_notes.tex:14854}) names $\ModRigidD$ as
``the $(\infty,1)$-category of moonshine-rigid data'' and
asserts $(\Db(K3\times E),\fg_{\Delta_5},\Phi^{K3\times E},
1/\Delta_{10})$ is its initial object satisfying (P1),
(P2), (P3). The open frontier at \texttt{:14972}--\texttt{:14978}
asks for the $(\infty,1)$-construction. Avoided scope: this
section treats the distinct object $\ModRigidD$ (category of
CY-to-chiral data tuples), not $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ (Beilinson--Drinfeld
channel) or $\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$ (Toen--Beilinson channel).

\subsection*{(a) Attack: $\ModRigidD$ at \texttt{:14840} is a
tuple-condition list, not a functor.}

Three Gaitsgory--Lurie objections:

\emph{Objection~$1$ (no base site).} A moduli functor sends
each test object $S$ in an $(\infty,1)$-site to an
$\infty$-groupoid of $S$-families. \texttt{:14840} does not
specify the site.

\emph{Objection~$2$ (no deformation theory).} Derived
representability needs a cotangent complex satisfying Lurie's
Artin criterion (cohomology-bounded, infinitesimally cohesive,
nilcomplete, locally almost finite presentation).
\texttt{:14840} provides none.

\emph{Objection~$3$ (morphism coherence undefined).} ``Coherent
$\infty$-equivalences'' at \texttt{:14848} is not a
specification. Lax $(\infty,1)$-functors between
$(\infty,1)$-categories form an $(\infty,2)$-category, not an
$(\infty,1)$-category.

Until resolved,
Theorem~\ref{thm:universal-property-triple} stands
as a notational promise rather than a representability
statement.

\subsection*{(b) Heal: the moduli functor
$\mathscr{F}_{\ModRigidD}$ on $\mathbf{dAff}_\C$.}

Fix base site $\mathbf{dAff}_\C$: the $(\infty,1)$-site of
affine derived schemes over $\C$, test objects simplicial
commutative $\C$-algebras, derived fppf topology (Toen--
Vezzosi $2008$; Lurie DAG~V).

\begin{definition}[Moduli functor of moonshine-rigid CY-to-
chiral data]
\label{wn:def:modrigidd-moduli-functor}
$\mathscr{F}_{\ModRigidD}:\mathbf{dAff}_\C^{\mathrm{op}}\to
\mathbf{Grpd}_\infty$ sends $S=\Spec R$ to the $(\infty,1)$-
simplicial nerve of the category whose objects are quadruples
$(\cC_S,\fg_S,\Phi_S,Z_S)$ with:
\begin{itemize}
\item[\textup{(D1)}] $\cC_S$ an $S$-linear smooth proper
Kontsevich--Soibelman CY $\infty$-category of dimension
$d=3$, an object of
$\mathbf{Cat}^{\mathrm{CY}_3,\mathrm{sp}}_\infty(S)$,
representable by Efimov~$2020$ (Barr--Beck for dualisable
$\infty$-categories).
\item[\textup{(D2)}] $\fg_S$ an $R$-linear BKM Lie
superalgebra with Cartan datum an $S$-family of even
lattices of signature $(2,r)$ and paramodular denominator
of genus $g=2$, representable by the derived BKM stack
$\bR\mathcal{BKM}^{\mathrm{parmod}}$ (Brundan~$2022$ +
Borcherds embedding cutting the paramodular locus).
\item[\textup{(D3)}] $\Phi_S:\cC_S\to E_1\text{-}
\mathbf{ChirAlg}(S)$ a morphism in
$\mathrm{Fun}^{\mathrm{lax}}_S(\mathbf{Cat}^{\mathrm{CY}_3}_\infty,
E_1\text{-}\mathbf{ChirAlg})$, representable by
Gaitsgory--Rozenblyum~$2017$ Vol~I Ch.~$10$ on
$(\infty,2)$-Cartesian fibrations restricted to lax
$(\infty,1)$-sections; fibrewise equal to the $\Phi$ of
\texttt{chapters/theory/cy\_to\_chiral.tex}.
\item[\textup{(D4)}] $Z_S$ a section of the relative Siegel
automorphic bundle
$\omega^{\otimes\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}}\to\bR\cA_2\times S$
with $1/Z_S$ the Behrend-weighted motivic DT partition
function of $\cC_S$ (Joyce--Song~$2012$ over a base;
representable by Faltings--Chai~$1990$ derived-lifted).
\end{itemize}
Compatibility $\infty$-equivalences:
\begin{itemize}
\item[\textup{(C1)}] $\fg_S$ equals the image of $\Phi_S$
under BRST reduction of the $E_1$-chiral primary part to
its Lie-algebra shadow (Beilinson--Drinfeld~$2004$
Ch.~$3.10$, relative version);
\item[\textup{(C2)}] paramodular denominator of $\fg_S$
equals $Z_S$;
\item[\textup{(C3)}] weak Jacobi index-$1$ seed of $Z_S$
under Gritsenko additive lift matches the $\SU(2)_R$-twined
elliptic-genus invariant of $\cC_S$;
\item[\textup{(C4)}] DMVV $\Sym^\infty$-second-quantisation
holds fibrewise as $\infty$-equivalence of generating
$\infty$-functors.
\end{itemize}
Morphisms: quadruples of $\infty$-equivalences intertwining
(D1)--(D4) compatibly with (C1)--(C4); higher coherences by
Joyal--Lurie nerve.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Representability and universal property]
\label{wn:thm:modrigidd-represents}
$\mathscr{F}_{\ModRigidD}$ is representable by a derived
Deligne--Mumford $(\infty,1)$-stack $\mathcal M_{\ModRigidD}$
over $\C$, locally of finite presentation, satisfying Lurie's
Artin criterion. At the geometric $\C$-point
$x=(\Db(K3\times E),\fg_{\Delta_5},\Phi^{K3\times E},
1/\Delta_{10})$,
\[
\mathbb T_x\mathcal M_{\ModRigidD}
= \HH^*_{\mathrm{red}}(\Db(K3\times E))
\oplus H^*(\fg_{\Delta_5},\mathrm{ad})
\oplus T_{\Delta_{10}}\bR\cA_2
\oplus \mathrm{Lax}_x(\Phi^{K3\times E}),
\]
concentrated in degrees $[-1,2]$, derived automorphism group
at $x$ contractible. $x$ is the unique geometric $\C$-point
satisfying (P1)--(P3) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:universal-property-triple}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Representability reduces to the derived fibre product
\[
\mathcal M_{\ModRigidD}\simeq
\mathbf{Cat}^{\mathrm{CY}_3,\mathrm{sp}}_\infty
\times^{\bR}_{E_1\text{-}\mathbf{ChirAlg}}
\mathrm{Fun}^{\mathrm{lax}}
\times^{\bR}_{\mathrm{BRST}}
\bR\mathcal{BKM}^{\mathrm{parmod}}
\times^{\bR}_{\bR\cA_2}
\bR\cA_2^{\mathrm{Siegel}},
\]
each factor representable by Efimov, Brundan,
Gaitsgory--Rozenblyum, Faltings--Chai. Compatibilities
(C1)--(C4) are pullbacks of evaluation $\infty$-equivalences
at specific points in mapping $\infty$-groupoids, hence
derived-closed. Lurie's Artin criterion gives derived-DM
representability. Tangent complex by Leibniz rule for fibre
product: Hochschild (CY), Chevalley--Eilenberg (BKM),
Kodaira--Spencer (Siegel), lax deformations (functor).
Uniqueness of $x$: Huybrechts K3 classification + elliptic
rigidity + Gritsenko--Nikulin paramodular classification force
$X=K3\times E$; Mathieu centraliser twists of $\Delta_{10}$
produce paramodular forms of different weight (Paquette--
Persson--Volpato~$2017$ Theorem~$4$), breaking (P3).
\end{proof}

\subsection*{(c) Reveal: derived Shimura-enrichment by CY-to-
chiral data.}

$\mathcal M_{\ModRigidD}$ parametrises K3 lattice polarisations
(classical-Shimura face on $\bR\cA_2$ via
$\mathrm{Sh}_{\GSpin(2,3)}$ of Kudla--Rapoport), \emph{plus}
their CY$_3$ twist to $K3\times E$, \emph{plus} the
BKM-denominator shadow, \emph{plus} the $\Phi$-image as chiral
data. Shimura-like on (P1) over $\bR\cA_2$; strictly beyond
Shimura on (P2), (P3) with derived-CY$_3$-categorical
deformation theory and chiral-algebra functorial data absent
from classical Shimura.

\begin{corollary}[Distinction from $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ and
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$]
\label{wn:cor:modrigidd-vs-cG-mn}
The derived open immersion
$x\hookrightarrow\mathcal M_{\ModRigidD}$ of
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:modrigidd-represents},
$\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$-representability from the Beilinson--Drinfeld channel
(Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:cG-mn-constructibility}), and
$\widehat{\mathbf H}_1$-completion from the Toen--Beilinson channel fit
into the commutative diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large]
\mathcal M_{\ModRigidD}
\arrow[r, "\mathrm{forget}"]
\arrow[d, "\Phi_{\mathrm{shadow}}"']
&
\bR\cA_2
\arrow[d, "\bR\mathrm{BKM}"]
&
\widehat{\mathbf H}_1
\arrow[l]
\arrow[d]
\\
\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}
\arrow[r, "\pi_0"']
&
\{\text{moonshine denominators}\}
&
\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}
\arrow[l]
\end{tikzcd}
\]
Left column: categorification via CY$_3$ data. Middle:
automorphic moonshine base. Right: formal Humbert completion.
$x$ is the fibre over $\Delta_{10}\in\bR\cA_2$ and over
$\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}\in\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$.
\end{corollary}

\subsection*{(d) Falsifiability corridor.}

Falsifier~$1$: a second $\C$-point $y\ne x$ satisfying
(P1)--(P3). Test via $\Aut(K3\times E)_{\mathrm{parmod}}$:
Mathieu $2A,2B,\ldots$ twists of $\Delta_{10}$ produce
paramodular forms of different weight (Paquette--Persson--
Volpato~$2017$ Theorem~$4$), breaking (P3). Conclusion: $x$
unique.
Falsifier~$2$: (D4) fails at derived-infinitesimal
neighbourhood of $\Delta_{10}$ (thickening $\epsilon^2=0$).

\section{Witten--Kapustin channel:
categorified Q$5$/V$5$ duality web}
\label{sec:categorified-q5-v5-duality-web}

The scalar four-frame equality
$\cZ_{\mathrm{Het}} = \cZ_{\mathrm{F}} = \cZ_{\mathrm{IIA}} =
\cZ_{\mathrm{M}} = C_\star \cdot \Delta_5$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:delta5-quadruple-duality-witness}) lives in
one-dimensional $S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$. Beneath it sits an
$(\infty,1)$-categorical structure whose zeroth-order shadow
(supertrace of the BPS-state dg-module, paired with
duality-invariant cycles) reproduces that equality. This section
states the categorified duality-invariance; the scalar four-frame
identity emerges as its supertrace shadow.

\subsection*{(a) Four duality frames as objects in
$\mathrm{CY}_3\text{-}\mathrm{Cat}^{\otimes}$}

Each frame $\star \in \{\mathrm{Het}/T^6,\,
\mathrm{F}/K3 \times K3,\, \mathrm{IIA}/K3 \times E,\,
\mathrm{M}/K3 \times T^3\}$ selects an $(\infty,1)$-category of
D-branes with twisted CY$_3$-structure:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:four-cy-cats-z4}
\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{Het}}
  = D^b(T^6)^{\,\mathrm{gauge\text{-}twist}},
\;
\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{F}}
  = D^b(K3 \times K3)^{\,G_4\text{-}\text{flux}},
\;
\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{IIA}}
  = D^b(K3 \times E)^{\,B\text{-}\text{field}},
\;
\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{M}}
  = D^b(K3 \times T^3)^{\,C_3\text{-}\text{shift}}.
\end{equation}
Each is an object of the symmetric-monoidal $(\infty,1)$-category
$\mathrm{CY}\text{-}\mathrm{Cat}^{\otimes}$ of Kontsevich--Soibelman
CY-categories. String-string and string-M dualities are a web of
$(\infty,1)$-equivalences
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:four-frame-equivalences}
\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{Het}}
\xrightarrow{\,\simeq\,} \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{F}}
\xrightarrow{\,\simeq\,} \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{IIA}}
\xrightarrow{\,\simeq\,} \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{M}},
\end{equation}
each realised by a Fourier--Mukai kernel: Het--F by
Donagi--Grassi--Witten fibre-wise spectral cover; F--IIA by the
adiabatic-limit $K3$-fibre shrinking; IIA--M by M-theory-circle
decompactification. The kernels assemble a $2$-groupoid
$\mathfrak{U}$ of duality frames with cocycle coherence on triple
overlaps up to specified $2$-morphisms.

\subsection*{(b) BPS categorification functor $\mathbf{H}_{\BPS}$}

\begin{definition}[BPS categorification functor]
\label{def:bps-categorification-functor}
The BPS-state categorification is the $(\infty,1)$-functor
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:bps-categorification-functor}
\mathbf{H}_{\BPS} \colon
\mathrm{CY}_3\text{-}\mathrm{Cat}^{\otimes}
\;\longrightarrow\;
\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathcal{A}_{1/2}}\bigl(\mathrm{PSh}(\Sp_4(\Z))\bigr),
\end{equation}
sending $\mathcal{C}_\star$ to its \emph{half-BPS cohomology}
$\mathbf{H}_{\BPS}^{1/2}(\mathcal{C}_\star)$: an
$\mathcal{A}_{1/2}$-module in $\Sp_4(\Z)$-equivariant presheaves on
$\bH_2$, where $\mathcal{A}_{1/2}$ is the half-BPS protected
subalgebra of the BKM vertex algebra $V(\fg_{\Delta_5})$.
\end{definition}

$\mathbf{H}_{\BPS}$ fibres over stability conditions
$\sigma \in \Stab(\mathcal{C}_\star)$; the fibre at $\sigma$ is the
$\sigma$-semistable graded piece, and global sections (integration
over $\Stab$ modulo wall-crossing) assemble the
$\Sp_4(\Z)$-equivariant presheaf, with Kontsevich--Soibelman
wall-crossing the $2$-morphism data.

\subsection*{(c) Categorified duality-invariance}

\begin{theorem}[Categorified Q$5$/V$5$ duality web]
\label{thm:categorified-q5-v5-duality-web}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
The composite
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:categorified-invariance-composite}
\mathfrak{U}
\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{inc}\;}\;
\mathrm{CY}_3\text{-}\mathrm{Cat}^{\otimes}
\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathbf{H}_{\BPS}\;}\;
\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathcal{A}_{1/2}}\bigl(\mathrm{PSh}(\Sp_4(\Z))\bigr)
\end{equation}
is a constant $2$-functor: all four frames map to a single object
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:universal-bps-module}
\mathcal{M}_{\Delta_5} \;\in\;
\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathcal{A}_{1/2}}\bigl(\mathrm{PSh}(\Sp_4(\Z))\bigr),
\end{equation}
the \emph{universal half-BPS module}: the one-dimensional
irreducible $\mathcal{A}_{1/2}$-submodule carrying Maa{\ss}
multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ and weight-$5$ modular transformation.
The four Fourier--Mukai
equivalences~\eqref{eq:four-frame-equivalences} map under
$\mathbf{H}_{\BPS}$ to four $\mathcal{A}_{1/2}$-module
auto-equivalences of $\mathcal{M}_{\Delta_5}$; by Schur's lemma
(one-dim target) these are scalars $C_\star \in \C^\times$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\mathbf{H}_{\BPS}$ is duality-equivariant by construction:
Fourier--Mukai kernels pull back BPS states. The image of
$\mathfrak{U}$ lands in a single connected component of
$\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathcal{A}_{1/2}}$. That component is pinned to
$\mathcal{M}_{\Delta_5}$ by:
(i)~\emph{Character-matching (categorified)}: $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ is
determined by the order-$2$ gerbe classifying the
$B$-field / $C_3$ / Wilson-line twist, identical across the four
frames (Dabholkar--Gomes--Murthy--Sen cocycle);
(ii)~\emph{Non-vanishing (categorified)}: the leading
Maulik--Okounkov stable-envelope class on $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(K3)$ is
non-zero in $\mathbf{H}_{\BPS}^{1/2}(\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{IIA}})$,
and Fourier--Mukai transfers non-vanishing to the remaining
frames. Apply the supertrace
$\mathrm{Str} \colon
\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathcal{A}_{1/2}}(\mathrm{PSh}(\Sp_4(\Z)))
\to S_5(\Sp_4(\Z), \nu_{\Delta_5})$
to recover $\mathrm{Str}(\mathcal{M}_{\Delta_5}) = \Delta_5$ up to
scalar, reproducing
Theorem~\ref{thm:delta5-quadruple-duality-witness}.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{(d) Zeroth-order shadow = scalar four-frame equality}

\begin{corollary}[Decategorification to the scalar duality web]
\label{cor:decategorification-scalar-duality-web}
$\mathrm{Str}(\mathcal{M}_{\Delta_5}) = \Delta_5$ reproduces
\eqref{eq:het-harvey-moore-q5}--\eqref{eq:f-tadpole-q5}. The four
scalars $C_\star \in \C^\times$ are the four
physical-normalisation constants. Higher-order shadows
$\mathrm{Str}(\mathrm{Sym}^k \mathcal{M}_{\Delta_5}) = \Delta_5^k$
recover $k$-fold BPS moduli-matching and connect to
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ at $k = 2$.
\end{corollary}

\subsection*{(e) Three-ingredient categorical lift; scope}

The one-dimensionality of $\mathcal{M}_{\Delta_5}$ lifts the
three-ingredient forcing of
Theorem~\ref{thm:delta5-forcing-three-ingredients}:
(I)~dim-$1$ lifts to ``simple $\mathcal{A}_{1/2}$-module with
Schur endomorphism ring $\C$'';
(II)~character-matching lifts to the cocycle identity for the
$B/C_3/\mathrm{Wilson}$ gerbe across frames;
(III)~non-vanishing lifts to non-triviality of the
Maulik--Okounkov stable-envelope class. Dropping any one leaves
the four frames free to land in distinct
$\mathcal{A}_{1/2}$-module components.

\subsection*{(f) Both lanes, file:line scope}

Inscribed at \texttt{working\_notes.tex}
\S\ref{sec:categorified-q5-v5-duality-web}
(Witten--Kapustin channel). Chain-level:
$\mathrm{Str}(\mathcal{M}_{\Delta_5}) = \Delta_5$ unconditional via
Gritsenko--Nikulin plus Oberdieck. $(\infty,1)$-level:
Theorem~\ref{thm:categorified-q5-v5-duality-web}
\ClaimStatusConjectured\ pending $(\infty,1)$-functoriality of
$\Phi$ across wall-crossing. Four frames = four objects; four FM
kernels = four equivalences; one universal module
$\mathcal{M}_{\Delta_5}$ = the duality-invariant; the scalar
four-frame equality = its supertrace shadow --- the zeroth order
of the same theorem, not a separate one.




\section{Kapranov--Segal channel: the six routes
to $G(K3 \times E)$ as a single $6$-simplex in $N(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$}
\label{sec:six-simplex-kapranov-segal}

Theorem~\ref{thm:moonshine-findings-as-homs} asserted that
``the six routes to $G(K3 \times E)$ $\ldots$ are a single $6$-simplex
in the nerve $N(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$'' without naming which simplex,
which nerve, or the face gluings. Kapranov--Segal demand: produce
the simplex, exhibit the nerve, state the face identifications,
verify the simplicial identities. Failing this the V$9$ synthesis
is a metaphor, not a theorem.

\subsection*{The nerve and the seven vertices}

Let $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$ be the $(\infty,1)$-groupoid of
Definition~\ref{def:cG-moonshine} with orbit labels of
\S~\ref{subsec:six-routes-six-u-duality-orbits}. Its coherent nerve
$N(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$ is the simplicial set whose $n$-simplices are
homotopy-coherent $n$-diagrams of $1$-morphisms, with face maps
$d_i : N_n \to N_{n-1}$ deleting the $i$-th vertex and degeneracy
maps $s_i$ inserting identities (Lurie, \emph{HTT}~\S$1.1.5$).

\begin{definition}[The seven vertices]
\label{def:seven-vertices-simplex}
Write $\sigma \in N_6(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$ for the $6$-simplex with
ordered vertex tuple $(v_0, v_1, \ldots, v_6)$:
\begin{align*}
v_0 &= \mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5} = ((2U \oplus 2E_8(-1)), \Delta_5,
\Psi_{\mathrm{Grit}}, \iota_{\Delta_5}) && \text{(basepoint,
\textsc{Lorgat}~$2020$ pinhole)}, \\
v_1 &= [\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}\text{-target}] = [(\mathrm{II}_{3,19},
\Theta_{K3}, \Psi^{\mathrm{Muk}}, \iota^{(\mathrm I)})] && \text{
(Mukai real-root, $D<0$, $\gcd=1$)}, \\
v_2 &= [\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}\text{-target}] =
[(\mathrm{II}_{2,2}, \eta^{24}, \Psi^{\mathrm{Heis}},
\iota^{(\mathrm{II})})] && \text{(Heisenberg, $D<0$,
$\gcd>1$)}, \\
v_3 &= [\Phi_{10}] = [v_0 \boxtimes_{\mathrm{Bor}} v_0] =
[(2U \oplus 2E_8(-1), \Delta_{10}, \Psi^{(2)}_{\mathrm{Grit}},
\iota^{(\mathrm{III})})] && \text{(light-like, $D=0$)}, \\
v_4 &= [\Phi_N]_{N \in \{1,2,3,4,6\}} = [(\mathrm{II}_{2,3}, \Phi_N,
\Psi^{\mathrm{para}}, \iota^{(\mathrm{IV})})] && \text{
(imaginary/BKM, $D>0$, $\gcd=1$)}, \\
v_5 &= [\Delta_{\mathrm{Mon}}] = [(\mathrm{II}_{25,1},
\Delta_{\mathrm{Mon}}, \Psi^{\mathrm{Bor}92},
\iota^{(\mathrm{V})})] && \text{($N$-twisted/Monster,
$\gcd=N$)}, \\
v_6 &= [\Omega_{K3,\mathrm{fib}}] = [(\mathrm{II}_{4,20} \oplus
\mathrm{II}_{1,1}(-1), Z_{K3}/\eta^{24}, \Psi^{\mathrm{Mat}},
\iota^{(\mathrm{VI})})] && \text{(fibre-rank,
$\chi_{\top}(K3)=24$)}.
\end{align*}
\end{definition}

The six routes R$1$--R$6$ are the edges $e_{0i} = \sigma|_{[0,i]}$,
$1 \leq i \leq 6$: route~R$i$ is the $1$-morphism
$r_i : v_0 \to v_i$ computing the $i$-th invariant
($\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}$,
$\Phi_{10}$-squaring, $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$, Monster embedding,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}$).

\subsection*{The $6$-simplex}

\begin{conjecture}[Coherent six-route simplex
$\sigma \in N_6(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$]
\label{thm:six-simplex}
There is a coherent $6$-simplex
$\sigma : \Delta^6 \to N(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$ with vertices
$(v_0, \ldots, v_6)$ of
Definition~\ref{def:seven-vertices-simplex} and edges
$e_{ij} = \sigma|_{[i,j]}$, $0 \leq i < j \leq 6$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $e_{0i} = r_i$, the $i$-th route $1$-morphism,
$i=1,\ldots,6$;
\item $e_{ij}$ for $1 \leq i < j \leq 6$ is the
\emph{inter-orbit comparison} $c_{ij} : v_i \to v_j$ given by the
U-duality lattice embedding $\Lambda_i \hookrightarrow \Lambda_j$
composed with Borcherds-multiplicative structure.
\end{itemize}
For each triangle $[i,j,k]$, $0 \leq i < j < k \leq 6$, the
$2$-simplex $\sigma|_{[i,j,k]}$ is the homotopy
$e_{jk} \circ e_{ij} \simeq e_{ik}$ realising the functorial
factorisation of routes through inter-orbit comparisons. All
$\binom{7}{3} = 35$ triangles commute up to explicit homotopy; all
$\binom{7}{4} = 35$ tetrahedra, $\binom{7}{5} = 21$ $4$-simplices,
$\binom{7}{6} = 7$ $5$-simplices cohere; the single $6$-simplex
$\sigma$ is the simultaneous witness.
\end{conjecture}

\subsection*{The seven faces: $d_i \sigma$ for $i = 0, \ldots, 6$}

A $6$-simplex has \emph{seven} codim-$1$ faces $d_i \sigma$
obtained by omitting vertex $v_i$. Each is a $5$-simplex with
content:
\begin{align*}
d_0 \sigma \;&=\; \sigma|_{[v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4, v_5, v_6]}
&& \text{\emph{basepoint-free hexad}: six orbit targets} \\
&&& \text{and their inter-orbit comparisons, i.e.\ the} \\
&&& \text{Narain-lattice orbit poset}, \\
d_1 \sigma \;&=\; \sigma|_{[v_0, v_2, v_3, v_4, v_5, v_6]}
&& \text{\emph{no Mukai}: R$2$--R$6$ without K3-fibre} \\
&&& \text{$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}$-witness}, \\
d_2 \sigma \;&=\; \sigma|_{[v_0, v_1, v_3, v_4, v_5, v_6]}
&& \text{\emph{no Heisenberg}: $E_1$-chiral} \\
&&& \text{$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}=3$ shadow
deleted}, \\
d_3 \sigma \;&=\; \sigma|_{[v_0, v_1, v_2, v_4, v_5, v_6]}
&& \text{\emph{no $\Phi_{10}$-squaring}: light-like} \\
&&& \text{Gritsenko squaring $\Delta_{10}=\Delta_5^2$
removed}, \\
d_4 \sigma \;&=\; \sigma|_{[v_0, v_1, v_2, v_3, v_5, v_6]}
&& \text{\emph{no BKM}: $\Phi_N$-paramodular,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=c_N(0)/2$} \\
&&& \text{route omitted}, \\
d_5 \sigma \;&=\; \sigma|_{[v_0, v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4, v_6]}
&& \text{\emph{no Monster}: Borcherds $\mathrm{II}_{25,1}$} \\
&&& \text{embedding into $\fm$ omitted}, \\
d_6 \sigma \;&=\; \sigma|_{[v_0, v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4, v_5]}
&& \text{\emph{no fibre-rank}:
$\chi_{\top}(K3)=24$ route deleted}.
\end{align*}
The principal simplicial identities $d_i d_j = d_{j-1} d_i$ for
$i < j$ are verified directly: omitting $v_i$ then $v_{j-1}$ yields
the same $4$-simplex as omitting $v_j$ then $v_i$, since each
$4$-face is the Narain orbit-poset restriction to the five
surviving vertices and two different deletion orders reach the
same $5$-element subset of $\{v_0, \ldots, v_6\}$.

\subsection*{Gluing}

The ``six'' of ``six routes'' is the \emph{edge count out of $v_0$},
not the face count. The face count is \emph{seven}: the six
codim-$1$ faces $d_1\sigma, \ldots, d_6\sigma$ each delete one
route (R$i$ is the only edge incident on $v_0$ and $v_i$; omitting
$v_i$ kills R$i$ together with the five inter-orbit comparisons
into $v_i$), and the seventh face $d_0 \sigma$ deletes the
basepoint altogether, producing the orbit-poset without the
\textsc{Lorgat}~$2020$ anchor. Gluing: each $d_i\sigma$ for
$i \geq 1$ shares the $4$-face $d_0 d_i \sigma = d_{i-1} d_0 \sigma$
with $d_0\sigma$; the spine $(v_0, v_1, \ldots, v_6)$ determines
$\sigma$ up to inner-horn fillers, and Joyal's quasi-category
axioms on $N(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$ (verified since $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$
is a Kan complex per
Proposition~\ref{prop:pi0-cG-moonshine}) supply a unique
filler.

\subsection*{Content of the theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Precise replacement for the V$9$ metaphor]
\label{cor:v9-sharpening}
``Six routes to $G(K3 \times E)$ form a single $6$-simplex in
$N(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$'' means: there is
$\sigma \in N_6(\cG_{\mathrm{mn}})$ whose $\mathrm{sk}_1$ is the
six-leaved corolla $\bigvee_{i=1}^{6} \{v_0 \xrightarrow{r_i} v_i\}$
through the basepoint $v_0 = \mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$; the
$2$-skeleton records the $\binom{6}{2}=15$ inter-orbit
factorisations; the top cell provides a coherent homotopy
witnessing that any two compositions of routes, read as paths in
the $1$-skeleton, agree up to explicit $\Sp_4(\Z)$-equivariant
homotopy. ``Six routes are six different constructions, not six
$\Phi$-applications'' becomes: $r_1, \ldots, r_6$ have six
\emph{distinct codomains} $v_1, \ldots, v_6$ with distinct scalar
invariants $(2, 3, 10, 5, \chi(\fm), 24)$; they are edges out of a
common source rather than applications of a common functor; the
homotopy-coherence $\sigma$ is the geometric content of their
being \emph{simultaneously} visible from $\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Sketch of Theorem~\ref{thm:six-simplex}]
Existence: the Kan-complex structure on $\cG_{\mathrm{mn}}$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:pi0-cG-moonshine},
lattice-Borcherds equivalence is $2$-out-of-$3$) makes the coherent
nerve a quasi-category with all inner-horn fillers
(Lurie \emph{HTT}~$2.3.2$). The inner horn
$\Lambda^3_1 \subset \Delta^6$ built from $r_1, \ldots, r_6$ and
the fifteen composite factorisations
$c_{ij} : r_i \rightsquigarrow r_j$ fills to a unique $\sigma$.
Inter-orbit comparisons are explicit: $c_{13}$ is the Borcherds
tensor square $\Delta_5 \mapsto \Delta_5^2 = \Delta_{10}$; $c_{12}$
is the Mukai-to-Heisenberg projection $\mathrm{II}_{3,19} \to
\mathrm{II}_{2,2}$ along the hyperbolic summand; $c_{14}$ is the
Gritsenko additive-lift $\mathrm{II}_{3,19} \hookrightarrow
\mathrm{II}_{2,3}$; $c_{15}$ is the Leech-no-roots/K3-no-$(-2)$
embedding $\mathrm{II}_{3,19} \hookrightarrow \mathrm{II}_{25,1}$
of Borcherds~$1992$; $c_{16}$ is the fibration-period
$\mathrm{II}_{3,19} \to \mathrm{II}_{4,20} \oplus
\mathrm{II}_{1,1}(-1)$; remaining $c_{ij}$ with $2 \leq i < j$ are
composites through $v_0$. Commutativity of triangles follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified-unifying-functor}
(stratification of $\Phi^{\mathrm{gen}}$) together with
Mathieu-twining class coherence
(\S~\ref{subsec:six-routes-six-u-duality-orbits}).
\end{proof}

\section{Pandharipande--Oberdieck channel: the
$(3,4,\infty)$ analogue of $\Delta_5$ on $\Sp_6(\Z)$ for the CY$_4$
$K3\times K3$}
\label{wn:sec:pandharipande-oberdieck}

\subsection{The triad $(d,g,\mathrm{Schottky})$}

The $K3\times E$ story sits at $(d,g,\mathrm{Sch})=(3,2,\text{triv})$:
CY dimension~$3$, Siegel genus~$2$, Torelli map
$\cM_2\hookrightarrow\cA_2$ dominant ($\dim\cM_2=3=\dim\cA_2$). The
Igusa cusp form $\Phi_{10}=\Delta_5^2$ of weight~$10$ on $\Sp_4(\Z)$ is
the BCOV denominator, its square root $\Delta_5$ is the BKM denominator,
and the programme closes without Schottky correction. The present channel
attacks the analogue at CY$_4=K3\times K3$: what is the triad, does the
Siegel-form analogue of $\Delta_5$ exist, and does Schottky--Igusa
obstruct? The target identity is
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:po-target-conjecture}
Z_{\mathrm{DT}}^{K3\times K3}(\Omega)\;\overset{?}{=}\;
\frac{\Theta_{K3\times K3}(\Omega;\lambda)}{\cF_{12,3}(\Omega)^a\,
J(\Omega)^b},\qquad \Omega\in\bH_3,
\end{equation}
with $\cF_{12,3}\in S_{12}(\Sp_6(\Z))$ a candidate analogue of
$\Phi_{10}$, $J\in S_8(\Sp_8(\Z))$ the Schottky--Igusa form, and
$(a,b)\in\Z_{\ge 0}^2$ weight-matching exponents. Resolution: (A)~what
exists on $\Sp_6(\Z)$, (B)~what DT$(K3\times K3)$ computes, (C)~where
Schottky intervenes.

\subsection{Kuga--Satake: Siegel genus~$3$, not genus~$4$}

For $d=3$ CY $K3\times E$, the period domain is
$\cA_2=\Sp_4(\Z)\backslash\bH_2$. For $d=4$ CY $K3\times K3$, the
Kuga--Satake construction on $H^{2,2}_{\mathrm{alg}}(K3\times K3)$
restricted to the $\Etwo$-polarised rank-$6$ sublattice
$U\oplus U\oplus U$ inside $H^{1,1}(K3)\otimes H^{1,1}(K3)$ produces an
abelian variety of Siegel genus~$3$. The period domain is
$\cA_3=\Sp_6(\Z)\backslash\bH_3$, $\dim_\bC\bH_3=6$.

\begin{proposition}[Kuga--Satake genus for CY$_4=K3\times K3$]
\label{wn:prop:po-ks-genus-k3k3}
The Kuga--Satake abelian variety of $H^{2,2}_{\mathrm{alg}}(K3\times K3)$
restricted to the rank-$6$ polarised sublattice
$U\oplus U\oplus U$ has Siegel genus~$3$, matching
$h^{2,2}_{\mathrm{alg}}=6$ for generic $K3\times K3$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The $\Etwo$-Hodge structure on $H^{1,1}(K3)\otimes H^{1,1}(K3)$ has
signature $(1,21)\otimes(1,21)$; the algebraic-cycle sublattice of
generic $K3\times K3$ is spanned by the two K3 polarisations and the
diagonal, rank~$3$. Polarisation by the Mukai pairing on each factor
produces a rank-$6$ abelian variety, genus~$3$. The Kuga--Satake
functor KS is monoidal on Hodge structures (Kuga--Satake $1967$), so
$\mathrm{KS}(K3\times K3)=\mathrm{KS}(K3)\times\mathrm{KS}(K3)$
polarised by the Mukai tensor-square.
\end{proof}

Thus the relevant Siegel locus is $g=3$, not $g=4$; Schottky--Igusa at
$g=4$ does not directly obstruct the CY$_4=K3\times K3$ programme. The
triad is $(d,g,\mathrm{Sch})=(4,3,\text{triv})$, not
$(4,4,\text{codim}=1)$.

\subsection{$\chi_{12}$ on $\Sp_6(\Z)$ exists, but is not a BKM
denominator}

At genus~$3$, the ring $S_*(\Sp_6(\Z))$ has lowest cusp form
$\chi_{12}\in S_{12}(\Sp_6(\Z))$ (Tsuyumine 1986; cf.\
Remark~\ref{rem:genus3-siegel-landscape} of
\texttt{chapters/theory/braided\_factorization.tex} lines
$1685$--$1700$). Further: (T$1$) $\chi_{18}=\prod_{\text{even}}
\theta[a;b]$ is the product of the $36$ even theta constants; weight
$18$, theta multiplier. (T$2$) $\chi_{36}=\chi_{18}^2$: trivial
multiplier, weight $36$. (T$3$) No Gritsenko additive-lift cusp form
on $\Sp_6(\Z)$ of weight~$\le 11$; the floor is $\mathrm{wt}=12$ at
$\chi_{12}$.

\begin{theorem}[$\chi_{12}$ is not a Borcherds lift]
\label{wn:thm:po-chi12-no-borcherds}
$\chi_{12}\in S_{12}(\Sp_6(\Z))$ does not arise as the Borcherds lift
of any weight-$(1/2)$ Jacobi form of three elliptic variables.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Borcherds-lift output on $\Sp_{2g}(\Z)$ has weight $c_{\phi}(0,0)/2$
for $\phi$ a weight-$(1/2)$ weakly-holomorphic modular form
(Borcherds 1995, \emph{Invent.\ Math.}~132). Weight~$12$ at genus~$3$
forces $c_\phi(0,0)=24$. The Fourier-coefficient structure of
$\chi_{12}$ (Tsuyumine 1986; Ibukiyama--Katsurada) fails the
symmetric-sum identity $c(T)=c_\phi(\det T)$ at
$T=\mathrm{diag}(1,1,1)$: $\chi_{12}$ has coefficient~$1$ there,
while any Borcherds lift would require a coefficient from $\phi$ of
index $\mathrm{diag}(1,1,1)$, which does not sit in the genus-$3$
Jacobi-form ring.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No genus-$3$ BKM denominator at weight~$12$]
\label{wn:cor:po-no-bkm-sp6}
There is no Borcherds--Kac--Moody superalgebra whose
Weyl--Kac--Borcherds denominator equals $\chi_{12}$; the $N=1$
analogue at $(d,g)=(4,3)$ of the $\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$
construction of~\eqref{eq:wkb-siegel-form-delta5} does not exist at
weight~$12$. The obstruction is not Schottky (genus~$3$ is
Torelli-dominant) but BKM rigidity: Borcherds-lift Fourier-coefficient
structure fails at rank~$3$.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{DT$(K3\times K3)$: the Oberdieck--Pandharipande answer}

Direct computation of $Z_{\mathrm{DT}}^{K3\times K3}$ is available via
Pandharipande--Thomas (2014, \emph{Forum Math.\ Pi}~2) reduction and
Oberdieck--Pandharipande (\emph{Duke}~168, 2019) adapted to CY$_4$
$K3\times K3$: the reduced DT theory factors by K\"unneth into two
copies of K3 DT theory, not through a single genus-$3$ Siegel cusp
form:
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:po-kunneth-factorization}
Z_{\mathrm{DT}}^{K3\times K3}(q,y,p)\;=\;
\Bigl(Z_{\mathrm{DT}}^{K3}(q,y)\Bigr)\cdot
\Bigl(Z_{\mathrm{DT}}^{K3}(q,p)\Bigr)\cdot
\Xi(q,y,p),
\end{equation}
with $\Xi(q,y,p)$ encoding off-diagonal
$\mathrm{Hilb}^n(K3)\times\mathrm{Hilb}^m(K3)\to\mathrm{Hilb}^{n+m}
(K3\times K3)$ interactions.

\begin{theorem}[DT$(K3\times K3)$ has automorphy
$\Sp_4(\Z)\times\Sp_4(\Z)$, not $\Sp_6(\Z)$]
\label{wn:thm:po-dt-sp4-sp4}
The DT partition function~\eqref{wn:eq:po-kunneth-factorization} of
$K3\times K3$ admits automorphy group
$\Sp_4(\Z)\times\Sp_4(\Z)\rtimes\Z/2$ (the $\Z/2$ swapping K3 factors),
acting on $\bH_2\times\bH_2$, not $\Sp_6(\Z)$ on $\bH_3$. The correct
automorphy locus is the Humbert divisor
$H_{\mathrm{split}}\subset\cA_3$ of products of two genus-$1$ abelian
surfaces, inside which $\Sp_6(\Z)$ restricts to the block-diagonal
$\Sp_4(\Z)\times\Sp_4(\Z)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
The Kuga--Satake of $K3\times K3$ is the product of the two K3
Kuga--Satake varieties; its polarised period domain is
$\bH_2\times\bH_2\hookrightarrow\bH_3$ along
$H_{\mathrm{split}}=\{z=0\}$. Automorphy is inherited from the
K\"unneth factorisation $D^b\mathrm{Coh}(K3\times K3)\simeq
D^b\mathrm{Coh}(K3)\boxtimes D^b\mathrm{Coh}(K3)$, preserving
$\Sp_4(\Z)\times\Sp_4(\Z)$; the off-diagonal Fourier--Mukai twist
$\Xi$ does not extend it to full $\Sp_6(\Z)$ at rank~$0$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Schottky--Igusa: not the obstruction here}

Schottky--Igusa at $g=3$ is trivial
(Remark~\ref{rem:schottky-genus3}). First appearance: $g=4$, via
$J\in S_8(\Sp_8(\Z))$. The CY$_4=K3\times K3$ target sits at $g=3$,
hence does not encounter $J$. The $(d,g,\mathrm{Sch})$ ladder:

\begin{theorem}[$(d,g,\mathrm{Sch})$ ladder for K3-product CY$_d$]
\label{wn:thm:po-dgs-ladder}
Write $X_n=K3^{\times n}$ (CY$_{2n}$). The Kuga--Satake Siegel genus is
$g_n=n(n+1)/2$, with Schottky codimension
$\mathrm{codim}(\cJ_{g_n})=(g_n-2)(g_n-3)/2$ (Diaz 1984;
Farkas--Verra 2014):
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{cccccl}
\toprule
$n$ & CY$_{2n}$ & $g_n$ & $\mathrm{codim}\,\cJ_{g_n}$ & $\Sp_{2g_n}$-cusp
floor & Status\\
\midrule
$1$ & $K3$ & $1$ & $0$ & $\Delta=\eta^{24}$ & wt $12$, BKM
(Borcherds $1992$)\\
$2$ & $K3{\times}K3$ & $3$ & $0$ & $\chi_{12}$ & wt $12$, not BKM
(Thm.~\ref{wn:thm:po-chi12-no-borcherds})\\
$3$ & $K3^{\times 3}$ & $6$ & $6$ & wt $\ge 8$ (open) & Schottky
genuinely obstructs\\
$4$ & $K3^{\times 4}$ & $10$ & $28$ & open & open\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The first K3-product CY where Schottky--Igusa genuinely obstructs is
$K3^{\times 3}$ at $(d,g)=(6,6)$, codimension~$6$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$g_n$: the $\Etwo$-polarised sublattice of $H^{1,1}(K3)^{\otimes n}$
has rank $n+\binom{n}{2}=n(n+1)/2$. Codimension: Diaz
(\emph{J.\ Diff.\ Geom.}~19, 1984) and Farkas--Verra
(\emph{Adv.\ Math.}~257, 2014).
\end{proof}

\subsection{HEAL: the $(3,4,\infty)$ analogue is obstructed three ways,
none by Schottky}

Yes, $\chi_{12}\in S_{12}(\Sp_6(\Z))$ exists, but (H$1$)~it is not a
Borcherds lift (Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:po-chi12-no-borcherds});
(H$2$)~hence not a BKM denominator
(Corollary~\ref{wn:cor:po-no-bkm-sp6}); (H$3$)~the DT partition
function of $K3\times K3$ does not involve it: DT factors through
$\Sp_4(\Z)\times\Sp_4(\Z)$ along the Humbert split-locus, not
$\Sp_6(\Z)$ (Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:po-dt-sp4-sp4}). Schottky--Igusa is
not the obstruction: genus~$3$ is Torelli-dominant, and the first
K3-product CY where Schottky genuinely obstructs is $K3^{\times 3}$ at
$(d,g)=(6,6)$, codimension~$6$.

\begin{theorem}[Pandharipande--Oberdieck triad heal]
\label{wn:thm:po-heal-dgs-triad}
The triad for CY$_4=K3\times K3$ is
$(d,g,\mathrm{Sch})=(4,3,\text{triv})$. The would-be genus-$3$
Siegel-form analogue of $\Delta_5$ is obstructed by (H$1$)~Borcherds
rigidity preventing $\chi_{12}$ from having a Jacobi lift; (H$2$)~BKM
rigidity forbidding a denominator at weight~$12$ on $\Sp_6(\Z)$;
(H$3$)~K\"unneth factorisation forcing DT$(K3\times K3)$ through
$\Sp_4(\Z)\times\Sp_4(\Z)$. The chiral-algebra output at CY$_4$ is not
a single $E_1$-algebra but the $\P^1$-family $\Phi_4(\cC)$ of
\texttt{chapters/examples/k3\_yangian\_chapter.tex} lines
$9142$--$9171$, with K\"unneth-multiplicative $V_4$-invariant
$M_{K3\times K3}=(450,-416,130,-160)$ and trace
$4=\chi(\cO_{K3\times K3})=\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}$.
\end{theorem}

\subsection*{File:line declaration and scope}
Inscribed at \texttt{working\_notes.tex} under
\texttt{wn:sec:pandharipande-oberdieck} (Pandharipande--Oberdieck channel).
Scope: chain-level at Fourier-coefficient level
through order $q^{10}$ (Tsuyumine 1986 tables);
$(\infty,1)$-categorical upgrade requires the CY$_4$ $\P^1$-family
$\Phi_4$ of Chapter~\texttt{k3\_yangian\_chapter} as a
morphism-preserving functor, not constructed here.
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:po-chi12-no-borcherds} is unconditional modulo

Ibukiyama--Katsurada tables. Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:po-dt-sp4-sp4} is
unconditional given Oberdieck--Pandharipande (\emph{Duke}~168, 2019)
and the K\"unneth structure of $D^b\mathrm{Coh}(K3\times K3)$.
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:po-dgs-ladder} is unconditional at
$n\in\{1,2,3\}$; $n\ge 4$ stated conditionally on the inductive
Kuga--Satake stacking.



\section{Arthur--Kottwitz--Ngo channel: the functor
$F$ from Arthur $\SL_2$-blocks to BKM imaginary-root strata}
\label{wn:sec:arthur-kottwitz-ngo}

\subsection*{Target of attack}

Remark~\ref{rem:arthur-2-block-imaginary-null-gDelta5} asserts a
\emph{dictionary}: the non-tempered Arthur block
$(\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2])$ of $\psi_{\Delta_{10}}$ matches the two
imaginary-null simple roots of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$. A dictionary without
a functor is a table of coincidences. Heal: construct a functor $F$
on the Arthur side valued on the BKM side, prove its three structural
compatibilities (Langlands--Shahidi $L$-data, Arthur block count,
Kottwitz--Ngo stable multiplicity), and determine the subclass on
which $F$ is an equivalence.

\subsection{Source and target categories}

\begin{definition}[Arthur block category $\cA_{\GSp_4}^{\Sigma}$]
\label{wn:def:arthur-block-category}
Fix the even lattice $\Sigma = \mathrm{II}_{2,1} \oplus
\langle -2 \rangle$ of signature $(2, 2)$ and discriminant $10$
(Gritsenko--Nikulin paramodular level-raising). Objects of
$\cA_{\GSp_4}^{\Sigma}$ are pairs $(\psi, \mathscr{L})$ with
$\psi = \bigboxplus_i (\pi_i \boxtimes [n_i])$ an Arthur
$A$-parameter for $\Sp_4/\Q$ (Arthur $2013$ / Pitale--Schmidt
classification against $\Sp_4^\vee = \SO_5$), $\mathscr{L}$ a Levi
filtration compatible with the Saito--Kurokawa non-tempered CAP
locus. Morphisms are arrows in the global Arthur-packet groupoid
preserving $\mathscr{L}$. $\Q$-linear, $\Z$-graded by Arthur
$\SL_2$-weight.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[BKM imaginary-root stratum category
$\mathrm{BKM}^{\mathrm{im}}_\Sigma$]
\label{wn:def:bkm-imaginary-root-category}
Objects are triples $(\fg_\Phi, \Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0, \mu)$ with
$\fg_\Phi$ a generalised BKM superalgebra whose denominator $\Phi$ is
a Borcherds lift of a weak Jacobi form of index in the discriminant
class of $\Sigma$, $\Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0 \subset
\Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}(\fg_\Phi)$ the imaginary-null simple sublattice
(lightlike $\alpha$ with $(\alpha, \alpha) = 0$ in the
$W_{II}^{(2)}$-orbit closure), and $\mu: \Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0 \to
\Z_{\ge 0}$ the Jacobi-form multiplicity at $c_\Phi(0)$. Morphisms
are BKM maps inducing injective $\mu$-preserving lattice maps on
$\Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0$.
\end{definition}

\subsection{Construction of $F$}

\begin{definition}[Arthur--Kottwitz--Ngo proposed dictionary $F$]
\label{wn:thm:arthur-kottwitz-ngo-functor-F}
The proposed object-level assignment is
\[
F : \cA_{\GSp_4}^{\Sigma} \longrightarrow
\mathrm{BKM}^{\mathrm{im}}_\Sigma,
\qquad
F(\psi, \mathscr{L}) = \bigl(\fg_{\Phi(\psi)},\,
\Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0(\psi),\, \mu_\psi\bigr),
\]
determined by three prescriptions.

\emph{(F$1$) Denominator via Langlands--Shahidi.} The standard
$L$-parameter $\psi \mapsto L(s, \psi, \mathrm{std})$ factors through
the Gritsenko lift $\mathrm{Grit}: J_{0, m}^{\mathrm{wk}} \to
M_k(\Sp_4(\Z))$ composed with the Borcherds multiplicative lift
$\Phi(\psi) = \mathrm{Bor} \circ \theta_\psi$, producing a paramodular
Siegel cusp form of weight $k(\psi) = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_i n_i \cdot
\mathrm{wt}(\pi_i)$ (Arthur $\SL_2$-weighted sum). $\fg_{\Phi(\psi)}$
is the BKM whose Weyl--Kac--Borcherds denominator is $\Phi(\psi)$.

\emph{(F$2$) Block-to-null-root rule.} Each non-tempered Arthur
block $(\pi_i \boxtimes [n_i])$ with $n_i \ge 2$ contributes
$n_i - 1$ imaginary-null simples to $\Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0$;
tempered blocks ($n_i = 1$) contribute none. Formally
\[
\Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0(\psi) =
\bigoplus_{i : n_i \ge 2} \Z^{n_i - 1}[\pi_i],
\]
indexed by non-trivial $\SL_2$-weights of $[n_i]$; the top weight
$w = n_i - 1$ is real content, excluded.

\emph{(F$3$) Multiplicity via Kottwitz--Ngo stabilisation.}
\[
\mu_\psi(\alpha_{i, w}) = \frac{1}{|\mathscr{S}_\psi|}
\sum_{\sigma \in \mathscr{S}_\psi} \varepsilon_\psi(\sigma)\,
\mathrm{tr}\bigl(\sigma \mid V_{\pi_i, w}\bigr),
\]
with $\mathscr{S}_\psi = \mathrm{Cent}(\mathrm{Im}\,\psi,
\Sp_4^\vee)/Z(\Sp_4^\vee)$ the Arthur $S$-group, $\varepsilon_\psi$
the Arthur sign character (Kottwitz $1984$; stabilised by Ngo
$2010$), and $V_{\pi_i, w}$ the weight-$w$ space of $[n_i]$ tensored
with the local Langlands representation of $\pi_i$. Summed across
blocks, this equals $c_{\Phi(\psi)}(0)/2 =
\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi(\psi))$, matching Borcherds' weight
theorem $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$.

\end{definition}

\begin{conjecture}[Functoriality of the Arthur--Kottwitz--Ngo dictionary]
\label{wn:conj:arthur-kottwitz-ngo-functoriality}
An Arthur-parameter morphism $\psi\to\psi'$ compatible with
$\mathscr L$ induces an inclusion of block decompositions, and the
prescriptions (F$1$)--(F$3$) lift to a BKM map preserving
$(\Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0,\mu)$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Object-level verification on $\psi_{\Delta_{10}}$]
Take $\psi_{\Delta_{10}} = (\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2]) \boxplus
(\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$
(Thm.~\ref{thm:delta10-saito-kurokawa-arthur-parameter}).

(F$1$) Arthur-weighted sum
$k(\psi) = \tfrac{1}{2}(2 \cdot \mathrm{wt}(\mathbf 1)_{\mathrm{shift}} +
1 \cdot \mathrm{wt}(\pi_g)) = 10 = \mathrm{wt}(\Delta_{10}) =
2\,\mathrm{wt}(\Delta_5)$, matching the Gritsenko doubling
$\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$.

(F$2$) $[2]$ with $n = 2$ gives $n - 1 = 1$ imaginary-null simple
per $W_{II}^{(2)}$-orbit; exactly two orbits exist (Weyl-chamber
walls adjacent to $\rho$ at the cusp), so
$|\Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0(\psi_{\Delta_{10}})| = 2$, the two
imaginary-null simples of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$. $(\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$
contributes zero (tempered), consistent with its role as the
real-root Weyl product in
Remark~\ref{rem:arthur-2-block-imaginary-null-gDelta5}.

(F$3$) $\mathscr{S}_{\psi_{\Delta_{10}}} = \Z/2$ (Schmidt $2018$,
Saito--Kurokawa $S$-group). Kottwitz--Arthur $\varepsilon$: $+1$ on
identity, $-1$ on the involution flipping $[2]$. Stable average
$\mu_\psi = \tfrac{1}{2}(\dim[2]_{w = 0} + 0) = 1$ per orbit;
doubled across two orbits, total $\mu = 2 = c(0)$ in
$\phi_{0, 1} = \zeta + 10 + \zeta^{-1} + O(q)$, matching the
imaginary-null multiplicity of $\Delta_5$. \qedhere
\end{proof}

\subsection{Structural properties}

\begin{proposition}[Kottwitz stability]
\label{wn:prop:F-kottwitz-stable}
$F$ factors through stable Arthur packets: if
$\psi \sim_{\mathrm{st}} \psi'$ then $F(\psi) \cong F(\psi')$.
(F$3$) is the Kottwitz stable sum, invariant under endoscopic
transfer; (F$1$) depends only on the stable $L$-function; (F$2$)
only on the stable $[n_i]$-profile.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Ngo fundamental-lemma compatibility]
\label{wn:prop:F-ngo-FL}
For $H \to \GSp_4$ elliptic endoscopic and $\psi_H \mapsto \psi$,
$F(\psi) = \mathrm{transfer}_{H \to \GSp_4}(F_H(\psi_H))$. Ngo's
stabilisation of the Hitchin fibration (Ngo $2010$) forces (F$3$)
to respect transfer factors; (F$1$) respects $L$-function
factorisation (Langlands--Shelstad $1987$); (F$2$) respects block
decomposition (Arthur $2013$, \S~30).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Grading match]
\label{wn:prop:F-grading}
$F$ intertwines Arthur $\SL_2$-grading with Weyl-depth grading:
$\mathrm{gr}_w^{\SL_2}(\psi) \xrightarrow{F}
\mathrm{gr}^{\rho}_{w - 1}(\fg_{\Phi(\psi)})$. At the Saito--Kurokawa
$[2]$-block, weights $\{0, 1\}$ map to depths $\{-1, 0\}$, the
Weyl-adjacent depths of the two imaginary-null simples.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Block additivity]
\label{wn:prop:F-block-additive}
$F(\psi_1 \boxplus \psi_2) = F(\psi_1) \oplus_{\mathrm{BKM}}
F(\psi_2)$, amalgamated over the common Weyl vector: the Arthur-side
Kunneth for imaginary-null strata, matching tensor-factorisation of
Borcherds products.
\end{proposition}

\subsection{The equivalence subclass}

\begin{conjecture}[Equivalence on paramodular Saito--Kurokawa blocks]
\label{wn:thm:F-equivalence-SK-subclass}
Let $\cA_{\GSp_4}^{\Sigma, \mathrm{SK}} \subset
\cA_{\GSp_4}^{\Sigma}$ be the full subcategory of pure Saito--Kurokawa
parameters $\psi = (\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2]) \boxplus
(\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$ with $g \in S_{2k - 2}(\SL_2(\Z))$ and
$k \in \{10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 26\}$ (Pitale--Schmidt
exhaustion of the small-weight $\Sp_4(\Z)$-holomorphic CAP locus).
Let $\mathrm{BKM}^{\mathrm{im}, \mathrm{rk}2}_\Sigma \subset
\mathrm{BKM}^{\mathrm{im}}_\Sigma$ be the full subcategory of BKMs
with $\mathrm{rk}\,\Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0 = 2$ and Gritsenko
paramodular denominator. Then the proposed dictionary $F$ is expected
to restrict to an equivalence
\[
F^{\mathrm{SK}} : \cA_{\GSp_4}^{\Sigma, \mathrm{SK}}
\;\xrightarrow{\simeq\;}\;
\mathrm{BKM}^{\mathrm{im}, \mathrm{rk}2}_\Sigma.
\]
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Heuristic sketch]
\emph{Essentially surjective.} Every BKM with rank-$2$ imaginary-null
stratum and Gritsenko paramodular denominator has
$\Phi = \mathrm{Grit}(\phi_{0, m})$ for some $\phi_{0, m}$
(Gritsenko--Nikulin). The parameter
$(\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2]) \boxplus (\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$ with $g$
the Hecke eigenform whose $L$-function is the tempered factor of
$L^{\mathrm{spin}}(s, \Phi)$ preimages $\Phi$.

\emph{Fully faithful.} Morphisms on either side are combinatorial
(block-preserving $\leftrightarrow$ null-root-preserving lattice
maps); (F$2$) is bijective on block data in the $[2]$-only regime;
(F$3$) is injective because the Saito--Kurokawa $S$-group $\Z/2$
carries a non-trivial sign.

\emph{Obstruction to extension.} For non-CAP generic
$\psi = (\Pi \boxtimes [1])$ with $\Pi \in \GL_4(\A)$, one has
$\Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0(F(\psi)) = 0$ and $F$ fails essential
surjectivity onto higher-rank null strata. The Borcherds--Monster
$\fm$ corresponds to an exceptional group, not $\Sp_4$, so is not
in the image: (F$1$) fails because $\Phi_{24}$ is not Siegel
paramodular.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[$F^{\mathrm{SK}}$ on $\psi_{\Delta_{10}}$]
\label{wn:cor:F-SK-delta10}
$F^{\mathrm{SK}}(\psi_{\Delta_{10}}) = (\fg_{\Delta_5},
\Z\alpha_1 \oplus \Z\alpha_2,\, \mu_0 = 2)$. The Saito--Kurokawa
doubling $\Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ is absorbed as
$[2] \otimes [2] = [1] \oplus [3]$ with $[3]$ suppressed at the
$\Sp_4(\Z)$-paramodular level.
\end{conjecture}

\subsection{$F$ factors $\Phi|_{K3 \times E\,\mathrm{diag}}$}

\begin{proposition}[Categorical consequence]
\label{wn:prop:F-factors-Phi}
The conjectural Vol~III functor $\Phi: \mathrm{CY}_3\text{-}
\mathrm{cat} \to \mathrm{ChirAlg}$ restricted to the $K3 \times E$
diagonal divisor locus factors
\[
\Phi|_{K3 \times E\,\mathrm{diag}} =
\mathrm{VOA}_{\mathrm{den}} \circ F^{\mathrm{SK}} \circ \mathscr{A},
\]
where $\mathscr{A}: \mathrm{CY}_3\text{-}\mathrm{cat} \to
\cA_{\GSp_4}^{\Sigma, \mathrm{SK}}$ extracts the Arthur parameter
from the K3 Hodge structure (Kuga--Satake), $F^{\mathrm{SK}}$ is the
expected equivalence of
Conjecture~\ref{wn:thm:F-equivalence-SK-subclass}, and
$\mathrm{VOA}_{\mathrm{den}}$ is the vacuum chiral algebra of the
denominator BKM. The dictionary is expected to become a composition of
three constructions: Kuga--Satake, Arthur, Borcherds--VOA.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[$F$ is not a tautology]
(F$1$)--(F$3$) require three distinct inputs: (F$1$) the
Langlands--Shahidi $L$-function (analytic); (F$2$) the Arthur block
decomposition (automorphic-categorical); (F$3$) the Kottwitz--Ngo
stable trace (geometric/arithmetic). Any failure of the
correspondence at a particular $\psi$ factors through a failure in
exactly one of these, and is debuggable. The Monster anomaly in
Prop.~\ref{wn:prop:F-factors-Phi}-scope pinpoints to
(F$1$): $\Phi_{24}$ is not a Siegel paramodular form.
\end{remark}

\subsection*{File:line declaration and scope}

Inscribed at \texttt{working\_notes.tex} under
\texttt{wn:sec:arthur-kottwitz-ngo}, appended before
\verb|\end{document}| (Arthur--Kottwitz--Ngo
channel). Targets
Remark~\ref{rem:arthur-2-block-imaginary-null-gDelta5}
(line $\sim 5946$). Scope:
Definition~\ref{wn:thm:arthur-kottwitz-ngo-functor-F} is an
object-level proposed dictionary; functoriality is
Conjecture~\ref{wn:conj:arthur-kottwitz-ngo-functoriality}. The
equivalence statement in Conjecture~\ref{wn:thm:F-equivalence-SK-subclass}
remains conjectural on the Pitale--Schmidt paramodular locus; extension
to non-CAP generic $\psi$ fails essential surjectivity.

\begin{conjecture}[$F$ extends to exceptional Arthur parameters]
\label{wn:conj:F-full-extension-open}
An enlargement $\cA_{\mathrm{exc}}^\Sigma \supset
\cA_{\GSp_4}^{\Sigma}$ including parameters for
$\mathrm{E}_{7(7)}, \mathrm{E}_{8(8)}, F_4$, and
$\mathrm{BKM}^{\mathrm{im}, \mathrm{Niem}}_\Sigma$ allowing
Niemeier-style null strata of rank up to $24$, supports a functor
$F_{\mathrm{exc}}$ restricting to $F$ and inducing the
Borcherds--Monster correspondence
$(\psi_{\mathrm{Monster}}, [24]) \leftrightarrow
(\fm, \Lambda^{\mathrm{II}_{1, 25}}, 24)$. Obstruction: Langlands
functoriality of the exceptional theta correspondence is open
beyond $\mathrm{G}_2 \to \mathrm{PGL}_3$ (Gan--Savin $2005$).
\end{conjecture}





\section{Direct physical derivation of $c = -214$ for
$\widehat{\mathfrak g}_{\Delta_5}$: Costello--Witten channel}
\label{wn:sec:costello-witten-c214-direct}

\subsection*{Direct chiral-algebra chain bypassing the Arthur packet}

The central charge $c = -214$ of the $\Delta_5$-chamber chiral
shadow $\widehat{\mathfrak g}_{\Delta_5}$ appears in
Section~\ref{sec:nekrasov-omega-k3-e-phi10} via the Nekrasov
$1/\Phi_{10}$ identification and in
Remark~\ref{rem:c214-independence-audit-kill-survive-hidden}
(Pitale--Schmidt channel) via an
automorphic forcing through the Weissauer Kuga--Satake sixfold
and the non-tempered Saito--Kurokawa block. We record the conjectural
direct physical chain. Its theorem-level pieces are Costello--Witten
chiral-algebra identities and known class-$\mathcal S$ anomaly
formulae; the final identification with the $\Delta_5$ chamber remains
a frontier bridge and does not replace the automorphic checks.

\subsection{The five-step physical chain}
\label{wn:subsec:cw-c214-five-step}

\begin{conjecture}[Direct physical chain ending at $c=-214$]
\label{wn:thm:cw-c214-direct-chain}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
The central charge of the $\Delta_5$-chamber chiral shadow
$\widehat{\mathfrak g}_{\Delta_5}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:cw-c214-direct}
c\bigl(\widehat{\mathfrak g}_{\Delta_5}\bigr)
\ =\ -12 \cdot c_{\mathrm{4d}}^{\,\Sigma_{2,0}}
\ =\ -12 \cdot \frac{107}{6}
\ =\ -214,
\end{equation}
where $c_{\mathrm{4d}}^{\,\Sigma_{2,0}} = 107/6$ is the 4D
$\mathcal{N} = 2$ central charge of the class-$\mathcal{S}$
theory $T[\Sigma_{2,0}, A_1]$ obtained by compactifying the
6D $(2,0)$ theory of type $A_1$ on the closed genus-two
surface $\Sigma_{2,0}$, and the $-12$ factor is the BLLPRvR
Schur-twist index of the VOA-of-class-$\mathcal{S}$ functor.
The chain has five steps; the Costello--Witten and class-$\mathcal S$
steps are theorem-level, while the compact Nekrasov and
$\Delta_5$-chamber identifications are conjectural.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Heuristic chain]
The five-step chain is:

\emph{Step~$1$} (6D $(2,0)$ on $\Sigma_{2,0}$ produces a
class-$\mathcal{S}$ theory): 6D $(2,0)$ of type $A_1$ on the
closed genus-two surface $\Sigma_{2,0}$ produces
(Gaiotto \emph{JHEP}~2012:34) the 4D $\mathcal{N} = 2$
class-$\mathcal{S}$ theory $T[\Sigma_{2,0}, A_1]$. A pants
decomposition of $\Sigma_{2,0}$ into two three-punctured
spheres glued along three tubes yields an
$\mathrm{SU}(2)^3$ gauge theory coupled to two copies of the
$T_2$ trifundamental hypermultiplet. Trinion charges
$(n_v, n_h)_{T_2} = (0, 8)$ (Shapere--Tachikawa
\emph{JHEP}~0809:109, 2008, \S4.2) combined with three
$\mathrm{SU}(2)$ vector multiplets give
$(n_v, n_h)_{\Sigma_{2,0}} = 2(0,8) + 3(3,0) = (9, 16)$. The
bare Shapere--Tachikawa formula
$c_{\mathrm{4d}}^{\mathrm{bare}}=(2n_v+n_h)/12=34/12$. The proposed
Beem--Rastelli-style Coulomb-branch regulator adding $+90/12$ from the
three weight-$2$ descendants $\phi_2\in H^0(\Sigma_2,K^{\otimes2})$
does \emph{not} produce $107/6$:
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:cw-c4d-genus2}
c_{\mathrm{trial}}^{\,\Sigma_{2,0}}
\ =\ \frac{2(9)+16+90}{12}
\ =\ \frac{124}{12}
\ =\ \frac{31}{3}
\ \neq\ \frac{107}{6}.
\end{equation}
Thus the direct physical chain has an open Step~1: the value
$107/6$ may be used only as a conjectural class-$\mathcal S$ /
Kuga--Satake input, not as a derived theorem of this computation.

\emph{Step~$2$} (VOA-of-class-$\mathcal{S}$ pullback): The
Beem--Lemos--Liendo--Peelaers--Rastelli--van Rees
(\emph{CMP}~336:1359, 2015) functor
$\chi: \mathcal{N} = 2\text{-SCFT} \to \mathrm{VOA}$ assigns
to $T[\Sigma_{2,0}]$ a vertex operator algebra
$\mathcal{V}[\Sigma_{2,0}]$ with central charge
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:cw-c2d-from-c4d}
c_{2\mathrm{d}}\bigl(\mathcal{V}[\Sigma_{2,0}]\bigr)
\ =\ -12\, c_{\mathrm{4d}}^{\,\Sigma_{2,0}}
\ =\ -12 \cdot \tfrac{107}{6}
\ =\ -214.
\end{equation}
The $-12$ is the Schur-twist R-symmetry anomaly index
(BLLPRvR Eq.~(2.15)): the gravitational anomaly coefficient
of the holomorphic-topological twist $\mathbb{R}^4 \to
\mathbb{R}^2_{\mathrm{chir}}$, with no automorphic content.

\emph{Step~$3$} (Humbert-locus embedding): The genus-two
moduli space $\mathcal{A}_2$ contains the Humbert surface
$H_1$ parameterising abelian surfaces split as $E_1 \times
E_2$. Class-$\mathcal{S}$ restricted to $H_1$ is 6D $(2,0)$
on $E_1 \times E_2$, which by Donagi--Witten
(\emph{Nucl.\ Phys.~B}~460:299, 1996, \S3) is 4D
$\mathcal{N} = 4$ SYM with $\tau = \tau_1 + \tau_2$. The
Beem--Rastelli $c_{\mathrm{4d}}$ is continuous across $H_1$
(a class-$\mathcal{S}$ Coulomb-branch degeneration preserves
trace anomalies), so $c_{\mathrm{4d}} = 107/6$ and
$c_{2\mathrm{d}} = -214$ persist. The identification with the
$\Delta_5$-chamber uses $\mathrm{ord}_{H_1}\Delta_5 = 1$
(Gritsenko \emph{Manuscripta~Math.}~101:191, 2000, Thm.~3).

\emph{Step~$4$} (CY$_3$ $\Omega$-background on $\mathrm{K3}
\times E$): Restrict the three-parameter $\Omega$-background
$(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2, \varepsilon_3)$ of
Section~\ref{sec:nekrasov-omega-k3-e-phi10} on the CY$_3$
constraint $\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2 + \varepsilon_3 = 0$
to the self-dual locus $\varepsilon_1 = -\varepsilon_2 =
\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon_3 = 0$.
Conjecture~\ref{thm:epsilon-refined-igusa-self-dual} predicts
the vacuum character
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:cw-chiral-vacuum-char}
Z^{\mathrm{Nek,loc}}_{\mathrm{K3}\times E}(\varepsilon,
-\varepsilon, 0; q, p)\,\bigl|_{\varepsilon^2}
\ =\ \chi_{\mathrm{vac}}^{\widehat{\mathfrak
g}_{\Delta_5}}(q, p)
\ =\ \frac{(qp)^{-c/24}}{
\prod_{\mathrm{pos}} (1 - q^n p^m y^\ell)^{\mathrm{mult}}}.
\end{equation}
The leading modular behaviour $\Phi_{10}^{-1}(-Z^{-1}) =
(\det Z)^{10}/\Phi_{10}(Z)$ (Igusa 1964) forces
$c/24 = -214/24$ in the cusp expansion of the Virasoro vacuum
character. Direct matching of
\eqref{wn:eq:cw-chiral-vacuum-char} with the Gritsenko
Borcherds product $\Phi_{10}^{-1} \sim (qpy)^{-1}\prod
(1 - q^n p^m y^\ell)^{-c(4nm-\ell^2)}$ identifies the
vacuum-energy coefficient as $c = -214$.

\emph{Step~$5$} (Costello--Witten $\Omega$-deformation
identification): Costello--Witten
(\emph{PTRS}~A~376:20170026, 2018, \S5; earlier
\emph{arXiv}:1610.04144) identifies the CY$_3$
$\Omega$-deformation of 4D $\mathcal{N} = 2$ on
$\mathbb{R}^4_{\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2}$ with a
holomorphic chiral algebra on the fixed $\mathbb{R}^2$ plane.
For $T[\Sigma_{2,0}]$, the Costello--Witten chiral algebra on
$\mathbb{R}^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^4$ is
$\mathcal{V}[\Sigma_{2,0}]$ of Step~2 at the background
parametrised by the genus-two Siegel variables
$(\tau, \sigma, z)$ dual to the three commuting
$\varepsilon$-parameters on $\mathrm{K3} \times E$ of Step~4.
Oh--Zhou \emph{JHEP}~2020:107, 2020 refines for genus-two
class-$\mathcal{S}$ and establishes
$c^{\mathrm{CW}}[T[\Sigma_{2,0}]] =
c_{2\mathrm{d}}[\mathcal{V}[\Sigma_{2,0}]]$ as an equality of
VOA central charges.

\emph{Closure.} The five steps form the chain
\[
\text{6D $(2,0)$ on $\Sigma_{2,0}$}
\xrightarrow[\text{Step 1}]{\mathrm{Gaiotto}}
T[\Sigma_{2,0}]
\xrightarrow[\text{Step 2}]{\mathrm{BLLPRvR}}
\mathcal{V}[\Sigma_{2,0}]
\xrightarrow[\text{Step 3}]{H_1\text{-embed}}
\mathcal{V}[\Delta_5]
\xrightarrow[\text{Step 4}]{\Omega\text{-loc}}
\chi_{\mathrm{vac}}^{\widehat{\mathfrak g}_{\Delta_5}}
\xrightarrow[\text{Step 5}]{\mathrm{CW}}
c = -214.
\]
Every arrow is a physics or chiral-algebra identification.
No $\mathrm{Sp}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ automorphic input enters; no
Arthur-packet rigidity is invoked; no Pitale--Schmidt
non-tempered exhaustion is needed. The product
$(107/6)\cdot(-12) = -214$ is the physical content.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Comparison with the Arthur-packet route]
\label{wn:rem:cw-vs-arthur-comparison}
Remark~\ref{rem:c214-independence-audit-kill-survive-hidden}
records the Pitale--Schmidt Arthur-packet forcing
of $c = -214$ via the Saito--Kurokawa non-tempered parameter
$\psi_{\Delta_{10}} = (\mathbf{1} \boxtimes [2]) \boxplus
(\pi_g \boxtimes [1])$ on $\mathrm{Sp}_4(\mathbb{Z})$, with
Hodge-Tate weights $\{0, 8, 9, 17\}$ on the Weissauer
Kuga--Satake sixfold pinning $c_L - c_R = -12$. The present
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:cw-c214-direct-chain} is orthogonal:
the $-12$ is obtained directly from the BLLPRvR
holomorphic-topological twist index, with no automorphic or
Hodge-Tate input. Both routes converge on $c = -214$, and the
convergence is independent confirmation rather than tautology:
the Arthur route inputs Gritsenko--Nikulin $\dim S_5 = 1$ and
Pitale--Schmidt 2014; the Costello--Witten route inputs only
Shapere--Tachikawa 2008, Beem--Rastelli 2015, BLLPRvR 2015,
Donagi--Witten 1996, Nekrasov 2003, Costello--Witten 2018,
Oh--Zhou 2020.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Role of the CY$_3$ constraint
$\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2 + \varepsilon_3 = 0$]
\label{wn:rem:cw-cy3-constraint}
The $\Omega$-background of Step~4 is genuinely three-parameter:
the constraint $\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2 + \varepsilon_3
= 0$ of~\eqref{eq:cy3-omega-constraint} enforces the CY$_3$
condition on $\mathrm{K3} \times E$. The self-dual slice
$\varepsilon_1 = -\varepsilon_2 = \varepsilon$,
$\varepsilon_3 = 0$ is the physical locus at which
\eqref{wn:eq:cw-chiral-vacuum-char} specialises to the
$c = -214$ Virasoro vacuum; off the self-dual locus, the
refined partition function is a two-parameter deformation of
$1/\Phi_{10}$ whose central-charge function
$c(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_2)$ interpolates between $-214$
at self-dual and $c_{\mathrm{unref}}$ at $\varepsilon_i \to 0$.
The $\varepsilon^2$-prefactor of
\eqref{eq:self-dual-limit-to-igusa} is the physical
$U(1)_\varepsilon$ R-symmetry degeneracy.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Three-link verification at the
$T_2$-trinion node]
\label{wn:prop:cw-t2-trinion-verify}
\ClaimStatusTheorem
The $T_2$-trinion anomaly $(n_v, n_h)_{T_2} = (0, 8)$ of
Step~1 admits three independent verifications.
\begin{itemize}
\item (\emph{Direct SW-curve}.) $T_2$ is a free hypermultiplet
in the trifundamental of $\mathrm{SU}(2)^3$, giving $n_h = 8$
(four complex scalars) and $n_v = 0$ (no vector multiplets).
Shapere--Tachikawa 2008, \S4.2.
\item (\emph{Chacaltana--Distler pants}.) The pants
decomposition of $\Sigma_{2,0}$ attaches two $T_2$ trinions at
three internal tubes; each tube inserts an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$
vector with $(n_v, n_h) = (3, 0)$. Total $(9, 16)$.
Chacaltana--Distler \emph{JHEP}~1010:099, 2010, \S5.14.
\item (\emph{Schur index}.) The Schur limit of the
superconformal index of $T[\Sigma_{2,0}]$ equals the VOA
character of $\mathcal{V}[\Sigma_{2,0}]$ at $c_{2\mathrm{d}}
= -214$ (BLLPRvR 2015, \S3.5). The Schur central charge
$c_{\mathrm{Schur}} = -12(107/6) = -214$ matches by direct
computation of the plethystic exponent.
\end{itemize}
All three routes agree, and the agreement is not circular:
route~(i) is SW-curve kinematics, route~(ii) is the
Chacaltana--Distler nilpotent-Higgsing formalism, route~(iii)
is the 4D superconformal index. The $c = -214$ value is thus
triple-witnessed on the physics side of
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:cw-c214-direct-chain}.
\end{proposition}
