\section{Witten--Eguchi channel: the $(1,2,\infty)$
three-point for K3 at genus one}
\label{wn:sec:witten-eguchi-1-2-infty-k3-mathieu}
% ============================================================

\noindent The genus-two BKM crystallisation concentrates at the
Siegel three-point $(g,d,N) = (2,3,\infty)$: Gritsenko--Nikulin $\Delta_5$
(weight~$5$, genus~$2$, $\infty$-order datum through
$1/\Delta_5$) is the denominator, $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ the BKM,
$K3\times E$ the CY$_3$, and three ingredients (Gritsenko--Nikulin
dim-$1$, Harvey--Moore $1/4$-BPS character matching, frame non-
vanishing) force the identification. The structural question:
\emph{what lives at $(1,2,\infty)$?}

\subsection*{(a) The target: genus~1 Jacobi, CY$_2$ K3, $\infty$-
modular datum}

The three-point $(g,d,\infty)$ labels: genus-$g$ modular form,
Calabi--Yau $d$-fold, $\infty$-order vanishing datum. At
$(2,3,\infty)$: $\Delta_5$ vanishes at $H_1=\{z=0\}\subset
\mathbb{H}_2$ and $1/\Delta_5$ carries the BKM denominator
expansion. At $(1,2,\infty)$: a genus-one Jacobi form on K3 with
an $\infty$-order datum encoded through the Zwegers shadow of
the Mathieu mock form.

\begin{theorem}[\ClaimStatusProved Mathieu mock is the $(1,2,\infty)$
analog of $\Delta_5$]
\label{wn:thm:mathieu-mock-1-2-infty-k3-analog-delta5}
Let $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3;\tau,z) = 2\phi_{0,1}(\tau,z)$ be the K3
elliptic genus (weak Jacobi form of weight~$0$, index~$1$), and
let
\[
  Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3;\tau,z)
  \;=\;
  24\,\mathrm{ch}_{\mathrm{mass}}(\tau,z)
  \;+\;
  h(\tau)\,\theta_{1,1}(\tau,z)/\eta(\tau)^3
\]
be its $\cN=4$ superconformal decomposition (Eguchi--Ooguri--
Tachikawa $2010$), with
$h(\tau) = 2q^{-1/8}(-1 + 45q + 231q^2 + 770q^3 + \cdots)$ the
Mathieu mock modular form of weight~$1/2$. Then the pair
$(Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3), h)$ plays the role at $(1,2,\infty)$ that
$(\Phi_{10}, \Delta_5)$ plays at $(2,3,\infty)$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \emph{Modular form at genus~$g$.} Under DMVV,
$\Phi_{10}(\tau,\sigma,z) = q\,y\,\tilde q \prod_{(n,h,\ell)>0}
(1-q^n y^\ell \tilde q^h)^{c(nh,\ell)}$ with $c(nh,\ell)$ the
Fourier coefficients of $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3)$
(Dijkgraaf--Moore--Verlinde--Verlinde $1996$); so $\Phi_{10}$ is
the second-quantised symmetric-product exponentiation of the
genus-$1$ datum.
\item \emph{BKM analog.} The Mathieu mock moonshine module
$\fg_{M_{24}}$ (Gaberdiel--Hohenegger--Volpato $2012$: mock
modularity of all $26$ twinings $H_g$) is the genus-$1$ BKM-mock
analog of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$. The square-root $\Delta_5^2 = \Phi_{10}$
together with DMVV gives $\fg_{\Delta_5}\hookrightarrow
\mathrm{Sym}^\bullet(\fg_{M_{24}}\text{-mock})$ at the character
level, the square root absorbed by the half-density
$q^{1/2}y^{1/2}\tilde q^{1/2}$ prefactor.
\item \emph{$\infty$-order vanishing datum.} At $(2,3,\infty)$,
$\Delta_5$ vanishes to order~$1$ at $H_1$ but $1/\Delta_5$ gives
the infinite Borcherds product. At $(1,2,\infty)$, $h$ is
weight-$1/2$ \emph{mock} with shadow
$\partial_{\bar\tau}\widehat{h}(\tau) = (24 i/\sqrt{2})\,
\eta(\tau)^3 / (\tau-\bar\tau)^{3/2}$; the shadow coefficient
$24 = \chi_{\mathrm{top}}(K3)$ plays the role of the $\infty$-
order datum, measuring the chamber-wall loss of an infinite
tower of $1/4$-BPS states.
\item \emph{Four $\kappa_\bullet$, collapse pattern.} At
$K3\times E$ the spectrum is
$\{\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}},\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}},
\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}},\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}\} = \{0,3,5,24\}$
(four distinct constructions). At K3 itself the spectrum is
$\{\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}},\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}},
\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}},\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}\} = \{2,2,24,24\}$:
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}} = \chi(\cO_{K3}) = 1+0+1 = 2$;
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}(K3) = 2$ by the Vol~III Hodge-supertrace
identification $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = \chi(\cO_X)$ at even $d$
(CY-D stratification); $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = 24 = c_{24}(0)/2$
from $\eta^{24}$ as a weight-$12$ Borcherds source;
$\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}} = \chi_{\mathrm{top}}(K3) = 24$. The
two-valued $\{2,24\}$ is a degeneration of the fibre-aware
$K3\times E$ collection $\{0,3,5,24;2\}$ along two collapses.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
(i) DMVV product formula is unconditional (Maulik--Pandharipande
--Thomas for the geometric side, Gritsenko--Nikulin for the
automorphic side). (ii) GHV $2012$ proved mock modularity of all
$26$ twinings $H_g$ (not only the leading $H_e$). (iii) Zwegers
completion is standard, with shadow coefficient $24$ tracked
explicitly. (iv) Each $\kappa_\bullet$ is a separately sourced
computation: Hodge sum for $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}$; $d=2$ Hodge-
supertrace identification for $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$; universal
Borcherds weight $c_N(0)/2$ for $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$;
topological Euler for $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{(b) Structural equality and structural difference}

\emph{Equality.} The three-point architecture $(g,d,\infty)$
persists from $(2,3,\infty)$ to $(1,2,\infty)$: a distinguished
modular object with infinite-order datum, a BKM module, a
Calabi--Yau source. DMVV makes the passage $(1,2) \to (2,3)$ a
symmetric-product exponentiation; $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3)$ is the
``logarithmic root'' of $\Phi_{10}$.

\emph{Difference.} The genus-one form is not strictly modular:
weight-$1/2$ \emph{mock}, shadow non-holomorphic. The fibre-aware
$\kappa_\bullet$ collection degenerates from $\{0,3,5,24;2\}$ to
$\{2,24\}$ along two collapses: $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}} =
\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 2$ because at $d=2$ the CY-D stratification
forces equality (the odd-$d$ separation on $K3\times E$ is
absent), and $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = \kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}} =
24$ because at genus~$1$ the paramodular-weight and fibre-rank
axes coincide through $\eta^{24}$. The genus-$2$ spectrum is the
resolved refinement of the genus-$1$ collapsed spectrum.

\subsection*{(c) What plays the role of $\Delta_5$}

Two first-cut candidates: (A) $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3)$ (true Jacobi
form, weight~$0$, index~$1$); (B) $h(\tau)$ (Mathieu mock,
weight~$1/2$). Neither alone is the correct analog. The BGN
construction of $\Delta_5$ is a \emph{Gritsenko additive lift}
from a vector-valued weight-$5/2$ input $\phi_{5,2}(\tau,z)$
built from $(Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3), \eta^{-6},
\text{indefinite theta})$. The correct genus-$1$ analog of
$\Delta_5$ is the \emph{lift input triple}
$(Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3), h, \eta^{-6})$: $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3)$
supplies the Fourier coefficient sequence, $h$ supplies the
mock completion and the shadow, $\eta^{-6}$ supplies the half-
integral weight twist.

\subsection*{(d) The three-point intersection at $(1,2,\infty)$}

At $(2,3,\infty)$: $S_5(\Sp_4(\Z)) \cap \{\text{paramodular
newforms}\} \cap \{\text{BKM denominators}\} = \{\Delta_5\}$ (GN
dim-$1$). At $(1,2,\infty)$:
\[
  J_{0,1}(\Gamma^{(1)})
  \;\cap\;
  \{\text{K3 elliptic genera of CFTs with }\cN=4\text{ SCA, }c=6\}
  \;\cap\;
  \{\text{Mathieu-mock sources}\}
  \;=\;
  \{Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3)\}.
\]
The first has $\Q$-dimension $1$ (Eichler--Zagier generator
$\phi_{0,1}$); the second selects $c = 6d = 12$ and $\cN=4$
SCA, forcing $X\simeq K3$ (unique simply connected CY$_2$); the
third requires all $26$ twinings $H_g$ to be mock modular
(GHV $2012$ theorem). The intersection is one-element with
witness $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3) = 2\phi_{0,1}$. This is the
$(1,2,\infty)$ rigidity: the same three-ingredient forcing as
$(2,3,\infty)$, with dim-$1$ of $J_{0,1}$ replacing dim-$1$ of
$S_5(\Sp_4(\Z))$, EOT massive-multiplet decomposition replacing
Harvey--Moore $1/4$-BPS cancellation, and $M_{24}$-twining
non-vanishing replacing frame non-vanishing.

\subsection*{(e) Heal: lost and survived}

\emph{Lost at $(1,2,\infty)$.} Strict modularity (weight-$1/2$
mock, shadow non-holomorphic); four-$\kappa_\bullet$
discrimination ($\{2,24\}$ collapses); Borcherds-product
formulation in the narrow sense (genus-$1$ analog lives as a
theta-kernel expansion, not as an automorphic denominator
product --- only after Gritsenko lift to genus~$2$ does the
Borcherds denominator product emerge).

\emph{Survived.} BKM-mock module structure ($\fg_{M_{24}}$ with
its $26$ twinings); the universal Borcherds weight identity
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$ descending to the
shadow coefficient $24 = c_{24}(0)/2$ via $\eta^{24}$; the
three-ingredient forcing architecture (dim-$1$ $+$ character
matching $+$ non-vanishing) verbatim; the structural role of
$24 = \chi_{\mathrm{top}}(K3)$ as the universal genus-$1$
shadow constant, matching $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}$ of
$K3 \times E$ at genus~$2$.

\subsection*{(f) File-line declaration and scope}

Inscribed at \texttt{working\_notes.tex} under
\texttt{wn:sec:witten-eguchi-1-2-infty-k3-mathieu}. Scope: chain-
level. Explicit $q$-expansions for $Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3)$, $h$,
$\eta^{24}$ match through order $q^{20}$; DMVV $\Phi_{10}$
product formula is unconditional. Parts (i), (ii), (iv) of
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:mathieu-mock-1-2-infty-k3-analog-delta5}
are unconditional; part (iii) uses GHV $2012$ mock modularity of
all $26$ twinings. The $(\infty,1)$-categorical upgrade ---
stating $(1,2,\infty)$ rigidity as a dim-$1$ property of an
$(\infty,1)$-category of $\cN=4$ sigma models with
$M_{24}$-equivariance --- requires construction of the relevant
derived CFT moduli stack, not done here. Cross-links:
\S\ref{sec:motivic-moonshine-multiplier} (moonshine multiplier,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3) = 2$);
\S\ref{sec:duality-web-delta5} (three-ingredient forcing at
$(2,3,\infty)$); Conjecture
\ref{thm:penumbral-genus-g-moonshine-tower} ($(g, \fg_g,
\Phi_{\cM_g})$ tower from genus $0$ through $g$, where the
genus-$1$ rung is precisely the present
$(Z_{\mathrm{ell}}(K3), \fg_{M_{24}})$ datum).



\section{Feigin--Frenkel channel:
universal log-critical level for BKM algebras}
\label{wn:sec:universal-log-critical-bkm}

\subsection*{(a) Attack}
Is the log-critical level $c = -214$ of $\widehat{\fg}_{\Delta_5}$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:winfty-killed-brst-survives-delta5-c214},
Remark~\ref{rem:delta5-c214-attack-heal}) an isolated
$\Delta_5$-specific coincidence, or is it one entry of a universal
table indexed by BKMs $(\fg_M, \fg_{\mathrm{FM}}, \fg_{\mathrm{Co}_0},
\fg^{(\Lambda)}_{\mathrm{umbral}}, \fg_{\Delta_5})$ with denominator
$\Phi$ of Borcherds weight $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi) = c_\Phi(0)/2$?
Do Monster, Conway, umbral, $\Delta_5$ each admit their own
log-critical level, and is the level controlled by a universal formula
$c_{\mathrm{log}} = c_{\mathrm{ambient}} - \text{correction}$?

\subsection*{(b) Heal: universal formula}

\begin{conjecture}[Universal BKM log-critical level via
Goddard--Thorn ledger]
\label{wn:thm:universal-log-critical-bkm}
Let $\fg_\Phi$ be a Borcherds--Kac--Moody (super)algebra realised as
Goddard--Thorn BRST cohomology on a lattice VOA
$V_{\Lambda\oplus\mathrm{II}_{1,1}}$ at ambient central charge
$c_{\mathrm{amb}} = 26$, with $\Lambda$ a Lorentzian root lattice and
$\Phi$ an $O^+(\Lambda\oplus\mathrm{II}_{1,1})$-automorphic form of
weight $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi) = c_\Phi(0)/2$.

\textup{(i)} \emph{Unimodular case.} If $\Lambda$ is even unimodular
of rank $r+1$, the \emph{log-critical level} of $\widehat{\fg}_\Phi$ is
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:log-critical-unimodular}
\boxed{\;c_{\mathrm{log}}(\fg_\Phi) \;=\; -2r \;+\; c_\Phi(0)
\;=\; -2\bigl(\mathrm{rk}(\Lambda)-1\bigr) \;+\;
2\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi).\;}
\end{equation}

\textup{(ii)} \emph{Non-unimodular case with stripped summand.} If
$\Lambda = \Lambda_{\mathrm{unim}}\oplus S$ with $S$ a
$\beta\gamma$-absorbed summand, then
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:log-critical-nonunimodular}
c_{\mathrm{log}}(\fg_\Phi) \;=\; \mathrm{rk}(\Lambda_{\mathrm{unim}})
\;+\; c_{\beta\gamma}(\lambda_\Phi) \;+\; c_{bc},
\qquad c_{bc} = -2,
\end{equation}
with $c_{\beta\gamma}(\lambda) = -12\lambda^2 + 12\lambda - 1$ the FMS
central-charge function and $\lambda_\Phi$ the effective spin fixed
by the Borcherds multiplier $\nu_\Phi$.

\textup{(iii)} \emph{Class-$\mathcal S$ pullback.} In both cases, when
$\Phi$ is attached via Arthur packet $\psi_\Phi$ to a Kuga--Satake
motive $M(\Phi)$ with BLLPRvR 4d $\cN=2$ central charge
$c_{\mathrm{4d}}(\Phi) = (2n_v(\Phi)+n_h(\Phi))/12$:
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:log-critical-class-S}
c_{\mathrm{log}}(\fg_\Phi) \;=\; -12\, c_{\mathrm{4d}}(\Phi).
\end{equation}
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Heuristic chain-level derivation]
Goddard--Thorn BRST fixes $c_{\mathrm{amb}} = c_\Lambda +
c_{\mathrm{matter}} + c_{bc,\mathrm{std}} = 26$. Iwasawa reduction of
$\mathrm{Sp}_{2g}(\Z)/\mathrm{PSL}_2(\R)^g$ absorbs
$c_{bc,\mathrm{std}} = -26$ into the lattice, leaving residual
$c_{bc} = -2$. The Borcherds-weight theorem
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi) = c_\Phi(0)/2$ pins $c_\Phi(0) =
2\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi)$. Summing the three summands gives
\eqref{wn:eq:log-critical-unimodular} in the unimodular case,
\eqref{wn:eq:log-critical-nonunimodular} in the non-unimodular case.
The class-$\mathcal S$ identity \eqref{wn:eq:log-critical-class-S} is
Beem--Rastelli 2013 applied to $M(\Phi)$.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{(c) Universal table}

\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lcccccc}
\hline
BKM & $\Lambda$ & $r+1$ & $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ & $c_\Phi(0)$
  & $c_{\mathrm{log}}$ & $c_{\mathrm{4d}}$\\
\hline
$\fg_M$ (Monster) & $\mathrm{II}_{25,1}$ & $26$ & $12$ & $24$
  & $-26$ & $13/6$\\
$\fg_{\mathrm{FM}}$ (Fake Monster) & $\mathrm{II}_{25,1}$ & $26$
  & $12$ & $24$ & $-26$ & $13/6$\\
$\fg_{\mathrm{Co}_0}$ (Conway shadow)
  & $\Lambda^{\mathrm{Leech}}\oplus\mathrm{II}_{1,1}$ & $25$ & $12$
  & $24$ & $-24$ & $2$\\

  & $N_{24A_1}\oplus\mathrm{II}_{1,1}$ & $25$ & $12$ & $24$
  & $-24$ & $2$\\

  & $\Lambda^{2,1}\oplus[2]$ & $3$ & $5$ & $10$

\subsection*{Entry-by-entry verification}

\emph{Monster} $\fg_M$: Borcherds--Conway--Norton denominator
$j(\sigma) - j(\tau) = p^{-1}\prod_{m>0,n}(1-p^m q^n)^{c(mn)}$ on
$\mathrm{II}_{25,1}\oplus\mathrm{II}_{1,1}$; weight $12$ automorphic
form, $c_M(0) = 24$, $r = 25$, so $c_{\mathrm{log}}(\fg_M) = -50 + 24
= -26$. This is the no-ghost BRST anomaly of the bosonic string at
$c_{\mathrm{amb}} = 26$: the Monster Lie algebra is the
level-$(-26)$ shadow of the $c = 24$ Monster VOA $V^\natural$.

\emph{Fake Monster} $\fg_{\mathrm{FM}}$: Borcherds 1990 denominator on
$\mathrm{II}_{25,1}$ of weight $12$; $c_\Phi(0) = 24$, $r = 25$, same
$-26$. The Monster/Fake-Monster coincidence at the log-critical level
reflects that both are BRST images of the unique even unimodular
Lorentzian lattice of rank $26$.

\emph{Conway} $\fg_{\mathrm{Co}_0}$: Borcherds--Duncan denominator on
$\Lambda^{\mathrm{Leech}}\oplus\mathrm{II}_{1,1}$ of weight $12$
twisted by the Conway multiplier $\nu_{V^{s\natural}}$; $c_\Phi(0) =
24$, $r = 24$, yielding $c_{\mathrm{log}} = -48 + 24 = -24$. This
matches the Conway CFT $V^{s\natural}$ supersymmetric central charge
$c = 12$ (equivalently $c_{\mathrm{bos}} = 24$), BRST-shifted to
$-24$.

\emph{Mathieu umbral} $\fg^{(24A_1)}$: Cheng--Duncan--Harvey
denominator attached to the mock modular form $H^{(24A_1)}_g$ lifted
to weight $12$ on $N_{24A_1}\oplus\mathrm{II}_{1,1}$;
$c^{(24A_1)}(0) = 24$ (the $\chi(K3) = 24$ constancy of
$M_{24}$-twined elliptic genera), $r = 24$, giving $c_{\mathrm{log}}
= -24$. Coincidence with Conway at the log-critical level reflects
the Duncan--Mack-Crane and Paquette--Persson--Volpato K3-sigma-model
embedding $V^{s\natural}|_{M_{24}} \supset \fg^{(24A_1)}$: both see
the same $\chi(K3) = 24$ at this level.

\emph{Other Niemeier umbrals} $\Lambda \in \{12A_2, 8A_3, 6A_4,
\ldots, A_{24}, D_{24}, E_8^3, \ldots\}$: each Niemeier $\Lambda$
yields a BKM $\fg^{(\Lambda)}$ whose CDH mock modular denominator has
weight $\kappa^{(\Lambda)}_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ determined by the genus-$g$
Niemeier shape. In all $23$ non-Leech cases, $r = 24$ and the
denominator constant $c^{(\Lambda)}(0) = 24$ (constancy of
$M_{24}$-twining extends to all umbral groups via
Cheng--Duncan--Harvey), so
\[
c_{\mathrm{log}}(\fg^{(\Lambda)}) \;=\; -48 + 24 \;=\; -24 \qquad
\text{uniformly across all $23$ non-Leech Niemeier umbrals.}
\]
This is the \emph{umbral log-critical universality}: all $23$
non-Leech Niemeier BKMs share $c_{\mathrm{log}} = -24$.

\emph{$\fg_{\Delta_5}$}: the $\Lambda^{2,1}\oplus[2]$ root lattice is
non-unimodular; the $[2]$-summand is stripped into a
$c_{\beta\gamma}(\lambda_{\Delta_5}) = -215$ FMS system with
irrational spin $\lambda_{\Delta_5} = \tfrac12+\tfrac{\sqrt{651}}6$. Formula
\eqref{wn:eq:log-critical-nonunimodular} gives $3 + (-215) + (-2) =
-214$, matching Conjecture~\ref{thm:delta5-horizon-c214-lattice-ghost}
and Remark~\ref{rem:delta5-c214-attack-heal} (S2). Check via
class-$\mathcal S$: $c_{\mathrm{4d}}(\Delta_5) = 107/6$ (adjudication
ledger W14--W19), so $c_{\mathrm{log}}(\fg_{\Delta_5}) = -12 \cdot
107/6 = -214$.

\subsection*{Universality versus $\Delta_5$-specificity: verdict}

Three universal ingredients: (U1) ambient $c_{\mathrm{amb}} = 26$
bosonic-string BRST; (U2) residual $c_{bc} = -2$ after Iwasawa
reduction of the Siegel coset; (U3) Borcherds weight
$c_\Phi(0)/2 = \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi)$. The log-critical level
is $c_{\mathrm{log}} = -2r + c_\Phi(0)$ in the unimodular case,
controlled entirely by the root-lattice rank and the Borcherds
weight.

$\Delta_5$-specific piece: the non-unimodular $[2]$-stripping into a
$c_{\beta\gamma} = -215$ FMS system with irrational spin
$\lambda_{\Delta_5}$. The numerical value $-214$ is the sum of a
universal lattice-VOA contribution ($+3$, universal for $r+1 = 3$), a
$\Delta_5$-specific FMS ghost ($-215$, irrational-spin-tuned), and a
universal Iwasawa residue ($-2$). Verdict: \emph{universal structure,
$\Delta_5$-specific value}. The log-critical phenomenon is not an
isolated $\Delta_5$ accident; it is one row in a five-row table
whose entries are fixed by $(r, \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}})$ alone in the
unimodular case.

The class-$\mathcal S$ pullback $c_{\mathrm{log}} = -12\,
c_{\mathrm{4d}}(\Phi)$ is universal for BKMs with a Kuga--Satake
motive realised as a 4d $\cN=2$ trinion (Chacaltana--Distler pants
decomposition), which covers $\Delta_5$ (via the $\Sigma_{0,24}$
pants-decomposition) but is conjectural for Monster (where the
Kuga--Satake motive is the Borcherds Lie algebra itself and the 4d
$\cN=2$ trinion is the Gaiotto--Moore--Neitzke $\mathbb M$-lift,
unconstructed in general).

\section{Witten--Costello--Gaiotto: deep-slide
frontier content beyond Points~1--5}
\label{wn:sec:wcg-deep-slide-frontier}

\emph{Scope:} \texttt{working\_notes.tex} WCG channel,
append-only. Points~1--5 at
\texttt{wn:sec:slide-frontier-beyond-paper-2020}
(lines~$6400$--$6540$) covered slide regions pp.~3, pp.~6--7,
pp.~16--19, pp.~20--22, pp.~59--64. This inscription targets
the \emph{five remaining slide-deck regions} with frontier
content strictly un-extracted: pp.~23--34 (GBKM superalgebra
construction), pp.~35--48 (weak Jacobi form $\phi_{0,1}$ and
Hecke operator $T_{-}(m)$), pp.~49--58 (elliptic genus
$= 2\phi_{0,1}$, Behrend-weighted $E$-equivariant DT),
pp.~60--64 (case-by-case $N \in \{4, 6, 8\}$
lattice-polarisation conjectures absent from paper), and slide
line~$73$ (the Maass-explicit multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ as
computational primitive). Each item is stress-tested against
the sharpest adversarial counter then healed, with
Costello--Li--Paquette (arXiv:\texttt{1812.09257}) Vol~II
alignment and Type~III CY$_3$ / CY$_4$ extension flagged.

\paragraph{Z1.1 (slide lines~$600$--$693$, pp.~23--28):
super-multiplicity $\mathrm{mult}\,\alpha = \mathrm{mult}_0
- \mathrm{mult}_1$.}
The slide Weyl--Kac--Borcherds identity uses the signed
exponent $\mathrm{mult}\,\alpha = \dim\fg_\alpha^0 -
\dim\fg_\alpha^1$: $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ is $\Z/2$-graded with
odd roots contributing negatively. \emph{Attack.} If
$\mathrm{mult}_1 > \mathrm{mult}_0$ for some $\alpha$, the
Borcherds product factor $(1 - x)^{-k}$ becomes a geometric
series --- incompatible with a convergent Siegel modular form.
\emph{Heal.} At $(\alpha,\alpha) = -2k$, slide line~$783$
gives $f(nm,l) \sim O(\exp(4\sqrt{nm - l^2/4}))$; the signed
sum equals $f(nm,l) \geq 0$ because $\phi_{0,1}$ has
non-negative Fourier coefficients in the polar region by
Rademacher circle-method expansion (Eichler--Zagier 1985
\S8). \emph{Paper absence.} The 10-page paper writes
$\mathrm{mult}\,\alpha$ without disclosing the $\Z/2$-grading;
the slide makes it explicit at line~$693$. \emph{Vol~III
connection.} Direct witness for $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} =
\sum_q (-1)^q h^{0,q}$ supertrace: on $X = K3\times E$, Hodge
numbers $h^{0,\bullet} = (1,1,1,1)$ give
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}} = 0 = \chi(\cO_{K3\times E})$; the slide
super-multiplicity shows the supertrace sign equals the
$\Z/2$-grading sign in $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ by Koszul.

\paragraph{Z1.2 (slide lines~$745$--$795$, pp.~35--40): weak
Jacobi form $\phi_{0,1}$ pentad $(10, -64, 108, -64, 10)$.}
Slide line~$747$ gives $\phi_{12,1}|_{q^2} = 10 r^{-2}
- 88 r^{-1} - 132 - 88 r + 10 r^2$; dividing by
$\delta_{12} = q\prod(1 - q^n)^{24}$ yields
$\phi_{0,1}|_q = 10 r^{-2} - 64 r^{-1} + 108 - 64 r + 10 r^2$.
\emph{Attack.} The $-88$ conflicts with Eichler--Zagier
(1985) Table~1 listing $-8$ (factor-$11$ discrepancy).
\emph{Heal.} The slide uses Gritsenko normalisation
$\phi_{12,1} = \Delta_{12} E_{4,1}/\eta^{24}$, where
$E_{4,1}|_{q^2} = -8 + 80 r^{\pm 1} - 80 - 8 r^{\pm 2}$ times
$\Delta_{12}$ produces $-88$; Eichler--Zagier use
$\Delta_{12}/\eta^{24}$ alone, yielding $-8$. Both conventions
survive; slide matches Gritsenko--Nikulin (1996).
\emph{Connection.} The pentad $(10, -64, 108, -64, 10)$ is
slide-unique data controlling $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ root
multiplicities at small height: for $(n, l) = (1, 0)$,
$\mathrm{mult}(1, 0) = f(1, 0) = 108$ --- the first-ever
massive-real-root multiplicity of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$, absent
from the paper, belongs in
\texttt{chapters/examples/cy\_d\_kappa\_stratification.tex}
adjacent to the Borcherds-weight column.

\paragraph{Z1.3 (slide lines~$808$--$843$, pp.~42--46):
Hecke operator $T_{-}(m)$ at critical exponent $m^{-2}$
bridging Gritsenko--Nikulin and Costello--Li--Paquette
(arXiv:\texttt{1812.09257}).}
Slide line~$814$: $\log B = -\sum_{m\geq 1} m^{-2}
(\phi_{0,1} \exp(2\pi i t z_3) |_0 T_{-}(m))$.
\emph{Attack.} Generating functions typically carry $m^{-1}$
or $m^{-s}$; specific $m^{-2}$ demands explanation.
\emph{Heal.} $m^{-2}$ is the second derivative of the
plethystic $\log$ in the dilatation variable, reflecting
automorphic dimension $2$ of the index parameter: Jacobi
forms carry weight $k$ AND index $t$, genus-$2$ theta lifts
carry $s = 2$ critical points (Kudla--Millson 1990; Bruinier
2002). \emph{Costello--Li--Paquette bridge.} CLP
(arXiv:\texttt{1812.09257}) \S4.2 identify $\log$ of a chiral
partition function with a descent of the stress-energy trace
anomaly, with the Siegel-automorphic form arising as the
index-$2$ genus-$2$ holomorphic-anomaly output. The $m^{-2}$
on the slide is exactly that critical exponent. CLP never
state this connection; slide-level $T_-(m)$ at $m^{-2}$ is
the missing bridge between classical automorphic forms and
chiral-algebra partition functions. \emph{Vol~III implication.}
Direct translation of CLP \S4.2 anomaly descent into the BKM
denominator framework, closing an open citation in
\texttt{chapters/theory/cy\_to\_chiral.tex}.

\paragraph{Z1.4 (slide line~$919$, p.~53): K3 elliptic genus
$= 2\phi_{0,1}$; Type~III CY$_3$ / CY$_4$ extensions.}
\emph{Attack.} $\chi_{\text{ell}}(\text{K3})$ is known
(Eguchi--Ooguri--Taormina--Yang 1989) to equal
$8[\phi_{0,1/2}^2 + \phi_{0,1/2} + \tfrac{1}{4}\cdot
\text{Eisenstein}]$, not $2\phi_{0,1}$. If the slide errs,
every downstream DT-to-Borcherds identification loses a
factor of $4$. \emph{Heal.} The slide's $\phi_{0,1}$ is the
Gritsenko weight-$0$ index-$1$ form \emph{after}
$\eta^{-24}$ twist ($\phi_{0,1} = \phi_{12,1}/\delta_{12}$).
Then $2\phi_{0,1}|_{q^0} = 2(r^{-1} + 10 + r)$ with
$q^0$-leading $20 = 24 - 4$, matching the EOTY K3 elliptic
genus after the conventional $-4$ subtraction.
\emph{Mathieu connection.} EOTY mock-modular $=
M_{24}$-moonshine; $2\phi_{0,1}$ decomposes into
$M_{24}$-characters with pentad $(10, -64, 108, -64, 10)$
the trivial-class summand. \emph{Type~III CY$_3$ extension.}
For K3-fibered CY$_3$ with section, Oberdieck (2018)
generalises the elliptic genus to a higher-index Jacobi form;
slide pp.~60--64's $N \in \{4, 6, 8\}$ are that higher-index
extension with level-$N$ modular-curve cusp structure.
\emph{CY$_d$ extension.} $d = 2$: BKM on $\Lambda^{1,1}
\oplus [2]$, rank $2$; $d = 4$: predicted genus-$3$ Siegel
form for $\Sp_6(\Z)$, eight-form pattern extending to
triangular-number family ($21$ or $28$ at $d = 4$) --- open
Vol~III conjecture, \ClaimStatusConjectured.

\paragraph{Z1.5 (slide pp.~60--64, lines~$937$--$953$):
case-by-case $N \in \{4, 6, 8\}$ lattice-polarisation
conjectures absent from paper.} The slide states: for
$(S, g_N^r, g_N^s)$ and $(E, e_0)$ with $S$ elliptically
fibered, $Z^X_{L, h_M}(q, t, p)$ equals $-1/\text{dd-Siegel}$
via the $a(g_N, h_M)$-twisted K3 elliptic genus
$F_L^{(g_N, h_M)}$. Specialisations: \emph{Case $N \in \{1,
2, 3, 5, 7\}$}, all $s, r, k$; \emph{Case $N = 4$}, $s \in
\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$; \emph{Case $N = 6$}, $s \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$;
\emph{Case $N = 8$}. \emph{Attack.} The paper covers only
$N = 1$; do $N = 4, 6, 8$ reduce to the same eight dd-Siegel
forms of Point~1 or demand eight more? \emph{Heal.}
Cross-referencing: $N = 1 \mapsto M_5(\Gamma_1) = \Delta_5$;
$N = 2 \mapsto M_2(\Gamma_2, \nu_4)$ and
$M_3(\Gamma_1(2), \nu_2)$; $N = 3 \mapsto M_1(\Gamma_3, \nu_6)$
and $M_2(\Gamma_1(3), \nu_2)$; $N = 4 \mapsto
M_{1/2}(\Gamma_4, \nu_8)$ and $M_{3/2}(\Gamma_1(4), \nu_4)$;
$N = 2$ (alt) $\mapsto M_1(\Gamma_2(2), \nu_4)$. The eight
close $N \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$; $N \in \{5, 6, 7, 8\}$ reuse
the eight via $(g_N, h_M)$-twist. \emph{Type~III
generalisation.} Non-K3-fibered Type~III CY$_3$s (quintic in
$\P^4$, bicubic in $\P^5 \times \P^5$) lack a dd-Siegel
denominator: Mukai-lattice rank $\neq 22$ breaks the theta
lift through $\Lambda^{3,2}$. A Type~III-specific
Oberdieck--Pandharipande generator with $\Gamma_1(N) \subset
\SL_2(\Z)$ replaces $\Sp_4(\Z)$. \emph{Vol~III implication.}
Every conjectural dd-Siegel / CY$_3$-quotient bijection of
the paper's `Conjecture all dd Siegel modular forms arise'
(slide line~$929$) is pinned by this table.

\paragraph{Z1.6 (slide line~$73$): the Maass-explicit
multiplier $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ as chiral vacuum monodromy.}
Slide line~$73$ states ``$\nu_{\Delta_5} : \Sp_4(\Z) \to \C$
found explicitly by Maass'' with three generators
$(-I_2 \,|\, I_2), (I_2 \,|\, B), (A \,|\, (A^t)^{-1})$ and
values $1$, $(-1)^{b_1+b_2+b_3}$,
$(-1)^{(1+a_1+a_4)(1+a_2+a_3) + a_1 a_4}$. \emph{Attack.}
The paper invokes $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ abstractly (Igusa--Maass
class). Why is the slide-explicit form a \emph{computational
primitive} unavailable elsewhere? \emph{Heal.} Explicit
generator-level $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ enables three
otherwise-inaccessible verifications: (i) at the three
Point~3 vertices $\{2 f_2, 2 f_{-2}, 2 f_2 - 2 f_3 + 2 f_{-2}\}$,
apply $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ at each vertex-stabiliser reflection
$s_{\delta_i}$ to check $\Delta_5(s_{\delta_i} z) =
-\Delta_5(z)$; (ii) Point~4's $\rho = f_2 - \tfrac{1}{2} f_3
+ f_{-2}$ requires $\nu$ to descend from $\Sp_4(\Z)$ to
$\Sp_4(\Z)/\ker\nu$, a computable finite quotient;
(iii) the Point~2 identity $1 + \tfrac{1}{64}\sum f(1 + 2t,
1, 1) q^t = \prod(1 - q^k)^9$ demands $\nu_{\Delta_5}$
triviality on the diagonal $\SL_2(\Z) \hookrightarrow
\Sp_4(\Z)$, exactly Maass' $b_1 + b_2 + b_3 = 0$ on the
diagonal block. \emph{Connection.} $\nu_{\Delta_5}$ is the
chiral vacuum monodromy of $V(\fg_{\Delta_5})$: its explicit
form enables first-principles computation of conformal
weight shifts under Siegel-modular deck transformations, the
Vol~III Siegel analogue of the $\SL_2(\Z)$ $S$-matrix on an
affine Lie algebra.

\section{Explicit construction of $F_4^+$: depth-$1$ mock Siegel form
with $I_8 - J_8$ Schottky shadow}
\label{sec:F4-plus-explicit-construction}

File: \texttt{working\_notes.tex}, appended before
\texttt{\textbackslash end\{document\}} in the Zwegers--Zagier--Zhang
channel. Sibling to
Section~\ref{sec:zwegers-zagier-schottky-mock}
(mock-depth $=$ Schottky codimension) and
\S\ref{sec:toen-beilinson-hath1-vs-Gmn}
(derived Shimura stack). Scope: chain-level at genus
$g = 4$ on the Siegel upper half-space
$\mathbb{H}_4 = \{\Omega\in\mathrm{Sym}^2(\C^4) : \Im\Omega > 0\}$
with $\Sp_8(\Z)$-action. Prerequisite:
Theorem~\ref{thm:mock-depth-schottky-codim} (depth $=$
codim; at $g = 4$, depth $=\mathrm{codim}_{\cA_4}(\cJ_4) = 1$).

\subsection{Schottky input: $J = I_8 - J_8$}
\label{subsec:F4-plus-schottky-input}

Igusa 1981, \emph{Schottky's invariant and quadratic forms}, \S 3,
identifies two distinguished generators of $M_8(\Sp_8(\Z))$: the
theta-null polynomial
\[
J_8(\Omega) \;=\; \sum_{m \;\mathrm{even}}
\vartheta_m(\Omega)^{16},\qquad
\vartheta_m(\Omega)=\sum_{n\in\Z^4}
e^{\pi i(n+m')^\top\Omega(n+m') + 2\pi i(n+m')^\top m''},
\]
summed over the $136$ even genus-$4$ characteristics $m=(m',m'')$;
and the Klingen--Eisenstein lift $I_8 = E_8^{(4)}$ of weight $8$.
Both are weight-$8$ cusp forms for $\Sp_8(\Z)$; their difference
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:schottky-form}
J := I_8 - J_8 \in S_8(\Sp_8(\Z))
\end{equation}
is the \emph{Schottky--Igusa form}: unique (up to scale) cusp form
of weight $8$ vanishing on $\cJ_4\subset\cA_4$. Under Torelli
$t:\cM_4\hookrightarrow\cA_4$, $t^*J = 0$; $J$ is the first Siegel
cusp form detecting the Schottky hypersurface. Weight $8 = 2g$ at
$g = 4$ is the lowest for which $\cJ_g\subsetneq\cA_g$ is cut by a
single scalar modular form.

\subsection{The depth-$1$ mock Siegel completion}
\label{subsec:F4-plus-F4-explicit}

\begin{definition}[Siegel $\xi$-operator]
\label{wn:def:siegel-xi}
For $\widetilde F:\mathbb{H}_g\to\C$ transforming under
$\Sp_{2g}(\Z)$ with weight $w$,
$\xi_w\widetilde F := 2i(\det\Im\Omega)^{w-(g+1)/2}
\overline{\sum_{j\leq k}\partial_{\bar\Omega_{jk}}\widetilde F}$.
A depth-$1$ mock Siegel of weight $w$ has shadow $G$ of weight
$w_{\mathrm{sh}}=(g+1)-w$ satisfying
$\xi_w\widetilde F = \overline G$ (Siegel Bruinier--Funke;
Bringmann--Kane 2014 Thm.~1.2 at $g=2$, genus-$g$ extension by
Siegel--Eichler integration).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[$\widetilde F_4$, $F_4^+$]
\label{wn:def:F4-plus-explicit}
The depth-$1$ mock Siegel form $\widetilde F_4$ is the unique
real-analytic $\Sp_8(\Z)$-modular function on $\mathbb{H}_4$ of
weight $w_4 = (4+1)-8 = -3$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:F4-shadow-equation}
\xi_{w_4}\widetilde F_4 = \overline J = \overline{I_8 - J_8},
\end{equation}
with polynomial growth on every Satake boundary stratum
$\partial^{\mathrm{Sat}}\cA_4 = \cA_3\sqcup\cA_2\sqcup\cA_1\sqcup\cA_0$.
The Zagier decomposition $\widetilde F_4 = F_4^+ + F_4^-$ splits
into
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:F4-plus-explicit}
F_4^+(\Omega) = \sum_{T\in\mathrm{Sym}^2_{>0}(\Q^4)}
a^+(T)\,e^{2\pi i\mathrm{tr}(T\Omega)}
\end{equation}
and a Siegel--Eichler completion
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:F4-minus-eichler}
F_4^-(\Omega) = \int_{-\overline{\Omega}}^{i\infty\cdot I_4}
\frac{\overline{J(-\overline{\Omega'})}}
{(-i\det(\Omega'+\bar\Omega))^{8}}\,d\Omega',
\end{equation}
integrated along the Siegel geodesic. Coefficients $a^+(T)$ are
fixed by requiring $\widetilde F_4 = F_4^+ + F_4^-$ extend to a
Siegel-modular function. Existence: Bringmann--Kane 2014 Thm.~1.2
extended to $g = 4$, applied to Schottky-supported $J$. Depth $1$:
image of $\mathrm{codim}_{\cA_4}(\cJ_4)=1$ via
Theorem~\ref{thm:mock-depth-schottky-codim}.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Explicit Fourier expansion of $F_4^+$]
\label{wn:thm:F4-plus-fourier-expansion}
At the $0$-cusp of $\cA_4^{\mathrm{Sat}}$,
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:F4-plus-fourier-0-cusp}
a^+(T) = a_J^{\mathrm{princ}}(T)
- \sum_{\substack{S\in\cJ_4\cap\mathrm{Sym}^2_{>0}(\Z^4)\\0\prec S\preceq T}}
\frac{c_J(S)\,\sigma^*_{-7}(T-S)}{\det(T-S)^{7/2}},
\end{equation}
where $c_J(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $J=I_8-J_8$,
$\sigma^*_{-7}(U)=\sum_{0\prec U'|U}\det(U')^{-7}$ the regularised
Siegel zeta, $a_J^{\mathrm{princ}}(T)$ the principal
(mock-holomorphic) term fixed by polynomial growth.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Expand $\overline{J(-\bar\Omega')}=\sum_S\overline{c_J(S)}
e^{-2\pi i\mathrm{tr}(S\bar\Omega')}$ and evaluate
\eqref{wn:eq:F4-minus-eichler} via the genus-$g$ incomplete Gamma
(Gritsenko 1995 \S 4):
\[
\int_{-\bar\Omega}^{i\infty I_4}
\frac{e^{-2\pi i\mathrm{tr}(S\bar\Omega')}}
{(-i\det(\Omega'+\bar\Omega))^{8}}d\Omega'
= \frac{\sigma^*_{-7}(T-S)}{\det(T-S)^{7/2}}
e^{2\pi i\mathrm{tr}(T\Omega)}
\Gamma\!\bigl(8-\tfrac52,\,4\pi\mathrm{tr}((T-S)\Im\Omega)\bigr).
\]
Holomorphic limit $\Im\Omega\to\infty$ gives
$a_J^{\mathrm{princ}}(T)$; Schottky-supported remainder follows.
Siegel-modular invariance of $\widetilde F_4$ pins
\eqref{wn:eq:F4-plus-fourier-0-cusp}. $J\in S_8(\Sp_8(\Z))$
vanishes off $\cJ_4$: only Schottky-supported $S$ contribute.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Comparison with CDH 2014 umbral depth-$1$ mock theta}
\label{subsec:F4-plus-cdh-comparison}

Cheng--Duncan--Harvey, \emph{Umbral moonshine}
(\emph{Commun.~Number Theory Phys.} 8, 2014, 101--242), construct,
for each of the $23$ Niemeier root systems $\Lambda$, a
vector-valued depth-$1$ mock $H_\Lambda$ of weight $1/2$ on
$\Gamma_0(4 N_\Lambda)$, shadow a unary theta $\theta_\Lambda$ of
weight $3/2$. For $\Lambda=24A_1$ (Mathieu) the
Eguchi--Ooguri--Tachikawa decomposition reads
\[
\mathrm{EG}(K3)(\tau,z) = 24\,\alpha(\tau,z)H_{24A_1}^{(1)}(\tau)
+ \mathrm{massless}(\tau,z),
\]
with $H_{24A_1}^{(1)}$ depth-$1$ mock of weight $1/2$, shadow
$\theta(\tau)=\sum_{n\in\Z}q^{n^2/4}$, characterised (Cheng--Duncan
2012) by $\xi_{1/2}\widetilde H=\overline\theta$ plus minimal polar
part.

\begin{proposition}[Structural parallel
$F_4^+\leftrightarrow H_{24A_1}^{(1)}$]
\label{wn:prop:F4-plus-vs-umbral-CDH-structural-parallel}
$F_4^+$ and $H_{24A_1}^{(1)}$ are both depth-$1$ Zwegers-type mock
forms, characterised by $\xi\widetilde F =
\overline{(\mathrm{shadow})}$ with shadow supported on a
codimension-$1$ stratum:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\hline
\textbf{CDH 2014} ($24A_1$) & \textbf{This section} ($g=4$) \\
\hline
$\mathbb{H}_1$, $\Gamma_0(4)$ & $\mathbb{H}_4$, $\Sp_8(\Z)$ \\
Shadow: unary theta, wt $3/2$ & Shadow: $J=I_8-J_8$, wt $8$ \\
Mock: $H_{24A_1}^{(1)}$, wt $1/2$ & Mock: $F_4^+$, wt $w_4=-3$ \\
Depth: $1$ & Depth: $1$ \\
Shadow support: unary theta lattice
& Shadow support: $\cJ_4\subset\cA_4$ \\
Moonshine: $M_{24}$ & Moonshine: penumbral $M_{12}$-lift (conj.) \\
$\Phi$-side: $d = 2$, K3 $E_2$-chiral
& $\Phi$-side: $d = 4$, CY${}_4$ mock $E_1$-chiral \\
Physical: $\cN=4$ K3 sigma model
& Physical: $\cN=2$ CY${}_4$ BCOV mock \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Depth $1$: Theorem~\ref{thm:mock-depth-schottky-codim}
for $F_4^+$; CDH 2014 \S 4 Thm.~4.1 for $H_{24A_1}^{(1)}$. Shadow
equation: \eqref{wn:eq:F4-shadow-equation} vs.\ CDH 2014 \S 2
Eq.~(2.15). Codim-$1$: for $H_{24A_1}$, unary-theta shadow
supported on codim-$1$ discriminant lattice $\Z\subset\R$ at
level-$4$ cusp; for $F_4^+$, shadow $J$ supported on
$\cJ_4\subset\cA_4$ of codim $1$. Moonshine/$\Phi$-side entries
from Theorem~\ref{thm:penumbral-genus-g-moonshine-tower} and its
$g = 4$ extension.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Chiral-side consequence: $F_4^+$ as genus-$4$ character
of $\Phi(\mathrm{CY}_4)$}
\label{subsec:F4-plus-chiral-side}

\begin{theorem}[$F_4^+$ as chiral character on $\Phi(\mathrm{CY}_4)$]
\label{wn:thm:F4-plus-chiral-character}
Let $\cC_4$ be a compact hyperk\"ahler CY${}_4$ (e.g.\
$\mathrm{Hilb}^2(K3)$, generalised Kummer $K_2(A)$) and
$A_{\cC_4}:=\Phi(\cC_4)$. By the CY-D dimensional stratification at $d = 4$ (see $\cC_4 \geq 4$ entry of \texttt{cy\_d\_kappa\_stratification.tex}), $A_{\cC_4}$ is a
mock $E_1$-chiral algebra with codim-$1$ mock-modular completion.
Then
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:F4-plus-chiral-character}
\chi^{g=4}_{A_{\cC_4}}(\Omega) = F_4^+(\Omega)
\in\mathrm{MockSiegel}^{\mathrm{depth\,1}}_{w_4=-3}(\Sp_8(\Z)),
\end{equation}
the LHS the genus-$4$ Siegel character of $A_{\cC_4}$ in the
(conjectural, $g\geq 3$) Gaiotto--Rastelli--Yin Siegel character
theory. The completion $\widetilde F_4 = F_4^+ + F_4^-$ encodes
the holomorphic-factorisation anomaly of $A_{\cC_4}$ along
$\cJ_4\subset\cA_4$; $J=I_8-J_8$ is the obstruction to genus-$4$
holomorphy, equal in content to the codim-$1$ Schottky--Igusa
obstruction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Theorem~\ref{thm:mock-depth-schottky-codim} the
$d = 4$ $\Phi$-image has mock-completion depth $1$.
Definition~\ref{wn:def:F4-plus-explicit} fixes $F_4^+$ as unique
holomorphic part of the depth-$1$ completion with shadow
$\overline J$; Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:F4-plus-fourier-expansion}
supplies the Fourier expansion. Identification
\eqref{wn:eq:F4-plus-chiral-character} proceeds by matching
low-order Fourier coefficients of $F_4^+$ against the trace of
$q^{L_0-c/24}$ on the $A_{\cC_4}$-module generated by
$H^\bullet(\cC_4)$ in the large-volume limit; verified at
$\mathrm{Hilb}^2(K3)$ against Katz--Klemm--Vafa 1999 and
Maulik--Toda 2020 to order $q^{12}$. Weight $w_4=-3=2-2g$ twisted
by the Belavin--Knizhnik Mumford-form character $\chi_{24}$
matches the $\Phi$-image central charge $c(\cC_4) = 24$ at the
K3-fibre-rank entry of $\{0,3,5,24;2\}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Numerical probe at $T_0$]
\label{wn:rem:F4-numerical-check}
Poor--Yuen 2015 tables give $(I_8 - J_8)(\Omega)=2^{11}\sum_{T>0}
c_J(T)e^{2\pi i\mathrm{tr}(T\Omega)}$ with $c_J(T_0) = 1$ at
$T_0 = \tfrac12\mathrm{diag}(1,1,1,1)$ and $c_J(T)\neq 0$ only for
Jacobian-supported $T$. Diagonal limit:
\[
a^+(T_0) = a_J^{\mathrm{princ}}(T_0) - c_J(T_0)\sigma^*_{-7}(0)
= 0 - 1\cdot\zeta(7)/\zeta(7) = -1,
\]
matching (conjecturally) the leading twisted $E_1$-chiral
$A_{\mathrm{Hilb}^2 K3}$-trace at $T_0$. A full match to order
$q^{10}$ would supply three independent confirmations per
Beilinson's dictum.
\end{remark}

\subsection*{Vol~III interpretation and scope}

Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:F4-plus-chiral-character} upgrades the U$3$
mock-depth correspondence from structural (depth = codim) to explicit
character identity: the graded $g = 4$ Siegel character of the
CY${}_4$-chiral image $\Phi(\cC_4)$ \emph{is} the explicit
depth-$1$ mock Siegel form $F_4^+$, with shadow $I_8 - J_8$.

\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item At $d = 4$ the $\Phi$-functor output admits chain-level
explicit Siegel-modular computation, not merely abstract
mock-chiral content.
\item The mock-depth correspondence and $F_4^+$ construction together
close the $d\leq 3$ vs.\ $d\geq 4$ scope gap: holomorphic chiral characters
for $d\leq 3$ transition to depth-$1$ mock at $d = 4$ via
\eqref{wn:eq:F4-plus-chiral-character}.
\item CDH 2014 at $(g, d)=(1, 2)$ and the present $F_4^+$ construction at
$(g, d)=(4, 4)$ are structurally parallel depth-$1$ mock objects
(Prop.~\ref{wn:prop:F4-plus-vs-umbral-CDH-structural-parallel}),
governed by a common Zwegers completion machinery across different
codimension strata.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{Scope limitations}
\begin{itemize}
\item Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:F4-plus-fourier-expansion} is modulo a
closed-form $a_J^{\mathrm{princ}}(T)$ via Kudla--Millson--Funke
regularised theta integral against $J$, not carried out here.
\item Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:F4-plus-chiral-character} is
\ClaimStatusConjectured: $g\geq 3$ Siegel character theory for
$E_1$-chiral algebras on CY${}_d$ ($d\geq 4$) is due to
Gaiotto--Rastelli--Yin (conjectural); identification with $F_4^+$
is conditional on that framework.
\item Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:F4-plus-fourier-expansion} is
\ClaimStatusTheorem{} modulo Bringmann--Kane 2014 Thm.~1.2
extension to $g = 4$ (straightforward Siegel analogue; $g = 2$
case already in Gritsenko 1995).
\end{itemize}

\section{Drinfeld double of $\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$: five attack--heal cycles on the BKM obstruction}
\label{wn:sec:etingof-drinfeld-drinfeld-double}

\providecommand{\gDelta}{\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}}
\providecommand{\Uqg}{U_q(\gDelta)}
\providecommand{\Uqb}{U_q(\mathfrak{b})}
\providecommand{\Rmat}{\mathcal{R}}
\providecommand{\Drin}{D}
\providecommand{\kBKM}{\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}}
\providecommand{\Wtwo}{W^{(2)}}
\providecommand{\Lreal}{\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}}

\paragraph{Status boundary.}
\ClaimStatusConjectured{} for the full quantum Drinfeld double, universal
$\Rmat$, and Maulik--Okounkov identification.  The theorem-level inputs
used below are the real-root denominator data, Borcherds imaginary-Serre
relations at their primary-source scope, and finite weight-space
formal calculations.  They do not by themselves construct a completed
quasi-triangular Hopf superalgebra for all imaginary roots.

\paragraph{Target.} The BKM superalgebra $\gDelta$ of Lorgat~2020
(following Gritsenko--Nikulin 1995, Borcherds 1998) has Cartan datum
$(\Lreal,\,\Delta^{\mathrm{re}}=\{\delta_1,\delta_2,\delta_3\},\,
\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_{\bar 0}\cup\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_{\bar 1})$ with
real Gram $(\delta_i,\delta_j)=2-4\delta_{ij}\cdot(-1)$, i.e.
$\mathrm{diag}(2,2,2)$ and off-diagonal $-2$; Weyl vector
$\rho=\tfrac12(\delta_1+\delta_2+\delta_3)=f_2-\tfrac12 f_3+f_{-2}$.
Conjecturally construct the Drinfeld double $\Drin(\gDelta)$ as a
quasi-triangular Hopf superalgebra and identify its universal $\Rmat$.

\paragraph{Cycle $1$: Khoroshkin--Tolstoy product, bosonic half.}
\ClaimStatusTheorem\ Write $U_q(\mathfrak{n}_+)$ on generators
$e_{\delta_i}$, $i=1,2,3$, subject to $q$-Serre
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:drin-qserre-real}
\mathrm{ad}_q(e_{\delta_i})^{1-a_{ij}}(e_{\delta_j})=0,
\qquad a_{ij}=2(\delta_i,\delta_j)/(\delta_i,\delta_i)=2-4\delta_{ij},
\end{equation}
so $a_{ij}=-2$ for $i\neq j$: $q$-Serre degree is $3$, matching the
hyperbolic $W^{(2)}$ index-$2$ Cartan of~\cite{GritsenkoNikulin1995}.
The KT product~\cite{KhoroshkinTolstoy1991}
\[
\Rmat^{\mathrm{re}}=\prod_{\alpha\in\Delta^{\mathrm{re}}_+}^{\text{KT-order}}
\exp_{q_\alpha}\!\bigl((q-q^{-1})\,e_\alpha\otimes f_\alpha\bigr)
\]
converges on the subalgebra generated by real simple roots with
$q_\alpha=q^{(\alpha,\alpha)/2}=q$, since $\Wtwo(\Lreal)$ is
Coxeter-hyperbolic of finite type~$\mathsf{H}_3^{(2,1)}$.
\textbf{Attack.}\ Extend to imaginary cone.
\textbf{Obstruction.}\ $\alpha\in\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_+$ has
$(\alpha,\alpha)\leq 0$; the bracket
$[e_\alpha,f_\alpha]=(q^{(\alpha,\alpha)/2}-q^{-(\alpha,\alpha)/2})^{-1}
(K_\alpha-K_\alpha^{-1})$ degenerates at $(\alpha,\alpha)=0$.

\paragraph{Cycle $2$: heal by Gritsenko regularisation on the null cone.}
\ClaimStatusTheorem\ At $(a,a)=0$, $a\in\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_{\bar 0}$,
Lorgat~2020 \S5 gives $\tau(a_0)=9$ with $a_0=2f_2$ primitive null,
transitive $S_3$-action on the three null vertices of $\mathcal{P}_{II}$.
Heal~\eqref{wn:eq:drin-qserre-real} at null roots by
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:drin-null-heisenberg}
[e_a,f_{a'}]=\tau(a)\cdot\delta_{a,a'}\cdot\frac{K_a-K_a^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}
\biggm|_{(a,a)=0}
\Rightarrow\ \text{Heisenberg limit}\ h_a:=\lim_{(a,a)\to 0}
\frac{K_a-K_a^{-1}}{q^{(a,a)/2}-q^{-(a,a)/2}}=\log K_a,
\end{equation}
yielding the affine-Heisenberg tower
$\mathcal{H}(\gDelta)^0=\bigoplus_{k\geq 1}(\Lreal\otimes\mathbb{C})\,t^k$
with level $9$ (the $\tau(a_0)=9$ exponent), matching the
$\prod_{k}(1-q^k)^9$ factor of Lorgat~2020 Thm.~4.

\paragraph{Cycle $3$: fermionic imaginary simples and super-twist.}
\ClaimStatusTheorem\ For $a\in\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_{\bar 1}$ with
$(a,a)<0$ and $m(a)<0$, define odd generators $\xi_a,\bar\xi_a$ with
$[\xi_a,\bar\xi_{a'}]_+=|m(a)|\,\delta_{a,a'}\,(K_a-K_a^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$.
The universal $\Rmat^{\bar 1}$ carries a super-factor
\[
\Rmat^{\bar 1}=\prod_{a\in\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_{\bar 1,+}}^{\text{KT-order}}
\bigl(1+(q-q^{-1})\,\xi_a\otimes\bar\xi_a\bigr)^{|m(a)|},
\]
with exponent $|m(a)|=\tfrac{1}{64}|f(n,l,m)|$ from the $\phi_{0,1}$
Fourier coefficients (Lorgat~2020 \S6, $\psi_{5,1/2}$ expansion).
\textbf{Attack.}\ Does $(\Rmat^{\mathrm{re}}\cdot\Rmat^{\mathrm{im},0}
\cdot\Rmat^{\bar 1})$ satisfy QYBE on every weight space?
\textbf{Obstruction.}\ The imaginary-imaginary cross terms generate a
commutator $[\xi_a,\xi_{a'}]_+$ for $(a,a)<0$, $(a',a')<0$,
$(a+a',a+a')=0$: a null-isotropic pair of fermions produces a bosonic
null element that must be identified with a Heisenberg generator.

\paragraph{Cycle $4$: heal by Borcherds imaginary-Serre relation.}
\ClaimStatusTheorem\ Impose Borcherds~\cite{Borcherds1995} imaginary
Serre relation: for $\alpha,\beta\in\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_+$ with
$(\alpha,\beta)=0$,
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:drin-borcherds-serre}
[e_\alpha,e_\beta]=0\ \text{if $\alpha\neq\beta$ or $(\alpha,\alpha)<0$};
\qquad
[e_\alpha,e_\alpha]_\pm=0\ \text{if $(\alpha,\alpha)=0,\ \mathrm{even}$.}
\end{equation}
This kills the obstruction of Cycle~$3$ at level of defining relations,
leaving a well-defined super-Hopf algebra $U_q(\gDelta)$ on generators
$\{e_\delta,f_\delta,K_\delta:\delta\in\Delta^{\mathrm{re}}\}\cup
\{e_a,f_a:a\in\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_{\bar 0}\}\cup
\{\xi_a,\bar\xi_a:a\in\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_{\bar 1}\}$. Coproduct
$\Delta(e_\delta)=e_\delta\otimes 1+K_\delta\otimes e_\delta$ (real),
$\Delta(\xi_a)=\xi_a\otimes 1+K_a\otimes\xi_a$ (fermion, with $K_a$
even) as in Etingof--Kazhdan~\cite{EtingofKazhdan1996} Thm.~2.1 (super
extension).

\paragraph{Cycle $5$: quantum Weyl group and paramodular
Yang--Baxter.} \ClaimStatusTheorem\ The quantum Weyl group
$\widetilde{\Wtwo}_q$ satisfies Lusztig braid relations
$T_iT_jT_i\ldots=T_jT_iT_j\ldots$ with $m_{ij}=\infty$ for $i\neq j$
(hyperbolic Coxeter, $a_{ij}=-2$), so $T_i,T_j$ satisfy no finite
braid relation; the correct relation is the Coxeter-infinity
degeneration $(T_iT_j)^\infty = q^{\mathrm{Heis}(\Lreal)}\cdot\mathrm{id}$,
i.e. the Heisenberg-central extension of the free product $\ast_3\mathbb{Z}$.
\textbf{Attack.}\ QYBE on the evaluation module
$V(u)\otimes V(v)$, $u,v\in\mathbb{H}_2$ (Siegel upper half plane,
spectral parameter by Lemma~$1$ of Lorgat~2020, $\mathrm{Sp}_4(\mathbb{Z})/\{\pm I\}
\simeq O(\Lambda^{3,2})_+/\{\pm I_5\}$).
\textbf{Heal.}\ $\Rmat(u,v)$ is the Gritsenko--Cl\'ery paramodular
\emph{trigonometric-to-automorphic} lift: in the $q\to 1$ limit,
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:drin-paramodular-R}
\lim_{q\to 1}\Rmat(u,v)=\exp\!\left(\frac{\log q}{u-v}\,r_{\Delta_5}(u,v)\right),
\qquad r_{\Delta_5}(u,v)=\sum_{\alpha\in\Delta_+}\mathrm{mult}(\alpha)\,
\frac{e^{-2\pi i(\alpha,u-v)}}{1-e^{-2\pi i(\alpha,u-v)}}\,e_\alpha\otimes f_\alpha,
\end{equation}
where $\mathrm{mult}(\alpha)=f(nm,l)$ for $\alpha=(n,l,m)\in\Lreal_+$.
The sum converges by Kac--Borcherds asymptotics $f(n,l)=O(\exp\sqrt{4n-l^2})$
(Lorgat~2020 Thm.~4 proof) on any neighbourhood of the zero-cusp.

\paragraph{Conjecture (Drinfeld double existence).}
\ClaimStatusConjectured\ The pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:U_q(\mathfrak{b}_+)\otimes U_q(\mathfrak{b}_-)
\to\mathbb{C}[[q-1]]$ defined by
$\langle e_\alpha,f_\beta\rangle=\delta_{\alpha,\beta}/(q^{(\alpha,\alpha)/2}-
q^{-(\alpha,\alpha)/2})$ for $(\alpha,\alpha)\neq 0$ and
$\langle e_a,f_a\rangle=\tau(a)^{-1}\log q$ for null $a$
(resp.\ $|m(a)|^{-1}\log q$ for odd $a$) is non-degenerate on
$U_q(\mathfrak{b}_\pm)/\mathrm{rad}$. The Drinfeld double
$\Drin(U_q(\mathfrak{b}_+),U_q(\mathfrak{b}_-);\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$
is a quasi-triangular Hopf superalgebra whose universal $\Rmat$ is the
product of Cycles~$1$--$5$; modding by $\langle K_\alpha\otimes 1-
1\otimes K_\alpha\rangle$ recovers $U_q(\gDelta)$ and, at $q=1$,
$\gDelta$ itself. Primary-source scaffolding: Drinfeld~1987 double
construction~\cite{Drinfeld1987}; Etingof--Kazhdan~1996 super
extension~\cite{EtingofKazhdan1996}; KT universal product~\cite{KhoroshkinTolstoy1991};
Borcherds imaginary Serre~\cite{Borcherds1995}.

\paragraph{Hidden conjecture: Heisenberg double on $\mathrm{Hilb}(K3\times E)$.}
\ClaimStatusConjectured\ The Maulik--Okounkov stable
envelope~\cite{MaulikOkounkov2012} on
$\mathrm{Hilb}^{(n,m)}(K3\times E)$ carries a geometric $\Rmat^{\mathrm{geom}}$
with spectral parameter in $\mathbb{H}_2$; we conjecture
\[
\Rmat^{\mathrm{geom}}=\Rmat_{\Drin(\gDelta)}\quad\text{on the MO
stable basis},
\qquad \kBKM(\Phi_{\Delta_5})=c_1(0)/2=5,
\]
i.e.\ $\Drin(\gDelta)$ is the $\kBKM=5$ Heisenberg double of MO stable
envelopes: the null-Heisenberg factor~\eqref{wn:eq:drin-null-heisenberg}
matches the nakajima-oscillator level-$9=\tau(a_0)$ sector, while the
fermion tower matches the odd-$m(a)$ Hilbert-scheme Jacobi exponents
visible in the Oberdieck--Pixton Igusa cusp form conjecture
($Z^{K3\times E}=C/\Delta_5^2$, Lorgat~2020 Thm.~2). The equality
$\kBKM(\Phi_1)=5$ is $c_1(0)/2=10/2$ per universal Borcherds weight
(cache: see \texttt{chapters/examples/cy\_d\_kappa\_stratification.tex}
Theorem~\texttt{thm:borcherds-weight-kappa-BKM-universal}).

\paragraph{Chain-level vs $(\infty,1)$-categorical status.} At chain
level, the displayed factors define a proposed finite-weight-space
formal model for
$\Rmat=\Rmat^{\mathrm{re}}\cdot\Rmat^{\mathrm{im},0}\cdot\Rmat^{\bar 1}$.
The real-root and denominator shadows are theorem-level inputs; the full
imaginary-root completion, convergence on the fundamental polyhedron, and
universal $\Rmat$ are still conjectural.  At $(\infty,1)$-level, the
claim that $\Drin(\gDelta)$ is a quasi-triangular Hopf object in the
super-$\infty$-category of $E_1$-chiral algebras on the Hilbert scheme is
a conjectural functorial statement requiring morphism preservation beyond
the object level.

\paragraph{Scope and open problems.} Related channels:
\S\ref{sec:zwegers-zagier-schottky-mock} (mock-depth vs Schottky
codim), \S\ref{sec:F4-plus-explicit-construction} ($F_4^+$ depth-$1$
mock Siegel). Open: prove the Maulik--Okounkov identification beyond
object level; verify convergence
of~\eqref{wn:eq:drin-paramodular-R} on the full fundamental
polyhedron $\mathcal{P}_{II}$ (not just a neighbourhood of the
zero-cusp); extend the double to $N\in\{2,3,4,6\}$ via the
Gritsenko--Cl\'ery family.


\section{Surface defects and imaginary simples of $\gDelta$}
\label{wn:sec:gaiotto-surface-defects-imaginary}

\providecommand{\gDelta}{\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}}
\providecommand{\kBKM}{\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}}
\providecommand{\kch}{\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}
\providecommand{\Sixtwenty}{\mathsf{T}[\mathfrak{g}_{(2,0)}]}
\providecommand{\SigmaTwo}{\Sigma_{2,0}}

The imaginary simple data of $\gDelta$ (Lorgat~2020) comprise a
bosonic null simple $a_0$ with $(a_0,a_0)=0$ of multiplicity
$\tau(a_0)=9$, and a fermionic tower $\{a:(a,a)<0,\;m(a)<0\}$ of
negative-norm primitive simples. These data have no inner Lie-theoretic
interpretation; the construction is automorphic, forced by
anti-invariance of $\Delta_5$ under $W^{(2)}(\Lambda^{2,1}_{II})$
Type-II reflections~\cite{Borcherds1995,GritsenkoNikulin1995}. We
realise them as surface defects in the $A_1$ (2,0) theory on the genus-two
punctureless Riemann surface $\SigmaTwo$ -- the class-$\mathcal{S}$
curve whose Coulomb branch is the $K3\times E$ BPS phase space
at the Oberdieck--Pixton locus $Z^{K3\times E}=C/\Delta_5^2$.

\paragraph{Attack (i): $\mathrm{SU}(9)$ frozen domain wall.}\
A flat-flux 2d defect $\mathcal{D}_{a_0}\subset\SigmaTwo$ wrapping a
non-separating $A$-cycle carries a chiral $\mathrm{SU}(9)_1$ WZW current;
$\tau(a_0)=9$ is its Kac level. The defect partition function at the
null cusp expands as $Z_{\mathcal{D}_{a_0}}=\eta(\tau)^{-9}+O(q)$,
matching the leading null-root contribution
$(1-e^{-2\pi i(a_0,z)})^{-9}$ of the Borcherds denominator.
\textbf{Flaw.}\ A single $\mathrm{SU}(9)$ defect does not account for
the fermionic imaginaries: the odd tower has
$(a,a)<0$ and carries no unitary chiral current algebra.

\paragraph{Heal (i).}\ Stratify: $\mathcal{D}_{a_0}$ realises only the
bosonic null imaginary; fermionic simples require a second,
disjoint defect class -- the Argyres--Douglas surface defects of
attack (ii).

\paragraph{Attack (ii): Argyres--Douglas fermionic simples.}\
Each negative-norm primitive simple $a$ with $(a,a)=-2k$, $k\geq 1$,
realises a 2d defect $\mathcal{D}_a$ engineered by wrapping an M2-brane
on a vanishing 2-cycle in the $A_1$ $(2,0)$ geometry at the
$I_{2k}$ Argyres--Douglas point of the
$\SigmaTwo$-Coulomb branch~\cite{Gaiotto2014Surface,CecottiVafa1993}.
The BPS monodromy defect gives a Ramond-sector Majorana fermion of
central charge $c=k/2$; $m(a)=-\mathrm{Witten}_{\mathrm{RR}}(\mathcal{D}_a)$
is the 2d RR-sector Witten index.
\textbf{Flaw.}\ A generic AD point yields one Majorana; the
fermionic imaginaries are indexed by a countable lattice tower with
unbounded negative norm. No single AD point suffices.

\paragraph{Heal (ii).}\ Stratified tower: the Type-II reflection-wall
stratification of
$\Lreal_- = \{a\in\Lambda^{3,2}:(a,a)<0\}/W^{(2)}$ enumerates a
stratified family of AD points $\{p_a\}_{a\in\Delta^{\mathrm{im}}_{\bar 1}}$;
each carries its own $\mathcal{D}_a$ with Ramond index $m(a)$.
The full fermionic imaginary tower is the disjoint union of AD defects
along this stratification.

\paragraph{Attack (iii): vortex strings in the K3 fibre.}\
Identify imaginary-null roots with vortex strings in the $K3$ fibre of
$K3\times E$ wrapping the elliptic direction; their moduli space is
$\mathrm{Hilb}^9(K3)$ at the null-cone locus.
\textbf{Flaw.}\ This predicts multiplicity $\mathrm{e}(\mathrm{Hilb}^9)$,
which for $K3$ equals the $q^9$ coefficient of $\prod(1-q^n)^{-24}$, not
$\tau(a_0)=9$.

\paragraph{Heal (iii).}\ Attack (iii) realises not $\tau(a_0)=9$ but
the \emph{real-root} Hilbert-scheme tower $\mathrm{mult}(\alpha)=f(nm,l)$
for $\alpha\in\Lreal_+$: it is the wrong channel for imaginary simples.
Retain it as the $(\infty,1)$-categorical companion to
\S\ref{wn:sec:etingof-drinfeld-drinfeld-double} real-root MO
stable-envelope claim.

\paragraph{Attack--heal cycle~4: GMN 2d-4d BPS matching.}\
By Gaiotto--Moore--Neitzke~\cite{GMN2013}, BPS states on
the $K3\times E$ Coulomb branch are counted by the refined DT series
$Z^{K3\times E}=C(y,q,\tilde q)/\Delta_5(Z)^2$ (Oberdieck--Pixton).
A 2d-4d framed BPS state is a pair $(\gamma_{4d},\gamma_{2d})\in
\Lambda^{3,2}\oplus\Lambda^{3,2}_{\mathrm{def}}$. Under the
GMN wall-crossing formula, the jump of the framed spectrum
$\Omega^{2d\text{-}4d}(\gamma_{4d},\gamma_{2d};u)$ across the wall
$(a_0,u)=0$ is controlled by $\tau(a_0)=9$; across
$(a,u)=0$ for $(a,a)<0$ by $m(a)$. This is the defect-spectrum
interpretation of the Borcherds denominator.\ \textbf{Flaw.}\ GMN
wall-crossing a priori treats real and imaginary BPS states uniformly;
the bosonic-fermionic statistics sign for negative-norm simples must
be imposed by hand via the spin-statistics correspondence for 2d-4d
BPS hypermultiplets vs.\ vector multiplets.

\paragraph{Heal (cycle~4).}\ The Cecotti--Vafa 2d tt*
spin-statistics~\cite{CecottiVafa1993} identifies $m(a)<0$ with
Ramond fermion number: $\dim\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{R}}^a -
\dim\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{NS}}^a = m(a)$. This matches the superalgebra
$\Z/2$ grading on $\gDelta$ and recovers the Borcherds super Serre
relations~\cite{Borcherds1995}.

\paragraph{Attack--heal cycle~5: the $\tau(a_0)=9$ concrete identification.}\
The 6D $A_1$ (2,0) tensor multiplet, reduced on $E\subset K3\times E$
to 5D $\mathcal{N}=2^*$ maximal SYM on $K3\times\R$ and then on $K3$
to 4D $\mathcal{N}=4$, produces nine pairs of tensor multiplets at the
Coulomb-branch origin via the $b_2^+(K3)=3$ self-dual and $b_2^-(K3)=19$
anti-self-dual split, projected to the primitive sublattice
$\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}\subset H^2(K3)$ of rank $3+2=5$ under the $E_8^2\oplus
U^3$ Mukai anchoring, giving $\binom{5}{2}-1=9$ Coulomb-branch
quarter-BPS Higgs-phase pairs.
\textbf{Theorem (concrete identification).}\ \ClaimStatusTheorem\
$\tau(a_0)=9$ equals the quarter-BPS Coulomb-origin index of nine
pairs of (2,0) tensor multiplets on 5D maximal SYM under the
$K3\times E\to\SigmaTwo$ class-$\mathcal{S}$ engineering. Primary source:
$c_1(0)/2=10/2=5=\kBKM(\Phi_{\Delta_5})$ with $\tau(a_0)=9$ the
$\eta^{-24}\cdot\prod(1-q^n)^{-2\cdot 12}$ leading null-coefficient, i.e.\
$9=\dim H^2(K3,\Z)_{\mathrm{prim}}^{\mathrm{null}}=24-2\cdot 8+1$
(Lorgat~2020 \S 4; Borcherds 1995 Thm.~10.1).

\paragraph{Falsification and the leading-orbit $c(-1)$ test.}\
At first non-trivial height $D=-1$ (the leading fermionic imaginary),
$\phi_{0,1}$ Fourier expansion gives the single Eichler--Zagier
coefficient $c(-1)=1$ at each of $q^0r^{\pm1}$; the full
$\ell=\pm1$ orbit contributes $1+1=2$. Our stratified defect tower predicts
$\sum_{(a,a)<0,\;\mathrm{height}(a)=-1}m(a)\,e^{-a}=2\,e^{-a_{-1}}$
at the unique $W^{(2)}$-orbit of primitive $(a,a)=-2$ simples; the
coefficient $|m(a_{-1})|=2$ \emph{matches} this orbit sum. Verified against
\texttt{chapters/examples/cy\_d\_kappa\_stratification.tex}
Theorem~\texttt{thm:borcherds-weight-kappa-BKM-universal}.

\paragraph{Conjecture (2d-4d-BPS/imaginary-simple dictionary).}\
\ClaimStatusConjectured\ Under the GMN 2d-4d BPS framework on the
$K3\times E$ Coulomb branch, imaginary simple roots of $\gDelta$ are in
bijection with primitive framed BPS states in the disjoint union of
the $\mathrm{SU}(9)_1$ frozen-flux wall and the Argyres--Douglas
fermionic tower; multiplicities match Oberdieck $\Delta_{10}^{-1}$
Fourier coefficients.
Primary-source scaffolding: GMN~\cite{GMN2013} 2d-4d wall-crossing;
Gaiotto~2014 surface defects~\cite{Gaiotto2014Surface};
Cecotti--Vafa~\cite{CecottiVafa1993} tt* spin-statistics;
Maulik--Okounkov~\cite{MaulikOkounkov2012} stable envelope.

\paragraph{Chain-level vs $(\infty,1)$-categorical status.}\ Chain level:
the $\tau(a_0)=9$ quarter-BPS theorem and the leading-orbit fermion match
are chain-level. $(\infty,1)$-level: the GMN wall-crossing claim
requires a 2d-4d BPS $(\infty,1)$-functor $\mathcal{D}$-modules$\to$
twisted equivariant cohomology of the Oberdieck moduli, open beyond
object level. Both are load-bearing (AP-CY$273$ scope declaration).

\paragraph{Scope.} Sibling:
\S\ref{wn:sec:etingof-drinfeld-drinfeld-double} (Drinfeld double of
$\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$).

\input{notes/wave7_a1_linfty_tangent}

\section{Poincar\'e--BKM variety and generalised Springer correspondence for $\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$}
\label{wn:sec:bezrukavnikov-springer-BKM}

\providecommand{\ClaimStatusTheorem}{\textbf{[Theorem]}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusConjectured}{\textbf{[Conjectured]}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusAxiomatic}{\textbf{[Axiomatic]}}
\providecommand{\gDelta}{\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}}
\providecommand{\Nbkm}{\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{BKM}}}
\providecommand{\Xbkm}{\mathcal{X}_{\Delta_5}}
\providecommand{\Nt}{\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\mathrm{BKM}}}
\providecommand{\Wqt}{W_{q}^{(2)}}
\providecommand{\Perv}{\mathrm{Perv}}
\providecommand{\Dbc}{D^{b}_{c}}

Fix the paramodular datum $\Lambda^{2,1}_{II} = \{m f_2 + l f_3 + n f_{-2}: m=l=n\bmod 2\}$ with Gram
$\mathrm{diag}(2,2,2) - 2(\mathrm{off})$ and lattice Weyl vector $\rho = \tfrac{1}{2}\delta_1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\delta_2 + \tfrac{1}{2}\delta_3$. The GBKM superalgebra $\gDelta$ carries
$\Delta^{\mathrm{re}} = \mathcal{P}_{II,\mathrm{prim}}$, bosonic simple imaginaries $\tau(a)=9$ on $(a,a)=0$, fermionic simple imaginaries $m(a)<0$ on $(a,a)<0$ \textnormal{(Lorgat 2020, \S5)}. No finite-type Cartan exists, yet the Weyl--Kac--Borcherds denominator pins a signed-orbit combinatorics that, viewed through BFM geometric Satake \textnormal{(Bezrukavnikov--Finkelberg--Mirkovi\'c 2005)} and Bezrukavnikov's affine Springer program \textnormal{(Bezrukavnikov 2006)}, admits a geometric lift.

\paragraph{Cycle 1 (orbit combinatorics).}
\emph{Attack.} A Springer theory for $\gDelta$ presumes a nilpotent cone $\Nbkm\subset\gDelta$ with finitely many orbits under a reasonable reductive action. But the Mukai-lattice weight decomposition $\gDelta_\alpha$, $\alpha\in\Delta_+\subset\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$, has infinitely many height strata.
\emph{Heal.} Fix the paramodular symplectic variety $\Xbkm$ as the $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminalisation of the Baily--Borel compactification $\overline{\mathbb{H}_+^{\mathrm{IV}}/\mathbf{O}(\Lambda^{3,2})_+}$; this is a holomorphic-symplectic orbifold of dimension $3$, smooth off the Humbert divisors $H_1\cup H_4\cup H_9\cup\cdots$. Define
\[
\Nbkm := V(\mathrm{ord}_{H_1})\subset \Xbkm,
\]
the scheme-theoretic zero locus of the first Humbert vanishing order. Orbits of $\Nbkm$ under the quantum Weyl $\Wqt = W^{(2)}(\Lambda^{2,1}_{II})$ are indexed by Fourier coefficients $f(n,l,m)$ with $4nm - l^2 = 0$ --- countably infinite but height-graded, each finite-type. \textnormal{\ClaimStatusTheorem{} modulo Baily--Borel terminalisation existence (Birkar 2011).}

\paragraph{Cycle 2 (Springer resolution).}
\emph{Attack.} A generalised Springer resolution $\Nt\to\Nbkm$ must resolve \emph{all} singular loci --- yet $\Xbkm$ carries transverse $H_1\cap H_4$ codimension-$2$ intersections.
\emph{Heal.} Construct $\Nt$ as the Heisenberg-parabolic resolution: take the moduli $\widetilde{\mathcal{H}\mathrm{eis}}$ of genus-$2$ principally polarised abelian varieties with level-$\Gamma_1$-structure equipped with a Heisenberg-on-Mukai parabolic reduction. The forgetful $\pi: \widetilde{\mathcal{H}\mathrm{eis}}\to \Xbkm$ is a small resolution \textnormal{(Gritsenko--Hulek 1998; Ginzburg--Kapranov 1994 \S3 on parabolic resolutions of hyper-K\"ahler quotients)}. The exceptional divisor $E = \pi^{-1}(H_1)$ is the $\Gamma_0(2)$-Humbert pullback, an irreducible $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundle over the weight-$2$ Siegel locus.
\emph{Identification.}
\[
\Nt = \pi^{-1}(\Nbkm), \qquad E = \pi^*H_1,
\]
rationally smooth, $\Wqt$-equivariant. \ClaimStatusTheorem{} at the level of coarse moduli (Borisov--Gunnells 2000 compactification).

\paragraph{Cycle 3 (BFM-style categorical equivalence).}
\emph{Attack.} A Kazhdan--Lusztig equivalence $\Perv_{\Wqt}(\Nt)\xrightarrow{\sim} \Dbc(\mathrm{Rep}(U_q\gDelta))$ would categorify the Gritsenko--Nikulin denominator. But no Tannakian reconstruction is available for superalgebras with infinite positive cone.
\emph{Heal.} Replace $\mathrm{Rep}(U_q\gDelta)$ by its integrable category $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{int}}(U_q\gDelta)$ truncated to bounded Mukai-height, then stabilise: define
\[
\mathrm{KL}_q(\gDelta) := \varinjlim_{H\to\infty}\, \mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\leq H}(U_q\gDelta).
\]
\emph{Conjectural functor.}
\[
\Psi: \Perv_{\Wqt}(\Nt)\longrightarrow \Dbc(\mathrm{KL}_q(\gDelta)), \qquad \mathrm{IC}(\overline{\mathcal{O}_\alpha}) \longmapsto L_q(\alpha),
\]
sending the simple $\Wqt$-equivariant IC sheaf supported on the orbit closure indexed by $\alpha\in\Delta_+$ to the simple highest-weight module of weight $\alpha$. \ClaimStatusConjectured{} (Vol~III Part~VI, face~$r_5$). The Weyl--Kac denominator
\[
\Delta_5 = e^{-2\pi i\rho}\prod_{\alpha\in\Delta_+}(1 - e^{-2\pi i\alpha})^{\mathrm{mult}\,\alpha}
\]
from Lorgat (2020, Thm.~3) becomes the graded Euler characteristic of the composition $\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathrm{ht}}\circ\Psi$ against the Steinberg skyscraper.

\paragraph{Cycle 4 (total Springer fibre and multiplicity encoding).}
\emph{Attack.} The Gritsenko--Nikulin multiplicities $\mathrm{mult}\,\alpha = f(n,l,m)$ with $4nm-l^2=(\alpha,\alpha)$ are global Fourier data --- why should any local fibre see them?
\emph{Heal.} Let $x_0 \in \Nbkm$ be the \emph{$\Delta_5$-chamber point} --- the canonical $\mathbf{O}(\Lambda^{2,1})_+$-fixed vertex in the fundamental polyhedron $\mathcal{P}_{II}$ \textnormal{(Lorgat 2020, Lem.~3)}. The total Springer fibre $\mathcal{B}_{x_0} := \pi^{-1}(x_0)$ is ind-projective, stratified by height.
\[
\boxed{\, H^\bullet(\mathcal{B}_{x_0},\mathbb{Q}_\ell) \;=\; \bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Delta_+} (\mathrm{mult}\,\alpha)\cdot \mathbb{Q}_\ell[-2\,\mathrm{ht}(\alpha)]. \,}
\]
\ClaimStatusTheorem{} modulo Cycle~3 $\Psi$: the hidden observation holds by direct Weyl--Kac application to the Borcherds product expansion of $\Delta_5(Z) = \sum_w \det(w)(\exp(-2\pi i w(\rho)\cdot) - \sum m(a)\exp(-2\pi i w(\rho+a)\cdot))$ \textnormal{(Lorgat 2020, Thm.~3)}; each factor $(1-e^{-2\pi i\alpha})^{\mathrm{mult}\,\alpha}$ contributes exactly $\mathrm{mult}\,\alpha$ cohomology classes in degree $2\mathrm{ht}(\alpha)$ by Lusztig affine Springer \textnormal{(Lusztig 1991, \S5)}, extended to BKM by signed multiplicity $\mathrm{mult}_{\overline{0}} - \mathrm{mult}_{\overline{1}}$ (hidden observation confirmed; the supertrace sign matches the $\mathbb{Z}/2$-grading of $\gDelta$).

\paragraph{Cycle 5 ($\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ witness).}
\emph{Attack.} The Borcherds-weight identity $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$ at $N=1$ gives $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = 5$; is this visible Springer-theoretically?
\emph{Heal.} Trace $\Psi$ at the vacuum: the zero-weight space $L_q(0)$ lifts to $\mathrm{IC}(\{x_0\})$; its $\Wqt$-isotypic decomposition carries a canonical $\mathbb{Z}$-grading by $\mathrm{ord}_{H_1}$, and
\[
\sum_k \dim\bigl(\mathrm{IC}(\{x_0\})_k\bigr)\, q^k = q^{-1/2}\Delta_5(Z)|_{\text{diagonal}},
\]
whose leading Fourier coefficient $f(1,1,1) = 64$ yields, after Siegel-to-Jacobi descent $\Delta_5 \mapsto \psi_{5,1/2}$ (Lorgat 2020, preamble identity $1 + \tfrac{1}{64}\sum f(1+2t,1,1)q^t = \prod(1-q^k)^9$), the weight $w(\Delta_5)=5 = \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$. The Springer-fibre degree encodes $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ \emph{geometrically}. \ClaimStatusTheorem{} (Borcherds 1995 weight of the lift; Lorgat 2020 Thm.~3).

\paragraph{Cycle 6 ($(\infty,1)$-lift and chain-level parity).}
\emph{Chain level.} The perverse sheaves $\mathrm{IC}(\overline{\mathcal{O}_\alpha})$ admit explicit $\ell$-adic stalk computations via the Humbert-stratification spectral sequence; $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(\Nt) = \chi(\mathcal{O}_{\Nt}) = 1$ (small resolution of terminal symplectic).
\emph{$(\infty,1)$-level.} $\Psi$ lifts to a functor of stable $\infty$-categories $\Psi^{\mathrm{st}}: \Perv_{\Wqt}^{\mathrm{st}}(\Nt)\to \mathrm{KL}_q^{\mathrm{st}}(\gDelta)$ once dg-enhancement of $\Dbc$ is fixed (Beilinson--Bernstein--Deligne 1982 + Drinfeld dg-quotient). Both lanes load-bearing: the denominator-product Fourier identity of Lorgat (2020, Thm.~4) is the chain-level shadow; Springer-functoriality of $\Psi^{\mathrm{st}}$ is the $(\infty,1)$-statement. Neither replaces the other.

\paragraph{Synthesis.}
The four statements:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\Nbkm = V(\mathrm{ord}_{H_1})\subset \Xbkm$ \hfill \ClaimStatusTheorem{};
\item $\Nt\to\Nbkm$ is the Heisenberg-parabolic small resolution \hfill \ClaimStatusTheorem{};
\item $\Psi: \Perv_{\Wqt}(\Nt)\to \Dbc(\mathrm{KL}_q(\gDelta))$ categorifies Gritsenko--Nikulin \hfill \ClaimStatusConjectured{};
\item $H^\bullet(\mathcal{B}_{x_0}) = \bigoplus_\alpha (\mathrm{mult}\,\alpha)\mathbb{Q}_\ell[-2\mathrm{ht}\,\alpha]$ \hfill \ClaimStatusTheorem{} mod $\Psi$;
\end{itemize}
assemble into a BFM-style dictionary for BKM Springer theory. Cite: Bezrukavnikov--Finkelberg--Mirkovi\'c (Publ.\ IHES 2005); Bezrukavnikov (ICM 2006); Ginzburg--Kapranov (\emph{Koszul duality}, 1994); Lusztig (\emph{Intersection cohomology methods}, 1991); Gritsenko--Nikulin (1996); Borcherds (Invent.\ 1995); Lorgat (2020).

\paragraph{Scope.} Sibling: \S\ref{wn:sec:wcg-deep-slide-frontier} (generalised BKM slide frontier). Scope: chain-level (denominator-product, Humbert stratification) and $(\infty,1)$-categorical (stable $\Psi^{\mathrm{st}}$) equal status; no Vol~III $\Phi$ collapse --- $\Psi$ is a Springer-side construction parallel to $\Phi$, not its pullback.

\section{$\Omega$-background $U(1)$ gauge theory on $K3\times E$, the additive Gritsenko lift of $\phi_{5,2}$, and the five equivariant directions of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$}
\label{wn:sec:nekrasov-omega-partition-delta5}

\providecommand{\ClaimStatusTheorem}{\textsuperscript{\textsc{[t]}}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusConjectured}{\textsuperscript{\textsc{[cj]}}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusAxiomatic}{\textsuperscript{\textsc{[ax]}}}
\providecommand{\fg}{\mathfrak{g}}
\providecommand{\cM}{\mathcal{M}}
\providecommand{\Hilb}{\mathrm{Hilb}}

The earlier section \S\ref{sec:nekrasov-omega-k3-e-phi10} recovered $1/\Phi_{10}=1/\Delta_5^2$ via three-parameter localisation on the CY$_3$ plane. A separate question stands untouched: does $1/\Delta_5$ itself, weight $5$ Siegel cusp form, carry a direct $\Omega$-background interpretation? The square sees DT reduced (Oberdieck--Pandharipande 2019); the single power sees the \emph{additive} Gritsenko lift of $\phi_{5,2}$, and with it the five simple-root directions of the BKM superalgebra $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ of Gritsenko--Nikulin.

\subsection{$U(1)$ ADHM data on $\C^2$ and the additive-lift seed}
\label{wn:subsec:b2-adhm-additive}

Fix rank one. The ADHM moduli $\cM^{\mathrm{inst}}_{n,U(1)}(\C^2)=\Hilb^{[n]}(\C^2)$ carries the $T^2=(\C^\times)^2$-action with weights $(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)$. The equivariant Euler characteristic
\begin{equation}
Z^{\mathrm{ADHM}}_{U(1)}(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2;q)
= \sum_{n\geq 0} q^n \, \chi_{T^2}\!\bigl(\Hilb^{[n]}(\C^2)\bigr)
= \prod_{k\geq 1}(1-q^k)^{-1},
\label{wn:eq:adhm-u1-unrefined}
\end{equation}
reproduces $1/\eta$ at the self-dual slice $\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2=0$ (Nakajima 1999, Nekrasov 2003). The refined K-theoretic version (Nekrasov--Okounkov 2006) reads $\prod_{k\geq 1}(1-q^k t^k)^{-1}$ with $t=e^{\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2}$.

Promoting the target $\C^2\to K3$: fibrewise on the smooth-$\C^2$-chart cover of $K3$, the Nakajima Heisenberg
\[
[\alpha_m(\xi),\alpha_n(\eta)] = m\,\delta_{m+n,0}\,\langle\xi,\eta\rangle_{K3}
\]
on the $24$-dimensional Mukai lattice produces, after specialisation to the index-one Jacobi slot and the $T^2$-character,
\begin{equation}
Z^{\mathrm{ADHM}}_{K3}(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2;q,y)\Big|_{\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2=0}
= \sum_{n\geq 0} q^{n-1}\,\chi_y\!\bigl(\Hilb^{[n]}(K3)\bigr)
= \frac{2\phi_{0,1}(\tau,z)}{\phi_{-2,1}(\tau,z)}\cdot\phi_{-2,1}(\tau,z),
\label{wn:eq:k3-adhm-jacobi-seed}
\end{equation}
whose index-two homogeneous part is Gritsenko's weight-$5$ index-$2$ weak Jacobi form
\begin{equation}
\phi_{5,2}(\tau,z) = \eta(\tau)^{9}\,\vartheta_1(\tau,2z)
\label{wn:eq:phi52-gritsenko}
\end{equation}
(Gritsenko 1999, \emph{Elliptic Genus and Siegel Automorphic Forms}; Gritsenko--Nikulin 1997). The Jacobi slot fixes the seed: $\phi_{5,2}$ is the unique weight-$5$ index-$2$ weak Jacobi cusp form with $\vartheta_1$-divisor. \ClaimStatusTheorem{} for (\ref{wn:eq:adhm-u1-unrefined})--(\ref{wn:eq:phi52-gritsenko}); \ClaimStatusConjectured{} for the compact-$K3$ equivariant localisation (\ref{wn:eq:k3-adhm-jacobi-seed}) at the full refinement (holomorphic anomaly potentially breaks strict equality off-slice).

\subsection{K3-fibre gauging by a flat $U(1)$ bundle on $E_\tau$}
\label{wn:subsec:b2-fibre-gauging}

Twist the $U(1)$ instanton moduli by a flat holonomy $y=e^{2\pi iz}$ along the elliptic fibre $E_\tau$; the resulting equivariant character promotes the one-variable $q$-series (\ref{wn:eq:adhm-u1-unrefined}) to the Jacobi form $\phi_{5,2}(\tau,z)$ after rank correction. Parametrise the fibre coupling by $p=e^{2\pi i\sigma}$ (the Siegel off-diagonal) and let $(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_3)$ act via the product tangent $T_{K3\times E}=T_{K3}\oplus T_E$ on the CY$_3$ plane $\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2+\varepsilon_3=0$. The three-parameter Jacobi-form-valued Nekrasov partition function
\begin{equation}
Z^{\mathrm{Nek}}_{\fg_{\Delta_5}}(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_3;q,y,p)\Big|_{\mathrm{CY}_3}
\label{wn:eq:znek-gdelta5-three-param}
\end{equation}
localises, by rigidity of the index-two Jacobi slot and the Gritsenko $\vartheta_1$-divisor at $2z\in\Z\tau+\Z$, to the index-two refined K3 one-loop determinant $\phi_{5,2}(\tau,z)\cdot p^2+\mathcal O(p^3)$ in the $p$-expansion.

\subsection{Gritsenko additive lift: $1/\Delta_5$ as a Siegel modular form from $Z^{\mathrm{Nek}}|_{\mathrm{CY}_3}$}
\label{wn:subsec:b2-gritsenko-additive}

The Gritsenko additive lift
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{Grit}(\phi_{5,2})(\Omega) = \sum_{m\geq 1}\bigl(\phi_{5,2}\big|V_m\bigr)(\tau,z)\, p^m
\label{wn:eq:grit-additive-lift}
\end{equation}
applied to the Jacobi seed $\phi_{5,2}$ produces the weight-$5$ genus-$2$ Siegel cusp form
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{Grit}(\phi_{5,2}) = \Delta_5 \in S_5(\mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z), \chi_2),
\label{wn:eq:grit-delta5}
\end{equation}
the character-twisted Gritsenko cusp form of weight $5$ on the paramodular subgroup \textup{(}Gritsenko 1999 Thm.~1.1; Lorgat 2020 \S3.1\textup{)}. \ClaimStatusTheorem{} --- this identification is classical: $\Delta_5=\mathrm{Grit}(\phi_{5,2})$, with $\Delta_5^2=\Phi_{10}=\mathrm{Bor}(2\phi_{0,1})$. The Borcherds multiplicative lift of $2\phi_{0,1}$ produces the square; the additive lift of $\phi_{5,2}$ produces the root.

The claim of this section is that $Z^{\mathrm{Nek}}_{\fg_{\Delta_5}}|_{\mathrm{CY}_3}$ of (\ref{wn:eq:znek-gdelta5-three-param}) equals $1/\Delta_5$ up to vacuum prefactor:
\begin{equation}
Z^{\mathrm{Nek}}_{\fg_{\Delta_5}}(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_3;q,y,p)\Big|_{\mathrm{CY}_3}
= e^{2\pi i(\tau+\sigma+2z)}\cdot\frac{1}{\Delta_5(\tau,\sigma,z)}.
\label{wn:eq:znek-equals-inverse-delta5}
\end{equation}
\ClaimStatusConjectured. Chain-level evidence: the $p\to 0$ leading Fourier--Jacobi coefficient of $1/\Delta_5$ is $1/\phi_{5,2}(\tau,z)$, matching the self-dual slice of (\ref{wn:eq:k3-adhm-jacobi-seed}); the $(\infty,1)$-categorical statement is that the fully-extended Nekrasov TFT on $K3\times E$, viewed as a functor from $(\infty,1)$-cobordisms of CY$_3$ data, sends the point to the graded character of $\fg_{\Delta_5}^+$ with multiplicity $c(4nm-\ell^2)$ at each weight $(n,\ell,m)$.

\subsection{Five equivariant directions $\leftrightarrow$ five simple-root directions of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$}
\label{wn:subsec:b2-five-directions}

The Nekrasov side carries five independent equivariant parameters $(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_3,q,y)$ modulo CY$_3$: three $\Omega$-rotations on the $T^3$ of $\C^3$ (with one linear relation $\sum\varepsilon_i=0$), one K\"ahler parameter $q$ for $K3$, and one fibre holonomy $y$. The BKM side carries five simple-root directions in the Gritsenko--Nikulin presentation of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$: three real roots $\delta_1,\delta_2,\delta_3$ spanning a hyperbolic lattice of signature $(1,2)$, and two imaginary roots --- the bosonic $a_0$ with $\tau(a_0)=9$ \textup{(}matching the $\eta^9$ prefactor of $\phi_{5,2}$\textup{)} and the leading fermionic root $\alpha_f$ \textup{(}contributing the $\vartheta_1$-divisor in (\ref{wn:eq:phi52-gritsenko}) and accounting for the superalgebra structure\textup{)}. The explicit identification
\begin{equation}
(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_3,q,y)
\;\leftrightarrow\;
(\delta_1,\delta_2,\delta_3,a_0,\alpha_f)
\label{wn:eq:five-param-root-match}
\end{equation}
carries:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\sum\varepsilon_i=0 \Leftrightarrow \sum\delta_i=0$ in the Cartan of the real-simple-root triangle (the Weyl chamber walls of the hyperbolic Kac--Moody real subalgebra of $\fg_{\Delta_5}$);
\item $q \leftrightarrow a_0$ carries the imaginary-root degeneracy $\tau(a_0)=9$, matching the $24$-dimensional K3 Mukai-lattice reduced by $K3$-rank: $24-15=9$ \textup{(}Gritsenko--Nikulin 1997 Prop.~4.2\textup{)};
\item $y \leftrightarrow \alpha_f$ encodes the $\Z/2$-grading: $y\to-y$ flips the $\vartheta_1$-sign, matching fermionic root parity.
\end{itemize}
\ClaimStatusConjectured: the identification (\ref{wn:eq:five-param-root-match}) is a sharpening of the Harvey--Moore BPS-algebra dictionary, chain-level consistent with Lorgat 2020 Conj.~1 on $8$ Gritsenko--Cl\'ery twined elliptic genera. The numerics $\tau(a_0)=9$ and the $\phi_{5,2}=\eta^9\vartheta_1(\cdot,2\cdot)$ factorisation are independently checkable (Poor--Yuen 2015 tables at $T_0=\tfrac12\mathrm{diag}(5,2)$).

\subsection{Falsifier: compact-ambient holomorphy break and MNOP--BKM heal}
\label{wn:subsec:b2-falsifier-heal}

The AGT dictionary (Alday--Gaiotto--Tachikawa 2010) is a non-compact $\C^2$ statement. On compact K3 the holomorphic-anomaly equation (BCOV 1993) breaks strict holomorphy; the $\overline\partial Z^{\mathrm{Nek}}$ has an explicit Eisenstein completion. The heal, internally consistent with the Pandharipande--Oberdieck modular identification, is: pass to the K-theoretic Donaldson--Thomas formulation, where MNOP (Maulik--Nekrasov--Okounkov--Pandharipande 2006) identifies K-theoretic DT on $(\C^2\times\C^\times)/\Z$ with refined Nekrasov, and the Gritsenko additive lift absorbs the MNOP prefactor into the Siegel modular $\Delta_5$; the anomaly survives only as the $\mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z)$-character twist, not as a genuine $\overline\partial$-obstruction. Five attack--heal cycles, chain-level:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item Attack: dimensional mismatch $\dim_\R(K3\times E)=6\neq 4$. Heal: three-parameter $\C^3$ with CY$_3$ constraint.
\item Attack: $U(1)$ is rank one, Nakajima $K3$-Heisenberg is $\rho(K3)$-rank. Heal: fibre over $\C^2$-chart cover; Mukai-lattice intertwines with Heisenberg on $H^*(K3)$.
\item Attack: $\phi_{5,2}$ has $\vartheta_1$-divisor; $1/\Delta_5$ has poles. Heal: vacuum prefactor $e^{2\pi i(\tau+\sigma+2z)}$ absorbs the Weyl-vector shift.
\item Attack: AGT is non-compact. Heal: MNOP--BKM reformulation (Maulik--Nekrasov--Okounkov--Pandharipande 2006; Oberdieck 2018) replaces AGT with DT/PT on compact K3.
\item Attack: $\Delta_5$ vs $\Delta_5^2$ ambiguity. Heal: additive Gritsenko vs multiplicative Borcherds --- the square is Borcherds, the root is additive.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Consequences and scope}

$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)=c_1(0)/2=5$ matches $\mathrm{weight}(\Delta_5)=5$ (Borcherds 1995). The Nekrasov partition function (\ref{wn:eq:znek-gdelta5-three-param}) is, on the CY$_3$ plane, a character of the positive half $\fg_{\Delta_5}^+$ on the Fock space $\bigoplus_n H^*(\Hilb^{[n]}(K3))\otimes H^*(E)$, with five-parameter weight-grading (\ref{wn:eq:five-param-root-match}). \ClaimStatusConjectured{} as a package; \ClaimStatusTheorem{} for (\ref{wn:eq:phi52-gritsenko}), (\ref{wn:eq:grit-delta5}); \ClaimStatusAxiomatic{} for the Lorgat 2020 Conj.~1 input. Cross-reference:
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}(K3\times E)=3$,
$\Xi(K3\times E)=0$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E)=0$,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)=5$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}=24$,
no conflation.
