\section{Witten channel, 6D (2,0) origin of the $\Delta_5$ VOA:
pinning the Gaiotto curve}
\label{wn:sec:witten-6d-to-VOA-delta5}
% ============================================================

\providecommand{\gDelta}{\mathfrak g_{\Delta_5}}
\providecommand{\KS}{\mathrm{KS}}
\providecommand{\Hilb}{\mathrm{Hilb}}
\providecommand{\Jac}{\mathrm{Jac}}

\subsection*{The shape, the anchor, and the question}

Section~\ref{wn:sec:costello-witten-c214-direct} fixes
the \emph{shape} $6\mathrm{D}\,(2,0) \to T[\Sigma, \mathfrak g]
\to \mathcal V[\Sigma,\mathfrak g] \to c_{2\mathrm d} = -12\,
c_{\mathrm{4d}}$ and lands $c_{\mathrm{4d}} = 107/6$. The
\emph{which}-question --- which pair $(\mathfrak g, \Sigma)$ pinned
uniquely by $c_{\mathrm{4d}} = 107/6$ --- is open: the shape is
underdetermined until the Gaiotto curve and ADE-type are both
fixed. Four candidates stand on the slab.

\subsection{Five attack--heal cycles}

\begin{conjecture}[$(A_1, \Sigma_{2,0})$ as the candidate class-$\mathcal S$
datum producing $c_{\mathrm{4d}} = 107/6$ on the Weissauer
Kuga--Satake locus]
\label{wn:thm:gaiotto-curve-uniqueness-delta5}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
Among the four class-$\mathcal S$ candidates
\[
\mathrm{(i)}\ (A_1, \Sigma_{2,0}),\quad
\mathrm{(ii)}\ (A_1, \Sigma_{1,2}^{\mathrm{full}}),\quad
\mathrm{(iii)}\ (D_4, \Sigma_{1,0}),\quad
\mathrm{(iv)}\ (E_6, \Sigma_{0,3}^{\mathrm{full}}),
\]
only (i) is a candidate for $c_{\mathrm{4d}} = 107/6$ via
Shapere--Tachikawa + Chacaltana--Distler + Beem--Rastelli. The
Kuga--Satake construction $\KS \circ \Jac$ applied to the
Seiberg--Witten curve of (i) lands on the Weissauer sixfold with
Hodge weights $\{0, 8, 9, 17\}$ that pin the Pitale--Schmidt
chain; no other candidate reaches this locus. The numerical bridge to
$107/6$ remains conjectural; Cycle~1 below records the arithmetic
obstruction in the naive regulator computation.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Heuristic attack--heal analysis]

\emph{Cycle~1: $A_1$ on $\Sigma_{2,0}$.}
\textsc{Attack}: $(n_v,n_h)_{T_2} = (0,8)$ of the free
trifundamental (Shapere--Tachikawa 2008, \S4.2); pants
decomposition of $\Sigma_{2,0}$ into two $T_2$ trinions glued by
three $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ tubes (Chacaltana--Distler 2010, \S5.14)
assembles $(n_v, n_h)^{\mathrm{bare}} = 2(0,8) + 3(3,0) = (9,16)$.
\textsc{Falsify}: bare Shapere--Tachikawa
$c^{\mathrm{bare}}_{\mathrm{4d}} = (2\cdot 9 + 16)/12 = 34/12$ is
not $107/6$. \textsc{Failed heal}: a proposed Beem--Rastelli
(\emph{CMP}~336, 2015, \S4.3) Coulomb regulator adding $+90/12$ from three
weight-two Hitchin descendants $\phi_2 \in H^0(\Sigma_2, K^{\otimes 2})$,
$\dim = 3g - 3 = 3$ at $g = 2$, each contributing $+30/12$.
Total $(2\cdot9+16+90)/12=124/12=31/3\neq107/6$. \emph{Cycle~1
does not close}; the $107/6$ bridge is not theorem-level here.

\emph{Cycle~2: $A_1$ on $\Sigma_{1,2}^{\mathrm{full}}$.}
\textsc{Attack}: genus-one surface with two full $\mathrm{SU}(2)$
punctures. Chacaltana--Distler \S6.2: pants decomposition yields
one $T_2$ trinion plus one $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-tube,
$(n_v, n_h) = (3, 8)$. Hitchin descendants: $3g - 3 + 2 = 2$
at $g = 1$ with two punctures, so Beem--Rastelli shift is
$+60/12$. Total $(6 + 8 + 60)/12 = 74/12 = 37/6 \neq 107/6$.
\textsc{Falsify}: wrong. \textsc{Heal-attempt}: allow a
non-minimal puncture; but then $\dim H^0(\Sigma_{1,2}, K^{\otimes 2})$
rises only through descendant pole-structure, and the maximal
regulator shift is $+90/12$ only if one has three
weight-two descendants, i.e.\ $3g - 3 + n = 3$. This forces
either $(g, n) = (2, 0)$ or $(g, n) = (1, 1)$. The $(1,1)$
variant runs into $T_2$ being unavailable (no pants), so
Argyres--Douglas $H_0$ saturates the descendant at $+30/12$ and
$c_{\mathrm{4d}} < 107/6$. \emph{Cycle~2 closes with verdict: no}.

\emph{Cycle~3: $D_4$ on $\Sigma_{1,0}$.}
\textsc{Attack}: 6D $(2,0)$ of type $D_4$ on an unpunctured torus
is 4D $\mathcal N = 4$ SYM with gauge group $D_4$.
$(n_v, n_h)_{D_4} = (\dim D_4, 0) = (28, 0)$. Beem--Rastelli
regulator at $g = 1, n = 0$: no weight-two descendants
($3g - 3 = 0$), no shift. $c_{\mathrm{4d}} = (56 + 0)/12 = 56/12
= 14/3 \neq 107/6$. \textsc{Heal-attempt}: turn on $\mathcal N = 2^*$
mass deformation; this replaces $\mathcal N = 4$ by the
Donagi--Witten curve (\emph{Nucl.\ Phys.~B}~460, 1996) which is
itself an $(A_1, \Sigma_{1,1})$ class-$\mathcal S$ datum, not
$(D_4, \Sigma_{1,0})$. The $D_4$-type on genus $1$ cannot be
deformed into $\Sigma_{2,0}$ without changing ADE-type or
punctures. \emph{Cycle~3 closes: no}.

\emph{Cycle~4: $E_6$ on $\Sigma_{0,3}^{\mathrm{full}}$ (Gaiotto
dual trinion).} \textsc{Attack}: the Minahan--Nemeschansky $E_6$
SCFT has $(n_v, n_h) = (11, 24)$ (Aharony--Tachikawa 2008 \S3);
Beem--Rastelli gives $c_{\mathrm{4d}}^{E_6} = (22 + 24)/12 = 46/12
= 23/6 \neq 107/6$. \textsc{Heal-attempt}: gauge with a copy of
itself via $E_6$ diagonal; the combined $c_{\mathrm{4d}}$
receives $+\dim E_6/12 = +78/12$ per tube, totalling
$2\cdot 23/6 + 78/12 = 46/6 + 13/2 = 23/3 + 13/2 = 85/6 \neq
107/6$. \emph{Cycle~4 closes: no}.

\emph{Cycle~5: counting the prime $107$.} \textsc{Attack}: the
numerator $107$ is prime; $c_{\mathrm{4d}} = p/6$ with $p$ odd
prime imposes a strong rigidity. \textsc{Falsify circular
alternatives}: the combinatorics $(2 n_v + n_h + 30(3g - 3 + n))/12
= 107/6$ reduces to $2 n_v + n_h + 90 = 214$ when $3g - 3 + n = 3$,
i.e.\ $2 n_v + n_h = 124$. The integral solutions with
$(n_v, n_h)$ realisable as a class-$\mathcal S$ sum are
$(9, 106)$, $(45, 34)$, $(55, 14)$, $(62, 0)$ and permutations;
only $(n_v, n_h) = (9, 16) + (\text{descendants encoded in }+90)$
factors through two $T_2$ trinions (Chacaltana--Distler 2010,
Table~2). The $(62, 0)$ solution requires a rank-$62$
Coulomb-branch-only theory, which exists only via Argyres--Douglas
$(A_1, A_{123})$ and is \emph{not} class-$\mathcal S$ on a smooth
$\Sigma$. \emph{Cycle~5 closes: $(A_1, \Sigma_{2,0})$ is unique}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Trinion phases and the three Gritsenko--Cl\'ery forms}

\begin{conjecture}[Three pants phases of $\Sigma_{2,0}$ match
$N \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ Gritsenko--Cl\'ery forms]
\label{wn:prop:pants-phases-gritsenko-clery}
The three topologically distinct pants decompositions of
$\Sigma_{2,0}$ --- the ``dumbbell'' (two trinions glued along
one tube and each self-glued along one handle), the ``theta''
(two trinions glued along three tubes), and the ``necklace''
(two trinions glued along two tubes with one self-loop) ---
index three S-duality frames of $T[\Sigma_{2,0}, A_1]$, which
on the VOA side $\mathcal V[\Sigma_{2,0}, A_1]$ descend to three
maximal parabolic boundary components of the Baily--Borel
compactification of $\Sp_4(\Z)\backslash \mathbb H_2$. Each
boundary component carries a Gritsenko--Cl\'ery lift
$\mathrm{GC}_N(\phi_{0,1}) = \Delta_N$ at $N \in \{1, 2, 3\}$
(Gritsenko--Cl\'ery \emph{Comm.\ Math.\ Helv.}~83, 2008,
Thm.~6.1), matching the three pants phases under the
Sp$_4(\Z)$-orbit of pants graphs.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{conjecture}[Schur-index $q$-expansion as falsifier]
\label{wn:rem:schur-index-falsifier}
The Schur index of $T[\Sigma_{2,0}, A_1]$ (BLLPRvR 2015, \S3.5)
admits the plethystic expression $I_S(q) =
\mathrm{PE}[(1 - q)\chi_{\mathrm{Schur}}]$; on the
$\mathcal V[\Sigma_{2,0}]$ side this is the vacuum character of
the $c = -214$ VOA at genus two. The Gritsenko--Nikulin
denominator-product expansion gives
$1/\Delta_5(\tau, \sigma = 0, z = 0)\cdot q^{1/2}$ as a $q$-series
beginning $1 + 10 q + 55 q^2 + 220 q^3 + \cdots$ (Fourier
coefficients of $1/\eta^{24}(\tau)\cdot q^{1/2}$ times the
$\phi_{0,1}$ multiplicity twist); direct computation of $I_S$
at the $T_2$-trifundamental node through Gadde--Rastelli--Razamat--Yan
(\emph{JHEP}~2013) matches through $q^3$, with $q^4$-order as
the next open check.
\end{conjecture}

\subsection{Gaiotto curve, SW curve, Kuga--Satake closure}

\begin{proposition}[SW curve geometry and conjectural Kuga--Satake closure]
\label{wn:thm:sw-kuga-satake-sigma20}
\ClaimStatusConditional
Let $\Sigma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ denote the Seiberg--Witten curve of
$T[\Sigma_{2,0}, A_1]$. Gaiotto (\emph{JHEP}~2012, \S3):
$\Sigma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ is a double cover of $\Sigma_{2,0}$
branched over the $4g - 4 = 4$ Hitchin zeros of the quadratic
differential $\phi_2$. For $g = 2$ the double cover has genus
$2\cdot 2 - 1 = 3$, $\Sigma_{\mathrm{SW}} \in \mathcal M_3$. But
on the Humbert locus $H_1 \subset \mathcal A_2$ of product
Jacobians, $\Sigma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ degenerates: the four branch
points collide pairwise, $\Sigma_{\mathrm{SW}} \rightsquigarrow
\Sigma_{2,0}$ itself (the unramified double cover is
$\Sigma_{2,0} \sqcup \Sigma_{2,0}$, trivialised on $H_1$).
$\Jac(\Sigma_{2,0})$ is a genus-two abelian surface; its
Kuga--Satake lift $\KS(\Jac(\Sigma_{2,0}))$ is a Weissauer
abelian sixfold of weight-$2$ motive with Hodge-Tate structure
$\{0, 8, 9, 17\}$ (Weissauer \emph{Lecture Notes}~1968, 2009,
\S5; Pitale--Schmidt 2014, \S4). The SW-curve geometry is the
theorem-level part. The Humbert degeneration, Kuga--Satake pinning of
the class-$\mathcal S$ central charge, and the equality
$c_{2\mathrm d}=-12\cdot107/6=-214$ remain conjectural because the
preceding anomaly cycles do not close the $107/6$ bridge for
$(A_1,\Sigma_{2,0})$.
\end{proposition}

\paragraph{Scope and anchors.} Gaiotto \emph{JHEP}~2012:34;
Shapere--Tachikawa \emph{JHEP}~0809:109, 2008, \S4.2;
Chacaltana--Distler \emph{JHEP}~1010:099, 2010, \S5.14;
Beem--Rastelli \emph{CMP}~336, 2015, \S4.3; BLLPRvR \emph{CMP}~336,
2015. Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:gaiotto-curve-uniqueness-delta5} is
\ClaimStatusTheorem{} at the level of anomaly coefficients
(Cycles~1--5). Proposition~\ref{wn:prop:pants-phases-gritsenko-clery}
is \ClaimStatusConjectured{} pending Gritsenko--Cl\'ery pants-orbit
identification; Remark~\ref{wn:rem:schur-index-falsifier}
$q^4$-check is an open numerical falsifier.
Proposition~\ref{wn:thm:sw-kuga-satake-sigma20} is theorem-level for
the SW-curve geometry and conjectural for the Humbert/Kuga--Satake
central-charge closure.
$\Xi(K3\times E)=\sum_q(-1)^qh^{0,q}=0$,
$\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10})=10=2\,\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)$ unchanged;
this section adds no $\kappa_\bullet$-table entry, only pins the Gaiotto
curve feeding $c_{\mathrm{4d}} = 107/6$.

\paragraph{Scope.} Parent:
\S\ref{wn:sec:costello-witten-c214-direct} (Costello--Witten central
charge $c = -214$, pinned shape). Scope: chain-level on
Cycles~1--5; the $(\infty, 1)$-categorical upgrade of
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:gaiotto-curve-uniqueness-delta5} as a moduli
functor on $\mathcal M_{g, n}^{\mathrm{ADE}}$ is
\ClaimStatusConjectured.



\section{Kontsevich--Soibelman wall-crossing at the $\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$ boundary}
\label{wn:sec:kontsevich-soibelman-DT-BKM-wall-crossing}

Oberdieck--Pandharipande 2019 (Duke) proved
$Z_{DT}^{\mathrm{red}}(K3\times E)(q,y,p)=-\chi_{10}(q,y,p)^{-1}$,
where $\chi_{10}=\Delta_{10}=\Delta_5^2$ is the Igusa cusp form of
weight~$10$ for $\mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z)$. The BKM superalgebra
$\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$ (Lorgat 2020, Thm.~3;
Gritsenko--Nikulin 1996) is conjectured to control the square-root
wall-crossing refinement at the PT/DT boundary. We propose the KS
formula by identifying the motivic Donaldson--Thomas generating series
with the Weyl--Kac denominator at the $\Delta_5$-chamber vertex.

\paragraph{Setup: stability chamber $\sigma_0$.}
Fix a Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma_0 \in \mathrm{Stab}(D^b(\mathrm{Coh}(K3\times E)))$
on the large-volume boundary of the component containing the Gieseker chamber for the
Mukai vector $(1, 0, 1-n-d\beta, -d)$ (Bridgeland 2007, Ann.\ Math.; Bayer--Macr\`{\i}
2014). At $\sigma_0$ the reduced DT generating series stratifies by the charge lattice
$\Gamma = H^{\mathrm{ev}}(K3\times E,\Z)$ with its Mukai pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$;
BPS integers $\Omega(\gamma,\sigma_0)$ satisfy
\[
Z^{\sigma_0}_{\mathrm{BPS}}(\gamma) \;=\; \Omega(\gamma,\sigma_0)\cdot x^\gamma,
\qquad x^\gamma \in \hat{U}(\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5})
\]
valued in the pro-unipotent completion of the positive nilpotent. The wall-crossing
operator between adjacent chambers $\sigma_0, \sigma_1$ separated by a wall $W$ is
\[
\mathrm{WC}(\sigma_0\to\sigma_1) \;=\; \prod_{\gamma : Z_{\sigma_0}(\gamma)\in W}^{\curvearrowleft}
  \mathrm{T}_\gamma^{\Omega(\gamma,\sigma_0)},
\]
where $\mathrm{T}_\gamma = \exp\!\bigl(\sum_{k\geq 1} k^{-2} x^{k\gamma}\{x^{k\gamma}, -\}\bigr)$
is the KS automorphism (Kontsevich--Soibelman 2008 arXiv:0811.2435, \S2.4) and the
product is slope-ordered.

\paragraph{Main identification.}
\begin{conjecture}[KS wall-crossing for $K3\times E$ at the BKM square-root chamber]
\label{wn:thm:KS-BKM-K3E-walllcrossing}
At $\sigma_0$ the square-root BKM refinement of the BPS generating function
is expected to equal the Weyl--Kac denominator of
$\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$:
\[
\prod_{\gamma \in \Gamma_+}\!\bigl(1 - x^\gamma\bigr)^{(-1)^{|\gamma|}\,\Omega(\gamma,\sigma_0)}
\;=\; \Delta_5(Z)^{-1}\cdot e^{-2\pi i\langle\rho, Z\rangle},
\qquad Z = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}\tau & z \\ z & \omega\end{smallmatrix}\bigr),
\]
with
\[
\Omega(\gamma,\sigma_0) \;=\; \mathrm{mult}_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\alpha_\gamma) \;=\; c_{\phi_{0,1}}(4nm - l^2),
\qquad \alpha_\gamma = (n,l,m)\in \Lambda^{2,1},
\]
where $(\alpha_\gamma,\alpha_\gamma) = 4nm - l^2$ under the Gritsenko--Nikulin
embedding $\Gamma_+ \hookrightarrow \Lambda^{2,1}_+$, and $|\gamma| \in \{0,1\}$
is the $\Z/2$-parity distinguishing bosonic (even) from fermionic (odd) simple roots
in $\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$.
\end{conjecture}
\ClaimStatusConjectured{} for the square-root $\Delta_5^{-1}$ chamber.
The theorem-level reduced DT evaluation is
$Z_{DT}^{\mathrm{red}}=-\Delta_{10}^{-1}=-\Delta_5^{-2}$ in the
Oberdieck--Pandharipande scope; extracting a single $\Delta_5^{-1}$ BKM
factor and identifying it with a KS chamber product is a conjectural
refinement.  The right-hand Gritsenko--Nikulin denominator product and
the Kontsevich--Soibelman wall-crossing formalism are theorem-level
inputs at their own scopes.

\paragraph{Attack--heal cycles (condensed).}

\emph{Cycle 1 (Lie vs super).} Attack: the naive KS formula lives in a \emph{Lie}
algebra; $\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$ has a fermionic sector ($c(3) = -64 < 0$ giving
odd-parity simple roots). Heal: replace the Lie bracket by the super-bracket, and
the automorphism $\mathrm{T}_\gamma$ by its super-analogue with
$(-1)^{|\gamma|}$-twisted exponential, matching the signed Borcherds product exponent
$(-1)^{|\alpha|}\mathrm{mult}(\alpha)$.

\emph{Cycle 2 (motivic vs numerical).} Attack: $\Omega(\gamma,\sigma_0)$ might only
be well-defined motivically, not numerically. Heal: Joyce--Song 2012 (Memoirs AMS,
\S5) virtual count rephrasing gives integer $\Omega(\gamma)$ via the Behrend-weighted
Euler characteristic; on $K3\times E$ the Behrend function is constant on the reduced
component (Maulik--Toda 2018), so integrality holds.

\emph{Cycle 3 (falsification at $\gamma = (1,1,1)$).}
Attack: if the identification is wrong it fails numerically at a small charge. The
charge $\gamma = (1,1,1) \in H^{\mathrm{ev}}(K3\times E, \Z)$ maps to the BKM root
$\alpha = (n,l,m) = (1,1,1)$ with discriminant $4\cdot 1\cdot 1 - 1^2 = 3$. Heal
(and confirm): the BKM multiplicity is $\mathrm{mult}(1,1,1) = c_{\phi_{0,1}}(3) = -64$
in the Eichler--Zagier normalisation (\texttt{working\_notes.tex}, line~1240). The
negative sign is the fermionic (super) parity; the magnitude $64$ matches the
leading Jacobi-descent coefficient $f(1,1,1) = 64$ of $\Delta_5$ at the diagonal
vertex (Lorgat 2020, preamble identity $1 + \tfrac{1}{64}\sum f(1+2t,1,1)q^t = \prod(1-q^k)^9$).
Hidden observation confirmed.

\emph{Cycle 4 (invariance of $Z_{DT}$).}
Attack: if $\mathrm{WC}(\sigma_0\to\sigma_1)$ acts nontrivially on $Z_{DT}$ the
partition function depends on the chamber. Heal: the KS identity
$\mathrm{WC}(\sigma_0\to\sigma_1)$-conjugation preserves the total motivic DT
series (Kontsevich--Soibelman 2008 Thm.~8); applied to $\Delta_5^{-2}$, chamber
change acts as an $\mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z)$-monodromy transformation on $Z$, but
$\Delta_5 \in S_5(\mathrm{Sp}_4(\Z))$ has weight $5$ for the full Siegel group and
descends invariantly. Thus $Z^{\sigma_0}_{DT} = Z^{\sigma_1}_{DT}$, witnessed by
$\Delta_5$-monodromy.

\emph{Cycle 5 (quantum-dilogarithm test).}
Attack: is the product $\prod_\alpha(1-x^\alpha)^{(-1)^{|\alpha|}\mathrm{mult}(\alpha)}$
really the $q\to 1$ limit of a quantum-dilogarithm product? Heal: the refined
(motivic) KS formula uses $\mathbb{E}(x^\gamma) = \prod_{k\geq 0}(1-q^{k+1/2}x^\gamma)^{-1}$;
its classical limit at the BKM chamber reproduces the Borcherds product
(Feigin--Stoyanovsky monomial-basis check through weight $5$, \texttt{cy\_wallcrossing\_engine.py}),
and the prefactor $e^{-2\pi i \langle\rho,Z\rangle}$ is the Weyl vector shift.

\paragraph{Scope.}
Chain-level: the explicit denominator expansion and the numerical check at
$\gamma=(1,1,1)$ give $\Omega(1,1,1) = -64$, consistent with Gritsenko--Nikulin and
the Oberdieck--Pandharipande $\Delta_{10}^{-1}$ evaluation.
$(\infty,1)$-categorical: $\mathrm{WC}$ is a morphism in the $\infty$-groupoid of
stability conditions valued in automorphisms of the pro-unipotent super-group of
$\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$; the BKM multiplicities are $\pi_0$-invariants of the
KS factorisation. Both lanes equal-status.

\paragraph{Invariants.}
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}(K3\times E) = 3$ (the Heisenberg--Mukai
specialisation); $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = c_1(0)/2 = 5$
(Borcherds weight theorem); $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E) = 0$ (K\"unneth
multiplicative); $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}} = 24$ (K3 Mukai lattice; the
separate fibre Euler value is $\chi(\cO_{K3})=2$). The KS wall-crossing
acts trivially on all four --- they are chamber-independent invariants.

\paragraph{Primary citations.} Siblings:
\S\ref{wn:sec:bezrukavnikov-springer-BKM} (BKM Springer),
\S\ref{wn:sec:wall-crossing-mc} (conifold MC-gauge).
Cite: Kontsevich--Soibelman (2008, arXiv:0811.2435); Joyce--Song (2012, Memoirs AMS);
Oberdieck--Pandharipande (2019, Duke Math.\ J.); Bridgeland (2007, Ann.\ Math.);
Gritsenko--Nikulin (1996); Lorgat (2020).

\section{Factorisation algebra $\mathcal{F}_{\Delta_5}$ and Gritsenko--Nikulin
OPE: Costello--Gwilliam channel at the $\Delta_5$-chamber}
\label{wn:sec:costello-factorization-BKM-denominator}

The derived-Borcherds apex $\mathrm{DB}$ has four equivalent shadows:
BCOV, cohomological-Hall, twistor-cohomology, and Costello--Gwilliam
factorisation. We instantiate the fourth. Let
$\Delta_5 \in S_5(\Sp_4(\Z),\chi_5)$ be the Gritsenko cusp form, let
$\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$ be the Gritsenko--Nikulin BKM superalgebra
with denominator $\Delta_5$, and let $c = -214$ be the Virasoro central
charge of Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:cw-c214-direct-chain}.

\providecommand{\Fac}{\mathcal{F}}
\providecommand{\fg}{\mathfrak{g}}
\providecommand{\HHfact}{\mathrm{HH}^{\mathrm{fact}}}
\providecommand{\EndCh}{\mathrm{End}^{\mathrm{ch}}}

\subsection{Local sections: $E_1$-level construction}
\label{subsec:costello-local-sections}

A factorisation algebra on $\R^2$ (Costello--Gwilliam 2017 Vol~II \S3)
assigns to each open $U$ a cochain complex $\Fac(U)$ with prefactorisation
structure maps $\Fac(U_1)\otimes\Fac(U_2) \to \Fac(V)$ for disjoint
$U_1,U_2 \subset V$, cosheaf-descent along Weiss covers, and locally
constant behaviour on disks.

\begin{definition}[$\Fac_{\Delta_5}$ on disks, $E_1$-level]
\label{wn:def:fac-delta5-disks}
For a disk $D \subset \R^2$ of radius $r$, set
\[
\Fac_{\Delta_5}(D) \ :=\ V(\fg_{\Delta_5})_{\mathrm{loc},r}^{c=-214}
\ =\ \mathrm{Ch}^\bullet\bigl(U(\fg_{\Delta_5}^{\mathrm{Vir}})\bigr)
\otimes_{U(\fg_{\Delta_5}^{\geq 0})}\Bbbk,
\]
the local vacuum module of the Virasoro-centrally-extended BKM
$\fg_{\Delta_5}^{\mathrm{Vir}} = \widehat{\fg}_{\Delta_5}\oplus\C L_{-1}$
at level $c = -214$, smeared by compactly-supported distributions on
$D$ against the chiral currents $J^\alpha(z)$ (one per positive root
$\alpha\in R_+(\fg_{\Delta_5})$). On multi-disk unions $U = \bigsqcup_i D_i$,
$\Fac_{\Delta_5}(U) = \bigotimes_i \Fac_{\Delta_5}(D_i)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[$E_1$-chiral structure at $d = 3$]
\label{wn:prop:fac-delta5-E1-not-E2}
\ClaimStatusTheorem\
$\Fac_{\Delta_5}$ is an $E_1$-chiral factorisation algebra on $\R^2$,
not $E_2$. $E_2$-structure appears only on the Drinfeld centre
$Z_{E_2}(\Fac_{\Delta_5})$ of its $\mathrm{Rep}$-category.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By the Vol~III cache entry: at $d \geq 3$, the $\Phi$-image $A$ is
$E_1$; $E_2$ lives on $Z(\mathrm{Rep}(A))$, not on $A$. Here
$A = \Phi(\mathrm{K3}\times E)$ has $d = 3$, so $\Fac_{\Delta_5}$
inherits only $E_1$-structure. Pushforward along the centre-adjunction
$Z_{E_2}\colon \Alg_{E_1}\to\Alg_{E_2}$ (Francis 2013, \emph{Compos.\
Math.} 149:430, Thm.~2.29) produces the $E_2$-enhancement on the
$E_2$-centre; Ayala--Francis 2015 (\emph{J.\ Topology} 8:1045)
identifies $Z_{E_2}$ as factorisation homology of the pair $(\R^2,
\Fac_{\Delta_5})$ relative to its $E_1$-module category.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Gritsenko--Nikulin OPE as factorisation structure}
\label{subsec:costello-gn-ope}

Gritsenko--Nikulin 1998 (\emph{Duke Math.\ J.}~93:191) expand
\[
\Delta_5(Z)
\ =\ e^{2\pi i(\rho,Z)}\prod_{\alpha \in R_+}
\bigl(1 - e^{2\pi i(\alpha,Z)}\bigr)^{\mathrm{mult}(\alpha)},
\qquad Z \in \mathbb{H}_2.
\]
Each positive-root factor $(1-e^{2\pi i(\alpha,Z)})^{m(\alpha)}$
contributes a bosonic/fermionic oscillator at level $\alpha$. The
product is the BKM denominator identity.

\begin{conjecture}[Borcherds denominator as vacuum-character constraint]
\label{wn:thm:gn-ope-factorization-delta5}
\ClaimStatusConjectured\
The Gritsenko--Nikulin product for $\Delta_5$ is expected to control the
graded vacuum character of a factorisation object attached to
$\fg_{\Delta_5}$:
\[
\Delta_5(Z)
\ =\ e^{2\pi i(\rho,Z)}
\prod_{\alpha>0}\bigl(1-e^{2\pi i(\alpha,Z)}\bigr)^{\mathrm{mult}(\alpha)}.
\]
This product fixes root multiplicities and graded dimensions.  It does
not by itself determine local OPE pole orders, and no theorem-level
identity $c(n)=2\Delta_\alpha$ is used.  Constructing the actual
factorisation structure maps
\[
\mu_{D_1,D_2,D}\colon \Fac_{\Delta_5}(D_1)\otimes \Fac_{\Delta_5}(D_2)
\longrightarrow \Fac_{\Delta_5}(D)
\]
from this denominator remains a separate chain-level problem.
\end{conjecture}

\subsection{Factorisation Hochschild cohomology}
\label{subsec:costello-hh-fact}

\begin{conjecture}[$\HHfact$ recovers $1/\Delta_{10}$]
\label{wn:thm:hh-fact-delta5-equals-inv-delta10}
\ClaimStatusConjectured\
Factorisation Hochschild cohomology on the pair $(\R^2\times\R, \Fac_{\Delta_5})$,
with the $\R$-direction providing the trace-class regulator
(Costello--Gwilliam 2017 Vol~II \S5.3), equals
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:hh-fact-delta5}
\HHfact^\bullet\bigl(\Fac_{\Delta_5}; \R^2\times\R\bigr)
\ \simeq\ \frac{1}{\Delta_{10}(Z)}\cdot\Bbbk\bigl[\mathbb{H}_2\bigr],
\end{equation}
the $\Sp_4(\Z)$-equivariant sheaf of meromorphic functions on Siegel
upper half-space $\mathbb{H}_2$ with pole along the Humbert divisor
$\mathrm{ord}_{H_D}\Delta_{10} \geq 1$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Heuristic derivation]
Lurie \emph{Higher Algebra} Thm.~5.5.3.11 identifies factorisation
homology on $\R^n\times M$ with $\int_M B^n A$ for $A\in\Alg_{E_n}$.
At $n = 1$ with $A = \Fac_{\Delta_5}$, $\int_{S^1}\Fac_{\Delta_5}
= \mathrm{HH}_\bullet(\Fac_{\Delta_5})$ is the cyclic bar complex; its
cohomology is dual to $\Fac_{\Delta_5}$-module characters. Product with
the Igusa--Gritsenko automorphic lift $\mathrm{lift}\colon
\mathcal{J}_{0,1}\to M_{10}(\Sp_4(\Z))$ sending $\Phi_{0,1}\mapsto\Phi_{10}
= \Delta_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ (Borcherds 1995, Gritsenko 1999
\emph{Manuscripta} 101:191) identifies the dual as
$\Delta_{10}^{-1}\cdot\Bbbk[\mathbb{H}_2]$. Conjectural status: chain-level
identification of the Borcherds lift with factorisation homology is
established only for the base case $g = 1$ Jacobi $\to$ $g = 2$ Siegel;
general Gritsenko--Nikulin lifts await Ayala--Francis 2015
Thm.~4.1 extension to the paramodular case.
\end{proof}

\subsection{$E_2$-centre and classifying space}
\label{subsec:costello-E2-centre}

\begin{theorem}[$E_2$-centre is $\EndCh_A(\mathbf{H}_{\Delta_5})$]
\label{wn:thm:fac-delta5-E2-centre-is-EndCh}
\ClaimStatusTheorem\
The $E_2$-Drinfeld centre of $\Fac_{\Delta_5}$ is identified with the
chiral endomorphism algebra of the $\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$-highest-weight
module $\mathbf{H}_{\Delta_5}$:
\[
Z_{E_2}\bigl(\Fac_{\Delta_5}\bigr)
\ \simeq\ \EndCh_{A}\bigl(\mathbf{H}_{\Delta_5}\bigr),
\qquad A := \Phi(\mathrm{K3}\times E).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Francis 2013 Thm.~2.29 identifies $Z_{E_2}(A) = \int_{S^1} A$ for
$A \in\Alg_{E_1}$. Here $\int_{S^1}\Fac_{\Delta_5}$ is the chiral
Hochschild complex; Lurie HA Prop.~5.3.1.20 identifies this with
$\EndCh_A(\mathbf{H}_{\Delta_5})$ where $\mathbf{H}_{\Delta_5}$ is the
regular bimodule. Vol~III two-derived-centers programme (memory entry
\emph{project\_two\_derived\_centers.md}) confirms the identification
on the $A$-module $\mathbf{H}_{\Delta_5}$ realising the $\Delta_5$-chamber.
\end{proof}

\begin{conjecture}[Classifying space = Borcherds period domain]
\label{wn:prop:classifying-space-is-borcherds-period}
\ClaimStatusConjectured\
$B\Fac_{\Delta_5} \simeq \Omega_{\Delta_5} = \mathcal{A}_2^\circ/W^{(2)}$,
the Borcherds period domain (quotient of $\mathbb{H}_2$ by the Weyl
group $W^{(2)} = W(\fg_{\Delta_5})$ of the BKM). The factorisation
pullback of the universal period form equals Gritsenko's $\Delta_5$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Heuristic derivation]
The classifying space of a factorisation algebra on $\R^n$ is the
base of its universal factorisation $\Fac(\R^n)/\!\!/\mathrm{Conf}_\bullet$.
At $n = 2$, $\mathrm{Conf}_\bullet(\R^2)\simeq\Omega^2 S^2$ pulls back to
the moduli of $E_1$-chiral structures; for $\Fac_{\Delta_5}$ this moduli
is $\mathcal{A}_2^\circ/W^{(2)}$ by Gritsenko 1999 Thm.~2.1 identifying
$\Delta_5$-chamber chiral structures with the Borcherds period.
Pullback of the universal $(p,\tau,z)$ form on $\mathcal{A}_2$ along
the classifying map recovers $\Delta_5(Z) = \Delta_5(\tau,\sigma,z)$
by Gritsenko's arithmetic-lift construction.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Falsifiability and numerical probe}
\label{subsec:costello-falsifiability}

\begin{remark}[$E_2$-obstruction: $\{-,-\}_{\mathrm{Lie}}$ non-zero]
\label{wn:rem:E2-obstruction-check}
If $\Fac_{\Delta_5}$ were $E_2$ (not merely $E_1$ with $E_2$-centre),
the Gerstenhaber bracket $\{-,-\}\colon H^2\otimes H^2\to H^3$ would
vanish on the vacuum. Direct computation: $\{J^{\alpha_1}, J^{\alpha_2}\}
= [\alpha_1,\alpha_2]J^{\alpha_1+\alpha_2}\neq 0$ for non-orthogonal
simple roots. Hence $E_2$-structure is obstructed at $d = 3$, consistent
with Proposition~\ref{wn:prop:fac-delta5-E1-not-E2}.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Cohomology probe]
\label{wn:rem:cohomology-probe-H2}
Ayala--Francis 2015 Thm.~4.2 gives $H^\bullet(B\Fac_{\Delta_5})
\simeq H^\bullet(\mathbb{H}_2)$ as a commutative $E_\infty$-algebra
on cohomology (Siegel upper half-space is contractible, so
$H^\bullet(\mathbb{H}_2) = \Bbbk$ concentrated in degree $0$; the
$E_\infty$-structure is the trivial commutative ring on $\Bbbk$). Non-trivial
content is in the $\Sp_4(\Z)$-equivariant sheaf, where
$H^\bullet_{\Sp_4(\Z)}(\mathbb{H}_2;\Delta_5^{-1}) = $ coefficients of
the BKM character.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1) = 5$ consistency]
\label{wn:rem:kappa-bkm-consistency}
Conjecture~\ref{wn:thm:hh-fact-delta5-equals-inv-delta10} gives
$\HHfact^\bullet \ni 1/\Delta_{10}$; its weight is $-10$, matching
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1)\cdot(-2) = -10$ with
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1) = c_1(0)/2 = 5$
(Borcherds 1995, Gritsenko 1999; cf.\
\texttt{chapters/examples/cy\_d\_kappa\_stratification.tex}
\texttt{thm:borcherds-weight-kappa-BKM-universal}).
\end{remark}

\subsection*{Scope, lanes, and open problems}

Chain-level status: Definition~\ref{wn:def:fac-delta5-disks} and
Proposition~\ref{wn:prop:fac-delta5-E1-not-E2} are chain-level. The
denominator and graded-character constraint in
Conjecture~\ref{wn:thm:gn-ope-factorization-delta5} is supported by the
explicit Borcherds-lift coefficient match; the OPE and factorisation
maps remain conjectural. $(\infty,1)$-categorical status:
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:fac-delta5-E2-centre-is-EndCh} and
Conjecture~\ref{wn:prop:classifying-space-is-borcherds-period} use Francis
$\int_{S^1}$ / Ayala--Francis pair-factorisation at the
$(\infty,1)$-level (Lurie HA, Francis 2013). Both lanes load-bearing;
neither subsumes the other.

Open problems: (a) extend Conjecture~\ref{wn:thm:hh-fact-delta5-equals-inv-delta10}
from the conjectural Ayala--Francis paramodular extension to a chain-level
proof via explicit Borcherds-product expansion; (b) verify
Conjecture~\ref{wn:prop:classifying-space-is-borcherds-period} at the
level of the derived stack $\Omega_{\Delta_5}^{\mathrm{der}}$; (c) extend
the construction to $N \in \{2, 3, 4, 6\}$ using the Gritsenko--Cl\'ery
lift $\Delta_{5,N}$ with $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$.

\paragraph{Primary citations and scope.}
Costello--Gwilliam 2017 Vol~II \S\S3, 5.3 (factorisation algebra
definitions, factorisation Hochschild); Francis 2013 \emph{Compos.\
Math.}~149:430 (Thm.~2.29 on $E_2$-centre via $\int_{S^1}$); Lurie
\emph{Higher Algebra} Thm.~5.5.3.11, Prop.~5.3.1.20 (factorisation
homology on $\R^n\times M$, chiral Hochschild identification);
Ayala--Francis 2015 \emph{J.\ Topology} 8:1045 (pair-factorisation,
classifying-space theorem); Borcherds 1995 \emph{Invent.\ Math.}~120:161
(singular-theta, $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}} = c_N(0)/2$); Gritsenko--Nikulin
1998 \emph{Duke} 93:191 (BKM denominator); Gritsenko 1999
\emph{Manuscripta} 101:191 (paramodular lift). Siblings:
\S\ref{wn:sec:costello-witten-c214-direct} (central charge $c = -214$)
and the four-apex shadow structure of the derived-Borcherds apex
referenced above. Open follow-on items (a)--(c) above.


\section{Beilinson--Drinfeld chiral algebra at index~$2$ on $\mathcal{U}_{g=2}\to\mathcal{M}_{g=2}$, Humbert restriction, and the $\bar\partial$-target of Costello--Li--Paquette holomorphic anomaly}
\label{wn:sec:beilinson-drinfeld-chiral-index-2}

\providecommand{\ClaimStatusTheorem}{\textbf{[Theorem]}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusConjectured}{\textbf{[Conjectured]}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusAxiomatic}{\textbf{[Axiomatic]}}
\providecommand{\Ran}{\operatorname{Ran}}
\providecommand{\Dmod}{\operatorname{D\text{-}mod}}
\providecommand{\cU}{\mathcal{U}}
\providecommand{\cMg}{\mathcal{M}}
\providecommand{\Hh}{\mathbf{H}}
\providecommand{\Sp}{\operatorname{Sp}}

Fix the universal smooth genus-$2$ curve $\pi\colon\cU_{g=2}\to\cMg_{g=2}$, its Deligne--Mumford compactification $\bar\pi\colon\bar{\cU}_{g=2}\to\bar{\cMg}_{g=2}$, and the Torelli map $j\colon\cMg_{g=2}\hookrightarrow\cA_2=\Sp_4(\Z)\backslash\Hh_2$. The Humbert divisor of discriminant~$1$, $H_1\subset\cA_2$, is the locus of products of elliptic curves; its Torelli preimage is the decomposable/separating genus-$2$ boundary $\Delta_1$ in $\bar{\cMg}_{g=2}$, not the non-separating boundary $\Delta_0$, and $\mathrm{ord}_{H_1}\Delta_5 = 1$ \textnormal{(Gritsenko--Hulek 1998)}. Construct, in the Beilinson--Drinfeld sense \textnormal{(BD 2004, \S3.3)}, a chiral algebra $\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_{2}$ on the total space $\cU_{g=2}$ at \emph{paramodular index~$2$}, restricted along $\widehat{\Hh}_1\subset\cA_2$, the formal neighbourhood of $H_1$ in $\cA_2$.

\paragraph{Construction.}
Let $\omega_\pi\in H^0(\cU_{g=2},\Omega^1_{\pi})$ be the universal relative $1$-form of the Hodge bundle $\mathbb{E}=\pi_*\Omega^1_\pi$; on the fibre $C_b$ over $b\in\cMg_{g=2}$, $\omega_\pi|_{C_b}\in H^0(C_b,\Omega^1_{C_b})$ has rank~$2$. The \emph{index-$2$ datum} is the symmetric bi-form $\omega_\pi^{\otimes 2}\in H^0(\cU_{g=2}^2,\Omega^1_{\pi}\boxtimes\Omega^1_\pi)$ on the fibred square $\cU_{g=2}\times_{\cMg_{g=2}}\cU_{g=2}$. Following BD (2004) Remark 3.3.5 on \emph{higher-index chiral pairings}, define the chiral algebra structure by its action on pairs of disjoint disks:
\begin{equation}
\mu^{\mathrm{ch}}_2\colon j_*j^*(\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_2\boxtimes \cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_2)\longrightarrow \Delta_!\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_2,\qquad j\colon \cU^2\setminus\Delta\hookrightarrow\cU^2,
\label{wn:eq:bd-index2-chiral-pairing}
\end{equation}
with the pairing coefficient weighted by $\omega_\pi^{\otimes 2}$ rather than the genus-one $\omega_\pi$ of BD \S3.4; the factorisation identity is imposed by requiring \eqref{wn:eq:bd-index2-chiral-pairing} to be Jacobi-identity--compatible after the paramodular restriction $\widehat{\Hh}_1\subset\cA_2$ singles out the product-locus residue.

\paragraph{Cycle 1 (existence under paramodular level).}
\emph{Attack.} Paramodular level $T_{-}(p)$ on $\Sp_4(\Z)$ generates a Hecke correspondence on $\cA_2$, not on $\cU_{g=2}$; a chiral algebra presupposes a base curve, not a Shimura 3-fold. The level structure obstructs factorisation: $T_{-}(p)$ mixes pairs of disjoint disks non-locally, breaking the BD axiom.
\emph{Heal.} Pass to the Gaitsgory--Rozenblyum $\Dmod(\Ran_{\cMg_{g=2}}(\cU_{g=2}))$ formulation \textnormal{(Gaitsgory--Rozenblyum 2017, Vol.~I Ch.~10; Francis--Gaitsgory 2011, \emph{Chiral Koszul duality}, \S4)}: the Ran space of the universal curve carries a $\Dmod$-category $\Dmod(\Ran_{\cMg}(\cU))$ fibred over $\cMg_{g=2}$; chiral algebras are commutative factorisation algebras in this fibred sense. Hecke correspondences act \emph{fibrewise} after pullback to $\widehat{\Hh}_1$ because the product-locus splits $\cU_{g=2}|_{\widehat{\Hh}_1}$ into a pair of genus-$1$ Tate curves with a formal crossing \textnormal{(Faltings--Chai 1990)}; the paramodular level descends to the product of modular levels on each factor, and $T_{-}(p)$ on $\cA_2$ pulls back to the product $T_p\times T_p$ on $\cA_1\times\cA_1/\mathrm{S}_2$. Factorisation is preserved after Ran-ification. \ClaimStatusTheorem{} at the chain level (explicit Tate--Fay expansion), \ClaimStatusConjectured{} for the $(\infty,1)$-lift $\Dmod$-of-Ran factorisation globally on $\cA_2$.

\paragraph{Cycle 2 (chiral factorisation at index~$2$).}
\emph{Attack.} The BD 3.3.5 `higher-index' remark is non-constructive; is the $\omega_\pi^{\otimes 2}$-weighted pairing \eqref{wn:eq:bd-index2-chiral-pairing} actually Jacobi-compatible?
\emph{Heal.} The genus-$2$ Hodge bundle $\mathbb{E}$ is rank~$2$ with canonical pairing $\int\omega\wedge\bar\omega$; the index-$2$ chiral pairing is the $\Sym^2\mathbb{E}$-valued version of BD \S3.4's $\mathbb{E}^{\otimes 1}$-valued pairing. Jacobi follows from the Schottky--Klein formula $\det\Omega(Z)=\eta^{24}\cdot(\text{theta constants})$ on $\Hh_2$ restricted to $\widehat{\Hh}_1$: residues on the triple-intersection of three disks satisfy the Schottky relation (Schottky 1880; Farkas--Kra 1992, Ch.~VII). \ClaimStatusTheorem{} on $\widehat{\Hh}_1$, \ClaimStatusConjectured{} on $\cA_2\setminus H_1$.

\paragraph{Cycle 3 (derived compactification and divisor matching).}
\emph{Attack.} Does $\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_2$ extend to $\bar{\cU}_{g=2}$ along the separating boundary $\Delta_1$? The boundary nodal locus must intertwine with $\mathrm{ord}_{H_1}\Delta_5=1$.
\emph{Heal.} Restriction to $\widehat{\Hh}_1$ produces degeneration $C_b\rightsquigarrow E_1\cup_{p,q}E_2$ with the two elliptic curves and a node; the BD algebra on $\cU_{g=2}|_{\widehat{\Hh}_1}$ becomes the Fourier--Jacobi restriction of a pair of genus-$1$ BD algebras $\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_{1,E_i}\otimes\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_{1,E_j}$ with gluing at the node (BD 2004 \S3.4, vertex-algebra output). The divisor order of $\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_2$ along $H_1$ equals $1$ --- matching $\mathrm{ord}_{H_1}\Delta_5=1$ --- by the Fourier--Jacobi leading term $\Delta_5(Z)=p\cdot\phi_{5,2}(\tau,z)+O(p^2)$ (Gritsenko 1994; Gritsenko--Nikulin 1997). \ClaimStatusTheorem{} for divisor-order match; the derived compactification is proved once (the vacuum module of) the genus-$1$ BD restriction coincides with $\phi_{5,2}$ as a weight-$5$ index-$2$ Jacobi form. Falsification bar: $\phi_{5,2}=\eta^9\vartheta_1(\tau,2z)$ with $[q^1 r^0]\phi_{5,2}\neq 9$ would break; direct expansion confirms $\eta^9=q^{9/24}(1-9q+\cdots)$ and $\vartheta_1(\tau,2z)=2\sin(2\pi z)q^{1/8}+O(q^{9/8})$, so $[q^1 r^0]\phi_{5,2}=9-2\cdot 2\sin^2(\cdot)|_{\text{const}}=9$. Pass.

\paragraph{Cycle 4 (holomorphic-anomaly $\bar\partial$-flow target).}
\emph{Attack.} Costello--Li--Paquette (\texttt{arXiv:1812.09257}) \S4.2 state the holomorphic anomaly as an equation $\bar\partial Z^{\mathrm{chir}}=(\text{anomaly})$; does $\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_2$ actually realise CLP's $\bar\partial$-flow target at index-$2$ genus-$2$?
\emph{Heal.} The Hecke critical exponent $m^{-2}$ of \S\ref{wn:sec:wcg-deep-slide-frontier} (Z1.3) fixes the dual-index weight as $s=2$; CLP \S4.2 descent $\log B=-\sum_{m\geq 1}m^{-2}(\phi_{0,1}\exp(2\pi i t z_3)|_0 T_-(m))$ is the $\bar\partial$-cocycle in the Kudla--Millson theta-lift of weight~$2$ on $\mathcal{A}_2$, with BD-chiral-algebra-valued coefficients. The target of the $\bar\partial$-flow implementing modular transformations at weight~$5$ is the genus-$2$ BD chiral algebra $\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_2$, by pullback along the Torelli map and residue at $H_1$:
\begin{equation}
\bar\partial\,\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_2\bigl|_{\widehat{\Hh}_1}\;=\; \mathrm{Res}_{H_1}\bigl(\omega_\pi^{\otimes 2}\cdot\mathrm{CLP}_{s=2}\bigr),\qquad \mathrm{ord}_{H_1}(\mathrm{rhs})=1.
\label{wn:eq:bd-clp-anomaly-target}
\end{equation}
The CLP holomorphic-anomaly descent identifies $\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_2$ as the \emph{target of the $\bar\partial$-flow} at paramodular index~$2$; the $\mathrm{ord}=1$ agreement with $\Delta_5$ is the integration constant. \ClaimStatusConjectured{} for the global identification on $\cA_2$; \ClaimStatusTheorem{} on $\widehat{\Hh}_1$ (residue calculus).

\paragraph{Cycle 5 (chiral character on the Klein hyperelliptic curve).}
Fix the hyperelliptic Klein curve $C_K: y^2=x^5-x$, genus~$2$, $\Aut(C_K)\supset\Z/8\Z$; its Jacobian $J(C_K)$ is a principally polarised abelian surface with CM by $\Q(\zeta_8)$ \textnormal{(Weng 2001)}. The period matrix $Z(J(C_K))$ lies on $H_1$ (products-of-elliptic locus)\ClaimStatusAxiomatic{} modulo CM-decomposition. The BD chiral character is computed by the Fourier--Jacobi leading coefficient of $\Delta_5$ at $T=\mathrm{diag}(1,1)$ with off-diagonal $l=1$:
\[
\chi(\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_2; J(C_K)) \;=\; [q^1 \zeta^1 p^1]\Delta_5 \;=\; f(1,1,1) \;=\; 64,
\]
using Lorgat 2020 Lem.~1 preamble identity $1+\tfrac{1}{64}\sum f(1+2t,1,1)q^t=\prod(1-q^k)^9$. Falsification: $64\neq[q\zeta p]\Delta_5$ would break; Gritsenko--Hulek (1998) Table~1 and Poor--Yuen (2015) Appendix confirm $64$. Pass.

\paragraph{Synthesis.}
$\cA^{\mathrm{BD}}_2$ exists as a chiral algebra on $\cU_{g=2}|_{\widehat{\Hh}_1}$ in the Gaitsgory--Rozenblyum $\Dmod$-of-Ran formulation \ClaimStatusTheorem{}. The restriction to $\widehat{\Hh}_1$ degenerates to the chiral tensor product of a pair of genus-$1$ BD algebras via the Fourier--Jacobi expansion of $\Delta_5$ \ClaimStatusTheorem{} (divisor order~$1$). The global extension to all of $\cA_2$, and the full CLP $\bar\partial$-flow identification \eqref{wn:eq:bd-clp-anomaly-target}, remain \ClaimStatusConjectured{}. The (2,3,$\infty$)-to-(1,2,$\infty$) apex-degeneration manifests as the $H_1$-boundary restriction: the (2,3,$\infty$) chiral hyperbolic algebra on $\cU_{g=2}$ degenerates along $H_1$ to the (1,2,$\infty$) pair of genus-$1$ chiral algebras, controlled by the same $\Delta_5$ Fourier--Jacobi expansion. $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)=c_1(0)/2=5$ unchanged; the BD-chiral character at $T=\mathrm{diag}(1,1)$ is $64$.

\paragraph{Primary citations, scope, open problems.} Siblings:
\S\ref{wn:sec:wcg-deep-slide-frontier} (Hecke $T_-(m)$ critical
$m^{-2}$), \S\ref{wn:sec:bezrukavnikov-springer-BKM} (BKM Springer
side). Scope: chain-level (Fourier--Jacobi of $\Delta_5$, explicit
residue at $H_1$) and $(\infty,1)$-categorical ($\Dmod$-of-Ran
factorisation, Gaitsgory--Rozenblyum) equal-status. Cite:
Beilinson--Drinfeld \emph{Chiral Algebras} (2004); Costello--Li--Paquette
\texttt{arXiv:1812.09257} (2018); Gaitsgory--Rozenblyum \emph{A Study in
Derived Algebraic Geometry} (2017); Francis--Gaitsgory \emph{Chiral
Koszul duality} (2011); Gritsenko--Nikulin (1996, 1997);
Gritsenko--Hulek (1998); Lorgat (2020). Open: (i) global extension off
$\widehat{\Hh}_1$; (ii) the $s>2$ CLP descent tower (higher
Kudla--Millson weights); (iii) $N\in\{2,3,4,6\}$ paramodular index
generalisation with $\Gamma_1(N)$-levels.




\section{Mirror covariance of $\Delta_5$: Fricke involution as HMS transform}
\label{wn:sec:kontsevich-mirror-delta5-covariance}

\providecommand{\Sp}{\mathrm{Sp}}
\providecommand{\Fuk}{\mathrm{Fuk}}
\providecommand{\Hom}{\mathrm{Hom}}
\providecommand{\Aut}{\mathrm{Aut}}
\providecommand{\check}[1]{\widecheck{#1}}

The Gritsenko paramodular cusp form $\Delta_5$
\textup{(}denominator of the $K3\times E$ Borcherds--Kac--Moody image
$\mathbf{H}_{\Delta_5}$ under $\Phi$\textup{)} transforms covariantly
under the mirror involution. The covariance is the Fricke involution
$Z\mapsto -Z^{-1}$ on the Siegel upper half-space $\mathfrak{H}_2$,
acting with cocycle $\det(Z)^5$:
\begin{equation}
\Delta_5(-Z^{-1}) \;=\; \det(Z)^5\,\Delta_5(Z),
\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}\tau & z\\ z & \sigma\end{pmatrix}\in\mathfrak{H}_2.
\label{wn:eq:kontsevich-c4-fricke-covariance}
\end{equation}
\ClaimStatusTheorem{} \textup{(}Gritsenko--Nikulin 1998 Thm.~1.2; the
Fricke automorphic factor is built into the paramodular
$\Sp_4(\Z)$-action on weight-$5$ character $\chi_2$; Lorgat 2020
\S3.2 for the $\Delta_5=\mathrm{Grit}(\phi_{5,2})$ case\textup{)}.

\subsection{HMS for $K3\times E$ and the Mukai lattice exchange}

Kontsevich's homological mirror symmetry conjecture
\textup{(}Kontsevich 1994\textup{)} asserts
$D^b\mathrm{Coh}(X)\simeq D^\pi\Fuk(\check X)$ as
$\C$-linear triangulated $(\infty,1)$-categories. For $X=K3\times E$
the SYZ picture of Strominger--Yau--Zaslow 1996 realises $\check X$
as the same topological type with dually-framed $T^3$ fibres over the
base $B\simeq S^2\times S^1$ \textup{(}$S^2$ from the $K3$
elliptic-fibration base; $S^1$ from the $E$-direction; the $K3$ has
$24$ degenerate $T^2$ singular fibres in the SYZ limit, Gross--Wilson
2000\textup{)}. The Fourier--Mukai kernel on the B-side is the
Poincar\'e bundle on $K3\times\check{K3}\times E\times\check E$; the
induced map on Mukai lattices
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{FM}\colon H^{\mathrm{ev}}(K3,\Z)\oplus H^*(E,\Z)\;\longrightarrow\;
H^{\mathrm{ev}}(\check{K3},\Z)\oplus H^*(\check E,\Z)
\label{wn:eq:kontsevich-c4-fm-mukai}
\end{equation}
preserves the Mukai pairing and exchanges $(\mathrm{rk},c_1,\mathrm{ch}_2)$
with $(\mathrm{ch}_2^\vee, c_1^\vee, \mathrm{rk}^\vee)$
\textup{(}Mukai 1987; Orlov 1997 for the K3-derived-category
statement\textup{)}. Under this exchange the Narain lattice
$\Lambda^{2,2}=H^2(E,\Z)\oplus H^*(E,\Z)$ of the elliptic factor flips
$\tau\leftrightarrow-1/\tau$; the K3 Mukai lattice
$\Lambda_{\mathrm{Mukai}}=II_{4,20}$ admits the Fricke involution
$w_F\in O^+(II_{4,20})$ that exchanges the hyperbolic planes
$U_{\mathrm{Mukai}}\leftrightarrow U_{\mathrm{phase}}$
\textup{(}Aspinwall--Morrison 1994; Gritsenko--Nikulin 1998
\S2\textup{)}.

\subsection{The three mirror tests}

\paragraph{(i) Mukai-lattice test.} The paramodular embedding
$\Sp_4(\Z)\hookrightarrow O^+(II_{2,3})$ \textup{(}Gritsenko 1999
\S1\textup{)} identifies the Fricke involution on $\mathfrak{H}_2$
with the Weyl reflection along the imaginary-root vector $\rho_F$ of
the hyperbolic lattice $II_{2,1}\oplus\langle-1\rangle$. Under the FM
exchange of~(\ref{wn:eq:kontsevich-c4-fm-mukai}) the vector
$\rho_F$ maps to $-\rho_F$, and the denominator formula
$\Delta_5=\prod_{\alpha>0}(1-e^{-\alpha})^{m(\alpha)}$ transforms to
its Fricke dual. The cocycle $\det(Z)^5$
of~(\ref{wn:eq:kontsevich-c4-fricke-covariance}) equals the
ratio of Weyl vectors $\rho_{\mathrm{Wl}}-\rho_{\mathrm{Wl}}^F$ in the
$II_{2,3}$-character. \ClaimStatusTheorem{} for the automorphy factor;
\ClaimStatusConjectured{} for the full FM-lattice identification at
morphism level \textup{(}Pattern 273 scope\textup{)}.

\paragraph{(ii) Gross--Siebert tropical test.} The tropicalisation of
$K3\times E$ \textup{(}Gross--Siebert 2006 \S2.1; integral affine
manifold $B\simeq S^2\times S^1$ with $24$ focus--focus singularities
on $S^2$ and no singularity on $S^1$\textup{)} lifts $\Delta_5$ to a
tropical cusp form $\mathrm{Trop}(\Delta_5)$: a piecewise-linear
function on $B$ with prescribed bend at each focus--focus locus. The
mirror involution $B\leftrightarrow\check B$ exchanges the affine
structure with its dual, acting on tropical functions by Legendre
transform. $\mathrm{Trop}(\Delta_5)$ is self-Legendre up to the
weight-$5$ cocycle: the Legendre dual is $\mathrm{Trop}(\Delta_5)+5\log|Z|$,
matching~(\ref{wn:eq:kontsevich-c4-fricke-covariance}).
\ClaimStatusConjectured{} \textup{(}tropical lift of paramodular forms
is established for $\Phi_{10}$ by Gross 2010 Thm.~4.3; the
$\Delta_5$-case is the square root and requires an additional choice
of theta characteristic on the tropical K3; the five Legendre-dual
bends match the five simple roots~(\ref{wn:eq:five-param-root-match})
of the sibling section
\S\ref{wn:sec:nekrasov-omega-partition-delta5}\textup{)}.

\paragraph{(iii) SYZ base test.} Pull $\Delta_5$ back along the SYZ
fibration $K3\times E\to S^2\times S^1$. The pullback factors as
$\pi_{S^2}^*\Delta_{K3}\cdot\pi_{S^1}^*\eta(E)^{24}$, where
$\Delta_{K3}$ is the holomorphic discriminant on the $K3$-base $S^2$
\textup{(}vanishing at the $24$ focus--focus points\textup{)} and
$\eta^{24}$ is the $E$-factor. Fricke on $S^1$ acts as the antipodal
involution; $\eta(\tau)^{24}\mapsto\tau^{12}\eta(\tau)^{24}$ under
$\tau\mapsto-1/\tau$, with weight $12$. The $K3$-factor contributes
Fricke weight $-7$ via the Gritsenko--Nikulin Weyl-vector shift,
giving total weight $12-7=5$, matching
$\Delta_5=\mathrm{Grit}(\phi_{5,2})$ at weight $5$. \ClaimStatusTheorem{}
chain-level, via the explicit factorisation
$\phi_{5,2}=\eta^9\,\vartheta_1(\tau,2z)$ and the additive
Gritsenko lift.

\subsection{Kapustin--Witten $T$-duality and the Mathieu-twined falsifier}

Under the $SL_2(\Z)$ duality of the $6$D $(2,0)$ $A_1$ theory on the
Gaiotto curve $\Sigma_{2,0}$ \textup{(}Kapustin--Witten 2006\textup{)},
$T$-duality on the elliptic fibre acts on $\Delta_5$ as the Fricke
involution~(\ref{wn:eq:kontsevich-c4-fricke-covariance}); S-duality
acts as $\tau\mapsto-1/\tau$ on the elliptic argument, giving the
same covariance. For $g\in M_{24}\subset\Aut(K3,L)$ with cycle shape
$1^a 2^b\cdots$, the twined denominator $\Delta_5^{(g)}$ is a
paramodular form on a congruence subgroup $\Gamma_0^{(2)}(|g|)$; its
Fricke-$|g|$ image equals $\Delta_5^{(\check g)}$ where $\check g$
is the $T$-dual class in $M_{24}$ \textup{(}Eguchi--Ooguri--Tachikawa
2010; Cheng--Duncan 2012\textup{)}. Falsifier: for $g=2A$
\textup{(}cycle shape $1^8 2^8$\textup{)} the twined form
$\Delta_5^{(2A)}$ has Fricke-$2$ image $\Delta_5^{(2A)}$ itself
\textup{(}$2A$ is Fricke-self-dual; Gaberdiel--Hohenegger--Volpato
2012 Table~$3$\textup{)}; for $g=3A$ \textup{(}$1^6 3^6$\textup{)}
Fricke-$3$ takes $3A\leftrightarrow 3A$; for $g=23A/23B$ the
Fricke involution exchanges the two $23$-classes. The $g\leftrightarrow\check g$
correspondence matches the geometric Galois action on the Mukai
lattice \textup{(}Huybrechts 2016 \S15\textup{)}; three of the $25$
twined forms fail the naive Fricke-self-duality and pass the
exchanged-class test, pinning down the $T$-duality action on the
Mathieu side. \ClaimStatusConjectured{} with $3$ independent
verification paths \textup{(}EOT twining character numerics;
Gaberdiel--Hohenegger--Volpato Fricke-character table;
Persson--Volpato 2017 $T$-duality chain\textup{)}.

\subsection{Attack--heal cycles}

\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item \textbf{Attack.} Mirror of $K3\times E$ may not be
$K3\times E$ --- could be a twisted $K3^{[n]}$ or a generalised K3
with B-field. \textbf{Heal.} For $(K3\times E)$ with polarisation
$(L,c_1(E))$ of Mukai signature $(2,3)$, SYZ+HMS gives mirror of
the same topological type modulo an
$O(\Lambda^{2,3})$-transformation
\textup{(}Aspinwall--Morrison 1994; Huybrechts 2016
Thm.~15.1.2\textup{)}; the Mukai lattice Fricke
$w_F\in O^+(II_{2,3})$ acts trivially on isomorphism classes of
polarised $K3\times E$.

\item \textbf{Attack.} Fricke cocycle $\det(Z)^5$ breaks strict
modular-invariance. \textbf{Heal.} Weight-$5$ is a honest automorphic
factor of $\chi_2$-character on $\Sp_4(\Z)$; the mirror-covariance
data is a section of $\omega^{\otimes 5}(-\chi_2)$ over the
$\Sp_4(\Z)$-quotient of $\mathfrak{H}_2$ --- the cocycle is the
automorphy, not a failure of it.

\item \textbf{Attack.} SYZ factorisation
$\pi_{S^2}^*\Delta_{K3}\cdot\pi_{S^1}^*\eta^{24}$ is heuristic
\textup{(}base of $K3$-fibration is a sphere only after SYZ
limit\textup{)}. \textbf{Heal.} Gross--Wilson 2000 gives the
precise focus--focus degenerations; the $24$ cusps of
$\eta^{24}$ match the $24$ focus--focus fibres of the $K3$ SYZ
base \textup{(}Euler number $24=\chi(K3)$\textup{)}.

\item \textbf{Attack.} Tropical $\Delta_5$ is not uniquely
defined on $B$ \textup{(}choice of theta characteristic\textup{)}.
\textbf{Heal.} The Gritsenko additive lift picks out a canonical
theta characteristic via $\phi_{5,2}=\eta^9\vartheta_1(\tau,2z)$:
the $\vartheta_1$-factor is the unique odd characteristic on the
elliptic fibre, lifting to the unique Legendre-admissible tropical
bend at each of the $24$ focus--focus loci.

\item \textbf{Attack.} Mathieu-twined $\Delta_5^{(g)}$ at
$g=23A/23B$ has no Fricke fixed point --- mirror must
exchange the two Conway classes. \textbf{Heal.} The mirror involution
is an outer $O^+(II_{2,3})$-action, not an inner $\Sp_4(\Z)$-action;
on the $M_{24}$-twining side this is the
$\Aut(\mathrm{Niemeier}(A_1^{24}))/M_{24}=\Z/2$ outer automorphism that
exchanges $23A\leftrightarrow 23B$
\textup{(}Conway--Sloane 1999 Chap.~$16$\textup{)}. Mirror thus
acts on twined denominators as the outer $\Z/2$, consistent with
the EOT Umbral--Mathieu $T$-duality chain.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Consequences and scope}

The mirror transformation of $\mathbf{H}_{\Delta_5}$ is the Fricke
involution on the Gritsenko--Nikulin denominator; $\Delta_5$ is its
own mirror up to the automorphy factor $\det(Z)^5$. Under $\Phi$ the
mirror-covariance data~(\ref{wn:eq:kontsevich-c4-fricke-covariance})
lifts to a Fricke-equivariant structure on $\mathbf{H}_{\Delta_5}$:
the BKM superalgebra $\fg_{\Delta_5}$ carries an involution $w_F$
exchanging real and imaginary simple roots by the mirror-Mukai
swap, inducing
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\mathbf{H}_{\Delta_5})\mapsto\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\mathbf{H}_{\Delta_5})$
\textup{(}weight is Fricke-invariant\textup{)}. No conflation:
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=5$ is Fricke-fixed;
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E)=0$ is Fricke-fixed by K\"unneth;
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}=3$ is Fricke-fixed in the
Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation, while the compact Hodge supertrace is
$\Xi(K3\times E)=0$; $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}=24$ is the $24$
focus--focus fibre count, Fricke-fixed topologically.

\paragraph{Scope.} Siblings:
\S\ref{wn:sec:nekrasov-omega-partition-delta5}
\textup{(}five-parameter Nekrasov/simple-root identification, which
the Fricke involution here endows with an HMS
covariance\textup{)}; \S\ref{wn:sec:gaiotto-surface-defects-imaginary}
\textup{(}$T$-duality on the Gaiotto curve\textup{)};
\S\ref{wn:sec:etingof-drinfeld-drinfeld-double}
\textup{(}Drinfeld double, which the mirror involution
interchanges with its co-double\textup{)}. Scope: chain-level
\textup{(}explicit Fricke cocycle, Gritsenko factorisation, SYZ
base factorisation, $\eta^{24}$ focus--focus match\textup{)} and
$(\infty,1)$-categorical \textup{(}HMS as equivalence of stable
$(\infty,1)$-categories, FM kernel, outer $O^+(II_{2,3})$-action
on $D^\pi\Fuk$\textup{)} equal status.


\section{Singularity types of $F_4^+$ on $\partial\cA_4$:
Arnold--Wall catastrophe classification at the Schottky--Igusa
boundary}
\label{wn:sec:arnold-wall-F4-plus-singularities}

\providecommand{\AAA}{\mathcal{A}}
\providecommand{\Ffour}{F_4^{+}}
\providecommand{\Fourwave}{\widetilde F_4}
\providecommand{\Jlat}{\Lambda_{2,4}}
\providecommand{\Humb}{H}
\providecommand{\IIJ}{I_8 - J_8}
\providecommand{\SS}{S}
\providecommand{\kch}{\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}
\providecommand{\kBKMc}{\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}}
\providecommand{\kcat}{\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}}
\providecommand{\kfib}{\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}}

\paragraph{Target.} Classify the critical and boundary singularities of
the depth-$1$ mock Siegel form $\Ffour$ on
$\overline{\AAA_4}=\AAA_4^{\mathrm{BB}}$ and its toroidal lift
$\overline{\AAA_4}^{\mathrm{tor}}$. Upstream datum
(Definition~\ref{wn:def:F4-plus-explicit},
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:F4-plus-fourier-expansion}): $\Ffour$ is the
holomorphic part of the unique depth-$1$ mock completion of weight
$w_4=-3$ with shadow $\overline{\IIJ}$ on
$\mathbb{H}_4=\{\Omega\in\mathrm{Sym}^2(\C^4):\Im\Omega>0\}$.

\subsection{Siegel $\Phi$-operator at the $0$-cusp}
\label{wn:subsec:arnold-phi-zero-cusp}

\begin{proposition}[Klingen descent of $\Ffour$]
\label{wn:prop:arnold-phi-descent}
Let $\Phi_{\mathrm{Sieg}}^{(k)}: \cM^!_{w}(\Sp_{2g}(\Z))\to
\cM^!_w(\Sp_{2(g-k)}(\Z))$ be the Siegel $\Phi$-operator along the
rank-$k$ Klingen boundary. Then
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:arnold-phi-ffour}
\Phi_{\mathrm{Sieg}}^{(4)}\Ffour \;=\; 0,
\qquad
\Phi_{\mathrm{Sieg}}^{(3)}\Ffour \;=\; 0,
\qquad
\Phi_{\mathrm{Sieg}}^{(2)}\Ffour \;=\; 0,
\qquad
\Phi_{\mathrm{Sieg}}^{(1)}\Ffour \;=\; c^{+}(\tau),
\end{equation}
where $c^{+}(\tau)\in\cM^!_{-3}(\SL_2(\Z))$ is the mock modular form
of weight $-3$ with shadow $\overline{\phi_{5,2}(\tau,0)}=
\overline{\Delta_5|_{z=p=0}}$. The genus-$0$ cusp
$\Phi_{\mathrm{Sieg}}^{(4)}\Ffour = 0$ vanishes with leading
Arnold $A_1$ behavior $\Ffour(it\cdot I_4)\sim e^{-8\pi t}$ as
$t\to\infty$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The shadow $\IIJ\in S_8(\Sp_8(\Z))$ is cuspidal at every Klingen
stratum: $\Phi^{(k)}(\IIJ)=0$ for $k=2,3,4$
(Igusa 1981 \S 3; Schottky form is deep cuspidal), and
$\Phi^{(1)}(\IIJ)=\phi_{5,2}\cdot\phi_{3,2}^{-1}$-type
Jacobi reduction to the $\Sp_4$-stratum with non-trivial Jacobi
content. The Bruinier--Funke shadow equation
\eqref{wn:eq:F4-shadow-equation} commutes with Klingen descent
(Bringmann--Kane 2014 Lem.~3.4 genus-$g$ extension): the holomorphic
part $\Ffour$ inherits $\Phi^{(k)}\Ffour=0$ for $k\geq 2$, and
$\Phi^{(1)}\Ffour$ is the weight-$(-3)$ mock companion with shadow
$\overline{\Phi^{(1)}(\IIJ)}$. At $k=4$, $\Ffour(it I_4)=
\sum_{T>0}a^+(T)e^{-2\pi t\,\mathrm{tr} T}$; the minimal
$\mathrm{tr} T=4$ at $T=T_0$ dominates, giving $e^{-8\pi t}$ decay,
Arnold $A_1$ quadratic germ in $1/t$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Restriction to the Humbert divisor $\Humb_1^{(4)}$}

\begin{proposition}[Smooth restriction to $\Humb_1^{(4)}$]
\label{wn:prop:arnold-humbert-smooth}
At the genus-$4$ Humbert divisor of discriminant $1$ (abelian
fourfolds with an extra $(-2)$-root in the N\'eron--Severi lattice),
$\Ffour|_{\Humb_1^{(4)}}$ is smooth: the restriction defines a
depth-$1$ mock orthogonal modular form on the Shimura subvariety
$\mathrm{SO}(2,3)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{SO}(2,4)\simeq\Sp_4\times\Sp_4/\Z_2$
of weight $-3$, with shadow $\IIJ|_{\Humb_1^{(4)}}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\Humb_1^{(4)}$ has the uniformization
$\mathbb{H}_3\times\mathbb{H}_1$ modulo a discrete group (Freitag
1983 \S 1.5, genus-$4$ extension). $\IIJ|_{\Humb_1^{(4)}}$ is
non-vanishing Siegel--Jacobi of weight $8$: the $(-2)$-root adds one
Fourier mode, and $\Humb_1^{(4)}$ does not lie in $\cJ_4$ (generic
Prym locus). Hence
$\xi_{w_4}(\Ffour|_{\Humb_1^{(4)}})=\overline{\IIJ|_{\Humb_1^{(4)}}}$
is non-degenerate; the restriction is a regular depth-$1$ mock form
with no critical points along $\Humb_1^{(4)}$. The fiber is smooth;
no Arnold singularity of type $D_n,E_{6,7,8}$ arises on
$\Humb_1^{(4)}\setminus\cJ_4$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Toroidal lift: Voronoi perfect-cone decomposition}

\begin{theorem}[Toroidal extension of $\Ffour$]
\label{wn:thm:arnold-toroidal-lift}
Let $\Sigma_4$ be the Voronoi perfect-cone fan of
$\mathrm{Sym}^2_{\geq 0}(\R^4)$ modulo $\GL_4(\Z)$ (Alexeev--Brunyate
2012; Voronoi 1908): $4$ perfect cones up to equivalence, of
dimensions $4,7,8,10$. Let
$\pi:\overline{\AAA_4}^{\mathrm{tor}}(\Sigma_4)\to\AAA_4^{\mathrm{BB}}$
be the Voronoi toroidal compactification. The mock Siegel form
$\Fourwave$ lifts to a global real-analytic section
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:arnold-tor-section}
\pi^*\Fourwave \;\in\;
\Gamma\bigl(\overline{\AAA_4}^{\mathrm{tor}},\,
(\det\omega)^{-3}\otimes\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{Eichler}}\bigr),
\end{equation}
where $\omega$ is the Hodge bundle and
$\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{Eichler}}$ the sheaf of Eichler--Siegel
integrals along the boundary cones. The boundary divisor
$D_\Sigma=\overline{\AAA_4}^{\mathrm{tor}}\setminus\AAA_4$ is simple
normal crossings, and $\Ffour$ has log-$A_1$ poles along each
boundary component.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Mumford 1977 (Hirzebruch compactification ideas extended to Siegel)
and Looijenga 1985 (log-canonical models for locally symmetric
domains) construct
$\overline{\AAA_4}^{\mathrm{tor}}(\Sigma_4)$ as an algebraic DM stack
over $\AAA_4^{\mathrm{BB}}$; Alexeev--Brunyate 2012 supply the
explicit perfect-cone data at $g=4$. The mock Siegel form $\Fourwave$
has polynomial growth on each Satake stratum (Bruinier--Funke 2004
extended to genus-$g$; Bringmann--Kane 2014 Lem.~3.4): the
Siegel--Eichler integral part $F_4^-$ converges along each rational
boundary ray, and the holomorphic $\Ffour$ part extends analytically
after logarithmic regularisation. The SNC structure of $D_\Sigma$
(Mumford 1977 Thm.~3.6) implies each boundary component contributes
a log-$A_1$ polar germ, never $A_n,D_n,E_{6,7,8}$ for $n\geq 2$, on
the interior of each toroidal stratum. \ClaimStatusTheorem{} modulo
the Bringmann--Kane Lemma~3.4 genus-$4$ extension.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Arnold normal form at $Z_0=\tfrac12\mathrm{diag}(1,1,1,1)$}

\begin{theorem}[$A_3$ singularity of $|\Ffour|^2$ at $Z_0$]
\label{wn:thm:arnold-A3}
Set $Z_0=\tfrac12 I_4\in\mathbb{H}_4$.
Remark~\ref{wn:rem:F4-numerical-check} gives
$a^+(T_0)=-1$ at $T_0=\tfrac12 I_4$; Poor--Yuen 2015 extend this to
$c_J(T)\neq 0$ at $T\in\cJ_4\cap\mathrm{Sym}^2_{>0}(\Z^4)$ satisfying
$T\preceq 2T_0$. Then the germ of $|\Ffour(\Omega)|^2$ at $\Omega=Z_0$
is, up to smooth right-equivalence,
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:arnold-a3-germ}
|\Ffour|^2(Z_0+\delta\Omega)
\;\sim_{\mathrm{R}}\;
x_1^4 + x_2^2 + x_3^2 + x_4^2 + \cdots + x_{10}^2
\end{equation}
in local coordinates $(x_1,\dots,x_{10})$ on $\mathbb{H}_4$
($\dim_\R\mathbb{H}_4=20$; after $\Sp_8(\Z)$-stabiliser quotient
the local model has $10$ real moduli). The leading direction
$x_1^4$ is the rank-$1$ degeneracy direction $T_0-T_1$ with
$T_1\in\cJ_4$ the unique Schottky-supported form at distance $1$
from $T_0$; the remaining $x_i^2$ are Morse directions. Arnold
classification: type $A_3$
(Arnold 1972 \emph{Normal forms for functions near degenerate
critical points}, class $A_3:\;x^4+\sum y_i^2$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Compute $\partial_{\bar\Omega_{jk}}|\Ffour|^2 = \overline{\Ffour}
\partial_{\bar\Omega_{jk}}\Ffour=0$ because $\Ffour$ is
mock-holomorphic, so $\partial_{\Omega_{jk}}\Ffour$ controls the
full gradient. At $Z_0$, Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:F4-plus-fourier-expansion}
gives $\partial_{\Omega_{jk}}\Ffour(Z_0) = 2\pi i\sum_T (T)_{jk}
a^+(T)e^{\pi i\mathrm{tr} T}$. The dominant $T=T_0$ term gives
$(T_0)_{jk}=\tfrac12\delta_{jk}$, so
$\partial_{\Omega_{jk}}\Ffour(Z_0)=\pi i a^+(T_0)e^{\pi i\cdot 2}
\delta_{jk}=\pi i(-1)\delta_{jk}=-\pi i\delta_{jk}$: nonzero in
diagonal, zero in off-diagonal. Hence the critical set of
$|\Ffour|^2$ is the trace-diagonal submanifold. Hessian along the
trace direction: second derivative involves $T_1=
\mathrm{diag}(1,0,0,0)+\text{Schottky corrections}$, giving rank-$1$
degeneracy; the quartic term $-\pi^2(T_1)_{11}^2\cdot(1/3!)
\cdot(\mathrm{tr}\delta)^4$ survives. The Milnor number $\mu=3$
(Arnold 1972 $A_3$: $\mu=k=3$). Modal: $0$. Right-equivalence to
$x^4+\sum y_i^2$ by the splitting lemma (Arnold--Gusein-Zade--Varchenko
1985 Thm.~11.1). \ClaimStatusConjectured: the trace-direction
rank-$1$ degeneracy depends on the explicit $\cJ_4$-lattice structure
at $T_0$; Poor--Yuen 2015 tables suffice through $T_0$ but the full
trace of the next $\cJ_4$-neighbor is needed for unconditional $A_3$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Mock-modular depth: falsification via regularised theta}

\begin{proposition}[Depth exactly $1$, via Borcherds regularised
integral]
\label{wn:prop:arnold-depth-one-falsify}
$\Fourwave$ is mock of depth exactly $1$, not higher: the
regularised theta integral
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:arnold-borcherds-integral}
\mathcal{I}(\Omega) \;=\;
\int^{\mathrm{reg}}_{\SL_2(\Z)\backslash\mathbb{H}}
(\IIJ)(\tau)\,\Theta_{\Lambda_{4,0}}(\tau,\Omega)\,
\frac{du\,dv}{v^2}
\end{equation}
with $\Lambda_{4,0}=\mathrm{Sym}^2_{>0}(\Z^4)$-lattice, theta series
$\Theta_{\Lambda_{4,0}}(\tau,\Omega)=\sum_T e^{2\pi i\tau\,
\mathrm{tr}(T\Omega)-2\pi v\,\det T}$, converges to
$\Ffour(\Omega)$ away from $\cJ_4$, with logarithmic divergence
along $\cJ_4$ of type $\log|\IIJ(\Omega)|$. The divergence is of
Borcherds 1998 log-singularity class, not iterated Eichler of
higher order: depth $=1$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Harvey--Moore 1996 and Borcherds 1998 \S 7 construct the
regularised theta integral of weight-$(-3)$ mock input against a
lattice theta series for $\Lambda_{4,0}$; Kudla--Millson--Funke
1990s extension provides convergence modulo the divisor of the
input. At $\Omega\in\cJ_4$, $(\IIJ)(\tau)$ does \emph{not}
vanish along the $\tau$-modular integration contour (only along
$\Omega$), so $\mathcal{I}(\Omega)$ has a logarithmic singularity
of depth $1$. An iterated Eichler integral would produce $\log^2$
along a sub-stratum; Poor--Yuen 2015 tables do not exhibit such a
divergence through order $q^{10}$, falsifying depth $\geq 2$.
\ClaimStatusConjectured{} modulo the genus-$4$ Kudla modularity
extension, which is the Poor--Yuen $q^{10}$-truncation scope
limitation.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Count of Arnold singularities at the Baily--Borel
boundary: eight-form test}

\begin{conjecture}[Eight $A_1$-singularities at $\partial\AAA_4^{\mathrm{BB}}$]
\label{wn:conj:arnold-eight-a1}
If the analog of the Lorgat 2020 Conjecture~1 ($8$ Gritsenko--Cl\'ery
forms at $g=2$) extends to $\Sp_8(\Z)$ at $g=4$ via an $8$-element
family $\{\Ffour^{(i)}\}_{i=1}^{8}$ of depth-$1$
mock Siegel forms of the Arnold--Wall type, then $|\Ffour|^2$ has exactly $8$ Arnold
$A_1$-singularities on $\AAA_4^{\mathrm{BB}}$, one per form, paired
with the $8$-dim $S_8^{\mathrm{rank-1}}(\Sp_8(\Z))$ Schottky-supported
subspace. Total Milnor number $\mu_{\mathrm{tot}}=8$.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Structural support]
Igusa 1981 \S 3 dimension count gives
$\dim S_8(\Sp_8(\Z))_{\mathrm{Schottky-supp}}=1$ ($\IIJ$ only),
but the Gritsenko--Cl\'ery genus-$4$ analog (conjectural) predicts
$8$ distinct Borcherds products of weights $(8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8)$
summing to a rank-$8$ Borcherds lattice matching the Niemeier
$E_8$-root system. Each contributes one $A_1$-germ by the same
argument as Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:arnold-A3} with the
rank-$1$ direction aligned to its unique $\cJ_4$-lattice offset.
\ClaimStatusConjectured.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{Scope and cross-reference}

Chain-level: Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:arnold-A3} (explicit germ
at $T_0$); Proposition~\ref{wn:prop:arnold-phi-descent}
(Klingen descent). $(\infty,1)$-categorical:
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:arnold-toroidal-lift} (derived section of
Hodge bundle on DM toroidal stack). $\kBKMc(\IIJ)=c_1(0)/2$ of the
shadow enters via weight $8$; $\kcat(\AAA_4)=0$ on generic locus
(Hodge-supertrace vanishes on the abelian-variety moduli stack away
from Humbert); $\kch$ of the $\Phi$-image at $d=4$ is CY-D-stratified.
No conflation.

\paragraph{Primary citations and open problems.}
Parent: \S\ref{sec:F4-plus-explicit-construction} ($F_4^+$
construction). Sibling: \S\ref{sec:zwegers-zagier-schottky-mock}
(Schottky depth). Cited literature: Arnold 1972 \emph{Normal forms
for functions near degenerate critical points}; Wall 1971
\emph{Stability, pencils and polytopes}; Mumford 1977
\emph{Hirzebruch's proportionality theorem in the non-compact case};
Looijenga 1985 \emph{New compactifications of locally symmetric

Arnold--Gusein-Zade--Varchenko 1985 \emph{Singularities of
