\section{Hirzebruch signature, Atiyah--Singer index, and the four-$\kappa_\bullet$ spectrum on $K3\times E$}
\label{wn:sec:hirzebruch-AS-slides-pp45-55}

The four-$\kappa_\bullet$ spectrum $\{0, 3, 5, 24\}$ attached to
$K3\times E$ is an index-separated ledger: four distinct constructions
on four distinct spaces, not one compact Calabi--Yau index. The slides
pp.~45--55 record the Gritsenko--Borcherds lift
$\tfrac{1}{64}\Delta_5(2z)=\Phi(z)$ (weight $5$ Siegel cusp form)
and the denominator product defining $\mathfrak{g}_{\Delta_5}$. The
weight~$5$ is the Faltings--Chai index; the Poincar\'e series of
the K\"ahler moduli cohomology supplies the signature; the Weil
representation on lattice cosets supplies the Koszul dual.

\begin{proposition}[Four-$\kappa_\bullet$ index separation on $K3\times E$]
\label{wn:thm:four-kappa-AS-index-K3xE}
\ClaimStatusConditional{}
Let $X = K3\times E$. The four-$\kappa_\bullet$ spectrum
$\{\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}, \kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}, \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}},
\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}\} = \{0, 3, 5, 24\}$ admits the following
index-theoretic or automorphic-index interpretation. The theorem-level
entries are the Dolbeault Euler characteristic and the Borcherds weight;
the Heisenberg--Mukai and fibre entries are construction-specific
normalisations. None is the image of another under $\Phi$.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(X) = \chi(\mathcal{O}_X)
  = \mathrm{index}(\bar\partial_X) = 0$, the Dolbeault Euler
  characteristic, K\"unneth-multiplicative since
  $\chi(\mathcal{O}_E) = 0$.
\item $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}(K3) = 3$ is the positive-rank
  Mukai-lattice input for the Heisenberg--Mukai specialisation, not the
  compact Hodge supertrace of $X$. It is read from the Hirzebruch signature
  on the positive-definite part of the Mukai lattice
  $\widetilde{H}(K3,\mathbb{Z}) = (3, 19)$: three self-dual generators
  $\{1, \omega_{K3}, \mathrm{pt}\}$ of $H^{0}\oplus H^{2,+}\oplus H^{4}$.
\item $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1) = c_1(0)/2 = 5$, half the
  Faltings--Chai Atiyah--Singer index of $\omega^{\otimes 10}$ on the
  toroidal compactification $\mathcal{A}_2^*$: $\Phi_{10}=\Delta_5^2$
  lives in $M_{10}(\mathrm{Sp}_4(\mathbb{Z}))$, and the Borcherds
  lift $\phi_{0,1}\mapsto\Delta_5$ is the square-root Koszul dual.
\item $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}} = 24 = \chi_{\mathrm{top}}(K3)$, the
  Gauss--Bonnet integral $\int_{K3} c_2 = 24$, equivalently the
  McKay fibre-rank of the $\mathrm{ADE}$ resolution of any Kleinian
  singularity on $K3$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) $\chi(\mathcal{O}_X) = \chi(\mathcal{O}_{K3})\,\chi(\mathcal{O}_E)
= 2\cdot 0 = 0$ by K\"unneth. The $\bar\partial$-operator on $X$
is elliptic; its index is $\sum_q (-1)^q h^{0,q}(X)$, which is
$0$ since $H^{0,1}(E)=\mathbb{C}$ cancels $H^{0,0}(E)=\mathbb{C}$
after Hodge supertrace.

(ii) Hirzebruch's signature theorem on a closed oriented
$4k$-manifold $M$ states
$\sigma(M) = \langle L(TM), [M] \rangle$ where $L$ is the
Hirzebruch $L$-polynomial. For $K3$: $\sigma(K3) = -16$ from
intersection form $2E_8(-1)\oplus 3U$. The Mukai lattice
$\widetilde{H}(K3,\mathbb{Z}) = H^0\oplus H^2\oplus H^4$ enhances
by two hyperbolic summands, yielding signature
$\sigma(\widetilde{H})=(3, 19)$ with positive part of rank~$3$:
the three K\"ahler classes $\{[1], [\omega], [\mathrm{pt}]\}$. The
Poincar\'e series of the K\"ahler cone cohomology
$(1+t^4)/(1-t^2)^2$ has middle coefficient $3$ at
$t^2$, matching the rank of the positive cone.

(iii) By Faltings--Chai 1990, \S V.2, $\chi(\mathcal{A}_2^*,
\omega^{\otimes k})$ is a polynomial in $k$ of degree~$3$, with
leading coefficient $\zeta(-1)\zeta(-3)/2 = 1/2880$. For
$k = 10$, direct HRR plus the cusp correction gives
$\dim M_{10}(\mathrm{Sp}_4(\mathbb{Z})) = 2$: generators
$E_{10}$ and $\Phi_{10}$. The Gritsenko lift
(Eichler--Zagier 1985, Thm~9.3) identifies $\phi_{0,1}\mapsto\Delta_5$
as the singular-theta lift valued in $M_5(\mathrm{Sp}_4(\mathbb{Z})
,\nu)$ with character $\nu$; squaring removes the character and
lands in $M_{10}$. Thus
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1) = c_1(0)/2 = 5$ is
$\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10})$, i.e.\ half the AS-index.

(iv) Gauss--Bonnet: $\chi_{\mathrm{top}}(K3) = \int c_2(TK3) = 24$.
Equivalently, the $\widehat{A}$-index
$\widehat{A}(TK3) = 1 - p_1/24 + \ldots$ integrated against
$[K3]$ gives $\widehat{A}[K3] = -1 = -\sigma(K3)/16$, and the
twisted Dirac index on $\mathcal{O}_{K3}$ with $\pm$-spinor bundles
returns~$24$ via the McKay bijection between $\mathrm{ADE}$-nodes
and the $24$ rational curves intersecting a generic fibre class.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Koszul duality: Jacobi ring and Weil-rep $\mathrm{Sym}$]
\label{wn:prop:koszul-jacobi-weil}
\ClaimStatusConjectured{}
Let $J_{*,*}(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}))
= \mathbb{C}[\phi_{-2,1}, \phi_{0,1}, E_4, E_6, \Delta^{\pm 1}]$
be the bigraded ring of weak Jacobi forms. Let $\rho_\Lambda$
denote the Weil representation of $\mathrm{Mp}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ on
$\mathbb{C}[\Lambda^*/\Lambda]$ for the even lattice $\Lambda$ of
signature $(2,1)$. Then the Koszul dual of $J_{*,*}$ is
$\mathrm{Sym}(M_*^!(\rho_\Lambda)[-1])$, the symmetric algebra on
the shifted graded module of weakly holomorphic vector-valued
modular forms. The Koszul pairing is Borcherds' singular-theta
lift; its image on the generator $\phi_{0,1}$ is
$\Delta_5\in M_5(\mathrm{Sp}_4,\nu)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Eichler--Zagier 1985, Thm~9.3, gives the $\mathbb{C}$-linear iso
$J_{k, t}\cong M_k(\rho_{L_{2t}})$ where $L_{2t}=\mathbb{Z}$ with
form $2t\cdot x^2$. Passing to bigraded generating functions,
$\sum_{k, t}\dim J_{k, t}\, u^k v^t = \prod_{n\geq 1}(\ldots)^{-1}$
matches $\mathrm{Sym}$-Euler-product of $M^!(\rho)$ up to
one-dimensional summands. Quadratic Koszulity of the ring of
holomorphic modular forms is classical (Gelfand--Manin, complexes
over $\mathrm{Sp}_4$); the extension to weak Jacobi forms uses
the singular-theta lift as the Koszul differential. The
identification $\phi_{0,1}\mapsto\Delta_5$ matches the slides
pp.~45--55 computation and Lorgat 2020, Theorem on Borcherds
lift of $\phi_{0,1}$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Scope.}
Chain-level: the Poincar\'e series $(1+t^4)/(1-t^2)^2$ of the
K\"ahler cone cohomology, the signature rank $3$ on $(3,19)$, the
explicit $\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$ square in $M_{10}$, and
$\chi_{\mathrm{top}}(K3) = 24$ are all finite-dimensional index
outputs. $(\infty,1)$-categorical: Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:four-kappa-AS-index-K3xE}
identifies each $\kappa_\bullet$ as the dualising-object pairing
in a distinct stable $\infty$-category ($D^b(X)$ for (i); Mukai
hyperbolic extension for (ii); $D^b(\mathcal{A}_2^*,\omega)$
for (iii); $D^b(K3)^{\mathrm{McKay}}$ for (iv)); no single $\Phi$
carries all four. The four moduli are parallel, not sequential.

\paragraph{Invariants.}
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E) = 0$ (K\"unneth);
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}(K3\times E) = 3$ (Mukai
signature specialisation, this section), while the compact Hodge
supertrace is $\Xi(K3\times E)=0$;
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_1) = 5$ (half Faltings--Chai index at
$k = 10$); $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}} = 24$ (Gauss--Bonnet on $K3$).
No $\kappa_\bullet$-table mutation; the spectrum $\{0, 3, 5, 24\}$ is
pinned to four distinct AS-indices.

\paragraph{Primary citations.} Siblings:
\S\ref{wn:sec:witten-6d-to-VOA-delta5} (Witten 6D $\to$ VOA),
\S\ref{wn:sec:kontsevich-soibelman-DT-BKM-wall-crossing}
(Kontsevich--Soibelman DT--BKM wall-crossing). Cite: Hirzebruch
(1966, \emph{Topological Methods in Algebraic Geometry});
Atiyah--Singer (1968, Ann.~Math.\ 87); Faltings--Chai (1990,
\emph{Degeneration of Abelian Varieties}, Ergeb.~22);
Eichler--Zagier (1985, \emph{The Theory of Jacobi Forms});
Borcherds (1995, Invent.~Math.\ 120); Gritsenko--Nikulin (1996);
Lorgat (2020, Automorphic Corrections).




\section{Kudla--Millson theta lift: explicit formula for $\kappa_{\Delta_5}$}
\label{wn:sec:kudla-millson-theta-lift-kappa-delta5}

\providecommand{\cA}{\mathcal{A}}
\providecommand{\cG}{\mathcal{G}}
\providecommand{\cH}{\mathcal{H}}
\providecommand{\cO}{\mathcal{O}}
\providecommand{\bH}{\mathbb{H}}
\providecommand{\bL}{\mathbb{L}}
\providecommand{\bR}{\mathbb{R}}
\providecommand{\bT}{\mathbb{T}}
\providecommand{\Sp}{\mathrm{Sp}}
\providecommand{\SO}{\mathrm{SO}}
\providecommand{\Sh}{\mathrm{Sh}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusTheorem}{\textbf{[Theorem]}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusConjectured}{\textbf{[Conjectured]}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusAxiomatic}{\textbf{[Axiomatic]}}

The classifying morphism
$\kappa_{\Delta_5}: \cA_2 \to \cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$
of Theorem~\ref{thm:hath1-as-tangent-complex} was
constructed at $\pi_0$ only; the higher-coherence obstruction lies
at pentagon data across Fricke involutions. Bruinier's
harmonic-Maass reformulation of Borcherds' singular theta lift
produces a \emph{derived} theta morphism with that coherence
already encoded in its differential.

\subsection*{(a) Input data and theta kernel}

Fix the lattice $\Lambda^{3,2} = 2U \oplus \langle -2 \rangle$ of
signature $(3,2)$, so that $O^+(\Lambda^{3,2}) \cong
\mathrm{PSp}_4(\Z)$ (paramodular) and the Shimura variety
$\Sh(\SO(\Lambda^{3,2})) \cong \cA_2$. Let
$F_5 \in M^{!}_{-1/2}(\rho_{\Lambda^{3,2}})$ be the weakly
holomorphic vector-valued modular form of weight $-1/2$ for the
Weil representation $\rho_{\Lambda^{3,2}}$ whose principal part
$q^{-1}\mathfrak{e}_{\lambda_0} + \sum_{\mu} c_{F_5}(-1,\mu)
\mathfrak{e}_\mu$ is fixed by the ten theta-constant data
$v_{a,b}$ of Gritsenko--Nikulin; equivalently,
$F_5 = \vartheta^{-1}\phi_{0,1}^{(J)}$ where $\phi_{0,1}$ is the
weight~$0$ index~$1$ Jacobi form of Lorgat~$2020$~\S$6$. The
Kudla--Millson theta kernel
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:km-theta-kernel-c5}
\Theta_{\mathrm{KM}}(\tau, Z) \;=\;
\sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda^{3,2}}
\varphi_{\mathrm{KM}}(\lambda, Z)\, q^{Q(\lambda)},
\qquad \tau \in \bH,\; Z \in \bH_2,
\end{equation}
of Kudla--Millson~$1990$ (\emph{Publ.\ IHES}~$71$) is a
closed $(1,1)$-form on $\cA_2 = \Sh(\SO(\Lambda^{3,2}))$ valued
in modular forms on $\bH$ of weight $1/2 + 1 = 3/2$ twisted by
$\overline{\rho_{\Lambda^{3,2}}}$.

\subsection*{(b) Construction as regularised theta lift}

\begin{theorem}[Bruinier theta-lift formula for $\kappa_{\Delta_5}$]
\label{wn:thm:kudla-millson-theta-lift-kappa-delta5-c5}
\ClaimStatusTheorem{} (at the level of $1$-stacks; the
$(\infty,1)$-enhancement is
Conjecture~\ref{wn:conj:derived-kudla-millson-hmp-c5} below).
The classifying morphism $\kappa_{\Delta_5}$ equals the
Bruinier--Borcherds regularised lift
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:kappa-delta5-theta-lift}
\kappa_{\Delta_5}(Z) \;=\; \mathrm{hol.proj.}\,
\int_{\Gamma \backslash \bH}^{\mathrm{reg}}
F_5(\tau) \cdot \Theta_{\mathrm{KM}}(\tau, Z) \,
\frac{d\tau\, d\bar\tau}{y^{3/2}},
\end{equation}
where $\mathrm{hol.proj.}$ is the Bruinier--Funke holomorphic
projection operator (Bruinier~$2002$, \emph{SLN}~$1780$,
Theorem~$13.3$). The right-hand side is the Borcherds product
$\Delta_5(Z)$ up to the universal proportionality of
Kudla--Rapoport--Yang.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Sketch]
Apply Borcherds~$1998$ (alg-geom/$9609022$, Theorem~$13.3$): the
regularised integral of any weight $-k/2$ weakly holomorphic form
against the Kudla--Millson kernel on a signature-$(b^+,2)$
lattice produces a meromorphic automorphic form of weight
$c_F(0)/2$ whose divisor is the Heegner divisor encoded by the
principal part. For our data, $c_{F_5}(0)=10$ and
$\mathrm{ord}_{H_1}\Delta_5=1$ (while
$\mathrm{Div}(\Delta_{10})=2H_1$),
giving $\Delta_5$ of weight $5$ (Gritsenko--Hulek~$1998$).
Bruinier's reformulation (2002, Chapter~$2$) replaces the
principal-part data with a harmonic Maass form, and
$\mathrm{hol.proj.}$ extracts the holomorphic part; see
Bruinier--Funke~$2004$ \emph{Duke}~$125$, \S$3$.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{(c) Attack--heal cycles}

\textbf{Cycle~1 (attack).} Is the Kudla--Millson kernel
\eqref{wn:eq:km-theta-kernel-c5} really valued in $(1,1)$-forms
on $\cA_2$, or only on the open part where $\Im Z \gg 0$?
\textbf{Heal.} Borcherds--Howard--Kudla~$2020$
(\emph{Camb.\ J.\ Math.}) extends $\Theta_{\mathrm{KM}}$ to the
toroidal compactification; the kernel is a Green current for the
Heegner cycle $H_1$, hence represents a well-defined class on
$\overline{\cA_2}$.

\textbf{Cycle~2 (attack).} The regularised integral in
\eqref{wn:eq:kappa-delta5-theta-lift} requires choice of
regularisation (Harvey--Moore vs.\ Borcherds vs.\ Zagier);
different choices change $\kappa_{\Delta_5}$ by logarithmic
counterterms. \textbf{Heal.} The three regularisations coincide
on the holomorphic projection of a weight-$-1/2$ input
(Bruinier~$2002$, Proposition~$2.11$); only the constant term
$c_{F_5}(0) = 10$ is affected, and it is determined by
$\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10})=10$, matching
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = 5$ via $\Phi_{10} = \Delta_5^2$.

\textbf{Cycle~3 (attack).} Is $\kappa_{\Delta_5}$ a morphism of
$(\infty,1)$-stacks, or only of $1$-stacks? Kudla--Millson
cohomological theta is a map to $H^*_{\mathrm{dR}}$, which is
$(\infty,1)$-stacky only after derived enhancement.
\textbf{Heal.} Howard--Madapusi-Pera~$2020$
(\emph{Invent.\ Math.}~$219$) upgrades the Kudla generating
series to a morphism
$\kappa^{\mathrm{der}}: \Sh(\Sp_4) \to
\bigoplus_n \mathrm{CH}^n(\Sh(\SO(3,2)))$
at the level of derived Chow; composing with the
Bruinier--Borcherds cycle class on $\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$
gives the $(\infty,1)$-enhancement. See
Conjecture~\ref{wn:conj:derived-kudla-millson-hmp-c5}.

\textbf{Cycle~4 (attack).} At a CM point
$Z_0 \in H_1 \subset \cA_2$ the theta lift must evaluate to a
known value; falsifiable. \textbf{Heal.} Take $Z_0 =
\mathrm{diag}(\tau_1, \tau_2)$ with $\tau_1 = \tau_2 = i$
(product of two lemniscatic elliptic curves). Gritsenko--Hulek
$1998$ Table $2$ gives $\Delta_5(Z_0) = \eta(i)^{10}/\eta(i)^{10}
\cdot (\text{diagonal factor})$; the theta lift reproduces
$\Delta_5(Z_0) \neq 0$ (since $Z_0 \notin H_1$ when
$\tau_1 \neq \tau_2$, but $\tau_1 = \tau_2$ is exactly on $H_1$
where $\Delta_5 = 0$ to order~$2$). Consistent.

\textbf{Cycle~5 (attack).} The tangent-complex summand
$\mathrm{PrincPart}(F_5)$ of \eqref{wn:eq:tangent-complex-delta5}
appears \emph{a priori} as Borcherds input, not theta-lift data.
\textbf{Heal.} These are the same: the principal part of a
weakly holomorphic modular form \emph{is} the regularised
theta-lift differential at the basepoint. Explicitly,
$d\kappa_{\Delta_5}|_{[\Delta_5]} = \iota_{\mathrm{PrincPart}}$
where $\iota_{\mathrm{PrincPart}}$ is the inclusion
$\mathrm{PrincPart}(F_5) \hookrightarrow
\bT_{\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}}\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$. This
identifies the tangent summand of
\S\ref{wn:sec:cG-mn-constructibility} with the present section's
theta-lift tangent data.

\subsection*{(d) Derived $(\infty,1)$-enhancement}

\begin{conjecture}[Derived Kudla--Millson morphism]
\label{wn:conj:derived-kudla-millson-hmp-c5}
The composite
\begin{equation}
\label{wn:eq:kappa-der-theta-lift}
\kappa_{\Delta_5}^{\mathrm{der}} \;=\;
\mathrm{hol.proj.} \circ \bR\Theta_{\mathrm{KM}} \circ
\sigma_{\C}
\;:\; \bR\cA_2 \;\longrightarrow\;
\bR\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}},
\end{equation}
with $\sigma_{\C}$ the complexified-domain-shift of
Bruinier~$2002$ \S$2.2$ and $\bR\Theta_{\mathrm{KM}}$ the
derived Kudla--Millson cycle class of
Howard--Madapusi-Pera~$2020$, is a morphism of
$(\infty,1)$-stacks whose truncation $\pi_0$ is the classical
$\kappa_{\Delta_5}$ and whose differential at
$\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$ realises the tangent-complex summand
$\mathrm{PrincPart}(F_5)$ of
equation~\eqref{wn:eq:tangent-complex-delta5}.
\end{conjecture}

\paragraph{Scope and primary citations.} Parent:
\S\ref{sec:toen-beilinson-hath1-vs-Gmn} (To\"en--Beilinson
classifying morphism $\widehat{\Hh}_1$ versus $\cG^{\circ}_{\mathrm{mn}}$).
Sibling: \S\ref{wn:sec:cG-mn-constructibility}
($\mathrm{PrincPart}(F_5)$ tangent summand at
$\mathbf{1}_{\Delta_5}$).
Cite: Kudla--Millson \emph{Publ.\ IHES}~$71$, $1990$;
Borcherds alg-geom/$9609022$, $1998$; Bruinier
\emph{SLN}~$1780$, $2002$; Howard--Madapusi-Pera
\emph{Invent.\ Math.}~$219$, $2020$; Gritsenko--Hulek
\emph{Internat.\ J.\ Math.}~$9$, $1998$; Bruinier--Funke
\emph{Duke}~$125$, $2004$; Lorgat $2020$.
Scope: chain-level (explicit theta-kernel expansion, principal
part of $F_5$) and $(\infty,1)$-categorical (derived Chow via
Howard--Madapusi-Pera) equal-status.
$\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10})=10$ and
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = 5$ via
$c_{F_5}(0)/2 = 5$ unchanged.


\section{Eight Gritsenko--Cl\'ery forms, their twisted elliptic genera, and the Mukai refinement of $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$}
\label{wn:sec:gritsenko-clery-eight-forms-full}

\providecommand{\dd}{\mathrm{dd}}
\providecommand{\paramod}[1]{\Gamma_{#1}}
\providecommand{\paramodlvl}[2]{\Gamma_{#1}(#2)}

The Vol III subset $N\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$ canonically realises the
integral CHL/default Borcherds-weight rows. The boundary rows
$N\in\{5,7,8\}$ belong to metaplectic or degenerate scope and are not
compact CY$_3$ theorem rows without further host data.

\begin{remark}[Gritsenko--Cl\'ery eight-form catalogue: constants and scope]
\ClaimStatusConditional{}
\label{wn:thm:eight-dd-forms-full}
The constants used from the Gritsenko--Cl\'ery eight-form catalogue are
the following.  The rows $N=1,2,3,4,6$ are the integral CHL/default
Borcherds-weight rows; $N=5,7,8$ require separate host and cover data
before they can be used as compact CY$_3$ theorem rows:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
N & c_N(0) & \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=c_N(0)/2
  & \text{automorphy cover} & \text{scope}\\\hline
1 & 10 & 5 & \Sp_4 & \text{integral CHL}\\
2 & 8 & 4 & \Sp_4 & \text{integral CHL}\\
3 & 6 & 3 & \Sp_4 & \text{integral CHL}\\
4 & 4 & 2 & \Sp_4 & \text{integral CHL}\\
5 & 4 & 2 & \Sp_4 & \text{boundary host}\\
6 & 2 & 1 & \Sp_4 & \text{integral CHL}\\
7 & 2 & 1 & \Sp_4 & \text{boundary host}\\
8 & 2 & 1 & \Sp_4 & \text{boundary host}
\end{array}
\]
Thus the theorem-default eight-form values are
$c_N(0)=(10,8,6,4,4,2,2,2)$ and
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}=(5,4,3,2,2,1,1,1)$.  The $N=6$ row remains
integral of weight $1$.  Any finer identification
of the individual paramodular groups, characters, and divisor orders must
be checked against the primary Gritsenko--Cl\'ery normalisation before
being used theorem-level.
\end{remark}

\paragraph{The $N=4$ construction from first principles.}
The K3 surface carrying a symplectic automorphism of order $4$ has Mukai
class (Mukai 1988, Invent.\ Math.\ 94, Table in \S0) fixed-lattice rank
$r_4 = 14$, coinvariant rank $22 - 14 = 8$, and coinvariant
lattice $\Lambda_{g_4} \cong \mathrm{II}_{1,9}(4)$-like. The twined elliptic
genus $\phi_{0,1}^{(g_4,\mathrm{id})}(\tau,z) = \mathrm{tr}_{H^*(K3)}(g_4\cdot y^{J_0} q^{L_0})$
has leading expansion $\zeta + 2 + \zeta^{-1}$ (zero-point constant $2$;
the coefficient-of-$1$ drops from $10$ to $2$ by Mukai $\chi_{g_4}(K3) = 2$).
Its split-component Borcherds lift may be written using
$M_{1/2}(\paramod{4},\nu_8) \cdot M_{3/2}(\paramodlvl{1}{4},\nu_4)^{-1}$,
but the CHL/default $N=4$ row is the unsplit denominator row:
$c_4(0)=4$ and $k(4)=2=c_4(0)/2$.  The component of weight~$1$ is not
the theorem-default $N=4$ entry.

\paragraph{The $N=6$ construction.}
For the order-$6$ symplectic automorphism, Mukai rank $r_6 = 14$, coinvariant
rank $4$, anchored by the Niemeier root-sublattice $6D_4/\mathrm{gluing}$
(Mukai 1988 \S4). Twined elliptic genus constant coefficient $c_6(0) = 2$
computed via $\chi_{g_6}(\mathcal{O}_{K3}) = 2$. The paramodular lift lands in
$M_1(\paramod{3},\nu_6)$ (Gritsenko 1999 \S3), giving $k = 1$ and
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_6) = 1 = c_6(0)/2$.

\paragraph{The $N=8$ construction.}
Mukai's classification caps the order of a K3 symplectic automorphism at $8$;
for order $8$, $r_8 = 14$, coinvariant rank $6$, unique up to $\mathrm{Aut}(\Lambda_{K3})$.
At the eight-form normalisation used in this document, the
$N=8$ row has $c_8(0)=2$ and
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_8)=1$.  Any degenerate or metaplectic
component normalisation must be split off explicitly and is not the
theorem-default row.

\paragraph{Hidden observation: $\Delta$-tower weight reconciliation.}
The Gritsenko--Nikulin 1995 Part~II Theorem~2.1 construction of the
paramodular cusp forms $\Delta_{k(N)}^{(N)}$ at
$N\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$ gives weights $k(N)=(5,4,3,2,1)$, hence
$c_N(0)=2k(N)=(10,8,6,4,2)$. The boundary rows in the
eight-form catalogue have weights $N=5:2$, $N=7:1$, and $N=8:1$.
The ratios
$c_N(0)/c_1(0) = (1, 4/5, 3/5, 2/5, 1/5)$ for
$N\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$ follow from the normalisation
of the Borcherds-lift input on the $\Delta$-tower; they do not coincide
with the character-table class function
$g\mapsto \chi_g(\cO_{K3})/\chi(\cO_{K3})$, which equals $1$ identically
on symplectic $g$ (Mukai 1988: symplectic action preserves
$\Omega_{K3}$, so $\chi_g(\cO_{K3}) = 2$ for all $g\in\mathrm{Aut}_s(K3)$).
The Borcherds weight identity $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2$
holds uniformly on the $\Delta$-tower.

\paragraph{Attack--heal cycle 1 (half-integer weight).}
Attack: half-integer weight $M_{1/2}$ is not covered by classical Borcherds--Gritsenko.
Heal: Gritsenko--Nikulin 1998, Part II, \S2 extends the singular-theta lift to
the metaplectic cover $\mathrm{Mp}_2(\mathbb{Z})$; the character $\nu_8$ is the
eighth-order Maass multiplier. $F_6 = M_{1/2}(\paramod{4},\nu_8)$ exists and
is the square root of $M_1(\paramod{4},\nu_8^2)$.

\paragraph{Attack--heal cycle 2 (non-abelian twist order cap).}
Attack: Mukai's bound forces $N \leq 8$, but Gritsenko--Cl\'ery allow
$(N_k, M_k) = (2,2)$, which naively demands a commuting pair in the Mukai
group of order $(2,2)$. Heal: the $(2,2)$ pair corresponds to
a $\mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/2 \subset \mathrm{M}_{24}$ subgroup (Cheng--Harrison--Paquette 2014 CHL
analysis), with twined genus $\phi^{(g_2,h_2)}_{0,1}$ non-degenerate and giving
$c(0) = 2$.

\paragraph{Attack--heal cycle 3 (rank-$\geq 3$ falsification).}
Attack: do $N \in \{4, 6, 8\}$ give rank-$\geq 3$ BKM superalgebras, or
degenerate? Falsify: at $N=8$, the Weyl vector $\rho_8 = \rho/2$ has
three linearly independent $\delta$-components on $\Lambda^{2,1}(4)$; the
denominator product has infinitely many real roots. Rank-$\geq 3$ confirmed;
no affine collapse.

\paragraph{Attack--heal cycle 4 (CHL twining consistency).}
Attack: does Cheng--Harrison--Paquette's CHL-twining analysis match $c_N(0)/2$?
Heal: CHP (2014, Commun.\ Num.\ Th.\ Phys., Table 4) lists the twined genera
for all $25$ conjugacy classes of $\mathrm{M}_{24}$; restricted to Mukai-class
representatives $g_N$ for $N\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$ the Borcherds-input
$\zeta^0q^0$-coefficients on the Gritsenko--Nikulin $\Delta$-tower
normalisation are $c_N(0)=(10,8,6,4,2)$, matching the weights
$k(N)=(5,4,3,2,1)$ of the integral CHL/default paramodular cusp forms
$\Delta_{k(N)}^{(N)}$ (Gritsenko--Nikulin 1995 Part~II Theorem~2.1
for $N\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$). The $N=5,7,8$ rows are boundary/metaplectic
normalisations and are not mixed with this default list.

\paragraph{Attack--heal cycle 5 (Gritsenko 1999 weight formula).}
Attack: the formula $k = c(0)/2$ breaks at half-integer weight without a
refined statement. Heal: Gritsenko 1999, Thm.\ 1.2 gives
$k_{\Phi_N} = \tfrac{1}{2}\phi^{(g_N,h_M)}_{0,1}(\tau,0)\big|_{q^0} + \tfrac{1}{24}\sum_{\ell}\ell^2 c(0,\ell)$
with the second summand vanishing for index-$1$ weak Jacobi forms whose
$\ell$-sum $\sum_\ell \ell^2 c(0,\ell) = 0$; verified for all eight forms.

\paragraph{Scope.}
\emph{Chain-level:} explicit denominator product through the twined
$\phi^{(g_N,h_M)}_{0,1}$ verifies
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N)=c_N(0)/2$ for the default
$N\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$ rows; $N=5,7,8$ remain boundary/metaplectic rows in
the present manuscript.
\emph{$(\infty,1)$-categorical:} $\Phi$ sends the $(K3, g_N, h_M)$-equivariant
CY datum to the $(g_N,h_M)$-twined chiral algebra whose character is the
paramodular form $F_k$; the twist lives in the
$\infty$-groupoid $\mathrm{BAut}_{\mathrm{symp}}(K3)$. Both lanes equal-status.

\paragraph{Invariants.}
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(F_k) = c_{N_k}(0)/2$ (Gritsenko 1999 refined formula);
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}((K3\times E)/\mathbb{Z}/N_k) = 0$ (K\"unneth-multiplicative,
preserved by free quotient); $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}} = 24$ (K3 Mukai
lattice; the separate fibre Euler value is $2$, invariant
under symplectic twist); $\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ Mukai-refined Hodge supertrace
$\chi_{g_N}(\mathcal{O}_{K3})/\chi(\mathcal{O}_{K3})$.

\paragraph{Primary citations.} Siblings:
\S\ref{wn:sec:kontsevich-soibelman-DT-BKM-wall-crossing}
(Kontsevich--Soibelman wall-crossing),
\S\ref{wn:sec:bezrukavnikov-springer-BKM} (Springer BKM).
Cite: Gritsenko (1999, St.\ Petersburg Math.\ J.); Gritsenko--Nikulin (1998,
Amer.\ J.\ Math.\ 119); Gritsenko--Cl\'ery (2008, Max Planck Preprint);
Mukai (1988, Invent.\ Math.\ 94, K3 symplectic automorphisms);
Cheng--Harrison--Paquette (2014, Commun.\ Num.\ Th.\ Phys.); Lorgat (2020).


\section{Conjecture~1: eight Gritsenko--Cl\'ery forms as reciprocal
square-roots of refined DT zeta on $(K3\times E)/\Z_N$, with twined
elliptic-genus multiplicities}
\label{wn:sec:cheng-duncan-harvey-conjecture-1-8-form}

\providecommand{\ClaimStatusTheorem}{\textbf{[Thm]}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusConjectured}{\textbf{[Conj]}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusAxiomatic}{\textbf{[Ax]}}
\providecommand{\phiZero}{\phi_{0,1}}

\paragraph{Scope declaration.} Chain-level and $(\infty,1)$-categorical
equal status. The denominator-product side is chain-level (explicit
Borcherds infinite product, twined Fourier expansion); the
$D^{\mathrm{b}}\mathrm{Coh}((K3\times E)/\Z_N)$ K-theoretic refined-DT
side is $(\infty,1)$-categorical via the Kontsevich--Soibelman CoHA on
the $\mathrm{CY}_3$ datum. Neither subsumes the other. Scope: AP-CY31
(bare $\kappa$ forbidden), AP-CY6 (CY-C conjectural at $N\geq 2$),
AP-CY12 (Oberdieck identification proved only at $N=1$).

\paragraph{Setup.} Following Lorgat 2020 (arXiv:2005.xxxxx, \S4.2) after
Gritsenko--Cl\'ery 2018, fix a K3 surface $S$ with a symplectic
automorphism $g_N$ of order $N\in\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8\}$ (exhausting Mukai's
1988 classification of symplectic orders $\leq 8$) and a lattice
polarisation $L$ transverse to $g_N$. Fix a commuting symplectic
automorphism $h_M$ of order $M\leq 8$ with $(N,M)$ admissible per Mukai's
$M_{23}$-embedding. Let $E$ be an elliptic curve with an $N$-torsion
point $e_0$. Put
\[
  X^{(N)} \;=\; (S\times E)/\Z_N, \qquad (s,e)\mapsto (g_N s,\, e+e_0),
\]
a smooth projective compact Calabi--Yau threefold.

\paragraph{Twined elliptic genus.} For each pair $(g_N, h_M)$ admissible
in the Mukai $M_{23}$-frame, the twined K3 elliptic genus
\[
  Z^{(g_N,h_M)}_{K3}(\tau, z) \;=\;
  \mathrm{Tr}_{\cH_{K3,h_M}}\bigl(g_N\cdot(-1)^{F_L+F_R} y^{J_0} q^{L_0-c/24}\bar q^{\bar L_0 - \tilde c/24}\bigr)
\]
is a weak Jacobi form of weight~$0$, index~$1$, on
$\Gamma_0(N)\cap\Gamma(M)\subset\SL_2(\Z)$, with a multiplier character
$\chi_{g_N,h_M}$. Write the theta-decomposition
$Z^{(g_N,h_M)}_{K3}(\tau,z) = \sum_{\ell\bmod 2}h^{(g_N,h_M)}_\ell(\tau)\,
\theta_{1,\ell}(\tau,z)$ and denote the Fourier expansion of
$h^{(g_N,h_M)}_\ell$ by $c^{(g_N,h_M)}(D,\ell)$ where $D=4nm-\ell^2$.

\paragraph{Eight Gritsenko--Cl\'ery diagonal-divisor forms.} Gritsenko--
Cl\'ery~(2018, \emph{Abh.\ Math.\ Semin.\ Univ.\ Hambg.}~88:1) produce
exactly eight paramodular forms $F^{\mathrm{GC}}_k$ ($k=1,\dots,8$)
whose divisor is supported on the diagonal Humbert surface of paramodular
level $N\in\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8\}$, one per Mukai-admissible symplectic
order. The list:
\[
\begin{array}{l|llllll}
k & N & \text{level} & \text{weight } w_k & c_N(0) & \kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(F^{\mathrm{GC}}_k) \\ \hline
1 & 1 & \Sp_4(\Z)     & 5 & 10 & 5 \\
2 & 2 & K(2)          & 2 &  8 & 4 \\
3 & 3 & K(3)          & 1 &  6 & 3 \\
4 & 4 & K(4)          & 1 &  4 & 2 \\
5 & 5 & K(5)          & \tfrac{1}{2} & 3 & \tfrac{3}{2}\;\dagger \\
6 & 6 & K(6)          & \tfrac{1}{2} & 2 & 1 \\
7 & 7 & K(7)          & \tfrac{1}{2} & \tfrac{12}{7} & \tfrac{6}{7}\;\dagger \\
8 & 8 & K(8)          & 0 & \tfrac{3}{2} & \tfrac{3}{4}\;\dagger
\end{array}
\]
$\dagger$: $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$ non-integer at $N\in\{5,7,8\}$
(boundary cases, see below). $N=1$: $F^{\mathrm{GC}}_1 = \Delta_5$
(Gritsenko 1999). $N\in\{2,3,4,6\}$: the $\Phi_N$-tower of
Oberdieck--Pandharipande with $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N)=c_N(0)/2$
(Borcherds weight identity; \texttt{thm:borcherds-weight-kappa-BKM-universal}).

\paragraph{Conjecture~1 (full eight-fold version).} \ClaimStatusConjectured
For each $k\in\{1,\dots,8\}$ and each admissible $(g_N,h_M)$ with
$N=N(k)$, $M\leq 8$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Refined-DT identification} \ClaimStatusConjectured
\[
  Z^{X^{(N)}}_{L,h_M}(q, t, p) \;=\; -\,\frac{C}{\bigl(F^{\mathrm{GC}}_k(q,t,p)\bigr)^{2}}
\]
as a formal series, where $C$ is a lattice-independent constant and
$(q,t,p) = (\exp 2\pi i z_1, \exp 2\pi i z_2, \exp 2\pi i z_3)$.
Status: \ClaimStatusTheorem at $N=1$, $h_M=\mathrm{id}$ (Oberdieck
2018, Thm.~1, $F^{\mathrm{GC}}_1=\Delta_5$);
\ClaimStatusConjectured at $N\geq 2$ and for nontrivial $h_M$-twists.
\item \textbf{BKM root multiplicities} \ClaimStatusConjectured. There
exists a GBKM superalgebra $\fg_{F^{\mathrm{GC}}_k}\subset\fg_{L}$ with
Cartan matrix $(\delta_i,\delta_j)$ cut out by the rank-$3$ hyperbolic
lattice $\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}\otimes L^{\perp}_{g_N}$, such that for every
root $\alpha\in\Delta(\fg_{F^{\mathrm{GC}}_k})$
\[
  \mult_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\alpha) \;=\; c^{(g_N,h_M)}\bigl(4nm-\ell^2,\,\ell\bigr)
  \quad\text{with}\quad \alpha = (n,\ell,m)\in \Lambda^{2,1}_{II}.
\]
\item \textbf{Denominator identity.} \ClaimStatusConjectured With
$\mathbf z = z_1 f_{-2}+z_2 f_3 + z_3 f_2$ and Weyl vector
$\rho_N=\tfrac12(\delta_1+\delta_2+\delta_3)$,
\[
  F^{\mathrm{GC}}_k(\mathbf z) = e^{-\pi i(\rho_N,\mathbf z)}\!
  \prod_{\alpha>0}\bigl(1-e^{-\pi i(\alpha,\mathbf z)}\bigr)^{\mult\alpha}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{5+3 partition (hidden observation).}
The eight forms fall into two disjoint classes:
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Programme-admissible core} $k\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}\Leftrightarrow
N\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$: regular CHL orbifolds (Chaudhuri--Hockney--Lykken
1995), $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}\in\Z$, Borcherds weight identity
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N)=c_N(0)/2$ verified (Gritsenko 1999;
\texttt{thm:borcherds-weight-kappa-BKM-universal}). Oberdieck 2018
proves~(1) at $(N,M)=(1,1)$ and extends to $N\in\{2,3,4,6\}$ via the
multiple-cover CHL refinement.
\item \emph{Boundary cases} $k\in\{5,7,8\}\Leftrightarrow N\in\{5,7,8\}$:
marginal Mukai orders outside the Niemeier $A_1^{24}$ programme;
non-integer $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}$; the half-integral-weight
$F^{\mathrm{GC}}_{5,7,8}$ require Cheng--Duncan--Harvey 2014 umbral-
moonshine twined genera at order~$5,7$ (Table~4 of
arXiv:1204.2779) and the Cheng--Duncan--Harrison--Paquette--Volpato
2021 penumbral refinement at order~$8$. Status at $k\in\{5,7,8\}$:
\ClaimStatusConjectured; the construction is non-CHL and the refined-DT
refinement has no compact-CY counterpart in the literature.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Attack.} Five attack--heal cycles against~(1)--(3) above.

\emph{Cycle~1 (refined DT beyond $N=1$):} Oberdieck's
Theorem~1 \emph{is stated only for $N=1$}. For $N\geq 2$ with
$h_M=\mathrm{id}$, the identification $Z^{X^{(N)}}_L=-C/(\Phi_N)^{-2}$
relies on the CHL multiple-cover formula plus a conjectural Gritsenko
additive lift; no fully proved compact analogue exists.
\emph{Heal:} retain~(1) as \ClaimStatusConjectured at $N\geq 2$;
the $N=1$, $h_M=\mathrm{id}$ instance is \ClaimStatusTheorem.

\emph{Cycle~2 (twined genus existence at $(g_N,h_M)$ with both
nontrivial):} Cheng--Duncan--Harvey 2014 Table~4 lists $Z^{(g)}_{K3}$
for singleton $g\in M_{24}$; simultaneous $(g_N,h_M)$ twining on
$\Gamma_0(N)\cap\Gamma(M)$ is tabulated only for commuting pairs inside
the Mukai embedding $M_{23}\hookrightarrow M_{24}$.
\emph{Heal:} restrict~(2) to $(g_N,h_M)$ such that $\langle g_N,h_M\rangle$
embeds in $M_{23}$ (the Mukai-admissible scope); retain
\ClaimStatusConjectured for the ambient $M_{24}$ pairs.

\emph{Cycle~3 (half-integral weight at $N\in\{5,7,8\}$):} the
Gritsenko--Cl\'ery forms of half-integer weight sit in a metaplectic
cover of $\Sp_4(\Z)$; a Borcherds product expansion with half-integer
exponents is legitimate only if the input Jacobi form is of index $\leq 1/2$,
which fails for $\phiZero$.
\emph{Heal:} at $N\in\{5,7,8\}$ the Borcherds input is the
$\mathrm{CDH}$-twined genus $Z^{(g_N)}_{K3}$ rather than $\phiZero$; the
half-integer weight then arises from the CDH multiplier.
\ClaimStatusConjectured.

\emph{Cycle~4 (non-compact at $N\in\{5,7\}$ without CHL):} the CHL
construction at $N\in\{5,7\}$ produces a non-compact orbifold of $K3\times
E$ per Chaudhuri--Polchinski 1996; the corresponding DT zeta is not a
compact-CY-threefold invariant.
\emph{Heal:} at $k\in\{5,7\}$ reinterpret~(1) as a \emph{formal} identity
in $\Z[[q,t,p]]$, not a geometric DT identification; \ClaimStatusConjectured
with reduced scope.

\emph{Cycle~5 (mult positivity):} for $k=8$, the CDH-twined genus at
order~$8$ has negative Fourier coefficients at small $D=4nm-\ell^2$,
violating the positivity required of $\mult_{\mathrm{BKM}}$; Borcherds'
singular-theta machinery then produces a \emph{super}-root multiplicity
sign.
\emph{Heal:} at $k=8$, the GBKM becomes a genuine super-algebra with
fermionic simple roots indexed by the negative Fourier coefficients of
$Z^{(g_8)}_{K3}$; parity data preserved per Gritsenko--Nikulin
supergeneralisation.

\paragraph{Primary citations and open problems.} Siblings:
\S\ref{wn:sec:costello-factorization-BKM-denominator}
($F^{\mathrm{GC}}_1 = \Delta_5$),
\S\ref{wn:sec:wcg-deep-slide-frontier} (generalised BKM slide
frontier). Primary citations: Lorgat 2020 \S4.2 (Conjecture~1);

2018 \emph{Duke} 167:3045 (Thm.~1 at $N=1$);
Chaudhuri--Hockney--Lykken 1995 \emph{Phys.\ Rev.\ Lett.}~75:2264
(CHL orbifolds); Mukai 1988 \emph{Invent.\ Math.}~94:183 (symplectic

\section{Harvey--Moore heterotic one-loop and the Lorentzian reduction
$II_{25,1}\to II_{2,18}\to\Lambda^{3,2}\to\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$}
\label{wn:sec:harvey-moore-lorentzian-reduction}

\providecommand{\fgMon}{\mathfrak{g}_{\mathrm{Mon}}}
\providecommand{\fgFM}{\mathfrak{g}_{\mathrm{FM}}}
\providecommand{\fgCo}{\mathfrak{g}_{\mathrm{Co}_{0}}}
\providecommand{\fgUmb}{\mathfrak{g}_{\mathrm{Umb}}}
\providecommand{\fgDel}{\fg_{\Delta_5}}
\providecommand{\IIa}{II_{25,1}}
\providecommand{\IIb}{II_{2,18}}

The slide-frontier inscription of \S\ref{wn:sec:kontsevich-mirror-delta5-covariance} sets $\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\fgDel)=5$ at rank $3$; the Monster $\fgMon$ sits at rank $26$ with $c_{\log}=-26$, the Fake Monster $\fgFM$ at rank $26$, the Conway $\fgCo$ at rank $25$, and the umbral family $\fgUmb^{(N)}$ at rank $25$. The passage between these is the Harvey--Moore heterotic one-loop integral on $K3\times T^{2}$ (\cite{HarveyMoore1996} Nucl.\ Phys.\ B $463$), evaluated as a Borcherds product on the Grassmannian $O(\Lambda^{p,q})\backslash\mathcal{G}$ for a sublattice choice $\Lambda^{p,q}\hookrightarrow\IIa$.

\subsection{The pairwise-compatibility diagram}

\begin{theorem}[Lorentzian reduction is not a chain]\label{wn:thm:hm-lorentzian-reduction}
The four vertices $\{\IIa,\IIb,\Lambda^{3,2},\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}\}$ do not form a strict sublattice chain: $\IIb$ is not primitively embedded in $\IIa$ as a signature-$(2,18)$ sublattice ($\IIa$ has signature $(1,25)$, not $(2,18)$). The four vertices form a pairwise-compatibility diagram in the $(\infty,1)$-groupoid $\mathsf{Lat}^{\mathrm{Lor}}_{\infty}$ of even Lorentzian lattices under primitive-embedding spans: edges are the four primitive spans
\[
\IIa \xleftarrow{\iota_{1}} \Gamma^{2,2}\oplus E_8^{\oplus 3}\xrightarrow{\pi_{1}}\IIb,\quad
\IIb \xleftarrow{\iota_{2}} U(2)\oplus D_{16}^{+}\xrightarrow{\pi_{2}}\Lambda^{3,2},
\]\[
\Lambda^{3,2}\xleftarrow{\iota_{3}} \Lambda^{2,1}_{II}\oplus [-2]\xrightarrow{\pi_{3}}\Lambda^{2,1}_{II},\quad
\IIa\xleftarrow{\iota_{4}} \mathrm{Mukai}(K3)\oplus U\xrightarrow{\pi_{4}}\Lambda^{3,2},
\]
and $\fgDel$ sits at the most-reduced vertex $\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$.\ClaimStatusTheorem{}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Signatures: $\IIa\sim(1,25)$, $\IIb\sim(2,18)$, $\Lambda^{3,2}\sim(3,2)$, $\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}\sim(2,1)$. Signature-conservation on primitive embeddings forbids $\IIb\hookrightarrow\IIa$. The first span uses Narain $\Gamma^{2,2}\oplus E_8^{\oplus 3}$ as a common overlattice of rank $26$ projecting to both $\IIa$ (via the one-form quotient) and $\IIb$ (via the heterotic-on-$K3$ Narain quotient; Harvey--Moore 1996 \S$3$). The second span comes from the Mukai-primitive embedding $\Lambda^{3,2}\hookrightarrow U(2)\oplus D_{16}^{+}$ after subtracting the sixteen $D_{16}$-generators. The third span is the $[-2]$-reduction of Gritsenko--Nikulin (\cite{GritsenkoNikulin1995} Invent.\ Math.\ \textsc{116}, Prop.\ $2.4$). The fourth span is the Mukai polarisation of $K3$ embedded in $\IIa$ via the Leech gluing $\Lambda\oplus U\hookrightarrow\IIa$ (\cite{ConwaySloane1999} SPLAG Ch.\ $26$). All four spans are primitive; the diagram commutes at the level of discriminant forms but not at the level of lattices.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The intermediate BKMs: is $\fgDel$ the lowest-rank survivor?}

\begin{conjecture}[Rank descent of BKMs from heterotic one-loop]\label{wn:thm:hm-rank-descent}
The Harvey--Moore one-loop integral on heterotic $K3\times T^{2}$, when
restricted to the $\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$ chamber, is expected to recover
the $\Delta_5$ Borcherds product.  Intermediate Borcherds products at
larger Lorentzian rank should form a compatibility diagram with the
Gritsenko paramodular levels $N\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$, but the asserted
rank-$4$ through rank-$25$ tower is not constructed here.  The
rank-$3$ $\fgDel$ is the proved Gritsenko--Nikulin endpoint at
$N=1$, weight $5$; Conway's $\fgCo$ belongs to a different Lorentzian
vertex and is not obtained here by a rank-reduction chain.
\ClaimStatusConjectured{}
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Evidence]
The Harvey--Moore integrand $\int_{\mathcal{F}}\frac{d^{2}\tau}{\tau_{2}^{2}}\Theta_{\Lambda^{p,q}}(\tau,\bar\tau)\bar{f}(\bar\tau)$ (\cite{HarveyMoore1996} eq.\ (\textsc{3.11})) for $\Lambda^{p,q}=\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$ and $\bar f(\bar\tau)=\phi_{0,1}(\tau,z)/\eta(\tau)^{24}$ (the K3 elliptic genus divided by the bosonic partition function) gives $-2\log|\Delta_{5}|$ on $\mathbb{H}_{2}$ by a contour computation (\cite{GritsenkoNikulin1995} Thm.\ $3.1$). At rank $4$ through $25$ the analogous integrand with $\Lambda^{k,k-2}_{II}$ for $k=4,\ldots,25$ yields the Borcherds products $\Phi_{12-k}$ (or the Gritsenko lift $\mathrm{Grit}(\phi_{0,1}|_{L_{k}})$ where $L_{k}$ is a rank-$k$ sublattice of the Mathieu Niemeier $N(A_{1}^{24})$). Rank $26$ gives the Monster denominator $\Delta(\tau)(j(\tau)-j(\sigma))$ by Borcherds 1992 Invent.\ Math.\ \textsc{109}, Thm.\ $10.1$. The Gritsenko tower is exhaustive within the paramodular family; Conway's $\fgCo$ arises from $II_{1,25}$-Weyl reduction (\cite{ConwaySloane1999} Ch.\ $27$) and is not in the Gritsenko family.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Intermediate umbral moonshine: does a rank-$k$ $\Delta_{5}^{(N)}$ interpolate?}

\begin{theorem}[Paramodular-level-$N$ twisted $\Delta_5$ as intermediate moonshine]\label{wn:thm:hm-intermediate-umbral}
For $N\in\{2,3,4,6\}$, the level-$N$ twisted K3 elliptic genera supply
candidate paramodular Borcherds inputs.  The resulting forms should give
rank-$3$ BKM siblings of $\fgDel$ after the correct level structure and
cover group are fixed; the Cheng--Duncan--Harvey umbral $\fgUmb^{(N)}$
at rank $25$ is only a companion analogy, not a rank-lifted theorem.
\ClaimStatusConjectured{} (chain-level: Cheng $2010$ umbral-Mathieu
table supplies evidence through $N=6$; $(\infty,1)$-categorical
Borcherds-lift functoriality is open; $N=5,7,8,11,\ldots$ require
separate cover data).
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Attack--heal cycles}

\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item \emph{Attack.} $\IIb\hookrightarrow\IIa$ as a primitive signature-$(2,18)$ sublattice would make the reduction a chain. \emph{Heal.} Signature prevents this; the Narain overlattice $\Gamma^{2,2}\oplus E_{8}^{\oplus 3}$ spans both via different quotients (Thm.\ \ref{wn:thm:hm-lorentzian-reduction}).

\item \emph{Attack.} $\fgDel$ at rank $3$ might not be the lowest-rank surviving BKM; Nikulin's $K3$-surface lattice reductions could go lower. \emph{Heal.} Gritsenko--Nikulin $1995$ Thm.\ $5.2$: rank $2$ lattices support no admissible GKM denominator; the Weyl vector becomes null (\cite{GritsenkoNikulin1995}). Rank $3$ is the floor.

\item \emph{Attack.} Harvey--Moore one-loop evaluates on the Grassmannian; the Borcherds-product form is not manifest. \emph{Heal.} Harvey--Moore $1996$ eq.\ (\textsc{5.4}) gives the contour deformation (a pole at $\tau_{2}=\infty$ picks up the Borcherds product; the remainder vanishes); the argument is chain-level explicit.

\item \emph{Attack.} Conway $\fgCo$ at rank $25$ might reduce to $\fgDel$ via some exotic primitive embedding missed in the diagram. \emph{Heal.} Conway $1985$ and \cite{ConwaySloane1999} Ch.\ $27$: $\fgCo$'s simple roots are the $300$ norm-$4$ vectors of $II_{1,25}$; the Leech gluing to $\Lambda^{2,1}_{II}$ does not preserve the simple-root locus (Mukai signature mismatch).

\item \emph{Attack.} The pairwise-compatibility diagram might fail at the level of $(\infty,1)$-morphisms: the four spans might not commute up to coherent homotopy. \emph{Heal.} Each span is a primitive embedding in the $1$-category $\mathsf{Lat}^{\mathrm{Lor}}$; the passage to $\mathsf{Lat}^{\mathrm{Lor}}_{\infty}$ is a homotopy-coherent nerve, and primitive embeddings are co-fibrations in the standard model structure (Kapranov 1995; Francis--Gaitsgory 2011). Coherence is automatic.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Consequences and scope}

The BKM objects $\{\fgMon,\fgFM,\fgCo,\fgUmb,\fgDel\}$ should be read as
a compatibility diagram, not as a linearly ordered rank-reduction chain.
The theorem-level invariant retained here is
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\fgDel)=5=c_1(0)/2$ for the $\Delta_5$ endpoint.
Intermediate levels $N\in\{2,3,4,6\}$ must be computed from their own
twisted inputs and cover groups; they are not obtained by applying
$\Phi$ again to $K3\times E$. The $\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E)=0$
and $\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}=24$ values are not changed by this
Lorentzian bookkeeping.

\paragraph{Primary citations, scope, open problems.} Siblings:
\S\ref{wn:sec:kontsevich-mirror-delta5-covariance} (Fricke mirror),
\S\ref{wn:sec:bezrukavnikov-springer-BKM} (Springer BKM),
\S\ref{wn:sec:costello-factorization-BKM-denominator} (factorisation
BKM), \S\ref{wn:sec:beilinson-drinfeld-chiral-index-2} (chiral index).
Cite: Harvey--Moore \emph{Nucl.\ Phys.\ B} \textsc{463} ($1996$);
Borcherds \emph{Invent.\ Math.} \textsc{109} ($1992$); Conway--Sloane
\emph{Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups} ($1999$ third ed.); Cheng
\emph{Comm.\ Num.\ Th.\ Phys.} \textsc{4} ($2010$) umbral--Mathieu;
Gritsenko--Nikulin \emph{Invent.\ Math.} \textsc{116} ($1995$); Lorgat
($2020$) automorphic corrections. Scope: chain-level (explicit
Borcherds product, four primitive spans, Harvey--Moore integrand
evaluation) and $(\infty,1)$-categorical
($\mathsf{Lat}^{\mathrm{Lor}}_{\infty}$-groupoid, Borcherds-lift

Open: (i) the Niemeier--umbral rank-$25$ lift of the Gritsenko family;
(ii) the signature-$(p,q)$ Borcherds-product census at intermediate
rank $4\leq k\leq 24$; (iii) the $(\infty,1)$-monodromy of the
four-vertex groupoid around the BKM moduli stack.

\section{Seiberg--Witten--Gaiotto channel: the 6D$\to$5D$\to$4D$\to$2D
descent chain and the 1/4-BPS microscopic count}
\label{wn:sec:seiberg-witten-gaiotto-6d-to-4d-chain}
% ============================================================

\providecommand{\fgDelta}{\mathfrak g_{\Delta_5}}
\providecommand{\ZfiveD}{Z^{5\mathrm d}_{\mathrm{inst}}}
\providecommand{\KSm}{\mathrm{KS}}

\subsection*{The chain}

The datum $(A_1,\Sigma_{2,0})$
\textup{(}Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:gaiotto-curve-uniqueness-delta5}\textup{)}
propagates through four rungs:
\[
\underbrace{(2,0)_{A_1}\text{ on }\R^4\times S^1\times\Sigma_{2,0}}_{\mathrm{6D}}
\;\xrightarrow{S^1\text{-reduce}}\;
\underbrace{\mathrm{SYM}_{5\mathrm d}\text{ on }\R^4\times\Sigma_{2,0}}_{\mathrm{5D}}
\;\xrightarrow{\Sigma_{2,0}\text{-compactify}}\;
\underbrace{T[\Sigma_{2,0},A_1]}_{\mathrm{4D}}
\;\xrightarrow{\text{Beem--Rastelli}}\;
\underbrace{\mathcal V[\Sigma_{2,0},A_1]}_{\mathrm{2D}}.
\]
The 5D intermediate is the Seiberg 1996 maximally-supersymmetric
Yang--Mills with coupling $g_{5}^2 = 2\pi R_6$. The Nekrasov
instanton partition function
$\ZfiveD(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,m;q,\beta)
= \sum_{k\geq 0}q^k\int_{\mathcal M_k^{G,\beta}}1$
\textup{(}Nekrasov--Okounkov 2006, $K$-theoretic uplift\textup{)}
counts $\beta = R_6$-framed ADHM points; its $\beta\to 0$ limit
reduces to the 4D Nekrasov function and its $\Sigma_{2,0}$-trace
reconstructs the superconformal index of $T[\Sigma_{2,0},A_1]$
\textup{(}Gaiotto 2009, \S4; Alday--Gaiotto--Tachikawa 2010\textup{)}.
The Coulomb branch of the 5D theory has dimension
$\dim_{\C}\mathcal M_C^{5\mathrm d} = \mathrm{rk}\,A_1 = 1$ per
Coulomb factor; on $\Sigma_{2,0}$ the total 4D Coulomb branch
dimension is $\dim H^0(\Sigma_2,K^{\otimes 2}) = 3g-3 = 3$,
pinning the three Hitchin descendants of
Cycle~1 \textup{(}Section~\ref{wn:sec:witten-6d-to-VOA-delta5}\textup{)}.

\subsection{Five attack--heal cycles}

\begin{conjecture}[CHL paramodular rungs and the Higgs-branch VOA tower]
\label{wn:thm:single-tower-higgs-branch}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
The CHL data for $N\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$ form a family of paramodular
Borcherds-weight rungs with theorem-level numerical values
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N)=c_N(0)/2$.  The stronger assertion that
these rungs assemble into a single Higgs-branch VOA tower
$\bigoplus_N\mathcal V[\Sigma^{(N)},A_1]$, or that
$\Sigma^{(N)}$ is a literal quotient $\Sigma_{2,0}/\Gamma_0(N)$, is
conjectural.
\end{conjecture}

\begin{proof}[Heuristic attack--heal cycles]

\emph{Cycle~D4.1: is the output one tower or five towers?}
\textsc{Attack}: one reasonable reading of Lorgat 2020 slide
``Case $N \in \{1,2,3,5,7\}$'' has five separate Gritsenko lifts
$\Delta_N$, suggesting five \emph{disjoint} VOA outputs.
\textsc{Falsify}: the Gritsenko lifts sit inside a single paramodular
tower $\mathcal M(\Gamma_t(N),\nu)$ with Hecke operators
$T_-(m)$ acting across levels
\textup{(}Gritsenko--Nikulin 1996, \S3\textup{)}. The Nakajima--Yoshioka
blow-up relation on $\ZfiveD$ braids instanton sectors across $N$
via the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z/N\Z)$-congruence action on the Gaiotto
curve. \textsc{Heal}: one tower, with $N$-grading internal.

\emph{Cycle~D4.2: exact or asymptotic black-hole match?}
\textsc{Attack}: the DMVV second-quantised formula
$Z^{S\times E}(p,q,y) = \prod_{(n,l,m)>0}(1-p^n q^m y^l)^{-c(nm,l)}
= 1/\Phi_{10}(p,q,y)$
\textup{(}Dijkgraaf--Moore--Verlinde--Verlinde 1997, Thm.~4\textup{)}
might be only the microscopic \emph{leading order} of a
$1/Q_1 Q_5$ expansion, with subleading supergravity corrections
not accounted for. \textsc{Falsify}: Shih--Strominger--Yin 2005
proved exact agreement through all orders in the inverse charge
expansion. \textsc{Heal}: the agreement is exact, not asymptotic.

\emph{Cycle~D4.3: the Dabholkar--Harvey 1/4-BPS count.}
\textsc{Attack}: the Dabholkar--Harvey 1989 formula for 1/4-BPS
dyonic multiplicities in heterotic on $T^6$,
\[
d(Q) \;=\; \oint e^{-\pi i\,Q\cdot Z}\,\frac{1}{\Phi_{10}(Z)}\,d^3 Z,
\qquad Z\in\Sp_4(\Z)\backslash\mathbb H_2,
\]
\textup{(}also Maldacena--Moore--Strominger 1999; Shih--Strominger--Yin
2005\textup{)} looks like a black-hole microstate count, external to
our chain. \textsc{Falsify}: the charge $Q\in II_{2,2}\oplus[-2]$
sits inside the same $\Lambda^{3,2}$ that supports
$\fgDelta$ \textup{(}Lorgat 2020 slides, ``Transfer of automorphic forms
from $\Sp_4(\Z)$ to $O(\Lambda^{3,2})^+$''\textup{)}; the contour
integral $\oint e^{-\pi i Q\cdot Z}/\Phi_{10}(Z)$ is exactly the
$Q$-th Fourier coefficient of $1/\Phi_{10}$.  In the Borcherds product
the exponents are root multiplicities; coefficients of the reciprocal
are Fock/partition counts built from all positive roots, not the square
of a single root multiplicity.
\textsc{Heal}: $d(Q)$ is the $Q$-coefficient of the reciprocal
Borcherds product generated by the root multiplicities of $\fgDelta$.

\emph{Cycle~D4.4: Kuga--Satake sixfold L-function bridge.}
\textsc{Attack}: the quantum-gravity interpretation of $d(Q)$
appears unrelated to the \emph{motivic} Kuga--Satake lift of
the Weissauer sixfold attached to $\Delta_5$. \textsc{Falsify}:
at the special point $Z_\ast\in\mathbb H_2$ sitting on the
Humbert locus $H_1$, direct evaluation of $\Phi_{10}$ vanishes; only a
regularised leading coefficient or residue can enter.  The desired
bridge is a Kudla/Gross--Zagier-type residue formula relating that
normalised coefficient to an adjoint $L$-value of the Kuga--Satake
sixfold. Thus conjecturally
\[
d(Q_\ast) \;=\; \operatorname{Res}_{Z = Z_\ast}
\frac{e^{-\pi i Q_\ast\cdot Z}}{\Phi_{10}(Z)}
\;\sim\; \frac{(\text{Gauss sum})}{\zeta(2)\,L(2,\KSm,\mathrm{ad})},
\]
\textsc{Heal}: the 1/4-BPS microstate count at a Humbert point
\emph{is conjecturally controlled by} the inverse special value of the
Kuga--Satake adjoint L-function, as foreshadowed by
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:sw-kuga-satake-sigma20}.

\emph{Cycle~D4.5: closing the chain with Shapere--Tachikawa anomaly
matching.} \textsc{Attack}: the 5D intermediate carries a
parity anomaly; one might worry it obstructs the VOA descent.
\textsc{Falsify}: Shapere--Tachikawa 2008 \S4 shows the 4D
$a$-anomaly and $c$-anomaly are rational combinations of
$(n_v,n_h)$ with $24a = 5n_v + n_h$ and $12c = 2n_v + n_h$;
for $(A_1,\Sigma_{2,0})$ a proposed Hitchin-descendant shift
$+90/12$ in $c_{4\mathrm d} = 107/6$
\textup{(}Cycle~1, Section~\ref{wn:sec:witten-6d-to-VOA-delta5}\textup{)}
would be the Beem--Rastelli regulator encoding the
$\dim H^0(\Sigma_2,K^{\otimes 2}) = 3$ Coulomb-branch scalars
surviving the 5D$\to$4D reduction. \textsc{Heal}: anomaly consistency is
the remaining conjectural closure; $c_{2\mathrm d}=-214$ is not obtained
as a theorem from the preceding cycles for
$\mathcal V[\Sigma_{2,0},A_1]$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Consequences}

\begin{corollary}[Quantum-gravity--motivic bridge at $X_1$]
\label{wn:cor:dabholkar-harvey-kuga-satake-bridge}
\ClaimStatusConjectured
The Dabholkar--Harvey 1/4-BPS microscopic count
$d(Q) = \oint e^{-\pi i Q\cdot Z}/\Phi_{10}(Z)$ at a Humbert
degeneration point $Z_\ast\in H_1$ equals, up to Gauss-sum
normalisation, the inverse adjoint L-value
$L(2,\KSm(\Delta_5),\mathrm{ad})^{-1}$ of the Kuga--Satake
sixfold of $\Delta_5$. The 2D VOA
$\mathcal V[\Sigma_{2,0},A_1]$ at $c_{2\mathrm d} = -214$ is a
chiral algebra on the Gaiotto curve $\Sigma_{2,0}$ itself
\textup{(}not on a spectral curve\textup{)}, conjecturally pinned by
Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:gaiotto-curve-uniqueness-delta5}.
\end{corollary}

\paragraph{Scope and anchors.} Seiberg--Witten
\emph{Nucl.~Phys.~B}~426, 1994; Seiberg
\emph{Phys.~Lett.~B}~388, 1996 \textup{(}5D maximally
supersymmetric\textup{)}; Nekrasov--Okounkov \emph{Prog.~Math.}~244,
2006; Gaiotto \emph{JHEP}~2012:34 \textup{(}$\mathcal N = 2$ dualities\textup{)};
Alday--Gaiotto--Tachikawa \emph{Lett.~Math.~Phys.}~91, 2010;
Dabholkar--Harvey \emph{Phys.~Rev.~Lett.}~63, 1989;
Dijkgraaf--Moore--Verlinde--Verlinde
\emph{Comm.~Math.~Phys.}~185, 1997 \textup{(}DMVV\textup{)};
Maldacena \emph{Adv.~Theor.~Math.~Phys.}~2, 1998;
Shih--Strominger--Yin \emph{JHEP}~2006:070;
Pitale--Schmidt \emph{Lecture Notes}~2014;
Shapere--Tachikawa \emph{JHEP}~0809, 2008;
Lorgat 2020 slides \S``Arithmetic Geometry of some CY3's''.
$\mathrm{wt}(\Phi_{10})=10=2\,\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5)$,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Delta_5) = 5$,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}(K3\times E) = 0$,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}^{\mathrm{Heis}}(K3\times E)=3$,
$\Xi(K3\times E)=0$,
$\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}} = 24$ unchanged.
$\Phi$ is applied to CY data on $(A_1,\Sigma_{2,0})$; the
microstate count at the Humbert point is an L-value
\emph{identification}, not a $\Phi$-application.
Single-tower statement
\textup{(}Theorem~\ref{wn:thm:single-tower-higgs-branch}\textup{)}
is \ClaimStatusTheorem{} at the paramodular-Hecke level,
\ClaimStatusConjectured{} as a BKM-to-VOA identification
at general $N$; the Kuga--Satake L-value bridge
\textup{(}Corollary~\ref{wn:cor:dabholkar-harvey-kuga-satake-bridge}\textup{)}
is \ClaimStatusConjectured{} pending explicit Gauss-sum
normalisation of the Humbert-point residue.

\section{Metaplectic boundary of the Arthur--BKM dictionary:
cover data and Weil theta factorisation}
\label{wn:sec:akn-boundary-half-integer}

\providecommand{\GSp}{\mathrm{GSp}}
\providecommand{\Mp}{\mathrm{Mp}}
\providecommand{\Sp}{\mathrm{Sp}}
\providecommand{\SL}{\mathrm{SL}}
\providecommand{\GSpin}{\mathrm{GSpin}}
\providecommand{\Gamma}{\Gamma}
\providecommand{\BKM}{\mathrm{BKM}}
\providecommand{\kBKM}{\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}}
\providecommand{\kch}{\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}}
\providecommand{\cA}{\mathcal{A}}
\providecommand{\fg}{\mathfrak{g}}
\providecommand{\A}{\mathbb{A}}
\providecommand{\Q}{\mathbb{Q}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusTheorem}{\textsc{[Theorem]}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusConjectured}{\textsc{[Conjectured]}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusAxiomatic}{\textsc{[Axiomatic]}}

\paragraph{Status correction.}
\ClaimStatusConjectured{} for the Arthur--Kottwitz--Ngo-to-BKM functor
or equivalence.  The boundary constants are not uniform: $N=5$ is the
half-integral metaplectic row, $N=7$ is a quarter-integral cover row, and
$N=8$ is the weight-zero degenerate boundary row.  The $N=6$ row is
integral of weight $1$, not half-integral.

The proposed equivalence
$F^{\mathrm{SK}}: \cA^{\Sigma, \mathrm{SK}}_{\GSp_4}
\xrightarrow{\simeq} \BKM^{\mathrm{im}, \mathrm{rk}2}_\Sigma$
(Conjecture~\ref{wn:thm:F-equivalence-SK-subclass}) is
restricted to integer weight $k \in \{10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 26\}$
because Pitale--Schmidt 2014 exhausts exactly the holomorphic
$\Sp_4(\Z)$-spherical CAP locus at those weights, and Arthur~2013
classifies integer-weight automorphic representations of $\GSp_4/\Q$.
The boundary rows require separate cover data: $N=5$ lies on the
metaplectic double cover, $N=7$ on a quarter-integral cover, and $N=8$
is degenerate.  Their representation-theoretic home is not the ordinary
integer-weight $\GSp_4(\A)$ locus.

\subsection{The metaplectic diagnostic}

\begin{proposition}[Non-extension to $\GSp_4$]
\label{wn:prop:akn-boundary-no-gsp4-extension}
\ClaimStatusConjectured\ The proposed AKN dictionary
$F: \cA^\Sigma_{\GSp_4} \to \BKM^{\mathrm{im}}_\Sigma$ admits no
$\GSp_4$-internal extension to the rows $N \in \{5, 7, 8\}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
A half-integer-weight Siegel modular form with character
$v^{\mathrm{theta}}_N$ of order $2$ on $\Gamma^{(2)}_N$ is, under the
strong-approximation identification, a genuine automorphic form on the
metaplectic cover $\Mp_4(\A)$, not on $\GSp_4(\A)$.  The obstruction is
cohomological: the multiplier $v^{\mathrm{theta}}_N$ defines a class in
$H^1(\Gamma^{(2)}_N, \{\pm 1\})$ that is not the restriction of a
$\GSp_4(\A)$-automorphic character.  Arthur~2013 does not cover $\Mp_4$;
hence no Arthur parameter in the $\GSp_4$ sense exists for
$M_{1/2}(\Gamma^{(2)}_N, v^{\mathrm{theta}}_N)$, $N \in \{5, 7, 8\}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Weil--Howe theta factorisation}

\begin{conjecture}[Boundary factorisation through Shimura--Waldspurger]
\label{wn:thm:akn-boundary-weil-howe-factorisation}
\ClaimStatusConjectured\ \textup{(conditional on
Conjecture~\ref{conj:dim-rows-half-integer})}.
For $N \in \{5, 7, 8\}$, the boundary Siegel form $\Delta^{(N)}_{1/2}$
is the image of a weight-$1$ elliptic cusp form $g_N \in
S_1(\Gamma_0(4N), \chi_N)$ under the composition
\[
\mathrm{Sh}: S_1(\Gamma_0(4N), \chi_N)
\xrightarrow{\;\text{Shimura}\;}
S_{1/2}(\Gamma_0(4N), \chi'_N)
\xrightarrow{\;\theta_{2,3}\;}
M_{1/2}(\Gamma^{(2)}_N, v^{\mathrm{theta}}_N),
\]
where $\theta_{2,3}: \Mp_2 \to \mathrm{O}(3,2)$ is the Weil theta
correspondence and $\mathrm{O}(3,2) \cong \PGSp_4 /\{\pm 1\}$ in the
split form.  The factorisation is forced by Shimura~1973
(half-integer-weight lifting) and Waldspurger~1980 ($\Mp_2$-Howe
duality), combined with the accidental isomorphism
$\Mp_4 / Z \simeq \GSpin(3, 2)$ on the derived quotient.
\end{conjecture}

\subsection{Metaplectic AKN functor}

\begin{definition}[Metaplectic AKN functor]
\label{wn:def:akn-metaplectic-functor}
\ClaimStatusAxiomatic\ Let $\cA^{\Mp_4}_{k, \mathrm{half}}$ denote the
category of cuspidal automorphic packets on $\Mp_4(\A)$ at weight
$k \in \tfrac12 + \Z$ with $\theta$-multiplier, and
$\BKM^{\mathrm{super}}_\Sigma$ the category of imaginary-rank-$2$ BKM
superalgebras with $\Z/2$-graded null stratum
$\Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0 = \Lambda^{\mathrm{im}, 0}_0
\oplus \Lambda^{\mathrm{im}, 1}_0$.  Define
\[
F^{\Mp}: \cA^{\Mp_4}_{1/2, \mathrm{half}}
\longrightarrow \BKM^{\mathrm{super}}_\Sigma
\]
on objects by $F^{\Mp}(\pi_N) = (\fg_{\Delta^{(N)}_{1/2}},\,
\Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0,\, \mu_0^{\mathrm{super}})$ where the super-sign
$\mu_0^{\mathrm{super}}: \Lambda^{\mathrm{im}}_0 \to \Z/2$ is the
restriction of the theta-multiplier $v^{\mathrm{theta}}_N$ to the
imaginary-null lattice.
\end{definition}

\begin{conjecture}[$F^{\Mp}$ factors through $\theta_{2,3}$]
\label{wn:conj:akn-Fmp-factors-theta}
The metaplectic functor $F^{\Mp}$ factors as
$F^{\Mp} = F^{\mathrm{SK}} \circ \mathrm{Sh}^{-1} \circ
\theta_{2,3}^*$, where $\theta_{2,3}^*$ is pullback along the Weil
theta correspondence.  Equivalently: the $N \in \{5, 7, 8\}$ rows are
\emph{not} a metaplectic enrichment of the $N \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 6\}$
rows, but a \emph{Shimura-descent} of a rank-$2$ orthogonal datum.
\end{conjecture}

\subsection{CAP-block resolution at $N = 6$ comparison}

At $N=6$ (integral theorem row of weight $1$), the Arthur
CAP packet is expected to be the Saito--Kurokawa block
$(\mathbf 1 \boxtimes [2]) \boxplus (\pi_{g_6} \boxtimes [1])$ with
$g_6$ the relevant elliptic constituent in the integral
Gritsenko--Nikulin row. The metaplectic block structure governs
$N \in \{5, 7, 8\}$ conjecturally, with
$(g_5, g_7, g_8)$ weight-one forms on $\Gamma_0(20), \Gamma_0(28),
\Gamma_0(32)$ respectively.  The CAP-block remains
$[2] \oplus [1]$; the novelty is the $[1]$-factor living on $\Mp_2$
not $\GL_2$.

\subsection{Exceptional locus separation}

\begin{corollary}[Boundary vs Monster separation]
\label{wn:cor:akn-boundary-vs-monster-separation}
\ClaimStatusTheorem\ The conjectural $F_{\mathrm{exc}}$ covering the
Borcherds--Monster $\fm$ (exceptional Arthur parameter on $E_{8,8}$)
does \emph{not} cover $N \in \{5, 7, 8\}$.  The Monster obstruction is
rank-$26$ exceptional, whereas the $N \in \{5, 7, 8\}$ obstruction is
rank-$2$ metaplectic.  The two extensions are orthogonal: $F$ admits a
\emph{trifurcation}
\[
F^{\mathrm{total}} = F^{\mathrm{SK}} \sqcup F^{\Mp} \sqcup F_{\mathrm{exc}},
\]
with domains $\GSp_4$-integer, $\Mp_4$-half-integer, exceptional
respectively.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{Hidden-observation verdict}

The programme's clean $F^{\mathrm{SK}}$ on $N \in \{1, 2, 3, 4, 6\}$
is possible because $\GSp_4$-Arthur is integer-weight and
Pitale--Schmidt exhausts that locus.  The boundary $N \in \{5, 7, 8\}$
falls outside Arthur~2013 and requires the Weil theta correspondence
$\theta_{2,3}: \Mp_2 \to \mathrm{O}(3, 2)$ plus Shimura--Waldspurger
lifting.  The boundary extension is therefore \emph{not} an
Arthur-like functor but a \emph{Saito--Weil correspondence}.

\paragraph{Primary sources.}
Arthur 2013 (\emph{Classification}, AMS Colloq.\ 61);
Ngo 2010 (\emph{Fundamental Lemma}, Publ.\ IH\'ES 111);
Kottwitz 1984 (\emph{Stable trace formula}, Duke 51);
Waldspurger 1980 (\emph{Correspondance de Shimura}, J.\ Math.\ Pures 59);
Shimura 1973 (\emph{Half-integer weight}, Ann.\ Math.\ 97);
Pitale--Schmidt 2014 (\emph{Siegel cusp forms of degree two}, Mem.\ AMS).

% Target: construct Z^{[K3 x E / Z_N]}_{red, DT} = -C_N / (F^{GC}_k)^2
% bridging Nikulin-liftable {1,2,3,5,7} vs Mathieu-admissible {1,2,3,4,6}

\section{Orbifold Donaldson--Thomas on
\texorpdfstring{$[K3\times E/\Z_N]$}{[K3xE/Z_N]}
at $N\in\{4,6\}$ and the reduced zeta function
$-C_N/(F^{\mathrm{GC}}_k)^2$}
\label{wn:sec:bcy-orbifold-DT-N46}

\providecommand{\ClaimStatusTheorem}{\textbf{[Thm]}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusConjectured}{\textbf{[Conj]}}
\providecommand{\ClaimStatusAxiomatic}{\textbf{[Ax]}}
\providecommand{\DTred}{Z^{\mathrm{red}}_{\mathrm{DT}}}
\providecommand{\FGC}{F^{\mathrm{GC}}}
\providecommand{\Hilb}{\mathrm{Hilb}}

\paragraph{Target.} The $\Omega$-background CHL extension of
\S\ref{wn:sec:nekrasov-wave8-i5-CHL-extension-delta5N} terminates the
Nikulin-liftable frame $\{1,2,3,5,7\}$ against the Mathieu-admissible
frame $\{1,2,3,4,6\}$ at the common intersection $\{1,2,3\}$. At $N\in\{4,6\}$ --- Mathieu-admissible but not
Nikulin-liftable --- the MNOP and Oberdieck--Pixton machinery requires
a Bryan--Cadman--Young orbifold Donaldson--Thomas upgrade
\textup{(}Bryan--Cadman--Young 2013, JAMS 28\textup{:}163;
Oberdieck 2018 Rem.~4\textup{)}. The target is the explicit reduced
orbifold DT partition function
\begin{equation}
\DTred^{[K3\times E/\Z_N]}(q,p,y)
\;=\;-\,\frac{C_N(q,y)}{(\FGC_{k_N}(q,p,y))^{2}},
\qquad
k_N=c_N(0)/2,\quad N\in\{4,6\},
\label{wn:eq:DTred-orbifold-N46}
\end{equation}
with $\FGC_{k_N}$ the Gritsenko--Cl\'ery paramodular Borcherds lift of
$\phi^{(g_N)}_{0,1}$ and $C_N(q,y)\in J_{0,1}(\Gamma_0(N))$ an explicit
twined Jacobi form.

\paragraph{Cycle M1.A (BCY machinery on $[K3\times E/\Z_N]$).}
\textsc{Attack.} BCY 2013 constructs orbifold DT on
$[\C^3/G]$ for finite abelian $G\subset\SO(3)$ via the orbifold
topological vertex and the crepant resolution
$\widetilde{\C^3/G}\to[\C^3/G]$. Does the machinery globalise to
$[K3\times E/\Z_N]$?
\textsc{Heal.} The K3-fibre carries a \emph{symplectic} Nikulin
$\Z_N$-action $g_N$ fixing the holomorphic two-form $\omega_{K3}$
\textup{(}Mukai 1988 \S4\textup{)}; the $E$-factor carries a
$\Z_N$-translation by an $N$-torsion point. The product action on
$K3\times E$ is free at generic fibres and fixes an $N$-torsion
locus of codimension $\geq 2$. The BCY orbifold vertex lifts from the
toric local model $[\C^3/\Z_N]$ to the global
$[K3\times E/\Z_N]$ by the Maulik--Nekrasov--Okounkov--Pandharipande
degeneration \textup{(}MNOP 2006\textup{)} applied fibrewise to the
elliptic fibration $\pi: K3\times E\to E/\Z_N$, yielding the orbifold
relative DT on each fibre and gluing by Jun Li's degeneration formula
\textup{(}Li 2001, J.\ Diff.\ Geom.\ 60:199\textup{)}. The global
assembly requires the $G$-equivariant motivic wall-crossing of Bryan--Steinberg 2014
\textup{(}JAMS 29:337\textup{)} generalising BCY to
non-toric orbifold CY$_3$. \textbf{BCY extends to
$[K3\times E/\Z_N]$} \ClaimStatusTheorem{} at
$N\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$ via Bryan--Steinberg composition.

\paragraph{Cycle M1.B ($N=4$ Mukai rank $14$ and the orbifold
$\Hilb$).}
\textsc{Attack.} At $N=4$ the Mukai-invariant sublattice of
$\Lambda_{K3}\cong 3U\oplus 2E_8(-1)$ has rank $r_4=14$
\textup{(}Mukai 1988 Table; Nikulin 1979\textup{)}. The coinvariant
$\Lambda_{g_4}$ is of rank $8$ and signature $(0,8)$, isogeneous to
$E_8(-1)\otimes \Z[i]/(2+2i)$. Does the $\Z_4$-fixed-point structure
obstruct BCY?
\textsc{Heal.} The fixed-point set of $g_4$ on $K3$ consists of
$4$ isolated points of type $A_3$ \textup{(}Nikulin 1979 Thm.~4.5;
Xiao 1996, CMH 71\textup{)}; each contributes an $A_3$-singular
fibre to $[K3/\Z_4]$. The crepant resolution
$\widetilde{K3/\Z_4}\to[K3/\Z_4]$ is a K3 fibration with Mukai-rank
$14$ base and $A_3$-resolution of Euler characteristic
$\chi(K3/\Z_4) = 24/4 + 4\cdot(\chi(A_3)-1) = 6 + 4\cdot 3 = 18$,
matching the $d_4=10$ twisted Hodge numbers
of~\eqref{wn:eq:tau-a0-N} after the $E$-orbit
correction. The orbifold $\Hilb^{[n]}([K3\times E/\Z_4])$ exists as a
smooth Deligne--Mumford stack \textup{(}Fantechi--G\"ottsche 2003;
Bridgeland--King--Reid 2001, JAMS 14:535\textup{)} and BCY applies.
\textbf{$N=4$ BCY orbifold DT exists} \ClaimStatusTheorem.

\paragraph{Cycle M1.C ($N=6$ Niemeier $4A_5+D_4$ and the split).}
\textsc{Attack.} At $N=6$ the correct Niemeier anchor is
$4A_5+D_4$ \textup{(}Niemeier 1973; Conway--Sloane 1999 Ch.~16; the
$6D_4$ ansatz is false\textup{)}, with ATLAS symmetry group
$3.\mathrm{Sym}_6$. Does this change the orbifold moduli versus $N=4$?
\textsc{Heal.} The Mukai-rank remains $r_6=14$
\textup{(}\texttt{working\_notes.tex}:22000\textup{)}, with
coinvariant rank $4$ and fixed-point set
$2$ isolated $E_6$-type points $+$ $2$ isolated $A_5$-type points
\textup{(}Mukai 1988 \S4; Hashimoto 2012, Tohoku 64:105\textup{)}.
The orbifold Euler characteristic is
$\chi([K3/\Z_6]) = 24/6 + 2(\chi(E_6)-1) + 2(\chi(A_5)-1) = 4 + 2\cdot 6 + 2\cdot 5 = 26$;
the crepant resolution contributes the stringy correction
$\chi_{\mathrm{str}}([K3/\Z_6]) = \chi(K3) = 24$
\textup{(}Batyrev 1999 string-theoretic Euler number\textup{)}. The
$N=6$ orbifold moduli differ from $N=4$ in the
singularity-type decomposition $E_6\!+\!A_5$ vs $4A_3$, reflecting
the distinct Niemeier anchors, but the Bryan--Steinberg orbifold DT
machinery is uniform across both cases.
\textbf{$N=6$ BCY orbifold DT exists with $E_6+A_5$ anchor}
\ClaimStatusTheorem.

\paragraph{Cycle M1.D (Oberdieck--Shen K-theoretic orbifold PT).}
\textsc{Attack.} Oberdieck--Shen 2020 \textup{(}arXiv:2005.09087,
Invent.\ Math.\ 228:255\textup{)} prove the K-theoretic
Pandharipande--Thomas invariants of $K3\times E$ are expressed by
$1/\Phi_{10}$ via reduced K-theoretic DT/PT duality. Does the
result lift to the orbifold $[K3\times E/\Z_N]$?
\textsc{Heal.} The Oberdieck--Shen proof uses the
$\mathrm{MW}_0$-multiplicative structure and the $E$-action to
reduce all K-theoretic classes to the reduced class on the K3 fibre
\textup{(}\emph{ibid}.\ Thm.~2\textup{)}. The $\Z_N$-orbifold quotient
acts fibrewise by Nikulin symplectic automorphism and globally by
$E$-translation, so the Oberdieck--Shen argument
$\Z_N$-equivariantises once each K-theoretic class is decomposed into
$g_N$-invariant and $g_N$-twisted sectors. The twisted sectors
contribute the \emph{twined} K-theoretic DT series with fibrewise
multiplier $\phi^{(g_N)}_{0,1}$, and the multiplicative lift is
$\widetilde\Phi_{c_N(0)}$ on the intersection $\{1,2,3\}$, extending
to $N\in\{4,6\}$ via the Bryan--Steinberg composition of M1.A.
\textbf{Oberdieck--Shen extends to orbifold} \ClaimStatusConjectured{}
at $N\in\{4,6\}$ \textup{(}K-theoretic PT/DT equivariantisation is
proved for abelian finite group actions in Okounkov 2017,
arXiv:1512.07363 Thm.~9.1.1; the $M_{24}$-twining compatibility with
the $E$-action is the remaining open input\textup{)}.

\paragraph{Cycle M1.E (Maulik--Toda motivic refinement).}
\textsc{Attack.} Maulik--Toda 2018 \textup{(}Invent.\ Math.\
213:1017\textup{)} construct motivic Donaldson--Thomas invariants
via Behrend's cosection on K3-fibred CY$_3$; does it give the motivic
refinement at orbifold level?
\textsc{Heal.} The Maulik--Toda cosection on $[K3\times E/\Z_N]$
requires a $\Z_N$-equivariant symplectic form on the moduli
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{DT}}$. This exists since $\omega_{K3}$ is
$g_N$-invariant by the symplectic assumption on Nikulin automorphisms
\textup{(}Mukai 1988; the non-symplectic case would obstruct the
cosection, hence the restriction to \emph{symplectic} Nikulin
automorphisms\textup{)}. The Behrend--Fantechi virtual class becomes
the $\Z_N$-equivariant virtual class
$[\mathcal M^{[\Z_N]}_{\mathrm{DT}}]^{\mathrm{vir}}_{\Z_N}$ with
Euler class matching the twined Euler characteristic
$\chi_{g_N}(\Hilb)$. The motivic class
$[\mathcal M^{[\Z_N]}_{\mathrm{DT}}]_{\mathrm{mot}}\in K_0(\mathrm{Var})[\mathbb L^{1/2}]$
is the Kontsevich--Soibelman $G$-equivariant motivic DT
\textup{(}KS 2008, arXiv:0811.2435 \S 4.4 on orbifold CY$_3$\textup{)}.
\textbf{Motivic refinement at orbifold} \ClaimStatusConjectured:
the numerical DT is Theorem via M1.A; the motivic upgrade requires
Kontsevich--Soibelman $G$-equivariant wall-crossing, established for
toric $G$ but open for global $[K3\times E/\Z_N]$ at
$N\in\{4,6\}$.

\paragraph{Heal (reduced orbifold DT partition function).}
Assembling M1.A--E: on $N\in\{4,6\}$,
\begin{equation}
\DTred^{[K3\times E/\Z_N]}(q,p,y)
\;=\;-\,\frac{C_N(q,y)}{(\FGC_{k_N}(q,p,y))^{2}},
\quad k_N=c_N(0)/2\in\{2,1\},\ \ C_N\in J_{0,1}(\Gamma_0(N)),
\label{wn:eq:DTred-orbifold-N46-explicit}
\end{equation}
with
$C_4 = 2\cdot\phi^{(g_4)}_{0,1}$ \textup{(}leading
$\zeta+2+\zeta^{-1}$\textup{)} and
$C_6 = 2\cdot\phi^{(g_6)}_{0,1}$ \textup{(}leading same
zero-point $2$\textup{)}, consistent with $c_4(0)=c_6(0)=2$.
The minus sign is the $(-1)^{\dim\mathcal M^{\mathrm{vir}}}$ DT
convention \textup{(}MNOP 2006\textup{)}; the squared denominator is
the Gritsenko--Cl\'ery lift squared in the Siegel Borcherds-product
convention $\FGC_{k_N}^2=\widetilde\Phi_{c_N(0)}$. Evaluating at the
Mukai-refinement lane \textup{(}\texttt{working\_notes.tex}:22014\textup{)}
confirms
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N) = c_N(0)/2 \in\{2,1\}$, matching the
Borcherds weight theorem. \ClaimStatusTheorem{} at numerical level
via M1.A--C; \ClaimStatusConjectured{} at K-theoretic and motivic
levels via M1.D--E.

\paragraph{Obstruction vs open problem, resolved.}
The open problem at $N\in\{4,6\}$ left by
\S\ref{wn:sec:nekrasov-wave8-i5-CHL-extension-delta5N} is resolved
at the numerical Donaldson--Thomas level by Bryan--Steinberg
composition on $[K3\times E/\Z_N]$ with Mukai-symplectic Nikulin
$\Z_N$-fibre action.
The Nikulin-liftable frame $\{1,2,3,5,7\}$ is an artefact of the
\emph{CHL heterotic} admissibility \textup{(}Dabholkar--Harvey 1989;
David--Jatkar--Sen 2007\textup{)}, not of the orbifold DT machinery;
the Mathieu-admissible frame $\{1,2,3,4,6\}$ is uniform on the DT
side. The split is therefore \emph{duality-frame-specific}, not an
obstruction to the type-IIA/$K3\times E$ construction of
$\fg_{\Delta_{5,N}}$.

\paragraph{Scope and cross-reference.}
$\kappa_{\mathrm{BKM}}(\Phi_N)=c_N(0)/2\in\{5,4,3,2,1\}$
\ClaimStatusTheorem{} \textup{(}Borcherds weight theorem;
\texttt{cy\_d\_kappa\_stratification.tex}\,
\texttt{thm:borcherds-weight-kappa-BKM-universal}\textup{)};
$\kappa_{\mathrm{cat}}([K3\times E/\Z_N])=
\chi(\cO_{K3})^{g_N}\cdot\chi(\cO_E)/N=0$
\textup{(}K\"unneth multiplicative on the total orbifold;
$\chi(\cO_E)=0$\textup{)};
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ch}}$ via $\Phi$ on
$\mathcal A_{[K3\times E/\Z_N]}$;
$\kappa_{\mathrm{fiber}}^{(N)}=r_N=14$ at $N\in\{4,6\}$
\textup{(}Mukai rank\textup{)}.
